The Equilibrium, a key to success!

Supply, demand and market balance form the basis of microeconomics. Take only 20 minutes and watch two videos.

Inserted Video

This example with apples shows our market situation. It's always about finding the best price, and the best price is always in balance. Here in the Forex market, there is a crucial difference to the example shown in the video.

Inserted Video

Every trader can sometimes act as a seller and sometimes as a buyer. And that is a very special opportunity. But I have to understand the connection between supply and demand. If I can determine the equilibrium on the basis of the Kurtselle, I turned the future probability in my favor.

For some years now, I've stopped by at Forex Factory and was always excited about the great contributions. Interesting opinions, charts and indicators should help to support the private trader. In this shark tank the forex market is turbulent. The beginners have a hard time. Just think about football once. If you want to learn football, you can start in a youth team and play up to the NFL.

In the Forex market, there is no beginner market, because the beginner plays against the biggest professionals in the world. And how that ends, everyone can think.

Well, if there are such platforms as Forex Factory, where traders from all over the world come together to face the biggest traders in the world. Of course, every trader is the competitor to the other, but you help each other out.

When trading, there are many keys to success. In my first post I want to show you a key to success. I do not want to discuss with you the meaning or nonsense of this key, but about the implementation to success. If the post is of any use to you, use the information, otherwise forget it again.

I do not claim that this key is the master key that always works.

This key works without indicators for all traders (of course only those who want to) in all time units.

The key "Equilibrium"

1. The price is determined by supply and demand in each market.

2. Any influence on the price will be returned from the price

3. Before the price moves up or down, a balance between supply and demand creates a balance.

4. If this balance is disturbed, the price moves in the direction of supply or in the direction of demand.

5. The price moves as long as supply or demand until there is a balance again. Then the whole thing starts from the beginning.

Most candles are where there is a balance. We do not want to trade there, because the price is not moving very much. So we have to act when there is no balance.

There are 3 different states in the market.

1. Offer outweighs the demand = price drops

2. Demand outweighs the offer = price rises

3. Supply and demand are balanced

According to the sellers the offer (short) there, while the buyers represent the demand (long).

1. Offer = Seller (short)

2. Request = Buyer (long)

The quantity available on the market represents the supply, the demand is the quantity that the buyer would like to purchase.

If you shop at the weekly market, do you want to pay $ 6 or 4 $ for 4 lbs tomatoes? Of course, only $ 4. So, assuming the product has the same quality, you will buy from the dealer, who only charges $ 4 for the tomatoes. Thus, the demand will be greater at the cheaper dealer than at the expensive dealer.

So what does the trader who sells the tomatoes for $ 6 / lbs do? For now, he only needs to sell 66% as much as his competitor to earn the same. Or he waits until the competitor has no more tomatoes, then sells his tomatoes for $ 6 / lb and earns 50% more. In the worst case, he has to go down with the price. These competing factors (supply and demand) meet each other in all markets and regulate the price.

In the stock market environment, the price strives to find a so-called equilibrium. At that moment, buyers and sellers are equally satisfied until an imbalance rebalances in favor of supply or demand. Then the prices rise or fall again.

But even if you can accurately identify supply and demand, you will not get on with it. Decisive are the zones where the supply outweighs the demand or the demand the supply.

Known as resistance or support.

These reversal points, which often have an increased volume, must be recognized.

There are many ways to work with resistance and support lines, I myself work only with horizontal lines, because I have the best experience.

Option A: Confirmation of resistance or support

If you have drawn resistance and support lines in the chart, look how the price is there. A later entry will often save you from big losses, but you will get into a less favorable course and minimize your potential profit. Important: the highest possible risk-reward ratio.

Option B: Enter without confirmation

You are sure how the course will behave at your indicated resistance or support line and will board immediately without waiting for a confirmation. If your expectation works out, you are at a bargain price, improving the chance-risk ratio. If the trade unfolds to your disadvantage, you need to get out early to protect yourself from major losses.

Identification of the equilibrium

The big problem with the candles in the chart is the period in which they are formed. Surely you know the candlestick formations like hammer, doji, engulfing, etc. Sometimes you work, but often not. This is due to the temporal composition of the candles. Candle formations in a certain time frame are therefore just a mere random product of the time, the broker and the dealer. If you change the time frame in which the candles are formed, so would the candles and their formations change. The doji is now a normal candle with no indication of a course change.

Therefore one should work with different time units to identify a possible equilibrium. Many turning points can be identified by means of the Equilibrium, but not all. The price in the chart is always random and nobody can predict 100% of the turning points in the chart. It's not necessary with strategic money management either. Decisive is the payoff ratio and the expectancy.

You can often see these turning points in advance and use them to your advantage. You have to look at the past of the charts, because the big traders (elephants) leave their mark in the snow, which is easier to recognize than the tracks of the small traders (hares).

Another advantage is that you do not have to load your screen with unnecessary indicators. Although I work with a self-created dashboard, which tells me primarily the momentary strength of each currency pairs and, for example, the dollar index, but I'm interested in this just before the entry or exit.

My main charts are almost entirely made up of my own resistance and support lines. The Candle Strength indicator often helps me to identify the effective candle thickness, which is not always easy with the above points.

The best indicator is the price chart and the orderbook. But the price chart is a trailing indicator, because only when the candle is completed, I get a meaningful information on the price level. But then it is often too late.

In my preliminary analysis, start with the day or 4H chart to determine the rough direction.

The 1H chart shows me the medium term bias and the 15min / 5 min chart the short term turning points in the market.

A very important instrument for me is the 15 second bar chart. In high phases of volatility you can recognize a structure faster.

A catchy example of equilibrium was in the EURUSD. After the price had risen from 1.03249 on 26.12.16 with a triple top to 1.20921 on 08.09.17 and slowly went into the correction phase, many traders wondered how far this correction would go.

The interesting thing is that the price of 1.15529 in the monthly chart was already reflected in a 2003 Equilibrium.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

If you look at the monthly chart from 1994 to 2018, you could derive some trading possibilities from the Equilibrium. This usually works in every unit of time.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Example Equilibrium in the 15 min chart between 11th and 13th October 2017

Now you will wonder if that always works. The answer is NO!

Then all traders would be millionaires. If someone wins $ 100, another will lose $ 100. That's the system.

If you have lost $ 100 you should not be sad. The money is not gone, it has only one other. And he's sure to be happy.

The identification of the relevant equilibrium is difficult and only possible through many years of experience. But as you can see, this trading option is well worth it. It is interesting for swing traders, day traders and scalpers and can be used in all timeframes.

To better identify an equilibrium, one should zoom down from higher time units to smaller time units. This filters out inaccuracies.

Incidentally, it is often helpful in the chart to remove the shadows to better recognize the Equilibrium.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Equilibrium in the 15 min chart with and without shadow

With Buy Limit and Sell Limit Order you can work well in this trading system, but is rather less recommended when scalping.

Even an Equlibrium professional will reach its limits, because trading has changed enormously in recent years. The price is unpredictable and still random. Even if you work with an orderbook, you often have to realize that there are many pseudo orders that are deleted shortly before the target. Oderflow, Footprint and Cumulative Delta are still good help, but unfortunately they can not look to the future.

Trading and making music have something in common. You can learn to play both, but in the end it's the right feeling and flair that determines success and failure.

I wish you a lot of flair and feeling for the great success.

Hello dear traders,

First of all thank you for your feedback and opinions. The question I was asked: How do I identify an Equilibrium?

The answer: with experience from the gut. If you spent 10,000 hours in front of the screen, you know how it works. At the beginning of the trader's career tried over 1,000 indicators, starting with the RSI, Stochastic, MACD and so on.

I could not do anything with that because these indicators are not ahead of the market, just like the price charts, they are just a thing of the past. So the fastest indicator is the candle, theoretically a 1 second candle, but there is too much inaccuracy to derive a future course.

After many 1,000 hours, I finally cleared most of the indicators on the screen. There had to be another way. If you have watched at least 10,000 hours of candles, you will notice recurring formations over time. I really like the shoulder-and-shoulders-shoulder-formation, but sometimes it only appears in different time-units and does not always behave like you expect.

You have to think and act as the big players. Many of them do not even have a bar chart, but sit in front of 8 screens where the orderbook plays thousands of numbers in seconds. If you refer this big player to the Metatrader, he will look at you questioningly.

In EURUSD, it often happens at 14:30 CET. The price suddenly drops 20 pips, then shoots and shoots up 60 pips. Often it is one and the same player. He pushes the price down first, stops the traders and has 20 pip below the price a big buy limit order. This chases the course upwards. Sure, you could put a buy stop order on the last resistance, the question is what price you come into the market. If you come in too late and the market is in the correction phase, you are outnumbered faster than you think.

It is easier to trade with small money than with big money. So the big player has to come up with something to make a profit. The small traders are not his problem, but the other big players. If two elephants fight with each other you should stay out of it. But you can wait until the fight is over and run with the winner. But that is easier said than done.

This brings us to Equilibrium. I can only write to you how I personally act. My opinion does not have to be right, because every trader has his own opinion and that's a good thing. Also, I do not want to be in the right, I want to trade because it makes me fun and you can also earn money on the side. But for me that is really secondary, because if you have to make money with it, it will be problematic because you have pressure. And printing is not good at trading.

First I search in a chart (the time unit does not matter) for an equibribrium where the price rises or falls sharply thereafter. Here is an example from today's EURUSD between 9:30 am and 2:00 pm CET.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

At 10:10 (dot1) and 10:15 (dot2) there was an equibribrium that I drew in the 1 minute chart. The price dropped by 14 pip and then went up again (point 3). Where did the course turn again? In the Equilibrium where afterwards the price fell stronger (point 2). At point 3 there was a bigger equilibrium and you see what happened when the course plunged into my marked area. The course was not so strong. Only at point 6 he went down a bit more. At point 6, a new equilibrium was formed, causing another slide. Point 5 signaled to me that the price would not continue to fall at the moment, but would rather rise.

You see (point 3 + 4) is a larger Equilibruim, the price is not strong. Points 1, 2, 5, 6 are smaller and more informative.

But that is no guarantee.

That was a small example in the 1 min chart. This works in the 4H chart and in all time units, but not always.

best regards

Hello dear traders,

some of you wanted to see some live examples about Equilibrium. On Fri 05.01.18 at 16:13 CET I posted a possible course in the EURUSD.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

I drew two resistance lines that were characterized by an equilibrium. I assumed that the first resistance line at which the course was breached and runs back down the second resistance line.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

An hour later at 17:12 CET you could see that the price did not reach the second resistance level, but it followed my marked course very nicely. I was convinced that the price would come up to this resistance later and then go down.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

As you can see on the chart at 20:08 CET, the price went to resistance at 19:00 CET for the first time and went down 5 pips. After that, he was in a sideways phase. (Here a nice equilibrium formed in the 30 minutes chart)

Nice thread Bionics! I like the topic, because I have also worked on this topic for years. Finally I found something that works for me well.

To find the equilibrium of the market (or called mid) is really really difficult. Let’s give some hints what I’ve found:

- a equilibrium needs a reference to a period of time, because price is a function of time, so let’s take the daily timeframe (open at 22gmt)

- what do we have? A Open, high, low and close. That’s not enough, we also need the tick data because price is a function of time. So when we have the ticks we also know what comes first high or low additionally we know when they made (in Asia, London or in US session)

now you have the data you need to calculate the equilibrium of a given period of time.

it works very well, but in major trends sometime buyer and sellers don’t need a equilibrium, but the price will always comes back to the equilibrium whenever possible.

Anyway there a 100000 possibilities to calculate a equilibrium!

Regards from germany

Hello Mr Brown,

welcome to our thread,

Why do some Equilibrium zones not work?

The big problem with the candles in the chart is the period in which they are formed. Surely you know how to hammer, doji, engulfing, etc. Sometimes you work, but often not. This is due to the temporal composition of the candles. Candle formations in a certain time frame are therefore just a random product of the time, the broker and the dealer. If you change the time frame in which the candles are formed, then the candles and their formations change. The doji is now a normal candle with no indication of a course change.

At the same time I have 6 different timeframes open for observation, so I can recognize the formation of an equilibrium faster. But still this system is not a system which can be solved with an indicator. It is very difficult and requires 10,000 hours of experience. But in the end you will be rewarded for it.

--- 帖子 #70 ---
Hello MaxenshteinD,

I have to go a bit further in calculating my defined candlestick strength. When looking at a typical candle, you will notice that the shadows are displayed in the respective candle color. Bullish candles have green shadows, while bearish candles have red shadows. This type of presentation is wrong in my opinion.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

A completed candle should usually show the correct price history.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Let's take a look at a bullish candle. The course starts at OPEN. Suppose that the course then runs directly to the LOW and then back to the OPEN. This means that the bears did push down the price, but the bulls had the upper hand in the end. So the bottom shadow should basically be green (bullish).

From the OPEN it goes now to the HIGH and back to the CLOSE, but above the OPEN. This means that the bulls raised the price but the bears were stronger. So the top shadow should always be red.

That means:

The bears were stronger in the upper shadow.

The bulls were stronger in the lower shade.

The correct graphical representation would look like this:

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Whether this graphic presentation, however, brings benefits, I can not judge. However, this calculation is important for my candle strength.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Whether you calculate the calculation in Pip or Mini Pip is irrelevant. I calculate with the 5th decimal place. The top shadow is calculated from HIGH / OPEN at the bearish candle and HIGH / CLOSE at the bullish candle. For the upper shadow, the value in Pip is always negative, and always positive for the lower shadow.

There are now 3 values that are added together. Wick (upper shadow), Candle and Fuse (lower shadow). This value is my pressure. It shows how strong the bears or bulls were at the end of the completed candle.

The actual candle body H/L or L/H is the decisive range in the particular time frame in which the candle is measured. With the% value, I look at the relationship between H/L (L/H) and pressure. From this it is now necessary to derive a proportionality.

To what extent this calculation is relevant for future price developments is in the eye of the respective observer. You know, a turnaround can be fast or slow. Using one indicator is one thing, interpretation is the other.

I hope I was able to help you just a little bit

Best regards

--- 帖子 #76 ---
Please be aware that Market profile/TPO charts are not indicators

TPO chart is a data base in fact.

The Equilibrium (in MP language called the POC or Price Of Control) is the place where the market has traded the most time on a certain time and period. Market is in balance on that level.

When the market wants to shift to an other level (for whatever reason) its looking for Gaps or Pockets called on the TPO chart.

The TPO peaks are the Supp/Res. levels which can be seen very easy on a TPO chart .

See the Euro/US$ Future chart on a Weekly base and you see the POC levels of each Week. (purple lines)

Right side TPOs are this Week TPOs

All TPOs plotted on the left are previous Weeks

--- 帖子 #108 ---
NIO, three factors that make it difficult to trade!

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

If you want to travel by boat from England to America, you should already look at the route and the possible weather conditions. When you're on the road, usually everything is different and you have to adjust individually to the situation. Storms have to be avoided, routes are recalculated, problems are eliminated and in the end you arrive anyway. But never as planned.

It's the same with trading. Before I make a trade, I should know where the course is going, otherwise I should rather leave it. And when the trade runs I need a "what if plan".

We are influenced by NIO. News, indicators and opinions

News

Not the news, but market participants influence the market.

In 2016, Deutsche Bank and many currency experts estimated that the EURUSD would reach 0.95 at the end of 2017. It came completely different.

It is always fun in the evening at NTV (German news channel) to learn why the DAX or EURUSD has risen or fallen. Of course the economy is important in the individual countries, but not for me. For me, how investors respond to the news is far more important.

It does not matter which news is about the ticker. The market is moving because people and computers are pushing the button BUY or SELL. And why are they pressing on BUY or SELL? Because they have an opinion. And this opinion often has nothing to do with the economic data.

Why does Apple share fall even though Apple released a sensational quarterly balance sheet? Well, maybe because investors believe Apple will not be able to make such profits in the next quarter or peak the stock. Anyway, we'll never know.

News causes storms on the stock markets, it often goes up and down. I prefer to wait, because sailing is simply no fun in a strong storm.

Indicators

An indicator does not care if the price goes up or down. It is trailing and less accurate than the price chart. Many traders need security and believe the indicator tells them where the market is going. But the market influences the indicator and not the other way round. That's why I work with auxiliary indicators, which I do not pay much attention to. If I can not trust myself, how should I trust indicators?

Opinion

Since about 97% of all traders are wrong, this means that 97% of all opinions are wrong. That's not bad, because since humans exist, he's wrong. Much more important it would be to set the 3%, whose opinion is correct. But finding them is a challenge. One solution would be to look at what opinion the majority has and then do exactly the opposite. So we should not listen to the crowd, but to ourselves.

Trading is a pure chance game, nobody knows where the journey is going. But with mathematical probability calculation I can beat the coincidence in my favor.

The big challenge of trading is not to win, but to behave properly when you are in loss.

I wish you a nice weekend

--- 帖子 #112 ---
Easy increase in trading efficiency!

Dear Traders,

As requested, you will receive a few tips today on the topic of financial management. I would like to neglect the chance risk ratio, stop loss or take profit. The background: Each trading style needs different values of these individual factors. There are traders who work with a stop loss of 5 PIP while others use 30 PIP or no stop loss. This risk limitation must be estimated by every trader. A scalper will often take a different chance risk ratio than a swing trader.

Today it will be about profit optimization in trading.

The calculation is relatively simple and only requires a few numbers. Let's take an example.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

In the left box you see the overall result within a period. In the middle box the split result of the buy order in the right box the sell order.

The two most important values are the pay-off ratio and the expected value.

Pay-Off Ratio = (Average Profit) / (Average Loss)

There are traders who have a hit rate of less than 40% and yet earn a lot of money. The secret, they have optimized their pay-off ratio. It means making sure the winners are bigger than the losers. A pay-off ratio of 0.2 means that in case of loss you need 5 winners to get back to 0. A pay-off ratio of 1 means that in case of loss you need 1 winner to be back at 0. The smaller the pay-off ratio, the higher the likelihood of total loss.

Expected value (Expetancy) = winrate * (average earnings) - loss ratio * (average losers)

In our case Expected Value = (0.729 * 10.34 PIP) - (0.271 * 7.45 PIP) = 5.52 PIP per trade

The expected value determines my profitability.

As you can see, we now differentiate between Buy Order and Sell Order.

I've found that the efficiency of the sell order is almost twice as high as the efficiency of the buy order. That means when I go short, I have almost twice the efficiency of going to long. Of course, this is often dependent on the trend that currently prevails in the market.

Now, if you perform this calculation for all the currency pairs you trade, you will have the following information.

1. Which currency pair is best for me?

2. Am I a seller or a shorter?

Now you can focus on the currency pairs, indicia or commodities where you are really good.

If you now only focus on the short positions in our example, that would look like this.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

In effect, you would have 200 PIP more income over the same period if you only trade short positions. And you have not changed your trading strategy yet. Of course, this result does not have to happen that way, but the probability is high.

Then it's all about optimizing the winrate, the pay-off ratio and the expected value to trade profitably.

Of course, there are very professional programs, I recommend: Think easy!!!

I wish you much success

Talk easy, but think complicated, not the other way around.

I'm not annoyed by that, but I'm glad that my assessment was correct, but I still have to work at the right entry point. I immediately forget about my loss and focus on the next trade.

So at some point I started to run the trade and after a while pulled the stop on the start and just waited. This made the win loss ratio much better. --- 帖子 #130 ---
Problem of traders: carbon dioxide

I've been asked what a small white box this is, left in the picture next to my trading station.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

It is a Co2 meter. What does a trader need a CO2 meter for?

Carbon dioxide or carbon dioxide is a chemical compound of carbon and oxygen with the molecular formula CO2. In high concentrations, this gas can be toxic to humans.

Outdoors there is a CO2 value of about 450 ppm (part per million). In closed rooms, especially in winter, the value can increase enormously.

For values below 800 ppm, the indoor air quality is considered good, values between 800 and 1000 ppm (0.08 to 0.1% by volume) are considered moderate, values from 1000 to 1400 ppm as moderate quality. For values above 1400 ppm, the indoor air quality is considered low. Then you should air. Before I bought the meter, I often had a headache while trading or was tired.

Carbon dioxide dissolved in the blood activates the respiratory center of the brain in physiological and slightly increased concentration. This means that the brain gets too little oxygen. In closed rooms, this often does not occur, you get tired and you get a bad headache.

Since I have the meter I'm warned. As soon as the room air reaches a value of more than 1,400 ppm, the device answers. Then I open the windows for 5 - 10 minutes and the value has dropped to 500 ppm.

Depending on how many people are in the room, the CO2 value goes up faster or slower.

Since then, I'm not tired anymore, I rarely have a headache and the concentration is optimal. I gave such a device to my son's school. If there are 20 children in a room, the CO2 levels are significantly worse. Since they now open the windows more often, the children can concentrate much better.

Such a device you get on Ebay or in stores, it costs about $ 130. Compared to the benefit is little money. Of course you can also open the window from time to time, but you know even if you are in a fever in trading that is quickly forgotten.

Healthy life includes good air and low CO2. Of course, this includes sports, the right diet and a lot of drinking.

Headache and tiredness done.

I wish you a nice week

How do I create important POCs from the past?

Hello dear traders,

As you know, there are 3 states in the market.

1st offer outweighs the demand = price drops

2. Demand outweighs the offer = price rises

3. Supply and demand are balanced

We do not want to act in equilibrium, so we wait until the price goes up or down. The price rises or falls on the POC lines, which we do not find with the help of indicators, but have to draw ourselves. Of course, there are indicators that are very unreliable.

If the course goes up in wavy lines and then falls again, it is easy to determine the POC, because the balance is in the immediate vicinity.

But what happens if the price rises like in the last weeks and you can not find a POC because there is no POC.

The answer: you just have to go far enough into the past.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

In the overview of the monthly chart you can see the yellow circle no. 1, which has given the course of 1.24 strong movements. So let's take a closer look at these movements in the 15 M chart. (If there is no important balance, we go to circle 2 or circle 3).

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

In 15 M Chart Dec 14 I then used the price equilibrium to draw my POC lines (in green). Note that these price movements are over 3 years ago.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Now let's take a look at the current chart EURUSD 23.-24. January 2018. As you can see, this works perfectly. While it is not always possible to predict how the price will behave at the POC, it is easier to anticipate in a smaller unit of time. It is crucial to first identify the balance. After that it can only go up or down. This helps me enormously in the calculation of my trades. With this help, I get a big advantage in the market. If you keep an eye on the momentum, anticipate how the big players think and read their footprints, you already have the key to success in your hands.

Best regards

How to use the POC profitably.

Hello dear traders,

From today's EURUSD, I'd like to show you how Equilibrium (POC) is determined and what happened next.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

The first POC was drawn at 12:20 CET, the second POC at 13:00 CET, the third at 13:50 CET and the fourth at 14:00 CET. In the second POC you can see very nicely how the price is in a downtrend. Suddenly a balance develops and then the course breaks down sharply. Therefore, this POC line was a strong resistance for me. The first POC was also strong but not that crucial. Although the 3rd and 4th POC lines are either resistance or support, they had to be watched closely when touched.
The lower POC was a strong resistance zone, let's see where it came from.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

On the 25th of January from 21:30 CET the first POC was formed. As you can see, this zone is crucial. When the price went down this morning at 9:30 CET, it was safe to assume that the price had fallen long enough to hold the resistance zone. Let's go back to the chart image.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

As you can see, you could have done quite clean 3 trades, even though we were actually moving in a sideways range. 90 Pip is a very good result in 2 hours, especially as there was a risk allocation here. The price was up again to the second resistance level on the first trade, but you would not have made a big loss here. Although the second trade went down about 2 pip, it would have triggered my maximum stop after 4 pip. Nevertheless, it went up 30 pip. The 3rd trade hesitated at the beginning because of the 3rd POC, but then went through cleanly up to take profit. My recommendation: Do not pull take profit up to the resistance level, so you better get something out in advance. The range was always 35 pip, so I only calculated with 30 pip.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Another interesting aspect: the big players. From 09:00 CET to 14:00 CET, the price today was about 60 pip down. At 14:30 CET there was a strong upward movement of 25 pip. Then it went downhill. What happened? A big player had placed a sell order within the 1st POC. At around 14:30 CET, where everyone thought the price was going down again, he gave up a buy order with a take profit at the price level of his sell limit order. The price jumped up, his take profit triggered and at the same time the sell limit order and the price went down automatically. The course came back a bit and was then pushed down by another order. The rest was done by the small players who wanted to go downstairs. So the big player was able to collect 70 pip in 45 minutes. That's not much, but absolutely sufficient for this range. Of course, there are 100 other reasons that may actually have expired, it is important to think about how the big players act. To juggle with 50,000 euros is easy, try that with a few million or billions. You have to be very creative in order to increase the assets of investors and to generate a return of 24% at the end of the year.

You see, it's important to take a closer look and study the big player approach. We can never win against the big players even if all the Forex Factory traders team up. The big ones would just laugh at that. We have only one chance, we can not fight against them, we just have to let them take us away. All we have to do is know where the big ones are going. Learn how to draw the POC correctly and practice it daily. The best total of 10,000 hours, then you are professional. Use indicators to support, but not in the main chart, only your POC counts and what you see.

Once you've found your profitable system, focus on it and forget about the POC. If not, you have a great chance to reach your goal with the POC.

Best regards

Hello phoenix168,

Thank you for your question, I recommend you to approach the matter easier. A balance arises in that the market participants (buyers and sellers) are satisfied. Demand and supply are thus balanced. After equilibrium, a pressure on demand or supply arises again. And until it comes to a balance again. This has nothing to do with the different trading venues. The different trading venues have only a different number of traders, which therefore move more or less money.

Let's look at an example:

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

On January 25, the EURUSD price was pushed down sharply. Looking at the picture, one could assume that the Asian market made sure that the price was pushed up again. In fact, the trigger for that was the US session.

For me, the London and US session is very important to trading. The best time for me in EURUSD is between 07:00 - 11:00 CET and 13:00 - 20:00 CET. There is often higher volatility and volatility is a key to success.

What I pay attention to when there is more volatility in the Asian market than usual on average. That was the case on the 24th / 25th of January. (I had published in a blog) Then the courses in the London session went up massively.

Any pronounced balance can be crucial, no matter what session.

I recommend that you first find out which currency pairs you have the most success with. Which trading style suits you? Can you better go up or down? What time unit is yours, your personal Moneymanagement as well as the chart setting, indicators and much more.

For this I have also published a blog.

At the beginning I made the mistake to trade too many currency pairs and lost the overview. The EURUSD currency pair is always dependent on the strength of the euro and the strength of the dollar. This strength is determined by many factors. Politics, industry, stability, economic growth, banks, ECB, Fed and much more.

How do you want to keep an eye on everything with different currency pairs?

In the EURUSD, for example, it is also important to keep an eye on the dollar index as well as the respective currency strength.

--- 帖子 #174 ---
Indicators- with 200 in the one-way street?

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Please note that this is just my personal opinion. Life experiences collected over the past 30 years should be thought-provoking and will not hurt or offend anyone. I am happy to learn something new every day. Especially by beginners who sometimes ask questions that stimulate thinking.

When I ordered my first shares by telephone at Deutsche Bank in the 90s, no one had any idea where the stock market and foreign exchange market would develop. By the year 2000, banks were struggling with liquidity problems in the foreign exchange market. Most banks were unable to handle the orders of many customers because there was insufficient liquidity in the market. Often the order was executed at less favorable prices than desired by the customer.

The Internet brought a new era and the stock market got the chance to win more participants for a more liquid market. If someone sells, it needs a buyer on the other side, otherwise the deal can not be settled. With many smaller traders, the principle of mutual funds is applied and is a profit for the liquidity in the market.

When I started trading many years ago, I was almost struck down by the amount of information on the market. To get a market overview, I started the hard way across the indicators. Indicators should indicate the future market direction and show me trade signals for the entrances and exits. I was hoping to see when a market movement ended and the likelihood of a change in direction being highest.

I researched over 2,000 different indicators, tried out concepts and functionalities, made comparisons and viewed hundreds of videos.

I still remember the first indicator. The famous moving average. When the blue line touches the red line we sell and when the red touches the blue line we buy.
That should have worked, just not with me. MACD, RSI, Stochastic, WPR I took the full program with me. Alone the theater the right attitude in the right timeframe was already challenge enough.

Then the videos of individual brokers where alleged professionals in addition to advertising for the broker, their best tips and tricks betrayed. One of them had a total of 15 indicators in the chart and explained the procedure. All students wrote so fast that their fingers were smoking. Today I understand why most people are not successful.

Sometimes I already thought that the big investors invented the indicators to take the money from the small trader.. After all, they know that many traders are speculating on a turnaround in the 61 retracement.

Through my job as a financial analyst, I knew some people who had dealings with the stock market. A hedge fund broker advised me to clear out all the indicators and look at the chart image for 10,000 hours. That's all, I asked? That's all he answered, then you know how to do it. I thought first, he does not mean that, but he meant it very seriously.

I sat in front of my screen and thought that you never could. But gradually I recognized recurrent patterns, began to draw resistance and support lines myself and began to sell the first trades. It did not work better in the beginning than with the indicators, but it got easier with time.Today I get along very well, am independent and can divide my own time.
Indicators are there to pretend to you a security that does not exist in trading. However, humans need security in order to put their sorely earned money at risk. Since you do not trust yourself, you are more likely to trust an indicator. If it goes wrong, the indicator is to blame, or the market.

The indicator is always trailing, that is, it derives its values from past price movements. How do you want to make the right decision with a trailing information in a live trade?

The indicator also does not take into account the situation in which the market is currently located, where the traders' orders are hidden, where the liquidity is located and which balance leads to a reversal.

Indicators are already working, some will say now. That's right, because assuming the RSI overbought reverses and many traders act on it, it can work now and then.

Most indicators are nonsensical to me and bring nothing but loss. Thus, no EAs come into question for me, because I have more information with the help of the POC and like to make the decisions myself.
However, I do not think indicators are fundamentally bad. So-called auxiliary indicators, facilitate my work and provide a better overview.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

The view is hardly limited, although here are almost 10 auxiliary indicators at work. The One Click Trading indicator is now indispensable to me. Many brokers already provide this tool for free. When I trade, all factors such as Stop, Take Profit, Trailing Stop, Time Close, Vertical or Horizontal Line Level are already set and cost me no time.

What alternative is there to the indicators?

To make long-term gains in the stock market, I need a knowledge advantage over the other traders. I can interpret this knowledge advantage only from the pure chart image. In addition, I have to put myself in the position of the big players and know how they think and act. Price Action Trading means to understand and apply market conditions.

Fundamental analysis is very important in equities trading, and the foreign exchange market is about balancing individual currency strengths. How do the different markets relate to each other and which market will make the day? But there are limits here. If there is a shutdown in America and there is no government in Germany, what is more affecting the price? The challenge is not to determine what affects the price more sustainably, but how the market reacts to it.
That's why I monitor these ratios, note also that there is an FED or ECB, but I am only marginally interested. So, if there is another session, I stay away from the market and read a good book at this time. Mostly nothing happens. The market is in high spirits and does not know where to go. An hour later, everything is clear again and it can go on. Yes, and if I missed a chance then it is not bad either. If I were to trade this kind of breakouts, I would have more loss than profit. Since I like the probability on my side. In addition, I am never so long-term oriented that fundamental analysis would be the right path for me.

So all that remains is the technical analysis. The technical analysis or chart analysis includes all assessments as well as trading decisions, which are made primarily on the basis of the price development.
The market technology has not brought me further, not because it is bad, but because it is unsuitable for me. I am very critical of the DOW theory, especially as it does not help me in smaller timeframes and the market has changed fundamentally today.
In candlelight analysis, one has to admit that, due to the formation of candles over time, different formations arise, which can be interpreted differently. That's too inaccurate for me.
So only the pure price chart remains. This is also inaccurate, due to the different brokers. It would change if you were shot straight to the stock market.
But the trick is to see more with one eye than others with two eyes.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

The key "Equilibrium"

1. The price is determined by supply and demand in each market.
2. Any influence on the price will be returned from the price
3. Before the price moves up or down, a balance between supply and demand creates a balance.
4. If this balance is disturbed, the price moves in the direction of supply or in the direction of demand.
5. The price moves as long as supply or demand until there is a balance again. Then the whole thing starts from the beginning.

Most candles are where there is a balance. We do not want to trade there, because the price is not moving very much. So we have to act when there is no balance.

There are 3 different states in the market.

1. Offer outweighs the demand = price drops
2. Demand outweighs the offer = price rises
3. Supply and demand are balanced
According to the sellers the offer (short) there, while the buyers represent the demand (long).

These competing factors (supply and demand) meet each other in all markets and regulate the price.
In the stock market environment, the price strives to find a so-called equilibrium. At that moment, buyers and sellers are equally satisfied until an imbalance rebalances in favor of supply or demand. Then the prices rise or fall again.
But even if you can accurately identify supply and demand, you will not get on with it. Decisive are the zones where the supply outweighs the demand or the demand the supply.
Known as resistance or support.
These reversal points, which often have an increased volume, must be recognized.
There are many ways to work with resistance and support lines, I myself work with horizontal lines, because I have the best experience.

If you apply these insights, you will soon realize that your trade will improve. It may take a little while until success starts, but in the end they will agree with me.
I wish you that you do not take as long as I do and would be glad if you can do some things of it.

Best regards

Hello Parisboy,

Nice story, so I recommend never to actions to increase a vehicle, as many pay more than the vehicle is worth.

Reminds me a bit of building society savings.

In 1775, building society savings were invented in England. A house cost 10,000 pounds and was a lot of money. 10 people found themselves each had 1,000 pounds and had to save 10 years to move into his own house. The 10 people had an idea. They each throw the 1,000 pounds in a pot from who may buy a house first. Everyone committed to pay the 1,000 pounds a year into the pot until the last of them moved into a house.

Normally, every 10 years should have been until the purchase and collection. Through this idea, 9 people could buy a house earlier and even the last of them had no disadvantage, as he would have bought a house only in 10 years.

Today everything is much more complicated.

How are you able to work with 4-5 pip SL in this respect? Do you have a recommendation about the SL for limit order?[/quote]

Hello Maddin,

this depends on the situation in which the market is located. If I have a strong resistance, I like to go in with a limitorder, as the price often comes off quickly after touching the resistance and I get in at a better price than with the manual order. If I am not so sure I go to the market manually.

If you have identified a POC, look at this POC in smaller timeframes. This allows you to limit the range and thus reduce the stop considerably. From time to time I also go in with a stop of 2-3 pip, so I can of course trade with a higher contract number.

This works best with trend reversals in the respective timeframes. In the middle of the price, such a small stop is just loss.

Particularly problematic to act are the extreme outbreaks. Often you can foresee that, if you pay attention to the big players in the market. Often this happens around 14:30.

Since the market usually only initiates a countermovement before it completes the actual outbreak, it is difficult to get the right entry there.

The big player pushes the price up to its limit order and then it goes off. This will stop all competitors from the market, so that the course runs as long as possible in the desired direction of the big player. It is also clear, if you take up a lot of smaller ones as a big player, they will start selling at some point. This obstructs the further price course upward.

For some years I used to go there with a buy or sell order in, but when the price goes down, you come in way too late, and when the price drops, you're stopped.

Today I prefer to go in manually, a limitorder is there too inaccurate, because here the POC can not be determined exactly.

Basically, you have to worry about what the limit is that you are willing to risk. After that, your number of contracts and your stop will depend.

The POC gives me a small advantage in anticipating what happens. However, the course comes at some point to the next POC line. There he can go through or come back directly. That's why I'm in the market for as long as I think I can assess the risk. Since I can only give the correct forecasts for a short period of time, a long stay in the market is not my thing.

But as I said, every trader has his opinion and is therefore right. Because everyone has to assess their own risk and then implement it.

For this implementation, I recommend a demo account until you have enough experience in this particular case.

Morning setup before trading

Dear Trader

Every morning at 05:30 CET I prepare myself for the trading day. Briefly skim the news and briefly check which meetings or news can affect my preferred currency pair during the day. This information can be found very well at Forex Factory.

It does not interest me in which direction the currency pair could develop, but only if there will be possible confounding factors. As already written, the news is not decisive, but how the trade reacts to it. And nobody can predict that.

That's why I'm not interested in predictions but only in probabilities. And if I manage to turn those probabilities in my favor by having an information advantage over many others, it often takes minutes to profit from it. This works best with the POC (balance)

First, I notice in the morning how the Asian market ruled London and the US.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

I once tried to highlight my favorite times in EURUSD.

From 06:00 to 08:00 CET, there is little momentum, but that is always very interesting to trade, as there are often clear trends during this time. At around 08:00 CET the volatility rises, after which there is often a minor correction.

I'm waiting a bit between 08:00 and 09:00 CET, with the London open, there is often a clear trend direction.

It's often quieter between 11:30 and 13:30 CET. Time to relax.

From 14.00 CET it continues until sometimes 20:00 CET.

For me a high momentum is interesting, I need clear statements from the market. As soon as an extremely high volatility prevails, I wait until the traders have calmed down again. With a little stop, you're at the wrong address.

Also, a ranking market can act in the short term with the POC super. Often it even works a few times, until the outbreak comes.

Outbreaks I rarely do. If I have identified a possible resistance zone and believe that the course goes through, I have to go in before. If it is a Fakeausbruch, I have earned nothing but nothing lost. When the course goes through, I did everything right.

During trading, only some of my POCs are crucial, yet I occasionally pay attention to my own dashboard about the short-term market condition. But with many indicators lagging behind, the price chart is the fastest way to get up-to-date information.

I hope there was some information that you can do, wish you much success and more trading profits than trading expenses.

Trades without any Candle

Many years ago I once dared to do a very interesting experiment.

Every time I went in the market, the course immediately went in the opposite direction and I was stopped out.
I looked at my quotas and found that I had correctly foreseen the course in 30%. In 70% of the cases, I was wrong. That could not be right.
I turned the tables. If you're 70% wrong, I thought, you just have to change your system. If you act the opposite of where you think it should go, it should work.

So I acted up, if I thought the price would fall and go down when I thought the price was going up. In fact, my profit ratio changed. However, I was now 60% correct. Well, that was an increase of 100%.

Then I came up with the crazy idea to act without a chart image, but only through indicators.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

I loaded the currency strength of two currencies as an indicator on the screen as well as the CFP indicator. I marked myself with green and red lines when the price had risen and fallen. Then I switched off the chart image and tried it.

Curiously, this worked, not always, but better than when I saw the chart.

That was because the indicator left me with little information where to go. Of course I have traded mini-contracts in extreme cases not so much to lose.
These days I do not act that way and I do not want to recommend it to anyone. But it has shown me that we have to process far too much information as a trader.

Less is more and from that day on, I've cleared most of the indicators off my screen and focused on the essentials.
That was the breakthrough for profitable trading for me.

A little tip on the edge: I have every 3 months my screens photographed and collected the pictures. So I could gradually see my development and my progress.

With the smaller timeframe to the POC

Dear Traders,

Let's look at the example. In the EURUSD uptrend we see two equilibria that are easy to draw. After the course went up, he came back, but not to our drawn POC. This POC was still active as a resistance and was touched later.

If the falling price on our blue arrow has been rejected, the question mark in the chart must have a POC. You can not see them at first glance though.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

When we switch to the 30M chart we already see a little balance. However, our resistance line that we draw is still too big. Since the stop would have to be drawn too far back if we want to go in with a buy limit order.

So we switch to the 15 M chart.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

We can now reduce our resistance and thus shorten our stop.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Back in the 1H chart, you can see how the course has responded to the POC. We were able to reduce the stop from 17 pip to 4 pip and have achieved a high chance risk ratio. 4 pip risk and possible 120 pip gain are a rare opportunity. For a beginner, it would have been safer to wait for the price to return to the top and then trade down to a sell limit.

That's why it pays off to search POC.

You can never see the market ahead, but you can still try.

Hello Techanalyst,

I am very glad that you have accepted the challenge and by the approach you are on the right path. You have correctly identified some Equilibrium.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

With 3-4 equilibria found I could agree, although you make it very difficult. Color your main candles dark gray and use the Momentum Candles indicator (setting for 15 minutes candle pipvalue 7-9 and hilow pipvalue 7-9 at your own discretion). Then you will see the equilibrium more clearly. The indicator can be found here in the blog.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Here you see the same time frame, with the POC I identified. Although these are some POC, this is also a range of 140 pip.

For me as Swingscalper, that's not too much POC, since I usually sell more trades and with the help of the POC love to act against the trend. That means I do not always take the whole upward movement with me, but also like to trade the corrections.

For example, if you are trading up as a day trader, these POCs are a good tool. Watch how the course behaves when it comes to this POC. That often gives you a hint. If you are experienced and have correctly drawn your POC, there are only 3 ways the course can behave there.

1. It forms a new equilibrium.

2. He walks through the POC

3. He turns off at the POC

If the POC is crucial, the course will be slowed down there. If you train this often and your POC are correct, you can do a precise and very profitable swing trading.

However, that is also a formality. There are days, I trade exactly with the zigzag up or down, and sometimes I manage nothing. Then I just stay out and wait for the next chance.

A big advantage of this POC is the range trading. The EURUSD often shows that the price is within a certain range. This is easy to recognize with the POC and can therefore lead to interesting profits on such days.

Of course you can not make an accurate prediction with the POC, but over time you get a good feel for the price. Whether the course is up or down, something happens at my marked POC.

It is often interesting to trade the counter-trend when the price has risen sharply. By your POC you can guess when the return comes, and you can quickly take 20 Pip. If you work here with a 4 pip stop the chance risk ratio is top.

I'm not a fan of working with 0.5 contracts and a 100 pip stop. With the help of my POC, I often feel like anticipating the market for a brief moment. The longer I am in the market, the less control I have.

The course rarely runs straight through, usually in a zig zag course up, down or to the side. If you take the price up, for example, you can do 100 pip, the zig zag price upwards is about 300 pip.

Of course you can never really hit the zig zag course, but I've often been lucky enough to have corrected in the uptrend and been in the middle of a strong downtrend.

The following situation that often happens at the moment:

The price is in a strong uptrend and is facing strong resistance. He bounces off it and tries it again a few times. I then try to move up from the underlying POC. If the price does not manage to break the strong resistance, I have no loss and can immediately go into the downtrend. If he breaks through the resistance, there are often large buy orders right there that push the price up quickly.

So that you sometimes see that I'm not perfect, I'll show you a POC that I did on Friday under stress because I had appointments. At the yellow circle around 09:00 am I have the POC quickly in the 15 M drawn without paying attention to the M5. Although I took the downtrend well, the POC could have been more accurate. Usually I do it in the morning in peace and with time. You see how important preparation is.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

So the POC are a kind of stopover on the way up or down. You can be very good at it, if you deal with it long enough. I also make enough mistakes in identifying the POC, so keep training, success will prove you right.

I wish you a lot of success.

Consumer protection in Europe is becoming ever more dramatic

As many European traders have already learned, ESMA is considering a series of proposals for retail investors designed to raise standards of behavior in the industry. This could affect European investors as follows.

Here are the leverage restrictions proposed by ESMA:

30: 1 leverage for major currency pair = 3.33% margin
20: 1 leverage for the major indexes = 5% margin
10: 1 leverage for commodities (gold not included) = 10% margin
5: 1 equity leverage = 20% margin

What impact do these suggestions have on traders?

These proposals would result in greatly increased margin requirements:

CFD

Market-------------- Size----------------Current Margin--------------- Proposed Margin (ESMA)
EUR / USD------- 1 contract----------------- $ 611----------------------------- $ 4,073
DAX ---------------1 contract--------------- € 1,650---------------------------- € 16,500
Oil -----------------1 contract--------------- $ 1,035----------------------------- $ 6,900
Apple----------- 1,000 shares------------- $ 8,950----------------------------- $ 35,800

For example, suppose you have $ 20,000 in your account and you open a DAX position with a required margin of $ 1,000 margin. If this position has a loss of € 500 (leaving € 500 as margin), the broker will be forced to close the position, regardless of the cash in the account and regardless of any winnings on other positions.

These proposals could result in traders being forced to act less or resort to the use of unregulated offshore brokers.

The proposed close-out rule appears counterproductive and prevents meaningful trading strategies. A meaningful protection for the investor is not recognizable. As it stands, CFD's are therefore only suitable for extremely short-term trading, as larger market fluctuations could lead to an unwanted liquidation too quickly. One becomes too easily the victim of short-term market manipulation. It should be enough if a position is sufficiently secured by an available account. It seems nonsensical to liquidate a position if holding the position could be realized by simultaneous sale / purchase of CFD (which would then lead to the initial margin being created).

We will see where that leads, should these regulations really become reality, there are enough possibilities for a way out.
Until then we will continue as before.

best regards

Why it is sometimes advantageous to be just a small trader.

Hello dear traders,

When I started trading many years ago, I realized that in the Forex market, I'm just a small fish in the big shark tank and this situation will never change. So what does a little fish do in the shark tank? He uses the opportunities he has!

There are three types of fish in the shark tank. First, the sharks, which eat the small fish. Then the fish that are eaten and the cleaner fish. This fish species cleans the teeth of predators and they are not eaten.

When two rival sharks fight each other, the cleaner fish is ignored. He waits for the winner to clean his teeth afterwards.

In the Forex market the sharks are the big players, the fish that are eaten are the small or medium traders who do not know how the market works. The Cleaner fish are the kind of traders who know roughly how the sharks react in the big shark tank. And that is exactly the key.

If you know the basics of supply and demand, you have a distinct advantage over the big players. You do not notice so easily in the market.

While the big players leave their mark on the market (through strong candles), you are so small that no one can identify your tracks. But you can not go on a track with the other traders, many small traders are in addition like a middle player and their tracks can easily be identified as a big player.

So we stay away from the tracks of most traders and we will not be discovered that easily. Of course there is an orderbook where all buy and sell orders are listed. The big players pay attention in the market to where most orders are. This approach sounds easier at first than it actually is.

The secret lies in the price chart. Delete unnecessary indicators from your chart and concentrate on the essentials. That's the price. Supply and demand regulate the price. So the key question is whether supply is stronger than demand or demand is stronger than supply. This can be well identified with the Equilibrium. Balance means uncertainty in the market. At this price level, supply was just as strong as demand. Curiously, these equilibrium zones (POC) point of control are often responsible for a strong trend change.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Let's take a look at EURUSD's 1H chart image. I have partially identified and drawn the POC lines from 2014. An exact explanation exists in the post 195.

I tried using the Momentum Candle Indicator to visualize the key momentum. You can see how the momentum behaves in or at the POC. Within 2 weeks, the momentum has responded 20 times and thus initiated a new trend, or confirmed the old trend.
Is that pure coincidence or just luck? Unfortunately I can not answer that. If coincidence or just luck, I have these factors in recent years, my income thanks.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

I have once drawn here 2 bullish and a bearish line. As you can see, certain price zones are used again and again to move the price into a trend. Is that also coincidence or luck?

Whatever it may be, what matters is what we conclude and implement from these findings. To avoid the suspicion, I would have picked out a special chart, I just took the latest chart (until Friday evening)

Take a currency pair and take a closer look at the chart image. Record your POC. You will be surprised what you discover. Put it to work for you and build a trading idea with you, which you strategically implement with the right money management.

It always looks so easy, but it means a lot of work and training.

Because being a cleaner fish from time to time, not being discovered so often and sometimes being pulled up or down by the big shark is worth the training.
It will not always work, I have often failed because my assessment was wrong. But I learned from it and developed further. It's not as easy as I thought in the beginning. Holding on is an important trait in trading, and good money management is crucial.

I wish you a very successful week

Greetings Michael

The tricks of high frequency traders

Hello dear traders,

As already described in some articles, today's big players are working with strategies that bring major disadvantages for us smaller traders.
This refers to the so-called high-frequency traders, which make up on some days up to 50% of the trading volume. They work with incredibly fast computers and programs. The speed of these programs is enormous, they can respond to price changes within milliseconds, allowing them to get into the market faster and out again.

We're talking about professional scalpers cutting out small pieces of the trading cake. You're investing millions in your hardware and software because it's about billions of profits. You place your computers as close as possible to the respective stock exchange, because every millisecond counts.
Traders who do not work with such a technique are clearly at a disadvantage.

You can clearly see the difference between Metatrader 4 and Metatrader 5. Compared to the high frequency traders, this is ridiculous, but still a big advantage for me. The speed order to place is much faster. Disadvantage: Long and short positions can not be held simultaneously in a single underlying. As a scalper, that does not matter to me. If your or execution is too slow, try Metatrader5, if your broker grants you that option. With the Metatrader 4, I would continue to work to use your proven indicators.

In addition to the tremendous speed, these high-frequency traders have a few tricks in store that are a little worrying on closer inspection.
They are able to change the picture of supply and demand in such a way that the investors are confused and thereby suffer considerable disadvantages with fast and mass orders.

Although these companies achieve only low profits, but the high number of orders come together in the month considerable sums together. The looser are the long-term investing funds and pension funds - and of course the classic retail investors.

Let's take a look at the tricks in detail.

Wash Trades: I have already described this approach in previous posts and is particularly controversial. The trader trades in here with himself. He hunts his buy order up to his sell limit or high, which then pushes the price down immediately. Or, in a rising market, a turnaround is suggested in order to buy cheaper again before the market turns sharply higher again. The goal is to squeeze traders out of the market or move them into transactions that they probably would not have done in other circumstances.

Quote Stuffing: Thousands of orders are abandoned and then immediately deleted. Thus, the high-frequency dealers generate a false picture of the existing relationship between supply and demand. The other traders can not analyze these orders in the short term and are confused. Since they do not know which orders are correct and which are only mock orders, this gives the high-frequency traders a time advantage, since they know their correct orders.
If several trading systems compete against each other, quota stuffing is often used as a very effective weapon.

Spoofing: The goal of outsmarting other program traders. The own system is tuned to analyze, anticipate and exploit the reactions as well as the functioning of other algorithms. The market participants should also be moved by the illusion of certain constellations to a desired reaction.

Sniping: With small, quickly issued orders, the market is searched for hidden orders. The goal of finding large buy and sell limits of other traders. Just before these thresholds, which promise the release large orders, then the own orders are placed. The limit order of the other participants will be triggered much later.

Scalping: Here is the decisive advantage, the speed of the systems. As soon as the system detects large order volumes, they are on the market at lightning speed. So they can still buy cheaper than the other dealers. Even before you can govern, the high-frequency traders are already out and the course immediately turns in the other direction. The slow traders are virtually eaten.

This approach can not foresee any indicator of the world. That's why I recommend looking for clues. By looking at the pure price charts, you get better with time. The POC are the tracks that leave everyone behind. We must learn to read and implement these traces. There are few ways to protect yourself from these tricks, Equilibrium is the most effective way for me to make a positive assessment at the end of the month.

I wish you a successful week

Meaningful chart images in FF post

Hello dear traders,

So that you are well prepared in the future and can post individual pictures here at Forex Factory, I would like to give you a few tips for fast image creation. I use Power Point for it, because for me it's one of the best programs for presentations. There are also free competing products, but you get Office for just $ 15 for a computer. Just have a look on the internet or on ebay.

If you do that with a high-quality graphics program, that's better of course.

If you have little experience so far, these tips might help.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

First, you need to take a picture of the picture you want to edit in Power Point on your computer. You do not need a cell phone, just take a screenshot on the computer. The keyboard shortcut for your computer can be found on the Internet

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Open Powerpoint and use Ctrl + V to paste screenprint into Power Point. I then set the slide size to (16: 9) widescreen because it is easier to read at Forex Factory.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Now you have to crop the image, there is an extra tool in Power Point. Be careful not to see your personal information, such as broker number or account information. I think this personal information is only yours.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

After dragging the image to the edges, you can now add all sorts of symbols, text or lines to your personal chart to your heart's content.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

When you're done, you still have to save your pictures. First, save a file as a PowerPoint presentation, then you can always change your pictures again.

To save the file as images go to "Save as" and save the file under PNG. Although there are synonymous jpg, but the file is synonymous of the resolution too low, since it is heavily compressed. The bmp file is very high on the resolution but also in storage. The best memory performance ratio for me has the PNG file, it is high in resolution and requires less memory than the. Bmp file. However, the opinions differ here, so try what you get along the best. Watch where you save the file so you can find it later.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

When will long-term demand dominate supply in EURUSD again?

Dear Traders,

How to identify key resistance and support zones from past courses is, in principle, quite simple. Two questions should be asked. When does demand dominate the supply = price rises and when does supply dominate demand = price falls. In between is the equilibrium or the POC.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

In the monthly chart from 1971 to 2017 you can see the dominance of supply and demand very nicely. On closer inspection, you will notice that this dominance often takes place at recurring price levels.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Between 1979 and 1990 there was a strong dominance of supply and demand twice. There I drew a brown line.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Also from 1996 to 2007, where demand dominated supply more strongly. (green line)

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

In the same period I have drawn a blue line, you can see very well in the weekly chart the POC.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

From 1998 to 2008 you can also see very well the Equilibrium with subsequent sale and then with a stronger price increase. The lines drawn in the past have already reacted to the price entry several times. There I have drawn a red line.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

The last line I derived from the years 2004 to 2014. Again, the already drawn lines respond well. I marked this spot with a purple line.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

The lines drawn so far set the framework for the last 4 years. It looks very nice, only when the price in December 2016 has entered the line, demand dominated the supply. That's why the course did not go well beyond the blue line.

Now the strong resistance of 1.25 has pushed the price down. We have marked the possible turning point with the red line. We now have to refine this line and look at the price within the yellow box.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

In the 15 minute chart you can see two decisive gap. I have marked this zone and refined it with the blue lines.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

This is the picture in the 4 H. Here you can see very well in the right circle which strong momentum prevails at this price level after a POC.
This zone is set for me. Since I expect a bullish annual candle this year, for me the price between 1.207 and 1.990 is the lowest point reached this year. I expect the price enter the zone in February or March, though that could happen later. When the price of this zone exceeds 1.25, the bulls will take the helm.

This is my own opinion and as you know, man is wrong every day. However, looking closer, there seems to be a lot on the POC. The most important thing is to see if supply or demand dominates. For this I have to work in smaller timeframes and watch how the course responds in or on my zone. This increases the probability of profit. And that is exactly what is important. The chance to improve in my favor.

I wish you a great successful Friday.

Dashboard to create

Hello dear traders,

I have already presented some interesting auxiliary indicators in the last contributions. Today it is about the compilation of individual screens and their indicators. From the basic indicators MACD, RSI, MA, Stochastic, Fractals, Zigzag and many more, I think nothing, because they are very trailing for me. Since the price chart is clearly in the advantage. I am well aware that the calculation of many of my auxiliary indicators is based on one of these indicators, so I do not make any purchase or sale decision.

Basically, I work on my main screens without the above mentioned indicators, but there are many creative programmers and traders at Forex Factory who have thought properly and developed great support indicators that make trading easier. I would like to present some of these indicators today, but I would like to do without a detailed description. First, because the developers can do that much better, and second, because I'm not a professional in this area.
In the many years of my full-time job as a trader, I have tried and analyzed a large number of different auxiliary indicators. As Swingscalper, I have been careful to use auxiliary indicators that give me a quick and rough overview. At some point I had the idea to use a separate screen for these auxiliary indicators.
I would like to present two overview screens today.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

This screen shows me the power of momentum once in the candles themselves and arranged next to each other. I have already explained the indicators in more detail in my Post 193. The time units for this screen are: 15sec, 1M, 5M, 15M, 30M, 1H, 4H and Day. By displaying the course line in each time unit, you can quickly identify the resistance and support zones.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

This screen is my own dashboard. This dashboard does not show me any entrances or exits, but I often get interesting information through this dashboard.
So that you can get an idea of how the Dashboard works, I have created a video for it.
We are in EURUSD on FR, 09.02.2018 in a larger timeframe in a sideways range. From 9:00 CET to 13:00 CET the course went down. Within this downturn there was a small pullback at 10:45 CET.

Experiment with doji

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Dear Traders,

As we already know, equilibrium is a crucial factor for future resistance and support zones.
I think little of candlestick formations because they are too inaccurate due to the time units. A small exception is the doji, although here too the time units are inaccurate.

A doji is a candle with the opening and closing prices at the same price level. The doji signals primarily indecision or a break in the price movement.
Exactly this uncertainty we want to take a closer look today and dare an experiment.

There are doji finders as indicators, but they were too inaccurate. For this I have found an indicator and adjusted so that he shows me the dojis in the market.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

We take a price chart between 1.21 and 1.26 and search from 2010 to 24.01.2018 for doji to look at the chart from 24.01.2018.
From 2010 to today, the course was four times in our price chart. With the help of our indicator, we are now looking for the doji in the 4H chart.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

From 22.01.2018 to 23.01.2018 we find two doji. Right in the middle of this doji we draw a gray line.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

It continues into the year 2014, where we again record all found doji.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Although we find some doji in 2012, we identified many in 2014. This means that there is always uncertainty at certain price levels.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

In 2010 we find a strong doji, so we draw this with a red line. Again, we do not find any other doji here.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Let's take a look at the result. Up to the red vertical line we drew the doji. Please note that we have not drawn any lines to the right of the red line.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

In the 30 M chart it looks much clearer now.

I think the result is very interesting.

You can also identify the doji in smaller time units, and if you use the POC in addition, you have a good chance to turn the probability in your favor.

I wish you a nice week

best regards
