--- 帖子 #475 ---
ESMA "What does the moon care if a dog barks at him"

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Hello dear traders, hello Klaus,

Now what is standard in the US for a long time is the traders in Europe: the 100% restriction of free choice. I had already published a detailed blog on 03.Feb: Post 218, so I will not go into the possible restrictions.

In the CFD market in Europe, there are approximately 1,500,000 accounts of 400,000 traders with a turnover of 24,000,000,000,000 € per year. In the foreign exchange market, the same amount will be converted worldwide in one week. Still, it's a lot of money for brokers offering CFD in Europe.

CFDs are a cash cow for brokers, so trading is pushed so hard. The biggest winner of the CFD is always the broker. Options and CFDs are quite different in one point.

CFDs have issuers.

Options have no issuer. As a result, options prices are not manipulated by issuers. CFDs have issuers and you trade them directly with the issuer. So the traders always act against the bank. This allows the courses of CFDs to be manipulated. This works indirectly, e.g. about unavailability of the CFD broker or extended spreads etc.

CFDs are traded through specialized CFD brokers. So you trade directly with or against the broker. Options are traded on transparent futures exchanges. Options are standard in the USA, CFDs are not allowed. US citizens, however, have the opportunity to trade futures and options directly through numerous US online brokers directly on the domestic and international futures markets. They can also trade equities, currencies and ETFS directly on margin long and short. They are thus directly trading the reference markets of the CFDs.

Although the obligation to make additional payments for CFD was banned in Germany, the risks for CFD are higher than for options or futures.

I welcome a regulated customer protection, but I find it questionable to limit the free decision of traders.

The leverage limit is particularly severe for smaller traders who have less money available. To trade 1 lot has been enough to give a margin of $ 250. In the future, the margin could rise to $ 3000. Then you can act the same as Future.

I find the new stop-out rules questionable. However, ESMA is seriously proposing that these margin close-out rules no longer be applied to the account balance, but to each individual position. The broker must close a position if the loss of the position is half of the margin. Each position would therefore have installed an automatic stop-loss in the future.

MetaQuotes, the provider of Metatrader 4 and Metatrader 5, has problems implementing these rules. That would be the end for many brokers and possibly also for traders working with the Metatrader. But I think that you can solve the problem in Metatrader with plugins.

Long-term hedging will no longer be possible, as will long-term oriented traders. For me as a scalper who has a maximum stop of 4-7 pip, that's less of a problem. And right now, the benefits of my trading strategy come from supply and demand. Without this strategy, I would not have been able to trade profitably in CFD.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Which solutions are there?

The brokers do not want to lose their cash cow and are already working on many solutions. They fear that many traders will move abroad. The brokers can give private traders the status of professional and thus circumvent the restrictions, or they can found a new company that is not bound by the restrictions of the ESMA. From there you can continue to act funny.

If you want to continue to trade CFD like in the past, you can also look for brokers on certain islands, but I advise against it. Australia is an interesting area where you should look for brokers.

If you forbid dealers in Germany to trade abroad, there are other options. My family is in Canada and Australia. I can certainly motivate my sister or brother to trade and support her a little from Germany.

So as long as there are regulations and restrictions in the world, there are people who are very creative. So no one has to worry that he will not be able to act tomorrow. It has always been like this: the creative people have always survived.

My proposition:

With a creative solution, you can continue trading for the next two years as before. But the clock is ticking. See that you build your fortune and then switch to the futures market. It is much cheaper and the price comes directly from the stock exchange. And you are no longer acting against your broker, but only against the market.

It is never eaten as hot as it is cooked. Therefore, there is no reason to worry. It's the same when the FED or the ECB is holding a meeting, the course starts to sway wildly and an hour later it's back where the whole theater started. The bottom line is, nothing happened. It will be the same here. Let's relax and concentrate on the next trading week.

But CFD will not be the future, that should be made clear. The creative minds will still have some time to raise capital and then make the right profits in a heavily regulated market. So deal with the futures in the future.

I hope I could bring some light into the dark room.

I kindly ask for your understanding because I am strongly involved in JAVA for the next 6 months.
Nevertheless, I will answer all questions as soon as possible.

I wish you a happy Easter and a good start into the new trading week.

best regards

Conscious incompetence

Conscious competence

Unconscious competence

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Record the resistance lines and observe the course of the course in all time units at the same time. If the price hits a resistance level defined by you in 4 time units at the same time, there is a high probability that your plan will work out.

This is unfortunately not a guarantee, but a significant improvement of possible probabilities in your favor. And that's where it matters to improve the odds in your favor.

ESMA: An immoral offer!

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Hello dear traders,

As already described last week in the Post 476 (ESMA "What does the moon care if a dog barks at him"), from the middle of the year the restrictions of ESMA are expected to take effect. The brokers are terrified of losing massive customers and are now trying to do everything possible to keep the customers. In doing so, all registers of creativity are drawn.

Here is a small excerpt from an offer from a broker. The name of the broker does not matter here, as it is a group of brokers who follow this path.

"European regulators have announced minimum margin installments for residential customers. Currently they are considered private investors. European regulators have announced restrictions on the sale of certain products to retail customers due to come into force in early July. That means minimal entry margin rates between 3% and 20% depending on the investment class at CFD. If you meet the regulatory criteria and choose to be treated as a professional client, these rules will not apply to you. However, they lose other legal protections. "
"Your Benefits as a Professional Customer Our margin rates will soon increase by up to 900% as a professional client would not be affected by margin rates. In addition, you would receive a 10% discount on their current margin rates. Some products and features will only be accessible to professional customers. As a professional customer, you must, among other things, forego the following FCA / BaFin protective measures. "
"Nachzuspflicht: as a professional customer, the negative balance protection is not for them. You are required to make additional payments if your account is in negative balance. "
"Restrictions on CFD and Binary Options: Regulators have imposed leverage and other measures to protect private customers. If you choose to be a professional customer, we are under no obligation to limit your account in this way, so these protections and any future measures will not apply to them. "

Conclusion:

Is not that great. The brokers can keep their cash cow and can even save the very expensive hedging of the additional repayment obligation. There are a few percent on the margin rate.

The question should be: Can any trader be upgraded to a professional trader? If this is possible, ESMA's duty of care has driven the private trader into long-term ruin rather than protected him. Congratulations.

That means you trade with an already expensive product CFD (compared to the futures) and lose the previously legal protection of the margin requirement.
Imagine you have $ 10,000 on the brokerage account. You place 1 contract buy order in the EURCHF with a stop of 20 pip. On January 15, 2015, the EURCHF fell from 1.20 to 0.97 within a few seconds. (2,200 pip). The stop was unable to grip.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

At the time, your account was down € 22,000.
With today's no repayment obligation laws, your account would be $ 0, but you would not be required to pay $ 12,000
If you now enter the broker's new offer, your account would be at $ 0 and you should pay € 12,000.
I would strongly advise against beginners of this offer.

Important:
That such an EURCHF situation repeats is quite unrealistic, but there is a likelihood. Of course, today you could use a guaranteed stop that prevents the worst. However, the terms are very bad for most traders.

If the spread was lowered by 50%, you could think twice. However, there are still brokers who offer a spread of 0.5 at no additional cost and have no repayment obligation. Such a broker is to be found in the future.

Which solution is there?

1. Continue to act on the requirements of ESMA
2. Change to the Futuremarkt
3. Seek brokers offering higher margin rates with no repayment obligation.

For beginners with little money, there is only solution 1 and 3.
For the advanced, there is really only the solution 2. The courses are better and the prices cheaper. The risk remains the same.
Until June there is still time to find a new broker, now comparisons have to be made to continue in the future.

best regards

How do I find the best broker for me?

Dear Traders,

When looking for the right broker, there are many hurdles to overcome. Not the cheapest broker is always the best. First of all, your investment behavior is a decisive criterion. As a scalper, spreads should be cheap and no further costs should be incurred. As a long-term trader, spreads can be less critical.
The right price performance ratio determines the right broker. Here is an example of what to look for in a CFD broker:

Accuracy of the courses
Analyzes aids
Arbitrage
Bankruptcy protection Internet comparison broker
Bonus
Capital gains tax
Customer Service
Demo account
Deposit guarantee
Deposit payment
ECN or STP
Execution time order placement
Fees Commission
Guaranteed stops,
Hedging
Lever
Margin
Margin Braids
Mini contracts
Minimum deposit
Minimum distance stop loss
Platforms
Real-time price
Regulation and location of the broker
Requotes
Rollover
Size of the broker
Slippage
Speed data transmission of the courses
Spreads
Stop and limitorder
Tradable products of your broker
Training

I once picked out the most important things for me.

For me natural conditions:

ECN/STP(DMA broker), deposit guarantee, no fees commission, good products: important to me dollar index, bankruptcy protection, capital gains tax is not withheld, good customer service, small margin, MT4 and MT5 platform, good realtime price, regulation of the broker, low requotes / Slippage, individual lever up to 400, low margin and the possibility of a guaranteed stop loss.

As a Scalper, I act almost only the majors and in more than 60% of the EURUSD, low spreads are required.
I've seen and tested a few brokers over the years, but there are so many brokers that no representative statement can be made here.
Unfortunately, there is no broker that meets all of my criteria so I opted for two brokers. IG Markets and Active Trades. Both combine my required criteria.

IG Markets is one of the oldest and largest brokers in existence. They offer a guaranteed stop loss, but it costs a lot of money, especially if you work as a scalper with only 4-7 pip stops. Then pay extra for a guaranteed stop is too expensive. The spread is quite expensive at 0.8 -1, but cheaper than many others. Unfortunately, the spread in volatile phases often rises to 1.5 in EURUSD, which is outrageous. Stop and Limitorder must be at least 5 Pip from the current course in the Metatrader, for me much too high. The accuracy of the courses is ok in volatile phases, the execution time is too slow. The stop loss must be at least 5 pip away, which is unacceptable. The speed data transmission of the courses is acceptable. The customer service is excellent. The lever goes up to a maximum of 200, no MT5, no dollar index. IG Markets has a very good internet platform and works very professionally. Basically for my needs a recommended broker.

Active Trades is a very interesting Swiss broker founded in 2001. The spread is very cheap at 0.5-0.7. In volatile phases it goes to 0.8 in the EURUSD, that's ok. Stop and Limitorder can be 0 Pip in the Metatrader from the current price, which is absolutely top. The accuracy of the courses is top in volatile phases, the execution time may suffer a bit. The stop loss can be 0 pip from the current price, which is exemplary. The speed data transmission of the courses is exceptionally good, often better than IG. The customer service, however, is not as good as IG. The lever goes up to a maximum of 400 and thus a 50% smaller margin than IG. No requotes guaranteed. With the MT5, the execution speed is once again significantly increased and in addition to the dollar index, there are other interesting courses. The internet platform is acceptable. Basically for my needs a recommended broker.

As a Scalper I have a broker for guaranteed stops and a broker for my daily business.

Important addition:

However, my opinion is not representative, as it applies only to me only in the CFD area. I am not married to these brokers and if I find a new broker that better meets my required criteria, I will not hesitate to use this broker for my business in the future. Especially with regard to the new ESMA regulations.

But I'll show you a solution with which you can find your personally best broker.

Basically you can compare most things on the internet, but you have to be careful. On the internet, there are always sites where brokers are allegedly compared independently. In 90% of the cases you can forget that. The websites are financially supported by many brokers. Forget about the comparisons, they are usually useless. In addition, there are often things that are uninteresting for a trader.

When winter tires are tested in Germany it is interesting for me how fast a winter tire slows down in ice and snow and how it reacts with aquaplaning. How fast it wears off or how high the noise level is, is not interesting for me. So I look for the best tires and then look for the best price performance ratio. These tires are my personal winner.

Create an Excel spreadsheet with the points that matter most to you. Then compare the brokers with each other. The best will win.
Unfortunately, one thing you can hardly compare: this is the speed of data transmission of the courses. Thus, the execution times of the order placements and the requotes / slippage are also related.

There is a simple trick for that.

Get one or two demo accounts from your chosen broker and create a new MT4 account. Then load my 7Zip packed indicators and the associated template into your old and your new demo accounts. Then you can compare the data flow, the spread and the prices.
That looks something like this:

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

The rows of numbers move very fast and you can easily see the data flow.

Inserted Video

On the top right you can see the S-KG Buyer Seller indicator. Developer: saronko high impact Member FF, Thanks to Kang Gun source code and FerruFx advice
The indicator, reacting quickly to price change. In addition, a current price indicator and the spread was incorporated. Since a lot of indicators are installed in the Metatrader, the S-KG Buyer Seller indicator moves a bit slower. You should therefore only install my three indicators for your test comparison.

Then look at how fast the numbers are moving and how the price behaves. This allows you to quickly compare the transmitted data flow of the brokers.
You will be amazed at the differences that can be identified and then finally make a good decision on your other criteria.

Please note that this comparison only applies to the CFD area and options or futures are excluded.

In my post 264 you can get more information about the other indicators.
https://www.forexfactory.com/showthr...0#post10767050

I wish you much success in the search and hope that these tips will help you a little bit.

--- 帖子 #501 ---
Science and practice

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Science means to explain what everybody knows so that no one understands it afterwards.

The truth is: science creates knowledge. It's good to know, but the more you know, the more you realize what you do not know yet.

This means that the more I know, the higher my doubts are whether what I know is right.

We all can be glad that science exists, because that benefits the whole world and our economic system. Without science, we would not be where we are today. But no one can say if science always helps us.

Each of us is a researcher and a small scientist, whether he is a doctor, professor, office clerk, worker or unemployed, our lives provide enough science to research.

By that I do not mean quantum physics, space research or medicine, but normal situations like parenting, relationship, communication, love, sex, sport, hobbies and many things of daily life.

Science is not the greatest error of life, but the conclusions we have drawn from it. So the problem is not science but man, because he is wrong.
Of course, a professor can prove his thesis to the student, but only because the student does not know better. But that does not necessarily mean that the professor must be right.

Man has been wrong ever since man exists, that's why science is wrong because it is man-operated.

The old thesis, "The earth is a disk," was also refuted, just as it was believed for 40 years that plants can not absorb solids or liquids through their stomata.

Science is based on possible theories that are either confirmed or refuted. If there were no theories, there would be no basis for discussion to refute them.

Every person who has completed an apprenticeship or a degree course knows it from personal experience. Theory and practice are often two different worlds.

Every person writes in his life a doctoral thesis or a professorship, not on paper but in his head, about things he has dealt with many years. This experience is very special, it is his own science, the experience of his own life.

It is good to know knowing how to correctly apply the fulfillment.

Science does not mean to hoard knowledge, but to pass on knowledge. It does not matter whether the knowledge is 100% correct, but whether one can help someone with it.

In principle, recognized science is nothing other than what most people have agreed on. Until one day you know better, then you have to agree again.

If we deal with the topic of brain research, and read the headline: "Love can be seen in the brain scan", you can only sit back and think: Yes you do. If I'm not sure in the future if I love my partner, I'll do a brain scan.

Science is special, but if it helps me to become really successful is a big challenge.

He was a mathematician and she was unpredictable.

Conclusion:

Science is not bad because there are wrong assumptions, but a good development process to get closer to the truth.

According to my theses, the some reasonable way of trading is to make more profit than loss if I properly implement the doctrine of supply and demand. Now there will be traders who say the opposite and think that equilibrium is just chance.

I find that exciting, because it causes the doubters to my theses to move to refute it. And that is exactly what will help us all, because movement brings us forward. As simple as that.

Science creates knowledge, we use the basics to build on it to advance our own knowledge in order to succeed.

And something else:

The term "self-confidence" puts it in a nutshell: I have to be aware that it is up to me. Only then am I in a position to change anything.

I wish you much success

Hello dear amenocy,

First of all, welcome to our blog and thank you very much for the very important question, which will certainly interest many traders who have dealt with the Equilibrium a bit.I would like to answer something in more detail.

For many years I have tried different types of Renko strategy and Heikin Ashi indicators and compared them with different bar charts. The result has unfortunately not brought me the hoped-for successes.

Let's take a closer look at the Renko chart. Basically, it should be noted that anyone who follows gullible technical indicators without understanding the trend dynamics is almost certainly doomed to failure in trading. This speaks against conventional indicators. The idea for Renko: It is about the visual representation of the true trend and to filter out fluctuations that could lead a trader in this trend following astray. Renko charts are not a basic recipe for success; you may be able to increase the chance of trading success with an additional strategy.

Due to their design, the Renko charts often do not match the original chart. Thus, different highs or lows can be achieved. However, sometimes trend patterns are more easily recognized. Determining the size of the renko, ie the minimum spread of the price movement, is a major challenge for which there is no standard rule. The choice of the minimum range depends on the volatility of the respective price.

This is where the first hurdle begins for me. I need an ATR. Since my optimal chart setting is now dependent on an indicator, another uncertainty has been added. Which ATR now reliably displays the values that I need exactly to represent my Renkochart optimally?

The normal chart (5M, 15M, 1H) may look a bit illogical for beginners, but it does show the unvarnished truth. For a normal chart I do not need an ATR because I see the volatility immediately. This makes my normal chart image independent of any other indicator.

Since the Renko is time-independent, it is difficult to detect strong price increases or price drops. Likewise, an Equilibrium is harder to identify.
These features make it difficult to identify a potential supply market or demand market.

The idea of working with Renko is initially tempting, I gave it up quickly because the pure price chart reflects the optimal translation of the market.
The price history is just up or down and a bit of a mess in the beginning. Just like a new language. But the longer you deal with it, the clearer it gets. So it's just a matter of time.

The situation is similar with Heikin Ashi. At first glance, it looks like a help, but you can derive few decisive equilibrium from it. Likewise, I can only advise against using one or more MA's from my own experience. The price does not matter if two MAs cross each other or not. In the future, therefore, he will not do what the cruising MAs predict. Indicators always follow the price. Therefore, one should pay the greatest attention to the pure price trend.

That's my personal opinion though. The fact that I have been able to live well from my Equlibrium strategy for many years should not be the decisive criterion for dealing more with supply and demand in the future. However, it should be a suggestion that this strategy could succeed if one can identify with this type of action. You can never tell a trader how to do business, he is always responsible. Here at FF there are many very good traders from whom you can learn a lot. But there are also many who have no success and confuse other traders by their recommendations or give you information that may bring very high losses. My tip: A good gut feeling is crucial which information is good and which information is bad. I wish you that you will always be able to make your best decisions from the many different pieces of information.

Best regards

What information is important?

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Hello dear traders,

FF has some 1,000 different trading themes. There are over 65,000 threads with 6,900,000 answers in 9 forums. Assuming that each answer contains only 100 words, that would total 6,900,000,000 words.

One reader manages about 200 words per minute.
To completely read through FF you would need almost 7 years without a break. (69,000 books)

Of nearly 500,000 members, approximately 50,000 members have published threads.
If I know what I'm looking for, I can get possible answers through my search.
So to improve your knowledge, finding keywords is the optimal alternative.

But what if I do not know what I'm looking for?
If I'm looking for new interesting knowledge how do I go about it?
In principle, I have only two options: searching for posts or searching through the members.

65,000 contributions face 50,000 members.
So I concentrate clearly on the members.

Members who publish regular contributions and communicate with other members are so-called impact members. They are marked with a rhombus.

Red = High Impact Member = Top 2% about 620 members

Orange = Medium Impact Member = Top 5% about 930 members

Yellow = Low Impact Member = Top 10% Top about 1,550 members

With that I can reduce my choice to 3,000 members. This does not mean that the other members do not post well, it just means that they do not regularly post information. Let's just stay with these 3,000 members for the sake of simplicity. There is interesting information about these members that makes it easy for a new reader to find the best.

For this we scroll down the main page of FF and click on Members. Then let's take a look at the member list.
There we get the following information:

Joined: month year
Buddies: number
Subscribers: number
Post: number
Last Online: Date
Trading from: Country

Now let's take 3 members who have different values. (we do not consider the country)

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

At first glance it looks like Trader A has the most experience as he has posted the most threads, most subscribers follow him and he is the longest in the process. After that Trader B comes and at the end Trader C.

Now let's have a closer look at the activity of the individual traders.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

We realize that the picture is completely changed now. Trader C has 6.97 subscribers per month while Trader A only has 4.68 subscribers per month. Trader A has sold almost twice as many posts as Trader A. (buddies and subscribers were added together)

Subscribers per month are a representative feature because people often only follow interesting topics that help them.
This proves that even new members post interesting topics that are often accepted by other traders.

A picture is worth a thousand words. Make sure that a post with examples and pictures conveys more information than just plain text.
Notice how the writer of a thread deals with its subscribers, how it criticizes, whether it makes fun of others and how it helps people.

An interesting feature is also the Ignored list. Sure, there are sometimes people who are annoying and you just have to lock. But if someone has 50 subscribers and has 25 on the ignored list, it might not just be the other one. This often has something to do with respect and interaction.

There are always exceptions, but the subscribers already have a reason why they follow certain people or not.
These factors do not guarantee that a trader will succeed or post topics that really help. But there are little hints if it pays to look closer.

With this little help, I can ever separate the wheat from the chaff and quickly recognize whether a second look worthwhile.
Take a distance from things that do not help you, meaningless discussions about topics that no one needs, you can find everywhere. Get involved and look for the topics and traders that communicate their strategy in an understandable way.

Unfortunately, it is often about vanities. But I think that most of us are able to distinguish between good and less good.

I think if you post here at FF already posts, you should either do it with passion or let it be better. The profession of the trader is simply too demanding for that. Every day we compete against the best traders in the world, and you need special qualities that are not taught at any university. Being a trader is something very special. You can be proud of that.

Best regards

The goal in trading is to optimize the probability of the trader in his favor. In the many years of my work, I have tried and analyzed hundreds of systems. I did not get any further. So I compared these systems one day. I found the equilibrium with supply and demand as my optimal way to success.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Hello newhope, hello dear trader,

First of all, thank you for your kind compliment and that you participate in this forum. Your questions are very interesting, which I would like to answer in detail.
The mathematical probability that the price goes to 1.28 /1.19 is 100%. However, this is clear, since we are in the middle of these two prices and a price can be achieved in any case in the foreseeable future. Now, predicting a price, the probability is 50%. This brings us to a problem why 95% of all traders lose money. No one, no computer can make a true statement about a price history. Everything is just pure speculation, but not less. Unfortunately, it is not possible for me to predict the next candle. If there are traders who can do it permanently, I would say my absolute respect.

My assumptions are based solely on supply, demand and equilibrium. These laws of the market apply in all forms of economy and that will never change. With this variant of the market observation, I manage to turn the probability in my favor. Another aspect must not be forgotten. The longer you are with a position in the market, the higher the likelihood that you will lose money. As a scalper, I reduce this probability, because sometimes I'm only a short time in the market. But here, too, the opinions of the traders diverge, which in my opinion is an individual question of faith.

I'll give you an example. The course comes from above and you believe that it is turning upwards at a certain resistance level.
The course brakes exactly on your resistance line and turns into an equilibrium. Now you wait for the optimal entry. Suddenly, the price goes up sharply. This is exactly where many traders are now entering. The big players know that and push traders off their positions with a sharp decline. The traders who have been stopped out now would never dare to press the BUY button in this situation as it now looks like the price is going down.

"A secret of success is to always trade the opposite of what you see. "

But we humans have a problem with that. Try it yourself. You think it goes down and you are trading down. What is happening? The price is rising extremely. You exit immediately and trade high. What is happening? The price drops sharply. You do that a couple of times, then you're served. You have to think anticyclically. So do the opposite of what you see.

You can even try it yourself. Take the Dollar Index and look at it, while depositing your trades in EURUSD. If you act now what you see, you will probably be more successful. But I can not recommend this strategy to you in the long term. In the last 10 years, I have clearly oriented myself to supply and demand and for me this way is the only right one. That does not mean that it has to be the right path for all other traders.

We come to another problem. These are the systems we use to succeed in the forex market. Here's an example: Investor A wants to invest in the best fund. As soon as there is a better fund, he takes out his money and puts it in the better funds. Investor B has his money in a mid-field fund. He leaves his money in it. After 10 years, Investor B has more money in his mediocre fund than Investor A who has always invested in the best funds. Why is that? Because a fund costs high fees.
That's how many traders are doing. You see an interesting blog and get a great indicator there. That motivates and gives the chance to finally make the breakthrough. Now a lot of time and money is invested in the new strategy, until the realization comes that it does not work that way. You are looking for a new system and the whole game starts from scratch.

Now comes a sobering sentence. It takes some 1000 hours of experience to be successful with a system. That is, most people give up too early instead of asking questions and moving on. The moment you look for other systems, you've already lost. That means you do not believe in your own system. I also did that earlier, from one indicator to the next. I just checked, there are 5,660 indicators on my computer. Certainly there are also some double, I'm crazy when I think about how much time it cost.

But it also got the experience that I can not get on with indicators. That's why I've been trading for supply and demand for 10 years. I also only speak of supply and demand and do not look for other systems. Not because they might be worse or better, but because I would need some 1000 hours to be successful. Since I live from trading, I have decided to continue to do so. The greatest likelihood of continuing to do so successfully as before is supply and demand for me as it has worked very well for the past 10 years. However, this is no guarantee that it will continue to work so well.

That's the bitter aftertaste when trading. If 10 times the red number came at the roulette, although the probability that a black number could come, but it can still come 10 times the red number.

Conclusion: Do not handle what you see when entering and act your system long enough to be successful.

You are on the right path if you trust yourself and no longer the indicators. If your feeling gives you more loss than profit, just turn the tables. That is very difficult.
Read the blog of supply and demand a few times and act accordingly. Maybe that's your way to success. I keep my fingers crossed and hope that you will be successful. I wish that to you and everyone else from the heart.

best regards

"A secret of success is to always trade the opposite of what you see. " why? Because...Price has to come down in order to go up Price has to come up in order to go down Someone has to Buy in order for you to Sell Someone has to Sell in order for you to Buy Market is filed with binary decisions... up and down, buy and sell, red and green, profit and loss, support and resistance, support and demand, tops and bottoms, breakouts and bounces, divergence and reversion, explosion and consolidation, acceleration and decelleration, accummulation and de-accumulation, adding in, scaling out, at pivot or not at pivot, at reference or not at reference, positive and negative sentiment, news release at met or not met, talking heads on TV saying buy buy buy and next day saying sell sell sell, previous candle up or down, ema cross up or down, macd showing red or green, overbought and oversold and the list goes on and on. "May the Odds be in your favor" is the biggest lie because your odds for trade to survive has changed the moment you enter a trade. All the analysis in the world that you have done before you enter is OBSOLETE the moment you enter a trade. Expecting a trade to hold on for a bigger RR under the same market conditions is a fallacy! Expecting the same trade setup to continue thru your exit setup is a fallacy.

There is NO Edge (i.e. secret formula or indicator) in the market place as every action we take ends up with a 50/50 probability before costs if you are not factoring what market HAS to do most of the time if not all the time. Taking actions that market is forced to do for it to exist is the ONLY logical way to beat the system.

Trade Small Trade, Often using the law of averages and law of large numbers to your advantage is the only quantifiable edge I could find in the markets within the context of what market HAS to do to enable trade between market participants.

Sorry for the bold and underline. I like to tell people with passion and intention leaving no room for deliberation so they may either take it or leave it. It's a binary decision (again). Everything in life has to be a IF or Else. the moment you introduce a MAYBE, you are f*ck*d 10 ways to Sunday. This has been my philosophy in life so let's stop with all the analysis and "Always Go LONG On Every Down Engulf Candle" or "Always Go SHORT On Every UP Engulf Candle". Obviously there is no edge in doing this or everyone will make trillions but there is an edge if you use this as a starting point for your entries only.

Patience in trade is tamed passion

Every trader knows the situation, one has been sitting in front of his screens for hours now and can not find a way to get started. The course may be in a state of equilibrium and does not really want to go up or down.

Time is money, we have been taught again and again. So now I finally have to sell a damn trade, because after all, I also want to make a profit.

Two hours later, the situation has not changed much. Now the course has to break out in one direction and if that happens I want to be part of it and not have to go down. Suddenly the course breaks short upwards. That's where our trader gets in and looks forward to having done everything right this time. The joy is short-lived, because the course stops suddenly and then breaks down sharply. The trader's stop is triggered and with a $ 100 loss he has to watch the price go down 50 pip. Since there is no Puuback, he has no chance to find another good entry. After 50 pips, another equilibrium forms and volatility drops sharply because individual markets close.

Balance: 8 hours serviced and $ 100 lost. Not a good hourly wage.

What did our trader do wrong? He had been waiting patiently and finally had the courage to sell a trade.

I like to compare a trader with the hunters from the Stone Age. This hunter lay in wait now waiting for the wild, animal. Often there was no wild, animal, then he returned home without meat. Sometimes he was lucky and could kill a wild, animal. From time to time a Mamut came the way, but the danger was great to kill himself.

If you are a Scalper, you will spend most of your time waiting, 90% of the time waiting and 10% of the time acting. For that, one particular trait is very important: patience. If, after waiting 8 hours, you feel the pressure to finally have to make a trade, you are not patient. You do not need to trade every day, but only when it's worth it. You can tell that with the Euilibrium very well.

Remember the following sentence: Even a slowman comes to the finish.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Take the EURUSD here an example of the last 8 weeks. High and low averaged 75pp per day. On average we can assume that we have 3 average days per week with 75 pip, 1 day with over 100 pip and a day with 50 pip movement. If we take as an example, the two most extreme days out, worthwhile 3 days on which you can achieve good profits.

For that you need patience and empathy. Watch the market as it has in recent days in different regions (London, USA, Asia) behaved. This often gives hints to the following day. I have fixed trading hours London Open + 4 hours as well as USA Open + 4 hours. When I realize that after the London open not much happens, I'm just free and waiting for the US Open. If nothing happens, I'll quit. That you can see well at the ATR or the volatility.

Of course, there may be strong movements in the short term, but this is less important for me.

With Equilibrium, I draw a resistance line as the course goes down. Only when the course comes close to my line I'm lying in wait. That means the Equilibrium shows me when it is worth trading. That's when I decide when to trade. You will find some examples in the block here.

Take action when it pays and you need patience. Sometimes it takes a while, but the result is worth it.

The word patience is a treasure in trading.

Good luck and best regards

Speed up Metatrader application

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Hello dear traders,

The decisive factor in trading are the access times to the servers of the respective brokers. This depends on the one hand on the servers of the brokers and on the other hand on your workplace. If the access times of the broker are too slow, you can easily change the broker. Before taking this step, you should check your own performance on your computer and make any necessary corrections.

On my side I can optimize three things:

1.Internet
2.Computer
3.Metatrader 4

Let's take a closer look:

Internet

Basically, I recommend a download of at least 50 Mbit and an upload of at least 20 Mbit. There are several options: cable, satellite or LTE, depending on where you live. This makes it possible to produce a faster Internet connection in the countryside. If you get your Internet via LTE, you should align your outdoor antenna with a special antenna program. The Internet access from the router to the computer I recommend basically a LAN cable, because the download rates are much higher and you have a better stability. If you only have a LAN cable from the router is available, but would like to connect multiple computers to the Internet you can also fall back on a splitter. The distributes the performance like a router on several computers.

Computer

In my detailed post 349

https://www.forexfactory.com/showthr...6#post10803976

I have already described what hardware is needed and how to increase the speed of the computer optimally.

Metatrader 4

At some point I noticed that my Metatrader 4 slowed down over time, and after a while I had to reinstall this MetaTrader. This is very annoying at some point and not efficient. On the internet I discover an interesting video that helped me:

How to speed up MT4

Inserted Video

The performance was much better, but I noticed that my CPU was busy. The CPU temperature rose to 75 degrees in peak hours and the computer's fan was running permanently.
That seemed strange to me because I only work with a few auxiliary indicators on my main screens.

So we come to a little tip if you work with indicators. Some indicators consume an awful lot of CPU. Open the Task Manager. Under Processes you can now see the CPU size of your MetaTrader. If you clear an indicator and the CPU value goes down significantly, you have discovered the performance culprit. Find a new indicator or optimize it.

Another tip for metatrader optimization.

I work with 2 computers, each serving 4 screens. To save the performance I work with external graphics cards.
What surprised me was that my Metatrader 4 needed a lot of CPU. I once tried an unusual way. My computer has 4 CPU cores. I took a closer look at these kernels in the Task Manager and found that the distribution of Windows is not optimal.
So I assigned 1 CPU cores to each Metatrader. The result was clear and startling.

1.The performance is much better
2.The CPU temperature has dropped by 30%
3.The fans run much slower
4.The Metatrader reacts much faster.

Since I do not know with which operating system and computer you work, unfortunately I can not show you exact instructions here. On Youtube or on the Internet you will find enough examples how to assign your own CPU to a program.

Unfortunately, after closing Metatrader, Windows does not save the CPU core settings.
But there is a solution:
With the freeware Easytoolz programs can be assigned to individual processor cores. Especially useful: The software integrates itself into the Windows startup folder. The set profiles can be saved so that they are active again after a restart.

According to the computer professionals, this should not be done because Windows distributes the 4 CPU cores individually to the programs. Only with Metatrader Windows does not seem to do it right. I can not tell you why this worked for me. The fact is that things are going better than before.
If you do, please do it yourself and if you know it.

I can finally recommend a permanent temperature monitoring of CPU, GPU and motherboard. The programs can be found on the net.
You may also read my post 349.

I hope I have been able to give you some tips that will make your life easier and give you more security and performance.

Have a nice day
Best regards

Hello Klaus,

At the weekend, the S / R lines are usually a little harder to draw than during the week, as we have a break on Friday evening. So there are 48 hours without trade in between. In this trade-free time, many big players pay more attention to world news. In these 48 hours accumulate a lot of messages. However, since there is no market and therefore no price position, it can not be determined how a message may affect a price. At the beginning of the week, there is often a wait and see attitude to see how the market reacts to the past weekend.

Nevertheless, one can anticipate the zones based on demand and supply. A little tip:

On Monday, I will take a closer look at the Asian market in the 5 M chart and determine the short-term price. Particularly interesting are the large price swings, it is easiest to derive the S / R zones.

Hello dear traders,

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

The purple lines were set by me for the coming week.

Three more red lines were added by me on Monday, Tuesday and Thursday.
I wrote on Sunday that creating a forecast on the weekend is very difficult and I like to wait for Monday. I want to show you why.

The top purple line was my resistance line which had strongly rejected the course on Friday for the second time. So I realized that this resistance is no longer fresh and the price is unlikely to reach this zone. On Monday, the price rose sharply for a short time and was then strongly rejected. There I drew my first red zone. (Equilibrium).

My 2nd purple line was broken down. After that, the course moved near my third purple line and from that very line it went down sharply. On Tuesday, I recorded the second red line, which resulted from the current price.

At the bottom thick purple line, I realized that there is a large demand market here. When the course reached the zone for the first time, it was turned up. Not so strong though. The course had to go down a bit further. Somewhat outside my lower line, demand was so strong that it made it to my red line on Tuesday.

He was pushed down again, had satisfied all sellers and could then continue his way up.

The course made it almost to my 2nd Purple Line (from the top) and was strongly rejected as expected. There was a strong supply market there. The was as you can see on Monday triggered. Then I drew the third red line on Thursday.

In principle, we had a big equilibrium here until the price finally came back to my red line from Tuesday. There was a big demand market there that drove the course up to my Monday line. There was again a strong supply market, which has strongly rejected the course.

You realize how important in the case was the Monday, there I have drawn the red line and could assume that there is a change of course here.

With these guides, some nice trades were possible this week. As you can see, the guidelines in the 4 H chart are only approximate.

I prefer to draw the long-term lines in the 1 H chart and then go into the 15 M chart. There I then draw in my guides. In the 15 M chart you can make more precise statements about a short-term trend change.

Procedure with supply and demand

Hello okshop, hello dear traders,

that you work on the principle of supply and demand is definitely a very good approach. However, I would advise against working in a 1H chart with a 5 pip stop because the overview is too inaccurate and volatility could quickly ruin your billing.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

I myself work with an overview that shows me 9 different time units. (20 sec, 1M, 5M, 15M, 30M, 1H, 4H, D and WK.
There I use two auxiliary indicators to show me the strong momentum and the trend strength.

In these time units I draw in my lines and balance these lines with the smaller time units. The matches signal me a higher hit chance. My trades are in the 5M or 15M chart. In the 5 minute chart, a small stop is easier to realize.

For entering a trade, I use a specially created dashboard next to my lines.
In Post 264 of February 11th I described this dashboard with indicators exactly.

https://www.forexfactory.com/showthr...0#post10767050

My Dashboard is regularly revised and equipped with new projects, so it differs from the post. Nevertheless, the main auxiliary indicators are available in the Post 264.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

I would like to briefly describe the essential overviews

Point 1
Here the currency strength in the 1 H chart for the euro (green) and the dollar (red) is shown. This makes it easier to derive the medium-term trend. It is very clear when the strength of the dollar or the euro increases or decreases.

Point 2
The currency strength of the dollar (above) and the euro (below) individually tailored to all important currency opponents. Likewise, an early warning system when changing the trend.

Point 3
The strength of the dollar (red) and the euro (green) in the 5 minute chart. The blue line represents the sum of dollars and euros. Important to quickly identify an Equilibrium. In combination with point 1 a very reliable early warning system.

Point 4
The candle strength in the different time units, including the candle formation as you can see in the chart image.

Point 5
Dollar Index (blue) and EURUSD (pink) brought to a common denominator in the 1M chart to see differences faster.

The basic focus is on my drawn lines which I have coordinated in different time units.

If I have made a line in the 15 M chart and 1 H chart, I switch to the 5 M chart where the line is drawn automatically.
If I can assume that a trend change could take place on this line, I now look at my dashboard. However, that depends on the situation. As a rule, I usually know in advance that a change in trend is announced. Then the dashboard is less interesting for me.

Basically you can say that you can never rely on indicators, but over time you get a feeling for each situation. I draw a lot of lines into my charts during the day, but sometimes I do not enter a trade right there because the situation is not clear enough for me. As a rule, I press on BUY still in the falling market or on sell still in the rising price, if the price comes to a decisive line.

This approach has proven itself, as I am in case of success relatively quickly in profit. After that, feeling is required to stay in the trade or to quit early.
The dashboard has sometimes served me very well. But I do not rely on indicators. They are sometimes a nice confirmation, as they are unfortunately trailing.

An exact statement gives you the current price chart.

But due to the formation of candles, the price chart is often difficult to interpret.
The decisive answer to my questions as to where the trend is lies in the supply and demand of the past prices.

But this is like driving a car, as a novice driver I have to look at the speedometer to know how fast you drive. A driving professional can do that without looking at the speedometer.

So it's like everything: a question of time.

Best regards

Hello dear traders,

Again and again one asks oneself the question, why the course goes up or down now and when there is finally a turnaround.

The answer to this is obtained from the market. Decisive are the supply zones and demand zones. So when does supply dominate demand and when does demand dominate supply?

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

For a better overview, I have shown a year chart from 1971 to today.

Let's start with point 1. There is a supply market in this zone, which means that there are fewer traders ready to buy in this area. From point 2 there was a strong demand in the market. There are more buyers than sellers in the market. Similarly, you can see from point 3 how the strength of the buyer increases. This fact prevented the EURUSD from falling below 1.03 and since then has risen sharply.

Point 4 signals a strong supply market, which was intercepted again from point 5 onwards. Now let's take a closer look at point 6. The EURUSD rose sharply to 1.255 and thereafter the price was turned down. You can see very nicely the parallel to point 1. There was also a strong supply market.

At point 7 there is again a strong demand market. The still red annual candle will develop like the candle over point 3 and shoot strongly upwards. Why? Because we have a strong demand in this zone.

Of course, these are pure hypotheses, because no one can predict the market. Certainly not in the long run. But the annual candles speak a clear language of supply and demand since they are more accurate than the monthly candles.

This means we have a strong demand market between 1.163 and 1.184, so the question is: how much does the price have to go down until the strength of the demand market is such that enough buyers get into the market? Why nothing happens?

Hello dear traders,

even if it does not look like it at first sight, the EURUSD is currently in an equilibrium. I once plotted the range with a blue field.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

This situation shows a clear uncertainty of traders. Equilibrium is always a clear statement, because if investors are uncertain, nothing happens. The challenge now is to determine the next direction, since after equilibrium often a sharp rise in price or price drop occurs. A price increases until it enters the offer zone. This means that the supply is greater than the demand. So there are no investors who are willing to buy at this price.

Depending on how strong this offer zone is, the price is strongly or weakly rejected. If the course is weakly rejected, equilibrium will be created. Under certain circumstances, the course must penetrate once again in the offer zone to then be rejected more. Then suddenly more sellers jump up and push the course down.

At some point, the course will be rejected again and there will be an Equilibrium.

The EURUSD has penetrated a demand zone, but this demand zone has not been so strong that it has been sharply turned upside. Now an equilibrium was created.

The price may need to penetrate more strongly into the demand zone to find enough buyers to push up the price. As already written yesterday, the situation before a turnaround is always a small challenge. As scalpers, these equilibriums are interesting for trading, but as day traders they are more of an ugly situation.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Whether the course turns at point 1 or point 2 is not quite clear with the Equilibrium. The stronger demand zone is at point 2, but I still believe that we have almost reached the reversal point.

The course has already run into the red zone, but demand has remained limited so far. Add to that the momentary uncertainty, but that will change quickly. How do I increase the probability of winning?

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Dear Traders,

If we compare trading with lottery games, there would only be 2 numbers in the lottery game. The number 0 and 1. The probability of winning would be 50%. The higher the probability to win, the lower the profit, because every lottery player would have the same chances. However, trading in the forex market looks a bit different. You press on BUY, the price initially moves up but suddenly the price breaks down and the stop prevents further losses.

Although the trader was right in the beginning, he now goes down with losses from the trade. The same rules of the game apply to all participants in the stock market, but there is a big difference if I'm on the market with $ 1,000 or $ 1,000,000 or $ 1,000,000,000.

In Germany, the most typed number in the lottery is the number 19. Why? Because people like to type their birth numbers and most players were born between 1940 and 1999. Likewise, many numbers between 1 and 31 are typed and fewer numbers from 32. The probability of winning does not affect this, but the win rate in case you win. On April 10, 1999, 40,000 players cheered over five correct numbers and each got $ 200 at the end. At that time it was about the numbers 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 26. Particularly artistic were the numbers of October 4, 1997: 9, 13, 23, 27, 38, 40. "The crosses on the ticket looked a sign and 134 had six correct numbers.

But the absolute record holds the draw of 23 January 1988. 222 players had the numbers 24, 25, 26 and 30, 31, 32 checked. Of course, the payout was very low.

What can we learn from it?

Well, we can not influence the probability of a win, but the odds if we win. For that we have to type numbers that most people do not type.

The same applies in the forex market. To act differently than most people do. What are the consequences? We need to be guided by successful traders and study their behaviors. What do these successful traders do differently than anyone else? Let's just take a look at their trading screens

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Do you see any indicators there, Heikin Ashi or Fibonacci lines? In principle only the pure price chart. Can this work successfully?

MACD, RSI, MA's and all standard indicators should disappear from the screen and pay close attention to the pure price chart. The less distraction there is, the more you can focus on the essentials. The main screen I recommend completely free to draw in your own resistance lines and support lines, which one works out of supply and demand of the market. In addition, I recommend creating your own dashboard. Currency strength, candle strength, trend strength, and the dollar index provide important information and possible projects you are working on.

Now you will say that the big players do not draw any resistance lines and you are absolutely right. But we must not forget an important point, the big players also determine the market. So why should they draw resistance lines if they are the only ones who determine the market.

We small traders do not have these options, so we have to go looking for clues. The big players leave their mark on the market, which can clearly be seen. We must evaluate these traces and use them for our purposes. A successful method for this is supply and demand.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Here is an example in the EURUSD in the 1H chart. I have drawn only a few equilibrium (yellow circle) and then drawn a line. Just look how the course behaves on these lines. Whether this is coincidence or not, derived from this one could have done some nice trades.

I do not know many traders who have geared up their trading strategy only for supply and demand, another reason you may want to consider in the future. I would like to give you 3 quotes in the weekend that are close to my heart.

"Cheap winds can only benefit those who know where they want to go." Oscar Wilde (writer)

"There are more people capitulating than those who fail." Henry Ford (American automaker)

"Be patient, all things are difficult before they become easy." French proverb

I sincerely wish you that you can establish yourself in this tough market.

Best regards

Progonosis 4 months ago and reality

Hello dear traders,

On the 23rd of January 2018 I published in this block (Post 14587) the following post:

https://www.forexfactory.com/showthr...0#post10700600

For many years now I am only following the POC principle.

The key "Equilibrium"

1. The price is determined by supply and demand in each market.

2. Any influence on the price will be returned from the price

3. Before the price moves up or down, a balance between supply and demand creates a balance.

4. If this balance is disturbed, the price moves in the direction of supply or in the direction of demand.

5. The price moves as long as supply or demand until there is a balance again. Then the whole thing starts from the beginning.

Most candles are where there is a balance. We do not want to trade there, when the price is not moving very much. So we have to act when there is no balance.

On 15.01.2015 there was the franc shock

Let's take a look at what happened to the USDCHF.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

The price slipped from 1.018 in seconds to 0.855 (1.600 pip). But already after 49 days the course came back into the POC zone. What happened? The price went down about 1,000 pip for the next 50 days.

Let's look at the EURCHF

The price dropped within seconds from 1.20 to 0.97. (2,200 pip)

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

The course has still not made it into the POC zone after 940 days. Now we are nearing a decisive phase. I think we will reach the zone relatively quickly. And then?

Now I recommend you to watch this zone as you enter the course. As it seems, the zone could push down the course and give us some good shorts.

Now let's look at the result 4 months later.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

In the daily chart large overview the result looks so far as follows.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

In the daily chart small overview, the course is clearer to see, the stop of 16 pip has been a small risk in terms of potential opportunity. So far you could win 270 pip with this information. As I find an interesting chance risk ratio.

How could I know that 4 months ago?
I could not know that, but due to the supply and demand I've been working on for over 10 years, the guess was obvious.
I do not want to express that I was right, but that one should deal with the subject of supply and demand. This information helps every dealer to significantly improve his performance. The principle of supply and demand applies in all currency pairs and can be applied easily.

Outlook 2018 EURUSD

Hello chonchy, hello dear traders

First of all, thank you for your encouragement and your kind words. I'm delighted that you like the supply and demand strategy and you want to know more about it.

I like to share my experiences and perspective.

Since you have been trading on the stock exchange for more than 10 years, or maybe even longer, besides winnings and losses, you have a decisive advantage over many traders. You have stamina and you are not too bad to take other ways. That's what distinguishes you. I did my first stock market transactions 30 years ago over the phone with my bank. To date, much has become more modern and efficient.

It is not the big ones who eat the little ones, but the slow ones are eaten by the faster ones. The high-frequency traders have noticed this long ago and, with their way of trading, make it hard for the big players in the market.

The entire market has changed enormously as a result of the various dealers that appear in the market. Many years ago I also started to analyze the market with the standard indicators and it has often worked. The MACD and RSI were also a life companion for me, but how many times was the market overbought and still the price went up.

If your competitor drives a 400 HP Ford Mustang, you can not win a race even with the best and fastest racehorse against him.

For many years I have dealt with the big players and analyzed how you do your business. There are no standard indicators and they are not used for trading. The big players know, however, that the small players pay attention to the indicators. Especially here in focus are the Fibonacci lines. These are good entrances for the high frequency traders to stop the small players.

10 years ago, this trend started slowly and I had to think about how I can have a chance in the market to survive in the future. I deleted all indicators from the screen and started over. In the beginning it was hell, because all aids (indicators) had disappeared at once. 5,000 hours later, the first findings came and another 5,000 hours later, the success was there. The road is tough, but it was the only way for me. Sometimes I have the feeling that the big players push the indicators forward to us small traders even better to be able to take the money. They know exactly that many traders hope for a change at the 61 retracement. A good point to stop everyone.

To be successful one should not attract attention and certainly not be predictable. A successful trader must be a perfect tracker to survive in the market.

If you can decipher the tracks of the big players, you know their next steps and can be pulled up or down nicely. You will not notice that as long as the amounts do not go well over $ 1,000,000. Because then you leave even small traces in the market. And the secret is to go undetected. That's why I do not trade with the crowd, but stay where few traders are. Only then will you remain anonymous.

The first step for this: All standard indicators go away and look for clues. I did not get any further with the market analysis, not because it is bad, but because it is not suitable for me. Supply, demand and equilibrium was finally the breakthrough for me. That's why I opened this blog many years later. The Equilibrium also does not always show the right way to a trader and I am also mistaken every now and then. But in more than 50% of the cases, I'm right and with a good Moneymanagement and a very good chance risk ratio, the ball is safe in goal.

Over the years, I've written 3 laws for myself that I've done very well so far.

News

Not the news, but market participants influence the market.

In 2016, Deutsche Bank and many currency experts estimated that the EURUSD would reach 0.95 at the end of 2017. It came completely different.

It is always fun in the evening at NTV (German news channel) to learn why the DAX or EURUSD has risen or fallen. Of course the economy is important in the individual countries, but not for me. For me, how investors respond to the news is far more important.

It does not matter which news is about the ticker. The market is moving because people and computers are pushing the button BUY or SELL. And why are they pressing on BUY or SELL? Because they have an opinion. And this opinion often has nothing to do with the economic data.

Why does Apple share fall even though Apple released a sensational quarterly balance sheet? Well, maybe because investors believe Apple will not be able to make such profits in the next quarter or peak the stock. Anyway, we'll never know.

News causes storms on the stock markets, it often goes up and down. I prefer to wait, because sailing is simply no fun in a strong storm.

Indicators

An indicator does not care if the price goes up or down. It is trailing and less accurate than the price chart. Many traders need security and believe the indicator tells them where the market is going. But the market influences the indicator and not the other way round. That's why I work with auxiliary indicators, which I do not pay much attention to. If I can not trust myself, how should I trust indicators?

Opinion

Since about 97% of all traders are wrong, this means that 97% of all opinions are wrong. That's not bad, because since humans exist, he's wrong. Much more important it would be to set the 3%, whose opinion is correct. But finding them is a challenge. One solution would be to look at what opinion the majority has and then do exactly the opposite. So we should not listen to the crowd, but to ourselves.

Trading is a pure chance game, nobody knows where the journey is going. But with mathematical probability calculation I can beat the coincidence in my favor. The big challenge of trading is not to win, but to behave properly when you are in loss.

Let's come to the specific question of how I see the EURUSD in the future.

Stock market wisdom, are they still valid today?

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Dear Traders,

In recent decades, the investor market has changed drastically. Laws that were still in force 20 years ago are outdated today.

The stupidest forex market wisdom in the world Risk and money management is what boring people, not traders. Always use the full leverage (leverage), because that's what it's made for. Divest profits as fast as you can and run losses. Never look at charts because that's information from the past. The market is your enemy, show him who's the fittest. Double your position after a loss trade to get the lost money back quickly. Always listen to analysts and trade based on their recommendations because they understand the market best. Buy every low / Sell every high because the market keeps coming back. Buy it as soon as the market hits you - every 10 pips. Act according to the motto "As long as a loss is not sold, it is not a loss."
Since the stock market, there are losers, winners and self-proclaimed professionals who could tell you in retrospect why you won or lost now.
Let's not fool ourselves. The stock market is pure gambling and has nothing to do with math or formulas. You can neither calculate the courses in advance nor can you make valid statements about a possible price course.

Prices rise as a larger number of call options outweighs a smaller number of put options (demand dominates supply) and prices fall when a larger number of put options outweighs a lower number of call options (supply dominates demand). Since you can draw as many lines as you want, take all the indicators to the aid, there are only two results in the end. You were right or you were wrong.

It is quite simple: Imagine sitting in a room 100 people you do not know. Everyone has two buttons in front of them Buy and Sell. Now you have to predict if Buy or Sell wins. You decide to buy. The chance that more people hit the buy button is now 50%. If you're right, that does not mean that you're a professional. You were just lucky. Now you have to predict how many people will hit Buy and Sell. You're guessing that 40 people press buy and 60 people sell. The probability that you are right now is now much harder. But exactly this point is crucial. The more people decide to buy, the more the price goes up. If exactly 50 people decide to buy and the other 50 people to sell, then an equilibrium is created.

The stock market is unpredictable, but that's exactly what makes it predictable for some professionals. We can never predict how many buy or sell orders are coming to market, but we can quickly identify equilibrium. And that's our only real chance we have. Equilibrium means uncertainty because the buy orders are roughly equal to the sell orders. It means that there are as many buyers and sellers on the market.

This equilibrium can be a turning point in the market, but need not. Now, if you focus on the equilibrium and analyze it in the market, you know exactly at what time an uncertainty in the market has occurred. This uncertainty occurs in certain price levels again and again and ensures in certain places again and again for a change of course. From this, possible reaction patterns can be derived. This is still no guarantee that you are right or can predict the prices, but it does help to turn the odds in your favor. And 51% (with a chance risk ratio of 1: 1) is enough to earn more than to lose.

You can not be better than the market, the market is always right

No matter what you invest as a small trader, in the long run your own portfolio return will equal the overall market return. An active action can thus bring no advantage. So you do not have to make an effort, trades are what dreamer.
If there are people who are worse than average then there must be people who are better than average. However, the argument often only aims at an upper limit, while nobody seriously doubts that one can be worse. That's why this wisdom may apply to a majority, but not to all traders.

Inside information is worth gold

Suppose you know exactly what information the Fed or ECB will announce next, then it will not do them any good. Why?
If nobody in the market knows at the moment which news the ECB or FED has in their hindquarters, then a market can not react. He only reacts when the "bomb bursts". Until then, the market can react very volatile and unintentionally stop them. And even if the bomb explodes, they still do not know how the market reacts.
That's why I do not necessarily see inside information as an advantage.

Academics are the better traders

The investment is not science, it is a craft. Or have you perhaps observed that academics in particular are good investors? That's not the case. Academics act just as well or badly as people who have not studied. So, if you make that statement, you're either too theoretical about forex, too academic, or simply not aware that there is a gap between general theory and solid practice. Since academics act as well as non-academics, the theoretical advantage seems to be a disadvantage rather than an advantage.

Back and forth bag makes empty

This saying is always used when someone comes up with the idea of introducing a trading approach. The commentators then want to prevent someone from trading already bought currency pairs (from time to time). Because only the passive holding of currency pairs brings in their opinion the highest return. And a trade also costs fees! Back and forth bag is empty "is in the sense of the above opinion just a blanket statement, which testifies to little knowledge about the subject of trading. But even the most fundamentally-positioned investor has to dispose of an investment from time to time. Scalpers in particular only live on being invested in a currency pair for a short time. Of course, if I put on the corrections in a downtrend, this back and forth can quickly lead to significant losses.

"If you have a lot of money, you can speculate; those who have little money must not speculate; If you have no money, you have to speculate. "

If you read this saying somewhere, it is often used in a diffuse trading context. One wants to teach a trading beginner with a small account the fear. He should save even better as long as he has only a few thousand euros. But that is definitely wrong.
Someone who claims this has no idea of the distinction between speculation, trading and investing. Mostly those are beginners who do not think outside the box. They believe trading would be a fundamentally unfluent or even reprehensible endeavor. For a rule-based trader speculation is out of the question. to make money means to make a bet. And you can only bet if you consider your bet as play money or if you have no choice but to take the risk, because there is no money. But if you have to budget, you should not bet. He should act strategically and bring the probabilities to his side instead of putting too much bet on a big but unlikely profit.

Not all eggs in one basket, lack of diversification is dangerous

There are people who believe that it is important to spread their money widely. And they also try to suggest to anyone who does something with stock market. Everything else is really dangerous, it can always lead to a crash!
For years, I have been dealing with the majors primarily with the EURUSD. Secondary currencies leave me outside and also with oil, silver and stocks, I hold myself rather in the background.
Diversification in the EURUSD alone is greater than one would initially assume. Of course, this is primarily the euro and the dollar included, but these currencies are also dependent on other currencies. That alone creates an enormous diversification. For equities, however, that looks different. If you're told it's unprofessional to just handle the majors, let them talk.

Conclusion:

Many stock market quotes have a true core and are helpful in many cases. But the market has changed significantly in recent decades. We must meet these changes by adapting to the circumstances.

Listen to her inner voice and do not let others unsettle you. No matter if you are an academic, a professor, a worker, a merchant or a school dropout. The chances to win more than to lose are 50%. Now it's up to you to find a strategy that will improve your chances.

That was my approach then and with the help of the Equilibrium I was able to improve this opportunity in my favor. Maybe you will find this way, I'll help you with it.

Good luck in the coming week

Best regards
