Which time unit is ideal?

Hello dear traders,

For a long time I searched for my personal time unit, in which I prefer to act. We know the standard time units 1M, 5M, 15M, 30M and so on. Those who were not satisfied with the standard time units had a much larger selection of time units with the Meta Trader 5, but there are still too few brokers who have the MT5 in their program.

So in the end, only the MT4, especially since the supply of support indicators there is significantly larger. As Scalper, the smaller time units have a clear advantage, so I only got M1, M5 and M15. The M1 is too volatile and too inaccurate for me. Since I would like to have a look over 2 days in a time unit, the M1 is out of the question.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

With the M5 we have the same problem, the bars are just too small to get an overview over 2 days.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

The M15, on the other hand, is too big again, an equilibrium can be identified much more difficult here, which often makes the drawing of the lines impossible.

I was not satisfied with that, so I was looking for an optimal combination. The middle would be the M10, but just this time unit was out of the question for me.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

It may sound strange now, but my preferred time unit for trading is the M8 and not the M10.

I would like to show you once the difference between the M8 and the M10. As an example we take the last 2 trading days in the EURUSD.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

On the left side you see an M10 and on the right a M8 Chart. Compare the points 1 and the points 2 together.

What is striking?

In the 10 minute chart we see stronger wicks than in the 8 minute chart. Especially the Wicks are often important to identify an Equilibrium. The bigger these Wicks are, the harder it will be to draw resistance lines. Now you might think that this chart image was just a coincidence, so let's take a look at the next day.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Again, you can clearly see that the Wicks in the M8 are significantly smaller than in the M10. If you look again at the M5 chart (slide 1) you will notice something. Curiously, we also have very big Wicks there, although this time unit is clearly smaller than M8 or M10.

Big Wicks are therefore counterproductive to see at a glance if supply dominates demand or demand dominates supply. So you have to find the time unit, which gives you an overview of the price history within seconds. Of course there are bigger wicks in the 8 minute chart as well, but compared to the 5 minutes Wicks they are usually smaller and the overview is much better. With that, I have created a good basis in the 8 minute chart to capture my personal equilibrium in the short-term, which shows me future resistance. To throw this 8 minute chart on your screen, proceed as follows.

You open a chart in the M1. Under Navigator you open the Period Converter under Scripts and enter the number 8 under Period multiplier factor. This means that the 1 minute chart is multiplied by 8. Now go to File: Open Chart offline. Now look for the EURUSD M8 and open this chart. Please note that you must not close your 1 minute chart, so that the 8 minutes offline chart is not interrupted. Of course, you can also insert saved templates into the offline chart.

Equally interesting is the 8-hour chart, which you can create on a H1 chart with the period multiplier factor 8.

Just try it if you can handle it better. The only thing you can lose is time, which is precious, but if you can use it more efficiently, the time spent is worth it.

I wish you a nice weekend
Best regards

Gap in EURUSD

Hello dear traders,

on May 25, 2018 at 23:00 CET, trading started the weekend after a downtrend. 48 hours later on May 27, 2018, trading at 23:00 CET was 37 pip higher.
A gap of 37 pip had formed. If you can trade a gap profitably, this is a question that daytraders are especially concerned with trading on the stock market.

What is a gap?

GAP comes from English. In short, it is a "gap" and is used in the financial sector for a price gap. This is visible in the chart image and can arise for several reasons. In the so-called order book, a large number of market participants are frequently available on both sides (supply and demand). Thus, only one GAP can arise if there has been a massive movement and no further market participants were in the order book at points further from the price.

There are several gaps: If the GAP moves in the trend direction and the market moves quickly away from the GAP, it is, for example, a break-away GAP. Likewise, a Measuring GAP can even confirm the trend. In contrast, an Iceland GAP or an Exhausting GAP is a hallmark of directional change. However, we do not want to deal with that today, just as little as a gap can be closed or not. By the way, in 90% of the cases a gap is closed, the question is only when? These are pure speculations for me, which I do not want to deal with today. Nevertheless, these gaps can provide traders with interesting information about a future price history. Let's take a closer look at this gap from May 27, 2018.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Here you can see how the gap has expired. In principle, you would have to draw a bullish green candle without shadow into the price gap. This candle was 37 pip. I have now drawn the range of this candle into the future and let's take a closer look. By the time the gap was created, the price of 1.255 total 910 pips has fallen. This gap was a small alarm signal for me, the bulls are slowly warming up. Of course, the course went down even more, but then formed the bulls and pushed the price massively upwards. It is interesting how the course has reacted within this range. After the course has penetrated into the range, you can see very well that this range has occurred as a kind of resistance. Of course you can not derive any generalization from it, but you can make an interesting discovery of it.

Take a look at strong price moves up or down. You will notice that this price level from which the price has gone up or down massively is a kind of resistance zone.
This gives us some information to anticipate possible price movements ahead. Especially if you pay attention to the Equilibrium and their strategy is oriented to supply and demand, these price levels will provide you with important information.

This information increases the likelihood of making the right decisions and 51% is enough to earn more than to lose.
I hope you got some ideas, now it's time to take a closer look at the market.

I wish you much success.

Easy Equilibrium

Hello dear traders,

Before we get to the very core of the matter, we have to briefly deal again with the market economy. As you may have already seen in the video on page 1 of my blog, the market is always the same in terms of supply and demand.

The EURUSD is primarily determined by the big players, let's take a closer look at that in the first step. In 2018, approximately $ 6,000,000,000,000 a day was converted into the foreign exchange market. The EURUSD has a share of about 25%. Thus, daily $ 1,500,000,000,000 is traded in EURUSD.

Now I have determined how high the average Pip per day is in the EURUSD. I have calculated the average of the last 10,000 candles.
On average, 90 pip are reached per day, 16 pip per hour and 2 pip per minute. It does not matter if the price is up or down. Since the price fluctuates every second and a minute candle does not generally go up or down, it can be assumed that at least 5,000 pips of fluctuation in the EURUSD will be achieved per day. Dividing the trading volume of $ 1,500,000,000,000 by the 5,000 pip volatility, a frightening insight comes to the fore.

To move the price around 1 pip $ 300,000,000 is needed. However, one can not analyze this in such a concrete way, as it always depends on how many participants are buying or selling in the oderbook. Now that you know that there are sometimes breakouts of 30 pip or more, you know roughly what money is being moved at that moment. So you can be sure, even if you shoot $ 100,000 in the market, no one will notice.

Take two market participants. The price of EURUSD is $ 1.20. Big Player A believes that the price will fall and Big Player B believes the price will rise.
Big Player A invests $ 900 million on a falling course and Big Player B $ 300 million on a rising course. What will happen? The course will fall. If both invest an equal amount at the same time, equilibrium is created and the price is still $ 1.20. But, strictly speaking, that's not true, as both market participants have different fees and thus one investor invests more than the other.

Take the $ 1.20 equilibrium zone. This means that market participants are in agreement and there are just as many buyers as sellers. Now some buyers are getting off and more sellers are entering the market. We now have a supply market and the price drops to $ 1.19. At $ 1.19, many sellers get off and some buyers come into the market. The course stops and in this zone an equilibrium is created again. More buyers enter the market, creating a demand market that will push the price higher again. The price rises until an equilibrium arises again, where buyers and sellers agree. Then it goes up or the course falls.
Since indicators have a trailing character, one should give the pure price chart the greatest attention. A price does not rise because the faster MA cuts the slower MA, but because more market participants believe in rising prices and therefore buy more traders than sell. But what happens if the price increase is just a jiffy break or a pullback? You can not see that either with indicators or the price chart. Even the order book, volume profile or footprints do not help there.

The only chance here is the price levels that signal me support or resistance. Decisive for this are the supply zones and demand zones which are analyzed with the help of the Equilibrium. And that has nothing to do with indicators, order books, volume profiles or footprints.
Let's start with the EURUSD in the hourly chart on May 25, 2018.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Once I have highlighted all the candles from 30 Pip within an hour in color. The 30 pip refer to the open and close, high and low is less crucial. These so-called color breakouts have the habit of always breaking a strong resistance zone. This means that within this breakout zone there is a resistance line that may once again play a crucial role in the future. In principle, the breakout I mentioned is a big jump or a dip in price, because after all, this candle has formed within an hour and not within minutes. The course is clear and in relation to the other candles, the color-coded candles stand out clearly from the gray candles.

In the upper and lower chart image you will see two yellow resistance lines from the past. I have drawn these lines on the same principle, which I will now explain below. Now we go on the search of the possible resistance zone, which is broken with my color-marked candle down or above.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Let's take a look at the first color-coded candle. We can clearly see by the yellow arrow next to the green candle what happens. The result is the gray candle, which lies in front of the green candle a kind of equilibrium between the open and the high. The course goes up and is rejected again. How do I choose the optimal entry?

You have two options. You put a limit order in the middle of its resistance zone and the stop just above or below the zone. The second option is to wait and see how the price reacts and to go up after the first pullback, so that you lose important points.

With this Equilibrium system, you can quickly see if the trend has changed or if it's just a pullback. If a price change has occurred, simply draw two lines on the trend change and look in the past. --- 帖子 #591 ---
Hi Bionics,

sorry to step in to your thread but I'd like to correct what you've said about equilibrium and about the way how and why the fx spot market is moving.

Unfortunately your assumption about what is causing market equilibrium is not correct. Sellers and buyers will NEVER meet as market participants. The simple evidence for that is spread. How the hell they could make any trade together and make equilibrium when price have a difference in form of spread between Bid and Ask? And so due to spread existence their orders won't never be "paired" (unless the traders in your example do not use some bucket shop brokerage ) and so simple orders difference can not really have influence on the market i.e. more buyers does not necessarily means the price will go higher and vice versa.

What potentially does equilibrium are actually limit orders and market makers providing the liquidity through them. Liquidity provided to the market in form of limit orders is what can eventually make some sort of market equilibrium, not balance of orders or balance of volume of market orders. Market orders move the market but only in the way where is the least liquidity. It's different concept than in stock market but this is really basic concept of FX spot market one should comprehend. It's crucial to know this FX spot market mechanics how and why is price really moving. And it's actually quite dangerous to teach the way how to spot the reversal points without that knowledge and without access to full order book, because order book is the only source where one could find real potential reversal points. Full order book is something one can never get neither from the retail broker nor from prime brokerage. Without it it's just guessing, that's why I quoted it as to be dangerous.

Simple example: even just 1 selling order of 1 lot can easily move the price when there is no buying liquidity even in the situation when, at the very same time, there is simultaneously put 100 lots of buy orders when there is enough liquidity available to fill the buy orders. So in this example we have 1 lot selling pressure and 100 lots buying pressure but price could easily go down despite the fact that there are much more buyers than sellers.

Easy Equilibrium the next part

Dear Traders,

The instructions in the post 590 was a first approximation to the Equilibrium and a rough analysis to show you which power can have certain price levels.

A sharp rise or fall in price means, in a sense, a high expenditure of energy in one direction or the other.

This sharp rise or fall is said to break certain resistance zones with a high force to reach the target. We need to find exactly these resistance zones, as these zones can play an important role again in the future. In the post 590 we first determined the average pip size with the average candle indicator in a certain time unit and then let us show the largest candles with the momentum candle indicator in color. From this, zones were identified which, in a sense, are called coarse zones in order to get to know the Equilibrium system.

If we have an average pip size of 15 at EURUSD in H1, but only the color of the candles that reach a pip size of at least 30 we will not find all  important resistance zones. That is, to find the most important resistance zones within a time unit, we need to reduce the pip size in the Momentum Candle indicator to a certain size. Before we realize that, another aspect is very important. The decisive factor for this calculation is the price history that exists in your meta-trader. So if you want to find the average of the last 1,500 candles in H 1, your Metatrader must provide the price data for the last 2 months in H1, otherwise the calculation is wrong.

You can try it yourself once a month. Most brokers provide price data in EURUSD MN from 1996/1999. My Metatrader provides me with the price data of the EURUSD of January 01, 1971, which is almost 560 months. The average pip size per month is 461 pip. If I now want to display the last 1,500 months, the indicator gives me a value of 173 Pip. This is clear, as the indicator now divides the same number of pips by a higher time value. Therefore pay attention to how many price data you can calculate maximum. In the monthly chart, it is sufficient to display the last 100 months, since the values should still be reasonably current.

My candles in the Metatrader are dim gray in color and with the Momentum indicator I indicate the strongest momentum. Depending on the time of day, the momentum indicator must be adjusted in a time unit.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Here are my settings with which I am well through the day. From time to time the settings have to be adjusted up or down.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Here you can see a chart in the M15. The candles are gray and the momentum indicator is set to 7. At the weekend, I prepare the next week in all 9 time units. I look at which zones in the coming week could be exciting and interesting. Of course, I can not predict if certain zones will be reached, but analyzing each zone by supply and demand will help a trader to make fewer mistakes.

Try it out for yourself, then you will quickly realize if you can handle it.

I wish you much success and a good trading week

Two charts two opinions

Dear Traders,

The views of whether a price goes up or down is different for each trader. That's exactly why the course is moving. There are 1000 ways to analyze a chart image, the question is: what type of chart analysis is the most likely to fulfill the prediction?

There are only 2 answers to this:
1.No chart analysis
2.The chart analysis that the trader considers appropriate.

Let's look at an example:

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

You can see the monthly chart of the EURUSD since 2003. Trader A has plotted two lines, claiming that the price will continue to fall sharply. And indeed, because of the drawn lines, it actually looks like this.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

You can see the monthly chart of the EURUSD since 1984. Trader B has plotted two lines, claiming that the price will now rise sharply. And indeed, because of the drawn lines, it actually looks like this.

But who is right now?

I believe that no one is right, because this kind of chart analysis is very dangerous in my opinion. Of course, sooner or later one of them will get the right, but not because of his chart analysis.

I also posted a similar chart image for the fun of the beginning of the year, but with the hint that you should be very careful here.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

If we look again at the chart image of 1984 we notice the 3 circles. Some see a shoulder-head-shoulder formation, others a sloping triangle or even an equilibrium. The likelihood here would be more likely to be a further uptrend, but this assumption I derived from my year chart and not from the two drawn lines. Nevertheless, the statement goes up or down, pure speculation.

There are traders who can work because of cross-lines and are successful, for me, the price levels are best captured in a horizontal plane. However, I am working out these horizontal resistance lines on the basis of supply and demand with the help of Equilibrium.

We humans think in pictures and draw our lines. We can draw lines everywhere and believe we can recognize something there. But the course is not based on pictures, but whether there are more buyers or sellers.

The nature of my approach, how to see and analyze the market, has caused a few  rejections. That's fine and I accept every opinion. However, I do not want to discuss or justify myself on this blog. Who likes it, tries to follow this path, who does not like it continues to search. I mean, there are a lot of great traders here who have great ideas and systems, and everybody will find something suitable someday.

Many articles say that 95% of all traders lose more money than they win. I do not want to support or reject this claim now. It does not matter if it's actually 90% or 95%. However, the fact seems to be that the majority is losing. If the majority loses, that means that the recommendations on how to act properly are 95% wrong.
That was the reason for me to follow a path that does not meet the expectations of the 95%. Whether I belong to the remaining 5%, I do not want to claim that. At the end of the day, every trader should be able to say: more was not possible.

I wish you good ideas and much success

EURUSD 300 Pip crash

Hello dear traders,

Yesterday on June 14, 2018, we saw a sharp drop of almost 300 pip in the EURUSD. That was the biggest drop for 720 days, because almost exactly 2 years ago on June 24, 2016, there was a drop of 510 pip. A few hours earlier I had already pointed out a strong resistance and noticed that it takes a lot of strength to overcome this resistance.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

This resistance was also overcome for a short time and then strongly rejected. Of course, I could not know which direction the course was going to be, but my identified zone was crucial.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

What happened?

I would like to introduce a possible scenario. The ECB press conference was scheduled for 14:30 CET. At 13:45 CET there was already a press release about the result. For a big player, this announcement was a reason to value the dollar higher than the euro. However, how do you trade down without taking many traders down? You lead the dealer first on the wrong track.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

In the M1 you can see what happened at 13:45 CET. The course was pushed up by the big player 40 pip. Many traders were aware of this strong line of resistance and many now assumed that the price is now heading higher. You can see nicely on the chart image that some traders, who were fortunate enough to be taken up, have sold their position. The course went back a bit. Some traders were hoping for another big rise now. Now the big player pushed down the course with heavy pressure, many stops were triggered and the few traders were in the game. The downside accelerated. The third candle was once again a strong sell and push down. The rest was pure mass psychology and the crowd followed the course. You can see that the course in the recorded resistance zone has briefly gone into equilibrium and another attempt has been made at the ECB press conference to get back up, but the overall pressure of the mass movement was simply too great.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

As the price dropped 300 pip, there were some attempts to push the price higher again. On average, a daily range has 91 pip. Many traders thought after the price had gone down 180 pip that it had to go up again. Unfortunately, these ideas did not work out.

One often has the feeling that the course runs faster down than up. Basically, this claim is not always correct, but it is similar to real life. Trust is gone faster than it builds. You can see in the picture how the price initially accelerated and the downtrend weakened over time.

If the price goes up sharply now, that does not mean that we are back on an upward trajectory. It could also be because the big player repurchases his shares.

So we are back in an equilibrium, buyers are not sure whether they should invest again and the sellers are wondering if the price could fall even further.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Although this strong downtrend is basically not a good prospect for a longer uptrend, but you can quickly be fooled. We have two strong resistance zones for a possible strong uptrend. Resistance zone 1 has already been reached and the price has been sharply turned upwards. Now the course has come back strong. Now it remains to be seen if the resistance zone holds 1 and the course can move up.

Resistance zone 1 is still strong for me, maybe the course needs to penetrate this zone a little more before a demand market re-emerges. Zone 2 is a stronger demand zone than zone 1. Should the price break zone 1 and see it as resistance from below, zone 2 would be relevant to me as a high demand candidate. However, there is still a blue line which could also push up the course as strong resistance.

Another possibility would be that the big player has identified zone 1 as the reversal point of a longer-term uptrend and has now pushed the price down sharply again to get a better starting price.

This assumption is purely speculative and every trader has his own opinion. It is crucial to evaluate the market according to his views and derive a strategy for himself. As a Scalper, I make it a bit easier for me by basically acting reversal points in smaller time units. Nevertheless, a longer-term trend analysis is also an important issue. I would like to point out again that my statements made are my personal opinion and I do not claim to be right. My hit rate is much higher, but I often wrong myself too.

Many years ago I also tried to trade currency pairs on a long-term basis, but found that I can make higher profits with the Equilibrium in smaller time units and larger contracts. Education is what is left when we forget what we have learned

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Before reading this article, please note the following. The statements made here are only my personal opinion. They are not scientifically proven and I do not claim to be right. These statements have only one goal: to help the reader.

At the beginning of my trader career, I had a friend who had tremendous trading expertise. At least that's what I thought at the time. He was able to explain all situations exactly and what he said sounded logical and understandable. He had an answer to every question and if you asked more precisely, he looked at you with wide eyes in the way: How can you ask such a stupid question?

A professor of business administration taught us at that time: There are no stupid questions, just stupid answers, but he did not allow such arguments.
This acquaintance regularly got involved with other specialists and sometimes the discussions about "China coming to the UN" did not stop there. I found his reasoning exciting and interesting at the time, but I could not understand it. I found this expertise impressive and one day hoping to have such profound knowledge to become a successful trader.

During my training as a Financial Analyst, I completed an intelligence test lasting several hours, which gave me an IQ well above average. This gave me further hope to understand this confusing stock market one day. One day I discovered the truth through a stupid coincidence. My friend, who had so much expertise, did not make a single dollar on the stock market. He lost more money than he invested. A world collapsed for me and I wondered how much knowledge one would have to have to succeed?

According to some studies, a high IQ does not guarantee a high income. Far more skills are needed to earn more money than the average in the long term. An important aspect is the emotional quotient and the art of simply grasping and formulating difficult things. The type of communication today more than ever decides on success and failure. If you have studied you will have noticed these differences among different professors. It was not the professor who made the wisest statements that was the winner, but the one who, through a simple and pictorial language, succeeded in inspiring the majority of students so much that it was easy for them to pick up and implement the material.

I have learned the following in my life:
Individuals who used their knowledge to humiliate other people were less successful in the long term than those who used their knowledge to solve problems together with other people. Knowledge is good, but not if you use knowledge to show others how stupid they are. How many times are there people who make statements that we can not immediately verify. So we do not contradict, because we lack the basics of knowledge. In most cases, the statements made are only hot air. However, we sometimes realize that only 10 years later, when we were able to gain experience in this area.

Now comes a truth that is very uncomfortable to accept.

Since the stock market, traders are trying to identify the secret of the stock market and find the holy grail. But look at the result after many trillion trades:
95% of all traders lose more money than they earn. Is that the holy grail? What does the result mean in terms of the secret of the stock market?
Well, we have not been able to decipher the secret with the last trillion trades and we will not decode it in the next few trillion trades. This is also logical and clear, since trading is based on a pure random principle. This principle ensures that the stock market can theoretically exist forever. If you were to crack the stock market code, that would be the end of the stock market right now.

If the stock code has not yet been identified, this means:
All statements on the stock market are purely hypothetical. A hypothesis is an assumption formulated in the form of a logical statement, the validity of which is considered possible, but which has not yet been proven or verified. This means whether the statement on the stock market sounds very smart or very stupid, in both cases it is not proven or verified and thus equally valid or invalid.

This applies to all the statements in the blogs of FF as well as for my blog, but I have never claims anything else. Of course, a hypothesis is hypothesized as long as it is verified, but since the stock market is based on pure coincidence, it may be very difficult to verify future hypotheses. This should not be dramatized negatively now, because after all, my statement does not change the already existing situation. There is no holy grail and no one can foresee the stock market concretely and permanently. These are the facts so far.

Let's take a look at nature. Nature has developed a thousand exciting things that look very complicated from the outside. On closer inspection, however, they are very simple. Maybe the stock market is also easier to understand. Trading is all about winning the majority of comparable trades over the long term. That's why we should start focusing on the simple things.

To gain more than to lose on the stock market, you have to optimize the probabilities in your favor. Objective: To find a system that increases the probability of winning more trades than losing. How can we achieve this goal faster? Answer: Through knowledge, intuition and information! Here are some tips on how to do it to save time. Please note that these tips are not completed.

How do I find my matching system?

Let's first define the word system. Under system I understand a trading setup, which allows the trader with a certain strategy buy or sell orders that he earns more money in the long term than loses. This does not mean automatic trading systems or a copy trading. What use are you automatic systems or a copy trading if you do not understand how the system works. The goal of a trader should be to be independent of others with his built-up system.

Once in the CFD area, take a break from costly indicators or tools. The same goes for seminars that often cost a lot of money. I do not want to say that these seminars do not work, but before they even know where to go, they do not need an expensive tool. If you find your way later, you can still invest your profits in continuing education. You are an entrepreneur and a real entrepreneur starts with small investments in the beginning. When the first successes occur, one can use these profits in the further development of his company.

How can I find an interesting system at FF now?

Let's start with the members. In total, there are almost 500,000 members at FF. Members who publish regular contributions and communicate with other members are so-called impact members. They are marked with a rhombus.

Red = High Impact Member = Top 2% about 620 members
Orange = Medium Impact Member = Top 5% about 930 members
Yellow = Low Impact Member = Top 10% Top about 1,550 members

With that I can reduce my choice to 3,000 members. This does not mean that the other members do not post well, it just means that they do not regularly post information. Let's just stay with these 3,000 members for the sake of simplicity. There is interesting information about these members that makes it easy for a new reader to find the best.

Unfortunately there is no search function in FF to filter out interesting blog writers out. But on each side of a member they get the following information.

Joined: month year
Buddies: number
Subscribers: number
Post: number
Last Online: Date
Trading from: Country

Now let's take 3 members who have different values. (we do not consider the country)

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

At first glance it looks like Trader A has the most experience as he has posted the most threads, most subscribers follow him and he is the longest in the process. After that Trader B comes and at the end Trader C. Now let's have a closer look at the activity of the individual traders.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

We realize that the picture is completely changed now. Trader C has 6.97 subscribers per month while Trader A only has 4.68 subscribers per month. Trader A has sold almost twice as many posts as Trader A. (buddies and subscribers were added together) Subscribers per month are a representative feature because people often only follow interesting topics that help them. This proves that even new members post interesting topics that are often accepted by other traders.

A picture is worth a thousand words. Make sure that a post with examples and pictures conveys more information than just plain text. Notice how the writer of a thread deals with its subscribers, how it criticizes, whether it makes fun of others and how it helps people.

An interesting feature is also the Ignored list. Sure, there are sometimes people who are annoying and you just have to lock. But if someone has 50 subscribers and has 25 on the ignored list, it might not just be the other one. This often has something to do with respect and interaction. There are always exceptions, but the subscribers already have a reason why they follow certain people or not. These factors do not guarantee that a trader will succeed or post topics that really help. But there are little hints if it pays to look closer.

Never underestimate the traders who are beginners. These traders may not have much experience yet, but they are not stupid. Only when a blog provides logical and interesting information, more and more traders will join this blog. Good and successful things communicate very quickly. I mean here only threads that provide information about a trading system and where to exchange regularly.

With this little help, I can ever separate the wheat from the chaff and quickly recognize whether a second look worthwhile. Under the heading: Trading Systems you will find nearly 3,000 different systems offered. Of course, they also get ideas and strategies in the other categories, but I would first start trading systems. As a rule, most of the contributions have also been published by Impact Member. Now we have to filter the 3,000 posts.

Take a distance from things that do not help you, meaningless discussions about topics that no one needs, you can find everywhere. Get involved and look for the topics and traders that communicate their strategy in an understandable way. Unfortunately, this is often about vanities and to prove that man are the best and most beautiful. But I think that most of us are able to distinguish between good and less good. Start with the latest blogs. Why? A current blog bears witness to current information. If a blog published in 2010 receives interesting and profitable information, it is still up to date today because it is simply good.

When they have selected the most up-to-date threads, they should check the match of a thread's statements. Take a look at the first and last post by the blog writer and compare these posts with each other? How long has the writer been working with this system? Is the first and last page similar or has the blog writer changed his system completely? How often do you have new information? Is the blog up to date or has it not been used for months? If a blogger has written several posts, they look at how strong the response was, or whether the blog was closed after a few posts already.

If you can answer these questions positively, you take the next step. Is the system simply explained? Can you understand it? Is it logical and does it fit with your trading style? Pay attention first of all to the statements of the blog writer and less to what the individual guests say. Often there are envious or disturbers who make unqualified statements, even though they do not know the system at all. If you do not understand a system because it's too complicated for you, leave it alone. If only indicators are used to make a buy or sell decision then you should be very critical and if that does not fit with your style, be finished the system.
If all questions are logical and understandable, try this system in different currency pairs at different times in a demo account.

After that you can make a decision.

If you try a system and do not implement it successfully, even though others may succeed, that does not mean that you are unable to do it. It just means that this system does not suit you. Forget it and keep looking.

Many traders are interested in optimizing their existing system or completely redesigning it. That's fine, because change means development, and the market we work in is evolving every day. However, you should not try to find a system that wins 100%. Each system has its advantages and disadvantages and will not produce the same results in every trend phase.

I admit that finding an optimal system is a big challenge and takes a lot of time. But believe me, that's worth it. Because if one day you have found the system with which you are successful, you can generate an interesting income. Forget about the great pictures that are often published in connection with Trading. A villa on the lake, sports cars, world travel and endless money. The truth is sobering in the beginning. An entrepreneur who rebuilds his company first has to invest in the beginning. And investment costs money and time. If you use these investments wisely you have a chance to become a successful trader. When I started trading, my main motivation was independence and not money.

Basically, I find it remarkable and exemplary when traders voluntarily and unselfishly offer their system to other people. Your personal success!

Demand and supply since 1975

Dear Traders,

Today I would like to describe three strong price zones which we have encountered again and again since 1975. I have calculated these zones based on supply and demand from the last 43 years in the weekly chart. Let's take a look at how the course reacted to these lines.

From this we can draw possible conclusions for the future.

1975 to 1984

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

You will see blue arrows in the chart image. I have refrained from marking the arrows in color. Arrows pointing down mean that supply dominates demand, there are more sellers than buyers, the price is pushed down. Arrows pointing up mean: Demand dominates supply, there are more buyers than sellers the price is pushed up.

Of course, there are other zones that have an impact on the price movement, but we do not want to take this into account here.

1986 to 1994

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Here we can already see significantly more supply and demand zones. It can be seen very clearly that the three zones are very often a start for a supply market or demand market.

1995 to 2004

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Although we have a stronger supply market in the first 5 years, the price returns to our zones after a sharp decline. In the second half you can clearly see how demand is increasing.

2004 to 2012

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

The upper zone seems to be a limit, the course is pushed up again and again. This shows the strong demand, which, however, slowly decreases from the middle of the chart image. Supply is getting stronger and demand is failing to make new highs. Nevertheless, the upper zone keeps the course.

2010 to 2018

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

In 2012 there was a last desperate attempt to push the course back up, but by the end of 2014 the course finally broke through this strong zone, breaking through the second zone which finally ended up in our lowest zone. There was now an equilibrium. Let's take a closer look at the last 4 years.

2014 to 2018

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

In 2012 we see a strong equilibrium at the top zone at point 1 and then a strong breakthrough to the bottom zone. Thereafter, the course fluctuated between the lower and middle zones. You can see the strength of the supply market in the middle zone, which has pushed the price down again and again. Within the blue rectangle an equilibrium was created.

At point 2, a supply market emerged, after which the price had gone deeper into the zone3. This supply market accelerated and with a strong force the middle zone was broken. Nevertheless, the price continued to rise. There was a pullback and the course continued its journey to the upper zone. Where, on the top left in 2012, a strong equilibrium arose, the course was slowed down. This is exactly where a strong supply market prevailed. That's why, on January 1, 2018, on my blog, I had suggested that the price at 1.25 would make it a stronger setback. Although I was correct, I misjudged how far the course would run back. From the lower to the middle zone there is a strong demand market. From the upper to the middle zone there is a strong supply market. Exactly on the middle line meet supply and demand.

There are now 3 scenarios if the price should reach the middle line.

1.It creates an equilibrium, as buyers and sellers agree. After that, the direction is open.

2.The course bounces off the middle zone and continues its journey upwards.

3.The course breaks through the middle zone. It depends on which strength he breaks through this zone to have enough power to continue down to run.

After equilibrium within the rectangle, the market has decided it is going up. The course broke through the middle zone and continued to run upwards. That was an indication that the sellers were satisfied. Only at 1.255 was again a strong supply market. I suspect that the middle zone could now appear as a strong resistance after the recent years.

This does not mean that the price is rejected directly, but that the price could move strongly towards 1.399 thereafter.

Look at the zones in the smaller time units, this gives a possible overview of supply and demand.

I wish you a successful week

What is your most important principle? If you place an order you should take as few traders as possible on the journey. Because as soon as these traders get off in the course of the course, this will slow the price down. This means the traders must be misled. Than you can placing your big order.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

At point 1, you see the morning pre-trading with little volatility. The market is in an equilibrium with a slight tendency to supply. After the course has reached this zone, the course drops to point 5. I wait a moment.

The trend is accelerating as more sellers join. The price drops to the strong resistance level at point 6. Many now assume that the price will rise again. I let the price go up a bit and push a massive sell order into the market. The price drops another 33 pip. At point 7, I gradually get off all orders. This ensures that the price rises massively. Twice I stopped the majority of traders in 15 minutes and was able to get through my course. The course returns to the mean resistance line and turns into equilibrium at point 8. This clearly shows the market uncertainty that prevails now. In principle, I could stock up on shopping orders unnoticed within Equilibrium. The market believes anyway that it goes up again and I'm now happy to take this trip with a few buy orders. I can not lose anything now because I took about 55 pip in the morning. For a day in which the high low 65 pip, the result was profitable at a manageable risk.

Certainly, the scenario has not developed exactly as I described it, but it is once to stimulate the situation of the big players to move. We as small players can hardly move the market, but let us drive from the market. But if we let ourselves drift from the market, we must at least know where the journey goes.

So we have to try to think like big players and start reading their tracks. This increases our chances of winning more and losing less.

Of course, the market is much more complicated and my point of view far too simple, but maybe this is the secret that makes the success.

Determine resistance lines

Hello dear traders,

On 19 July at 19:00 CET, the M30 Chart saw a strong uptrend of 70 pip. (Point 1) As already mentioned, this candle broke up some strong invisible resistance lines.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

I have drawn these resistance lines once at point A, B, C, D, E. Now please pay attention to these points only once.

Point A was a special case for me, but one would have to go back in the past therefore I would not go into that here. Since my marked point E was not touched, we deal only once with the points B, C, D.

After the price went up high, you could expect a small pullback. No one can predict how this pullback will work. Precisely for this reason, the resistance levels B, C, D were a decisive criterion for me.

First, the course go down to point C and was pushed up again. On the second run down, the course came the second time to resistance C and was pushed up again. There the resistance line A came into play.

On the next run down, resistance D became active, pushing the course up again. A further downtrend stopped the third time in the resistance line C. The resistance line B show that the course could move further up.

So a little tip. These strong upward or downward candles break through invisible resistance lines. We must identify and draw these invisible resistance lines. This works in almost all time units. If we combine these time units wisely, we will see that there are matches.

These matches have a strong meaning.

The resistance lines running through a strong upward candle are identified only by the upper wicks of previous candles. The resistance lines that run through a strong downwards candle are identified only by the lower wicks of previous candles. It does not matter whether it is a bullish or a bearish candle.

Decisive is also always the previous course, the offer zone the demand zone as well as the Equilibrium which are in this zone. In truth, it's much more complicated, I just tried once to show you how to start with simple means. Over time you get out which zones you have to draw in order to determine the concrete resistance lines.

That is why my recommendation to work without indicators, as these indicators only distract. The art is to determine and mark these resistance zones in the pure chart image. Start with the simple variant, as I described it. If you have done that 1,000 times you can see which zones are relevant and which zones are not interesting.

I hope I could give you some tips and information try it yourself now. And before you act: Whenever you are sure that the price goes up or down, you will be wrong.

I have not been acting for years for what I see but only for my determined resistance zones. Whoever acts according to what he sees in the movements of the candles sees losing more money than he wins.

Have a nice week

How did I start...

Like most beginners, many years ago, like a madman, I repeatedly tried new indicators and discarded them again. A system that I managed for the first time and won the first significant amounts, I would like to introduce you today. The basis for this was an M5 chart. There were 3 Moving Average. A fast MA simple 8 in the hourly chart (green) and a slow MA simple 39 in the hourly chart (red). A third exponential MA 8 in the M5 chart (white) for early detection rounded off the matter.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Here is an example in the current EURUSD chart.
We see here just under two weeks at a glance. If the green line was above the red line I basically just bought and if the red line was above the green line I basically only sold.

Let's start at point 1. The green line breaks through the red line. From that time on, only selling came into question. Shortly before point 2, the green line came up to the red line. At point 2, the green line broke the red line. Now I waited for the price to return to the red line to enter with a buy order.

You see 2 red and 2 green horizontal lines in the chart. These showed me from when the course went up or down. Let's take a look at the upper red line. Interestingly, at point 1,3,5, and 7, it worked well. However, you can not always rely on it.

Now, when I got into point 2, I let the track go. At some point I set my stop to zero, so I could not lose anymore. Fortunately, the price was up now. As the price went over the top red line, I was a little more cautious and put my stop on the underlying green line. The course continued upwards. Now the green MA was the deciding factor to exit. As soon as the green line was broken, I waited until the uptrend returned to the green line. There I am then out.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Here you can see very nicely how the MA 8 in the M5 chart signaled the approaching downtrend. At point 1, the Ma pushes through the slow-moving green line. At point 2 the downtrend is confirmed. Then I let the course down and waited until he returned to the red line. The point 3 was then the entry down. From point 4, I would have become a little more cautious and would have sought a good exit.

Of course, this is one way to trade, the downside for me: you just get in late into the market and also out too late. In addition, the risk is significantly higher than trading in supply zones and demand zones in Equilibrium. As I have developed into a scalper over time, longer trading periods (overnight or over the weekend) are taboo for me.

Even if one should not act with MA, this compilation of indicators for beginners has a small advantage. You can quickly see in which areas you should not buy or sell.
Nevertheless, I generally advise against acting with standard indicators. These run after the market and are just too slow. But everyone starts once and we all made a lot of mistakes in the beginning. As a beginner one does not always listen to the experienced traders, one prefers to make his own experiences.

Trades without indicators is like riding bareback. It is really hard and takes a long time until the first successes occur. But when you master it, a lot becomes easier. Do not be dictated by indicators when to buy or sell. Any trader with his knowledge can do that 10 times better. Start trusting yourself, this is the first step to become a professional trader.

I wish you every success in the first ride without a saddle

Bear or bull trap?

Hello dear traders,

you've heard or read it many times, what is a bull or bear trap? It is supposed to be a trap in which the investor, who expects falling or rising prices, invests on the basis of his analysis and subsequently turns out to be a misjudgment. Are these traps really, or is that just a myth?

Let's first look at an H4 in the EURUSD from January 2018 to the end of April 2018.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

At the beginning of the year there was a strong uptrend, at point A a strong equilibrium was created, after which the price continued to rise sharply. There I have marked a resistance zone. The price was 1.255 (point B) and then came into my resistance zone at point C for the first time. The course was rejected and a great equilibrium was born. Thereafter, the price moved back to the resistance line and broke through at the point D. This point D we now look more closely at the M15 chart.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Due to the price development, I refined my in H4 pink drawn resistance line with two blue lines. In addition, I drew two more blue guides. From point 1, the course went slowly down. Shortly before the lower high resistance line he ran slowly up again. A clear equilibrium.

There are 3 different states in the market.

1. Offer outweighs the demand = price drops

2. Demand outweighs the offer = price rises

3. Supply and demand are balanced

1. Offer = Seller (short)

2. Demand = Buyer (long)

The quantity available on the market represents the supply, the demand is the quantity that the buyer would like to purchase. In the stock market environment, the price strives to find a so-called equilibrium. At that moment, buyers and sellers are equally satisfied until an imbalance rebalances in favor of supply or demand. Then the prices rise or fall again. These competing factors (supply and demand) meet each other in all markets and regulate the price.

In the stock market environment, the price strives to find a so-called equilibrium. At that moment, buyers and sellers are equally satisfied until an imbalance rebalances in favor of supply or demand. Then the prices rise or fall again. At point 2, the course came after point C (Figure 1) for the second time in the resistance zone. He was a little more dismissed and ran into my drawn blue zone (point 3). From there he ran back down to the point 4 and came back into the resistance zone. This time around, the course was not so heavily dismissed and started a third time to break the zone. Some traders now make the mistake of placing a sell stop order below point 4. That would have gone well for just under 10 pip at point 5, after which the price went up by 66 pip (to point 6) and would have stopped many traders. Pay attention to what the course does after entering the blue resistance zone at point 3. The course was turned down, came into the large resistance zone and then ran back up. There he was rejected again and ran back into the big resistance zone. By now you should have noticed that the selling pressure is not strong enough to break the resistance zone. That means there are still buyers who need to be satisfied. Only at point 6, the buyers were satisfied and the seller could prevail. As the course went up again I realized that he could run down to the red zone at the latest. If you look at the overall picture in the H 4 Chart, it will be clearer. The upper red zone was therefore also a very strong resistance zone. So you could have taken the risk to trade down from that zone, or wait until point 7. Once the price broke the blue resistance line at point 7, you could trade down.

There is a fixed rule for me. I basically do not buy or sell in or after such a strong zone, but always far ahead. As the price tends towards this strong zone, I am able to set my stop to zero relatively quickly, and wait for what happens. Of course I can not know how the course develops exactly. The advantage is, as soon as the course comes back I am stopped out and have lost nothing. I can repeat this until the price breaks through the strong resistance zone and my plan with it rises. Some traders are also going to go below the resistance level above the entry level. It depends on your perspective………………….to those who understand the basic "Laws of Supply and Demand" it's just MYTH, it only becomes a trap for those who think in straight lines……..

If you foolishly believe :

Price rises due to an increase in demand

Price drops due to an increase in supply

Then of course the investor, who expects falling or rising prices, invests on the basis of his analysis and subsequently turns out to be a misjudgment.

That linear type thinking goes against the basic "Laws of Supply and Demand"

Retail traders think in straight lines…….they "believe" there is a direct (linear relationship) between Price and Supply/Demand. That makes them uninformed, and predictable, and easily exploited by the informed.

But then again, an Investor isn't a Trader either………..

You postulate that price rises due to an increase/imbalance in Demand

But the "Law of Demand" (economics 101) shows that's not true…………..

A. The Law of Demand

The law of demand states that, if all other factors remain equal, the higher the price of a good, the less people will demand that good. In other words, the higher the price, the lower the quantity demanded. The amount of a good that buyers purchase at a higher price is less because as the price of a good goes up, so does the opportunity cost of buying that good.
Read more: Law of Supply and Demand: Basic Economics https://www.investopedia.com/univers...#ixzz5OYZB807T

the higher the price, the lower the quantity demanded

Anyone who knows how Auction Markets operate, knows price rises to cut off the flow of Buyers/Buying

You postulate that price drops due to an increase/imbalance in Supply

But the "Law of Supply" (economics 101) shows that's not true…………..

B. The Law of Supply

Like the law of demand, the law of supply demonstrates the quantities that will be sold at a certain price. But unlike the law of demand, the supply relationship shows an upward slope. This means that the higher the price, the higher the quantity supplied. Producers supply more at a higher price because selling a higher quantity at a higher price increases revenue.
Read more: Law of Supply and Demand: Basic Economics https://www.investopedia.com/univers...#ixzz5OYZB807T

the higher the price, the higher the quantity supplied

Anyone who knows how Auction Markets operate, knows price drops to cut off the flow of Sellers/Selling

Price fluctuates regardless of Supply and Demand……….

It's being able to differentiate when price rises/falls due to a shift in demand/supply curve, and when a price rises/falls when there is no shift in the shift in demand/supply curve.

What you see on the price chart are the (after) "Effects" of the changes /shifts in the supply & demand curves, not the impetus.

If you want to see shifts in supply & demand you need to be looking a graph of S&D, rather than a price chart.

Supply and demand and equilibrium price are all NONLINEAR FUNCTIONS of price……………….

The solution to Supply and Demand is given by a nonlinear equation…………………….

We know it's nonlinear function, because it's data plots a CURVE……………………………..

NONLINEAR PRICE EVOLUTION By G. CAGINALP Mathematics Department, University of Pittsburgh, Pittsburgh, PA 15260-0001

"However, the demand and supply are generally nonlinear functions of price. We show that the information on this nonlinear variation of demand and supply leads to a more accurate description of price evolution toward equilibrium. With this additional information the optimal forecast for the price of the good or asset is given by a nonlinear equation. This yields an advantage to traders utilizing all of the available information on supply and demand functions, rather than simply the value at the current price………….."
Attached Image

Supply & Demand

In microeconomics, supply and demand is an economic model of price determination in a market. It postulates that, holding all else equal, in a competitive market, the unit price for a particular good, or other traded item such as labor or liquid financial assets, will vary until it settles at a point where the quantity demanded (at the current price) will equal the quantity supplied (at the current price), resulting in an economic equilibrium for price and quantity transacted.

Graphical representations
Although it is normal to regard the quantity demanded and the quantity supplied as functions of the price of the goods, the standard graphical representation, has price on the vertical axis and quantity on the horizontal axis.

Since determinants of supply and demand other than the price of the goods in question are not explicitly represented in the supply-demand diagram, changes in the values of these variables are represented by moving the supply and demand curves (often described as "shifts" in the curves). By contrast, responses to changes in the price of the good are represented as movements along unchanged supply and demand curves.
Pasted from <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supply_and_demand>
Attached Image

What is "equilibrium"  "equilibrium price" and in what "Context" is it used in "Supply and Demand"?

The price that makes quantity demanded equal to quantity supplied is called the equilibrium price. It occurs where the demand and supply  curves intersect .
Pasted from <http://www.dummies.com/education/eco...ly-and-demand/>

(Did you notice the "Context" does not refer to locations on a price chart)

equilibrium price

the price that balances quantity supplied and quantity demanded. And the price at the point of intersection of a supply and demand curve. Sometimes called the market-clearing price because at this price everyone in the market has been satisfied.
Pasted from <https://quizlet.com/47239203/chapter...n-flash-cards/>

equilibrium

a situation in which the market price has reached the level at which quantity supplied equals quantity demanded. The point where supply and demand curves intersect.
Pasted from <https://quizlet.com/47239203/chapter...n-flash-cards/>

A Linear Price chart and a Nonlinear S&D chart

Two completely incompatible charts

Supply & Demand has price on the vertical and quantities on the horizontal

MT4 Price charts have price on the vertical and time on the horizontal
Attached Image

Supply & demand is a nonlinear function, a nonlinear system of equations can not be solved, graphed, interpreted, or calculated using a linear systems of equations. (STRAIGHT LINES) This isn't an opinion, it is a fact.

Linear EquationsA simple linear equation is of the form: y = mx + c A linear equation looks like a straight line when graphed. It has a constant slope value. The degree of a linear equation is always 1. Superposition principle is applicable to a system characterized by a linear equation. The output of a linear system is directly proportional to its input.

Non-Linear EquationsA simple non-linear equation is of the form: ax2 + by2 = c A non-linear equation look like a curve when graphed. It has a variable slope value. The degree of a non-linear equation is at least 2 or other higher integer values. With the increase in the degree of the equation, the curvature of the graph increases. Superposition principle does not apply to the systems characterized by non-linear equations. The input and output of a non-linear system is not directly related.

Supply & demand is nonlinear, a nonlinear equation cannot be solved or measured using linear functions (straight lines & price charts)

The distance between 2 points/price is a "Direction" (linear function…….. measurement along a line) , not an "amount"

Supply & Demand is not a direction…………it is an "amount"

Just a little "Food for thought"

Hello Xniobi,

First of all, welcome to the blog: Equilibrium a key to success. I am glad that you are dealing with the Equilibrium and I would like to write you a few sentences about it. Basically my way of doing trend reversal is based on working without standard indicators. However, I do work with auxiliary indicators that give me some additional information. This type of trading is much more demanding than with two MA, but it takes more time to achieve satisfactory results. Analyzing the pure price chart is a great challenge, as the formation of candles is represented differently in each time unit. The larger the time unit in which a candle is formed, the more accurate the information. But the larger the time unit, the higher the fluctuation range of a candle. To derive information for an Equilibrium from this is not always easy.

At the beginning of my contributions, I first tried to show the reader a feeling for the Equilibrium. It's about the 3 different states in the market.

1. Supply dominates demand

2. Demand dominates the supply

3. Equilibrium

The first picture was to identify the equilibrium and derive a possible scenario for the future. Therefore, the visibility of the wicks was reduced and the momentum indicator made the strongest candles visible. This would make it easier and faster to identify an Equilibrium. The lines that you draw to the right from equilibrium are somewhat inaccurate and can only roughly determine resistance levels.

If there is an uptrend in the market and then an equilibrium is formed, it means that supply and demand are equally satisfied. This does not mean that the course has to go down again. Equilibrium means that buyers and sellers agree, but it also means uncertainty about where to go next. Within equilibrium there are small price fluctuations. (Of course there is also large equilibrium, in higher time units, we do not want to take this into account).

When a course goes up, it can suddenly turn down, continue up, or go into equilibrium. When the course is in equilibrium, it can only run up or down from this range of equilibrium. That's why I pay more attention to the Equilibrium. However, equilibrium does not always result in a turnaround. I basically do not work with candle formations or pictures, because the candle formation in every chart image is purely coincidental. This makes the Equilibrium more interesting for me.

The determination of support and resistance lines is often based on empirical values with the help of Equilibrium and with the help of supply and demand. Crucial here are the above-average price movements up or down. When a price moves sharply up or down, the price breaks an invisible resistance line. Exactly this invisible resistance line must now be found. The likelihood of this line returning as a resistance at a later date is very high.

In the second picture you can see how I try to refine and narrow the zones. As Counter Trend Scalper, I often act against the trend, which has the advantage that I am very fast in the plus. This trading offensive is very dangerous as I often go down in a strong uptrend. For less experienced traders, I'd rather recommend longer term trades with the trend. Scaling as a beginner against the trend is pure money destruction. It takes at least 20,000 hours of trading experience to be profitable. So it's perfectly normal that you can not handle this kind of trading in the beginning. For that you need a lot of time and experience.

Deciding zones

Hello dear traders,

Let's take a closer look at the offer zones and demand zones in the monthly chart.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

In 1980 there was a very strong offer zone at point 1 which pushed the price down to 0.56. There was then a strong demand zone to 1.45. Thereafter, the price was pushed to 0.86. At point 2 there was a strong demand zone which brought the price up to 1.60. From 1.60 the price went down in waves. The strongest demand zone (at point A) was terminated precisely in this green zone. There was an equilibrium and at point B a strong demand zone was created which ended exactly in the green line. Then the price ran to 1.255 and was pushed down again. At point C, there was again a strong demand zone. Between point B and C, at the beginning of 2017, a new uptrend started at 1.03. From 1.255 to 1.13 we speak of a pullback so far. It looks like the end of the pullback is reached in the green line (point C).

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

In the daily chart, we see the strong demand zone which has brought the price up sharply. This was followed by a pullback. This pullback is now back in a stronger demand zone (point 3). I recommend keeping this zone in mind. You see 3 blue zones point 1,2,3). These zones symbolize a strong demand. Maybe the course could run down again. The purple zone (point 4) would be another demand market, which could then be crucial for a further course.

However, the price is now on a daily chart in a demand zone. If the dealers do not agree, we will first see an equilibrium. From this current line, the price can only go up or down sharply. If the price goes up the first blue line (point A) could be breached and the price will start another pullback on the red line above (point B). Where is the middle of EURUSD?

Have you ever wondered where exactly the concrete middle of EURUSD lies? This question I once pursued for fun.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

On 01/01/1971, the EURUSD's lowest converted rate was 0.5365, the highest ever EURUSD rate was 1.6038. Adding these numbers and deriving the arithmetic mean results in a value of 1.0697. But this value can not be correct because the price is composed of many different individual values.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

A monthly candle is very informative because it represents the largest unit of time in our chart. From 01.01.1971 to 31.08.2018 574 months have passed. For these 574 months I evaluated all data sets on Open, High, Low, Close and Volume in EURUSD. Regardless of whether one forms the mean value of the individual values Open, High, Low, Close or balances the average of Open and Close with the mean of High and Low, the result remains almost always the same.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

In the novel The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy, a supercomputer named Deep Thought has given the answer 42 after a few million years of computing time to the question "life, the universe and everything". The answer to the question where is the middle of EURUSD is: 1.0680. With that you can start in any case more than the answer 42.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

The volume in the EURUSD first rose to just over 200,000 shortly before the introduction of the EURO. So let's take a closer look at this time.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

After the introduction of the euro over 6 years passed until the volume first broke through the 500,000 mark. At the beginning of 2016, we peaked at just under 4,000,000. This makes the EURUSD one of the most successful currency pairs in the world today. Of the 5 trillion euros that are converted into currency trading on a daily basis, the EURUSD has the highest value of more than 25%. That's the most important insight to me about the volume.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Therefore, we consider the time frame from 01.01.2002 to 31.08.2018 to calculate the mean value in this period. The lowest price during this period was 0.8570, the highest price at 1.6038. The mean of this gives 1.2304. In fact, the middle is at 1.2525. The candle that has formed in this period can be seen on the chart image. It is a strong bullish candle that is back on the uptrend after a long pullback.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

With the introduction of the euro, the right candle was formed. Now I have the remaining period divided and formed two more candles. You can see very well a strong upward trend and then a doji which shows the uncertainty. With the introduction of the euro, there was again a strong upward trend. Definitely, we are currently above the middle of 1.0680 of the entire period and below the middle of 1.2525 from the launch of the EURO.

What happens next?

In the EURUSD there are no top and bottom and therefore unfortunately no middle. When the EURUSD reached 0.80 shortly before the euro launch, no one could imagine that the EURUSD doubled to 1.60 just 7 years later. Likewise, no one today can imagine that the EURUSD may one day be at 2.30, or maybe even 0.57 again.

Since there is no top and bottom, the price does not matter. That is also the reason why I often do not know what price the EURUSD currently is. Decisive for me is how a candle develops and with it the course. This results in demand and supply and, in the case of unity or uncertainty, an equilibrium. The current price therefore has no relevance for me. In the same way, I do not pay attention to volume. In a market where there is no top or bottom, only the demand or supply is the limit. A price can never be oversold or overbought, so for me, indicators like the RSI are a relic of the past. The price always moves up or down in wavy lines, so I do not care if the EURUSD costs $ 0.50 or $ 1.60. Of course you have to adjust the number of contracts, but on average it does not really matter.

We then earn money when we identify a demand market and get on time with a BUY order and exit at the latest when the price enters a strong supply market.

We then earn money when we identify a supply market and get on time with a sell order and exit at the latest when the price enters a strong demand market.

That's the only secret, but unfortunately that's not always that easy. Forget about the top and bottom, the price, the volume and all the standard indicators. Let's look at supply and demand and success will prove us right. We do not fight against other market participants in this market, but only against ourselves.

best regards

Hello emicovi,

First of all, welcome to our blog and thank you for your request.

For your question note the following information.

I work with 3 time units.

MN or W1 for the parent trend
D1 or H4 for the middle trend
H1 or M15 for the short-term trend

Depending on volatility or candlelight, I use these individual time units to plot my supply and demand zones. In the M5 I open and close my positions.

Of course, I also draw supply zones and demand zones in the M5, however, these zones are very inaccurate and not very meaningful. Decisive are my zones for the overall trend, the middle trend and short-term trend. For me, the zones I draw in the M5 are the ultra-short-term trend and are only noticed when these zones match the parent, middle or short-term trend. So it may well be that on my M5 Chart 20 zones were drawn, of which, however, are again erased 50% in the course of the course. In addition, my way of working is different than that of many traders. Basically, I also try to act with the trend, but I often act against the trend. The short-term pullbacks are a safe source of income for me, as I am one of the first in the market, rarely in minus and the short-term pullback can usually take complete.

Thus, I often draw zones, which I can act against the trend in the short term. However, this pullback is often of short duration, until it then continues with the parent trend. If you misinterpret these zones and act on them, you lose money. The larger the time unit, the more accurately one can determine the supply market or demand market. Since I work with very small stops of 5 pip to achieve an above-average opportunity-to-profit-ratio, I have to localize supply and demand in smaller time units. However, these zones are currently being matched against the parent zones. If I post an M5 with supply zones or demand zones and you act accordingly, you may lose money. In addition, not all zones will work because I will delete more than half in the course of the course.

In the next few days I will try to post an idea how to possibly proceed here.
