New project work for you

Education is what is left when we forget what we have learned.

Hello dear traders,

For many years, I have been working as a full-time scalper and day trader in international currency trading, where over $ 5.1 trillion is transacted every day. Foreign exchange is now regarded as a separate asset class, as the market has grown enormously in recent years. The price is determined by supply and demand in each market. Therefore, I only act according to specially created supply and demand zones which I identify with the help of the equilibrium (price equilibrium). Indicators should not be used for buying or selling decisions, but they can be very helpful at work. The programming language these indicators are programmed in has a lot in common with Java and C ++. That was the approach for me to learn a programming language to better understand the indicators and their calculation principles.

I made comparisons between C ++ and Java and finally decided on Java because it was easier to learn from my point of view and possibly had the bigger future. Java again took first place in the TIOBE Index in 2018. The TIOBE Index is a ranking of the most important programming languages. Over 9 million Java programmers worldwide are proof of that. Java is one of the most popular programming languages in the world and is used on more than three billion devices. However, MQL4 has more to do with C / C ++ than with Java, but to learn a programming language, I have chosen this way only once.

In January 2018, I finally opted for a study online course that ran from march to august 2018. The costs of more than 12,000 euros were athletic, but absolutely justified to reach the goal. 8 hours per day over 6 months, that's just 10 € per Java hour. If I compare there other courses, which cost 2.500 € for 5 days my selection was a cheap offer. The timetable was structured, 2.5 months (400 hours) OCA (Oracle Certified Associate) instruction, then the OCA exam. 1.5 months (200 hours) OCP (Oracle Certified Professional) lessons, then the OCP exam and then another 2 months (300 hours) the Enterprise Edition followed by the OCM (Oracle Certified Master) exam. A total of more than 900 teaching units Java and additional learning units totaled more than 2,000 hours.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

After this stressful Java study, I know what it takes to pass the Oracle Certified Associate (OCA), Oracle Certified Professional (OCP) and OCM (Oracle Certified Master) exams on average with over 86%. It took a lot of time and work, but in the end it was worth it.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

The three exams that took 2.5 hours each in the Oracle Exam Center were not as stressful as I initially guessed, actually I did not need the exams because I did not want to become a Java programmer, but my ambition was that. In retrospect, however, I'm a little proud that I made it. I'm not a professional for a long time yet, just like stock market trading you need at least 10,000 hours to become a pro. But Java was just the basis for me to learn and build on a programming language.

MQL4 is an object-oriented programming language developed specifically for the Metatrader platform. Originally, its syntax was based on C. The other platform, MetaTrader 5, was released together with MQL5 in 2010, and MQL4 now has new graphics objects and functions from MQL5 for chart analysis. Both languages support almost all standards of object-oriented programming, with the exception of multiple inheritance: data encapsulation and type extension, inheritance, polymorphism, overloading, virtual methods. The main disadvantage of the MQL family languages is the impossibility of creating independent applications.

The first crucial step is to understand how an indicator works. From this I can deduce how this information is important to me or if I need it at all. Basically, you first have to understand how such an indicator is composed. The data input of an indicator receives only price information, time information and the volume from interbank trading. From this information, very different indicators are then created.

The second crucial step is to collect and combine information that is important to me. This creates new forms of information that are crucial to me as a trader.

The third and final step is to create indicators that do not yet exist and to gather information from them that will give me additional arguments for my decision.

Based on the results of indicators, I will never open or close a trade, but only on the basis of my zones of supply and demand, which I come from purely price information. Even the volume is completely irrelevant to me. Nevertheless, so-called auxiliary indicators help me in my decision-making. It will take a while until I am able to independently program these required indicators, but in the last months I have been diligent, very creative and had the professional help of an experienced MQL4 programmer from Germany.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Together we have been following some projects in the last 6 months, the results of which I will introduce to you in the next few weeks. The resulting indicators support my approach to demand and supply in a particular way. --- 帖子 #661 ---
Determine trend strength in any period

Dear Traders,

As promised, I would like to start today with my first project, which has developed over many months. Before I publish the related indicators, a detailed explanation for success is crucial. I think we'll be through with the first project by the end of the week and by then I can upload the first indicators. The information that you receive with these indicators is very valuable and could bring you interesting additional income in the future.

When I made the first attempts to trade successfully in the forex market many years ago, I had no idea how difficult this path would be for me. In these beginners' years, many indicators were used. At first, the motivation to finally have found the right indicator, then came the attempt to act profitably and finally the angry awakening. The indicator was deleted, a new one searched and the whole crap started again.

Then it was time for the Expert Advisor. Who does not dream of making a living while sleeping, while an EA earns many thousands of dollars for you? There were impressive performance curves with incredibly low loss phases. However, these performance curves were not due to a sophisticated system, but to the so-called "curve fitting". For this purpose, the variable optimization is used on a trading platform in such a way that it adapts the values of the indicators used in such a way that the best combination emerges. It is clear to everyone that you can always build an optimal EA in the aftermath, but I do not know any EA that has really worked sustainably in all market phases.

Then there was the possibility of Nachhandelns in the live trading room, while you could trades for a fee, the trades of professionals 1: 1. This type of trading is very controversial, as the equity ratio of individual traders is very different. In addition, I do not want to be dependent on other traders or EA, I would like to know myself what I'm doing and why.

Especially beginners get the feeling that they just have to find out the right indicator settings, then they get a system that magically attracts the profits. This hope is certainly understandable, but this is a fallacy. An indicator basically shows only what the naked chart shows, but with a time lag and often in a smoothed form. Foresight is impossible to achieve with you.

This is certainly a normal learning process and things change over the years until one day I no longer made my actions dependent on indicators and only had the pure chart image in mind. Concentration on the essential was the motto. I'm not against indicators, it just has to be the right ones. The right indicators will give you information and support you to make better trading decisions. But indicators should never make you trade decisions or make decisions for you.

Indicators are generated from the price information of the market and are therefore always trailing and slower than the price information itself. Even the price information is in the moment where they arise already past, because at the same moment again a new price information arises. What we see on the chart picture or in the order book is the past. Although we can guess the future, we can never know what will happen next. Nevertheless, we can use indicators for our purposes if we know that their information is trailing. But just with past information we can get important information regarding supply and demand.

The price in the forex market is arbitrary and random, which is why one can only make inaccurate and random predictions for future price movements from the price information. Scientific findings help in a market that arises by accident, not further. This means that all laws that we know from business can not be applied in a random market. Just think of Lotto or the Powerball. How do you want to proceed scientifically here? The likelihood that a sequence of numbers pulled last week will come back the next week is as high as any other sequence of numbers. This is because the balls on which the numbers are printed have no memory.

There is a small ray of hope in interbank trading and on the stock market, behind the pricing are people who buy or sell. There there are and emotions and with it a memory. And the most important thing is that there is an opinion and a belief, but we can not get on with science here. If the forex market had to be scientifically researched and explained, the stock market code would have been broken long ago. There have been stock exchanges for more than 500 years and until today hardly anyone is able to act in a sustainable and profitable way over the years. The findings so far seem to be purely speculative. 1,000 traders have 1,000 different opinions and that's a good thing, because that's why a stock market works. Even the worst trader is someday right. A clock that has stopped is showing the right time twice a day.

Warren Buffet, George Soros, and James Simons all own over $ 11 billion in private wealth, making them the most successful traders. But they have not earned their wealth day-trading, but funds that have a long-term investment bias. This does not mean that you can not make money with day trading, it's just very speculative and dangerous if you know that over 80% of all traders lose. You do not believe that? Take a look at the website of all brokers in Germany and read on the first page at the bottom of the fine print. There it says:

CFDs are complex instruments and because of the leverage they are associated with the high risk of losing money quickly. 80% of retail accounts lose money on CFD trading with this provider. You should consider whether you understand how CFD works and whether you can afford to take the high risk of losing your money. For professional clients, losses can exceed deposits. Trading carries a high risk.

Note: I believe more than 80% of traders lose.

This is proof that in 500 years of stock market history, there is no significant insight into how to act profitably. So you have to go other ways and experiment to improve the probability to your favor.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

As a trader who trades for Equilibrium, one dreams of a chart image that always indicates exactly the supply zones and demand zones. From this one could always deduce in which trend phase the course is currently. As such an indicator would have to look to the future, it quickly becomes clear that this wish will always remain a dream. Nevertheless, one can gain an advantage with the right tools in the large shark tank.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Some subscribers have often wondered what the numbers below or above my candles mean. These numbers belonged to my project, the idea was born a few years ago but was not realized until this year. Let's start from the beginning.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

As a beginner, one eventually comes to the ZigZag indicator and believes that it can predict future price movements better. At first I was interested in an ordinary ZigZag Color indicator, which colored the ascending lines green and the descending lines red. For the MT5, I quickly found it, however, I found no ZigZag Color indicator for the MT4.

The indicator seeks to represent only significant movements in the market and to eliminate unnecessary "noise". For a 3% Zig Zag, a market movement must have been> 3% from the last relevant point for it to be considered. This indicator is totally unsuitable for accurately predicting future market movements. The last Zig Zag line is only completed when the market has changed direction in the meantime. This means that the last line will be fixed only after the course has long since changed direction. Zag Zag lines should not be confused with trend lines. The supposed accuracy arises from the retroactive adaptation. This means that a supposedly completed line can also extend. The last line is always under reserve and has no significance where the market is next.

Thus, the indicator for a future course prediction is completely unsuitable. Nevertheless, the ZigZag indicator provides a visually highly visible picture of the market direction and the extent of trend and correction movements. The length ratio of individual lines can provide indications of the expected extent of market impulses.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Take a look at the H1 chart in EURUSD. In 100 hours there was a supply market and a demand market. Which trend was stronger? A or B? If you look at the strengths of bullish candles, you would automatically consider Trend B as the stronger trend. In fact, Trend A is just as strong as Trend B.

I wanted to take a closer look at this approach, I was interested in how strong the trend was within a line period and whether it was possible to deduce from it. So I did some calculations for that. I will post these in the next few days.

The ZigZag indicator therefore records lines and I wanted to measure the strong of the candles within a line period. I took the number of pip and divided it by the number of candles. The result was the average pip per unit time. The simplest things are often very efficient. Let's take a look at the previous example in H1:

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Our journey begins on August 22, 2018 in the H1 chart at the yellow arrow. From there, the supply market runs to point A. Precisely at point A, the demand market has covered 92.7 Pip within 30 candles. That's 3.1 pip per hour or per candle. This value is now projected by the indicator in the chart. A market demand arises and brings the price to the point B. At the end of point B, the demand market has covered 205 pip within 66 candles. That's also 3.1 pip per hour or per candle. Thereafter, the course goes down to the point C and once again up to the point D. After the point D is created, so point C can not change.

At this moment I have three pieces of information: Trend A has a power of 3.1 Pip, Trend B has a power of 3.1 Pip, and Trend C has a power of 3.7 Pip. If you look at the overall chart for an overview, you will see that the price before point A has been in a strong uptrend. Trend A was a pullback. Trend A and B are equally strong. As point D emerged, it could be seen that trend C was significantly stronger than trend A and B. When point D was created, a value of 3.3 pip was displayed. This value is much weaker than the trend C and stronger than trend B. This could also be concluded on a pullback, but I can not pay attention to this value because the point D is only then established when point E is created. However, the information is quite interesting, Trend A and Trend B are equally strong, and Trend C is stronger than Trend A and Trend B, Trend D might be weaker than Trend C.

Of course, you can not derive any trade decision from this information alone, but it will be a lot easier with supply zone and demand zones. Now some will say for sure that I get very late the information about how strong a trend has been, but also pay attention to the settings of the zigzag lines. The setting is 24/12/6. This value is very high and if I choose the setting 4/2/1, of course, I get much earlier trend trend information, but this is somewhat inaccurate, we will come to this later.

Tomorrow we will look at the calculations and some examples.

I wish you a nice evening.

Best regards

--- 帖子 #665 ---
Start with the project

Hello dear traders,

As we have noted - the standard ZigZag is not what we mean by a technical indicator. He is one who takes his time to make his decisions. In reality, the ZigZag only knows at a significant turning point whether the previous already marked turning point is valid at all. It may even be that the Zig - Zag decides completely new and totally changes his picture. The ZigZag pretends so something. He always reacts retroactively and therefore does not provide any information that can be used for trading decisions. The ZigZag standard can be used to analyze the nature of a market, its cycles and price swings. It is basically a noise filter that only marks price movements that are larger than the set filter. It marks the current trend direction with great clarity and ignores price fluctuations below the filter size.

Programmers of trading systems can thus gain an overview of the expected price movements and their intensity. That was the main reason why I used this indicator as the basis of a new calculation.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Before it went into the programming, I wanted to know whether the new calculation basis provides any useful information. That's why I retroactively calculated half a year in H1.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

During this period, 69 zigzags were formed and the pips divided by the number of candles. From this, the average number of pips per candle in each period was determined.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Slide 3

The entire period has been graphically presented to get a first overview. Interesting was also the graphical overview of the Pip change in this period.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

I reduced the time to the last 14 ZigZag lines, where I did not consider the last line because it could change.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

In turn, I presented the result graphically to get an overview.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

This resulted in the first draft of a possible view. Each of the three adjacent blue numbers means: number of pips in this period, number of candles in that period, and average pip per candle in that period. The bottom histogram should again graphically indicate the size of the average pip.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Here you can see the result. Alone I would not have been able to do it at this time, so I would like to thank Georg, (SwingMan) a very professional trader and programmer from Frankfurt. I would also like to thank Nicholishen, who is a very intelligent and strategic programmer and trader. I think it's great how unselfish these people support others, many thanks for that.

Now I would like to do an experiment with you. As you can see, we have a scale of values that ranges from 0 to infinity. Now let's just assign a trend to the values:

Very strong trend = A (2.0 - 3.9 pip)

Strong trend = B (4.0 - 5.5 pip)

Weak trend = C (5.6 - 8.4 pip)

Very weak trend = D (from 8.5 pip)

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Let's go into the individual analysis. Beginning in 2018, the price starts at around 1.20 and then goes up to 1.255. At point A we are at 1.22. where the course price does not matter here, it's just about the overview in which area we are. Please note that with a setting of 24/12/6 we can not record every change of course.

Let's start with our experiment. Trend number 1 was very strong and Trend 2 was very weak (pullback). This increases the likelihood of a further rising trend. The Trends 3 is completed and you can see that after 54 hours the trend strength has decreased significantly compared to Trend 1. The probability for a trend reversal exists. Trend 4 is very strong and in principle initiates a longer-term downward trend. There is a pullback with trend 5. Trend 6 is weaker than trend 4, which increases the likelihood that it will go higher.

When Trend 7 is completed, you realize that the bullish trend has become weaker than Trend 5. A good sign for the bears. At point 8 we see how strong this bearish pressure has been and can hope for a bullish comeback. Point 9 and 10 is very interesting. Point 9 shows how strong the bears are now at the helm and point 10 how weak the pullback was. That speaks for further rising courses. Trend 11 was much weaker than Trend 9, so it's a great way to trust the bear. Point 12 was very strong over 80 hours, the bullish pullback point 13 weak. Point 14 was as weak as point 13, indicating a sideways market. Items 12 and 13 suggest that the bears are still at the helm. After a sideways phase, it finally went down further.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Next, let's take a look at the weakest points in this overview. Here you can see very well that after each a very strong trend has gone up or down.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Now let's have a look at a current chart picture until 10:45 CET. The last point C is of course not yet completed, if you look at the history with this course I believe that this indicator can pass on very interesting information. Of course, one can not derive any fundamental laws from this. The market is constantly changing, but I believe that this indicator can help you to make even more precise decisions. Likewise, the numbers certainly need to be adjusted in different market situations to get even more accurate information.

In concrete terms, this is a project and not a finished concept. Of course, the two indicators are already operational, but they still need to be modified and adapted. For that, we need the help of all.

That's exactly the advantage of a large community, I have now posted an idea and will publish the indicator with a detailed guide by tomorrow at the latest. Thereafter, they are all called upon to apply this indicator in different time units and with different settings themselves once and gain experience. Common we will certainly gain further insight and possibly even more concrete statements. I am pleased to implement this joint project with you and wish you a successful trading day today.

Hello dear traders,

In the last two blogs I have presented you the benefits of the two trend strength indicators, the application and a possible interpretation. In principle, it is an indicator that is displayed in the chart image and a histogram. Both have the task to output the same values.
The idea for this trend strength analysis I already had many years ago, when I started to trade only in the pure chart image of the Equilibrium. Since I did not have the programming skills, I put this project back. I focused, the following years, only on supply and demand. --- 帖子 #697 ---
Project number two

Hello dear subscriber,

I think there is a consensus that most of our traders are only small fish in the big shark tank of the forex market. The daily turnover in the Euro US Dollar is about $ 1.5 trillion. If you were to trade ten contracts in US dollars in one day, that would mean $ 1 million in sales. It's like putting $ 1 against a $ 1.5 million market. I think it soon becomes clear that we can not move anything in this market. In principle, there are only two ways to win, you move the market or you follows the big Player. In order to get involved, you have to recognize relatively quickly where the big players want to go. As most of us have already realized, this assessment is a ride on the volcano. This is also the reason that about 90% of dealers make a wrong assessment and therefore lose. The big players in the market not only earn more money but also have a much better market appreciation. Let's look at a concrete example of Goldman Sachs in the years 2011-2014.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

In these examples, I'm less concerned with showing the net gains in millions made by Goldman Sachs, albeit this scoring would be frightening enough. Much more interesting, however, is the ratio of the winner days to the loss days.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Of course, the loss days in 2015 were significantly higher than in the previous years, but let's take a closer look at the average values achieved in 2011-2015. 1,132 winning days are faced with 134 losing days. That means in nearly 90% of the time Goldmann Sachs is right with his market assessment. If you then compare the amount of losses with the levels of profits, the extent of the professional approach becomes clear. At least now you know against which professionals you act daily. We should have respect, but do not be afraid. But we need information about what these big players are going to do next.

The entire market has changed enormously as a result of the various dealers that appear in the market. It is not the big ones who eat the little ones, but the slow ones are eaten by the faster ones. The high-frequency traders have noticed this long ago and, with their way of acting, make it difficult for the big players in the market. 10 years ago, this trend started slowly and I had to think about how I can have a chance in the market to survive in the future. If your competitor drives a 400 HP Ford Mustang, you can not win a race even with the best and fastest racehorse against him. What to do if you can not afford a Ford Mustang? Get carried away by the big player, you will never be the first to finish, but the result is enough to make interesting profits. However, you need a good brake and a quick reaction to avoid total loss.

Over many years, I have developed 3 laws that I adhere to.

Indicators

Many years ago, I too, like many others, began to analyze the market using the standard indicators and it has often worked. The MACD and RSI were also a life companion for me, but how many times was the market overbought and still the price went up. An indicator does not care if the price goes up or down. It is trailing and less accurate than the price table. Many traders need security and believe the indicator tells them where the market is going.

The market influences the indicator and not the indicator the market.

My first step for this: delete all standard indicators and search for clues. I did not get any further with the market analysis, not because it is bad, but because it is not suitable for me. Supply, demand and equilibrium was finally the breakthrough for me. The road is tough, but it was the only way for me. That's why I opened this blog many years later. Today I am working with auxiliary indicators, which I pay attention to, but these do not decide on entering or exiting a trade. If I can not trust myself, how should I trust indicators?

The big big players do not work with standard indicators and they are not used for trading. The big players know, however, that the small players pay attention to the indicators. Especially here in focus are the Fibonacci lines. These are good entrances for the high-frequency traders to stop the small players.

Sometimes I have the feeling that the big players push the indicators forward in order to be able to take the money from the small trader even faster. They know exactly that many traders hope for a change at the 61 retracement. A good point to push many out of the market.

News

In 2016, Deutsche Bank and many currency experts estimated that the EURUSD would reach 0.95 by the end of 2017. It is always fun in the evening at NTV (German news channel) to learn why the DAX, gold or the EURUSD has risen or fallen. Of course, the economy in each country is important, but not for me. For me, how investors respond to the news is far more important.

It does not matter what news goes about the ticker. The market is moving because people and computers are pushing the BUY or SELL button. And why they will BUY or SELL? Because they have an idea. And this idea often has nothing to do with the economic data. Why goes the stock of Apple down, although Apple released a sensational quarterly balance sheet? Well, maybe because investors believe Apple will not be able to increase or maintain profits in the next quarter. However, we will never know.

Not the news, but market participants influence the market.

When the FED or the ECB are holding their meetings, I take a break and let the big boys play with each other. This is not my league, so I stay away from the market. These FED or ECB sessions can not be assessed with the Equilibrium, it goes up and down indiscriminately and after an hour the price is often where the big outbreak started. Gambling is not one of my peculiarities, I try to act only in situations in which I think I can assess the market. But I'm also often wrong.

Opinion

100% of all dealers have an opinion, but only 10% are right. But which traders are right? Bertrand Arthur William Russell an English philosopher, mathematician and logician coined the phrase in early 1900:

That's all the trouble: The stupid are so safe and the clever ones so full of doubt.

Self-reflection is the mature form of self-doubt. People who are self-reflective are always in question, but not to become anxious and insecure like self-doubters, but to strengthen themselves from within. The clever doubt. They question their views, but they do not question themselves. Reflection protects against stupidity. It testifies to greatness, to revise his opinion of yesterday.

Maybe that's just our problem, we doubt it, so we listen to those who are sure, and then what happens can anyone think. We have to have the ability to form our own opinion - even against the tide. This "idiosyncratic" attitude results from the motif of independence. Only a few people have such a capability.

Conclusion:

If we know that 90% of all private traders lose, there is an easy way to change that. Whenever you want to move up, you have to do exactly the opposite and act down. But our brains are not prepared for a course that shoots high, acting exactly in the opposite direction. The fear of losses is often greater than the prospect of profits. If a craftsman did only 50% of his work correctly, he would be unemployed quickly. A trader who is 50% correct, would quickly succeed with the right money management. We have learned to make few mistakes, but in action you have to make mistakes to win.

The big challenge of action is not to win, but to behave properly when you have losses.

Since the big players know exactly where the other traders' stops are, we should make it difficult for them. That's why I often act against the trend and stay where only a few traders are. In order to be successful you should act contrary to the mass and certainly not be predictable. In addition, a successful trader must be a perfect tracker to succeed in the marketplace. But which tracks are decisive and which tracks can I neglect? An answer to that is provided by the equilibrium within the supply and demand zones. Nevertheless, it does not matter which strategy you use for your actions, the main decision to enter into a trade should always come from your main strategy. In my case, that is supply and demand.

If you have a particular zone in mind, you need a medium-term and short-term confirmation that this particular zone is relevant. I have already shown you a way of confirming the medium term, the trend strength within certain time units. This will provide you with basic information about a possible trend direction. Now it's about the short-term confirmation that could trigger my main decision. We should note here that the confirmations usually only take a few seconds. If you wait too long, the chance is over faster than you can imagine. Especially as Countertrend Scalper you have to make a decision within a few seconds and can not wait too long for confirmations. Every trader has his own individual strategy and procedure here. Let's take a look at different options that help a dealer make decisions.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

When you first see the volume profile, order flow, footprint charts, or DOM orderbook as a CFD Forex trader, you think that these views of the market are the solution to all problems. Often we get a false truth in advertising these modules. Of course it's interesting to look inside a candle and see how many buy and sell orders have taken place within a certain price level and how big the volume was. This information is of no use to them to predict a future price development. When I was confronted with these techniques for the first time, I also thought that it was the solution to wealth. Of course, a trader gets a lot of information about what's happening in the market right now, but I get the same information with the candles. However, it is much harder to decipher this information from the candles.

Even a DOM order book does not do you any good, here are manipulations on the agenda. Large orders that are at a certain price level are erased shortly before reaching this price level and massively traded in the other direction. Another point is that we trade in interbank trading through a broker who passes on the prices. If I want to work with a Future Oderbook, of course I have different price than in CFD trading. It certainly looks nicer and more professional, whether it's actually an advantage is always at the discretion of the individual trader.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Let's take a look at the main indicator in CFD trading: the candles. There are different forms of presentation of prices. In addition to the Bar Chart and the Candle Chart, Heikin Ashi also has a smoothed candlestick display or the Renko, which is time-independent. Each form of presentation finds its followers and thus an authorization to exist in the market. The most widely used form of candlestick is the Candle Chart, and let's take a closer look.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Here you can see a bullish candle (close is above the open) and a bearish candle (open is above the close). For the bullish candle, the upper shadow ranges from close to high and the lower shadow from open to low. In the bearish candle, the upper shadow ranges from the open to the high and the lower shadow from the close to the low. The candle body shows the essential course within the candle from open to close. The candle is usually displayed in solid color or with gray shadows. This presentation is actually wrong for me, so you see in this image the correct form of representation. In the Bullish Candle, the upper shadow is red, while in the bearish candle the lower shadow is green. Why is this presentation more logical for me?

A candle displays the past price movements for a specific time unit. There are 4 crucial points open, close, high and low. Take the example of the bullish candle. From the open the course is running low, at this moment the candle body is red. Then the course goes back to the Open. The shadow is green, that's correct. The course is going to high, that means from the open to the high we have a green candle body. Then the course goes back to the close. Now the upper shadow must be colored red, because at the time of the close the price has gone from high to close. If you look at the finished candle, the bears at the top wick and the bulls at the bottom wick have the last word. The candle is now complete and past. In order to correctly display this past, the lower shadow should always be green and the upper shaddow always red.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

If you see the left candle in a chart image, you can never tell exactly how the price within that candle has moved. It may well be that the course first runs from the open to the low, or from the open directly to the high. In case B we see a strong downward trend, which was immediately intercepted. In that case, one might be more cautious as to whether the course will not make such a strong setback again.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

A similar situation, but in the bearish area. Not uncommon that in spite of a bearish candle, the course is pushed up sharply in the short term. Basically, it is very difficult for me to predict a further course from candle pictures. That's why I basically do not pay attention to doji or other candle pictures.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

The next step I took was to eliminate the shadows and color them properly. With the bullish candle and bearish candle, there is no reference to the open, but the close can also be seen from the last candle and draw conclusions from it. Nevertheless, you can quickly cast the close on your chart image, if you need this information. The advantage of this view, you can see at a glance how strong the bulls and the bears were at the end of the candle. You can really see how the bears and the bulls are fighting with each other and can identify trends before that. Gaps are therefore very difficult or even impossible to localize, but gaps can not be used to derive reliable conclusions about future price developments. You realize that less information can be processed with this new candle view and less can sometimes be more. One point was crucial for me, I wanted a real price history, not smoothed, not time-independent like the Renko but with less information to capture the situation faster.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Here is a concrete example of how the chart looks in H1. In addition, the trend strength indicator was used by me, which gives me more information. You can see very well that trend reversals announce early, through the respective pullback within a candle. The type of candle representation I called Bionic Chart. Bionics (also biomimicry, biomimetic or biomimetic) deals with the transfer of phenomena of nature to technology. A well-known example of this is Leonardo da Vinci's idea of transferring bird flight to flying machines. An example from modern life is the velcro-inspired velcro, or think of dragonflies and helicopters. Also, the lotus effect has been brought from nature into our lives, which discs clean themselves, because no dirt sticks.

Bionics is based on the assumption that living nature, through its evolutionary course, develops optimized structures and processes from which humans can learn. The earth is nearly 4.5 billion years old and during this time nature has developed incredible things that benefit man already today. But we have not realized most things yet. Applying these 4.5 billion old processes to today's stock exchange (which is only 500 years old) or the forex market will bring significant benefits. Nevertheless, these processes only become an advantage if used and applied correctly. This brings a short lead to the point where everyone benefits from this. Maybe they have a small lead with this chart. At the latest when everyone uses this information, the market will be balanced again. But I have some more ideas ...

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

At first glance, they will not see a big difference with the Bionic Chart compared to the other chart models. The difference is in the detail. And we will deal with these details in concrete terms. The result is clear and fascinating at the same time. To illustrate the benefits of the Bionic Chart, I have to make some videos. Unfortunately this takes a few more days, so I ask for leniency and patience. Since we are still working on the first project, I am pleased about their further feedback.

I wish you a successful trading day

best regards

Update smZigZag-Bionics and smZigZag-Bionics Osc

Hello dear subscribers,

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

While our second project has already started, we are continuing to work on our first project. Both indicators of the first project have now been extended and should now run optimally. Let's look at the individual extensions.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

With the smZigZag-Bionics_v3.3 you are now able to assign individual colors to the lines as well as the numbers underneath, which, as you know, show the average Pip per Candle within a range. Now you can hide bullish / bearish numbers or lines and make only upward or downward trends visible. These qualities are needed for our second project. This indicator is very flexible so that you can use it as a pure ZigZag Color in case of doubt.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

In addition, the smZigZagOsc_1.3 has been extended. It is now also possible to display only bearish lows or bullish highs. In addition, the highs / lows can be connected to a line. We can also use these properties very well in our second project.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

In this example I once hidden the bars. Thus, only the bearish low points and the bullish high points are connected. For this view, I had no time to make a concrete evaluation. I am convinced that we will make some interesting discoveries here.

The indicators would have to be ready so far now it is up to us to move forward in this project. That's why I'm still looking forward to your discoveries and contributions in the first project. The second project seamlessly follows the first project and supports the findings of the trend.

To summarize this once again:

The main decision to trade is always based on your personal strategy. That could be Fibonacci, or the Moving Average in my case it is demand and supply.

Our project 1 serves only to determine a possible medium-term trend direction with a higher probability.

Our project 2 serves only to determine a possible short-term trend direction with a higher probability.

Example:

A trend is moving up and in my analysis, I have identified a resistance line. Now I compare my analysis with my project 1. This will tell me if it could be a sustainable trend or a pullback. Once the course reaches my drawn resistance level, I am able to make a very short-term trading decision with our Project 2.

However, the main decision is always based on my personal strategy of supply or demand. Only from Strategy 1 or Strategy 2 alone would I never make a trading decision. Therefore, the indicators I have developed are purely supportive indicators.

I have aligned these support indicators with my demand and supply principle in order to make even more accurate trading decisions. Since I do not act according to other strategies, I can not assess to what extent these support indicators are useful and relevant for you.

I wish you much success today

best regards

Hello pakeha,

First of all, welcome to our blog and thank you for your interest. To answer your question, I draw my supply and demand zones exclusively by hand, based on the current price trend. I tried to show that with a video. I used a 5 sec chart for two reasons. First, 200 candles were drawn in 10 minutes, the 1 minute chart would have taken too long and second, to prove that it was not a fake video. (A 5 Sec chart history can not be retroactively rotated, no tick data will be provided.)

There is no indicator of how I act because the criteria are constantly changing based on the current price trend. We have to keep in mind that the price is a random buy and sell order. I can only estimate potential resets of the course on the basis of several years of experience and my type of supply and demand. In the video, as the price went down, I saw another resistance zone signifi- cantly weaker than the overlying resistance zone. This zone was not started, so I was wrong here. Exactly I could not draw the resistance zones, however the assumptions were approximately correct. Nevertheless, I am also mistaken in certain situations, as a course can not be foreseen.

The closer I get to the course, the better I can assess a possible course. That's why I developed a new chart image for me to make even faster decisions.

I tried to explain in detail the criteria of the Equilibrium with supply and demand zones in this blog. I ask for leniency, I have been dealing with Equilibrium for a very long time and from my point of view, it is not easy to explain and implement. If you have analyzed some 10,000 hours of candles, you will also have your own view of the market. I do not mean to say that my point of view is right or logical, it's just different and I get along well with it.

I work with indicators, but they do not decide on the entry or exit of my actions. In the next few days I will explain and upload the Bionic Chart in detail, this is our 2nd project. The 3rd project is about the auxiliary indicators that provide me with important information about trading.

I would like to invite you to participate and hope to have helped you a little.

I wish you a nice evening.

Hi Michael,
Many thanks for your post and your kind comments, and Happy New Year to you also.
In MT4 I think you can change the outline color and the fill color of the candle, rather than the entire body and the entire wick/shadow. But I could be wrong, there might be ways in the latest MT4 builds that I'm unaware of.
If I understand correctly, you're effectively asking for the lower shadow on every candle to be boxed green, and the upper shadow of every candle to be boxed red. This amounts to a change in which the OHLC data is being presented, as opposed to a change to the data itself. I think it's possible to create synthetic candles by plotting truncated histograms in the main chart, but I'm not sure. It's been a while since I looked at anything like this.
I'm not sure how this change of presentation would provide an advantage to the retail trader, but then I've not really spent any time researching this kind of approach. If you've read my recent posts you'll know that my own approach uses a lot of FA rather than purely chart-based analysis. Of course I understand that different traders find certain types of chart-based 'road maps' helpful as a visual aid. Each trader must ultimately find an overall approach that he is personally comfortable with.
Although I'm happy to continue sharing some of the indicators and EAs that I write for my own use, I'm sorry, but I'm no longer undertaking programming requests. I posted a list of possible alternatives in the 'MT4 programming' section here. I hope that you can find a way of achieving what you're looking for.

Finally, I would like to show the form of presentation as a candle chart, as it would be logical. Normally, the wicks are colored in the respective candle color or in gray. Now, one could say that a wick is a so-called equilibrium. Because as the course has gone up, so has the run down again. In principle, this theory would be correct, but at the end of the candle the course went down. Once a candle is finished, it should show the past price history correctly. If a course has gone up and then gone the same way down again, we have here at the end of a bearish trend. This would make all the upper wicks red and all the lower wicks green. However, this is just a presentation options that you have in addition to the bionic chart.

Hello dear traders,

Among other things, they also act in the area of demand and supply and were thus able to quickly classify the project. They were absolutely excited and could not understand that I pass this project on free of charge to everyone. My answer: "Quid pro quo" has astonished her.

"Quid pro quo" is similar to "manus manum lavat" ("One hand washes the other") or ("I give, you give"). In the last 9 months at Forex Factory, I've met a lot of unselfish people sharing their knowledge with each other every day. If everyone kept their knowledge to themselves, there would be no progress. In addition, I earn my money by trading rather than selling indicators or coaching. They both understood this attitude, and one of them asked me: If everyone is using your system, are not you worried that your indicators will not work as you expect?

No, I answered. First, many traders will not use this indicator because it is too much effort to deal with it, and second, the human being who makes the trading decisions. I am not afraid that anyone will take anything from me, because as a counter-trend scalper, I trade where   only a few dealers act. "Quid pro quo" Let's take a look at the benefits: There will be some traders who see an advantage in the way they trade and they will look into these indicators. This results in aspects and possibilities that no one has ever thought of. Alone, I would never be able to do so, because if 100 people work with these indicators and share their experiences, we will reach our goal 100 times faster than I would have been able to do alone. And nowadays, time is more valuable than money. Can we also work with the indicators, my two trader friends asked me. "Quid pro quo" I answered: "How much are you willing to pay for it?" The program is older, but works very well. The diagram is executed offline. Of course, once they close the screen, the data will no longer be processed. When you open the screen again, the course will continue at the current location. Of course, if you work in the 5 seconds chart, it will take some time to get enough information together. Of course, you can make different settings every second. For the indicator there is a detailed description, although older, however, I think that they will manage it.

If you have both charts running, please note that you are loading the bionic chart into the offline chart, otherwise it will not work. The M1 chart in which you drew the Flexichart indicator must not be closed. If they then make the same settings as in my picture, nothing should go wrong. In the end, you just have to align the two seconds charts on one screen and you're ready to go.

Important

Please note that the Flexichart indicator will only work when current tick data is delivered. So from Sunday evening to Friday evening.

You should watch these two charts very closely at the beginning and draw their conclusions. This gives you incredibly interesting information, especially in the short term. --- 帖子 #720 ---
Different than others

Hello dear trader,

Supply zones and demand zones always work on the same principle in different time units.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

At point A they see the formation of an Equilibrium, then the price goes down sharply. This will tell you how strong this supply zone is. As soon as the price falls into a demand zone, an equilibrium arises again, ie a sideways trend. After the price penetrated somewhat deeper into the demand zone, finally a strong upward trend developed. Only when the price at point C came back into this strong supply zone, he turned off and went down sharply. Point B is also a supply zone which was not strong enough to stop the uptrend.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Let's look at a second example. We see again an equilibrium and then a strong supply market that catapults the price from point A downwards. It creates a great equilibrium and after the price has penetrated slightly deeper into the demand zone, the upward trend began. Only when the course had arrived at point C and penetrated into this strong supply zone, he was strongly dismissed down. Point B is also an offer zone but could not push the price down.

The first chart is a weekly chart in EURUSD on the second chart is a 5 minute chart today.

They recognize the importance of identifying demand zones or supply zones. This identification of the zones is always a challenge, but we get here with the new trend strength indicator some clues that can help us. The background of these three projects is to find these important supply zones or demand zones faster and more effectively. Decisive here are always the zones from which a course goes strong high  or strong low.

Pay attention to these strong zones and try to draw them in your chart. Start by researching why a certain course went up or down. This gives you a first feel for what is happening in the market right now. Then you can draw these zones in their current price history and see if they hit the exact zones. Whether the zones were right or wrong, then you should analyze what mistakes they made and what things they overlooked.

As you know, the time-definite candles (M1, M5 ....) Are created by chance from a random course. If you're lucky, you'll see a Doji announcing a turnaround, but due to the candlelight, it's a coincidence and you should not rely on it. You may already have noticed that extreme course changes take place at full hours or half hours. Although the bionik chart allows for a bit more accurate views despite random candle formation one should try to change the time content in order to avoid as many full or half hours as possible. Odd time units are optimal.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Since for me a time unit for trading between 5 and 10 minutes is optimal I once compared the minutes between 6 minutes and 9 minutes. How often is a candle displayed within 24 hours at exactly the full or half hour?

When setting 6 minutes starting at 0:00 am, 24 candles end at the hour and 24 candles at half hour.

At the setting of 8 minutes 12 candles end on the hour and 0 candles at half hour.

At a setting of 9 minutes, 8 candles end at the hour and 8 candles at half hour.

At a setting of 7 minutes, 3 candles end at the full hour and 4 candles at half hour.

Thus, the setting of 7 minutes for me would be the most optimal to optimize the randomness of candle formation something.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Now I have used the trend strength indicator and compared a current M5 chart with a current M7 chart. While I only got strong pullback identification in the M5 chart, M7 Chart already had 3 pullback identifications. It turns out, therefore, that a small change in time, in which the candles are formed, can give rise to some advantages. The pricing is exactly the same, the candle formation was only slightly changed by the time unit.

Unlike others, often the right way can be.

I wish you a successful day

best regards

Recognize trend consequences

Hello dear Subsciber,

Once in the monthly chart from January 1971 to today, I divided the EURUSD into a demand market and a supply market. In addition, I examined the trend strength of the individual zones with the bionic trend indicator.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

The green bars represent the demand market while the red bars represent the supply market. The uptrend No. 1 was very sustainable and strong. The number 56.6 means that each candle was on average 56.6 pip. After that, there was a relatively short supply market in No. 2, which pushed the price almost back down. The average candle size here was 95.5 pip. Although the price was down sharply, the trend was not sustainable enough.

The wider a beam, the more sustainable the trend. In this picture you can see very well that the first two uptrends have been very strong and sustainable. The two subsequent downtrends, however, were less sustainable, but very strong. The third uptrend was less sustainable than the two uptrends ahead. But the last downtrend was the most sustainable so far. Of course you have to keep in mind that a course often goes down faster than up. Nevertheless, prices have risen overall and the uptrend has been more sustainable than the downtrend. From 1971 to today, the price has risen by 6,100 pip. One dollar would have turned $ 61,000 today, equivalent to a return of 26.4% per annum.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

The bionic trend strength indicator shows us, the smaller the number the weaker but more sustainable the trend and the larger the number the stronger but less sustainable the trend. That is, larger numbers often indicate a pullback. The first two uptrends were sustainable and followed by a short pullback. Now the downtrend is more sustainable than the uptrend for the first time. However, one can say that the downtrend has weakened and the uptrend has become stronger. If the trend continues and the downtrend remains more sustainable than the uptrend, it could go much further down.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Now I've refined the setting a bit to get an accurate overview. The width of the bars makes it easy to identify a sustainable trend and a pullback. I divided the downtrend and uptrend into strong and weak respectively. In addition, there is a strong and a weak pullback. The strength or weakness of each trend does not relate to price appreciation but to the sustainability of the trend. The longer a trend runs, the more sustainable it is, as can be seen by the width of a bar. Let's take a look at whether this graphic makes it possible to identify long-term reversals.

Trend1

In 1971 it started with a strong uptrend followed by a weak pullback, followed by a weak upward trend. The weak pullback hinted that there could now be a stronger uptrend. After the strong uptrend there was a strong downward trend. Here you could not find a conclusion on a trend reversal, however, if you look at the course within the blue circle once, you could draw conclusions from it.

Trend2

After a strong downtrend followed by a weak pullback, then the downtrends were significantly weaker which has given an indication of a possible trend reversal.

Trend 3

It followed a strong upward trend, which was not quite so sustainable. It was followed by a relatively strong pullback. From then on the uptrends became much weaker and with the blue arrow they can see very well that a strong pullback took place. This pullback was more sustainable than the uptrend ahead. That gave an indication that there could soon be a turnaround.

Trend 4

There followed a strong downtrend and a strong pullback. The pullback was stronger than the last uptrend ahead. This was followed by a strong downward trend. The turnaround was not correct, but you could guess, as the second downtrend was less sustainable than the first downtrend.

Trend 5

This was followed by a strong and sustained upward trend. The pullback was relatively weak and the result was another relatively strong uptrend but weaker than the first uptrend.

Trend 6

The downtrend began with a very weak trend followed by a very strong pullback. This was followed by two more weak downtrends and two more strong pullbacks. In principle, this is a big equilibrium before the price went down. That was an indication that the bulls were not quite satisfied yet. For this reason, this downward trend is the most sustainable in the EURUSD to date. The blue arrow shows a strong pullback that took place within an equilibrium.

Trend 7

In relation to the other uptrends, the last upward trend of € 1.03 is the weakest so far. However, he is stronger than the last five downtrends. You can clearly see that the volatility has decreased significantly in recent years. Within a trend, the trend reversals have increased significantly. This is an indication that the trade has become much difficult, especially the high-frequency traders have contributed a lot.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

The sustainability of the upward trend has increased in the last three trend sequences. This is particularly interesting in the smaller time units, so you can make more short-term statements.

Overall, the uptrends have been more sustainable than the downtrend so far. From 574 months we were 347 months up and 227 months down. That means 40% down and 60% up.

You see that it's not just price increases that matter, but the sustainability of a trend. From this it is also possible to derive conclusions about future trend movements.

I wish you a successful week

best regards

Bionic Dashboard Installation

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Hello dear subscribers,

Finally the time has come and it was very time-consuming to create the dashboard so that you have as little work as possible with it and at the same time a quick sense of achievement. This dashboard was populated with different indicators created by great programmers and dealers. In addition I will write in the next contributions still a lot. Thank you very much for this great and professional work.

First, unpack the zip file. So nothing goes wrong creating a new Metatrader MT4. Of course you can also paste the files into your existing Metatrader MT4. As a precaution, back up your most important templates.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Open the data folder in your Metatrader. In the Profiles folder, insert the Bionic "Dashboard with Dollar Index" and the "Bionic Dashboard Standard". In your indicators folder you insert unpacked 21 indicators. Then close the Metatrader and start it again.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Now open the profile: "Bionic Dashboard Standard". This can be found under Profiles. Your chart will probably look similar to my photo now. If there are some missing lines in the chart image at the top left, just set the time unit to 5 minutes and then back to 1 minute. After that, the lines would have to be complete.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Next we want to activate the 4 empty windows of the MAdash indicator. There are two options. Click in one of the windows and open the indicator MADash and press on edit. After that, the window would have to rise as in the picture. Then only on o. K. Press to activate the indicator. If that does not work, open a new chart window and load the MADash indicator into it. Then the window will open on o. K. Press and indicator will be activated.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Next, load the profile: "Bionic Dashboard with Dollar Index". To work with this profile you need the US Dollar Index from your broker. Open the market overview, with a right click you indicate that you want to display all symbols. Once you've found the Dollar Index, just drag it into the bottom window and the indicator works.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Now open the indicator: 1overlaychart_line. There you enter the correct name for the US dollar index, which is given by your broker. Then press Color and o. K. Now, a red line should appear next to a green line in your chart. If not, change the color and press o. K again. after that, everything should work for them.

If you do not have a dollar index, you can re-enable the first profile (Bionic Dashboard Standard), so you can work just as well.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Now her chart is almost done. The picture shows a series of letters. If you now click through these letters from A to Z on the respective pictures, your chart would have to look like mine.

Please note the following: If you make a change within your chart, this is automatically saved in the profile. Therefore, save the original profiles and if necessary upload them again to the Metatrader.

Since the market is still running for about 5 hours today, I have already uploaded the indicators and the installation instructions in advance. This allows you to try the chart before. I will finish the explanation of the individual indicators in the next few days.

Take another look at the video from post 737.

I would like to remind you once again that these are purely auxiliary indicators. This dashboard will not give you entry or exit signals. But you get important trend signals that support you in daily trading.

I wish you the best of luck if you have any questions, I'm happy to help. If you are satisfied, I would be very happy to receive your feedback.

best regards

Explanation to the bionic dashboard

Hello dear traders,

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

At the beginning of the year I have already published a dashboard and as you can see, that has already changed a lot. This is simply because there are indicators or signals that just work better for me. This does not mean that the indicators are bad, it just means there are indicators that give me the signals more clearly. As you know, the only constant is the alteration. Two-thirds of the indicators have been preserved, an essential aspect was the news indicator. Since news for me are not relevant at all, it could be replaced. In addition, some indicators were placed more efficiently.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Essentially, there are four windows for me that deliver decisive signals. Below, I will discuss these four windows individually.

Inserted Video

Here is the video again:

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

In the first window we have four ads. In the first two windows we each have a currency strength indicator. While the first bearish indicator indicates a medium-term bias, I get short-term signals from the second currency strength indicator.

1. CCFp Indicator, Developer: SemSemFX, Interesting currency strength gauge

2. + RS_Group EUR & USD indicator, Developer: unknown, Very interesting strength indicator that reacts faster than the price chart. Here, the EUR was currently compared with the dollar.

3. CFP indicator, Developer: SemSemFX, An indicator that gives almost the result of the euro and dollar strength.

4. smZigZagbionicsOsc, Developer: Bionics, Swingman, new treadmill dosimeter,

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

In my second overview window the following indicators are included.

The green line is the EURUSD shown as a line chart. The red line is the mirrored dollar index, as it usually behaves contrary to the euro US dollar. In addition, my trend strength indicator was used.

1. Overlay Chart Indicator, Developer: S.B.T. ,This indicator works only if your broker provides you the dollar index. He compares the EURUSD with the dollar index in the 1M chart. You may need to change the name of the Dollar Index as this varies from broker to broker.

2. smZigZag-Bionics, Developer: Bionics, Swingman, new threshold strength indicator,

Here you can see the essential dates that are coming up in the EURUSD. The important dates appear in red and the unimportant dates in yellow. I prefer yellow and orange appointments, as I often do not work on red dates.

3. News Calendar Indicator, Developer: eucild high impact FF member, Important dates that can affect my currency pair are displayed here from Forex Factory. Many settings are possible.

Here is an interesting currency strength indicator that shows the changes with arrows. There is already a newer indicator yes also reacts faster, but I like the display of the old indicator better.

4. CM Strength Indicator, Developer: palpite high impact FF Member, An interesting indicator about the strongest currencies.

Next to it is a clock that you can set individually.

5. Time indicator, Developer: FX Automated,

The display below shows me the average pip number within a certain time sequence. It is always easy to see the current volatility.

6. Average candle, Developer: cja high impact Member FF, The average candle time can be set individually here. I work here with 3 averages 900/30/1.

7. In addition to the important dates you will see three lines a green red and white.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

In principle, this is a 5 minute chart with three moving averages. An exponential MA with the setting 9 in the 5 minute chart (white line), a simple MA 9 from the H1 and a simple MA 38 also from the H1. This is just an overview of the trend consequences for me. If the red line is above the green line = downtrend. If the green line is above the red line = uptrend. The white line shows a faster change.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Here you see twice an M1 Bionic Chart, which is divided into bullish and bearish candles. In addition, the density indicator has been added. In Post 283 I have written a detailed report about it.

https://www.forexfactory.com/showthr...6#post10777396

Now the indicator has been modified and divided into bullish and bearish strength. The indicator can be downloaded at the end of the blog.

1. smBionicChart-Histogram_v1.ex4, Developer: Bionics, Swingman, completely new chart view,

2. smZigZag-Bionics, Developer: Bionics, Swingman, new threshold strength indicator,

3. Density_Histogram_Red_Green, Developer: palpate high impact Member FF, idea: Bionics, Thank you very much, palpite,

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

The following overview window is structured so that I have arranged the bullish segments in the upper area and the bearish segments in the lower area.

The left overview panel is the decisive one for me. In the upper part the euro is compared with all the major currency pairs while the bottom the dollar is compared with all the major currency pairs. If the upper part is green and the lower part is red we have an uptrend if the upper part is red and the lower part is green we have a downtrend. Green means strength, red means weakness in the respective currency. Please note that this is only the 1 minute chart, which is a very short term range.

1. MADdash indicator, Developer: honestknave high impact member FF, A multi timeframe dashboard looking at price. Listed are 17 ads from 1-17. Here the size can be changed individually. Green means Euro strength, red means Dollar strength. Timeframes from left: 1M, 5M, 15M, 30M and 1H.

Next to it are two candles in the M1 once from the EURUSD and once from the Dollar Index.

2. Chart Indicator, Developer: fxcoder, that was linked to the dollar index

Next to it are two more strength ads in Euro and Dollar.

3. Cruscotto indicator EUR and Dollar, Developer: Andrea Salvatore, Interesting strength indicator of time units in the EUR

In the middle is the Candle Strength indicator for all time units. The Candle Strength indicator displays the distance between the open and close as a percentage of the total height of the candle.

4. Candle Strength indicator, Developer: Hanover high impact member FF, Hanover has adjusted the indicator for me, I used the following time units: 1M, 5M, 15M, 30M, 1H, 4H, D, W1, MN

6. Spead_5Digit, Developer: Andrij Moraru,

7. S-KG Buyer Seller indicator, Developer: saronko high impact Member FF, Thanks to Kang_Gun source code and FerruFx advice, The indicator, reacting quickly to price change. In addition, a current price indicator and the spread was incorporated.

At this point I would like to thank all programmers who have programmed these great tools.

Of course there is also a small hook in this great overview. The more information I get, the harder it gets to keep track. However, like everything in life, this is a matter of training. Of course, you can set up the dashboard at any time to suit your individual situation. As you've noticed, my dashboard changes regularly as I notice there are other signals that give me faster information.

This dashboard gives me another confirmation once I have already made a decision to enter a trade. So you should only use it for support. But it is extremely well suited for this and delivers signals quickly and efficiently. However, you have to work with it for a while to get used to it and to handle it. Remove the indicators that do not help you. I am convinced that one or the other tool will certainly help you.

The dashboard in Post 739 was built so that you can easily install it. The optimal screen size is 1920 x 1080, otherwise you will need to customize the dashboard.

I wish you much joy and success with your dashboard and I am pleased about your feedback.

Post 500: How do I find the important turning points?

Hello dear traders,

This is my 500th contribution in this forum and thus a small anniversary. I came here to help other traders and get help as well. If you read my first article and compare it with the last article, you will find that a significant development has taken place. What has remained is my system of supply and demand. I have developed it together with you so far that it is getting easier.

At this point I would like to express once again my heartfelt thanks, because all projects would not have been possible without the help of you. One hand washes the other, we say in germany.

That's why I put together a very special article for you today.

Every trader wants an ad that always tells him exactly when a trend is going up or down. The area of supply and demand has always given me very reliable information about the trend consequences, but I often lacked crucial information that I did not recognize quickly enough.

The creation of the Bionic Chart and the Bionic Trend Strength Indicator had a very definite reason. The goal was to be able to recognize the trend reverses more precisely with the help of demand and supply. I clearly succeeded in achieving this goal and today I would like to show you a concrete example of this.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Here is a D1 chart from the EURUSD from April 2017 to October 2018. Using the smBionic-ZigZag indicator (setting: 8/2/4), I once worked out and colored the strongest uptrend and downtrend. It can be seen here that Trend B, C & D were the strongest in this period. The Bionic Chart I need to make the candles monochrome without wick. This clearly shows the strong uptrend or downtrend in the daily chart.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Next, within these strong trends, I picked the strongest day candles and drew a resistance line out of them. In total, this resulted in four resistance lines from number one to number four. Sure, I could have drawn more, but to illustrate the whole thing I leave it at these four resistance levels. After drawing the resistance line number 4 you can see how the course within these lines behaved afterwards. This aspect is quite interesting.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Now, at point 5, another resistance line has been added, you can see that after the line was drawn, the course did not manage to cross that line.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Now it's time to determine the concrete resistance line within the drawn resistance lines. For me it is clear that a crucial resistance within the strongest candle is in the strongest trend. This strong candle is so strong because it breaks through a very strong resistance. We have to find this resistance. A line of resistance is characterized by the fact that a course of her strong upward and / or downward runs. From the resistance line A, the price went up sharply. The course, which went up below point A, bounced off this line exactly. That's why I drew this line and as you can see, the course was bounced right there with the yellow arrow and went back up.

At point C we see the next strong candle within a very strong trend. It was relatively easy to draw the resistance line because there was a small downtrend in front of the candle that was the deciding factor. If we look at how the course reacts with the blue arrows on it, we realize that it is a strong resistance.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Here you can see again the confirmation for the point A. We scroll back to November 2016. We can see here how the course from the point A runs very strong down. After the course ran back to this line, he was again briefly dismissed and then went up with an extreme strength. This strong candle thus proves that it must be a very strong resistance.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Following the same principle, I have drawn the resistance line B. The upper line I would have had to pull up a bit to have some air. This line was for me the decisive turning point for a further upward trend in the EURUSD. The resistance zones D, E & F come from the past. Let's take a closer look at where they came from and how they came about.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

To do that, we have to go back to October 2014, where we identified two very strong downtrends. From point F, the strong downtrend began and ran down. At point E you will see a gap of 50 pip in the yellow circle. The 50 pip are not the deciding factor, but they still represent a resistance for me. Below that you will find another gap, which also had significant effects, but I did not want to go into that for reasons of efficiency. Shortly before the point D, an equilibrium is created, the course goes into zone D and is strongly rejected there. After that, the price goes down very sharply. At the blue arrow you can see how the course is strongly turned down. If you go back to the previous slide, you will see how the individual zones developed. We now have six resistance levels from A to F. Now let's look into the past and see how the course reacted.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Here you can see how the course reacted to resistance line E and F.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Again, you can see that the individual resistance lines are working. It's not about the price bouncing off this resistance line, it's about the price going up or down sharply from that resistance line. Often this resistance is broken several times until the price breaks up or down.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Again, you can see very well that the resistance lines are in zones that appear again and again, to which the course reacts. Of course it can also be a coincidence but I do not believe it, because a coincidence happens by accident but the lines always work. These lines I have drawn are in the daily chart and show me a medium term trend. Of course, I can do this in every unit of time.

I can recommend four time units.

The weekly chart for the long-term trend. The daily chart for the medium term trend. The H4 / H1 chart for the short-term trend and the M15 / M5 for the ultra short-term trend.

Work your way down from the high time units. Try it yourself and start to identify the trends. This approach can be well combined with their system. After all, it's all about recognizing reversals early.

I hope you enjoy trying it out and looking forward to your feedback.

For project number 3 I will post more information in the next few days.

I wish you a successful trading week

best regards
