Experience with the new trading approach

Hello dear pakeha, hello dear subscribers,

First of all thank you for your encouragement and your question. You are right that there are different ways to find S / R zones again. My basic and first approach was to find zones in which the price goes directly into the turnaround. Your point C is the best example. However, there are situations where a course is in equilibrium for a long time and then it is crucial to determine these two zones where the course is moving.

Let's look at a concrete example. On October 19, 2018 at 12:00 CET, I posted the following:

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

We are back at a point where the course has been before and maybe we can now see a small uptrend again. However, if I go a little into the past and look at the supply zones and demand zones, this results in a slightly different picture. The course may need to return to the 1.133736 -1.13641 zone to get the buyers back on track. Should the price once again start a strong downtrend, that does not mean that the price ends exactly on my red resistance line. Within the red resistance line, in my view, a strong uptrend could arise. These are of course pure forecasts, it is important to observe the course in the smaller time units. The price still seems to have strong bearish pressure.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Here we see the point A and the point B. At first glance, it looks like a double top and the assumption is obvious that the course now continues to run upwards. Exactly at point B, I gave my assessment. As I said, all assessments are basically just forecasts, because no one can know exactly what happens before. Let's go into the 5 minute chart.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Here you can clearly see that the course as well as predicted runs around the line. Perhaps the price could start from this line another upward trend. It was interesting that I could find here a stronger future Equilibrium. Maybe it was just luck.

Due to the new approach of the Bionic zigzag trend strength indicator, indirect new candles are formed, which are different in width. This creates new zones that we are currently analyzing. This type of zoning was not there before because there was no such indicator.

Therefore, I can not say too much about the new destination of these zones. For me personally, it was all about optimizing the S / R zone determinations. How far that works with the new indicators will show the time. Basically, it is interesting to first realize that it works.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

When analyzing when the trend reversal direction 1.28 takes place I noticed the following.

The upwards trend from December 2016 from 1.03 to 1.255 took place in different trend sequences and strengths. The strongest trend sequence between 1.03-1.20 can be seen at point 1. Within the blue square I have drawn two resistance lines. It is very nice to see how the course at point A reacted to the upper resistance line. However, this has only brought the course to point B. Thus, the red strong zone could not be broken again. The course was strongly dismissed and ran to the point C.

The zone in which the square was drawn is a very strong demand zone. The zone 1,118 would be for me the deepest zone in which the course could run. As we are still in an uptrend, this drawn zone for me is the end of the pullback of 1.255.

Should the price move strongly down from my defined zone 1.133736 -1.13641, two more zones could be considered.

1. The course goes slightly below the zone A from then upwards (arrow Y)

2. The course runs slightly into zone D then upwards (arrow Z)

Due to the price development, it is currently very difficult for me to determine the exact turning point. Here you can only observe the price course and make his decisions in smaller time units.

This type of trade is very demanding, as it is done without great aids. Every little movement has to be taken into account. The same motion sequences hardly ever occur in practice. Exactly, that makes this trade so difficult, but also so effective. That's why I share this idea with everyone, because everyone is called to make their experiences and share them with everyone. This will help us move faster. In the different trend sequences there are HH, HL, LH and LL. The goal is to be able to better determine the HH and the LL in the future. Knowing the trend order I'm in is making trading easier.

I would be very happy if many Subscribers participate in it, because with it we all faster together successfully. The key is independence. Nobody can take away what you are learning. Once you've mastered that, you can log in to any chart image and know what's going to happen next. This allows you to draw zones, wait for the course to enter this zone, and then begin trading.

Here's an example.

On January 29, 2018, I posted a forecast in the EURCHF.

https://www.forexfactory.com/showthr...7#post10719117

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

The course has still not made it into the POC zone after 950 days. Now we are nearing a decisive phase. I think we will reach the zone relatively quickly. And then? Now I recommend you to watch this zone as you enter the course. As it seems, the zone could push down the course and give us some good shorts.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

It was not until April 18, 2018, just under three months later, that the EURCHF price has come to these zones. You would have had to work with a stop of 22 pip. So far, the price has gone down 820 pip. As you can see, you can also track long-term trading approaches that are very interesting in terms of the risk-reward ratio. With this type of trading, you can plan interesting trades on a long-term basis and only trade when it really pays off.

Of course we can also be wrong, because after all, we are human and we are often mistaken. But there are stops that minimize our risk significantly.

A decisive advantage of this new S / R zone determination. This allows me to identify sustainable trends. These sustainable trends are the deciding factor because the fast trends are often just pullbacks without sustainability. This approach greatly reduces loss trades and improves my Moneymanagement.

I hope I could give an answer to the question and I am glad that so many are taking part in this challenge.

best regards

Trust yourself the most

Hello dear subscribers,

If you are still relatively new to the Forex market or have not yet found your right system, I would like to give you some tips today. I would like to concentrate on the traders who are already full-time in the trade or want to become full-time traders in the long term.

The fact that they are at FF clearly shows that they still want to learn or have to learn. Incidentally, that's the case with me as well. I'm not at FF to prove I'm a great guy, but to explain to myself why I've done a lot right in the past. That's why I designed this blog. In the past I dropped my trades intuitively, with a very good hit rate. My brother asked me one day why I was going down or up at a certain point. Although I could give an explanation, but this statement has not satisfied myself. So I started to describe my own trading style. Forex Factory is an excellent platform for this because there are like-minded people from all over the world to talk to.

Explaining how something works is a great way to get on with it. This is also a reason why I prefer a traceable loss rather than an unexplainable profit. Of course you should not lose permanently. The background is quite simple if I can not explain why I made a profit at the moment, I'm not able to repeat that. And if I can not repeat certain things, my future results are purely coincidental. And that is no basis for successful trading. Of course, trading is random and arbitrary, yet there are certain situations where a trader has a certain idea that actually works. What one can explain to oneself remains easier in the long-term memory.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

I would like to describe it as follows: Imagine you are not musical and look at a sheet of music. The notes will seem like hieroglyphics to them and they will not recognize a song from it. However, as you train and practice, they will one day hear the song in their head. It's the same with the course. In the beginning, it's just an arbitrary ups and downs over time, you realize what's happening in the market right now. By that I do not mean patterns like a double top or a doji because these patterns have no relevance to me. The point is to interpret the individual notes or candles and draw their conclusions from them. Since a single candle has no significance for me, it's about the overall picture.

If you look at any chart you will see that there are many resistance lines and support zones within the chart. Each of these zones has a certain strength. We now have two challenges to master. First, to identify these invisible zones and, second, to see how strong each zone is. This can then make easy trading decisions.

If you are a professional and realize that a certain resistance zone is very strong, you can use this information to make a longer trade with a very interesting risk-to-reward ratio. This means they would only be able to enter the trades that are interesting. This procedure is incredibly difficult and requires many years of training. Unfortunately, because each candle formation is different, there are no indicators that show us exact resistance zones.

That's exactly why I achieved my breakthrough with supply and demand. It's easy to say, buy when the price is down and sell when the price is up. However, most have determined that this is not a real down and no real top there.

The process is always the same in principle. When demand outweighs supply, prices rise. When supply outweighs demand, prices fall. When supply and demand are balanced, equilibrium is created. However, one can draw interesting conclusions from exactly these movements. And that is exactly the goal. To recognize this, you need time and a lot of time. This can be trained by opening the chart and paying attention only to the course of the candles. We have already noticed that indicators are trailing behind the candles. That means an indicator reacts slower than the candle itself. That's why the candle is the fastest indicator on the chart. That's why you should pay the most attention to the candles. Of course, I also work with so-called auxiliary indicators that help me translate the movements of the candles. However, I would never enter a trade based on the indicators. The auxiliary indicators that I work with are in principle a project that is constantly being changed and optimized. To get back to the sheet music, these indicators help me to translate certain notes that I do not immediately recognize.

My biggest goal as a trader was to be independent. What good is an EA or a Copytrader if I do not understand how market works. I do not mean to say that my view is the right one, but I have long since achieved my goal of independence and that is a crucial point for me. If I rely on an EA or Copytrader, what happens if these two factors fail? Then I would have to look for something new, but if that works so well is the question. Since I prefer to rely on what I have learned. Nobody can take what you once learned.

Many who start in this industry dream of big and fast wealth. Of course, there are dealers who have managed to get rich quickly but there is also almost every week in the lottery a millionaire. If you want to get rich fast in the forex market, you have to work with very high risks. You can be lucky twenty times in a row, but the twenty-first time makes you lose everything again. So it's nonsense to dream of driving Ferrari tomorrow but much more important to live from the stock market. Whoever manages to do this over many years is a professional and successful dealer. Of course, the capital build-up in wavy lines, is important that the lines run upwards. And that is much more difficult today than it was many years ago.

Another challenge as a beginner is the stock market news. I used to see it on my screen earlier and try to act accordingly. But one day I had the insight. Not the news affects the stock market but the stock market influences the news. Take a look at what arguments are used on television in the evening to explain why a given currency has fallen or fallen. This statement is a pure speculation, because you would have to ask several million traders why they have traded up or down. And believe me, each of these dealers will have a different opinion. No matter what news appears in the media, it is always crucial how the individual trader reacts to it. Bad news should actually always lead to falling prices on a stock, and that's just not the case. That's why I do not care about news.

Let's get to the last point that will trap traders in a trap. It's about the opinion of the supposedly professional traders. The following situation: You prepare for the day, they expect strong rising prices. After the London Stock Exchange opens, the course makes strange leaps that they can not understand. You go into a chat that deals exactly with this currency pair. Many traders discuss the future course of the currency pair. You see great pictures and hear comprehensible arguments. The price of their currency pair is just going up, as you read of a supposed bull trap. Many merchants in the chat say the same. Actually, they just wanted to go up but the arguments of the other dealers unsettle them. It all sounded logical what the long-standing successful dealers have written. You will not enter the bargain and 1 hour later you realize that it was a mistake. Why do not you trust yourself?

Let's look at the following situation.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

They see a chart of the EURUSD in the M 30 from November 5, 2014 to November 18, 2014. There are two traders who make two different statements at the point shown. The first trad claims that the price continues to fall the other one claims that the price continues to rise. The result: Both traders are right and both traders earn $ 500 on their trades. How can this work?

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Now let's look at the result. Trader A has entered into a long-term trade over 129 hours. During this time he has reached 150 pip and earned $ 500 with 0.3 contracts. Trader B has entered short-term trading of 12 hours and has earned 50 pip and $ 500 with one contact. Both traders were right but entered the market at different times. Since each trader takes a different approach and works with other systems, their opinion should not be relevant to them. Not because the retailers have no idea but because you do not know the exact backgrounds. Especially interesting for me are the recommendations like:

Short 1.23456, SL 50 Pip, TP open

How does he know that exactly, has a glass ball where you can look in or a lucky fairy whispering him when the course goes down. You realize, it's best to just rely on yourself. By this I mean also, that you should not believe me, the most trustworthy person is yourself. You should start trusting yourself if you do not have enough experiences for that , you must start to gain experience. If you now open an M1, it will take an awfully long time to reach a resistance line that you have drawn. Here's a little trick. When you start trading in the morning, create a 5 second chart in parallel and build the Bionic Chart there. Refrain from additional indicators. Now let the chart run for about 30 minutes and start drawing resistance lines as in my next video.

Inserted Video

Since making a candle takes only 5 seconds, you can learn 20 times faster with this type than in the 1 minute chart. You will also quickly realize that you are often wrong. Just when one believes that it goes further up or down happens exactly the opposite. After gaining some experience in this area, you can now run the 5 second chart in your demo account. Now begin to trade. Decide on a contract number and please do not change it. At the end of the day, export your account history from MT 4 to Excel. Now sort all winners and losers. Then they know the average loss or gain of a trade. The goal is to limit the losses and increase the profits. Of course, there are many more important calculations that you have to do but I want to keep it relatively simple.

It is crucial that they can recognize daily successes and improvements with this approach. Try to keep it as simple as possible in the beginning, it could still be complicated later. I hope to have given you some help and I wish you a successful trading day.

Inserted Video

The advantage of this chart view is that the supply market and demand market have been separated. This allows trend reversals to be identified more clearly and more quickly. The prerequisite for this chart to work is the Flexichart Indicator. This allows you to create seconds charts. This indicator generates an individual seconds chart from the ticks of your broker. The better the tick data the more accurate is your chart. First, you need two new MT 4 units. You can usually download them from your broker. Now install the Flexichart indicator in your two new MT4 units.

https://www.forexfactory.com/showthr...3#post11555813

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

After the MT4 is opened go to file and under profiles you can see the two files. Open "5 seconds Bull". The chart image should now open. Click on the button "EURUSD, M8 (offline)", then the right chart appears. You may not delete the second chart "EURUSD, M1", otherwise you will no longer receive tick data. This window has to run in the background. Of course, then only starts the candle, it takes a while (about 20 minutes) until everything is displayed correctly. Then open the second MT4 unit and upload the "5 second Bear". Now they just have to align both charts on your screen and you're ready to go. Please note that this is a selection of different dashboards. You have to personally find out for yourself if you can and want to work with it. Bionic Dashboard currency strength

Hello dear traders,

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Today I would like to introduce you to another interesting dashboard in our project 3. This is primarily about the respective currency strength of the euro and the dollar. It is important to note that the currency strength indicators are influenced by the price, not the other way around. In addition, indicators are always lagging behind the current price. That's why I never recommend trading based on indicators. Nevertheless, you will receive interesting information from this type of compilation. Before we start, first take a look at how this dashboard looks in practice. The dashboard was recorded for 5 minutes on Friday at 14:31 CET. There was a high volatility. The course has risen first and then run down.

Inserted Video

Let's take a closer look at the indicators

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

CCFp Indicator
Developer: SemSemFX
Interesting currency strength gauge

The indicator at point A indicates the strength in the euro with the green line and the strength of the dollar with the red line. It responds somewhat slower than the underlying currency strength indicator. The dashed white line is the zero line. If a currency lays over it is considered strong if it is lower than weak. However, this line also includes other currencies that were made invisible. Of course, you can compare all main currencies with each other.

+ RS_Group EUR & USD indicator
Developer: unknown
Very interesting strength indicator that can reacts faster than the price chart. Here, the EUR was currently compared with the dollar.

The currency strength indicator (point B) is a kind of currency basket where two different indicators, in this case the euro and the dollar indicate the current strength. This indicator responds very quickly to currency fluctuations and is therefore a nice confirmation to the upper indicator. In doing so, I made a very interesting observation that sometimes this indicator reacts faster than the price. The following situation: The red line of the dollar and the green line of the euro are both slowly going down. So we are in an equilibrium. Suddenly the green line shoots up. Which means that the euro will be much stronger against the dollar. A few seconds later, a bullish candle is created. I once tried to act for fun. This has worked a few times, but I strongly warn against doing it. This type of ad now takes some getting used to. If the green line is up and the red line down, it means we have a strength in the Euro and a weakness in the Dollar. That speaks for rising prices. If the red line is up and the green line is down, it means that we have a strength in dollars and a weakness in the euro. That speaks for falling courses. Since many of them also deal with other currency pairs, I have posted them at the end of the RS Group currency basket. There you will find the major currency strengths.

CFP indicator
Developer: SemSemFX
An indicator that gives almost the result of the euro and dollar strength.

The CFP indicator (point C) is, in principle, the result of the strength of the euro and the dollar. So it's a translation of the chart. If you compare this line with the price history they will realize that there are some differences. Since one can do without the indicator, I have installed it only once in the M1. However, it is certainly helpful for a start.

smZigZag-Bionic Oscilator
Developer: Bionic/SwingMan
Interesting trendindicator

At point D you will find the Bionic Oscillator. As soon as a green dot emerges, the price could go up, as soon as a red dot appears, the price could run lower. Under no circumstances should you enter a trade in the creation of these red or green points. These points are generated from the zigzag indicator. This means that always the penultimate green or red dot is no longer changeable. Thus, the newly emerging point can actually only occur at a later date.

smZigZag-Bionic Chart
Developer: Bionic / SwingMan
Interesting new candle

At point E, the Bionic Chart is a single current candle. This is actually only a small help to the overview.

At point F you will find a candle count-down, which shows you how long it will take until a new candle appears.

This dashboard consciously integrates all time units so they can choose their own time unit to focus on. As already described in Post 777, load the indicators into your MT4 and put the folder "8 Stärke CCFP Neu" in your folder: Profiles. After closing and reopening your MT4, you can now access this profile: "8 Stärke CCFP Neu ". Of course you can exchange the required currency strengths in this dashboard. The dashboard can be a good help now and then. Just install it and judge for yourself how the currency strength behaves during the day. ESMA will not let up

Hello dear trader,

ESMA has extended the restrictions on CFD and Forex trading for another 3 months. The restrictions that have been in force since August relate primarily to the amount of leverage that can be speculated on in CFD and Forex trading. On 26th September the European regulator ESMA decided that the restrictions on CFD and forex trading for retail customers, which had been in force since 1 August 2018, would be extended for another 3 months until 31.01.2019. The protection of retail investors in CFD trading can only be guaranteed if the restrictions set by ESMA continue to apply. It has therefore decided that the restrictions will continue to apply from 1 November. A few weeks ago, ESMA also extended the ban on Binary Options for another 3 months.

Until further notice, the following restrictions apply to CFD trading:

30: 1 leverage for major currency pair = 3.33% margin

20: 1 leverage for the major indexes = 5% margin

10: 1 leverage for commodities (gold not included) = 10% margin

5: 1 equity leverage = 20% margin

Margin Close Out: a defined threshold at the account level, upon reaching which the providers are required to close the open CFD positions (at 50% of the required margin). As a result, an investor can lose a maximum of 50% of the invested capital with one transaction.

Prohibition of additional liability (had already applied in Germany before the intervention by ESMA)

Restricting the incentives to trade in CFDs (bonus on deposits, etc.)

A standardized risk warning that must include an indication of the percentage of retail investors in the specific CFD provider that are making losses

The CFD industry has massive problems

Due to ESMA's restrictions, there have been massive relocations abroad where high leverage can still be traded. These new ESMA rules are already beginning to impact the earnings of CFD brokers. Last month, big brokers announced sales declines of up to 21%. There were already increased profit warnings for shareholders.

The professional trader is a VIP in CFD trading

However, there are still customer groups that are allowed to trade unchanged without any leverage restrictions. These are customers who are classified as "Professional Customers". This is why most brokers have created two account models, divided into private investors and professional investors. The Client must demonstrate that, on the basis of his experience, knowledge and expertise, he is in a position to make an investment decision and to adequately assess the risks involved.

He also has to fulfill two of the following three criteria:

1.In the past four quarters, it has been proven that leveraged financial derivatives have traded in significant sizes.
2. You must own a portfolio of financial instruments in excess of € 500,000.

3.Man must have been proven to have worked for at least one year in a relevant position in the financial industry requiring knowledge of trading in derivative securities.

Many brokers now want to specialize in professional traders. If you look at the distribution of sales, this becomes clear. Professional customers bring the most sales. According to some brokers, the share of professional traders is 40%. If you look at the balance sheets of the largest brokers, you find that a good broker earns between 3,000 and 3,600 euros per annum and customer on average.

That means:

5% are approx. Professional traders = 40% turnover

95% of the remaining traders make up 60% of their turnover and more than 85% lose their money

Let's assume that the broker would only offer CFD (which of course is not the case, but is only to be taken as an example). When you trade a lot, the broker receives about $ 10 in fees. If the broker now makes 3,600 € revenue per customer, that's 360 Lot per customer per year. Suppose the broker has only 1,000 customers, then the breakdown looks like this.

1 lot costs 10 € / 360 contracts per customer

1000 customers = 360,000 Lot per year

Division:

50 professional traders trade 144,000 lots per year

950 normal traders trade 216,000 lots per year

Result:

50 professional traders trade 2,880 lot / year equivalent to 12 lot / day

950 normal traders trade 227 lot / year equals 1 lot / day

While a professional trader makes € 1.2 million in sales per day, the average trader comes to just € 100,000. In this case, the broker only needs to gain 125 professional traders to generate the same revenue as currently with 1,000 traders. This drastically reduces the costs, since he does not need so many employees anymore. On average, the brokers come to 1 employee per 100 customers. In our case, the broker could reduce 80% of the employees. And employees in a company are always the highest cost factor. If the broker drastically reduces the fees for professional traders, he will quickly gain new professional traders. At the same time he is relocating his employees. The return will please the shareholders.

This scenario is not a nice thought for non-professional traders. We will see where these restrictions lead in Europe. It will not be that bad, because in America this scenario has been in place for many years and it works.

Schoppenhauer once said aptly: Mostly only the loss teaches about the value of things.

I wish you a great weekend.

best regards

Hello dear traders,

In some of my post I have repeatedly noted that it is not worthwhile for me if the FED or ECB holds a meeting, because often in the overall course, nothing changes. An important election in America is an equally important moment, leaving its mark on the EURUSD. In the Midterm elections, America has re-elected the composition of the House of Representatives and parts of the Senate. The US republicans were able to defend their majority in the Senate, while the congress will be dominated by Democrats. It is already becoming apparent that this is a choice with many historical results: for example, more women than ever will be in the House of Representatives in the future. At midnight local time (6 clock German time) closed the last polling stations in the western US state of Alaska. Because of the many time zones in the US, the election had a total of 18 hours. It will take a few more days until the final result is known, because in California, for example, absentee ballots are only counted in the days following the election.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

At 1:30 CET, EURUSD had its first reactions at point A and lasted 6.5 hours to point B against 08:00 CET. Let's take a closer look at the movements.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

At 1:30 CET, the price went up 38 pip, then down 79 pip, then 77 pip up, and finally 36 pip down. A total of 115 pip up and 115 pip down. A nice equilibrium. The key is not the choice, but how the participants respond to these results.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

The price came from a strong 1.13 demand zone and was on the way up. At 1.14353 the game started. Up and down and ended again at 1.14353. I have cut out these 6.5 hours once and you can see that nothing really has happened. Nevertheless, money was shifted, one won, the other lost. These situations are a chance for many traders to make quick money, but don't risk too much.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Quite interesting is that the resistance zones have not changed, quite the contrary, the course has continued on a path as if nothing had ever happened. Of course you can be lucky and make a lot of money in such a situation, but it's always stupid if you do not know why you won this trade. Crucial are the winning trades that are repeatable and which a successful retailer should look for.

To compare that with a sailboat: Of course I can get from A to B faster in a storm, but in such a situation you can not control well and you are focused on not going down. That's why I prefer to stay in the safe harbor. As soon as the storm clears, I sail out. The journey from A to B takes longer, but I arrive relaxed and can enjoy sailing without destroying my boat. If you see strong candles on the chart afterwards, do not be sad that you were not there. Bionic trend strength indicator

Hello dear traders,

A few days ago I promised to post more information on the new and already published Bionic trend strength indicator. The blog was a little more elaborate than expected, but I hereby release my promise.

During my many years as a trader, I've always wanted to have an ad next to my chart that always tells me exactly if we have a supply market or a demand market. I have tried some 1000 indicators and have always failed. Several years ago I started to develop my own ideas that bring me closer to this goal.

An indicator for me is like a kind of navigation system, It calculates for me an optimal way and makes me a suggestion. However, I'm in the car to give gas, steer and brake. And I do not depend on my navigation system. I am in control of my vehicle and not the navigation system. Nevertheless, it often helps me to achieve my goal faster.

In each market, the price is determined by supply and demand. The quantity available on the market represents the supply, while the demand is the quantity that buyers would like to purchase. Any change by offer and demand will be returned from the price. Before a price rises or falls, an equilibrium is created. Once this balance is disturbed again, the price moves in the direction of supply or in the direction of demand. The price goes up in a demand zone until the pressure of the supply zone is greater.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

In the EURUSD monthly chart of 1972-2018, the price moved into a strong demand zone in January 1985 (zone A). Zone A was so strong that it pushed the price up for ten years until March 1995. In Zone B, the supply market was so strong that it pushed the price down for over five years until it entered Zone C in October 2000. Strong demand in Zone C eventually pushed the price higher again.

In Zone A, demand was much stronger than supply, which increased prices. In zone B, supply was much stronger than demand, which resulted in a price drop. Within this demand or supply zones, one sees many equilibrium that represent a balance between supply and demand.

Since I act exactly according to supply and demand, I am of course looking for the zones that initiate a turnaround. Of course, there are different trends in different time units. As an example, let's just take a look at the demand market from Zone A to Zone B. Within this uptrend, you can also see some downtrends that have taken several years.

So I'm looking for a navigation system that helped me identify these zones. Here I came to an indicator (ZigZag) which is actually no indicator. With the zigzag indicator you can not trade, because only the penultimate tip is fixed. Even if he creates a new syringe, this situation may still change. However, this indicator has a property that no other indicator possesses. With the right attitude he shows me all HL, HH, LH and LL in each time unit. And that was the breakthrough for me. For me, it is crucial to know what strength the price has been within a demand market or supply market. And that's relatively easy to figure out over the average pip per candle.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Point A

Let us take a closer look at a concrete example in the weekly chart of the EURUSD from 1998-2003.

At point A, the price fell within an offer market, averaging 60.4 pips per candle. Dividing 2296 pip by 38 candles is the result. This means that the price has dropped by 2296 pip within 38 weeks. Of course, this result also includes the upward trend of over three weeks that has taken place within this supply market. This downtrend was very sustainable because it took over 38 weeks.

Point B

We are in a demand market and the price went up by an average of 240 pip. This means that the strength has increased significantly, but with a low sustainability. That speaks for a possible pullback.

Point C

The course has now gone down by 90.2. That means the strength down has increased.

Point D

The uptrend finished at 157.2. We recognize that the strength of the uptrend has slowed significantly and the strength of the downtrend has increased significantly. The two uptrends could be identified as a pullback. That speaks for a further downward trend.

Point E

A sustainable downward trend has continued, but sustainability has slowed somewhat. The trend has become a bit stronger.

Point F

A fast and strong uptrend with 285.3 has emerged. This trend was not sustainable and therefore a potential pullback. The likelihood of another downtrend is given.

Point G

The downtrend has become stronger, however, has lost in sustainability. The stronger a trend becomes, the higher the opportunity to identify the trend as a pullback. If you look at the strength of past downtrends, you find that we had the second strongest downtrend here.

Point H

The uptrend was now 136.9 strong. Compared to the last uptrend, this trend has weakened. This situation also speaks for another downtrend. But there could soon be a major turnaround, as the price wants to go up.

Point I

The downtrend has ended with a magnitude of 48.1. That was the lowest strength in the entire downtrend. From this one could conclude that a trend reversal can take place. Of course, this trend reversal has already taken place, but you can not know that at this point.

Point J

The uptrend ended at 89.9. The strength has indeed declined compared to the two previous uptrends, but we have no typical pullback here. The trend has definitely become more sustainable. That too could speak for a further upward trend.

Point K

The downtrend with 40.7 shows the least strength, however, a greater sustainability. Once you compare the last three strengths of the downtrend, you can see that they have become much weaker. That could be an indication of a possible further upward trend.

Point L

The uptrend ended at 68.7. Although the strength has diminished, sustainability has increased significantly, which could speak for a further upward trend.

Point M

The downtrend has become much stronger than the last two before. In addition, the downtrend is somewhat weaker than the uptrend. Of course the candles are also important and the ZigZag indicator can not always work 100% properly. You can see here a typical equilibrium due to an uncertainty. As you can see, the course went down quickly and then turned into equilibrium. Displaying this situation correctly is a challenge for the zigzag indicator. However, based on the information given, one can expect a further upward trend.

Point N

At 59.2, the trend has weakened, however, the sustainability of the upward trend has increased.

Point O

For me, this 585 return is clearly a pullback, but this trend is very strong as well and it gives me a warning that a stronger downtrend could possibly take place after the next uptrend.

As you can see, these numbers are based only on conjecture and are of course not specific indications. Since the course is formed by chance, it always behaves differently at high points. Sometimes a trend change takes place quickly, sometimes it takes a long time. In addition, you should of course see the candle movements. Nevertheless, these trend strengths help in identifying possible long-term trends.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Let's take a look at different trends.

The smaller a number the weaker but more sustainable the trend. The larger the number, the stronger the trend but less sustainable.

Strength

The strength of a trend is determined by how high a trend is within a short period of time. Strong and short-term trends often characterize a pullback. These strong trends are often needed to break strong resistance zones.

Sustainability

The sustainability of a trend is determined by how far a trend runs over a longer period of time. If a trend goes down for a longer period of time, it means there was no objection from the buyers within that period. And it also means there were no major resistance zones, otherwise the course could not go down over this long period of time. This sustainability is a very decisive factor for me.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Let's take a look at this course after I have colored it. The red zones show the supply market while the green zones show the demand market. Zone A and E are the most sustainable zones in the downtrend. You can see very well that the uptrend has taken some time to actually go up. Zones B, D, and F are not sustainable, so they did not pose a threat to the downtrend. Zones H and J were much stronger than B, D, and F. In principle, we moved from point G to point K in Equilibrium. It can be seen that at point L, the sustainability of the upward trend has increased significantly. This gives a clear indication of a longer uptrend.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Let's look at another example from the EURUSD week-start 2010-2015.

Point A

The value of 140 below the trend A indicates a pullback and there is an indication that the downtrend has become much stronger. This trend has closed at 129.1.

Point B

The trend has closed at 110.1. Although the strength of the downtrend has diminished somewhat, it is still very strong.

Point C

The uptrend has closed at 101.6. the strength of the uptrend has diminished and is less strong than the last downtrend.

Point D

With 101.3, the strength of the downtrend has subsided. It can also be seen from the candles that a strong pullback has taken place within this trend. Of course, this strong pullback has massively reduced the overall average trend strength.

Point E

The uptrend has closed at 143.6, indicating that the trend strength is increasing.

Point F

The downtrend ended at 65.6. That was sustainable, but also very weak. Let's take a look at the past points. The downtrend has weakened as the uptrend has strengthened. That could be an indication of a possible further upward trend.

Point G

The strength of the uptrend has increased significantly.

Point H

The downtrend of 63.7 is not a typical pullback, but it has weakened.

Point I

The uptrend has now become much weaker, a possible setback is in question.

Point J

In fact, the downtrend has now become stronger. From another reset you can go out.

Point K

The uptrend has become significantly weaker again, a possible setback is in question. However, this upward trend is also very sustainable.

Point L

220.2 is a typical pullback so it could go up.

Point M

The uptrend has become stronger, but less sustainable.

Point N

268 is a typical pullback so it could go up. However, this downside strength shows that we can soon expect a longer-term downtrend.

Point O

The uptrend has become stronger, but less sustainable.

Point P

Now the downtrend has become much weaker, but sustainability has increased.

Point Q

At 39.7, the strength has dropped significantly. If you see how the strength of the downtrend has developed you can draw conclusions from it.

Point R

The downtrend has gone down but it has lost much of its strength. Then the course went into a two-year Equilibrium.

So you realize that both the strength and the sustainability of a trend matter. There may be different interpretations of a trend. I would like to emphasize once again that my interpretation is certainly not correct and 100% effective. After all, it is a new indicator that did not exist in this form. Therefore, we must certainly work on the interpretation a little more closely. Nevertheless, these values help me in my daily work to recognize certain trend consequences.

As already written, I focus exclusively on my supply and demand zones. These auxiliary indicators help me with this. Maybe you too have some experience with this indicator and I am looking forward to your feedback.

I would like to warn once again against entering into a trade on the basis of this indicator. This indicator may provide very important information, but should only be used as a supportive tool.

The next project we are going to deal with will be exactly this trend indicator, but it will take some time.

I hope I could give you some information and I look forward to your feedback. I wish you a successful trading day.

best regards

Annotation:

When the video started, I had roughly drawn two resistance lines. Although I knew that the course was still a bit down, but how far he came down, was very difficult to see. Another challenge was that I did not use higher time units to find zones, but only took the 5 sec chart as the basis, so my resistance zone was only 0.3 pip wide. Responding to this is a challenge. In the video you can see that I was unsure when running down the course and had no proper starting points. So you can only improvise and try to predict the course of the course on the basis of the many information.

If I have a strong resistance zone and I can assume that the price can break that resistance zone, then I'm basically looking for a good entry point below that resistance zone. If the resistance zone fails and runs back, I have no loss, so it's important to get in front of the drag zone. The advantage is that I am already in the market when the price is now high through the zone. If I put a sellstop over the drag zone, it can really go wrong if the price is turned down sharply. When things go well and the price goes up sharply, I usually enter the market way too late and lose enormous potential. That's why a sellstop is not an alternative for me.

If you look at the video, please note that no one is able to accurately predict all trend sequences and trend lengths, especially in the 5 second chart is extremely difficult. My marked resistance zones in the video had a width of 0.3 Pip, which is already sporty. My rough assessments of individual zones were correct and decisive was the overall result and that was true.

A possible trading scenario

Hello dear subscribers,

a subscriber privately asked me how to plan and execute my trades. Since I find this topic very crucial, I would like to post it here in the forum, so that all traders can benefit from it.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Here is a possible example:

At Post # 799, at 16:00 CET, I identified a resistance zone in H1 between 1.12879 and 1.12941. In the M5, I have identified the zone 1,12920, which I have given up as a sell limit order. My stop was 4.8 pip higher at 1.12968. At 1.12915 I came to the market. My guess was that the price could run to 1.12522, because there was a strong resistance zone in the M5. However, I wanted to get out a little earlier, so I took the preceding resistance zone 1,12572 as TP. At 1.12570 the TP has been triggered. 34.5 pip were reached against a risk of 5.3 pip including spread. The risk-to-reward ratio of 1: 6.5 was okay.

At 17:25 CET my sell limit order was triggered. Initially, the price went 2.5 pip down and then 13.5 pip down. After that, the price went up within the next 12 minutes and my trade was 3 pip down. Then it went first 20 Pip down. There was a pullback of 5 pip. 40 minutes later, my TP was triggered. After equilibrium, the course went down another 5 pip before continuing up the course.

If I had set my TP of 1.12522, I would not have been picked up and would have had to close the trade manually. I would have been about 5 pip worse off. Therefore one should never be too greedy and prefer to get out of a resistance zone before.

Usually, I often pull my stop in the profit when the price has gone down sharply. In this case, I did not do that because the price went up in a weak but sustainable uptrend. Therefore, there may still be some buyers who were not satisfied yet. The course had to penetrate even deeper into the resistance zone to satisfy the remaining buyers. Luckily it was the same.

Of course, the course could have run into the stop, the risk of 5.3 pip was manageable. If you only look for trades that have at least a risk-profit ratio of 1: 5 you are on the safe side. You could lose 4 out of 5 trades and still have not lost any money. If you had a success rate of only 50%, the bill would look like this.

3 x 5.3 pip loss and 3 x 34.5 pip profit = 87.6 pip gain. Provided you trade the same number of contracts. Usually I work with stops of a maximum of 4 pip, but if there is a stronger resistance zone, I'll increase the risk, but the risk-reward ratio must be right. Since I sometimes trade with higher lots, it is important for me to refine the resistance zones in the M5. This reduces the size of my stop, increasing the risk-reward ratio.

In that case, I traded the pullback within an uptrend, a downtrend within a strong uptrend. Why do I do this? Now the pullbacks often have a habit of going through relatively quickly and are easier to calculate for me.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

My trade ran 137 minutes to get 34.5 pip. The uptrend before lasted 364 minutes, earning 71.7 pip. Uptrend = 0.19 pip / min, downtrend = 0.25 pip / min.

If I had traded 137 minutes in the uptrend, the average yield would have been 26 pip. That would have been 25% less revenue in the same time and a risk-profit ratio of 1: 5. The longer I am in the market, the higher the risk of being stopped out by an unpredictable breakout. Had I traded the uptrend, the risk would have been significantly larger in relation to the gain. That's why I prefer the pullbacks rather than the uptrend. Decisive, however, are the resistance zones that are determined. A strong resistance zone also brings with it a stronger pullback, so you can get a good risk-reward ratio.

The Bionic Trend Indicator gives incredibly good information on how strong the price has been in the past, which is often not visible to the naked eye through the candles. A single candle is not a clear statement, a complete trend against it. Please look the bionic strength indicator, you will discover very interesting things. If you trade the EURUSD for many years you will discover that basically the same things happen again and again. This can not be discovered with candle formations or indicators, because the course is always completely different. When a big player enters the trade, it's just about fooling the other traders, which in fact will not happen. So if you act according to what you believe you will inevitably lose.

The Bionic Trend Indicator is not an indicator to trade with and it is only an aid. But it shows you exactly what can happen next, because it shows exactly where in the market the strength and the weakness lies. And exactly this information I need to get an overview of which resistance zones can be crucial. I deliberately say "can be decisive" because there is no security in this market. And that's a good thing, because otherwise the chances of winning a lot would be much smaller. Why can a lotto person become a millionaire? Because many people lose their bets at the same time. That's the game we play. Read my post no. 699

https://www.forexfactory.com/showthr...2#post11542672

You will see that Goldman Sachs wins in 89.4% of all cases. So we know with which opponents we have to deal. And believe me Goldman Sachs does not bet on his luck, but on fooling us into something that will never happen in reality. And in that they are absolutely world champions. So, if we want to cut some of the profits out of the forex market, we have to think like the big players and then get carried away by them.

This has nothing to do with complicated trading, but one should not make that too easy. Why are over 90% of traders losing their hard earned money?

Now some are working with the standard indicators that follow the course and give information when it is already too late and others rely on their luck. A crucial point is the respective market situation, which occurs so differently that a single indicator can not help. The more indicators you use, the more information is watered down. That is why I also regularly warn against entering into trade on the basis of indicators.

If you shoot clay pigeons and are a good shooter, explain to a beginner how to shoot properly. This does not work because many factors are crucial. Weight of the clay pigeon, the speed with which the clay pigeon is shot down, weather conditions, wind conditions, light conditions, gun barrel, cartridge, respiration, and much more. A good shooter has to adapt to the situation and make his decision within milliseconds and there are no textbooks or templates, but only the experience in practice. In the forex market, we have significantly more uncertainty factors. We never know what the ultimate dealer, who is currently moving the market strongly, really wants.

That's why every seasoned trader has his own approach and strategy, and if he succeeds, he's right on. I would never question that strategy. --- 帖子 #814 ---
[quote=DonSergion;11741811]Hello, Bionics. Looked your thread, signed up. Very interesting topic.

Hello DonSergion,

First of all, welcome to our blog and I am glad that this topic appeals to you and helps you in trading. Your idea to add a volume change to the Bionic indicator is a really great idea of you and I thank you for your creativity.

However, there is a small problem. Futures are traded on the stock market; the moment a buyer and a seller trade a certain stake, a certain volume is created. There I get worldwide correct stock market data about the price and the volume. CFD are contracts for difference traded over the counter. If you trade CFD, you trade only with the broker and not directly on the stock market. We get from the broker off-exchange data about the price. The volume we receive is the tick volume calculated by the broker. This tick volume differs significantly from the volume determined by the real stock market data. This means that we would trade with incorrect volume data. That was the reason why I have never considered the volume profile before. This is another story for futures. Of course, the prices are different, but the deviations here are not quite as extreme as the volume. Of course this depends on the respective broker.

However, the idea is very good and I will like to deal with it once, we just have to keep in mind that the volume data are partly calculated from the prices and therefore provide many false signals. The Bionic Starch Indicator is generated exclusively from the price.

Project 4, which is now in preparation, gives us important information about the key supply zones and demand zones. Although these zones are calculated from the prices, but the individual candles play often only a minor role here. If we have completed this project, I will be happy to deal with your proposal. Thank you again for this great idea, I am very glad that you have thought about how to optimize the secret of successful action for all. And that's what motivated me the most.

Project 4 the key zones in EURUSD

Hello dear subscribers,

As I have been successfully dealing with Equilibrium for many years, my greatest desire was to make the crucial supply zones and demand zones clearly visible in the chart. The first step was the Bionic Chart, which eliminated the wicks and made the course clearer. The second step was to show the strength of the supply zones and demand zones. In the third step, I have published several auxiliary indicators in different dashboards that provide important information in the area of currency strength. The fourth step with Project 4 is now to show the supply zones and demand zones with different colors and time-independent in the chart.

The basis for this was the ZigZag indicator, which is actually completely unsuitable for deriving possible trading decisions. But he has a decisive advantage, he shows the concrete HH, HL, LL and LH of the respective course. From this one can, depending on the right attitude, make the supply zones and demand zones graphically visible. With the ZigZag indicator, only the penultimate top is up-to-date, as the price can still change. In our case, that does not matter, because I use this indicator to identify the key supply zones or demand zones. From this I can derive a possible trend reversal in the future. Thus, it is completely irrelevant whether the ZigZag indicator provides current data or not. It is crucial that the data from the penultimate top are current and thus unchangeable. The actual trading decision is made solely through the identified zones. In addition, I get from my dashboards then the specific information, if my zone is relevant.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

This example clearly shows that the supply zones and demand zones are completely time-independent. Within these zones there are different trends. The numbers above or below are crucial. The smaller a number, the weaker, but more sustainable the trend. The larger the number, the stronger the trend, but less sustainable.

The strength of a trend is determined by how high a trend is within a short time. Strong and short-term trends often indicate a pullback. These strong trends are often required to break strong resistance zones. The sustainability of a trend is determined by the extent to which a trend runs over a longer period of time. If a trend goes down over a longer period of time, it means buyers have not objected within that time. And it also means that there were no major resistance zones, otherwise the course could not give way over that long time. This sustainability is a very decisive factor for me

In the Post 789 I have delivered a concrete explanation.

https://www.forexfactory.com/showthr...7#post11677547

Basically, it is crucial that the indicator does not provide trade decisions, but only the crucial zones that can then lead to a trade decision.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Here you can see a line chart in W1 from 1971 to 2018. I would now like to use three examples to identify points A, B and C using the supply and demand indicator. In order to identify a particular zone, I need a reference value for this. At point A, B and C, there is a reference value since the price has already been in this price range. The points D, E and F can also be determined, but this is much harder because there is no reference value. This slide should serve as an overview so that you always know where we are at the moment. Why is the overarching trend important when trading only in the M15 or M5? The overarching trend sets the long-term direction of the trend, and of course there may be a multi-year pullback in a long-term uptrend, but this information is crucial in identifying medium-term and short-term supply or demand zones. So it's a kind of navigation system that helps you get there faster. Let's take a look at how the supply and demand indicator helps us to identify the critical zones. Of course, this indicator is also able to identify medium-term and short-term supply zones or demand zones, but we start with just these three decisive zones, A, B and C.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

We are here in 1971 in H4. An uptrend is starting and we are looking for a strongest and most sustainable zone that has taken place within this uptrend. The information from Post 789 is crucial for this. At point 1 we find what we are looking for and draw a blue zone into the future. Since this zone is 420 pip thick, we need to downsize the zone. At point A and B you can see two more uptrends entering our zone. These are resistors, which allows me to reduce the blue zone by my green lines to 230 pip. Since the course has come from above a distance of 5,700 pip, the 230 pip correspond to just 4%. Of course you can reduce the zone significantly in the smaller time units, but unfortunately my H1 is just enough for the year 2008. If you expand your history database you can spend 2 months in the M1, 1 year in the M5, 2.5 years in the M15, 5 years in the M30, 10 years in the H1 and from the H4 to 1971 go back. To determine the current zones that should be enough. We have now reduced our zone to 230 pip and now look at what happens as soon as the course from above enters our zone.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

We are now in the years 1983 to 1986. The course comes from above and penetrates into our zone at point A. They recognize what happens. The price is turned up sharply and goes up 8,980 pip. Joke: Even with a stop of 230 pip that would have been a good risk-reward ratio, but that would have taken ten years. The fact is that we had already identified the possible turnaround 48 months earlier with the indicator. What does that mean in concrete terms? If there is a possible big turnaround at this zone, it means the course would have to go down by then. And that's just crucial information. How many times have we wondered if we can get on a trade before the big turnaround begins? Of course, a pullback can always occur within a trend, but we will receive this information in the future with project 4.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

In 1985, we are back on the upswing and three years later, we are looking for the strongest and most sustainable zone that has taken place within this uptrend.

At point 2 we find what we are looking for and draw a blue zone into the future again. Since this zone is 520 pip thick, we need to downsize the zone. At point A and B you can see two more uptrends entering our zone. With these resistors, I can downsize the blue zone by my green lines to 220 pip. We will talk in detail about the specific localization of these zones, as the course always behaves differently. Therefore, you always have to create this identification manually and can not build an EA from it. This time the price has gone up 7,800 pip. The fact is that with the indicator we would have already identified the possible turnaround 60 months earlier. From this information we could have derived very interesting bearish trades.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

In May 2000, the course at point 0 entered our blue zone for the first time. Since we have reduced our zone with the two green lines, we can assume that after a short pullback the price will continue to run downwards. After pullback, a very strong supply zone emerged at point A. I once drew this strong supply zone red. In October 2000, the course entered our zone for the first time. (Point 1). As you can see, the price was strongly but not sustainably rejected. A strong rejection always speaks first of all that the course comes back again. In fact, the course came back again and then went up strong and sustainable. It was precisely from this sustainable and strong zone that a green demand zone was drawn at point C. The next step was to watch what happens when the price enters our offer zone. Since this zone is very strong, the course would have to make a strong move upwards to get out of this zone. At point 2 that did not happen and the course went down again.

The background was that at that time the sellers were still not satisfied and pushed the price down again. The course was now up to point 3 and came once again in our zone. After that the course ran to the point 4 and on the way formed at point D a strong and sustainable upward zone. That was a good sign that the cops have slowly taken the helm. One recognizes that the offer zone was only briefly overcome at point 4 and the course went down again. The course was now heading towards point 5, returning to the strong green demand zone. Between point 4 and point E it is clear that the supply zones were significantly stronger than the demand zones. From the point B and F the demand zones were clearly in the advantage. Finally, you could see at point G, how strong the uptrend from the offer zone has come out. That was clearly the breakthrough to the uptrend. In the normal chart you would have had difficulty drawing in the green and red zones.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

On the chart, it looks like the price is only rising very slowly, but that's wrong because I wanted to show as many zones as possible. As of February 2002, we were on the upswing again, and once again we are looking for the strongest and most sustainable zone that has taken place within this uptrend. At point 3 we find what we are looking for and draw a blue zone into the future again. This blue zone is only 270 pip strong this time. At points A and B, we see two more uptrends entering our blue zone. This allowed me to reduce the green resistance zone to 42 pip in H4.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

In March 2015, the course entered our blue line at point A for the first time. However, he has not yet reached our identified green line. It can also be seen that after the strong downtrend a strong and sustainable green zone is formed. At point B, the course is not even in our blue zone, for us a crucial indication that the uptrend is not yet active. Finally, at the end of December 2016, the price will be in our crucial zone at point D and will be turned up. Since the strongest supply zone at point A was taken out of it and there were no other strong supply zones, we could now assume a further uptrend.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Basically, there was the problem that we had a very strong supply zone from 1.3990 - 1.0460 in the W1. This strong offer zone was taken out with the price development until 1.03 only once. After that, there was a very strong uptrend that went to 1.255. There was a very strong resistance zone that pushed the course down to 1.12140. Within the uptrend from 1.03 to 1.255 we are now looking for the strongest and most sustainable zone in H4. At point 4 we find what we are looking for and again we draw a blue zone into the future. Since this zone is 320 pip strong, we need to shrink the zone. Due to the equilibrium that developed at point A, this identification is a bit more difficult. Based on the price history and the resulting resistance, I was able to limit this zone to 30 pip. As you can see, the course has touched the zone at least briefly and has been strongly and sustainably rejected. However, the course then came back again. In any case, I strongly believe that within this blue zone the price will continue its upward trend. Maybe December could be the decisive month.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Let's go to the D1 again. The zone I've calculated for a trend reversal is between 1,11300 and 1,11600. There are several reasons for that. At point E, we see a strong but less sustainable downtrend with a magnitude of 71.7. This downtrend is not settled for me yet and the price would have to drop below the 1.12140 to see this downtrend. In Equilibrium at point D, the greatest strength in the downtrend was 35.4. This means that the strength of the downtrend has increased in this zone so far. At point A we see a very strong pullback with a strength of 516.5 that has passed through my zone. However, the decisive clue is point B. First, there was a sustained downtrend before, then a pullback up and from point B, the price went down sharply. That's exactly the lower resistance zone for me. If the price broke through this zone, a further downtrend would be expected. Another and additional point is the psychological aspect. Christmas and the New Year are just around the corner, giving you the chance to look positively into the New Year. Maybe this positive mood could affect a trend change.

--- 帖子 #826 ---
Improve unclear price progressions

Hello dear traders,

As we have already noted, past prices and the resulting supply or demand zones are crucial to future price movements. From these zones you can derive important information that will be confirmed in future price movements.

One of the reasons why I like to trade the EURUSD is, in addition to the very high liquidity, the fact that the price goes back to 1971. This is the so-called synthetic Euro. This is nothing but a synthetic exchange rate calculated taking into account the overall exchange rate of all euro currencies. The introduction of the euro on 1 January 1999 goes back to 1971 with this conversion.

With this recalculation of the EURUSD there is the advantage that I have many reference values, ie zones in which the price has already been found. The more reference values I have about a certain zone, the more accurately I can derive statements from it.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Hello dear traders,

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

There are 3 concrete demand zones and 3 concrete supply zones in the EURUSD monthly chart from 1971 to today. Whether zone no. 7 actually develops into a concrete demand zone, is not certain at the present time. Within these 7 zones there are again subordinate supply and demand zones. Although we have been in a demand zone above 1.03 since January 2017, the price was rejected at 1.255 in Feb 2018 and has since fallen below in a subordinate supply market. However, demand Zone no. 7 is not yet confirmed and may still change.

It could be different, though. Demand Zone no. 7, which we've been in since January of 2017, is just a pullback and the no.6 supply market is still in the higher category. As soon as the price falls below the 1.03 level, green zone no.7 would disappear and you would see a wider zone no.6 on the chart. In any case, the sustainability of the demand market has been reduced while the sustainability of the supply market has increased. I assume that we are again in a demand market, but that is also pure speculation. The course runs in undulations up and down. With the Supply and Demand zones, I can capture the strength and sustainability of a trend. The greater the time unit, the more accurate statements can be made.

When a price moves lower in a supply market, demand must be greater than supply, so that a real turnaround can occur. The course case may be stopped by higher demand or a lack of further supply. Equilibrium is an interesting indication that supply and demand are balanced. However, this is no guarantee for a possible turnaround. For an upward or downward price, therefore, only an imbalance between supply and demand can always be responsible.

Future trend forecasts remain a major challenge.

--- 帖子 #841 ---
The most efficient currency pair

Hello dear traders,

On the way to becoming a successful trader you have to make many decisions.

Which system do I use? Stock, Future, CFD or options? Which platform? Which broker? Personal money management. Optimal workplace design. Just to name a few things. When these key issues are resolved, it's essentially about what to trade? Commodities, stocks, indicia, or currency pairs, the offer is very diverse. For me the essential aspect was to find a market that is highly frequented. This is clearly the currency market. But within this currency market, there are an awful lot of currency pairs. Today I would like to show you how I proceeded in the selection of my optimal currency pair. If you want to dance and really party, you will rather choose a club or a nightclub which is highly frequented. Being alone on a dance floor will not be fun. It is the same in the foreign exchange market.

If you've ever traded stocks, you'll know that: you want to go to the market at a certain price, but at that price, there are no sellers. So you have to accept a higher entry price to get into the market. The whole thing will be extreme when the course goes down. You want to sell fast but there are no buyers who buy you your stock at this time. This has already cost many investors head and neck. The Forex market generates $ 6 trillion in sales each day. The six largest currency pairs (majors) of which manage just under 4 trillion dollars. Let's take a closer look at the majors.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

On the right side you can see the use of the individual currencies in the years 2001-2016 which were traded within different currency pairs. From 2001-2016, an average of $ 3.5 trillion per day was traded on the foreign exchange market. The dollar was always involved in 88% of the cases. The euro and the yen are also interesting for me.

On the left side are the six main currency pairs listed. With the dollar, the euro and the yen being the most widely used currencies, it is not surprising that EURUSD and USDJPY are among the most traded currency pairs. I have now examined the average pip in these individual currency pairs in seven time units from M1 to D1. For that I used the average of the last 1,500 candles in each time unit.

The term volatility refers to trading price changes over a certain period of time. The greater the extent of price changes, the higher the perceived volatility. Higher volatility currency pairs are considered riskier as price movements, whether down or up, are larger in comparison to similar, but less volatile, currency pairs.

It is striking that the volatility of the individual currency pairs are relatively close to each other with the exception of the GPBUSD. Here there is a deviation from the average over all time units of 50%. That's why this currency pair GPBUSD is the riskiest for me in the majors field. This leaves two currency pairs, EURUSD and USDJPY, with high liquidity. The volatility of the EURUSD over the measured period is about 20% higher than the USDJPY.

An average of 82 Pip per day, 14.5 Pip per hour and 1.5 Pip per minute are achieved in EURUSD per day. It does not matter if the price is up or down. Since the price fluctuates in seconds and the minutes candles do not always go up or down, you can roughly assume that between 4000 and 5000 pip per day in fluctuation in the EURUSD will be achieved. However, this is different from day to day. The USDJPY is therefore between 3,200 and 4,000 pip fluctuation.

Another important aspect for me is the unpredictability of the share price. Let's take 23 June 2016 as an example. On that day, the price went down sharply. EURUSD = 500 pip, USDJPY = 772 pip and GPBUSD = 1,760 pip. The most extreme example is certainly the EURCHF on January 15, 2015 with 2200 Pip within seconds. If you did not use a guaranteed stop there, it could be very bad.

Another very important point is the history database of the individual currency pairs. At EURUSD I have stored up to 54,000 candles. I am able to go back 1 month in the M1, 5 months in the M5, 15 months in the M15, 30 months in the M30, 60 months in the H1 and in the H4 and D1 47 years. This is excellent in terms of supply and demand, as I work with reference courses.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

As already stated, my main system is supply and demand and I think a traceable loss is preferable to an unexplainable gain. I have focused my screens exclusively on the EURUSD and receive up-to-date and very important information through my help indicators. A permanent switch to other currency pairs is eliminated and is therefore very relaxing. I have often traded the strongest currencies against the weakest currencies in earlier times, but I did not succeed as well as with supply and demand.

As we have already noted, there is no up and down in the EURUSD and therefore no middle. But there is demand and supply and, in the case of unity or uncertainty, equilibrium. The current price therefore has no relevance for me. In the same way, I do not pay attention to volume. In a market where there is no top or bottom, only the demand or supply is the limit. A price can never be oversold or overbought, so for me, indicators like the RSI are a relic of the past. The price always moves up or down in wavy lines, so I do not care if the EURUSD costs 0.50 or 1.60. We then earn money when we identify a demand market and get on time with a BUY order and exit at the latest when the price enters a strong supply market. We then earn money when we identify a supply market and get on time with a sell order and exit at the latest when the price enters a strong demand market. That's the only secret, but unfortunately that's not always that easy. We do not fight against other market participants in this market, but only against ourselves. When you enter into a trade, you should know in advance what will happen. With supply and demand that is conditionally possible.

If you have focused on a currency pair, there are a few days where the price is sideways or with less volatility. However, that's just an advantage if you're a scalper in terms of demand and supply. In these sideways markets, it's great fun to trade the ups and downs. Even though it is usually only 20 pip up and down.

Currency pairs are influenced by external factors that affect the value of the currency. The EURUSD is subject to fluctuations caused by different key interest rates, which are determined by the European Central Bank (ECB) and the Federal Reserve (Fed). Any market impact of the ECB to strengthen the euro would most likely lead to a rise in the value of the EURUSD. If, on the other hand, the Fed tried to strengthen the dollar by influencing the market, the value of the EURUSD would probably fall. Bigger pauses I only do when the Fed or ECB give out a new information. However, I can draw on the basis of the resulting extreme price movements again very interesting zones that are very important for the next few days.

The trading hours are optimal

There is less volatility between 06:00 and 08:00 CET, but it is always very interesting to trade, as there are often clear trends during this time. At around 08:00 CET, volatility rises, after which there is often a minor correction. I'm waiting a bit between 08:00 and 09:00 CET, with the London open, there is often a clear trend direction. From 9:00 - 11:30 CET you can make very interesting trades. It's often quieter between 11:30 and 13:30 CET. Time to relax. From 14.00 CET it will often continue with high volatility until sometimes 20:00 CET. I earn my pay between 6:00 to 11:00 CET, in the afternoon you can risk something. Outbreaks I rarely do. If I have identified a possible resistance zone and believe that the course goes through, I have to go in before. If it is a fake outbreak, I have earned nothing but nothing lost. When the course goes through, I did everything right.

Important: I do not pay attention to news, opinion from other traders and standard indicators during my trading. That would only dissuade me from the path.

Summary:

For each currency pair, other factors are more important than for equities or for gold. Behind it is always a variety of information, news and investor behavior. Keeping this in view for many currency pairs at the same time and being guided by it is impossible. The EURUSD is not necessarily an exciting currency pair, but a very reliable one. Security will never exist in this market, but if I compare all currency pairs, the EURUSD is one of the safest currency pairs I can trade.
