What happened if...? The mirror strategy!

Hello dear traders,

Today I would like to post something interesting for reflection. As we all know, more than 90% of all traders lose more money than they gain over time.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

This is confirmed by most brokers even in writing on their website. But why is that and is not there a quick uncomplicated solution? If you want to learn football in an association, you start a beginner course and work your way up through experience and dedication over the years. On the stock exchange or in the interbank market, there is unfortunately no beginner's course, every participant immediately plays in the Super Bowl and how that ends, is already on the website of the brokers. The fact that so many beginners dare to compete against the elite of the financial market is often due to the fact that advertising in the media makes trading very easy. When the Internet greatly simplified the stock market, trading was still a very complicated process. In order to make it easier for the beginner, indicators have been developed that should give the beginner a simple picture of the opaque market. The beginner is thrilled and looking at the past price history, it actually looks very easy. In addition, the profits and the prospect of a beautiful life beckon. But why does the dream come true for only a few?

The stock market and the interbank market are a bit comparable to the game Dodgeball, which certainly many know. Two teams play against each other with the aim of hitting the opponents' players with the ball so that they are eliminated in order. Agility, meeting and safety, endurance and speed are in demand. The playing field is the stock exchange, on one side are the buyers and on the other side are the sellers. The ball is the course price. If you hit the ball and the ball touches the ground after that, you are at a loss from the market. If you get hit by the ball and you catch it, you are still in the game or profit from the market. The ball is now thrown back and forth, the price goes up and down. The longer you are in the game, the higher the chance that you will be hit. When a big player enters the field, he never comes alone. Suddenly 100 men are on the field and all throw the ball at the same time on the opposing team. You think that's not fair?

Is it fair that a big player pushes the price up 30 pip and after pushs the price down 60 pips in seconds, so you were not able to make profits or close your stop? Everyone tries to play a game in a way that wins. Losing a game may be about honor, but in the stock market it's about a lot of money. The big players not only determine the market, but they are definitely the better players. From 250 trading days, Goldmann Sachs has been making 225 days profit and only losing 25 days.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

I calculated this slide roughly. In 25 losing days, Goldman Sachs lost $ 775 million and won $ 13,950 million on 225 days. This is $ 31 million per loss day and $ 62 million per profit day.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Pay-off ratio

There are dealers who have a hit rate of less than 40% and still make a lot of money. The secret, they have optimized their payout ratio. It means making sure that the winners are bigger than the losers. A payout ratio of 0.2 means you'll need 5 winners in the event of a loss to get back to 0. A payout ratio of 1 means that if you lose, you need 1 winner to be 0 again. The lower the pay-off rate, the higher the probability of a total loss. Expected value = profit rate * (average income) - loss ratio * (average losers)

In our case, expected value = $ 52.7 million per trade, whether they win or lose. I think that makes clear which opponents we have to deal with. Should one be afraid of it now? No, but maybe a little more respect.

If you have 2 options (buying or selling) and in 90% of all cases wrong, you must do the opposite to improve your odds.

Maybe you know that: You are standing in front of a door trying to press it on. It does not work you realize that you have to pull the door. The trading is similar, the course is always against you. Whenever you want to pull the door, you realize that the door has to be pressed open or vice versa. When you stand in front of the mirror and take an object in your right hand, the mirror looks as if you have the object in your left hand. Take this principle once for a trial in the CFD area.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

We now assume that our test trader belongs exactly to this category, which suffers a loss in 90% of all cases. We reprogram his trading buttons. If he presses on buy a sell order is given up and if he presses on sell a buy order is given up. He works with the same stops as always and we expect his stops to be adjusted to the current volatility.

What will happen?

Possibly, profits will increase and losses will be reduced. The danger is that the test trader will eventually know that when he presses on buy, in fact, a sell order is abandoned and when he presses on sell, a buy order is actually abandoned. This can cause him to press buy if he really wants to sell or vice versa. Then he is back where he once started, at 90% loss. But the idea is not completely stupid. If the losses are higher than the profit, one would only have to consistently do exactly the opposite to succeed.

The big players know that most traders are predictable. However, if these traders would do the opposite of what the big players expect them to do overnight, something very interesting would happen. The traders would no longer be stopped at the crucial zones, but the big players would now take these traders on their journey up or down. As a result, the big players would not reach their destination so quickly. Whether they would notice immediately, I doubt, since very few traders would take such a strategy.

It would be interesting for some traders, who are affected by 90% loss, to try this strategy once. The first step, programming the buy and sell order bar. Then I would try this strategy with a demo account. Try that, you can not lose anything, just win.

I would not take part in it because I act differently anyway than most expect. This means I would lose more with the mirror strategy than I win. If I want to buy, I would like to also press the buy button and not have in mind that I actually have to press the sell button.

And that's what the secret of being a successful trader seems to be: doing exactly what you should not do according to the trading textbooks. Maybe that's a good sign if 90% of traders tell you that you're on the wrong path and that your path will never work. That's exactly why I took my own path many years ago and did not follow existing laws. So far, no strategic path has been developed to be success in the long term. At the moment, I would call my success pure luck, which is certainly favored by an "different than others Strategy". Decisive for me, it is my approach to describe concretely and to explain myself. This will take a while, because I have not am a member of FF for a long time to solve the mystery.

That 90% of all traders loosing, just proves that you have to do exactly the opposite to be successful. Perhaps the mirror strategy could be a short-term solution for some traders. I'm curious.

With a wink, I wish a nice weekend

Lovely wishes

How to make a resistance zone smaller?

Hello dear traders,

Today I would like to show you how to determine and reduce concrete resistance zones with the help of the Bionics supply and demand indicator.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

We are in the D1, from May 2016 to December 2018, the Bionic supply and demand indicator is set to 8/4/2. At point A, you see a strong demand zone that pushes the price down. At point B, a strong demand zone followed, which brought the course up to point C. Thereafter, a sideways market was created with an Equilibrium.

Between point A and point C, we mentally draw a resistance zone because the supply market started there and the demand market was terminated there.

From June 20 to August 1, 2017, there was a very strong demand zone at point D. This demand zone was so strong that it severely disrupted our intellectual resistance zone. This Zone D is so strong that the price that will later go down in a supply market will accept this demand zone as resistance. And that is exactly the question, how can we determine the course of 12 November 2018 on the basis of the resistance zone D exactly. First we mark zone D with a blue background and then look at this zone in H1.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

The blue background now represents our zone D. The zone has been stretched for a better overview. In this zone D we notice two very strong zones, which we mark with E and F. As we know, strong price movements always break through strong zones. Our task now is to find the concrete resistance zones of Zone E and F.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

First, let's take a closer look at Zone E. We can see by the yellow arrow that a very strong day candle breaks through a resistance zone. Since we can not pinpoint this resistance zone at this time, we take the entire bullish candle minus the last pullback.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

According to the same principle, we record a possible resistance zone within the demand zone F. Since we can not pinpoint this resistance zone at this time either, we take the entire bullish candle minus the last pullback.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

We now switch back to the overview D1. We can now see in this overview how the price reacts to our resistance zones. At point 1, the course is turned up. When the price of 1.255 goes down, it is exactly the second time that it is turned up in that zone. Afterwards, a sideways market develops, whereby this zone continues to react as a resistance zone. With point 3, a strong supply zone breaks through our resistance zone for the first time. In the direct connection at point 4, the course comes back again. At point 5, we can see very well how the resistance zone holds. Finally, at point 6, with a strong supply market, the price breaks through our zone. When returning, this zone is accepted at point 7 as a resistance zone down. Starting at point 8, the course enters our resistance zone at point E for the first time and has since been in a sideways trend.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Now, looking at this overview in H4, we see that our resistance zone E is 64 pip in total. In order to enter a reasonable trade here, we must reduce this zone significantly. Let's take a look at what we need to do to get the 12 November 2018 demand trend right.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

For this, let's take a look at our already drawn zone E in chart M 15. Here we can already see that the upward candle is already much smaller than our marked zone. However, we would not get a very big advantage.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

We stay in chart M 15 and change the setting of our indicator to 3/2/1. If we take a closer look at the course of 1.2 and 3, we can derive two concrete resistance zones from it. The strong upward candle at point 4 breaks through exactly this determined resistance zone. With this help, we are able to reduce the resistance zone from 64 pip to 12 pip.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Looking at Chart M 15 on November 12, 2018, we can see how exactly our zone; the price was turned and goes up. Our guess was correct.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

In chart H1 we now look at the complete process. In the lower section you can see how we have reduced the resistance zone from 64 pip to 12 pip. So far we know that within the yellow zone there is a very strong demand zone. Now we can determine a possible offer zone according to the same principle. Here we work out two zones A and B. The zone B is 140 pip away and would have brought a risk-profit ratio of 1:12, while the point A would be 260 pip away and would have brought a risk-profit ratio of 1:21. Basically, I do not recommend completely exhausting the resistance zones. Personally, I would always plan my exit somewhat below these zones.

Of course you can also reduce the zones a bit, in which you can view the zones in the M5 or M1. As a result, the stop can be significantly reduced again. The only problem with that is that it will cause more supply zones that confuse me once more.

Anyway, it's a question of risk taking and how long you want to stay in the market to reach a specific goal. The longer you are in the market, the higher the likelihood of loosing some of the profits again. Nevertheless, you realize that you can choose concrete trades with the help of supply and demand , usually a few days before. By determining supply and demand zones, not only the stop but also, specifically, the risk-profit ratio can be determined. Thus, I can see at a glance whether the trade is worthwhile or not.

Unfortunately, not all trades can be planned so well, but it often helps, if I know within which trend phase I am. As a result, trades can be planned more efficiently. I am aware that this procedure is very complex, but I find it very exciting if you have the freedom to choose your trades. With demand and offer that is conditionally possible.

I wish you a nice evening

Within a supply or demand market, there are strong and weak zones. When the market returns to a supply zone at the end of the demand market and goes down again, the strong zones of the previous demand market are crucial as they have a very high resistance potential. You have to imagine this as a magnet if you try to bring two identical magnet zones together. These zones repel, and the stronger these zones are, the sooner the repulsion of the magnets occurs.

Within this demand market I have marked the two strongest zones. These are two very strong day candles. Determine specific trend reversals

Hello dear subscribers,

Over the last few days, I have analyzed zones based on the supply and demand indicator and have been able to determine some specific trend reversals and their lengths. However, I need to more concrete statements and further attempts to derive a legality from it. Let's take a closer look at the supply and demand zones.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Here is a comparison between a H4 candle chart and the Bionic supply and demand market indicator within two years. Individual candles, no matter in what time unit, are in principle only a small snapshot within the entire price history. The Bionic supply and demand market indicator translates these individual price developments into supply and demand zones. These zones are different in width and high. You can clearly see that the supply and demand market indicator gives clearer signals and information than the pure candle chart. If you know how to interpret these signals correctly, you can use them to derive future supply or demand zones.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Let's take another look at different trends. The wider a zone, the more sustainable but weaker the trend. The higher the zone, the stronger the trend, but less sustainable.

Strength

The strength of a trend is determined by how high a trend is within a short time. Strong and short-term trends often indicate a pullback. These strong trends are often required to break strong resistance zones.

Sustainability

The sustainability of a trend is determined by the extent to which a trend runs over a longer period of time. If a trend goes down over a longer period of time, it means buyers have not objected within that time. And it also means that there were no major resistance zones, otherwise the course could not give way over that long period of time. This sustainability is a very decisive factor for me

Conclusion: The narrower a zone is, the more likely it is to be considered a pullback, and the wider a zone, the more likely it is to attribute to a trend. Alone from this information, one can derive many future movements. In principle, this is just a translation of the current price in supply and demand.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Let's take a look at the price trend in the daily chart from 2012 to 2018. At point A, we see a strong and sustainable trend. Shortly before point B, a strong bullish pullback ensues, followed by a strong supply zone. This is a typical future resistance that I once dyed blue. The uptrend from point G was strong and sustained, but failed at point B's strong blue zone. With a smaller shot you can clearly see that from point H the downtrend was obvious. Attached Image (click to enlarge)

From point C, the breadth of the demand zones was clearly in the advantage and the price moved upwards. On the way up you can watch how the supply zones are getting wider and wider. That's an indication that things are going downhill soon. With point D, another supply market was launched, but it was caught by the strong demand market. I would not have expected so fast at Christmas time. Volatility was very low at that time, so I was willing to stay in the market for more than 4.5 hours and make the two trades.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Although I achieved a risk-profit ratio of 1: 6 with Trade A and a risk-profit ratio of 1:13 with Trade B, I was far too long on the market. You know the longer you are in the market, the higher the chance to be stopped by a break out, or to give back a large part of its profits.

Trade C would have been the optimal trade in our case, 35 pip in 50 minutes. That's equivalent to 0.7 pip per minute. Therefore, it is crucial to choose the trades from the outset, have a high risk-profit ratio and achieve their goal within a very short time. Unfortunately, only limited market volatility can be predicted.

EURUSD past = future?

Hello dear subscriber,

The year 2018 is over and with a close of 1.14403 the EURUSD says goodbye to the old year. At the end of the year 2018, I would like to take stock of the situation and see if it will make a possible forwardlooking for the coming year. Last year, I assumed that the price would pick up faster, but I did not have the interesting overview of the Bionic supply and demand indicator and the Bionic chart at this point. Although you can not predict the future with these tools, there are many starting points that make trading easier.

Exactly 48 years ago, the first price calculation in EURUSD was made on 04.01.1971. These are 576 monthly candles, 2,448 weekly candles, 12,607 day candles and 38,564 different H4 candles. There is no currency pair that has more information and that's why I like to work with the EURUSD.

The course of a price is basically random, you can only work with probabilities to derive possibly a profitable trade. Why today can weather forecasts be predicted more accurately than a few hundred years ago? This is due to the huge amounts of data available today and from which one can draw certain conclusions. Of course, weather forecasts are not always accurate, but the more data records are available, the more accurate hit rates are possible.

We want to check whether it is possible to calculate or predict a future price from past data.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Although I used annual candles during the course of the stock market from 1971 to today (Figure A), Figure B gives me much more information through the Bionic supply and demand indicator. We will talk about this in detail next year. On the right-hand side, we see the two developed auxiliary indicators (bionic supply and demand indicator and bionic chart) in operation for the year 2018. Here we see how the demand market has increased in relation to the supply market in the last 2 months. From that we could assume for 2019 another demand market.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

I once created an interesting calculation. This is about the annual range (high-low) of EURUSD. In the last 48 years 25 times the bulls and 23 times the bears have the nose ahead. On average, a demand market managed 1717 Pip, while a supply market averaged 1914 Pip. The graph shows how the demand and supply markets have changed. You can clearly see that in the last five years four times the supply market had the nose ahead. In 2018, the supply market, at 1341 Pip, was 30% below the average. From this one could assume a possible demand market for the year 2019.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Let's leave the annual range of high and low and deal specifically with supply and demand in the form of uptrends or downtrends. From 1971-2018 I once drew the main trends with the respective strength in Pip. Here it is noticeable that the average demand market was at 3600 pip while the average supply market reached 3100 pip. Interestingly, the smallest trend had reached at least 1300 pip. If you look at the entire course as a whole, it is noticeable that all previous supply markets can be regarded as pullback in principle, since the price has basically moved upwards since 1971. Of course, there were up and down trends within the price history. It's interesting to point out that trends between 1300 pip and 3000 pip pullbacks represent, movements above 3000 pip a true trend. If we followed this principle, we would still be in a downward trend.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Now let's take a closer look at these trends. There is no temporal division, as a trend is not oriented to months or years. The supply and demand markets have been evenly distributed over the past 48 years. While the demand markets reached 47,100 pip, the supply markets added up to 40,800 pip. Figure A compared the strength of the two markets. Figure B shows the respective difference from the demand market to the supply market graphically. Here you immediately notice a repetition of the lines. Based on this presentation one could have the assumption that the year 2019 brings a further upward trend.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

The basic past trend of the past 48 years is bullish and has moved in a range of 10,700 pip. From the first price record in 1971 until the end of 2018, the price has increased by 6,300 Pip. This means that in 2018 he achieved about 60% of the overall rank. On average, the price has risen by 1,002 pip per year and dropped by 868 pip at the same time. Based on this consideration, one could expect a further increase.

We once calculated that the volatility of the price reached on average per minute between 3,000 and 5,000 pip per day. Now assuming 250 trading days per year and assuming 4,000 pip per day, that would be a cumulative volatility of 1,000,000 pip per year. However, since the price has risen on average by only 134 pip during this time, one could conclude that the price is mostly in a sideways range in most of the time. This increases the likelihood that it could continue in the future. Incidentally, that's one of the reasons why I became a Scalper. In a market that consists almost entirely of sideways movement, long-term trend trading is too risky and unprofitable for me.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Normally, the movements build on each other and give the typical graph that we know from the month chart from 1971 to today. I have not cumulated the flow of trends so they are running around a zero point. From this graph, one could also assume that the next trend could be an uptrend. However, we do not know at the moment if the last downtrend is actually over.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

I have shown these trends once with bars. If the last downtrend is completed, a higher uptrend would be expected. But even this assumption is purely speculative, since the last red bar could also extend.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Point A and B was the beginning of a strong demand market. Whether point C can become a stronger demand market again is open. If we look at this trend C in our well-known overview, it looks at first glance very logical. The only problem is that at the moment we can not say if the last downtrend is actually over. The fact is that we can expect an upward trend again after the end of a downtrend. Unfortunately, we never know if the current trend is actually a trend or a pullback.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

It is therefore very difficult to determine what will happen in the future. What we know with great certainty is that the market is always on the move and that a price basically moves up and down in undulations. In addition, we also know that a trend (with our attitude) has moved up or down by at least 1300 pip. However, this is also due to the attitude of our indicator. But that is no guarantee for the future. A trader needs movement to derive a trade and this movement is definitely there.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

We realize that you can not make a binding statement about a future price development. One can indeed make a statement, if this statement occurs, however, is pure coincidence. Regardless of whether one balances individual currency strengths in the market, observes news, applies technical analysis, is influenced by analysts or acts purely on indicators, the result remains a coincidence. Thus, all statements made to the trade are, no matter whether they sound logical or not a mere random product. Neither science nor logic is able to create order in a random market. Therefore, I believe that such a random market can only be countered with its own chaotic strategy. Computer technology and algorithms are successful when the necessary capital is available to strongly influence markets. It is clear that discussing about a random market would not help, so every trader must seek his optimal path.

In fact, it does not matter if we have a supply or demand market, because within these different markets, there are up and down trends again, always moving up or down in undulations. Even if we knew that at the end of the year the price would be 1.35, we would not benefit from it. The background is, we do not know how far the price is going down. So if we were to trade in January at 1.145, it could happen that the price goes down to 1.122 before moving back into an uptrend. Crucial is exactly what happens at this moment. That's exactly what the Bionic Supply and Demand Indicator was developed for. The graphic presentation gives us important information about how strong a supply market or demand market has been in the past. From this we can roughly deduce what could happen next. Of course, this is not a guarantee, but the hit rate is over 50% and that is a crucial factor for long-term profitability. In 2019, we will deal with this topic in concrete terms and get to know many different examples. At first glance this looks very complicated, but the more often you deal with it the easier it gets. The goal of every trader is profitable trading, I am convinced that our way of dealing with supply and demand can make a big contribution.

I sincerely wish you to find a possible way to make it even more successful next year.

best regards

Only a miracle ...

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Tess a magical eight-year-old, went into her room and pulled a glass jam jar from the hiding place in the closet. She poured all the money on the floor and counted it carefully - three times. The entire sum had to be exactly the right one. Carefully she put the coins back in the glass, close the lid on and slipped out of the back door. She walked six blocks down to the Drug Store with the big red Indian chief on the sign above the door.

Patiently she waited until it was her turn. "Well, little lady, how can I help you?" Asked the pharmacist. I want to buy a miracle, Tess replied. A miracle, asked the pharmacist? My little brother Andrew is very ill, something bad is growing in his head, and my dad says that only a miracle can save him. What does such a miracle cost? "We do not sell miracles here, little girl. I'm sorry, but I can not help you, 'said the pharmacist.' Listen, I have money to pay for it. And if it's not enough, I'll get the rest. Just tell me how much it costs.'

Behind her stood a well-dressed man. He leaned down and asked the little girl, 'What miracle does your brother need?' 'I do not know,' Tess answered, her eyes filling with tears. 'All I know is that he is really sick and Mommy says he needs surgery. But my daddy can not pay her, so I want to take my money. 'How much do you have?' asked the man. 'One doller and eleven cents,' Tess answered barely audibly. 'And that's all the money I have, but I can get more if I have to.'

Well, what a coincidence, 'smiled the man. 'One dollar and eleven cents - exactly the price for a miracle for little brothers.' He took her money in one hand and with the other hand he grabbed hers and said, 'Show me where you live. I want to see your brother and meet your parents. Let's see if I have the miracle you need.'

This well-dressed man was a surgeon specializing in neuro-surgery. The surgery was done for free, and it was not long before Andrew was back home and fine. Mom and Dad happily related the events that had happened so well. 'This operation,' whispered her mom, she was a real miracle. I would like to know what it costs. '

Tess smiled. She knew exactly how much a miracle costs ... a dollar and eleven cents ...

On the stock exchange, an unexpected earnings message can also cause a fall in price as investors do not believe that such a return can be repeated. Similarly, a profit warning can provide a rising price because investors believe in the company. Likewise, Fed or ECB actions have a positive or negative impact on currencies.

We work in a market that does not act logically. Because if everything was logical, most could understand it and thus the market would be predictable. And unfortunately he is not. Maybe one could also say, luckily it is not logical and therefore it is profitable for the traders who do not approach the market with logic.

The price was 70 pip down and 70 pip up today, was that the shutdown or was it due to other reasons? Although a shutdown weakens the dollar for a moment, it does not strengthen the euro. Of course, this has an impact on the EURUSD, but unfortunately we just do not know when and in which strength.

And this approach is worth a lot if you only move in the market for a short time. Why are the high frequency traders today so dangerous for all traders? Because they complete their trades within a few minutes. They are not predictable. Being Scalper is dangerous, but very effective in mastering this type of trade. No matter what happens in the market, the hardest job of a trader is to find his right way. Maybe supply and demand will help you a bit, but it takes a lot of time and nerves to find your way. Important movements within supply and demand

Hello dear subscribers,

We have already talked about supply and demand in great detail. With the help of the bionics offer and demand indicator we are able to visualize these crucial zones graphically on the MT 4 surface. In today's blog I would like to point out another way I have gone.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Within a supply or demand market, arbitrary candle formations arise in the form of bullish and bearish candles. With the original candles, it is often difficult to see the clear strength at a glance. The Bionic Chart filters out just these bullish and bearish moves, so you can immediately see the crucial moves at a glance. Nevertheless, within a demand market there is often a strong downward movement. Being a demand market, the main move goes up, but within that main move, there are some moves sideways or down. What exactly interested me now was the countermovement within a supply or demand market. So all bearish movements within a demand market and all bullish movements within a supply market.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

The result can be seen here. Within a demand market, only the bearish movements were made visible and within a supply market only the bullish movements. I wanted to find out if it is possible to filter out certain information in order to increase the probability of winning.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

At point 1 we can see how a strong supply market is going down. Between points 1 and 2, there were no objections from the cops. The course could therefore run down unhindered. Only at point 2 there were again buyers who came to the market. From point 2 to point 3, the course went unhindered down again. Only from point 3 you can see again how the buyers came more into the market. As we know, these fast downward moves are usually attributed to a pullback, so I've marked the zones where the sellers came heavily into the market with a blue line. It is interesting to realize that this zone can also be considered as a kind of resistance zone.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Here we see the EURUSD in H1 and can also see here that in a strong supply zone, we can always expect the same price regions with strong buyers.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Please note that this is only about the offer zones within which some buyers were willing to bring the price up. It is interesting to realize that within a supply market, level buyers have occurred at a similar price each time.

From this, it is also possible to determine resistance zones that could be interesting for future price developments. In addition, one can deduce when a supply market or demand market may possibly be over. Another interesting aspect:

If I am on an upward trajectory and realize that there are no significant bearish moves, I would be able to stay longer in my trade.

The information I got during some trading days was very interesting and I am convinced that it is worthwhile to deal with this kind of consideration.

I've created a profile for you to download as Zipp. You store the indicators in your MT4 and the profile folder sets your profile from the MT4. Then you just call up the profile in the MT4. I have already explained several times how you are doing this installation and you are welcome to read it again in the past blogs.

I hope that it will help and wish you a successful trading day.

best regards

Project No. 5 begins!

Hello dear traders,

As a counter-trend scalper you have to be able to make the right decisions within a few seconds. If you want to counter trend in a strong trend, it requires the highest concentration and commitment. With the development of the Bionic charts and the Bionic supply and demand indicator, we have succeeded in an interesting project to trade the respective pullbacks in the different trends. A pullback has the advantage that the movement is very fast and efficient on the stage. Within minutes, 6-10 pip profit can be achieved with relatively small stops of 1-2 pip. This kind of trades can be found very often during a trading day and are very efficient for me. I prefer 6 pip yield in 6 minutes rather than 24 pip in 120 minutes. In the first case one reached 1 pip / min, while in the second case a 5 times worse result was achieved. In Case 2, I am helplessly exposed to a randomly acting market for an additional 114 minutes. The chance of a strong unexpected breakout is 20 times as high as in 6 minutes within 120 minutes. Since I attach a high priority to the pip / min ratio in my money management, these pullbacks come first with me.

With the Bionic supply and demand indicator this ride on the razor blade succeeds quite well, but there is still considerable room for improvement. This brings us to the next project no. 5.

The bionic supply and demand indicator is time-independent, but the chart image is not. Now you could combine a Renko chart with the Bionic supply and demand indicator, but the Renko chart is created from the inaccurate price data that most brokers pass on. In addition, the Bionic supply and demand indicator generates the broker's OHLC data rather than the Renko chart.

Tick charts are time-independent charts. A tick represents a transaction between buyer and seller at a given price and volume. In this form, you determine after how many trades a period has ended. A tick chart with the setting 63 Tick means nothing else, that after 63 new trades a new candle is drawn. It does not matter if in a trading transaction only 1 contract or 100 contracts are traded.

This has the advantage that in many trade transactions, such as economic numbers, many candles arise or in pre-market and nightly trade, where there is little going on, only a few candles. Disadvantage, the presentation is that you see virtually no hammer or shooting stars. If you look at the volume, you can see that almost every candle in the tickchart is converted into the same volume. But this disadvantage is not a disadvantage for me, because I basically pay no attention to the volume in time-based charts and the chart images. However, the volume in the tick chart offers an interesting opportunity. If the tick chart is compared in combination with the classic time-based chart, very interesting aspects arise.

Not time based

At times with little buying and selling activities, such as just before the market closes or at lunchtime, the market usually relaxes a bit. A classic 1-hour chart shows us many little candles without basic information during these periods. On the other hand, during quieter periods, the tick chart only shows us one or two candles, avoiding a collection of small candles. Thus, a trendless section in a time-based chart can dramatically change the support and resistance levels, leading to completely different investment decisions.

More meaningful price analysis

If many investors are active, a time-based chart is not always "fast" enough. Even if you choose a 1-minute chart, a strong price rise or fall is displayed as a long candle in this case. The tick chart divides these strong candles. This allows you to draw in a clear resistance line that gives you a clearer trend over a period of time.

Confirm trendline breakthroughs

Support and resistance lines can be completely different depending on the time view used. In the tick chart stops the resistance. A trader who has both charts available can wait until a clear trend is visible below or above a resistance line, and thus make a more efficient decision.

Clear signals to the market exit

Since resistance zones can be identified even more clearly, both market entry and market exit can be seen even more clearly. We will analyze this background more clearly in the coming weeks.

Coherence of volume and price development

In the normal time-based chart, the volume only indicates the amount of traded securities during a given period. He does not provide any information as to whether the title was bought or sold by major investors or private investors. In the tick view, on the other hand, each volume bar represents the number of titles traded per candlestick. Since the number of transactions per candlestick is the same, each volume bar displays the average volume of all transactions of the corresponding candlestick. If a volume bar is higher than the average in the Tick volume chart, it can be assumed that the transaction was made by a large investor. Major players often have more information and are more critical about their investments. Their market entry at a certain price often suggests the future trend.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Here you can see a comparison M1 with a tick chart. Both were equipped with the Bionic chart and the Bionic supply and demand indicator. Now it is interesting to filter out the strongest movements within the strongest zones. These strongest moves give us a clearer indication of future resistance zones. The tick chart is able to better divide these strong moves. In addition, the supply and demand zones are changing. Perhaps this information could lead to an even more reliable statement and reduce our risk even more.

We are curious what the results will be. In any case, we will share this information with you on a regular basis.

Hello dear subscribers,

In the last few weeks, we compared and tested different tick charts for the MT4. What remained are two providers of tick charts: Rainwood and OVO.

Basically one can say that both tick charts have achieved equally good results, but we were looking for the optimal tick indicator for our personal requirements.

Rainwood tickchart indicator:

The indicator costs $ 49 for an unlimited license, but there is no description of whether there is any limitation on the trading account and whether this license can be run on different computers. There is no demo version, you first have to buy a month license for $ 7 to test the indicator. The installation is a bit more complicated than with the OVO, if you call the indicator you have to enter two previously sent passwords within 30 seconds, otherwise the indicator will close again. The selection of tick data is much better than the OVO, you can load tick data without histiorie, tick data generated from the M1 and download tick data from a third party. Which third party it is, is not explained. Depending on the period of tick data, this download may take some time. A 60 tickchart from the last 2 weeks took a total of 5:47 minutes with a 100 Mbit line at the weekend. Unfortunately, the tick data of the third party was nothing as accurate as the tick data of my broker, that clouded the advantage a bit. The tick charts can be displayed directly below the M1 chart and / or in the offline chart. A clear advantage over the OVO, but the change to another tick size is very cumbersome and takes longer than the OVO. Similarly, installing a second tick chart on the same screen is very confusing and complicated. The performance suffers significantly when multiple charts are open. Interesting: There are many additional tools that are not available at the OVO. In the offline chart all indicators can be used.

OVO tickchart indicator:

There is a demo version that you can test for 2 weeks for free, then an unlimited license costs $ 45. This license is for 3 Windows accounts and within these accounts there is no limit on open windows. Theoretically, if you split the three accounts, 3 traders can pay $ 15 for access. There is an indicator that serves the offline chart. The tick data is generated from the M1 of the broker, tick data of a third party does not exist unfortunately. When you call the tickchart in the morning, it sometimes comes in the past courses to the same size candles that look like a Renkochart. We also noticed this at Rainwood, but you can also download the data from the third-party provider there to avoid this problem. As soon as the tickchart starts to run, the tick data are drawn correctly on the Rainwood and OVO. However, it is crucial here which tick data your broker delivers. With the free indicator Omnia Remote you can change the number of ticks in the offline chart very quickly. The OmniaAutoVolume indicator automatically changes the tick count as you type, but this indicator is rather counterproductive to our application.
Installing a second tick chart on the same screen is much easier than with the Rainwood. Performance does not suffer in OVO when multiple charts are open.

Conclusion:

Both indicators generate very good tick charts from the M1, although there were differences here as well. However, it is not possible to determine which indicator has the nose in front, as there is no exact reference value. The Rainwood offers the tick data of a third party, if you have a broker that offers inadequate data, the Rainwood is the first choice. For the handling with the OVO is easier and the performance suffers much less. That's why we chose the OVO, although you can not say it's better than the Rainwood. Both indicators have their strengths and weaknesses. This is like the Mercedes and BMW, both are excellent vehicles, but I opted for the Mercedes, because it offers more benefits for me than the BMW. Nevertheless, the BMW is the first choice for many others. The key is that one product offers you more benefits than another. Project 4

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Hello dear traders,

In the last weeks we have examined different settings with our tickchart. The goal was to find out if these tick charts can be used to identify trend reversals more quickly than with a standard chart.

Basically, after a few years I realized that as a trader you should not use the standard indicators like MACD, RSI or Moving Average. The fastest indicator is the candle chart. So I focused primarily on the candle presentation.

Conventional charts are time-based charts, each time unit is specified. The standard time settings M1, M5, M15, M30, H1, H4, D1, W1 and MN have been set arbitrarily. The intervals of the time units are not uniform, but distributed very differently. From M1 to H1 there are 5 different time units, from H1 to MN there are just 4 different time units. The greater the time unit, the more accurate the expressiveness of a candle. Strangely, standard settings place more emphasis on inaccurate statements. Whether a uniform time distribution brings greater benefits, I dare to doubt strongly.

In the past I compared the Heiken Ashi strategy with the standard candle. Heikin Ashi Charts smooth the price movements and thereby create a clearer chart image. This allows the viewer to easier identification of the major trend movements. Normally, the parameters are chosen so that green candles are upwards and red candles are downtrend. In strong uptrends candles without shadows occur, in strong downward trends are primarily candles without wick to be found. In strong trends, the candle bodies are larger. Occur small candles, this is an indication of a consolidation or a trend change. The same applies to candles with wick and shadow. In consolidation and trendless phases, a frequent change between red and green candles is typical. What bothered me here was that you should also use an RSI as confirmation to enter into positions in oversold or overbought market situations. In addition, it is still a time-based chart.

The main reason why there used to be only time-based charts in the past is the lack of technology in the past. At the time, exchanges simply did not have the ability to provide market participants with access to real-time data. However, with the advancement of technology, when stock market trading took place around the clock, which was associated with higher volatility, traders experimented with a variety of charting methods. This created the first time-independent chart images.

An ordinary chart represents the price within a set timeframe. Renko charts, on the other hand, only visualize the price, regardless of time. They only present the price once it has passed through a certain minimum amount of movements. Price changes that do not reach this minimum amount are ignored, making it easier to focus on significant movement and hide the background noise. However, the movements refer to Pip rather than ticks.

When we focus on ticks, we distinguish range charts, volume charts and tick charts. Since rangebars are not suitable for OHCL analysis, only volume charts and tick charts are shortlisted.

The volume chart creates a new candle every time a predetermined volume of contracts is traded. The volume corresponds to the trading activity and is thus the energy of the market movements. With fixed volume charts we can observe what the market is doing with the same amount of energy. Tick charts are comparable to the volume charts. Instead of using the volume as a basis, we use a tick on the tick chart as a basis. These charts set a certain number of ticks (trades) regardless of the volume traded. This presentation was the most optimal for our type of trade.

With the development of our supply and demand indicator, supply and demand zones were drawn on our chart automatically which were absolutely time-independent. The problem was still the candle, which was formed only time-dependent. Although we were able to use the Bionic Chart to depict a candle structure that at one glance could only show the opposite pullback within this movement, this candle was also time-based.

With the now used Tickcharts the first goal could be achieved. Both the candle formation in the Bionic Chart and the supply and demand zone formation are now based on a time-independent calculation. Interesting are the supply and demand zones, which are now formed from the ticks. From our point of view, these zones are now formed even more precisely and in combination with the Bionic Chart, even more reliable statements can be made.

In the last 2 weeks we had an average of about 92,160 ticks per day. That would be about 64 ticks per minute. In other words, we could consider the following tick sizes in our time-based charts: M1 = 64 ticks, M5 = 320 ticks, M15 = 960 ticks, M30 = 1,920 ticks, H1 = 3,840 ticks, H4 = 15,360 ticks and D1 = 92,120 ticks

In our tickchart, however, we can make any setting in increments of 1 tick, so that all possible time units can be set every second.

In a 3,840 tick chart we can see the resistors in a medium trend and now go down slowly in 100 tick steps to analyze how the candle formation in this resistance zone changes. As a result, the resistance zone can often be reduced to 0.5 Pip. In the time-based chart, we were happy when our zone was 3-5 pip.

Conclusion:

With the tickchart, the zones can be significantly reduced. This increases the risk profit ratio tremendously. However, you have to proceed very carefully in these small zones so as not to be permanently stopped. Very interesting are auxiliary indicators, such as the Denstiy indicator, which measures the individual candle thickness. In the tickchart I get here once more detailed information that help me a lot in the trade implementation. A time-independent chart image will definitely provide more accurate information than a time-based chart image. This will allow us to significantly reduce our resistance zones and optimize the risk-to-reward ratio. There will be some examples within the next few weeks.

I wish you a successful trading day

best regards

Download and test a tick chart

Hello dear subscribers,

After testing several tick charts within a few weeks, we came to the conclusion that the OVO Tick Chart offers the most benefits to our approach. In order to avoid surreptitious advertising for a particular provider, I would like to reiterate that the Rainwood Tick Chart delivers just as good results and even offers more benefits in some areas. Unfortunately, you have to invest at least $ 8 for the Rainwood Tickchart to try it for 30 days. I do not think that's customer friendly.
The OVO Tickchart is free for the first 15 days and then you can decide whether a tickchart brings significant benefits or not.

Under

https://ovo.cz/products/offline-char...t-volume-bars/

you can download the indicator. In addition, I recommend that you also download the free indicator Omnia Remote Control. The two indicators are simply stored in the folder indicator of the MT4.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Now open the tick chart indicator in the M1 Chart. It is important that you allow the import of DLL. (Point 1) At point 2 you write the number of ticks you want to show and under point 3 the number of candles you want to start with. That was all.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

In your M1 Chart you can now see on the bottom of the number of ticks you have entered and the button M61. At this very moment, an offline chat called M61 was created. If you press this button the offline chart M61 opens.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

At first, you will only see candles for this now open offline chart. Now you can populate this offline chart with all the indicators that are important to you. In this offline chart you now take the indicator Omnia Remote Control. Then a control field appears in the lower field. This allows you to change the number of ticks directly in the offline chart.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

An average day contains about 92160 ticks. On average, that's 64 ticks per minute. Converting the known time units from M1 to MN into ticks, for example, gives 15,360 ticks for the 4 hour chart.

To enter these numbers again and again was very stressful for me. There is a little trick here, though. In the remote control, there is an arrow to the right and left of your specified number. If you press the right arrow, the number of entered numbers will double and if you press the left arrow, the value will halve.

If you start now with the value 4 and press the right arrow again and again you get to the known time units already very close to it. The right table shows the number of ticks and the time units translated for them.

However, we have to be aware that we are leaving the time-based units with a tickchart. Accordingly, the time units known to us are no longer so crucial.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

This can be seen very well in the following example. In the picture above, I have shown an M1 chart in EURUSD on Friday, 22/02/19 from 16:00 until the close of trading.

Below that is a 64 tickchart within the same time window. If you compare the HH and the LL with each other, you will notice that these changes are shown on the chart. The timing of a HH and LL is always the same, however, a 64 tickchart means that as soon as 64 trading orders are received a candle is formed. Of course, the resulting price will also be charged. This means that the faster the number of ticks runs, the larger the time window will be, as more candles are formed at this moment. For example, if fewer ticks are running within a time period in the Asian market, the displayed time window will apparently be smaller.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Shortly before point 3, the M1 forms a strong bullish candle that goes up. In the 64 tick chart you will see four candles instead of one candle. If you pull the strongest candle to the right, you will notice the resistance area as soon as the course returns. In the M1, this resistance range is 3 times greater. And that is precisely the concrete advantage in terms of supply and demand for me. With the help of the tick charts I am able to reduce my resistance ranges significantly. In the M1, the resistance range was 10 pip and I would have reached a price-to-earnings ratio of 1: 0.8 with great difficulty at the close of trading. In the 64 Tickchart you could have achieved a price-earnings ratio of 1: 6. Of course, with a lot of experience you can significantly reduce the M1 resistance range, but this is also possible in the 64 Tickchart.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

In the following case, we reduced the tickchart to 16 ticks and were thus able to reduce the resistance range to 1.5 pip. This increases the risk profit ratio to 1:12. However, the profit pip / min was just 0.13 pip but you have to take the risk if you are dealing with the trend. The big advantage is that with this tickchart I can reduce my resistance ranges very flexibly.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Finally, I wanted to know how many different tick charts I'm able to install on a chart. On the left side you will see the candle strength indicator of Hannover and on the right the Zwinner Trend indicator. I have each made a subdivision of the bulls and bears and processed from the middle evenly rising ticks. This allowed me to easily accommodate 40 different tick charts in one MT4. In addition, there were in no way any performance issues. I built this scoreboard for testing purposes only, but I was very surprised how exactly this scoreboard works. If there should be need in this area, I am ready to post a profile. I will do a video on Monday and post, then you can even make a picture yourself.

If you create different tickcharts created by M61, consecutively (M61, M62, M63 ....) In the offline folder, this simplifies the installation significantly.

Of course, I do not know if this tick indicator makes sense for you, I can only recommend it for free for two weeks. If it brings you something, then you have come a little closer to your goal. Of course, I can not say if in your case the Rainwood Tick chart might be the better choice. No matter which area you choose, the biggest advantage is to say goodbye to the time-based charts. However, this also requires a certain habituation effect. I hope I could give you some information.

Where is the strongest movement?

Hello dear subscribers,

In the area of supply and demand, the strongest movements are a decisive feature in order to determine future resistance zones. However, this is difficult when a course has gone up or down sharply.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

On the 21st of February at 14:30 CET, the course in the M1 has gone up by just under 17 pip within 1 minute. Since the price moves on average by 1.3 pips in the M1 (average of the last 30,000 candles), a movement of 17 pips is already above average. Placing a resistance range of 17 pip here would be ineffective. So we have to figure out in which area the movement was strongest.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

For that, we need to examine the movement more closely. A seconds chart would help, but has the disadvantage that it is a time-dependent motion. In the tick chart you can see how you can easily filter out the strongest movement. In this case, the resistance zone was reduced from 17 pip to 3 pip.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

If you look at the resulting price history, it becomes clear, which advantage one has thereby.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Even when the course entered the zone from below, it was possible to enter into two interesting trades with this resistance zone. Basically, this procedure is only recommended for Scalper, of course, swing trader have an advantage when resistance zones can be reduced.

A tick chart offers the advantage of dividing a strong candle into individual movements, a kind of MRI Magnetic Resonance Imaging. If I know in which area the strongest movement has started, I am able to significantly reduce my resistance zones. This allows me closer entry points a much smaller stop and thus a better risk profit ratio.

As you know, there are certain price levels where the big players always like to buy or sell. The Tick Chart helps to pinpoint these price levels. I've seen in the last few weeks that many movements have become clearer. I still do not manage to anticipate every move exactly. But the rate has improved significantly. Maybe it's because I now have a chart image that works completely independent of time. The division of the candle is clearer and with the Bionic chart you can see the pullback within a candle even in the smallest movements.

The supply- and demand Indicator are time-independent anyway, and the Bionic chart now also uses the Tickchart indicator. All other indicators that you would use are also independent of time. The numbers above or below my zones show me by the time-independent view now more accurate values. However, it will take some time to draw concrete conclusions from this.

Conclusion:

The results so far exceeded my expectations, the movements are becoming clearer and the mistakes made are significantly reduced. Pullbacks within a trend can be identified more quickly for faster profits. By reducing the stops, the risk profit ratio could be improved. Getting used to is the time-independent charting. If you have always acted time-dependent you need some time to get along with this presentation. All in all, it is worth pursuing this idea, we will of course keep you up to date.

The bionic chart

Hello dear subscriber,

As requested, I would like to take a closer look at the Bionic chart and explain why it was developed.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

A normal candle comes from the OHLC data given by the market. If the close is above the open, the candle is bullish, the close is under the open, it is a bearish candle. Due to the given time units M1 to MN arises in most candles, an upper and a lower shadow. The focus is on the actual candle body, so the shadows receive less attention. The open and the close arise only because of the timing M1, M5, M15 ... and have nothing to do with the strength of the current trend.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

The Bionic Chart recognizes at first glance that there are no shadows and that the open has been dispensed with. As a rule, one can do without this information as the close of the previous candle usually indicates the open of the new candle. The close is basically displayed in the Bionic Chart, so that the open of the new candles can be recognized quickly. Of course, gaps also occur in the course of the price. Price gaps do not only arise between the candles but also within the candles. Only inside the candles they are not recognizable. At first it looks like the Bionic Chart can not show the gap because of the abandonment of the Open, but with the help of the bar chart I can also show the Bionic Chart open if it is important. With that you can also identify gaps.

When a candle closes, two pieces of information are important to me. First, it is a bullish or a bearish candle and how strong was the pullback inside the candle. Take a bullish candle as an example.

The course opens at the open and then runs down to the low. At this moment, the candle is colored red. As soon as the course goes up again and over the open, a lower shadow is created and the candle turns green. Actually, this is already a pullback. However, this pullback is no longer interesting for me when the candle closes and the Close is over the Open. Much more interesting for me in this case is the pullback from high to close.

What is the reason for that:

In principle, the two shadows of a candle are pullbacks. As a rule, they are displayed neutrally. In the case of a bullish candle, in most cases the lower shadow is displayed first and the upper shadow is created just before the close. This means that the last pullback (upper shadow) for me is closer to the current price than the first pullback (lower shadow).

This gives me with the last pullback far more information than from the first pullback. Another point is very important. The lower shadow has been clearly overcome by the course, as the open is below the Close. The upper shadow, however, seems to be initially a limit.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Now let's look at a normal candle chart in EURUSD H1. Of course you can draw in this picture also resistance zones, but I miss in this picture a certain clarity.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

With the Bionic Chart, it is easier for me personally to locate resistance zones more easily. And these zones can also be drawn more accurately.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Here's the same time window on how to use the Bionic chart to highlight the pullbacks within a candle. You can often see in the course of a downtrend or uptrend how the pullbacks within a candle become stronger and eventually the trend changes. Pullbacks within a candle help to identify upcoming trend reversals faster.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Of course you can only visualize the pullbacks. This will quickly reveal what bearish objections are in an uptrend or what bullish objections are in a downtrend.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Here we have turned the tables once and made the Bionic candle movement visible. It can be seen very often, the more the strength of this movement decreases the higher the probability of an upcoming trend reversal.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

As you can see, the two views differ from the candle chart and Bionic Chart. This is simply because the first pullback in the ongoing movement is included. To make the picture clearer, I recommend using the Bionic chart to gray the pullbacks.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Finally, I would like to introduce you to another way to present the candle in one color. This type of presentation is suitable for a rough overview and shows the clear trends faster.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Here I would like to show you an interesting example:

Here is a Bionic chart displayed in a 64 tick chart. The candles were all colored gray and the momentum indicator ensures that all candles that have reached at least 1 pip from the open to the close are marked in the respective color. These are each the strongest movements. Trend views can also be identified more quickly with this view.

Conclusion:

We recognize that the Bionic Chart is very flexible and reduces the information to the essentials. Turnarounds can be identified more quickly by the pullbacks as well as by the pure movements. This makes it easier to identify and draw resistance zones. With the help of a tick chart, the time factor can be eliminated and thus the information can be displayed even more accurately. Since the open was waived, one can make much better statements with 25% less information in the future.

I hope I have been able to give you some information and I wish you another successful trading day today

best regards

The new Bionic Pullback Indicator

Hello dear subscribers,

Over the past few weeks, we've been busy setting up and optimizing the tick charts. That's why I posted fewer posts, as the time was huge. Nevertheless, we have come a step further in the findings.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

The development of the supply and demand indicator and the Bionic candle served to identify the strongest zones within a trend. Within a downtrend, here an example in H1, there are strong and weaker moves down. As soon as the course goes up again you can see that he overcomes the weak movements downwards, while he fails at the strong movements and is pushed down again. The goal is to filter out the strongest movements to identify future reversals. This was possible with the previous color setting of the Bionic candle, but not as clear.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

In my previous post I have written some information about this. A key advantage is that you only see the last decisive pullback within a candle. Thus, the strength of a candle can be seen at a glance. The larger the last pullback, the weaker the movement. However, the limitation of these movements is in the M1, since this is the smallest time unit. To bring the stops below 1pip, I have to be able to look closer into the candle. This is often only possible in a tickchart.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Let's look at a concrete example. On Friday the 08.03.19 between 14:28 to 14:45 CET there was suddenly a strong movement within 5 minutes at 23 pip and then a movement around 27 pip down. In the following 7 minutes the course went up again. In the past it was difficult for me to draw a resistance zone from this movement, because in this case I only had 17 candles and the candles were often not clear enough.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

In the 32 Tickchart I received in the same time 228 information about the strength of the individual movements. That was an average of 13 candles per minute. This immediately enabled me to identify the strongest zones within these uncontrolled movements. You can see very well how the strongest movement at point 1 ensures that at point 2 the decisive downward trend is initiated. The two underlying candles also showed a strong movement and had an influence on the price performance. You can see that the course just before point 2 starts to weaken.

What does it mean to identify the strongest candle within a downward movement? This strongest candle means that most of the sales have occurred at this price level at this time. The likelihood is very high that when the price goes up again, it will be in this strong price level again to strong sales.

However, there is no guarantee for this because the strength of the lower resistance is crucial to the uptrend. And if the lower resistance is stronger than the upper resistance, the upper resistance zone is broken by the upward trend.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

First let's look at a very interesting discovery. As a rough example, I'm using the EURUSD in H1 from Jul to Aug 2018. We see a downtrend and immediately thereafter an uptrend of 440 pip each.

In the downtrend we can see that the bullish pullbacks within the Bionic charts are much stronger than the bearish pullbacks. In the uptrend, the bearish pullbacks within the Bionic charts are much stronger than the bullish pullbacks. This is not about the number of pullbacks, but about the size.

In the indicator I developed, you can see these pullbacks very nicely and you can see that in a downtrend bullish pullbacks are much stronger. When a downtrend is strong, the effort to turn it over is very high. As long as the bullish pullbacks are small within the downtrend, the downward trend is strong. As soon as the pullbacks get bigger, the trend weakens.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

At points 1,2 and 3 we detect the strongest movements down and record our resistance zones there. At point 4 we identify the strongest upward movement and record our resistance zone there. They recognize how exactly the zones are to be identified.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

To make it easier for most, I switched the colors of the pullback indicator. So you can immediately tell if it is a strong uptrend or downtrend.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Please note that these calculations are the relevant pullback for me. Within most candles, there are two pullbacks, which are presented in the form of a shadow. The lower shadow of a bullish candle is not relevant for me, as the price went up significantly above the open afterwards. The upper shadow of a bearish candle is not relevant for me, as the price went down significantly over the open afterwards. The pullback in the Bionic chart is for me the last relavant price movement just before the Close. Of course, there are exceptions in some cases, but they were not taken into account.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

I have created the two important indicators for you here. The Bionic chart Historam pullback indicator, which on the chart instead of the normal candles, filters out only the pullbacks of a move. The Bionic Pullback Indicator below shows in the overview the strength of the respective trend.

However, you always have to keep an eye on all the movements in order to draw possible conclusions. As already mentioned, a time-based chart is clearly at a disadvantage compared to a tick chart. Although the indicators running in the tickchart, they still need to be adjusted.

I am convinced that in many situations you can now identify the trend reverses faster. But it is like all a matter of time and exercise. The small pullbacks seem to be a crucial key to success, but unfortunately there is no basic statement in forex, which always holds. That would speak against the principle of the stock market.

Conclusion:

Based on the findings so far, we will continue to optimize and expand these pullbacks in the future. It is crucial to get a deeper insight into the candle. This information must then be adapted to the particular situation in order to make possible derivations. I still think that the candle is absolutely enough to make a trading decision. For a rough overview, I also recommend using the supply and demand indicator. You will find detailed information and instructions here on the blog.

The way seems to be the right one, but we will significantly improve the calculations over the next few years to make even better decisions. Who manages to take big profits within the small movements, for the big trend consequences are no longer relevant. Then it does not matter if we are now in an uptrend towards 1.25 or even further down. Every trend moves up and down in wavy lines and we want to take those wavy lines with us. Very small stops with big lots means a small risk for me within a short time. The shorter I stay in the market, the lower the risk of being stopped by unforeseen movements.

This trading style involves a lot of time and experience. In recent years, I have noticed that it is easier for me to anticipate short-term movements more accurately than long-term movements. Therefore, I would prefer 10 to 15 trades in a day rather than a trade to hope the price moves in my direction. With this style of trading a long-term equilibrium can be traded profitably and low volatility phases. So there is no reason to look for rewarding trades in other unpredictable currency pairs. With 3,000 trades within one year, a high level of experience is also created at the same time. But this decision must be made at the end of each trader for himself.

I wish you now that these indicators help you a little bit to capture the market faster and to identify trend reversals even more precisely. I am happy about your experience.

A successful trading week

Additional Bionic strength indicator

Hello dear subscriber,

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

In yesterday's post, I showed you two key indicators that will help you identify trend reversals more easily. For this you have once received the Bionic Chart indicator, which shows the color of the pullbacks and an additional graphical overview. Since the candle in the Bionic Chart differs significantly from a Basic Chart, I would like to make two more indicators available today for your convenience.

As I have already said, for me in the current trading bionic pullbacks are crucial factors for a possible trend reversal. In the Bionic Chart, only the bearish pullbacks are displayed in an uptrend, while in a downtrend only the bullish pullbacks are displayed. Depending on the selected time unit, candles that do not contain a pullback are also produced. I would like to elaborate on that today.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

In the Basic Candle Chart, strong candles without shadows are displayed when:

Bullish candle open / low and close / high are the same
Bearish candle open / high and low / close are the same

You will soon realize that these candles are very rare. The probability of finding such candles becomes greater the smaller the unit of time is.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

As already written, the lower shadow on a bullish candle in the Bionic Chart is completely uninteresting as it clearly overcomes the open. As soon as the high and close are on a level, this candle is drawn without a pullback as a gray candle. The same is true of the bear candle just the other way around. Of course, this is completely clear that with this form of presentation there are significantly more strong candles in the Bionic Chart than in the typical candle chart. At the same time I already get more information about a trend strength.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

As you can see there are different candles with different strengths in the Bionic Chart. As soon as a pullback is created, the candle strength is clear and clear. The gray candles without pullback are a challenge though.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Here is an example in the 1 minute chart of this morning. At least 10 gray candles without pullbacks were created within 65 minutes. Depending on the shape of the candle, it can sometimes be difficult to tell immediately if it is a bullish or bearish candle.

Here I have followed different approaches to make the gray candles visible. First, I added another indicator to the Bionic Chart that shows only the gray candles in each color. The problem was that my tidy chart became very confusing. I tried to color the strong candles in different shades of gray but that too was confusing.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Finally, I have overcome the use of an indicator, which is displayed in a separate window. This shows at a glance how big and strong each candle has been. This leaves my main chart clearly arranged to draw dark blue resistance zones.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

My basic approach has been Equilibrium for many years. An Equilibrium is relatively fast to identify in the chart and I have already written about it a few times. An equilibrium within a candle is called doji. This doji arises whenever the open and close are on a price level. In the Bionic Chart, this doji is also relatively difficult to recognize. A doji always means agreement on the price and, at the same time, an uncertainty.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

For those of you for whom this uncertainty may be important, I've added another indicator that shows you this doji in a separate window. For myself, this uncertainty is already evident from the current course, so I do not work with this indicator myself. But he helps in the beginning in identifying the doji.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Overall, the chart image would now look like this. The main chart should be cleaned up and still give as much information as possible in order to mark resistance zones efficiently.

The Bionic Pullback Indicator helps identify the current trend direction. As we noted earlier, in a bullish trend there are strong bearish pullbecks while in a bearish trend there are strong bullish pullbacks. In this indicator, only the colors were turned over to capture the trend direction faster.

Underneath you can now see the two new indicators that you can download at the end of the article. Which indicators they use for this is purely a matter of taste, I myself usually only use the Bionic chart indicator because this already provides me all the information. However, the bottom indicators might help you get a baseline in the beginning. After that I recommend to delete all indicators and to work only with the Bionic Chart.

In principle, these indicators under the main chart are a kind of support wheel on the bicycle. When I learn to ride a bicycle, I am glad to use these support wheels in an emergency. As soon as I can ride a bicycle I do not need them anymore. The more information I get as a dealer, the more insecurity arises. A little tip on the edge:

As soon as an uptrend may be over and the price is already heading down, just draw a line above the last high. Now look for a reference price on the left side within the same price level and consider the strength of this candle. This often gives them a lot of information about the strength of the possible trend sequence.

Unfortunately, the statements in a time-based chart are often very inaccurate and not clear. At some point you should consider if you do  use a tick chart.

The clear advantage of this approach is the rapid identification of the trend strength. Now try to find out for yourself which strength prevails. They'll quickly find that they'll make more accurate trade decisions over time.
