ILS system in trading

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Hello dear subscribers,

If an aircraft wants to land safely in difficult weather conditions, it will use the existing ILS system. These are beacons that are emitted from the ground. Using the instruments, the pilot knows exactly where his assigned runway and aircraft are. If he now follows exactly these beams, he is able to accomplish a complete blind approach.

We have traders struggling with the same problem every day, because we too are constantly blindfolded and do not know where the course is going. There is a kind of ILS trading system and that is the reference course for me. Let's take a look in the examples below to see how the reference course could help us in our future trading.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

In the chart you can see how a key candle forms at point A, because we had a strong resistance there. Then the price went down sharply. Based on the key candle I have marked a resistance zone. Now the course went to point B, where there was a strong demand market. This demand market pushed the price to the point C. There one could have started a nice trade in the supply market. The course went now to the point D, whereby thereby another key candle formed. From the point E onwards, a strong supply market was formed which pushed the price down to point F.

If you draw resistance and support zones, you will need a past price history, the so-called reference price. At point F you can see that we still have a reference course on the left side where we can orient ourselves. But when the price went down over the point F, the reference price of point D was no longer valid. But there was a new reference course, which was only a little further away at point B.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

In W1 you can see the course of the EURUSD within the last two years. In the area of point A, the reference price was within a small range, at point B, the range was already significantly larger. The range was greatest when the course at point C ran to 1.11. In that case you had to go back two years to find a reference course.

In the case of the reference price, the past is important because the price often moves in certain price zones, resulting in resistance and support lines.

In principle, it is relatively easy to keep track of the reference course by simply opening a W1 and observing the course. A weekly chart is very accurate, but the smaller resistance zones can not be read from it. You have to change to a smaller unit of time. But then the candles turn so small that you can not see the zones. For a Scalper in the M1 a horror scenario.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Let's first look at the H1 of the last three days. At point C the course went up through a strong resistance zone to point D. Then the course went back to point C. Zone A was crucial for the course to go up again at point E. Then the course went from point F to zone B. Since the course has already run under the point E, this zone does not interest. Decisive is to compare the zone A with the zone B.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

We are now in the M 15 and realize that the candles have become very small . The resistance zones are very difficult to identify. However, since we want to compare the two zones in the M1 with each other, the only option left is to create two different charts.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

On the left side you can now see the zone A which is shown in the M1 and beside that the zone B which is also shown in the M1. Right now I have more reference courses that I can compare with each other. In order to get an impression of it, I have created a short video. In the 3 minutes you can see that the course is in a strong resistance zone. Immediately afterwards he ran down twelve pips. In equilibrium zone 1.12 there was a strong move up to 1.127.

Inserted Video

You realize that this can be very advantageous to compare the reference price in the same time unit. Of course you have to adjust the charts from time to time but it helps to create resistance and support zones.

For example, working with Fibonacci will allow you to work in two distinct zones with two different Fibonacci. Basically, it's always about getting as much information about the price history. With the reference course, you can make it easier.

I wish you a successful trading day

best regards

Bioniccandle survey indicator

Hello dear subscribers,

In the past, I've written extensively on the Bionic Candle several times and why I've developed it. What always bothered me in the past in a normal chart picture was the upper and lower wicks. The larger the time unit I changed to, the bigger the wicks became. This confused me more. I wanted to create a candle that shows me its strength at a glance. With the development of the Bioniccandle a very good result could be achieved.

There are only two movements in the bionic candle, one main movement and one pullback. I have often reported that the pullback is more important to me than the actual main move. The larger the pullback within a candle, the weaker the candle and the smaller the pullback, the stronger the candle.

Let's look at an example

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

In the picture, we see an uptrend first, followed immediately by a downtrend of 30 pip each. As a time unit, I used a 256 tickchart comparable to an M5.

A

The course starts relatively strong at first. The first major movement is the strongest, but there are some objections from the bears due to the pullbacks.

B

At first we are in an equilibrium, which is easy to see that the pullbacks on both sides are very large. There is a bullish candle that has a relatively small pullback. The subsequent downward candle is very weak, a clear sign that the price may go higher.

C

The upward candle at C breaks through a resistance zone, the candle is relatively strong and ensures that the course continues to run upwards.

D

Here we see that the upward candle is very weak due to the pullback. Although the bulls are trying to push the course up again, but the course is initially a bit down. Based on the pullback that forms in the bearish candles, you realize that it is not a strong pullback. Our resistance zone at point C will not be overcome. Here we see that the upward candle is very weak due to the pullback. Although the bulls are trying to push the course up again, but the course is initially a bit down. Based on the pullback that forms in the bearish candles, you realize that it is not a strong return. Our resistance zone at point C will not be overcome.

E

A strong bullish candle with no pullback arises, showing how strong the resistance zone was.

F

The price is now very high and the two bearish candles are not strong. From point E to point F, the strongest bullish movement in this trend occurred.

G

On another return, we see the bearish candles getting stronger, but the bullish strength is still at an advantage.

H

Although this is only a small return, but you can already see here how strong the bearish pressure is slow. Exactly this area is already a sign to me that the course will not run too far up. However, a strong resistance zone once again forms a strong bullish candle with a small pullback that keeps the price higher.

I

In the area you can see clearly that the bullish candles lose significantly in strength. There are three strong bearish pullbacks. With the information I have already received at the point H & G on the strength of the bear candles, a good sign of a turnaround.

J

The price is initially down and a key candle is forming which could stop a possible uptrend.

K

The course is initially held back by the strong movement that has gone up from point H out. However, one can already see here that the pullbacks in the two bullish candles are very strong. This shows that they are weak upward candles. Our resistance zone at point C will not be overcome.

L

The downward movement is getting stronger, the small upward candle is relatively weak, which suggests that the price is still down.

M

The bearish move downwards becomes significantly stronger, which is also logical, because from point E to point F we had the strongest bullish movement. To break this zone you need many sales orders.

N

The course also stops short of this resistance zone and you can see that the upward movement is relatively strong. But the previous strong downwards candle can not be broken.

O

Here you can see that the bulls are slowly starting to fight back, but the bears are still on the stronger side.

P

The bears are getting weaker, which is due to the opposite equilibrium at point B.

Q

The downtrend has weakened a bit. That gives the bulls the opportunity to fight back.

R

The two upward candles are medium strong. The bulls had their chance but it is not yet so far.

S

The bears had to fight because the bulls got a little bit stronger and now there was a very strong bearish down movement. However, this movement was directly opposed by the bulls. Then another uptrend began.

Of course, you can not pinpoint each turnaround with the help of candles. Due to the Bioniccandle I get significantly more signals that give me better information than a normal candle.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Since candles experience moving in a zigzag line up and down, it is relatively difficult to compare these candles with each other. I wanted to create an environment where I could compare the bionic candles next to each other. The Bioniccandle survey indicator was created for this purpose.

Surely you have already noticed that the indicator does not display Doji, or in this case an empty field is created. Although a doji means an uncertainty, but since open and close are the same, it is not relevant for me course. Basically, the indicator distinguishes between upward and downward movements. We distinguish between main movements and pullbacks. In the case of the bullish candle, the pullbacks are drawn in red and in the bearish candles the pullbacks are drawn in green. Of course, you can design the colors differently.

In addition to the main movement and the pullbacks you will notice that there are candles that are completely gray. This is a candle without a pullback. These candles can also be displayed in different colors. With the help of this indicator you will be able to see immediately how strong the individual pullbacks are in the movements. This makes it easier to compare individual candles. I have deliberately separated the main bullish and bearish movements in the indicator. You could also place all the candles next to each other, but that is very confusing.

This indicator is very individual and flexible, we look first at what he can do everything.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

On the left side you can see the individual settings that are possible. For that it is important to know which settings cause what exactly.

With 0 and 1, you decide whether a pullback is displayed or not.

With 2 and 3 you decide whether the main movement should be displayed or not.

With 4 and 5 you decide if the candles should be displayed without pullbacks.

With 6 and 7 you decide if a line should be drawn. Please note that the line does not take the pullback into account, but only includes the main movement.

On the right side you will find the concrete settings for the lower display. The line width of five was only created to improve the presentation. In the main chart I work with a width of 2-3. I optimized the main movement with DarkGray and the setting of 515151. That's the best way for me.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

This is basically the same setting as before, except that the candles that do not have a pullback are shown with a different color.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

In this case, all candles with a pullback were omitted and only the candles are shown that have not formed a pullback.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Here you can see only the pure pullbacks. This is a very interesting presentation but takes some getting used to. The smaller the pullbacks are, the stronger the trend. The color might be a bit confusing, but you can change that at any time.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Here you have the complete package, containing the main movement, the pullbacks and the strong moves without pullbacks. Of course, you can change the colors of the three different types of movement.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

In the example, only the pure main moves without pullbacks are made visible. Thus, a trend strength can be detected quickly.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

In order to visualize the representation a bit better, you are able to use a line to narrow down the main movements.

The indicator can be used both in the normal chart and in the tick chart. Although this is an indicator, it directly reflects the price scale and is based on the calculations of the bionic candle. If you work with the indicator, look at the pullbacks in the individual movements and try to create a derivation. Still, the biggest benefit is to immediately realize how strong a single candle is. Of course you can not foresee the next candle movement, but we know that trading is all about probabilities. And they may now be able to turn the odds slightly in their favor.

--- 帖子 #932 ---
Learning from high frequency dealers

Hello dear subscribers,

As I've already said in a few posts, high-frequency traders have entered the stock markets in recent years and have made life difficult for big players such as banks, asset managers, life insurers, pension funds and mutual funds.

A meeting with a friend from Switzerland who worked for Virtu Financial, one of the biggest high-frequency trading and market-making companies, has opened my eyes in some areas. Basically, our trade is clearly different from the high-frequency traders. It's like comparing a car to a Formula One race car. The processes and the strategy are not comparable, so it is very difficult to derive concrete recommendations. Nevertheless, there is a ray of hope to which we can orient ourselves.

High-frequency traders are, in principle, scalpers who trade within seconds after having previously scanned the market for supply and demand. In principle, every trader who has enough money can get the same market overview. The art consists in the interpretation of the data obtained. Of course, among the high-frequency traders, there are also some candidates who read certain data by means of unauthorized means, which can be heavy proven by the regulators.

Comparable is this approach with the Darknet, which obscures the IP origin. While access to the Internet via the Internet provider is running, in the Darknet access is routed through different computers to hide the origin. For this purpose, the data is encrypted and sent to a random computer in the network, this forwards the data, but retains the address of the sender. So the next recipient will know from where the data packet came last, but not where it originally came from. The final recipient decrypts the data packet, processes the request, and returns the answer in the same way that it came. This is how a data exchange takes place in Darknet.

However, the stock exchange always knows which address gave up buy or sell orders. But if a trader in London uses his order to scan the market for supply and demand and transmit that information to another trader who gives up the crucial orders, it's hard to prove.

If you imagine the stock market as a big sea, it is logical that a large container ship produces larger waves than a small speedboat. This makes a container ship faster to locate. In addition, a container ship takes forever to turn, while a speedboat can turn almost on the spot. A speed boat on the stock market could change a lot.

More than 10 years ago, a number of successful investment bankers, creative computer scientists, specialist network engineers and physicists with doctoral degrees have joined forces to usher in a new era on the stock exchanges. The approach of the idea: size is not important, you have to be fast.

First of all, the algorithms were developed that could automatically deliver massive orders within milliseconds. By hand, a few hundred traders would not be able to.

The high-performance computer systems built for this work with the fastest processors that are not yet on the market. The money does not matter, because you can afford a lot of technology for $ 2 million profit per trading day. The fastest processor takes much less than 1 microsecond to exchange data. Thereafter, the processors are still overclocked so much that the computing power for the algorithms only takes 0.1 microseconds.There are special employees at the chip manufacturers, who only take care of these optimizations. By contrast, the computing power of the new Intel Core i9-9980XE @ 3.00GHz is very sluggish.

To send the orders to the stock market, fast data lines are required. Fiber was previously a fast standard, after which the microwave was able to transmit data up to 40 times faster. Data is transmitted within fiber optic cables by means of light pulses. With a new technology from Australia, this light is simply turned and can therefore absorb more information. This allows the data to be transferred up to 100 times faster than before.

The stock exchanges sell the high frequency traders trade data and computer places directly beside the stock exchange computers. The shorter the way to the stock exchange, the faster the trading implementation. The decisive advantage lies in the deeper insight of the electronic order book, in which all buy and sell orders arrive. The exchanges offer different packages. A five-fold data update per second or in the luxury version ten times more data feeds. So within 1 second up to 10 data updates can be received from the main computer.

Of course, Goldman Sachs' big players can afford those data feeds, but the key point is that the custom algorithms evaluate the data feeds and place them in a dedicated platform. From this, the trading decisions are made.

Every microsecond the buy and sell offers are displayed on special screens. The trading platform does not comply with our known principle of price-time priority. The basis is breaks in the trade between 10-50 milliseconds, thus creating a uniform starting point. Just as there is always a fixed volume value in the tick chart, the breaks of 10-50 milliseconds are written down there. A kind of microequilibrium. Now we realize how important Equilibrium is for successful trading. That was a decisive hint for me.

Parallel to this run special calculators that scan the market and look for hidden orders and stops. Among other things, they work with the tricks already described: Wash Trades, Quote Stuffing, Spoofing and Sniping. The resulting losses are in principle only a small collateral damage. The information of these particular computers run into a host that internally makes the decision: yes or no and buying or selling and then gives up the ultimate order.

Thanks to the special programming, the main computer recognizes when a given address always buys certain stocks or currencies within seconds. From this a recurring principle is recognized and the high performance computer comes before the secret buyer. Within a millisecond now very high quantities are bought and thrown back a few seconds later with a high profit in the market. This works in 4 of 5 cases. Very interesting is that the calculator can distinguish the different buyers or sellers from each other.

When an ACDC concert takes place, you are standing at the front of the people queue at the ticket counter and there are still 15 cards, then you know supply and demand. They buy the last 15 tickets for $ 1,500 and then sell them to the highest bidder. You will earn at least $ 500 within a few minutes. According to a similar principle, the high-frequency traders work because they always know supply and demand with their special programs and strategies.

The stock market and supervision have no problem with the market becoming divided into a two-tier society. As long as everyone who can afford it gets a quick data feed, that's ok. The stock market sells their fast data feeds and earns ten times as much on a scalper as on a daytrader. In addition, the high-frequency traders increase volatility tremendously. This is a good figurehead for a stock or currency on the stock market. So why bother the high frequency trader?

Virtu Financial made losses only on a single day within 5 years (2009 to 2013). That was a total of 1,238 trading days. Goldman Sachs lost about on 124 days in the same period. Goldman Sachs is absolutely top with a 90% win rate, but with a 99.8% win rate, the Scalper Virtu is clearly outperforming. Scientists investigated on Virtu's trading activity found Virtu not taking much risk in trading. Scalpen seems to be the more profitable business.

In the meantime, however, that has changed a bit because other high-frequency traders have joined the market and make future business difficult. Long-term players such as banks, asset managers, life insurers, pension funds and mutual funds have already reacted to the high-frequency traders. They migrate to other markets, or set up their own markets, which are banned for high-frequency traders. As high-frequency traders take advantage of speed, more and more big players are throttling their orders and trying to get all of their sub-orders to hit different exchanges simultaneously. For example, high frequency wheels lack the time to respond to orders spread across multiple exchanges - and big players and funds can buy their paper at the current price.

Virtu has gone public, many believe that there are emerging problems for the high-frequency traders, because Virtu did not need money. Many high-frequency traders have withdrawn and the technical progress is already exhausted. Virtu has earned $ 7,000,000,000 in revenue over the last 9 years. The money is missing from the other big players. Earnings after taxes were around $ 850 million. Virtu's earnings after tax of $ 284 million in 2018 shows that it still works great.

The platforms these professionals work with can not be compared to a Metatrader or Ninjatrader. A lot of things are fully automatic, people only intervene when computers and algorithms fail. Sometimes the algorithms are written so elaborately that even the programmers have problems finding possible sources of error. As a result, there were always failures or massive problems in the past.

About the existing EAs on the market, my friend could only smile. If one would compare the programs of high-frequency traders with a EA, it would be like comparing a NASA space program with a code that controls a refrigerator. The algorithms of the high-frequency traders were programmed according to the market, each market has special requirements that are taken into account. Within a market, the algorithms are changed within seconds to respond to new demands. Even if an EA were elaborately programmed, the challenge would still be with the processors and the data lines.

A major disadvantage is the programming language MQL4 or MQL5. Although both languages support all object-oriented programming standards except multiple inheritance: data encapsulation and type extension, inheritance, polymorphism, overloading, and virtual methods. I already noticed this difference with my Java knowledge. The downside of MQL is that you are not able to build independent applications because MQL is only connected to its corresponding platform and the programs only work there. Java, on the other hand, has platform independence and runs on the phone, workstation, or enterprise class server, regardless of the type of operating system or hardware. Write Once Run Everywhere. Interfaces can be developed to all environmental systems and thus fit into most existing IT infrastructures.

Java programs are initially compiled into neutral byte code. These bytecodes are similar to machine instructions, but are not specific to a particular machine. The source code in Java is compiled into .class files that contain the program in bytecode. These bytecodes can now run on any platform that supports Java. They are almost interpreted and executed at startup.

If MQL had a similar structure, one could easily integrate its indicators or EA into other systems. Another problem: Our EA and indicators require a lot of performance and may delay trading execution. Therefore, a trading screen where we sell our orders should be free from all indicators.

So far, the big players such as banks, asset managers, life insurers, pension funds and investment funds have claimed the market for themselves. Then, 10 years ago, the first high frequency dealers came onto the market and took away money from these big players. They in turn have upgraded and made a counter-attack. Therefore, the market has become even more confusing and difficult. And in the future, it will be even harder to earn money in these markets.

An important insight is that predicting a future course from the current chart is wrong in most cases. The recommendation that we pay less attention to the current chart image and focus more on the Equilibrium, so the small breaks in which the price is balanced.

How can we protect us from the high frequency traders?

One possibility would be to switch to markets that are uninteresting for high-frequency traders. These are markets with low volatility. But we also need some volatility to be successful.

The second option would be to switch from EURUSD to the trading hours from 05:00 to 09:00 CET, from 11:00 to 14:00 CET and from 21:00 to 00:00 CET. But even that makes only limited sense.

High-frequency traders are only active in markets with high volatility, the bigger the better. The higher the volatility, the greater the chance of unpredictable breakouts. Since I seldom handle high volatility this is rather positive for me.

An ATR calculation for e.g. The last 500, 100, 50, 10 and 5 candles are recommended, so you can immediately see a strong increase and can act with extreme volatility with caution.

My friend has absolutely confirmed me in some things. Trading in the tick chart with the simultaneous consideration of the equilibrium are the best options for me. One would only have to pay more attention to the Equilibrium. In addition, Scalpen is the best trading strategy because you are short on the market and have done your business in seconds. So you can switch from one market to another and keep the risk low. The higher the lot and the shorter the length of stay, the less risky the trade. However, one must also have the right information, otherwise it costs the right amount of money.

We should look for medium volatility and wait for extremely high or low volatility or go to other markets. If the big players argue in the market, you can only lose.

Positive he finds the small stops of 0.5 pip, but a chance risk ratio of 1:10 for him is a much too high risk, because one are far too long in the market. The smaller the unit of time, the better, with time being an uninteresting factor in the market. The focus on the Equilibrium is interesting because it shows the uncertainty of the market. Out of certain equilibrium, it can only run up or down a lot.

You do not always have to be the first in a turnaround. His recommendation: First let the others initiate the turnaround and then you wait for the pullback. When you realize that more are coming into the market, you just step in for a few seconds. If the 10 lot win is not enough for you, you can increase the number anytime. Virtual stops that the broker does not see are beneficial. He was enthusiastic about the fact that I could act as a professional trader with a maximum of 1: 400 and in the case of total loss no additional payment must be made. In addition, there are no requotes and an additional 20% discount on my spread. That puts me at 0.4 to 0.45 Pip total cost per trade. While these are still lunar prices versus the high frequency traders, I have far less risk in case of total loss.

High frequency traders do not have this advantage. Nevertheless, their success is much greater.

In the future, speed will no longer bring the absolute advantage, the new strategy is called confusion. In doing so, a course is moved in an equibribrium until most are stopped out or get off. Then comes the decisive movement until the next equilibrium.

At the renko is the pip, at the candlechart the time and at the tickchart the contracts the fixed factor. For the Equilibrium there is something like that not yet in the MT4.

I will think about these suggestions in peace, possibly a new Equilibrium chart will be created, which defines Equilibrium as a fixed value. Or there is a combination of both. Because the advantage in the tick chart is the number of plumb bob we get. In combination with the Equilibrium this could be very exciting.

Incidentally, my friend confirmed to me that the high-frequency traders work with the Fibonaccis. The Fibonacci are included in the algorithms of the calculation programs. Not to generate trades, but to find other traders even easier. Of course, there are other indicators that are respected.

Nevertheless, I believe that the best algorithms have their limits because they were programmed by humans. Although they are able to execute much faster jobs, they are not able to react properly in exceptional situations. And these exceptional situations will trigger the long-term investing big players again and again and thereby prevent the high-frequency traders have a safe market entry and massively miscalculate.

The programmers are convinced of their algorithms, but very few would use their own money to trade with it. In addition, different algorithms have been programmed for the high-frequency wheels for safety reasons, so that a single programmer can never have a complete overview. A good protection against possible competition.

When the two towers of the Deutsche Bank were built in Frankfurt in 1984, there were 20 different companies responsible for different alarm systems in the main safes. This made it impossible for a company to rob the safe at a later date. Trust is good, control is always better.

My Swiss friend also read some posts from me and was impressed by the many creative ideas. Of course, my trade is no protection against a sudden breakout of a high-frequency trader, but he has given me something very important. With the nature of my trade, I am very rarely in the focus of high-frequency traders. In other words, I have little exposure to these high-end scalpers because I am dealing in zones that are either too uncertain or too unattractive for high-frequency traders. In any case, there is still need for action to catch even better entrances. In return, I often catch the zones of the long-acting big players and this guarantees a faster and more sustainable trend, which has a positive effect on my trade.

Furthermore, the tracks of the long-acting big players are the most important indicator. They have responsibility for millions of retail investors and investors and therefore need to be long-term and strategic. We should avoid the high-frequency wheels because we can not follow your actions anyway. For this we need a deeper market insight. I always thought that the DOM in the futures market would bring this market insight, but there are an incredible number of pseudo orders that are deleted within milliseconds again. This creates a false truth of supply and demand. The only truth is the resulting candle, but the moment we see the candle, that's already the past.

I have not found the optimal solution yet and maybe there will never be a correct solution. But the crucial point: The most successful traders in the world rely exclusively on the Equilibrium. This path seems to be the right one, now it just has to be optimized. It looks like a lot of work and time, but in the end it could pay off for us all.

Hello rosalieone,

I also found the information very exciting, to what extent they will help us, we will see.

An idea that I brought from Italy could help us. Every day on Lake Como we watched the kite surfers, how they started, their turns and their extraordinary jumps. Most of the time they did not start until around noon and a few hours later it was all over.

To go kitesurfing you need wind. Which wind is suitable for kitesurfing? Today, almost every kite manufacturer has a light wind kite in the offer that promises the gliding experience even under 10 knots. With the right board and the right driving skills, this is actually possible. At the top, of course, it gets more and more dangerous and at some point is reserved for the pros. The best is a constant wind, which side-shore (the wind blows parallel to the shore) or side-on-shore (oblique onshore wind) comes. With appropriate material and enough experience, winds of more than 40 knots are possible with a kite. Beginners are in good hands between 12 and 22 knots.

The wind direction is almost more important in kitesurfing than the wind force.

Since kite surfers mostly drive at right angles to the wind direction, in side- or side-on-shore winds the kiters always drive away from the shore and then back to the shore. As a result, everything is better distributed on the water. Onshore wind can of course also be gekitet, but then all go parallel to the shore and depending on how full it is in the water, it is difficult even for experts to come through. Onshore wind also has the disadvantage that falls near the shore can be very dangerous, because there is a risk of being pulled onto the land.

Depending on the experience, kiting is possible between 10 and 40 knots of wind speed. Every kiter has to find his comfort zone individually. If there is not enough wind you can not get ahead, too much wind could be dangerous.

We traders should also find our comfort zone, the ATR helps us. Too little volatility means one is too long in the market, too much volatility may mean loss of control.

It is recommended to calculate the ATR in the time unit in which one acts. I have three different ATR areas that are critical to me. The last 900, 30 and the current candle. The last 900 candles are a longer term average, the 30 candles a medium term average and the last candle the current situation. With these three values, I can immediately see how the ATR behaves and align my trading style with it.

It is crucial to find out in which area you feel comfortable and act best. Once you've set your range, an alarm could show that the range is leave.

The ATR is just one point of many to watch out for, but it's definitely a start once you've found your comfort zone.

Bionic-candle-size-indicator

Hello thelord14,

I would like to thank you on behalf of all subscribers for your kind words. Because this blog lives from the subscribers and their creative ideas. I've read your idea a few times, but I have to admit that unfortunately I do not understand your idea.

Basically, there is only a past in the chart, because if a candle close, it is also a thing of the past. The currently forming candle is the present until it is closed. This means all the candles we see in the chart are past, except for the current candle.

You can calculate a certain number of candles within a certain period with the Bionic Bull Bear Overview Percent BAR1.4. I understood that over each candle numbers should stand to find the strongest candle.

If you have read my Post No. 906 and 907, a strength calculation in the normal candle chart would make no sense, because you can only read in the tick chart, the number of used Lot. And the solder used is the only reason why the price is moving. Thus a correct strength calculation would be possible only in the tickchart. There are many possibilities in the calculation of strength, so I developed the Bioniccandle which displays only 2 movements (main movement and pullback). One possible theory was that the biggest candle in the tick chart would be the strongest candle at the same time and would have to reverse the trend, but unfortunately this is not always correct.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Within one price development supply and demand markets arise. With the Bionic Supply and Demand Indicator, I once attempted to graphically represent these zones. The numbers you see above the HH, HL, LH and LL are the average pip values per candle that have taken place within this movement. It should be noted that only the main movement is counted. In a bullish candle (close-low) and in a bearish candle (high-close).

While the largest candle in the tick chart has the most plumb bob within a constant contract number, it is not necessarily the strongest candle. Crucial for a turnaround is the so-called key candle. This key candle is usually not the strongest candle, but it overcomes a very strong price level. Here is an example

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

At points A and B you will see a strong candle pushing the course downwards. I mark the beginning of this strong movement with a line. At point C and D you will see the key candles, as these candles break through this strong price zone. At E you see a much stronger candle, which, however, had no effect so far.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

At point A and B you will see the result of the key candles shown. At point C you can see how the price goes up. The start is marked with a line. The candle at point D overcomes this price zone. This creates a resistance zone again. This can be repeated indefinitely.

Hello Thelord14,

The Bionic Percentage Balance Indicator has an upper and lower level. The upper level displays all bullish movements and the lower level all bearish moves. Both levels each receive a range of 100%. The indicator now measures the ratio between the main motion and the pullback within the bioniccandle. This will enable you to look even faster and deeper into the candle.

The Bionic percentage balance indicator is calculated within a fixed range. Each movement within a candle is displayed in percent, no matter how big this candle is. That brings even faster information. The basis is the Bioniccandle, which is known to consist of 2 movements. With the Strength setting weaker movements can be filtered out in small steps.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

At maximum, all candles that have a pullback can be filtered out, which means: All bullish Bioniccandle where High == Close and Bearish Bioniccandle where Low == Close are kept. The numbers you have to enter vary depending on the price and volatility, so there is no fixed rule here.

How do I optimize my strategy?

Hello dear subscriber,

If a trader is not satisfied with his results, it is often because he is following the wrong strategy. There are many strategies when trading, finding the right one is the challenge. Unfortunately there is no standardized solution in trading. If you read somewhere "This strategy always works" or "it's just that way", then you should be skeptical. A strategy consists of various parameters such as setup, trading style, time units, money and risk management, etc. Let's look at a few different setups first. I would like to limit myself today only to 5 essential setups.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

1. Breakout setup

Breakouts do not only occur in sideways-running markets, but often within trends. With a breakout setup, you try to catch this outbreak. Since most outbreaks fail, a breakout setup is a trade with a low probability. However, it remains very popular as the chance of catching a new trend is too tempting for most traders. The risk is high and the chance of winning low. If you win it can be well worth it, provided you are already in the market before the outbreak. If you go with a buy order in the market, you could come in late, which reduces the RRR (Return / Risk Ratio) significantly. A limit order is indeed more effective, but here the stop must be big enough not to fly out of the market. Therefore, the RRR in the overall result is rather smaller.

2. Reversal setup

A trend either continues or turns. Similar to a continuation trade, we must have an existing trend before looking for a reversal setup. However, we are not moving in the direction of the trend, but we are looking for a reversal. Reversal trades have a high risk and a low hit rate, but high potential, if you let run the profits. This can achieve a high RRR.

3. Pullback setup

Within a trend, larger or smaller pullbacks arise as some trend followers go out, of the market to realize their profits while traders enter because they believe the trend is over and now a new trend is starting. Pullback trades have a medium hit rate and a medium chance, as you never know how far this pullback is going. When a new trend develops from the initial pullback, you're the first one  and can follow the trend longer. Therefore, the risk is more balanced relative to profit.

4. Range Bound Setup

Within an equilibrium, there is no clear market trend. What happens if the market is caught in a sideward movement? In this case, a range-bound strategy is ideal. The goal is to buy deep and sell high within the sideways movement. As long as the sideways movement does not break out and become a trend, such trading setups have a high win rate. However, since our take profit is mostly within the equilibrium zone, there can only be a small profit on every trade. Lower risk, higher probability of winning less profit and a small RRR.

5. Continuation setup

A continuation setup offers the opportunity to enter in an existing trend. The setup will earn you money as the trend continues. For this, we must already have identified a trend reversal and the first or second pullback. The probability is highest here of all setups. However, the profit may not be so high as the trend could soon be over quickly. If you take the risk to stay in the market and the trend continues to develop, you can sometimes achieve a higher RRR.

Basically, I recommend a beginner to start with the continuation setup and, if successful, sometimes try a range bound setup. If you make a profit in the long run within these two setups, you can risk the other setups. The profits are not so high, but you have a smaller risk. And in the beginning it is important to make a profit, how high should not be matter. The breakout setup is at least 5 times more difficult than the continuation setup. As a beginner you should start with the easiest.

If you've been trading for a few years and have not had success, I'd recommend that you think over and possibly change Setup. The greater the risk, the greater the profits but also the loss. A lower risk with high profits is a dream, such a setup will never be.

If you've been trading for a few years and found your optimal setup but are dissatisfied with the revenue, I can give you e easy advice. Stay true to your setup. Increasing the lever or the number of lot will help you to maximize profits. If you do that within your familiar set-up, increasing your winnings is likely to be easy.

After the setup, we now look at which trading style suits you best.

Position Trading

It follows the long-term trend for weeks to get the maximum gain from a large price movement. A long-term trader uses charts with the closing prices of each day.

Swing Trading

The positions are held over several days and the goal is to benefit from short-term price formations. A swing trader usually uses the 30-minute or 1-4 hour chart. Of course you can trade in Swingtrading for several weeks.

Daytrading

This type of trades, as the name implies, is closed before the end of the day. This avoids the risk of major market movements - and thus possible losses - at night. The trades only run for a few hours and bar graphs with a timeframe of 15 or 5 minutes are used.

Minutes scalping

The trades run only for a very short time - often only a few minutes to an hour. The Scalper quickly tries to beat the spread between supply and demand and settles for only a few pips before closing the deal. Usually the M5, M1 or tick charts are used.

Seconds scalping

The trades only run for a few seconds to a few minutes. One second Scalper quickly tries to beat the spread between supply and demand and settles for only a few pips before closing the trade. As a rule, only the tick charts are used.

Of course, completely different time units or trading periods can be used within the different trading styles.

Time units play an important role in trading, because each time unit shows you a different course of the chart, whereby the course is of course the same in all time units. It's just the graphical resolution that's different. Basically, I recommend in addition to the time unit in which you act to pay attention to a parent and subordinate time unit. If you trade as a swing trader in the M30, I would recommend the H4 as a higher-level unit of time, where you can very effectively determine the resistance zones for a take profit. An M5 may help as an inferior unit of time for an efficient start.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Now let's compare these five trading styles. Please note that this is a purely hypothetical comparison, as there are many different possibilities in reality.

The same RRR was used in all five trading styles. Risk and profit also do not differ from each other to make a possible comparison. The position trader, who may act for a few weeks, should not be taken into account.

As a result of this comparison, it will be noted that the seconds scalper can achieve a $ 200 win within 1 minute while a swing trader would need a week for the same gain. However, in the same ratio, the risk is also higher for the seconds scalper.

While a swing trader can lose $ 100 within a week, the seconds scalper can do it within a minute. This can be seen very nicely in the table under Profit $ / min and Risk $ / min. In the given and calculated case, a swing trader could lose around $ 0.014 in the event of a loss per minute if his trade runs against him exactly over a week. The seconds scalper can lose $ 100 within 1 minute. That's 7,200 times faster than the swing trader.

The swing trader has a stop of 100 pip while the seconds scalper has just a stop of 1 pip at his disposal. The ATR in H1 is 15 pip while the ATR is in the 16 tick chart at 0.74. In this case, the swing trader has a significantly larger reserve in his stop than the seconds scalper. Also you should pay attention.

The time unit in which you feel most comfortable to trade also decides a bit about which style of trading might suit you. The larger the time unit, the more accurate the message of a candle, which has to do with the fluctuation. Higher time units give you more reliable signals than the minute charts. Whether you are Scalper, Daytrader or Swing Trader, you should never look at a time unit in isolation, but always in conjunction with higher / lower time units.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

From point A to point B in the EURUSD D1 we see that a bullish result of 272.1 pip was reached within 11 days. That's 25 pip bullish increase on average per day. The ATR of the last 1,500 candles in the D1, however, show a range of 82.18 pip. How does it fit together?

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Within a day candle we see a M5 Zigzag course. This course is very volatile. At point A, you see the candle in the daily chart. In some post I have already pointed out that the smaller the unit of time, the larger and more uncertain is the range that goes through a course.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

If you divide the ATR (average range of bullish and bearish movements) in minutes, you find out: The smaller the time unit, the stronger the average range of the pip. This gives many traders the hope to make  faster profits in smaller time, and better control trades. That is a fallacy.

A day candle is 1,440 times more accurate than a minute candle and 48 times more accurate than a M30. The logical conclusion: one can make clearer and more reliable statements about the single candle in higher time units. Likewise, resistance and support zones can be drawn more accurately. One problem is the coarse candle structure. The larger the time units become, the larger the upper and lower wicks of a candle become. With the bioniccandle one can eliminate these ambiguities.

Now let's take a look at what risk we take in daily trading.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

The following table has been developed by me and should exemplify the risk that we enter daily. The comparison only relates to the time unit and the setup. A continuation setup is definitely safer as a breakout setup. A D1 candle is much clearer than an M1 candle. From this I have created a risk profile that is considered purely hypothetical.

In the table you see different numbers, the larger the number, the safer the system is within setup and time unit. The average is 600. We find that a continuation setup in D1 is the safest setup (7,200) and a breakout setup in the 16 tickchart (0.25) is the most dangerous setup. Weeks and monthly charts were not taken into account.

Let's say you use a reversal setup and trade in the M5. Then you'll see the number 10. That means you trade 60 times less effectively than the average of 600. If you trade in the M30 instead of the M5, you increase your effectiveness six times. If a beginner in the M1 acts a reversal setup it is 300 times heavier than the average. If he would act a continuation setup in H4, it would have 600 times easier to trade than a  M1reversal setup.

The table is intended as an example for those who want to increase their effectiveness. I myself work with the Reversal-Setup, Pullback-Setup and the Range Bound-Setup in the Tick 32 and Tick 16. My risk is on average 1 and is therefore very high. However, in the past I have tried all sorts of setups and I am best at using this system. It is only one of the riskiest in the Forex market. The higher the risk, the higher the profit within a certain period of time. If my system were ineffective, I would have to change my setup and time unit.

A minute candle is about 50 times more volatile than a day candle considering the average ATR. The same ratio has the maximum speed of a moped against a fighter jet. Beginners who wait of a breakout in the M1 often wonder why they crash very quickly.

If you were to start as a novice driver with a Formula 1 racing car right away, that would have fatal consequences. First of all, start with a small kart, get bigger and faster later, is easy. A Formula One driver will drive the Monza circuit faster with a big kart than we all do in a Formula 1 car.

Sideline novices basically have only two options.

In the long term swing trading would be the optimal alternative for the side job, but many need the thrill and start scaling after work. That costs real money and is one of the reasons why many lose. Keeping your fingers quiet and learning is sometimes more important than taking unnecessary trades. But it takes time.

Focus and specialize in a single market. If you have understood for years what the real motivations of this market are, much will become easier. You can also make a profit by selling $ 1 for 90 cents to buy $ 1 for 50 cents.

In addition to the right trading platform, the technology and the right money management, your health and condition is a very important foundation for success.

Regular timeouts are crucial to letting all your knowledge sorted and reconsider how you can continue to use it. I have learned from many people, but I have also rejected a great deal of knowledge. You always get insights when you can think about it in peace. When you absorb knowledge, it is like throwing a stone into the water. The water must first come to rest, so you get a deeper look.

Trading can not be taught to anyone, success is possible only because of your own development phase. In order to gain knowledge the blogs help with FF, but you have to learn to renounce certain knowledge in order to find your own way. Trading consists of 80% Psychology and 20% technical knowledge. The art is to deal with defeats properly.

Basically, I believe that nobody makes a functioning and very profitable system public. Because with it, he can earn more money than with the sale of books or with paying customers who demand a daily market assessment and thus put him under pressure. Most trading books and many recommendations from self-proclaimed coaches are their own interpretations and bring us at most a good idea. The idea must be in line with our psyche and we can only help ourselves.

Most traders have developed their own trading logic slowly and independently, the many failures were an important component on the way to success. The pro does not know where the course is going as well as a beginner, but he is decisively ahead of the beginner in one thing. He has a thoughtful strategy within the probabilities. He wins and he loses, that's perfectly normal. But he takes significantly less risks than a beginner.

Therefore, do the same in all FF blogs, take the best ideas, and build your own strategy. Each person trades uniquely, copying that would be hopeless from the outset. But what you have developed yourself can be brought forward with passion. It takes time, but in the end you have something that belongs only to you and no one can take it away. And that's what I recommend to you.

I wish you a successful trading week.

AAA Bionic Power x candle indicator

Hello dear traders,

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

On request of a subscriber, I would like to provide you today with a modified strength indicator. The bioniccandle has only one main movement and one pullback inside a candle. The main movement of the bullish candle goes from low to close and the pullback goes from high to close. The main movement is thus the deciding factor. In this indicator, this main movement also receives a special bonus and is thus able to show the strength of a single candle in more detail. If the value is 0 in the strength setting, it means that all candle thicknesses are calculated. Increasing the number now filters out weaker candles. Depending on the time unit and volatility, different numbers must be entered. The strongest candles arise when high and close (bullish candle) or low and close (bearish candle) are equal. These candles are not filtered out. There is only one bullish or bearish strength per candle. If you use the filter, I recommend you turn off the white border in the setting.

The indicator works in the candlechart as well as in the tickchart. However, it is only possible in the tick chart to draw a conclusion on the Lot used. The candle chart mixes the volume and the number of lot. The justification can be found in the Post 906 and 907. However, the prospect of determining a specific lot number in the Forex market is almost impossible.

There is no real volume in the Forex market because the Forex market is an over-the-counter market. Thus, the volume can not be measured there with the usual tools. If someone buys five contracts in the futures market, this also corresponds to a volume of five in the order book of the respective stock exchange. In the forex market, on the other hand, volume can not be measured by the number of contracts purchased. It is done by summing all price changes found during a specified period of time. In a forex pair, a certain number of completed transactions must be determined for a price change.

That is also the reason why we want to combine the advantages of the interbank market with the advantages of the futures market with our project 6. That we need real stock market data should be clear. Because only with this one can determine the concrete number of lots. And the lots are the deciding factor for a price movement. It should therefore be clear that many indicators in the forex market are not working properly. That's one of the reasons why more traders lose money than win.

With correct stock market data, the indicators would show concrete data, unfortunately, one would have to work at least with the new modified MT5, since the MT4 can not process stock market data. I think that our new project will be a further step forward, but this project will take some time.

The goal is to get specific data about the Lot and still work with the MT4. It is reassuring to know that the future market is not the holy grail either.

For this I will post more information in the next few days.

best regards

Hello hfzazh7,

There are many ways to identify an Equilibrium, one can even detect Equilibrium in a smaller time units with the eye. Equilibrium in the EURUSD arises when the buyers of dollars and buyers of euros agree. An equilibrium shows the fair price within a price zone. Equilibrium also means a fight for supply and demand. It is difficult to predict the course of the course within an equilibrium. Even a brief breakout from an equilibrium zone is no confirmation that the price continues in that direction.

I would like to comment on the statement that an equilibrium can only be identified by means of a trendline. Every trader has his personal strategy that he pursues. For the one who made that statement, it may be that way because he succeeds. And if he succeeds, it is right for him. I myself do not work with trendlines. In trading there is no right and no wrong. Everyone interprets the market for themselves, it is only bad if he believes that his statement must apply to everyone.

If you read through our blog from the beginning, you will realize that there are many ways to recognize an Equilibrium. What matters is what brings you the identification of an Equilibrium and what conclusion do you draw from it. In addition, identifying a trend is very difficult as we have to make a decision between Renkocharts, Candlecharts and Tickcharts within different time units.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Let's look at an example in the monthly chart of the EURUSD. From September 2000 to June 2008 we had an uptrend. From June 2018 to January 2017 we had a downtrend. From January 2017 to February 2018, the price has gone up. Since February 2018, the price is in a downward trend. Now comes the exciting question. Is the price progression from point 3 to point 4 the beginning of a new uptrend, or is it just a pullback within the downtrend from point 2 to point 3? Finally we had a short pullback at point 6 and then the course went down. At point 7 we had a big equilibrium over two years as the price moved within a certain price range. This could be a possible indication of a new uptrend, but that is a pure speculation.

At the moment we are in a weekly chart in a kind of equilibrium, in the daily chart and in H4 possibly in an uptrend. In the H1 and the M30 we are in the downtrend and in the M15 and in the M5 in an upward trend. In the M1, it looks like we're in a pullback within a downtrend.

This means that we always find different trends within different time units. To make a concrete deduction from this is pure speculation. As a scalper, I am unable to give a long-term reliable forecast of a possible trend. The only advantage we have is to know that a course always moves up or down in wavy lines. We must identify these wavy lines correctly as traders and swim with the wave. Equilibrium can help identify certain resistance zones. However, the problem is that we do not get exact data in forex which gives us a closer look at the strength of a candle. Thus, the speculation in the forex is much greater than in the futures market.

I have compared the forex market in the last few weeks with the futures market, there were very interesting findings. For this I will publish a detailed report in the next few days.

Forex versus future

Hello dear subscribers,

Today's report is about the differences between the forex market and futures. The most important backgrounds are illuminated and some very interesting findings came out. Therefore, this report has become slightly longer than usual.

For many years I work full-time as Forex Scalper and use this platform with FF for me as a kind of development diary. I am neither a trading guru nor do I want to convince others of my way of trading. I have found my basic strategy for myself and live from my business, but I am motivated to optimize this strategy every day. It took me many years to realize that supply and demand are the only way for me to be profitable. When you write down your insights, new aspects come up, which you scrutinize and analyze. It took me almost a month to develop this report today.

This is the same when a racer is to explain exactly how he approaches the vertex of a curve optimally. I make no claim that I am right or that my view of the market is correct. Nevertheless, my way of trading is absolutely correct for me, since I live from trading for many years. Since I follow through this blog no financial interests, I do not have to prove my success. My motivation within this blog is to take ideas, develop them and then make them available to everyone. That's how everyone gets ahead. And experience always needs its time.

Through exchanges with some subscribers, over the last few years many good ideas have come together that I have developed within supply and demand and then made available to everyone again. Quit pro quo, one hand washes the other. The market is not easy, although the price can only go up or down, the odds are effectively only 1:19. Why this is so, I will explain later exactly. Let's first look at the forex market.

Interbank Market

The interbank market is the market where money and credit business takes place only between banks. Banks and financial institutions trade with one another in the interbank market, lend each other money and can thus ensure that they remain liquid. Securities, money, foreign exchange, precious metals or derivatives are exchanged in the interbank market. The interbank market is assigned to the money market. The rates of currencies are not determined by a government as long as they are freely tradeable and not linked to another currency. They are based solely on supply and demand. Forex trading is usually OTC, i. E. it is not centrally organized, but takes place directly between the market participants or through a broker.

Bank risks are to be spread across the interbank market. Through it, the banks can carry out liquidation of open positions that were previously established in the customer business. Or the banks operate proprietary trading on the interbank market. In addition, interbank trading should ensure sufficient liquidity at all times for the banks.

The biggest "players" in the forex market are governments and the central banks, which generally participate in foreign exchange trading in the interests of the government. Due to their financial capabilities, central banks are able to exert a noticeable influence on the foreign exchange market. In principle, however, they use currency trading only to adjust and hedge their foreign reserves. The next largest participants are banks and other credit institutions. The proportion of private speculators is very low here in comparison.

EBS (Electronic Broking Services) is the world's largest trading platform for foreign exchange in interbank trading. The price, which arises at EBS, is the reference for any FX derivatives. EBS Markets maintains an anonymized central limit order book. FX trading banks can trade on the market and trade via these hedge funds & CTAs (Prime Brokerage Arrangements). Although the data is collected anonymously, EBS Markets recognizes whether it is a human or an algorithmic interface (AI). In addition to the classification, the EBS regulations provide for a minimum quota life (MQL). This is to prevent the high-frequency traders from the fact that they have only by their speed advantage over the other market participants. In addition, since there is no specific trade information in the interbank market, this market for high-frequency trading is not quite as interesting as the stock market environment.

The big players therefore have sophisticated computer systems to detect inconsistencies in the currency pairs. These inconsistencies usually last only a few seconds. With so many market participants and the large volume of daily sales, it is more important to keep an eye on the trend and the flow of capital than to recognize an undervalued currency. The cash market is the so-called Leitwolf, it is based on all markets. When the EURUSD course is mentioned on television, it is always about the cash market.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Over $ 5 trillion is being transacted daily in the forex market. By the end of 2019, the $ 6 trillion limit is to be reached. This would have increased the volume of 1995 almost sixfold. In 24 years, the Forex market has thus achieved an average increase of 7% per year.

The EURUSD trades around $ 1.7 trillion per day and the retail trader share is around 5.5% = around $ 94 billion. Worldwide there are about 5 million traders and about 50,000 institutional traders. If 1 million traders per day trade the EURUSD, the average turnover would be 1 lot. Assuming that 10,000 global institutional traders per day trade in EURUSD, their average turnover would be around 1200 per day. This quickly reveals the unequal distribution of powers. The big players act and the retail traders react.

The interbank market has repeatedly come into disrepute, as banks had made price agreements with each other, which had a negative impact on other market participants. In addition, foreign exchange trading almost led to fraud: 98 percent of transactions are conducted in direct trading between banks rather than via a stock exchange. There is no regulatory authority. Only twelve banks control 85 percent of the market. Banks do not trust each other and no one provides information about their trading activities. Therefore there is no real volume or an order book in the interbank market. The resulting volumes in MT4 are a pure estimate.

That's exactly the difference between the two markets. On the stock exchange all market participants have the same extensive information. In Forex market, most market participants have insufficient information. With a trading volume of over 21% in the interbank market, Deutsche Bank has so much experience that analysts and programmers are able to develop interesting strategies from the existing data. This brings clear advantages in the trade. With an average daily sales volume of 3,600,000 plumb bobs, they simply have more background information than the small retail trader. In addition, the Big Boys spend billions on their analysts and traders. A truly successful trader earns millions of dollars a year in these financial firms, after all, he should not have to worry about financing his house, his cars and vacations. He should be free in his mind and concentrate 100% daily on the market.

It scared me that some banks are investing 20-30% of their available funds in the forex market and with that gaining up to 65% of their yearly total profits. So, if you make a bank transfer again and it takes 2 days to land on the other account, it could well be that, among other things, this money is being used in the EURUSD to fund a breakout that may even stop you.

MT4 is the world's most popular forex trading platform. His next competitor is the MT5, which, as the name suggests, is also built by MetaTrader. It is conceivable that even some larger traders will work with this platform in the forex market.

Nevertheless, the forex market is more opaque to the retail trader than the exchange-regulated market.

Futures

The buyer of a futures contract undertakes to buy the underlying asset on the due date at the agreed price. The seller of a futures contract, however, to sell the underlying asset on the due date at the agreed price. At first glance, futures trading thus does not differ from ordinary cash markets, such as the stock market.

But there is one major difference: futures are related to an Underlying, and their Derivative Market price-depends mostly on the spot rate. The price of the Euro FX Future is always slightly above the spot rate of the EURUSD. There is a simple reason for this: if an investor buys the EURUSD on the cash market, he must pay the entire purchase price immediately. On the other hand, if he opens a long position in the Euro FX Future, he only has to deposit a fraction of the current market value as collateral for the futures exchange.

The difference between this margin and the full market price may be invested at a safe interest rate. The returns to be achieved with this safe interest rate correspond to the price difference between the spot rate and the forward rate. Investors can basically trade two different motivations futures. Firstly, futures trading is suitable for speculative purposes because capital investment is low, liquidity is high, and the range of tradable markets is ready. Second, futures are suitable for hedging economic or financial risks. A farmer can sell the late summer corn crop at a fixed price as early as spring, and a portfolio manager can hedge a stock portfolio against general market risk.

Futures trading also offers several benefits to private investors. First, almost no other financial instrument makes it so easy to speculate on falling prices. For this purpose, only a short position must be opened in futures trading, while short sales in equities are only relatively cumbersome. Futures offer much simpler pricing than options, where residual maturity and volatility sometimes influence the option price more than the actual performance of the underlying.

Second, unlike certificates and contracts for difference, investors can be confident in trading futures on a futures exchange of regulated and closely supervised settlement. The business model of many brokers and issuers is precisely to pass on the bid / ask spreads of the futures market at a premium to their own customers. Third, futures trading requires very little capital investment compared to a direct investment in the underlying asset. This allows trading to leverage: Investors can move many times their assets in the market and thereby generate disproportionate returns relative to their use.

The Chicago Mercantile Exchange (CME) announced in early January of this year that it would reduce the tick size for the futures contract to EUR / USD from one pip ($ 12.50 per contract) to ½ pip ($ 6.25 per contract). With this measure, the CME makes the Euro FX future even more interesting, especially for day traders and scalpers.

Futures Trading has a large selection. The exchanges offer forward contracts on stock indices, individual stocks, bond indices, volatility, exchange-traded index funds, interest rates, commodities, exchange rates and even real estate prices. Even if the individual contract specifications differ, the actual trade always runs the same way.

Who sets on rising prices in, opens a long position. If investors expect falling prices, a short position will be opened. In this case, it is an opening position. Even though futures are unconditional forward transactions with a concomitant obligation to buy or sell, it is very easy to exit the market. Investors open a closing position. A short position is closed by opening a long position with the same number of contracts. The market risk is completely eliminated and the investor acts as if he had not previously opened a position.

The performance of the futures depends exclusively on the performance of the underlying, the margin on the futures exchange, the market interest rate and the remaining term of the contract. As a rule, the price of the futures is only a few points above that of the cash market. In the FX Future, the minimum bet is 1 lot ($ 125,000), a tick is 0.5 pip and thus the volatility is slightly lower than in the Forex market. Depending on the broker, leverage is possible up to 200. The minimum deposit is $ 5,000 for most brokers and there are also brokers who charge significantly less. However, this is not recommended, because a futures account under $ 20,000 makes no sense to me.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

More than $ 800 billion is being transacted every day on the world's top 10 exchanges. By the end of 2021, the $ 1 trillion limit could be reached. The forex market is 12x larger than the futures market and 27x larger than the stock market. Since only professional traders trade in the futures market, there is no such thing as the typical retail trader. Of course, there are big players, and especially the dreaded high frequency traders, who are quite different from the smaller traders.

In the regulated stock market, price fixing which had a negative impact on other market participants is more difficult. There is a real volume and an order book in the futures market. All market participants have the same information. The key is the interpretation of this information.

The MT4 does not work on the Future markets, however, the MT5 can be used here, which is too confusing for me, however. A Ninja Trader already has clear advantages but is not as clear as the platform ATAS, which, however, costs a one time $ 2,500. What matters is what information you need for your trading strategy.

Before we start with a comparison between the forex market and the futures market, we first look at how difficult it is to survive in the different markets.

Which markets are particularly hard to trade?

Since 1984, the World Cup Trading Championships (WCTC) holds a Trader World Championship every year. There are different categories whereby I would like to compare only 3 categories stocks, Forex, and Future. The rules are simple. All participants who want to participate in the same broker open a trading account with $ 10,000 in the future or $ 5000 in the forex. Traded only with real money over a period of one year. Every trader can individually trade from home within this year. There must be at least ten round-turn trades. At the end of the period, the three winners with the highest net return are determined. Some traders trade at very high risk, and some drawdowns are above average speculative. However, everyone in this contest has the same opportunities to compare each category. The returns are not representative but provide a rough guide as all participants have the same requirements.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

On the right side you will see a table where the respective World Champions are listed in each category. The period is between the years 2000-2019, with the figures from 2019 being an intermediate, as the competition will run until the end of this year. The average return across all categories is 190% per year. That such a return can only be achieved with an increased risk in the trade, everyone should be clear.

Although we only need the forex and futures markets for our comparison, I included the stock market for additional comparison. Incidentally, I have used all the figures that have been provided to me.
