Conclusion and knowledge

In my opinion, the stock market is one of the most difficult markets you can trade on the stock exchange, because a lot of background information is needed for a good performance. In addition, you have to be able to interpret a trade balance correctly and read between the lines. A return of over 81% is an absolute top performance in this market segment.

Let us now compare the forex market with the futures market. Basically, it is striking that the yield in the futures market is almost three times higher than in the Forex market. The best return in the forex market does not even match the average yield of the futures market. The 5 worst returns in the futures market correspond to the average yield in the forex market.

The fact is that the yield in the futures market is three times higher than the yield in the forex market. However, it should be noted that in the forex market trades very many beginners, while the future market is used almost exclusively by professionals and experienced traders. Many traders who started in the forex market trade now in the futures market.

Since the forex market is the interbank market, where banks trade with each othernot in a regulated market, it should be clear that the challenge in trading there is significantly higher than in the futures market. Based on the numbers, it can be assumed that trading in the stock market is almost 4 times and in the forex market is three times as heavy as in the futures market. This is basically an important insight, if you are in one of these markets.

Many believe in the beginning of their trading career that the chance of winning is 50%, as the price may only rise or fall. But that is a mistake. 95% of retail traders lose their money over a long period of time in the forex market. The profit probability of retail traders is thus 1:19. Take 19 cards, place them on the table and pick a specific card. Now close your eyes, shuffle the cards and draw a card from the stack. If it is the previously chosen card, you have won.

The losses are so inevitable and no one should be sad if he loses, that's completely normal. The only chance is to get closer to the market every day through personal experience. This only works if you limit the losses severely and act more defensively than aggressively. As a rule, one lets losses run too long, because one hopes that the market comes back again. Profits are taken too fast because you do not want to give back your win. And then there are the revenge trades to recover his losses. These are typical human habits that you should quickly forget as a daytrader or swing trader.

If you start as a beginner in the EURUSD Seconds Chart with Scalpen and make your entries and exits dependent on indicators, the loss is a sure thing. If you start with table tennis, the ball at the beginning is also played slowly back and forth to get a feel for it. Over time, you become safer and able to accelerate your game. If, as a beginner, you face the multiple table tennis world champion Ma Long from China you will not win a game.

When trading our opponents are almost exclusively world champions, but since many beginners sit in front of their screens, and the opponents do not see, most believe that you have a real chance. If a beginner could see the professional traders of the banks, the initial losses would probably be much lower. The problems are the many self-proclaimed trainers who have no idea about the trade, who pull the money out of your pockets and let you believe that trading is easy. It recommends strategies that could be downloaded for free from the internet. Add to that the many trading books that are recommended on the internet and are actually worth a penny. I was fortunate to not read any of these books at the beginning. When, after a few years, with some experience, I took these books in hand, I was glad that I could not orient myself to it.

The forex market is three times heavier than the futures market, it is crazy that a beginner starts in the heaviest market and when he has success, to move into the lighter market. Normally it should be the other way around.

Comparison Forex Market / Future Market

In the following comparison, the EURUSD in Forex is compared to the Euro FX E6 Future. As I already wrote, these are two completely different markets, which also differ in pricing. Nevertheless, the futures market is based on the cash market, which means that the markets are indirectly linked.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

As we already know, $ 1700 billion is being converted into EURUSD Forex per day. At a Lot value of $ 100,000, this equates to an average daily turnover of 17 million lot. In the futures market, 1 lot equals $ 125,000 in sales. From the stock market data of the CME we can see that on average 150,000 lot are traded per day in Euro FX. That's equivalent to $ 18.75 billion in revenue. The Euro FX Future is 90 times smaller than the EURUSD Forex.

Volatility is significantly higher in the forex market at 0.1 tick than in the futures market at 0.5 tick. In the forex market, the leverage for a non-professional trader is 30, while the lever in the futures market can be up to 200. Both accounts can be opened by beginners, whereby the advantage in the Forex market is that a trader maximally can lose his deposit. With his Trader account he does not run into the minus. In Europe, it is much harder to gain a professional trader status in the Forex area than in the futures market. Only about 4% of all forex traders in Europe achieve these special conditions.

Let's come to a key point: the profit and loss ratio. The probability to win in the forex market is 1:19, as 95% of retail traders lose permanently. Assuming that it is three times easier to make profits in the futures market, there would be around 85 losers for 15 winners. The odd is 1: 6. This ratio could potentially be very realistic, as the futures market is almost exclusively made up of experienced traders.

An interim conclusion:

Looking first at the two different markets, we find that we are gaining 61.5% in the forex market, while the futures market is up 38.4%. This is primarily because the entry criteria in the forex market are easier and the security is much higher.

The fact that one achieves three times higher profits in Future market than in the Forex market, lies essentially in the fact that one gets more concrete market data available in the Future market. First let's look at the market data, which disadvantages there are in the Forex market.

In the forex market, we do not receive a specific volume (number of lots) or a specific number of completed trades. Therefore, there can be no Dom and no Time & Sales list. It is also impossible to display a footprint chart, a volume profile, deleted lots in the dome or an imbalance in bid and ask. For this, the largest banks would have to be willing to publish their data. And that is exactly what will never happen in the forex market. Due to poor data information, the forex market comes to an advantage of 30.7% while the futures market comes to an advantage of 100%. This makes it clear that the futures market has over three times more information than the forex market.

If you add all the advantages together, the forex market would come to 90% while the futures market gets just under 140%. We realize there is no clear market that only has benefits. But a smart trader tries to optimize the benefits and minimize the disadvantages. First, let's see if such a strategy is even possible.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

As we know, there are different prices in the EURUSD Future and Forex market. In the picture above we see the Future FX market in H1 and in the lower picture the EURUSD H1 in the forex market. If you compare the candles, you will find that the differences are marginal. And yet the prices are different. This realization is very important to make a further decision.

I compared the data feed of the futures with the data feed of the Forex market over several months and found that the data feed of the futures had significantly more problems. But that could been coincidence. I myself have a very fast data feed in the forex market, which runs very stable even with strong volatility.

The cost of a lot for me are significantly cheaper than in the futures market. On the Forex market I pay average $ 4- $ 4.5 per roundturn per lot, between $ 5 and $ 10 in the futures market. With 200 trades per month, that's a big difference.

The chance to win in the forex market is 1:19, while the chance in the futures market is 1: 6. Consider, for a brief moment, the opportunities that result. A winning chance of 1:19 means that the trader wins, what the other 19 traders loose. In the Future Market, the winner receives the money from 6 traders who have lost.

We must note that in the Forex market 90 times more money is converted than in the futures market. Let's just do it all down. The forex market is $ 1700 while the futures market is $ 18.75. Thus, it is clear that the profits in the forex market in the ratio are significantly higher than in the futures market. In contrast, of course, there is the much higher risk.

The ESMA regulations made me register a year ago as a professional trader within the Forex market. Since I can never lose more money than I have in my account, in the event of an uncontrolled breakout, my account will not go down. A possible minus account is excluded. That has kept me from trading futures. With the franc shock in the EURCHF, a few years ago, the price went down by 2200 pip within a few seconds and plunged many dealers into misfortune. Anyone who believes that such a thing can not happenmore, is wrong. At the beginning of 2019, some of the prices dropped 700 pips within minutes. So, if someone had just set five lot on a rising course, he would inevitably have been dragged down. In these fast movements, it is questionable when the first buyers come back into the market and the stop finally starts. In the most extreme case, that would have been a minus of $ 35,000. Had the account been $ 15,000, a $ 20,000 back payment would have been due. In my case, I might have lost a maximum of $ 2000. This is a crucial aspect that should not be neglected.

The typical business model of retail brokers is in most cases not suitable that customers make money. It is crucial that one can recognize potential conflicts of interest of the brokers. The danger is that the forex brokers usually know very well where customers are stopping, and that the prices are being pulled up or down around one or the other PIPs to "fetch" those stakes. Compare once in the cash market in EURUSD the highs and lows on major chart brands. If the cash market prices deviate too much from the broker, you should investigate more intensively and possibly change the broker.

Since I have multiple accounts with my broker, I can shift my money within seconds if I want to market with a higher number of lots. In the same way, I can again take my money from the risk area (my current trading account) and transfer it to the second account. In case of a uns in the 1 Tick Chart. Since I trade in the forex market, the specially created Time & Sales list helps me a lot more than thstrong drawdown, the secondary account is not affected. I basically work with virtual orders and stops that my broker can not see. In recent months, the market orders were clearly in the advantage, often I'm so fast in the market and out again that the broker would have no chance to chase me in the stop. Although I believe that the manipulation with an ECN broker is rather not given.

What remains at the end is the chance to win. In the futures market, the probability is three times higher than in the Forex market. We have already analyzed the reasons in detail. The reasons for the higher odds are the much better and more accurate data. Let's first look at the data we can get in the futures market.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

At point 1 we see the Time & Sales list, which is going down relatively quickly in periods of high volatility. In the middle of this list you can see the number of lots traded within one tick. The representation, the displayed Lot is not optimal. For me it is a significant difference if 1 lot or 20 lots were traded in one tick. Accordingly, the Time & Sales list should be adjusted accordingly. For the forex market I have built up a time & sales list, in the form of a graphical representation, which re list from the futures market. I will publish an extra post in the next few days.

Under point 2 you will see a way to view the cumulative trades that were carried out on different price zones. This presentation does not help me personally, but you have many options to change the presentation form. Under point 3 you can see a footprint chart in two different tick charts. This is a very interesting form of presentation for me, which gives me a clear advantage in the trade. Under point 4 we see the DOM. Many Forex market traders believe that this DOM is the holy grail, unfortunately this is a fairy tale. Point A shows the current price in the market and the spread (Level1). Point B shows an inventory of current buy and sell orders. In the context of this list, the entire folders are arranged according to their limitations. (Level2) Unfortunately, this is just a so-called limit order. However, this view is only half true, since the market is essentially determined by market order. The come, however, without notice in the market. Likewise, no stops are displayed in level 2. Point C shows the orders that have moved the price. This information is very interesting and can be found in the footprint chart again.

A big problem is the so-called spoofing. Many traders orient themselves on the Oderbruch to see at which level there is greater buying or selling interest. Often, larger dealers place orders in the market and thus fool a buying interest. Just before the limit order is picked up, it is deleted again. Under point D you can see exactly these deleted orders and immediately find out at what level a spoofing has taken place. Under point E you will find the volume of the current day and under point F the volume of the previous day, but this can be adjusted individually.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

The following overview shows a footprint chart in the 512 tick chart. On the left side you can see the accumulated volume, on the right side the Oderbuch Level 2. The red and green bars represent the respective movement between Open and Close. Unfortunately there is no Bioniccandle in this area, which may change in the future could. Inside a candle you will see two different numbers. The left number represents the settled bearish lot, the right number represents the settled bullish lot at a certain price level. The colored numbers indicate the imbalance in the market. BIDxASK Imbalance is a way to read the volume. It makes it possible to measure the difference of executed market orders on BID and ASK via a percentage filter and thus to see more aggressive market participants. As you can see in the graph, aggressive buyers are shown in green and sellers in the chart in red. Correspondingly, market reactions can occur again at these "aggressive" price levels. The imbalance in a chart, recognized in advance, can help you use relevant prices where there was aggressive pressure from buyers or sellers to time your entries and exits. These key areas show us the intentions of aggressive market participants and we recognize the prices at which the buy or sell activity begins. Resets to the relevant prices show here in the screenshot a clear reaction in favor of a bullish continuation. It is assumed that markets are driven by the positioning of institutional money. This can be seen by studying the large orders / volume. The BIDxASK Imbalance Chart gives us the advantage of not positioning ourselves against the prevailing order flow. Also at point 1 you will find two red colored zones. A very interesting algorithm searches out the strongest movements in the market and marks them. This form of presentation of the footprint chart is interesting in that one can immediately recognize at certain resistance zones whether strong buy or sell orders are absorbed.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Here we see another illustration in the 512 tick chart. The numbers on the left represent the number of the volume, the numbers on the right represent the number of completed trades. From this one can draw very interesting conclusions.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

In this form of representation, the volume in a candle is exactly divided within the tick chart. This allows you to see the strength within the candle relatively quickly and to deduce possible conclusions about a future resistance range.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

The same presentation as in slide 9, but here the volume was divided into bearish and bullish movements. The candle thickness can be seen even faster in this area.

Basically, I still record my resistance zones in the forex market within a 16-tick chart. As soon as the price reaches my marked resistance zone, I collect the data from the futures market. If I realize that very strong buy orders are coming in, but they do not lead to any price changes, I can assume that a larger player will absorb these buy orders. This approach increases my likelihood of predicting a trend change more reliably. However, it should be noted that I am a scalper only very short in the market and thereby achieve significantly higher profit quotas. It is also very interesting when the futures market often runs three times in a row at the same price, while the forex market ends in different prices. This is because the Future needs 0.5 pip per tick and the Forex 0.1 pip. This gives me much more accurate information in the forex within the price. That's crucial for a scalper.

Neither of the two markets is leading, so it could generate a potential advantage. The only advantage in the futures market is the deeper market insight that can be implemented well in the forex market. However, you only have an advantage if you have already marked your resistance zone within the Forex market. The procedure becomes very interesting, if one acts within a strong upward trend, the countertrend. If you have a particular zone in mind, you will need a medium term and short term confirmation that this particular zone is relevant. I've already shown you a few ways in different blogs to analyze the trend strength within specific time units. It should be noted that the confirmation usually take only a few seconds. If you hesitate too long, the chance is over quickly. Every trader has his own strategy and approach here. However, this additional information from the futures market is not cheap.

When a big player pushes the price up, he buys the euro and at the same time sells the dollar. The problem of big players is often not the entry, but the exit. So he needs enough traders willing to buy him the euro. So he searches the stop zones of retail traders. Right there he finds enough customers and can repel his order within a short time.

A big challenge is the differentiation of different orders in the market. A price is in an uptrend and suddenly there is a turnaround and the price is going down. Now there are three options. Pullback, trend reversal or equilibrium. Either somebody sells his previously purchased euro because he wants to realize the profit, or somebody buys the dollar because he thinks the price falls. In the third case, there is a struggle between buyer and seller within an equilibrium. Of course, there are different ways of acting in each price level, the key is to identify the strongest key player. Unfortunately, most come at the last moment with a quick market order. Although much more information can be obtained with the data in the futures market, this information is also severely limited.

In recent years, more and more coaches have entered the market who have sold the footprint chart and volume profile trading as a Holy Grail. There is no way to predict the market, as this market is purely coincidental. Although there are always the same processes, but also these processes wear off over time. Once many traders can identify certain processes, the big player has to come up with a new strategy. It's always about it. Deceive, camouflage and cash in. Since I act in very short time units, I can often take the fast movements with me. With small stops of 0.5 pip the losses are limited.

In a tick chart the differences between forex and futures are clearly visible, while in forex 5 movements take place, there isonly one movement in the future. I do not want to suggest that you should trade Forex with information from the future market. For my trading style, the information from the futures market seems to be worthwhile, whether this will last, we must wait and see.

Professionals act and anticipate, the retail trainers react and help with their stops the professionals to leaving. Professionals work strategically and follow the money and volatility while retail traders give up as soon as their strategy stops working. All who climb into the boxing ring must know the rules and know that they face a world champion. The unfair is that when the big player hits us, it hurts a lot. If we hit the big player, he probably will not even remember it. That's why we often leave the boxing ring with a black eye.

In principle, changes in exchange rates arise through the supply and demand behavior of the market players. Exchange rate changes have great macroeconomic significance and therefore play an important role in economic policy. Looking at changes in exchange rates over time, it can be concluded how market actors assess the development of an economy. A currency undergoes an appreciation when its price rises in the foreign exchange market; there will be a devaluation if their price on the foreign exchange market falls.

Who knows that and takes care of it, is already a long way ahead.

A kind of time & sales for MT4?

Hello dear subscribers,

Our project # 6 is about improving the probability of winning in the forex market from 1:19 with data from the futures market to possibly 1: 6. Today I would like to introduce a kind of time & sales list for the forex market. The idea to create a time & sales list for the MT4 was born when I started drawing in my resistance zones in the tick charts. However, this presentation can only use the data from the forex market and is therefore not comparable to a real time & sales list from the futures market.

Our project # 6 will deal with the largest currency pair in Forex (EURUSD) and Future (Euro FX E6). The best-known currency futures contract is the Euro FX Futures, which is listed on the CME (Chicago Mercantile Exchange) and can be traded 24 hours a day in electronic Globex trading. The ticker symbol is 6E and in this foreign exchange future, the euro is traded against the US dollar. The quotations are made with five decimal places, thus e.g. 1,12770 USD for the dollar. The smallest price change, a tick, is set at 0.00005. The tick value is 6.25 USD (0.00005 USD * 125.000 EUR / Lot.

First let's look at a time & sales list in future market (Euro FX E6).

Inserted Video

On Friday evening we had some volatility, on the left side you could clearly see the Time & Sales list. Any small $ 0.00005 change will result in a tick. In addition, the list also shows the number of traded lots at the respective price level.

In the futures market we get clear information about the number of participants and the number of traded lot. Although there is no allocation how many lots each player deals within a given time, there is a trick, however, how to recognize the big players anyway. But I will go into that in more detail in the next few weeks, when we take a closer look at the future data. In addition to spoofing identification, there are historical volume levels as well as high frequency trader algorithm tracking. In the last few days I was able to clearly identify and take some breakouts before they took place. These are the topics for the next weeks.

In contrast to stock trading, the Forex market does not take place at a central trading venue. Therefore, the volume can not be measured with standard tools on the stock market. If a trader buys a single share, then this corresponds to a volume of 1 in the order book of the respective stock exchange. However, this is not possible in currency trading designed for global trading. As a consequence, the volume can not be measured in terms of the number of shares acquired, but only by summing up all the price changes recorded during a fixed period. For a price change in a currency pair, a certain number of completed transactions must be determined. The volume is a popular instrument in the technical analysis of markets, as it offers an additional dimension in the analysis of the price development of an asset. It helps to determine the strength of price movements. If a price movement is accompanied by a proportional increase in volume, it is considered more important than without. Traders will have to wait until the end of the day for accurate volume counts. However, there are other ways that traders can determine the market volume, e.g. with the tick volume or with the number of price changes. A rapidly changing market price can be an indicator of high trading volume. Therefore, a tickchart in the forex market is the only alternative to get as close to the volume as possible.

Since we do not receive any lot in the forex market, our self-made time & sale list is no concrete statement about the traded lot. If you run my idea of the time & sales list in the MT4 over a tickchart, they come a bit closer to the volume. The best data is the stock market data, but this is a short-term alternative in the forex market.

Let's take a closer look at the idea.

If we take a closer look at a 1-tickchart in forex, we will notice that no real candles are formed. The chart shows only a few lines that have a different price structure. The question was, with which indicator we are able to combine these individual lines. If you use a regular Bull Baer indicator, it will not work. So we need an indicator that includes in its calculation the close of the previous candle to make a candle out of two strokes. One solution is the Heiken Ashi calculation. The disadvantage of this indicator is that it smoothes the individual values. However, the smoothing in a 1 tickchart is not quite as dramatic, so that good values can still be achieved.

The idea was simple, we create a second MT4 with a 1 tickchart into which the Heiken Ashi indicator comes in. For all traders who do not have a tickchart available, it is also possible to operate the Heiken Ashi in a 1 second chart. However, the values in the 1 second chart are much slower and less accurate. For this I have created a video.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

On the right side is the Time & Sales list from the futures market, where I have only made visible the number of traded lot in the futures market. We have to keep in mind that in the futures market a tick starts at $ 0.00005, while in the forex market a tick starts from $ 0.00001. Within the same period, there are significantly more ticks in the forex market than in the futures market. First of all, please pay attention to the difference between the 1 tickchart and the 1-second chart in connection with the course price. At first, the price goes down, there is a short pullback and then another price down.

Inserted Video

In the video you can see that the 1 Tickchart works much faster and cleaner than the 1 second chart. In the process, bearish or bullish investments in the market can be detected very quickly. Likewise, the volatility is relatively easy to detect. If the ad moves faster, the volatility increases. When the price goes up, you can see in the ad exactly the bearish objection that come in during the price. Pay close attention to the different circumstances of the bulls and bears. From this you can make assumptions, but the main decision to open a trade should always result from your strategy. In the past I have marked my resistance zones in the 16 tick chart. Once the uptrend came into my zone, the ad has often served me well. However, one has to keep in mind that the price often goes beyond the resistance zone, catch the trader's stops and then starts a stronger downtrend.

If you want to work with this indicator, you must first create a tickchart or a seconds chart in a second MT4. The indicator is then called in the offline chart. Let's come to your chance discovery. One speaks of chance when an event is unpredictable, when it is not deterministic. Science was originally operated to suppress chance. Today, however, we know that chance is an indispensable and fundamental part of nature. Unfortunately, the course is unpredictable and thus the formation of candles is a coincidence. You may have noticed some similarities over the past few weeks, and you are now creating a policy. Personally, I find that very dangerous because trading often involves a lot of money.

Let's return briefly to the construction of the bionic candle.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

At point A and B you will see a standard candle on the left side and next to it the representation of the Bioniccandle. While you get several movements with four pieces of information (OHLC) in a standard candle, the Bionicchart only has two movements with three pieces of information (HLC). The open can often be estimated from the close of the first candle. Gaps between the candles are not relevant to me. But if you look for gaps between the candles, you should also pay attention to the gaps in the candles, which in my opinion are just as important. However, one can often not recognize them in a normal chart.

A trader needs to gather a lot of information within a day. With the Bionik candle I have reduced this flood of information a bit, because you can identify only two movements. At point C you can see the gradations of each bioniccandle. Underneath you will find a table about the respective candle strength at point D.

The bullish bioniccandle eliminates the lower wick. If in this candle the high and the close are on a price level, then it is a strong candle for me. The bearish Bioniccandle eliminates the upper wick. If in this candle the high and the close are on a price level, it is also a strong candle. Footprintchart in the forex market?

Hello dear subscribers,

The identification of many resistance zones was made significantly easier and clearer with the use of the developed Bioniccandle. In contrast to the Renkochart and Heiken Ashi who smooth the course, the Bioniccandle shows the same course as a candlechart only a little clearer, since the Open was omitted. There are a maximum of 2 movements in each candle, the main movement and if the price does not close at high / low, additionally a pullback from high / low to close. The pullbacks within a bioniccandle have so far been more crucial than the main move to identify a possible turnaround.

In Project No. 6, we first test whether the detailed data from the futures market is useful for making trading decisions in the forex market. So far, the results are very promising, but the price movement in the Forex market is much finer, since a tick is $ 0.00001 and the future market is $ 0.00005. The price developments of both markets run almost parallel to each other, the reasons for which I have already described in detail. Post 967.

https://www.forexfactory.com/showthr...8#post12383408

Before I created my own blog at FF in January 2018, I spent many years visiting FF on a regular basis and noticed the professional contributions of a very creative programmer Hanover. This post by Hanover and some other professional traders was the reason why I opened a blog here. I was particularly proud when my post received 967 a Like from Hanover. This may seem ridiculous to many, but I appreciate the work and opinion of Hanover very much. As I only trade in the forex market because of the much lower risk, the data from the futures market is very valuable, but I wanted to check first whether a cluster chart (footprint chart) also works in the forex market. From the pure logic ago, that should not work, since the Forex market does not provide Lot, which are needed among other things to the calculation of a Footprintcharts. The market offers some footprints for the MT4, I chose the most effective one and bought it. The advertising sounded promising at first.

There are 6 criteria of cluster generation: Time interval, the criterion is set in seconds. Price range, the criterion is set in points. The current cluster is closed when the deal price goes beyond the specified price range. In that case, the current deal is included in the current cluster, while the next one opens a new cluster. The range is calculated as the difference between the High and Low price in the cluster. The difference (delta) between buy and sell volumes. The current cluster is closed when the delta with the next deal exceeds the specified volume. The next deal opens the next cluster. Total volume of deals. The current cluster is closed when the total volume of purchases and sales in the cluster exceeds the specified volume after one of the deals. Number of ticks. The cluster is formed by the specified number of ticks. Deal type. A cluster is formed by deals of the same type.

There are 7 types of cluster representation: "Delta" - display the delta. "Delta %" - display the delta as a percentage of the corresponding ASK or BID volume. "BID + ASK" - display the sum of BID+ASK volumes. "ASK & BID" - display the ASK and BID volumes separately, the ASK volume is drawn in the upper half of the cluster cell, the BID volume is drawn in the lower half. "BID x ASK" - display the ASK and BID volumes separately, the ASK volume is drawn to the right, while the BID volume is drawn to the left of the cluster center. "Delta and BID+ASK" - display the delta and the sum of BID+ASK volumes. "Delta% and BID+ASK" - display the delta as a percentage and the sum of BID+ASK volumes.

YuClusters features built-in volume filters, indicators of cumulative delta and weighted average price of the cluster volume.

YuClusters has a powerful system of alerts, which can be set to events related to clusters, volumes, prices and built-in indicators.

In the interbank market, there is no concrete volume, but only approximate values, since I use a very good ECN broker, I was sure to test that this advertising promise of YuClusters with the help of the data from the futures market. Of course, these are two different markets that are difficult to compare, but as the markets are linked by swaps, it should be possible.

Project 6 Forex & Future

Hello dear Subscriber,

Dark pools are bank or exchange trading platforms for the anonymous trading of financial products that are traded outside the open securities trading of the stock exchanges. The dark pools include areas such as Forex (Spot Currency Trading) and CFD (Contract for Difference). Dark pools are not subject to the rules and supervision of the European stock exchanges. There is no transparency in these markets. In the LIT market or light pool market, which refers to the ECN stock exchanges, there is an order book that will be published for everyone. This market allows traders to see the amount of liquidity.

Worldwide, there are about 70 exchanges, the ten largest produce a daily turnover of $ 800 billion. It is estimated that about $ 1.6 trillion will be transacted every day on all stock exchanges worldwide. The darkpool of the forex market converts about $ 5.4 trillion daily. Thus, the stock exchange has a share of about 25% of the total turnover (forex and stock market). Most of the trade is thus via the unregulated stock market.

Since the dollar is involved in currency trading in 88% and the euro in 38% of all cases, EURUSD is one of the most traded currency pairs in the Forex market and Euro FX in the futures market. Adding up the daily flow of capital in both markets adds up to $ 1,718,750,000. On average, Euro FX trades 150,000 Lot a day, making the futures market just 1%. That means the EURUSD is almost 100 times bigger than the Euro FX. 99% of the market is not regulated by stock exchanges and only 1% of total turnover gives us specific stock market data. Actually, it would be unwise to assume that one could use the Euro FX stock market data to make specific assumptions about the EURUSD forex. However, since the EURUSD is linked to the Euro FX via the swaps, this assumption is not entirely outlandish.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

In my post 967 forex versus future, I made a candle comparison between the two markets and found that the movements are almost identical. I have already explained the reasons for this in detail. Next, I wanted to know how the markets relate to each other in a very small amount of time. Since the ticks in the forex market are significantly smaller than in the futures market, I had to make an adjustment for a comparison. I would like to give a brief explanation of our upcoming project no. 6.

The goal is to match the forex data and future data so that it is possible to trade more successfully in the forex market due to the better information of the futures market. While in the forex market about 100 times as much money per day is converted as in the futures market, the profit opportunity of 1:16 is significantly smaller than in futures market with 1: 6. The attractiveness of the forex market is much higher and more interesting, but also more risky. As we have noted, this is due to the insufficient data provided in the forex market. In project # 6 we want to try to use the advantages in the futures market to realize higher profits in the forex market. Please note that this is only a project and not a recommendation based on futures data to trade in the forex market.

In addition to a MT4 with its own generated indicators, I have selected one of the best platforms for the futures market, which I think is currently available. ATAS is a professional trading and analysis platform for order flow and volume trading and offers many features for quick and easy market analysis: time and sales, level II data, current and historical volume levels, and HFT algorithm tracking. The platform prepares raw order flow data to present it to the trader in an intuitive manner. The range of functions includes very good filter options as well as flexible and dynamic setting options. The analytical tools of the platform significantly enhance the information content of the raw market data, leading to a comprehensive view of the market and, subsequently, improved trader performance.

Equilibrium, the key to success.

The market equilibrium is defined by the intersection of market demand and market supply curve. At the equilibrium price, the market is vacated, i. the quantity of goods offered corresponds to the quantity of goods demanded. At a higher price, the supply would be higher, but this quantity would find no buyers. Conversely, the demand quantity is greater than the supply quantity if the price is below the equilibrium price. In the case of an imbalance, undercutting or overcalling processes are set in motion by the providers or buyers, who still want to get a chance. In the undercutting process, those suppliers whose costs are higher than the new price are excluded from the overbidding process whose customers are willing and able to pay less than the increased price. At the same time, the suppliers are increasing their offered quantity with rising prices and the demanders are increasing their demanded quantity with decreasing prices.

A market is a trend after which equilibrium is created. After equilibrium, the trend continues or the trend direction changes. On the pullacks that form within a trend, I have now deliberately renounced. Within a trend, there are one or more strong major movements, then exhaustion and possibly absorption.

Equilibrium does not necessarily have to be created between different trend phases, in addition, the market consists largely of a sideways market. And exactly this market situation is for me a very interesting aspect, with which I will deal again in the next few weeks.

As soon as a trend has reached its exhaustion phase, an equilibrium or possibly a sideways market is usually created. A very interesting point is the absorption, which of course you can already see in the candles, but then it is often too late. Let's say, a course is going up a lot and eventually comes a period of exhaustion. The market initially moves sideways. Suddenly, strong buy orders come in, but they only change the price marginally. That could be an indication of absorption. Many big players first collect larger orders before pushing the price down in one fell swoop. As soon as they have collected their necessary folders, the course will be pushed up again to trigger the sellers' stops. As a result, the course shoots straight up. After that, the big player pushes the price down, because the fewer traders on the flight down, the better for the big player. And that is also logical, the many sellers that are already in the market, no longer help the big players to drive down the price, but they can only harm the big player. When the big player drives the price down, many small traders will exit this way to realize their profits. If many do that at the same time, that stops the course. Therefore, the big player has to push everyone out of the market before. Then the way down is a bit freer.

This absorption is to be identified in the futures market, it is not easy but it is possible. By setting a 1-tick chart, only one trade is shown to me. With that, I am able to recognize relatively quickly whether there are 10 Lot or 100 Lot in this trade. This could identify the big players. In addition, the order book and the time & sales list help me a lot. The most important point is the price change and a sense of the market. In the last week I was able to identify and take some breakouts in advance. Trading a breakout is one of the toughest and most dangerous challenges besides the pullback trade. The advantage: It is fast in and out again.

Basically, you never know how much market movement is created by ten lot, but you can determine a rough average value, which does not always help in the trade. It is crucial to identify a trend and then to recognize when this trend is exhausted. Another very interesting aspect is to put yourself in the position of a trader. Create a typical chart in the M15. There we build the most popular trader indicators. MACD, RSI, Stochastics, Moving Averages, Bollinger Bands and Fibonacci. This makes it even easier to estimate the possible stops of many traders. Or check out FF's chat, there you'll even find current stops in your currency pair. This helps in analyzing whether a big player might trigger a high number of stops.

The data from the futures market, especially processed with Atas, are already a clear advantage over the data from the forex market. But the biggest challenge is the interpretation of the recorded data. And we know, you can interpret each number differently.

If you give up a large ask order in the market, you buy the dollar and at the same time sell the euro. Maybe the course goes down. To get out now, I have to sell my dollar and buy euros at the same time. This means that the price can rise. An increasing price can therefore be triggered by two different market behaviors. A market participant who has set on a falling course wants to get off now. Another market participant who believes the price will rising, buys the euro and at the same time sells the dollar.

Of course, one could now assume that both market participants are right. The one who leaves the falling course may assume that the price can not fall further. The other market participant, which is on a rising course, expects the price to go up. For me, the distinction is already very crucial, but it is very difficult to find out the concrete.

Many market participants see this situation as a market recovery and bet on bid. The market trader who traded down and got out might have wanted to realize his profit and try to push the price down again after a pullback.

Behind a tick is always a buyer and a seller, we just have to find out who is the stronger of the two. With the data from the futures market, we already have a much deeper insight, but this is far from a guarantee to win.

In the next few weeks I will check to what extent the data from the futures market is useful for the forexmarket. I would like to emphasize once again that this is a project and not a recommendation. I'm very curious what comes out of it. Of course, I will regularly post the latest findings to you.

60% better trading in the forex market?

Hello dear subscribers,

In today's article, we want to deal with various information that we receive in the forex or futures market. This information is hugely important as we derive our trading decisions from it. So we have to be careful to get only information that is correct.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

In my post 906 and 907 we have already talked in detail about the three different data available to us in the Forex market. (Time, OHLC and Volume)

Over the past few days, I have compared the price of the EURUSD Forex with the Euro FX from the futures market. We found that the price trend is almost identical. We can assume that the OHLC and time data in the forex as well as in the futures market are represented very accurately. Provided that your broker transmits this price data without manipulation. Result: In this area, the futures market does not differ from the forex market. About the volume we have already spoken in great detail. In the forex market, it is not possible to provide a specific volume throughout the day. After the day is over, the forex market subsequently provides the specific volume, but then it is often too late. The volume refers to the number of lot, that are calculated on the bid or ask. Although the volume in the Forex market is already approaching the volume of the futures market a little, in the course of the day it is an estimate. In the futures market, in addition to a precise volume, there are also the number of traded transactions. This is important for the identification of big players, although the larger trading businesses usually run on market order.

If we now compare the forex market with the futures market, we get only 2.5 correct data from four important data in the forex market, while we have all the important data in the futures market. In the forex market, we therefore achieve a data efficiency of 62.5%, while we achieve 100% data efficiency in the futures market. This is an increase of 60% over the forex market and the reason for our project number 6.

While we have three dimensions in the forex market, of which one dimension (volume) provides insufficient information, the futures market has four dimensions. Today we want to take a closer look at these four dimensions.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

As soon as I create a chart in the futures market, I have to choose a dimension. This dimension is fixed and thus the three other dimensions are variable. When I choose a standard Chart M5, I choose the dimension of time. That means each candle is rebuilt after 5 minutes, and the data OHLC, trades and volume are subordinate and variable in their values. In the forex market, I have to choose a tick chart to be closest to the volume. In the futures market, I am now spoiled for choice, which information has the highest priority for me. In the stock market I only get these four values Time, OHLC, Trades and Volume. There are also delta, reversal, range candles and much more, but these are calculated from these four values. Likewise, there are indicators that show the speed of a candle, but this calculation is also created using these four values. First let's look at these four values in the chart.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Here we see a normal time chart M20 in the futures market. A footprint chart showing the imbalance in the price is shown. In the lower area you will find two indicators. The upper area shows the number of Lot (volumes) traded within 20 minutes. The bottom indicator shows how many trades were completed within 20 minutes. Time is the set value. The size of the candles (OHLC), the volume and the number of trades settle this fixed value of time. That means they have different values.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Here we see a Renko chart in Euro FX. The value has been set so that the main movement of a candle is at least / at most 6 ticks until a new candle is formed. This means all candles have a major movement of six ticks. Of course, the high to low can be different in size, the decisive factor here is only the main movement. The three other dimensions, such as volume, trades, and time, reorder and achieve different values. The two lower indicators may look like they have the same values, but that's not the case.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Here we see a 1024 Tick Chart in Euro FX. This means that after 1024 trades a new candle will be formed. We see, the lower indicator always has the same values, the last value could not close the 1024 trades, since Friday night closed. Again, the three other dimensions are subordinated again.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Here is a 1600 volume chart in Euro FX. This means that once 1600 lot have been made, a new candle is formed. In the upper volume indicator, we can clearly see that it is always a fixed value. As always, the three other dimensions are subordinated and each receive different values.

It is not possible to define two fixed values within the four dimensions. We always have to make a decision about what is important to us. However, this is a little different in the futures market than in the forex market. For example, if we choose a time chart M20, the volume and trades indicator gives us the option of displaying the respective values. Since we have no concrete volume values in the forex market, it is much harder to get clear and clean information.

It will be interesting for the next few months to find out how to coordinate these four dimensions to obtain crucial information. The presentation of the Bioniccandle should also be an interesting aspect.

First let's look at the leverage effect in the futures and forex mart.

In the financial sector, leverage is used to increase investment through debt and minimize the use of equity. The ratio of debt to equity (leverage) is the formula for the so-called leverage effect, with the more debt being used, the greater the leverage.

If a company, an investment or a fixed asset is described as "highly leveraged", this means that more debt than equity capital is used. If the investor succeeds in using the leveraged debt in such a way that its return is higher than the interest he has to pay for the debt, he has successfully traded. However, this also carries the risk of being unable to repay the debts incurred.

The use of a lever serves the following basic purposes:

Extend the investment size of a business or private investor and generate return on venture capital. In particular, the return on equity (ROE) and earnings per share (EPS) are to be increased.

Trading with a lever allows the trader to trade high sums with a low deposit in the live account. Levered trading is also known as margin trading. As a trader you can deposit a small amount with a broker and then borrow money from the broker to open a higher position. This allows the trader to maximize his profits. Conversely, however, potential losses can be maximized.

Many traders would call the leverage" loan", the broker would grant to their clients. This is not entirely true, since the lever does not share the properties of loans. If you trade CFD with leverage, no one expects you to repay a loan. You only agree to close the open position again or to hold it until it is done automatically by a margin call. A deadline does not exist and there is no interest to pay. Instead, swaps are raised when positions are held overnight. Unlike loans, these swap payments can even be profitable for the trader.

It is not easy to set the right lever for your trading, as it always depends on the individual strategy of the trader and his overview of the markets. As a rule of thumb you can say: the longer you intend to hold your position, the lower your lever should be. Long-planned positions are usually opened when large market movements are expected. And since you do not want to be stopped out by market fluctuations, especially in such, you should not exaggerate the leverage. On the other hand, when positions are opened that are expected to last only a few minutes (or seconds), traders prefer to use large leverage to maximize profit over a very short time, even with the smallest of price fluctuations.

Let's take an example of three different market participants. First of all, we have the non-professional forex trader, who is subject to ESMA regulations in Europe. He can act with a maximum lever of 1:30, but also microlot are possible. Then we have a standard account in the futures market, which in principle every trader can conclude. Here I have a standard lever of 1: 250 in Euro FX, but the minimum bet is 1 lot. At the end we still have a professional account in the forex market. Just 4% of all traders in Europe fulfill this requirement. There is a standard lever of 1: 400, it can also Microlot be traded, and if you're very lucky, there is no additional funding. This means the account can never go to minus, due to an uncontrolled breakout.

Let's take a closer look at these three different market participants.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

In the upper part, we find that when it comes to security, there are only two alternatives and these two alternatives can only be found in the forex market. Although the chances of winning are significantly lower there, with the data from the futures market we want to drastically increase the chances of profit in the future.

Now, for fun, we trade in the futures and forex market. Of course, there are different prices in both markets, but the price movements are identical, so for our example, let's just assume that we have the same prices in both markets. We are entering at a market price of 1.12525, our stop is 1.11515 and our target is 1.11575. We assume that this trade goes smoothly and we reach our goal.

The non-professional trader from the forex market has the same risk-to-reward ratio as the professional trader: 1: 3.6. Now many will think: This bill is not right. The stop was 1 pip, the profit was five pip, which is a risk-reward ratio of 1: 5. What was forgotten here is the cost of the spread. If I'm stopped, I'll have to pay the cost of the stop plus the spread. In this case, we had $ 14 risk to win $ 50. And that's a risk-reward ratio of 1: 3.6 at least that's my basis of calculation. The risk-reward ratio in the futures market is a bit smaller.

Crucial for me is another value and the ratio of profit to margin. As we all know, most traders get leverage from their broker and have to deposit a margin. This margin is a kind of risk capital. Now the question is: what is the return of my risk capital? And here there is a clear winner, the professional trader in the forex market. From 250 € risk capital, he makes 50 € profit while the future trader comes to a return of 12.5%. Since the non-professional trader has to provide a higher margin, the return here is only 1.5%.

But the calculation is not quite correct, because you are liable not only with your margin, but at least with the capital in the account and even beyond. With a leverage of 1: 250, the margin is $ 500 to trade 1 lot ($ 125,000) in the futures market. It's about the specific risk that I went in to win this $ 62.50. No matter how much money is on my futures account, I am unlimited in my private wealth. So far, there have been some major crashes within the stock markets, you always have to expect that there can be another crash. In principle, a crash would not be a problem if you were also able to manually exit at the moment, but unfortunately there are in a sharply falling market few buyers who are ready to buy your lot in the moment. From this risk perspective alone, the forex market is the only alternative to rationally protect its capital.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

In the following case, we assume that four times the capital of the required margin is in the brokerage account. In the futures example, that's $ 2,000, although I've already written that making an under $ 30,000 account in the futures area makes no sense. This is just an example. We have already determined that the future market is not an alternative in terms of safety.

So let's take a look at the three examples below within the forex market.

In the first example, a trader who has $ 100,000 on his forex account trades $ 100,000 for a total of 1 lot. He does not need any money from his broker. His profit is $ 50 for which he has risked $ 100,000. Of course, the EURUSD would have to fall to $ 0.1, which seems impossible from today's point of view. However, since there are $ 100,000 in the account, the forex account is also the liability capital. As a result, you would risk $ 2000 to win a dollar. This corresponds to a return of 0.05% in relation to the risk.

The participant, who is subject to the ESMA regulations, reaches with a leverage of 1:30 after all with $ 266 risk 1 dollar profit and comes thus to a yield of 0,38%.

A professional trader in the forex market, who trades with a leverage of 1: 400, in this case with a risk capital of $ 20, a profit of $ 1. The effective return is thus 5%.

I know that's a very unusual approach, so I'd like to say a few words about it. I think that beginners in the forex market are overwhelmed with a high leverage, because many are driving inappropriately high stakes and can quickly destroy their capital. However, I am a professional trader who has been trading in the forex market for many years. For me, a high lever is a low risk because I could trade the same position even without levers. But I do not do it to minimize my risk.

Why that is so I would like to explain. Suppose I trade a lot and use $ 100,000 in equity. Now there is a big crash like in Euro Swiss Francs. 2000 pip, the price goes down until the stop is triggered. Then I make a loss of $ 20,000.

In the second case, only $ 1,000 is in my account, I'm trading again with a margin of $ 250. In the case of the Euro Swiss franc, the price is again 2000 pips against me. Then my $ 1000 is gone and that's it. That's a difference of $ 19,000.

Since I act sometimes with more than 10 Lot, everyone can quickly figure out that this approach is very interesting. Basically, I recommend only to act with a high level of leverage, if you can afford it and have enough experience. My approach should also not be a call to act at high risk.

For the broker, the lever is an interesting business. A lever of 1: 400 means a four-hundred times higher fee for the broker. No matter if we trade only with our own money or get a lever from the broker, the spread is always the same. Interestingly enough, many brokers allow trading only with margin, you do not have to say anything more.

In certain circumstances, a high level of leverage is even very safety-oriented. It is always a question of view. Of course, in the case of a loss with a lot and a high lever, the money is faster away than with a smaller lever. But if I acted without leverage, my money would be gone just as fast. And in case of an absolute fall, I would not have any security.

It does not work in the futures market, I liability with my entire fortune. Many claim that a professional trader would only trade in the futures market. Maybe you will see it now with different eyes. That's one of the reasons why I'm not afraid of trading because what can happen to me? In the worst case, there are a few $ 1000 gone, but we also have to be fair to offset the odds we have in this market. In that sense, I am very happy about the ESMA regulations, because it protects our hard-earned money in the Forex market, there can not be anything better.

And if we manage to use the data in the futures market for the forex market, we have killed 3 birds with one stone. We have improved our profit share, can make significantly more profits and have a high level of security. We will see if it works.

I wish you a successful week

Anniversary 1,000 posts

Self-employment in the forex market

Hello dear subscribers,

In early January 2018, this blog was launched as a kind of trading diary. The goal was to explain myself my own trading style, to learn to correct mistakes and to develop myself further. That's why it's not uncommon for me to have a writing share of 66.6% on this blog. With over 300,000 words we could already fill 3 books. During this time I have posted over 90 interesting indicators, over 1000 images and 5 completed projects including the Bioniccandle. The 6th project has already started and seems to be the most important project. In 19 months, over 95 subscribers have joined this blog. Quit pro quo, is my motto, I am ready to share my knowledge, even if you are ready for it.

At this point, I would like to thank all subscribers and former subscribers who have brought this blog forward. I am very proud of the fact that more and more a group of great different people from all over the world is forming in this blog, which receives and shares information. That's exactly the goal of moving forward together. I am particularly pleased that this blog is friendly, open and fair. In the beginning, I have also been in other forums to find like-minded people for this blog, but I now think that sometimes less is more. Of course, we are happy when other subscribers share the idea of supply and demand and come up with ideas. This blog is a kind of buffet, there are many different dishes that do not suit everyone. But nobody is obliged to try everything. You get the best out and you're satisfied.

On the occasion of the 1000 contribution in this blog I would like to write today about the independence of a Traders. Maybe they are now changing from amateur to professional. The difference between the two is that the professional lives off his job, while the amateur has his cost of living regulated by other income.

Annotation:
This text was a bit more difficult for me in the translation, I ask for leniency, if it comes to misunderstandings that I like to clean up.

Why do you want to become a trader?

money

The financial industry is the industry that makes the most money. Hourly wages between $ 50 and $ 500 are not uncommon and thus guarantee an above-average quality of life, which in this form is reserved for only a few people. Many people dream of financial independence. But most people do not achieve this independence, because it does not allow the job situation in most countries. Here, the financial market offers excellent prospects, which can be achieved with an efficient way of working. However, the stock market is one of the most difficult markets in the world.

life quality

Everybody dreams of things he could not afford in the past, such as a car, home, vacation, jewelry, fancy food, beautiful clothes, expensive leisure activities. Few people get the chance to achieve this because they are hindered by social norms in their professional advancement. Then they lose the desire for a career someday. However, you also have to be prepared to work harder and more strategically.

fun

There is nothing better in life than to practice a job in which growth rates are automatically preprogrammed, where there is no unemployment and people are rewarded for what they do. This brings freedom and independence and a lot of fun.

open time-management

As a full-time trader you should complete a weekly time of about 60 hours. This means you work either 5 days á 12 hours or 4 days a'15 hours. With open time, you decide when to start working, take a break, end your day, and when to spend your weekend and vacation. 60 hours a week is only an approximation, to become successful in the long term as a trader. So it's just a matter of efficiency, because there are people who can do it in 40 hours.

high reputation

Many people dream of becoming a doctor, lawyer, stockbroker, judge, pop star or actor in order to enjoy a high reputation in public. The stock market offers in public an excellent platform for high reputation and recognition.

recognition

It has been proven that people receive too little recognition in their work and leisure activities. While the supervisor usually lies in wait and seems to be waiting for mistakes in order to blame you in front of others, you will immediately receive your confirmation or blame in the stock market.

leisure

On average, Europeans work 250 days a year, although there are small differences within each country and region. This means that you not work for 115 days to enjoy your free time and vacation. If you divide your life into work, leisure and sleep, you will find the following: for the work you have an expenditure of 8 hours which is the pure working time. There are also breaks and possibly overtime and the commute. Overall, this results in a complete time of about 11-12 hours you have to calculate for the work. Within one year, this results in approximately 2,900 hours of effort for your work, in individual cases, of course, more.

365 days by 8 hours of sleep are also about 2,900 hours. The remaining 2,900 hours remain for family, leisure, body care, food, etc. This means you spend a third of your life on work, one third with leisure and one third with sleep. Because you do not consciously experience life in your sleep, it means: Your conscious life is 50% work and 50% leisure. Depending on your life situation, you have to deduct at least 50% of this free time, which you need for private obligations. So you may only have 25% of your free time (sometimes much less) available for recreation and with the financial resources also different ways to spend your free time.

It would be nice, however, if you could turn your hobby into a job and thus pursue an activity that you do not necessarily feel as work. Now, if you're ready to do more work, believing that you'll have to sacrifice a lot of free time, that's only partially true. After all, leisure is not a question of duration but of intensity. It always depends on what time frame and what kind of leisure activities you want to pursue. How many times have you been bored in your free time, because you may have lacked the financial resources to engage as you would have liked?

Motivating workplace

When working at home, often eliminates a costly and long journey. You are flexible with the establishment of your workplace and can thus ensure a comfortable atmosphere.

independence

The word says it clearly. You decide for yourself what you think makes sense in your life. However, the word independence means having to kick your ass. This requires a personal responsibility for his job and his personal success. You decide yourself where to prioritize. You will not be patronized by an unpleasant boss who only works for his own wallet. Self-employment makes you independent and gives you the feeling of freedom. However, you must be willing to fight hard for your success.

security crisis

The financial services market is one of the most expansive markets in the world. Double-digit growth rates in the area are completely normal. They work in a non-cyclical market as the markets interact. For example, if one particular market weakens slightly, other markets will increase sales. We work in the largest market in the world, money is always exchanged.

entrepreneur

As an independent trader you are an entrepreneur. You receive significant tax benefits and are exempt from social security in certain countries. Your taxes will not be deducted from earnings as usual. Some do not have to pay the overpaid taxes in the form of a wage tax compensation, but at the end of the year pay the maximum tax due to the tax office. As an entrepreneur, you can deduct things tax that are not possible for the simple salary recipient, eg. Your office, brokerage, your computer equipment u.v.m. However, you have to generate revenue for it.

Of course, it is nice as a trader to take advantage of the pleasant pages and thereby push the unpleasant side. But to become successful and to remain so there are conditions for traders that are not to be talked away.

Prerequisite for success

No 40 hour week

If you want to be successful, you must be aware that you can not cope with this with 40 hours. Certainly it depends on the type of activities that you can do within a certain time frame. However, you will not know a tax accountant, solicitor or entrepreneur who has succeeded in spending less than 50, 60 hours of work per week.

It is a question of efficiency and the willingness to spend, if necessary, in one week the time required to achieve the goal. So it can happen that you have to work 70 hours in one week and 50 hours in the next week. The sometimes consistent renunciation of freedom and comfort ensures a lasting, advancement in the profession.

Irregular working hours

As a trader you often work at times when other people have free time. The markets are not mine, so I have to follow the markets and then work when it's worth it. After working on the stock market comes the analysis and preparation for the next week. Maybe I have to revise certain strategies or develop new strategies that only works in times when you are not in the trade. This willingness requires some flexibility on your part and, of course, on the part of your family, which will certainly be accepted if a corresponding financial compensation is created.

Permanent training

Standstill is a step backwards, as a trader you must endeavor to learn more every day. Through targeted reading of books, information from the Internet, memorizing key figures, data and facts, you will strategically advance not only in your personal development but also in your area of expertise. This will enable you to develop further. Most traders fail because of your attitude. They already believe they know everything. As an eternal student, however, you have the opportunity to become a master in many areas by continuing your education and training on a regular basis.

Absolute concentration when the markets work

As a rule, I got up at 5 o'clock in the morning, breakfast, sports, showers, then from 6:30 CET preparation for the day. From 7:00 CET it started in EURUSD until about 12:00 CET. Then 2 hours break until 14:00 CET. Full concentration from 14:00 CET to 17:00 CET, with the highest volatility in Europe and the US. From 17:00 CET 1.5 hours break and from 18:30 CET again 2 hours of trading, sometimes longer. That was 10-12 hours a day and weekend was time for strategy and evaluation. Important: If the markets are running and I have to earn my money, I have no time for phone calls, Youtube, programming or other disruptions. I have to concentrate 100% and do not let myself be distracted. If I lost 3 trades in a row, I took a short break, then it went on. In the beginning there were weeks where I worked 80 hours. The time factor was the crucial point. A successful stockbroker told me that I should watch 10,000 hours of candles, after which the breakthrough might come. I do not completely share this view, but there is some truth in every sentence. The fact is that after 10,000 hours I have more experience than after 2,000 hours, provided I focus on the right goal.

If I spend 5 hours trading daily, it takes me 8 years to complete 10,000 hours. With 10 hours of trading per day I reach the goal in 4 years. When I focus on the right things, after 4 years I have completed my education and can now work to become a professional. If you spend 2 hours trading daily with your main profession, you need 20 years to get to the 10,000 hours. The profession trader is one of the most difficult professions in this world and experience is the most important trait to pass. And experience takes time. Of course, there are natural talents who have reached their destination in less time, there are also lottery millionaires who have become rich without working.
