Gold in Forex

Hello letsride,

First of all, welcome to our blog. The same question I asked myself many years ago, because gold has always fascinated me.

Precious metals have always had a special place in human history. It used to be exchanged for goods, but with the entry of currencies it lost its importance in trade. Today it is considered a security in currency crises.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

The total amount of gold produced is estimated at 195,000 tonnes and corresponds to a cube with an edge length of approximately 21 meters. 3,500 tons of gold are added every year. Central banks and other institutions own just 18% of total gold. Of these, the US is in first place with 28.8%. Since gold is practically indestructible and, strictly speaking, is not consumed, theoretically every ounce produced is still available today. By value, this amount of gold today equals $ 9.37 trillion. For comparison, the Forex market trades more than $ 5 trillion per day. When all currencies lose value, gold provides the necessary security, but food and water are more important to survive.

In addition to the geopolitical tensions caused by the trade dispute between China and the US or the increasing tensions in the Persian Gulf, economic data point to weaker global economic development. This burdens the mood of companies and corporate profits. Increased volatility could cause investors to diversify risk by adding gold to their portfolios, as the correlation of gold with equities is low to negative. For me these are too many different factors that have an impact on all commodities. Some factors affect prices, but many do not. In the field of precious metals, platinum and palladium are predicted to have a greater future, as it is more urgently needed in the industrial sector.

A very important aspect, one should not forget when trading forex with gold. There is no physical gold, only money. And if the price of gold should rise so high because the money is no longer worth it, a huge profit in the form of money on the stock market will not benefit me. For that you should put physical gold in the vault. Gold is an insurance against devaluation. And insurance costs money and often brings no returns. Of course, the short-term speculation in the forex market is not comparable.

To identify a strength in gold one would have to work with correlations, e.g. Compare the dollar index with the gold price, but these correlations are constantly changing. Also the euro and dollar strength are no guarantee for a secure profit in EURUSD. Of course, one can make good profits with the speculation in the precious metals. The decisive factor is: to have an information advantage.

For me, there are too many different influencing factors to consider in the precious metals or currencies area to make a long-term future forecast. Therefore, I am working with the short-term stock market data and trying to scan the market in the sideways phases for bid and ask absorptions. You can react to that very quickly. This also works very well in the precious metals sector. Gold was interesting to me many years ago, but today I prefer to trade in a high-volume market with low drawdowns. And the EURUSD is a very good choice.

If you specialize in gold, you should create an individual setup. What information, indicators or stock market data will help you make the right decision? Unfortunately, this is a process that can often take many years, but once you have found your optimal setup, it will pay off. No matter if it is EURUSD or gold.

best regards

Delta from the past

(Volume data of the last 7 years as excel file to download)

Hello dear subscribers,

at certain price levels, there is an above-average increase in trade than at other price levels. From this, interesting assumptions can be derived. I would like to post some examples today.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

First, with the stock market data, I have retrieved a list of all price levels from 01.12.2012 to the present day. On the list next to the price we see the cumulated volume, the cumulative trades as well as the cumulated ask and bid at the respective price levels. The delta results from the cumulated ask and bid. For me, this delta is a crucial factor for possible resistance and support zones.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Then I copied the data into an Excel file and analyzed the ratio of the volume to the number of trades. At the bottom we see the number 1.83 and above the number 1.64. The smaller the number, the higher the probability that more big players were involved in this price level than in the higher numbers. From this, further assumptions can be derived.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Here we see a volume delta of this last 7 years in the weekly chart. When you mark the largest deltas, this gives a rough overview and a range is created. This range we now want to look in smaller time units.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

On the left side, I first displayed the delta volume in the weekly chart and compared it with a H1 chart in the exact price comparison. With the three largest Volumendeltas again a rough price range arises in the H1 from the 25.September to today.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Now we zoom in and take a closer look at the last trading day from 10:00 CET. Again, the three largest deltas were used to form a range. By looking at the volume, I can list Bid and Ask individually and thus make the zones even more concrete. We recognize that the past delta volume may have an impact on future price performance. Of course, you can also further narrow down the individual zones with the current Market Profile in order to receive a confirmation.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

The goal is to get below the Vol Low or above the Vol High a good entry to trade direction POC. In the area of the POC, on the other hand, one should be more cautious. The accumulation or distribution phases in the vicinity of the POC (points A and B), on the other hand, are particularly valuable and give a trader interesting information about a possible further course of the price. Even with the argument: I do not make forecasts where the price goes, I just trade with the price, you always have to make an assumption where it can go. But with the right information, it is possible to get an information advantage. And that is our chance to turn the odds in our favor.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

If I drive my vehicle in an unknown area, I get help with a map or a navigation system. Take a look at this map and ask yourself where we are right now. They will not always be right, but at every stage there are certain behaviors of the big players, with which they betray themselves.

Therefore, it is important to work only with information that helps me determine my location. There are different market situations, only certain information will help me. Therefore, I recommend to use different information in different market situations. It is enough to analyze the points A to D closer and to think about what happens in these crucial phases. Information and indicators help not in each phase. Once they are able to identify these individual phases, they are already ahead of most traders. After that, it's only about a good entry and exit.

Go back in time and identify these 4 phases. Afterwards they look with the help of the stock market data exactly, which happened exactly in these phases. This will allow them to put together exactly the indicators or charts that will help them in this phase. This will also enable you to find out where you are. Compiling this navigation system is a real project and can only be done by you. Even if the road is difficult, in the end you will know why.

I wish you that you find this way for yourself.

A successful trading week.

best regards

--- 帖子 #1105 ---
[quote=jusiur;12557588]Dear Bionics, I'm very interested in your posts, they have a great value.

Hello jusiur,

First of all thank you for your kind compliment to this blog. My idea to investigate the relationship between forex and future was based on the fact that both markets are almost tick-matched. This resulted in our project Nr.7. The leading factor is clearly the forex market which is over 100 times bigger. Since I act basically only in the EURUSD I compare here only the EURUSD with the Euro FX. Further information can be found in my very detailed article on the futures and forex market.

Forex versus future

The forex and futures market are linked to the swaps in order to prevent interest rate differentials that have a negative impact on the market as a whole. A foreign exchange swap (FX swap or forex or foreign exchange swap) is a foreign exchange transaction that consists of a foreign exchange spot transaction (FX spot) and a forward exchange deal (FX forward). Two currencies are exchanged for one another by spot and swapped back at a later date (swap). Both transactions of a foreign exchange swap are concluded simultaneously and with the same counterparty. The price in the Futuremarkt lies about 50 pip over the price of the Forex. The variable swaps close this difference.

The EURUSD in the forex market is the biggest challenge in the market because there is no specific volume information for market participants. The EBS (Electronic Broking Services), the world's largest trading platform for foreign exchange in interbank trading leads an anonymous central limit order book, to prevent high-frequency traders from their speed alone have an advantage over the other market participants. Therefore, this market for high-frequency trading is not quite as interesting as the stock market environment. Since the sales in the futures market are 100 times smaller, this market is less interesting for me. If you want to have an execution in the Forex market, you usually get them immediately, no matter how many Lot you want to trade. Since the prices of both markets are almost tick-to-toe, I came up with the idea of using the information of the futures market for trading in the forex market without taking a big financial risk. My assumption has been confirmed in recent weeks, but stock market data is a big challenge. Since I am very creative, I combine different information of the stock market data with the data from the forex market. I work on 8 large screens exclusively in EURUSD and Euro FX. This gives me the comfort of creating interesting shortcuts that nobody would ever come up with.

As both markets are indirectly linked, the trades of the high-frequency traders naturally have an indirect impact on the cash market. But interestingly enough, I get a little closer to these high-frequency traders every day with the stock market data. However, the big focus is on the 12 banks (big players) that control 85% of the Forex market. These banks decide where the course is going and not the news or economic conditions. In the accumulation or distribution phases, the big players try to acquire as many as possible Ask or Bid to push the course up or down. And it always depends on whether retail traders are willing to provide ask or bid. After all, only retail traders are usually loser in this market.

As I wrote in my last post Delta from the past I will create my individual card views of the 4 crucial patterns on the market.(Accumulation, re-accumulation, distribution and re-distribution). From this, interesting possibilities can be derived. I can not prove that my assumptions are correct. After all, this is a project and the results so far are promising. I also have no problems to share my findings with everyone, because with my setup anyway no one can do something. For the compilation of ideas, however, every trader is responsible. But that's the only way to be profitable in the long term.

--- 帖子 #1109 ---
Identification of the big players

Hello dear subscribers,

As we have already stated several times, we have to put ourselves in the situation of big players to follow you. For this, it is important to first understand what is causing movements in the market. 12 banks control 85% of the forex market, identifying them is easier than with 50 banks.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

When I press the buy button, I get Ask. The price goes still up. Now I want to sell my Ask and hit the sell button. That means I sell the euro and buy the dollar at the same time. I buy Bid to dissolve my previously acquired Ask. This sale could cause the price to go down. If the price does not develop in my desired direction, but runs down and triggered my stop, I buy at the moment also Bid which can make sure that the course is even more down. This strategy is very much used by the big players in stop fishing. When I press on the sell button I buy Bid. That could make the price go down. As soon as I want to resell my Bid, I have to buy Ask. This allows the price to go up. And this is where we come to an important insight. A course goes down and suddenly there is a strong bullish candle. That does not necessarily mean that someone buys the euro. It could well be that a big player who pushed the price down now sells his dollars. Of course, it does not matter if you buy the euro or sell the dollar. In both cases Ask is required. But if a big player gets out to sell his dollars, the price is unlikely to rise immediately, but rather to run sideways. Therefore, it is crucial to know if someone is buying the euro or selling the dollar. However, identifying this is a big challenge.

The big players have so much money that they can push the price up or down within a few seconds. Why this would not make sense, I would like to point out now.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Point A

The price is at 1.10250 and we assume that there are limit orders of 100 lot at each price level. Of course, the market is usually determined mainly by the market order, which we want to exclude for our example. Now, if a big player buys 1100 Lot Ask, the price will run to 1.10305. With the purchase he has broken through eleven price levels, each with 100 Lots.

Point B

The price is now at 1.10305 and the big player has received 1100 lots at an average price of 1.10280. This purchase creates a large bullish candle. We now assume that this will attract more buyers, driving the price to 1.10360.

Point C

At this stage, the big player now wants to get rid of his purchased 1100 lot.

Point D

By selling the price has gone back to 1.10305. The big player was able to sell his 1100 Lots at an average price of 1.10335.

Point E

1100 Lot Ask were bought at an average of 1.10280 and sold at 1.10335. This gives the big player an advantage of 55 ticks and a profit of $ 393,250 without spread and fees.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Point A

First, the big player collects 600 Lot Ask within a sideways market. After that he drives the price up by 5 ticks with 500 Lot Ask. In total, he also invested 1100 plumb bobs.

Point B

Now the price is at 1.10275, with a bullish candle upwards. This bullish move attracts more buyers. In total, the big player has purchased on average 500 lots at 1,10265 and 600 lots at 1,10225.

Point C

The price runs as in the first example to 1.10360. At this price level, the big player wants to sell his 1100 Lot Ask.

Point D

By selling the price goes back to 1,10305. The big player has sold his 1100 lot at an average price of 1.10335.

Point E

Result: 1100 Lot Bids were sold at an average of 1.10335. On average, 500 lot Ask were bought at a price of 1.10265 and 600 Lot Ask at a price of 1.10225. This results in a profit of $ 656,500 without spread and fees.

I believe that you can see from this example that it makes no sense to simply push up or down a price. Crucial is the collection of ask or bid in the sideways phases. Therefore, I concentrate exclusively on these phases and try to find out what is mainly bought there.

Important: As a rule, the big players do not sell their Ask or Bid in one fell swoop. Ask can only be sold if other market participants still expect prices to rise. Therefore, a big player sells his ask in small numbers in the rising market. He does not try to slow down the course. The advantage: The course continues to run upwards and the Big Player receives even better prices when exiting. Once the big player is out, there is no one more who drives the price up. What happens afterwards is clear and the last will bites by the dogs.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

If you work with the stock market data, I recommend you to pay attention to the accumulated delta. If the delta falls, it means that more Bid have been invested, than Ask. As the delta increases, it means that more than Ask as Bid has been invested. In the sideways phase at point B you can see very well how the cumulative delta falls sharply down. At first the price rises, but after that the price drops more. With the cumulative delta you can see many market situations faster.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Another example in the stock market is the distinction between smart money and dump money. We have already talked about this in detail.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

When looking at different price developments, I always ask myself the question with a bullish candle: Is the Euro being bought or the dollar sold? With a bearish candle: Will the dollar be bought or the euro sold?

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

In my stock market software, I have the indicator: "Big Trades" available. This indicator finds large trades in the current market and represents them within the chart. This requires a special algorithm that sums up a large number of similar trades in a trade and presents them in an individual size. Than I thought about the price course and labeled the single big trades. Of course, this is purely speculative and based solely on my personal opinion. But it helps me to analyze the market better.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

From my individual opinion I drew resistance zones. At point A (Friday morning), a good friend told me that he wanted to go short now because he was firmly convinced that the price was falling. I told him that this was just a stop fishing and I assume the price will go up sharply thereafter. The background was that at point B very strong purchases took place in the market, which led me to this assumption. Maybe it was just luck, but I seem to have more luck with it than with other views.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

If you do not have stock market data, you should focus on the currency strength in the forex market. I have already reported on this in detail in the last posts.

Currency strength in the forex market

Point A

The course initially went down and there was a sideways market.

Point B

In this sideways market, the dollar initially still has the upper hand, but it moves in parallel to the strength of the euro.

Point C

Here you can see that within the sideways phase of the dollar is sold strongly. That alone is a good indication that the market is saying goodbye to the dollar. At the end of the sideways phase, one can finally see that the market is beginning to buy the euro. All these are clear signs that the course may be goes up.

Of course these are just assumptions and pure speculations. But to win in this market, one must always assume assumptions. Only the one who has an information advantage over all others, is able to optimize his profits. And that's exactly what works on probabilities. If one realizes that the market sells the dollar, the probability is very high that the price will rise. Of course, it can also be different in reality, but we have our stops, for avoid greater damage. With the currency strength in the forex and the Bid and Ask in the future, I'm not always able to turn the odds in my favor. But when I realize what happens in a candle with Bid and Ask, the probability of winning is already much higher. And since this market is only about probabilities, this information advantage could help you a lot.

Try to get rid of the price, because the price is just a reaction to the previously invested Ask and Bid. With the stock market data, the view is much easier but also with the currency strength can be made quite interesting assumptions in forex.

I keep my fingers crossed for you and wish you a successful week

--- 帖子 #1110 ---
Trading, every risk is also an opportunity.

Hello dear subscribers,

There are approximately 5,000,000 traders worldwide. In relation to a world population of 7.75 billion people, this is just 0.6%. Even the proportion of doctors is 3 times higher, as there are 1000 doctors for two residents. Trader is a very special profession and if you're wondering if you want to become a long-term trader, you should first look at opportunities and risks. Konrad Adenauer, a former Chancellor of Germany, used the Adenauer Kreuz when he had to make an important decision. On one sheet he noted on the left: "What speaks for it?", On the right side he noted: "What's speaks against it"? After he had noted all the points, he forgave every single point a value. The values were added together and at the end he had a decision-making aid. This works with all questions and helps us to get a quick overview. Us are often unaware, that we have a choice. We just have to learn how to get the most out of these choices. It often happens that we decide wrongly. It does not matter how we decide between A and B, but that we first make sure there is a C and D. For many of us, this is unthinkable at first because we usually only make A or B decisions and exclude C or D decisions. But these alternatives are often the best.

Let's look first at what speaks against trading.

1.The most difficult market in the world

The interbank market is the market where money and credit business takes place only between banks. Banks and financial institutions trade with one another in the interbank market, lend each other money and can thus ensure that they remain liquid. The rates of currencies are not determined by a government as long as they are freely tradeable and not linked to another currency. They are based solely on supply and demand. Forex trading is usually OTC, i. E. it is not centrally organized, but takes place directly between the market participants or through a broker. Over $ 5 trillion is being transacted daily in the forex market. By the end of 2019, the $ 6 trillion limit is to be reached. This would have increased the volume of 1995 almost sixfold. In 24 years, the Forex market has thus achieved an average increase of 7% per year. There is no regulatory authority. Only twelve banks control 85 percent of the market. Banks do not trust each other and no one provides information about his trading activities. Therefore there is no real volume or an order book in the interbank market. The resulting volumes in MT4 are a pure estimate.

2. The trade strains our nerves

Depending on which market you are in, different volatility arises during the day. If they are on the right side, strong volatility creates a quick profit target. On the other hand, high volatility may also cause a quick loss. In 70% of the cases the prices move in sideways phases, what makes it difficult to trade for the swing and day traders. Of course, if you win, you can get positive feelings, with big loses you get the opposite. These feelings affect our behavior on the stock market. In an emergency, our body is focused on it: fight or flight. At that moment, our body releases hormones like adrenaline, norepinephrine and cortisol. The heartbeat is increased, the respiratory tract widens and the digestive system shuts down its function. This stress situation is permanently harmful to our body. Therefore, a balance like sport is a crucial point in order to be successful in this profession over the long term.

Many beginners are afraid and panic when the first trades fail. Instead of gaining distance and strategically realigning, the beginner wants to recover his loss as quickly as possible. All strategies and rules are forgotten. Often this is the beginning of the end. The same is true when greed makes you want too much. The stock market is a sea of emotions and it requires a high degree of psychological discipline to succeed in the long term in this market.

3.How successful are traders really?

Unfortunately, there is no trader in the Forbes list of the richest people in the world. If it is really possible to systematically predict price movements, there would have to be somebody who made millions or billions. The biggest billionaires are pure investors. An investor who speculates in investment funds has the advantage that he can buy his shares with the so-called cost average effect. In addition, his costs are significantly cheaper than if he speculated on the stock market.

Cost Average Effect

This does not mean that you as a trader could not be successful, it is only much harder than an investor. Trading stocks, CFD or futures is a special challenge. The chance to win as a trader is 1:23 in the stock market, 1:19 in the forex and 1: 6 in the futures market. The 1:19 chance in Forex means that 95% of traders lose long term. One of the main reasons for the loss is the high trading fees. The more you trade, the more likely you are not to be profitable. This gives a Swing Trader better cards than a Scalper. In search of successful traders, one inevitably comes to the trading experts who offer training, indicators or individual training.

4.The illusion of trading experts

In times of social networks there is a lot of envy, at the same time feelings arise: "That's what I want to achieve". On Instagram, YouTube and TicToc, many traders show their profits and tell of their rise to the league of the beautiful and the rich. Some also tell the supposed truth and start trading as a coach one year later. The alleged evidence these self-proclaimed trainers deliver can be forgotten. Nowadays you can fake the best stock market evaluations so that nobody notices. And even if real trades are mapped, it is hard to see whether this profit is actually based on competence or only by pure chance. Because there are over 5,000,000 traders, it is just by chance clear that some without any talent or skills to earn their money. Success can not be judged solely by whether someone makes money on the stock market. It is crucial that he is able to show others how to live long term from trading. This will succeed in the rarest cases, since each person is different. In the great YouTube videos where huge profits are shown, it is amazing that the losses are left out. That is also clear, because with losses one can not win customers. In principle, all this is a Facebook world, you see beautiful pictures and envies the other for his life. In reality, the other's life is only average and he show a life that he does not have in reality, just to attract customers. The fact is: a really successful trader will never act as a coach, or have you ever seen that Warren Buffett in the internet offering seminars? A successful trader trades for a few hours each day and enjoys the rest of the time with friends or family. Why should he take the stress out of running some $ 1,000 seminars and messing with dissatisfied customers. Believe me, most trainers are eunuchs who speak of intercourse and have no more idea than most beginners.

5.A critical look at the money

Everyone dreams of a beautiful life, with all amenities. What do you think why so many people play the lottery? Did you actually know that not the amount of money in a job is crucial, but first and foremost a balanced work-life balance, followed by leadership style and corporate culture? Makes money really happy now? Some studies have shown that it depends on how the money was earned. Assuming that the money was earned honestly and conscientiously, happiness is higher than if it was generated in a morally reprehensible manner. What matters is that morality thwarts us when we make our money with a guilty conscience. Honestly earned money actually makes you happy, if only for a short time but unfortunately not permanently. Before I started trading, I earned above average money in my job. The reason I chose to trade was the work-life balance that allows me to trade and not the tempting millions one can earn from it. Maybe that was the reason why I can live on it today. I love my work and find it very challenging to survive in these insanely heavy markets every day. I have been doing this for ten years now and believe me: Trading does not mean earning money in a simple way. If I counted the hours I spent in front of the screen with my previous hourly wage as a self-employed, trading in the first few years would not have been worth it. But the more experience you have, the more effectively you can act on the stock market. Under 10,000 hours of experience, this is not possible in my opinion to be profitable. If someone says otherwise, he is either a lucky guy or a trading coach.

6.We invest something more valuable than money

If you earn a 10% return on your trading while trading $ 10,000, you will receive $ 1,000 a month. After deducting taxes, there are about $ 700 left. You spend 10 hours per day and with the preparation at the weekend you work over 200 hours. That's an hourly wage of $ 3.50. 120% return is a very good performance as a beginner and yet the merit is lower than the social assistance. Why do you do that? Because you have the hope that one day it will get better. However, a person who is very ill, will see things differently. For him, time is the most important factor. Maybe we should also think about the time factor. Of course, for a beginner, the time factor is an investment, but how much time are you willing to invest? Remember, all the time you spend is lost to your family, friends, and yourself. That's why we should handle it carefully.

7.You always have to stay on the ball

A trader who does not trade does not earn money. As a trader, you have to watch, buy, analyze and sell every day in front of the computer. If you are ill or on vacation you do not earn money. As an employee, you will continue to earn your money, even when ill and on vacation. As a trader, however, you have one major disadvantage: you work diligently and still lose your money. That's a crucial point to think about.

8.Be on your own

As a trader, you sit alone in front of your screens every day and have few like-minded people to talk to. Of course, there are forums in which one can exchange views, but this is not comparable to a real conversation among traders. Even your family will rarely be able to help you, because they do not understand the matter. Therefore, you must be prepared to work alone. You have to motivate yourself and sometimes slow down yourself. That's one of the biggest challenges in the life of a trader. Think carefully about whether you can succeed with it.

Each coin has two sides, a shadow side and a sunny side. Let's take a look at what's speaks for trading.

1.Long or short around the clock with small capital

Previously there was no way to sell / short sell stocks and securities to make a profit. The only thing that could be achieved by selling stocks that lost value was to limit further losses. Today, traders can also make profits when markets fall. Financial crises do not disturb forex traders. You just click on Sell. The markets are open 24 hours a day from Sunday evening to Friday evening. This also helps beginners to start part-time. Trading accounts can be opened today with relatively little capital investment and additionally you can trade with demo accounts at the beginning. As forex traders the risks are manageable, in the futures market the risk is very high. That's great opportunities for a future future.

2.Some costs for self-employment

In most countries, you do not have to sign up for an expensive trade or start your own business. You do not need an expensive office because you can trade from home. Those who are married can get health insurance free of charge via their partner and in case of profit a maximum of 30% is taxable. The top tax rate in Germany is 45% plus an average trade tax of 15%, which is 60% in total. The tax situation of the traders is therefore a very interesting aspect. Most of the time, the internet is already there and the computers and screens you need are affordable. The investment of stock market data and a good stock exchange software costs a maximum of $ 50 a month. An optimal condition for a favorable start.

3.Trading is scalable

Anyone who has found his optimal setup with increasing experience and gains regular profits over time, has the option to optimize his earnings. You can scale the number of invested lots as you like. Of course, so does the risk. But with strategic money management you can oversee your risks. Winning 60% of the time on an average Return/Risk Ratio of 1: 2 gives you an experience, that's well worth scaling. This makes it possible to double its revenue relatively easily. Please note the total risk that you are willing to accept. This scalability is possible in the least professions. This is a special feature that is possible in trading.

4. Exchange time for more money

The longer and more successful you are in trading, the more you have the choice. I would like to invest more time to earn more or would prefer to spend more time for my family or hobbies. Due to the scalability you are flexible and can determine the optimal ratio of time and money with the help of your trading overview and a good Moneymanagement. Of course, one is exposed to the risk of losing every day, but since it is always about probabilities, one can still create a possible plan.

5.Trading is possible worldwide

The beautiful thing about trading is you can do it very easily and anywhere in the world. If you have the dream of moving to Australia, it's easier for you as a trader than for someone who needs to find a job first. Of course, there are some things to keep in mind, but as a trader you can earn your money everywhere. It will be interesting if you are very successful. In certain countries, taxes are much cheaper than in your country. If you earn $ 300,000 a year as a trader, you'll pay nearly $ 100,000 in taxes in Germany. In some countries, you can quickly save $ 60,000 in taxes. This allows you to pay your living expenses in the new country without giving up your old profits. An interesting thought.

6. Fun and free time sharing

As a successful trader you always have the choice. More time or more money. Scalability makes it possible to earn what you have earned in a month within a week. Now you can make the decision to work 2 weeks a month and earn twice as much as you did before. In addition to the free time division is now added the fun to enjoy its higher earnings in the double free time. But I always recommend save some money, because there are times when things do not go so well and then it is good to not have to rely on the income.

7.No physical effort

If you've worked hard and physically in your life before, you'll appreciate the convenience of a trader. Of course, Traden is a mental and psychological challenge that can be very tiring in the trade. But calculate yourself how often you are in the trade on a day. I am on the market about 10 times a day for a few minutes. Total maybe a maximum of 1 hour. The rest I sit in front of the screen and have a nice day. One can overcome that psychologically. If I imagine 8 hours of doing a hard physical work, I am glad to have chosen this profession 10 years ago.

8.Image and development

Being a trader is something special, I do not need to tell you how people react when they ask you what you do for a living. Only 0.6% of all people are traders, even doctors are 3 times more likely. We work in an environment that is associated with Wall Street. The only problem is, if you sit alone all day in front of the screen, that you should still evolve. During the last year, I did my master's degree in Java at Oracle 2,000 hours to better understand the indicators. That has brought me madly forward. In this blog I have written a total of 3 books, as a kind of trading journal. I've improved my English skills and regularly watch interesting trading videos in English. This year, I have dealt extensively with the stock market data and now develop interesting strategies to better identify the big players. If you rest, you rusts. Whoever is on the move, don t rusts. The key is that you are happy.

In my opinion, these were 8 reasons that speak against and for trading. I do not belong to the group of people who claim that everyone can trade. Trading is a very demanding profession and only about 2% manage to survive in this market in the long term. First and foremost, this is because of perseverance and less intelligence. Into a market created by chance is not the intelligence decisive, but rather the experience. And experience just needs time, nothing more, nothing less.

To be successful, I need optimal risk management. Professional risk management begins with the identification of risky problems. Risk management requires incalculable risks. Example: If you trade, you can never be sure that in the end you will win more than you lose. Qualitative risk management is therefore not limited to avoiding all risks in the first place, but rather is the process of identifying risks, then assessing them and then deciding whether it is necessary or even worthwhile to take risks. Risk management therefore means overcoming obstacles and taking advantage of opportunities. Often it is not considered that risks can certainly have positive effects. At this point, risk management builds up: every risk always has an opportunity at the same time. Just to take advantage of these opportunities - and thus to generate an added value from the conscious or already indispensable assumption of a risk. This is an important aspect of successful risk management. Who behaves better: Is it the person who sees everything new as an opportunity to be start, or is it still the one who first waits for developments and, in addition to Plan A and B, still devises Plan C and D? Basically, this question can not be answered. But every human being should ask himself whether he is suddenly too spontaneously plunging into something new, or whether on the other hand fear does obstruct new paths?

Almost everything new is once unfamiliar. Different people with different previous experiences and different natures will perceive something new as a chance or as a risk. And the vast majority of people will not only see one or the other, but both opportunities and risks, but with different proportions. And then it's about the willingness to take the risks in order to secure opportunities. The human risk appetite varies according to the situation, so that the basic attitude to risks is a stable psychological feature. People are more cautious in one situation and more risk-tolerant in the other. Thus, the level of risk-taking is individually rooted in the character of each person. If you put up with uncertainty, you might get more tension. What should we do now: Take or avoid risks? Or should one take careful and planned risks? A well-planned assumption of calculable risks initially sounds very good. When it comes to how calculable the risk must be, there is again a wide range of different answers.

In addition, one can also set different priorities when calculating risks: We can think about the probability of our behavior having negative or positive consequences. Traden offers opportunities for profit and fun, but at the same time is something we should not ignore risks. If we trade with real money, we can lose real money. And it should not be the money that we need for the next rent. In these situations, the actual questions that come to the fore come to the fore: What makes me happy and satisfied? We do not have to be a particularly risk-taking or cautious person to lead a happy and contented life. But we should ask ourselves what our risk behavior looks like and if it makes us happy. If we can answer that yes, that's fine, otherwise we'll have to change something. And if it does not work as a trader, that is not dramatic. Over 7.75 billion people are not a trader and still satisfied and hopefully happy.

Unfortunately, our personality does not change that easily. A person who avoids risk does not suddenly become a very risk-taking person and vice versa. But that is not necessary. Often a small step in the right direction is enough to cover a decisive path.

I wish you from the bottom of my heart, that you find this path.

Bionic time is money indicator

Hello dear subscribers,

During my daily trading I noticed that one often notices at the price change of the EURUSD , whether the course that runs in a particular direction is slowed down or not. Unfortunately, you can not see that in the current course price but well as in his current account balance in the terminal of the MT4. This was the idea to simulate an account balance. There are nine time units in MT4 from M1 to MN. The start is the close of the last candle, e.g. the Daily Close. From this point on you invest one lot on rising prices. When the price goes up, the indicator shows the gain in euros, when the price falls, the indicator shows the loss in euros. From the next Daily close the indicator starts again at zero. The M1 candle is recalculated every minute, the monthly candle every month. The calculation is done with the bid. If the value is positive, a green number is displayed, if the value is negative, the number is red.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

On the left you see the indicator Bionic Time is money EURUSD Daily, on the right side you can see all nine time units. For this I shot a short video to show you the indicator in action.

Inserted Video

Advantages of the indicator:

Resistances in the course of the price can be identified more quickly.
Trends are easy to grasp
Based on the profits or losses, the trend strengths can be recorded.

Disadvantage:

At each full hour, the H1, M30, M15, M5 and M1 begin with the same value.
The change in the presentation is very flexible, but also a bit laborious
The presentation is right-justified and optimized exclusively for the EURUSD.

I work here with two forms of presentation.

In my main chart, I work with the presentation in Dailychart, so that course obstacles are quickly recognizable for me. In addition, I placed an extra chart with the nine time units in a small corner. Thus, I recognize trend consequences and trend strengths very well. There is one more version for use in the chart. The monthly and weekly candles are a good long-term indicator, the day and H4 candle are a medium-term indicator and the remaining candles are an important clue to the short-term range. It may also be interesting what you could have earned if you were not out of the trade too soon. Just like what you would have lost if you were out later. You can learn something from that as well. Please note that this is 1 lot (100,000 euros). If you deal with a higher / lower number of lot you have to convert the value accordingly.

Another interesting point is the up or down counting of the respective amounts in certain price courses. With this you can quickly grasp, in which time unit, which sums can be earned or lost. The respective spreads or fees are of course to be added.

This is only an auxiliary indicator that should give us additional information and it goes without saying that we should not trade because of this information. Nevertheless, I hope the information will help you and I look forward to your feedback.

I wish you a successful Friday

--- 帖子 #1119 ---
The strategy of big players

Dear Subcribers,

the work of the big players is a big challenge every day for us as well as for the big players. As I've already said, it makes no sense for the big players just to push the price up, as they earn less. A concrete example can be found here:

Identification of the big players

Basically, it is important to understand the approach of the big players.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Here we see a chart in EURUSD H30. First, the price goes down, which means that a higher number of Bid will go into the market. To buy Ask, I need participants to sell the Bid. In this case, the big player starts to buy the first Ask already at point A. Starting at point B, the course is again higher. This arises partly because someone sells his dollars and partly because the big player buys the euro. Now many traders believe that the price continues to rise and start buying the euro. At point C, the big player buys a high number of dollars and pushes the price down sharply. Under point B are the stops of the traders. Once the stops are triggered, the downward trend accelerates. Professional big players are waiting at this point and are buying a large number of euros into this strong downtrend. At the same time the big player now sells his dollars, the price goes up again.

With the action of buying dollars and selling dollars right away, the big player does not make much money, but it stops many traders who think the price is now up. And that's how the big player secures its position upwards. Why does he do this?

If the big player at point C immediately pushes up the price, he would pull up many traders. In principle, that would not matter to the big player, but there is a problem. As the price moves higher, some retail traders start to step out to take their profits. For this they have to sell the euro and buy the dollar at the same time. This slows down the price trend. This would make the big player earn significantly less because he wants to push the price strongly up. So he has to make sure that these potential troublemakers are stopped out, before they can do any damage.

Now the price is going up to the point E. There, some traders get off to secure their profits. The big player is already waiting for it and buys in this downtrend again a high number of Ask. You can see that the price does not fall down sharply because someone absorbs this Bid under it. Then the course is pushed higher again. The game often runs on the same principle. The big player first pushes the price higher, many traders see a strong green candle and now enter. This is where the big player starts to get out of the euro. For this, initially little by little Bid is thrown in the market to sell the euro. Finally, the new buyers continue to believe that the price continues to go up. More retail traders enter the market and the big player gets its best out of its position. This happens exactly from point F. As a rule, I note the following, when the strong movement has gone up, I do not get in anymore. Because I do not want to be the one who helps the big players get out of their position cheaply. Because if the get off, a turnaround is likely.

The fac,t that the price is still up for a while is due to the retail traders, who believe that it is still going up. The big player sells its euro in small numbers so that the price does not fall too low. At point G many retail traders notice that there is no one who drives the price higher and a small panic sale begins, to get a good exit. At point H, a big player catches the course and pushes it up. Now the retail traders are getting back in and the big player is starting to buy the dollar sideways. A extreme stopfishing is omitted this time, because there were not many participants who would have expected falling course.

After that, the course was pushed to the point K and there was a re-distribution phase. Bid was collected there again and the course continued down. From point L, the big player has started to get out of the dollar. We recognize that the retail traders are basically used as cannon fodder to support the goals of big players. We have to keep in mind that the big banks sometimes make 60% of their total profits with the forex market. The forex market is for the big player a money printing machine. Anyone who believes that this described approach is always the same, is foolhardy. There are different market participants with different intentions. We also have to watch out for the high frequency traders, who are totally confused supply and demand. You can find some reports in this blog.

The tricks of high frequency traders

The hard unvarnished truth

Learning from high frequency dealers

Those who ignore these things will inevitably lose, lose and lose again. The whole strategies with market technology, indicators, trend trade, MACD, RSI are doomed in the long run, if one does not know, what happens in the market right now. If you know in more than 70% of the time whether the dollar is being bought or sold, or the euro is being bought or sold, you can take a look at the market and possibly guess what might happen next. Unfortunately, that does not work with the forex data because we just do not have enough information. Although the time and OHLC data are correct in the forex market, they lack the volume data (bid and ask) and the number of trades. Therefore you can not do without the stock market data. But also the pure stock market data are interesting only, if you use a Prop stock exchange software. This Prop software translates the stock exchange data for your requirements correctly. And now comes the biggest challenge. The setup and setting of the Prop Exchange Software. This takes the biggest time because the market never works equal.

There are many trainers who offer their strategies for volume trading. What they tell, is the biggest nonsense. The first time you see a footprint chart, the volume profile, or a DOM, you think this is the solution to all the problems. But you can not identify absorption with a footprint chart or the volume profile. At the beginning, the new stock market data is like a new indicator, one realizes that one eventually gets stuck and certainly can not find the holy grail. There is only one way to be profitable in the long term. You first have to know what's happening in the market right now.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

For that, the sideways phases are a decisive clue. I like trading in the sideways markets, which dominate the market 70% of the time. Of course I occasionally take a strong move up or down, but that's just a small side income I never count on. The sideways markets are very interesting. Suppose the course comes from above and there is a sideways market. Why is a sideways market forming?

Because the big players first get out of their positions or sub-positions and then absorb Bid or Ask. This means that in the first half of the sideways market positions are closed and in the second half Bid or Ask are bought. Therefore, the first half of the sideways market is a safe channel for me. Because the big players are slowly emerging from their positions while the retail traders believe that it goes up or down. The course is slower but you can trade very safe in a range. Once the absorption starts, you have to interpret it correctly if you want to take the strong move afterwards. As soon as a stronger absorption begins, the previous range is left, where you have to pay attention to an increasing volatility. I like doing downward movements as they run 30-40% faster and I have a lower risk. There is a detailed report on this:

Who is faster the euro or the dollar?

Let us now turn to the stock market data translated by a Prop software. Our project # 7 is about optimizing the settings in order to be able to detect possible absorption more quickly. This gives me the opportunity to determine the position on my navigation map.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

In my Prop software there are unlimited possibilities to analyze and highlight different clusters. I can decide if I want to analyze Bid, Ask, Delta, Volume, Ticks or Time. Min Value, max value, Bid Ask imbalance and Delta filter can be set. You can filter between bullish and bearish candles, the price range and the average number of trades. If I want to highlight a certain range within the candle, this is very variable possible. The presentation of the ad is very flexible. I do not write that to advertise this prop software, (because there are significantly cheaper software) I write this to you to describe the next experimental setup more precisely. For me, a software was decisive, with which I can identify very different clusters very flexible.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

On the left side I have filtered the clusters that have at least 50 lot Ask and at least 50 Lot Bid in a bullish candle. This will enable me to detect within an uptrend when the euro may be bought and sold again. The ask in a bullish candle is often the push up, while the bid can often signal the selloff. I deliberately emphasize the word "can", because a bid can also be a dollar bought.

On the right side I have filtered the clusters which have at least 50 lot Ask and at least 50 Lot Bid in a bearish candle. This will enable me to recognize within a downtrend when the dollar may be bought and sold again. The Bid in a bearish candle is often the push down, while the Ask can often signal the sale of the dollar. Now it's time to label the navigation map, to see if my settings help me. After that it's about the optimization. This should serve as a simple example, but you still have to pay attention to many more things. I recommend working with a footprintchart, as it allows you to identify the number of lots in the Bid and Ask. This can simplify the cluster search.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

From the previously identified map can now determine certain zones. It is well known that the big players run certain zones over and over until they stop working. Then new zones are searched. However, this depends on the extent to which retail traders are willing to buy Bid or Ask.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

The zone marked here is also interesting, after that, the price has gone down by 100 ticks or 50 pip in forex. Interestingly, I would have drawn this zone in the forex market wrong, even with a tick chart.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

With the stock market data, I was able to identify two strong moves that were a strong resistance area for me. Although I was not able to predict which of these two zones would push the price down, it became apparent that the dollar was being bought more heavily in the lower zone. That was the crucial point to decide on another short. Of course, there could have been a Stopfishing, then you would have been stopped, but would have had the chance for another entry.

This should only be a simple example of ways to better identify the market. However, you need more information, such as the time and sales list and the DOM. Basically, this does not always work, because the market in my view is random and therefore can not be grouped. Nevertheless, certain information helps to make assumptions that increase our probability of winning. Every trader has to create this setup individually, so you don t need any coaches. A few good books and a lot of time in front of the screen bring the necessary success, with time being the deciding factor.

Unfortunately, there is little information on, how the big player works. Good, if you know some high frequency traders or big players. But also their ways of trading change with time. With today's computer technology, self-learning algorithms and today's market conditions, one has to assume that every day it will be more difficult to survive in this market.

We know, not the big ones eat the little ones, but the fast ones the slow ones. That's why even smaller traders have a realistic chance in this market. And we should use this opportunity.

I wish you a successful trading week

Euro buy or sell, dollar buy or sell?

Hello dear subscribers,

In the last article I tried to describe a few approaches of the big players. The problem that we have in the forex market, is that we do not receive any Ask or Bid that is importend to the price. For this reason, I use the stock market data to obtain this very important information. Anyone who has ever worked with stock market data will quickly find out that the information about Ask and Bid is not the holy grail. Ask stands for the purchase and Bid for the sale. If a price is going down and I see a high number of Ask in the footprint chart, it does not necessarily mean that someone buys the euro. Before the course can go up again, two things have to happen. The big player has to get out of the dollar first, so he has to sell it first. Ask is thrown into the market to sell the dollar. So, if a large number of Ask shows up after a downtrend, this could be a sale of the dollar. Once the big player is out of position, a sideways market may emerge. Within this sideways market Bid or Ask is collected again. Conclusion: A high number of Ask can mean two things: the dollar is sold or the euro is bought. A high number of Bid can mean: the euro is sold or the dollar is bought. I have already described this situation in detail in the article

Identification of the Big Player

In my cluster project, I have now tried to divide the different movements in the course.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

A red circle in the chart means the dollar is being bought, a blue circle means the dollar is being sold. A green square means that the euro is bought and a yellow square that the euro is sold. The different size of the respective symbols depends on the number of the respective Bid or Ask. The settings I have made in the cluster search are, first of all, a rough approximation to a possible solution. The result is so interesting that I like to publish it.

Point A:

After a downtrend, we are initially in a smaller equilibrium. At first, smaller participants try to push down the course even further, but there seems to be resistance there. Then you see that a larger number of euros are bought. The course moves slowly upwards.

Point B:

The Euro Buy continues, with some blue dots now showing that the dollar has been sold. This shows that some participants who bought the dollar at Point A were stopped out. That's a good sign of another uptrend.

Point C:

The price is now higher and you can see that the Euro is selling heavily. As a result, the course goes down a bit and it creates an equilibrium.

Point D + E

Within the equilibrium, a larger number of dollars are purchased. The course will be pushed up again until the point E and then goes down sharply.

Point F:

At point F, the price initially stops, but you can see immediately that the dollar is now being bought heavily. After that, the price goes down.

Point G:

Here the dollar is bought again strongly and one recognizes that already the first participants get out of the the dollar.

Point H:

After the price has gone down even more, more participants get out of the the dollar.

Point I:

The first participants are already starting to buy the euro again and the price is going up.

Point J:

Now more participants are joining in, who buy the euro stronger. Although there are partial sales in the euro, the price is initially in a Equilibrium bring, but within this equilibrium, the euro is bought even more. The sluggish price trend suggests that few big players were involved in the uptrend. From this one can conclude that the downtrend is not over yet.

Point K:

After the price has gone down by a few euro sales, from the point K the euro is bought stronger again. The course now runs to the point L.

Point L:

At point L you can clearly see, that the euro is selling strong. This is an alarm signal that it may not go higher. At the same time the dollar is bought stronger. A sign of a pending downtrend.

Point M:

From here, the price is pushed down stronger again and you can see that in the course of the course again dollars are bought, which accelerates the price further down.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

On the right side of the chart, you can see that after the downtrend, a stronger uptrend begins that goes to point 1. Then there is the typical stop fishing, where the price is pushed down sharply. With the green arrow, I started my video, because I assumed that the course is now going uphill again. The background was that until the point 1 strong Euro were bought. The blue line I have drawn in the video, as the course at the green arrow is slowly upwards. Next to the DOM I used the time and sales list and a spread tape. On the upper right side, I filtered the number of Lots from 1-20. Although the big players are also working with larger volumes thrown into the market, they prefer to work with algorithms that buy smaller quantities of Ask or Bid within the sideways markets. Here I noticed that the algorithms like to use 5 and 8 Lot. However, it is still too early to make concrete statements. Here is the video first

Inserted Video

In the video you can clearly see how the number of euro purchases increases sharply. It is interesting that in the beginning a high number of Bid comes into the market, which are however absorbed immediately. This can be seen very well in the DOM. Then the course goes up.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Overall, the course went over the last high, as I had suspected. However, the course has been slow to run up and you can see at the high that the participants have dropped out of the euro. Thereafter, the dollar was bought heavily, which caused a strong downward trend.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

At 14:30 CET most of the big players got out of the dollar, you can see that in the blue big circle. Then the course in wavy lines has gone up 18 pip.

Conclusion:

Of course, my settings are not 100% correct yet and I still need to make some improvements. Nevertheless, it is very clear how important it is to distinguish whether the euro is bought or the dollar is sold and whether the dollar is bought or the euro is sold. In combination with the DOM and the time and sales list you get a little bit closer to the solution. In principle, the price history tells a story and if one day I am able to break down this story more precisely, you can use it to optimize its profit probability. But there is still some time left to make concrete statements. The fact is that you do not get this information in the forex market. But exactly this information is important to make concrete action decisions. When you get specific information, the price history is not just a wild back and forth, but tells us a story we can follow. Maybe my current attitude is a pure coincidence and might not work so well in other situations. That's why I need some more time to optimize the settings and adapt to the respective market conditions.

But the result so far looks promising in any case.
