--- 帖子 #1127 ---
Help for better trade

Hello dear subscribers,

This post is about important information that makes trading in the forex market much easier. First, you will get some information from the futures market, which are essential for trading in the Forex market. It's about understanding the way big players work to avoid the mistakes of most traders. In addition, you will receive a detailed explanation of a trend strength indicator that gives you important information in daily trading.

In our project no. 6, we first checked whether the data from the futures market would bring potential advantages for trading in the forex market. This result was clearly positive. In our current project no. 7 we want to find out, how to set and filter the future data in order to obtain an informational advantage. In the forex market, I clearly get less information than in the futures market. This is primarily due to the volume that can not be displayed correctly in the forex market, as it is calculated from the tick volume. The reason for this can be read here:

Volume in forex

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

The volume in the futures market is calculated from the number of bid and ask. The delta volume is the result of ask and bid. In this example, the horizontal and vertical delta volume (ask-bid) was used. This information does not exist in the forex market, as no bid and ask is provided by the banks. Although there are indicators that supposedly map this information in the MT4, but this representation is wrong. When faced as a forex trader for the first time with a footprint chart presented here, one quickly believes that one can use this information to find the holy grail. But that is unfortunately a big mistake. However, you have to know that bid and ask are the only reason why a price moves. Therefore, this information from Bid and Ask is essential. In a footprint chart, the number of bid and ask is shown exactly. The big problem is the time in which it is formed. A H1 footprint chart shows the accumulated Bid on the left side and the accumulated Ask on the right side, which are traded at each price level. What you do not realize is how often the price has gone back and forth within this candle. This makes it difficult to determine certain resistance zones. Iceberg orders as well as absorption in accumulation and distribution phases are thus very difficult to identify.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

In order to actually recognize what is happening in the market, it is important to work with a time and sales list, the DOM, a spread tape and a sorted volume. It is crucial to filter the data according to the respective volatility to get specific information. Anyone who has previously traded only in the forex market, for whom it is a great challenge. Many big players work exclusively with this information and usually do without a chart as we know it in Forex. I have only been working with this form of representation for six months and today I am able to derive important information that has often protected me from major damage. More information is not always an advantage, the right information is crucial. But unfortunately we do not get this crucial information in the forex market. I will deal with that again in a separate article.

Inserted Video

To get a better impression of how this presentation works in practice I would like to show you another video. At the time of the video creation, my assessment was bullish. In the video, I predicted a share price, which was also achieved overall. Pay attention to the high number of Ask that has come to the market. This can be seen in the DOM and in the time and sales list. In addition, you will also find my sorted single volume there. It is noticeable that here relatively few large Ask Order come into the market, but the market with small orders is driven upwards. Since the time and sales list lists the order cumulatively, this can only be seen in the sorted single volume.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

I would like to show you a concrete example. In the Asian market, the following scenario occurred on 5 November at 4:00 CET. In the downtrend that occurred before point A, the euro was bought heavily. At Point B, a big player pushed the price down sharply, causing Point C to trigger retail trader stops. Thereafter, from point D, the price was pushed up again. At Point E, I showed this strong candle once in the footprint chart. With this information you can start relatively little, so I have allowed myself to expand this information.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

This 30 second candle consists of a total of 17 price levels (17 ticks in the futures market or 8.5 pips in the forex). Here I would like to outline what information is available in the futures market. First of all, we recognize the volume. The volume is the addition of bid and ask that came on the market at a certain price level. In addition, we see the individual division of Bid and Ask. The delta is the result of bid and ask. If more Bid than Ask was traded on a price level, the delta is negative. In addition to the delta, we find the number of trading transactions, but it can not be deduced from how many participants have completed these transactions. To filter that out more, you have to work with a 1 tick chart. In a 1 tickchart, only one trading transaction is shown.

This immediately shows how much solder a single trader has given up. In addition to the trades you can see how long the price has been in the individual price levels. Unfortunately, the time here is a bit inaccurate because it is not calculated in milliseconds. However, you can see that in the time and sales list. Right next to it, I once listed the imbalance in bid and ask, which of course you can set individually. On the right side you will find a value: Volume / Trades. The larger this value, the fewer trading transactions were involved in the volume. This is an interesting way for me to identify the big players. Of all this information, in the forex market, one could just calculate the time in seconds a price spent in a particular price level. (However, such an indicator is not known to me) All other information can not be displayed in Forex. In this example we see at point A how a big player drove the price down. The value volume / trade is above average. Thereafter, the course runs to the point B. There, the stops of retail traders are triggered, who have previously bought the euro. It can be seen that an above-average high number of Bid traded on 4 price levels. These stops seem like a chain reaction. As soon as a stop is triggered, the course jumps down, triggering the next stop. So the big player only has to push the course down once until the first stop, then there is a fireworks display down. Now the price is accelerating downwards and you can see at point D how the big player starts to buy the euro in the downtrend. Then the course is pushed up.

Please read my article:

Euro buy or sell, dollar buy or sell?

It is crucial to know whether a bullish candle is the result of buying the euro or selling the dollar, and whether a bearish candle is the result of a dollar buy or a sale of the euro. These factors are a crucial element for a possible probability calculation. If a bullish candle is caused by a strong euro buying, it is more likely that the price will rise in the medium term than if this candle comes through a strong dollar sale. The background for this. If a big player leaves the dollar in a falling price, there could be several reasons. He no longer believes in the dollar or he has reached his goal. As a rule, big players never sell the dollar low as they hold larger positions. If a big player sells the dollar he has to bring Ask into the market. Either slowing down a falling course or the course starts to rise. In order to get off the dollar well, the big player needs participants who continue to believe in a falling price and bring a higher number of bid into the market. Precisely for this reason, a big player gets out of the dollar even before the low with its main positions. However, there are still other participants in the dollar at this time and these participants must get out of this dollar. This increases the likelihood that the price may fall further. That's why I have to differentiate between buying and selling.

A trend upwards usually proceeds as follows. An accumulation phase arises, the big player is already out of the dollar with its main position. Within the first half of this accumulation phase, the remaining dollars will be sold. In the second half, the big player starts to buy the euro. Often it then comes to Stopfishing, the price is pushed down strongly, as in our example. The strong upside comes from the fact that the big player is selling his dollar (which he bought for stopfishing before buying the euro). The upside now runs to the point where the stopfishing started down. Most traders are cautious as they believe the price could go down sharply again. Now the big player pushes the price strongly upwards, the fewest market participants are in this push with it. Now many traders see a strong green candle and massively enter the euro. This situation is often used by the big player to get out of his position now. After the big player is out of position, he uses the on-going course to buy the dollar. At some point, the retail traders notice that there is no longer anyone who buys the euro. Now everyone wants to get out of his euro position. The price is going down and a small panic sale is starting. This accelerates the downtrend and the big player starts selling his dollar. If you see a strong bullish candle after a slight uptrend, you must be aware that the big player is already starting to exit the euro. This means that the subsequent uptrend is much slower than the previous breakout. However, the subsequent uptrend could be a safe bet if you have the right information. The big players have a major disadvantage over the retail trader. They can not just press the button to buy in the Euro FX 1000 Lot Ask on a price level. And just as little are they quickly out of the market. They must take a high risk by starting to collect ask or bid. In many situations, they often go down a lot until they have the chance to drive the course in their desired direction. It is often said that the big players work together. I'm less convinced of that. Rather, I believe that the other big player recognizes what's going on in the market right now and follow the other. The win of the two big players will be a little smaller, but it's still better than fighting each other. Therefore, it often seems like the big players work each other. No matter what, the loser is always the retail trader.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

To distinguish these different purchases and sales, I use an individual algorithm that helps me to differentiate between the different positions. These filter settings are adjusted and changed daily by me. The individual volatility in different market situations must also be taken into account. This is a crazy job, as there are several million different filtering options. My filter settings currently only refer to the EURUSD otherwise such an approach would not be possible in terms of time.

With these filter settings, I am still in the initial stage. I got the idea while creating a post for FF. As you know, this blog is a kind of diary for me, which adds to my English skills. Writing down your thoughts often results in the best ideas. This set-up is the biggest challenge of my trading career so far, and I'm convinced that it may take years to find the optimal setup for me. Therefore, initial mistakes are unavoidable.

At Point A, the course opens with a bearish gap and initially goes up. At Point B, you can see how smart money buys heavily the dollar. At Point C it is noticeable that the euro is bought heavily. At first the price goes down and there is a pullback upwards. At Point D, retail traders are starting to buy more euros, while smart money is rising out of the dollar. Basically, this is a good starting point for a possible upward price trend. If the big player pushed the price higher at point D, there would be too many retail traders who would eventually start selling the euro again. That would slow down the course massively and the big player would not be able to get away with his position. For this reason, the big player initially drives the price down to trigger the stops of retail traders. After that, the way up is free. From point E the course is pushed down. It starts a chain reaction. The first stops of the retail traders are triggered and drive the course now more down. Starting at point G, the big player begins to buy into the falling price by selling his previously purchased dollar and buying the euro. He will no longer get many euro positions in the price development, he has already acquired his big Euro purchase at point C anyway. At Point H we can see that the first retail traders are already leaving the euro. This filter setting includes both the big players and the retail traders.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

In the following filter setting I tried to emphasize the big players a bit more. The larger euro purchase at Point A has an interesting resistance effect. It can be seen after the course has gone through this resistance zone that it runs more strongly upwards. After that, the big player starts to get out of the euro in small units. It is a mistake to assume that the big players always bring a high number of lot in the market. The opposite is the case, because with a high number of lots, the big player can be quickly identified. The big players work with algorithms that make sure to buy 100 times 4 lots in seconds, than once 400 lots. Of course, the number of lots is different, because 100 × 4 lots can also be identified.

Ten years ago, the action in the Dom was still a comprehensible matter. In the DOM you will find the limit orders waiting to be executed. If there was a many of lots on the Ask side at that time, it could be assumed that the price would go up as soon as it reached that price level. But it is clear that if every market participant can assume that the price will go up there, this approach is no longer worthwhile. Then the first big players started spoofing. High limit orders were issued to signal interest in the DOM and deleted shortly before execution. After that, the price was pushed in the opposite direction. Spoofing still takes place in the Future Market, but does not have the same effect as it did many years ago. I do not pay any attention to the limit order in the DOM. Much more decisive for me are the orders that are deleted or added shortly before the execution. For some years there has been a very interesting trick with which the big players gain advantages in the market.

A course goes up and on the highest point, 80 lot Ask come into the market. The retail traders see this big order and start buying the euro. After all, this order was actually abandoned and the big player seems to have thought something of it. With its algorithms, the big player manages to sell this large order immediately in small pieces and then push the price down sharply. That means a big order can do exactly the opposite. Therefore, it is crucial for me to know the difference between Dollar / Euro - buy / sell.

In the forex market, the big players have sophisticated computer systems to detect inconsistencies in the currency pairs. These inconsistencies usually last only a few seconds. With so many market participants and the large daily volume of sales, it is more important to keep an eye on the development and cash flow than to recognize an undervalued currency. This advantage does not have the retail traders in Forex market.

Basically, I recommend working with stock market data and studying the habits of big players closely. Big players dominate the market and the only chance to win is to follow them. For that, I have to know exactly what is happening in the market right now. If you do not have sophisticated computer systems available, you have to work with stock market data to have a higher chance.

If these stock market data are not available to you, I would now like to show you an idea that I had for many years and realized in the last year. Please take a look at the following article in this context. Below I will explain this indicator exactly.

Determine trend strength in any period

The indicator can be found here for download

Update smZigZag-Bionics and smZigZag-Bionics Osc

A ZigZag indicator is completely unsuitable for accurately predicting future market movements. The last zig-zag line will not be completed until the market direction has changed. This means that the last line will not be set until after the course has changed direction. Zag Zag lines should not be confused with trend lines. The presumed accuracy results from the subsequent adaptation. This means that a supposedly completed line can also be extended. The last line is always reserved and has no bearing on where the market is next. Thus, to work with the indicator for a future price forecast is completely unsuitable. Nevertheless, the ZigZag indicator provides a visually highly visible picture of the direction of the market and the extent of trend and correction movements. The length ratio of individual lines can give indications of the expected extent of market impulses. I wanted to implement this advantage for a trend strength calculation. As a rule, a ZigZag indicator shows the length of a trend line and the number of candles within that trend line. I have modified this information. Dividing the trend length by the number of candles gives you the average candle size of each candle. From this one can derive a trend strength. For the example below, I have modified an existing indicator, the numbers above or below the candles indicate the average candle size in pipettes. You can download the indicator at the end of my article. Basically, I recommend to use the indicator in a tick chart because it gives significantly better results there.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Let's start with our example with stopfishing in the Asian market on 5 November. The chart was created with a 128 tick chart in the forex market.

Point A

The downtrend had a magnitude of 14 (each candle averaged 1.4 pips). This value was already significantly higher on average than the other trends. That showed me that there was a strong downward pressure. At point A, I drew a line that was a possible future destination for me. But initially the course went up again.

Point B

Here the uptrend reached a magnitude of 4.3 which signaled to me that the uptrend had become very weak. I drew a finish line again. At first the course went down again.

Point C

The downtrend reached 4, indicating a possible equilibrium. This downtrend was initially not strong.

Point D

Now we have a stronger pullback upwards with a value of 20. Again, I drew a finish line. After that course went down.

Point E

The downtrend had a magnitude of 11.3 and went above the point C. This means that the downtrend had now gained significantly in strength. Since a strength of 20 was achieved at point D, this line was now my new target. The course went up again.

Point F

My finish line was not reached and the uptrend had a magnitude of 7.3. This shows that the upward movement has dropped significantly and the downtrend with 11.3 was much stronger. The course went down and reached my finish line at point E. Thereafter the course accelerated and continued to run down. The new target zone was now at point A with a strength of 14.

Point G

The price did not reach the target zone of point A and had a value of 5.7. This means that the downtrend had eased a bit. My target zone was still at point A. The course went up again.

Point H

The strength of the trend was 5.2. This showed that the uptrend was weaker than the last downtrend. The assumption was now obvious that the course could reach my goal of point A. Then the course went down.

Point I

The price went very well through my goal at point A. In such a case, you have the opportunity to pull the stop down to hedge a partial profit. Then you can continue the course or you can get off the finish line from point A. The strength of the trend was 17.9. Here too I drew a finish line which later became interesting. The following upward trend had the goal point H and then point D.

Point J

The finish line at point H was reached and had a strength of 11.1. In addition, the line of Point H was overcome. My new goal was initially at point I, but based on the price history, one could already guess that it could be a Stopfishing. Thus, the first target point was at point A and the second target point at point I.

Point K

Interestingly enough, the course is right up where the stops were triggered. The strength was 6.9 and the downtrend has decreased significantly. My new goal was now at point J.

Point L

The price continued to climb, reaching my goal of Point J, closing at 5.1. This strength was relatively low and the new target was at point K, as it had a magnitude of 6.9.

Point M

The goal at Point K was not reached and the strength was 6.2 well above the last uptrend. So you could guess that the course could run again in this area.

Point N

The trend strength increased to 18 and showed now another strength upwards. My first target was at point M and the second target at point K.

Point O

The strength of the downtrend was 12, which was significantly stronger than the last downtrend but at point N was a magnitude of 18 and above at point D a strength of 20. So there were more reasons to run up than down. The goal of point N and D has been reached.

Basically, a course always moves in undulations up and down. Of course, the zigzag indicator only gives out its information relatively late and you have to know that the current number can still change. Nevertheless, this indicator gives an interesting overview of the existing strength in the market. It is important to correlate the strength of the upward and downward movements in a trend. From this, possible goals can be derived, which of course are not always achieved. It is always only about probabilities, that we must never lose sight of. In addition, you still have the option to switch to a smaller time unit to read smaller movements. Please note that the 128 Tickchart average is a 2 minute chart. Up to 16 Tickchart you can get interesting information. This gives you the opportunity to react much faster to possible trends.

Let's look at another recent example from the EURUSD from last Friday 10:00 to 13:00 CET.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Point A

The downtrend had a magnitude of 8.1, which was a relatively low value during this volatility phase. The course initially went up.

Point B

The following upward trend had a strength of 13.9. The assumption was that the price could move higher. Initially, my goal was at point A.

Point C

The subsequent downtrend had a strength of 21, the goal of point A was not reached. The strength of 21 indicated a more imminent downtrend.

Point D

The following uptrend had a magnitude of 20.5. The previous downtrend was a bit stronger. With the two equally strong trends, my assumption was that it could be a kind of equilibrium, the new target was now at point C.

Point E

The goal of Point C has been reached. The strength was 10 and so the downward trend was significantly weaker. At point D was a magnitude of 20.5. Since this goal was not reached yet this was my new goal.

Point F

The new uptrend had a magnitude of 6.2, well below the recent downtrend. My goal was now at point E.

Point G

The goal Point E was reached, then accelerated the course down. The strength at 12.0 was stronger than the last downtrend. As before, for the uptrend, my goal was at point D.

Point H

At 20.0, the upward trend became much stronger.

Point I

The subsequent downward trend of 12.3 was well below the last uptrend. The goal of Point G was not reached.

Point J

With 13.0, the uptrend was significantly weaker, the goal of point H was reached.

Point K

The strength of 29 at point K was an interesting aspect. The downtrend has increased significantly and may have been facing a major downtrend. As before, my goal has been the uptrend at point D. With this indicator you will often find that a strong pullback up or down announces an imminent strong trend.

Point L

At 13.5, the uptrend has increased little over the recent uptrend. The underlying downward trend was significantly higher at 29.0. The goal of point D with a value of 20 was not reached. The downtrend of 29 was significantly larger than the target at point D. The first downtrend target was at point K, then point I and then point G. With a good stop strategy, one could have optimized his profits here as well. In the lower area at point M to P, an equilibrium was initially formed.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Here I once presented an example in EURUSD in four different time units. The setting of the zigzag indicator is 4/2/1. The advantage of this presentation is that we have a nice overview of the individual trend strengths in the long term as well as in the short term. Nevertheless I recommend you to use a tickchart. I work very successfully with the following four time units: Tickchart 64, 256, 1024 and 4096. This corresponds approximately to the M1, M5, M15 and H1. However, the representation in the tick chart is much more accurate. The big advantage of a tick chart lies in the presentation of the price development. If the volatility is small, a tick chart forms fewer candles. If volatility increases, many candles are formed. This makes it possible to define its resistance zones more precisely in periods of strong volatility. If there is nothing going on in the market, there are only a few candles, and when it burnes around, there are many candles. A breakout in the M1 is often just a big candle. In the tickchart 10 candles are formed in the same time. Thus, the advantage should be obvious.

You have two options for working with the two different indicators. The bionic zigzag indicator, which you can download in the upper link, has a few flexible options in the setting. However, it indicates the trend strength in Pip. The modified zigzag Easy 1,2 is only displayed in one color, but has the advantage that it provides up-to-date information relatively quickly. It's best to try both to find the best one for you.

Making short-term trade decisions with these indicators is not recommended. Since I myself worked with resistance zones in the area of supply and demand, this indicator regularly provides me with good information about the currently existing trend strength in the market. This gives you interesting information and a small information advantage over other market participants. In order to obtain concrete information, one must inevitably resort to stock market data. If this is not possible in the short term, this indicator gives you another chance to see what is happening in the market right now. I hope that this information will help you a bit and I look forward to the feedback.

I wish you a great weekend

best regards

Hello mikeeating,

First of all, welcome to our blog and thank you for your kind words. I am very happy if this contribution helps you:  Help for better trade

Price formation is very similar in the forex and futures market, so the indicator also gives you specific information in the forex market. I do not work with the ZigZag indicator in the futures market because it does not give me the information that matters to me. Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Unfortunately, the delta and a volume display in the Forex market is not possible, since this requires the specific number of Bid and Ask. The volume in the forex market is calculated on the ticks and is therefore inaccurate or wrong. The other 3 data ticks (pips), bars and time can also be displayed in the forex market. Mad world

Hello dear subscribers,

The stock market world, as we know it, has not existed for a long time. When we think of Wall Street, we see brokers shout at each other and acting with each other. Stock exchange trading today takes place beyond the major stock exchanges, usually in large data centers of banks and institutions. While in the past traders were decisive factors in trade, they were long since replaced by physicists, mathematicians and programmers. At the heart of today's trading decisions are the algorithms that control highly complex trading bots. Over 10 years ago, the first high-frequency traders who penetrated the stock exchange markets in order to make life more difficult for banks, asset managers, life insurers, pension funds and investment funds became established. The three most common strategies used by high-frequency traders are the provision of liquidity, arbitrage, and the detection of liquidity. When providing liquidity, high-frequency traders behave like traditional market makers: they offer buying and selling prices, but without the commitment of traditional market makers to always be present on the market. In doing so, these dealers access a strategically sophisticated software environment.

Inserted Video

Interesting high-frequency trading algorithm that has taken place in the S & P 500 futures contract. In 7 seconds, there were over 7,000 trades (52,000 contracts). The video shows in 7 minutes what happened in the 7 seconds.

In 1,238 trading days, the largest high-frequency trader made a loss on only one day, at the same time Goldman Sachs came to 124 loss days. Goldman Sachs tops the charts with a 90% win rate, but the largest high-frequency trader Virtu is still significantly better. Scientists working on Virtu's trading activity found Virtu not taking much risk in trading. High frequency trading is a worthwhile business. The big players have long recognized this and made a counter-stroke. They work with the same tricks to compete in the market. As a result, three major banks were also fined millions of dollars for spoofing. Therefore, the market has become even more confusing and harder. And in the future it will be much harder to earn money in these markets.

Although there are many more private traders trading on the stock exchanges than big players, the turnover of big players is well above retailers at 90%. For the stock exchanges, the big players are therefore clearly more important, what that means, is clear for everyone. There are significant differences in data feeds and fees, as well as the speed of order execution. The big players are able to trade millions of shares within 2 minutes without overly large orders. This is made possible by the special algorithms that take over the trade.
While the traders continue to upgrade, the stock exchange supervision hardly comes after. Traders generate up to 1,000,000 data records per minute via Eurex alone. If you want to track down grievances, you can immediately get a container ship with printouts of trade data. Complete monitoring of market manipulation is therefore no longer possible. That an authority can do something with the complicated algorithms, is also difficult to imagine. This facilitates future market manipulation. Techniques were banned by the stock exchange, where an algorithm stops orders in the trading system that should not be executed at all. However, it is hard to imagine that Deutsche Börse voluntarily puts rules in its statutes that annoy high-frequency traders. Its ten largest customers generate 50% of sales and provide additional liquidity in many markets.

As retail traders, we do not have complicated algorithms, fast data cables, high-performance computers or the capital needed to move markets. That's why we need to look more closely at the big player approach. Between the high-frequency traders and big players, I would not like to differentiate at this point, since the big players have already begun to work with the tricks of high-frequency traders. It is crucial to know the way of working in order to draw insights that protect us from possible losses.

Spoofing
The practices often used in the past are called smoking or spoofing, which enables large market participants to gain trading advantages at the expense of slower acting business partners. This is because very short-term participants analyze the purchase and sale orders very precisely because they hope to obtain information about imminent price changes. For the big market participants, this offers the opportunity to simulate large orders, which in reality do not exist by the rapid adjustment. The other traders can not analyze these orders in the short term and are confused. Since they do not know which orders are correct and which are only fictitious orders, this gives the large market participants a time advantage, since they know their right orders. The big orders are then withdrawn at lightning speed as soon as the big player has executed its set counterorder in the market. Many high-frequency traders place their computers not so close to the exchange's main computer to trade faster, but to be able to cancel orders at lightning speed.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Many market participants are guided by the set limit orders in the Oderbuch, which represent the relationship between demand and supply. Some years ago, on the New York and German Stock Exchange more than 90% of orders were not executed. Therefore, I strongly recommend to pay less attention to these limit orders. While a good prop software can detect the deleted and added limit orders, in very volatile phases this is often useless. However, deleted limit orders help identify a new demand or offer. Certain algorithms use these phantom orders to try to get the opponent's algorithm to buy. It analyzes when the opposing algorithm begins to abandon its buy order. After that, exactly that number of limit orders that trigger the opposing algorithm are given up. For this reason, it will still continue to come to the known spoofing.

News Reader
It is a software that is able to read current business news into the marketplace by launching a specific algorithm that immediately places buy or sell orders in the market before the actual prices can react.

Arbitrage
Here, price differences are exploited on different stock exchanges. Thereby, papers are bought on one stock exchange and immediately resold on another stock exchange. The price differences are small, but the larger the number of pieces, the sooner the deal is worthwhile.

Pinging
An algorithm is programmed to send small orders to different exchanges to find out where liquidity exists and at the same time to look at the trading books.

Snipping
With small, quickly issued orders, the market is searched for hidden orders. The goal of finding large buy and sell limits of other traders. Just before these thresholds, which promise the release of large orders, then the own orders are placed. The limit orders of the other participants will be triggered much later and drive the course in the desired direction of the big player.

Scalping
The faster the respective system, the higher the decisive advantage. As soon as the systems detect large order volumes, they are on the market at lightning speed. So you can buy even cheaper than the other dealers. Even before you can govern, the dealers are already outside again and the course turns immediately in the other direction. The slower traders are virtually eaten by the market.

Quote Stuffing
This is a fight between HFT algorithms. Some of these companies have chosen to fool their fellow competitors by placing thousands of orders within a second and immediately deleting them. This can be up to 15,000 orders within a few seconds. The point is that other algorithms have to handle this flood of data and are thereby deceived. The algorithm that sends these data knows that they are wrong and need not be analyzed. This saves time and they can wait for opportunities in the market that the other algorithms fail to recognize due to their "preoccupation" with the fake orders.

Wash trades
I have already described this approach in previous posts and is particularly controversial. The trader deals with himself here. He hunts his buy order up to his sell limit order, which then pushes the price down immediately. Or, in a rising market, a turnaround is suggested in order to buy cheaper again before the market turns sharply upwards again. The goal is to push merchants out of the market or to induce them to make transactions that they probably would not have done in other circumstances.

Front Running
This procedure is particularly nasty. A player is to buy a specific currency pair at a specific price for his customer. The player buy for himself, before acting for his client. Since this procedure is forbidden, the trading is done by another company. This makes it harder to prove an offense.

Big buy, small sell
This is a procedure I have been able to observe myself in the last few months, that's why I called it that. On a high, suddenly a huge purchase order is placed in the market. This purchase order is not a bogus order but an order actually placed in the order book. Traders see this single order and start buying. After all, a big player does not invest such a large order for nothing. The big player is starting to sell up his big order in small pieces. As a result, the price does not go up. Then the big player pushes the course down. As many buyers enter the market there is enough liquidity available. Once the Trader's first stops are triggered, there is a chain reaction down. Already there the big player gets out again. On his big order, the big player loses maybe a few dollars, which he get back but immediately.

Fake resistance zones
Since many traders believe in resistance zones, the big players produce artificial resistance zones by bouncing off the course at certain price zones. These resistance zones are exploited to get high liquidity at this price level, which is detrimental to most retail traders. Since many traders work with the Fibonacci, this type of trading is also incorporated into your strategy. At the 50 retracement, the price is pushed up, which attracts many buyers in the market, the short time later all are stopped. It does not matter if you work with an MA, Fibonacci or Candle Patterns, what we see is really different. How else can you explain that over 90% of traders are wrong?

The tricks of the big players create a false truth about supply and demand. The only truth is the resulting candle, but the moment we see the candle, that's already the past. Individual papers can lose 20 or even 40% of their value within seconds without fundamental justification, only to recover a short time later. Once the algo trade has spied a strategy, it is outdated. This approach makes the entire fundamental analysis almost superfluous.

Here you can see a Nanex animation of the S & P 500 futures during the Flash crash on May 6, 2010.

Inserted Video

Market depth is a possible step to analyze demand and supply, but usually uses limit orders, which often give a false picture of demand and supply. Much more important seem to be the orders actually placed.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

An important insight is that predicting a future course from the current track is wrong in most cases. The recommendation that we pay less attention to the current chart image and focus more on the Equilibrium. So on the small breaks in which the price is balanced.

First, we should deal with the reality that awaits us in the market.

There are 12 big players in the forex market that account for 85% of the total market. Essentially, these banks control the price performance of the EURUSD. However, the willingness of individual retail traders to invest is also highly dependent on this. As we know, the big players in an equilibrium or sideways market must raise ask or bid to then push the price in their desired direction. It is crucial in which amount the retail traders are willing to invest ask or bid. As a rule, the retail traders are encouraged by the big players to make certain investments at certain price levels. The big players are able to project typical resistance and support zones to deceive retail traders. But this approach does not always work as the big players imagine. Therefore, they are trying all tricks, to lure the dump money on a wrong track. Spoofing, fake resistance zones, Big buy, small sell and stophunting are just a few of the endless possibilities to get the money from retail traders. When a big player has collected a large amount of Ask, news, politics and currency strength are no longer important. Even if news or politics point to dollar strength, the big player will push the euro higher to realize its gains. Therefore, news or political circumstances are often not relevant. The decisive factor is what happens in the market right now. Will the dollar or the euro is bought, will the euro or the dollar is sold. This situation needs to be analyzed daily and can change at any time. Of course, the central banks play a decisive role.

The big players rarely buy the euro at the low and usually never sell it at high. Likewise, they rarely buy the dollar high and never sell it low. The background is that the big players are implementing a high amount of lot. A big player buys the euro and pushes up the price. More traders enter the market and ensure a further increase in prices. To get out of the euro, the player now has to bring a high number of bid into the market. But there must be traders who continue to believe in the euro and invest in the market so that the big player can sell his euro. To get a good price, the big player has to get out of the euro before the high. This way of working distinguishes the big players from the retail traders. The most successful big players are day traders who realize their main profits within a day. Even more successful are some high frequency traders.

So it's always about gathering in the sideways markets Bid or Ask to realize profits. This situation can change any time a big player leaves his position. For this reason, a long-term forecast of a price development is not possible. The key is to recognize whether Bid or Ask is being collected. Unfortunately, no indicator in the forex market is able to recognize this, as no bid and ask are published in the forex market.

A short-term forecast is also not possible because the big players first collect a certain number of bid or ask in order to move the price in the medium term. If you are able to find out what the big players are collecting, it is possible to anticipate the medium term movement. Unfortunately, the exact time of an outbreak is difficult to see ahead.

In the following video, I have set up a cluster search in which, using bid and ask, the market divides as follows: buy euro = green square, sell euro = red square, buy dollar = red circle and sell dollar = green circle. The filtering takes into account both a certain number of trades, an imbalance, an identification of the big players, and the delta between ask and bid. The setting is still incorrect, but should clarify the future goal.

Inserted Video

You can already see the individual relationships between bid and ask and the resulting results. The filtering has to be optimized and adapted to individual market situations. From this one can not fundamentally derive a future movement, as the big players often work with a time delay. You must first collect before pushing the course in a particular direction. This approach is interesting in the sideways markets or within an equilibrium. There you can implement the information faster.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Let's summarize the information briefly again

Point A
First, we realize that there is a stronger dollar sale, then the euro is bought on a larger scale, the price goes up.

Point B
Already here, a stronger euro sale takes place, which indicates that the price could not rise so much.

Point C
Already here, the first larger dollar purchases take place, the price goes down for a brief moment and is pushed up again.

Point D
Here comes a big dollar buyer in the market and pushes the price down a bit more.

Point E
In the smaller equilibrium you can see that the euro is bought very heavily at the end and the price goes up.

Point F
The euro sellers hold back first, when the course runs down the dollar is bought heavily.

Point G
Here, the euro is bought stronger and pushes the course again stronger. A short time later, a strong dollar buyer came into the market, pushing the price down.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

If we look at an M1 in EURUSD at the same time, it quickly becomes clear that we can not read this information based on a candle. That is also clear, because the important information of Bid and Ask is missing.

Conclusion

Whether the price rises or falls more or less in the short and long term is unpredictable. Predictable is that the course moves in waves up and down. Trading is always in the direction that promises the most profit for the big players, and that may be identifying in a medium term area. The crucial zones are the sideways markets or an equilibrium. There is often collected in the second half, a larger number of bid or ask, which can anticipate a possible future price course.

With the optimal filtering of individual clusters, it is easiest to be able to recognize what is happening in the market right now. The way the big players work is not like a racing boat but rather a container ship. Sometimes collecting bid or ask can take days before a sharp price move up or down. And a big player does not always have to be active in the market. Often the smaller players are allowed to operate in the market and big players only intervene in certain regions to build certain fake resistance zones, which are then exploited at the crucial moment.

The real stock market data have clear advantages over the Forex data, this is undisputed. But the trick is to filter that stock market data. The information obtained from this must show a trader whether a bullish move is caused by a euro buy or dollar sale. That's a big difference. If the bullish movement comes about through a dollar sale, it is likely that an equilibrium will be created first, and the euro will have to be rebuilt before the price moves higher. If the bullish movement is created by buying more euros, there is a greater likelihood that the market will continue to move higher. In addition, you should also pay attention to Euro sales and dollar purchases.

With the correct filter setting, triggered stops can also be displayed. This is just before major outbreaks a crucial indicator of the future price performance. The challenge is the exact filtering of individual data. And that is the crucial point, which will take a lot of time. In my opinion a decisive strategy to survive in this tough market in the long term.

I wish you a successful trading week

best regards

Hello dear subscribers,

Like me in my last post: Mad World

over the Big Player tricks wrote, a long-term and short-term prediction of a price course is hardly possible, since the Big Player are rather medium-term oriented. The goal in our new Project No. 8 is to enable the identification of the following scenarios:

When will the euro be bought?

When will the dollar be bought?
When will the dollar be sold?

When will stop loss sell be triggered?

I have already published a rough overview of this goal.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

In addition I recommend to read the first half my contribution again.

Help for better trade

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

In the Asian market, the following scenario occurred on 5 November at 4:33 CET. In the downtrend that occurred before point A, the euro was bought heavily. At Point B, a big player pushed the price down sharply, causing Point C to trigger retail trader stops. Thereafter, from point D, the price was pushed up again. At Point E, I showed this strong candle once in the footprint chart. I first examined this candle in more detail.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

This 30 second candle consists of a total of 17 price levels (17 ticks in the futures market or 8.5 pips in the forex). Here I would like to outline what information is available in the futures market. First of all, we recognize the volume. The volume is the addition of bid and ask that came on the market at a certain price level. In addition, we see the individual division of Bid and Ask. The delta is the result of Bid and Ask. In addition to the delta, we find the number of trading transactions, but it can not be deduced from how many participants have completed these transactions. To filter that out more, you have to work with a 1 tick chart. In a 1 tickchart, only one trading transaction is shown. This immediately shows how much Lot a single trader has given up. In addition to the trades you can see how long the price has been in the individual price levels. Unfortunately, the time here is a bit inaccurate because it is not calculated in milliseconds. However, you can see that in the time and sales list. Right next to it, I once listed the imbalance in bid and ask, which of course you can set individually. On the right side you will find a value: Volume / Trades. The larger this value, the fewer trading transactions were involved in the volume. This is an interesting way for me to identify the big players.

Of all this information, in the forex market, one could only calculate the time in seconds a price spent in a particular price level. (However, such an indicator is not known to me) All other information can not be displayed in Forex. In this example we see at point A how a big player drove the price down. The value volume / trade is above average. Thereafter, the course runs to the point B. There, the stops of retail traders are triggered, who have previously bought the euro. It can be seen that an above-average high number of Bid traded on 4 price levels. These stops seem like a chain reaction. As soon as a stop is triggered, the course jumps down, triggering the next stop. So the big player only has to push the course down once until the first stop, then there is a fireworks display down. Now the price is accelerating downwards and you can see at point D how the big player starts to buy the euro in the downtrend. Then the course is pushed up.

The problem is that although the bid and ask options in the futures market are different, but the number of trades between bid and ask not exist. I first wanted to find out if such a distinction is important to understand this situation even better.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

In order to be able to penetrate even deeper into the market, I first called up a 1-tickchart and analyzed these 30 seconds more closely. Since a 1-tick chart only consists of individual points in the chart, I have used the Heiken Ashi for a better representation, since he always includes the close of the last candle. This makes the course clearly visible. The deviation caused by the smoothing of Heiken Ashi is within acceptable limits. In the picture below you can see the split between Bid and Ask. In the 1 tickchart, each stroke is a trade made by a trader. In the 30 seconds we look at, the biggest buy order was 8 lots and the biggest sell order was 14 lots. Nevertheless, 1373 lots were traded in 30 seconds. In the 30 seconds, the price went through a total of 17 price levels. I first assigned the number of bid and ask to each price level to find out how many bids and ask trades have taken place. Overall, I had to assign 788 trades to the price level.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Here we have the result.

Point A
The total volume (addition of bid and ask) is already known and can be seen in the image.

Point B
Unfortunately, the number of trades quoted in the futures market always refers to the total volume.

Point C
Likewise, the number of bid is known on the individual price level and is shown in the picture.

Point D
Here you can see the number of trades that refer to the Bid. I have not yet found such a representation in the futures market.

Point E
The number of each Ask can be displayed individually at each price level.

Point F
Here you can see the number of trades that relate to the ask of the respective price level.

Point G
The volume delta results from the difference between Ask and Bid. If more Bid than Ask has been traded, a negative value will appear. This form of presentation is also known and used in the futures market.

Point H
The trades delta is the difference between the number of ask trades and the number of bid trades. Since there was no distinction between the number of trades between Ask and Bid, these values could not be used so far. Anomalies between the volume delta and the trades delta could be interesting.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

The result of points C and D is given by points A and B. Here, in principle, the distribution or proportionality between Bid and Ask is shown. For the number of trades that was not possible. At first glance, the proportionality of points C and D seems to correspond to the proportionality of points G and H. Nevertheless, there are some anomalies that should be considered even closer.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

From the data obtained, there are now three different factors.

Point A
Dividing the total volume by the number of trades gives you a number. The larger this number, the more likely the involvement of a big player in the price level. This is usually because a big player trades more Lot , than a small retail trader.

Point B
Here the value Bid / Trades was determined based on the new calculation basis.

Point C
Here the value Ask / Trades was determined based on the new calculation basis.

The average result volume/trades, Bid/trades and Ask/trades does not identify at first a big player. When this calculation was made in the Asian market, I assumed a value of at least 1.9 to identify a big player at the price level.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Here now a division was made. The yellow marked fields indicate a possible participation of a big player (> 1,9) within the respective price level.

Point A
When looking at the total volume, it seems at first that the big player has invested, in the upper range, 23 and 59 lot Bid, to trigger the price slide down. Likewise one recognizes in the lower third a participation of the Big Player.

Point B
After splitting the trades between bid and ask, we get a very interesting presentation. Initially, a higher number of Bid is invested at the top of Point C to push the price down. This triggers possible stops, which I marked in blue. You realize that the values are well below 1.9. In the lower part of the big player has invested another 61 Lot to even take out the last stops.

Point D
At the same time, it is possible that the big player has already bought Ask in the yellow marked boxes while the course goes down.

By the time the big player pushed the price down, there were participants who entered massively into the falling price. At the low of the candle, the big player sold his dollar in small numbers, so that the course went up again. There was enough liquidity, as most participants assumed that the price would continue to go down.

In the lower section you can see the overall result, divided into Big Player and Retail Trader. At point B we see the big player investing 363 lots to push the price down. He triggered a few stops. The value of 682 lots not only refers to stops being triggered, but also traders who entered the falling market and bought the dollar.

It is very clear that an accurate evaluation will never be possible. But I'm convinced that the division of trades by Bid and Ask can bring a clear lead. Similarly, the trades delta should bring another and very big advantage.

The wrong truth?

Hello dear subscribers,

Some universities have studied the quality of decisions in recent years, depending on the amount of information available. The question was, is more information leading to better decisions? It turned out that more information is not crucial, but the quality of the information.

In Forex market, we rely on the information we receive from our broker. Because of this information, we risk more or less every day a small fortune. Too much information hinders our willingness to make decisions, so we need a small amount of accurate information. The first question we need to ask ourselves is, is the information we receive in the forex market correct and of high quality? I have already answered this question in my contribution Forex versus future for me.

Forex versus future

The fact is that the quality of the available data in the futures market is 200% better than in the Forex market. That is the reason why I base my trading decisions in the forex market exclusively on the data of the futures market. Why should one act with lower quality data, after all we risk a lot of money every day.

That was the reason that I first informed myself comprehensively in order to get a high-quality data source. This data source initially consists of genuine stock market data, which is identical for all market participants. The next step was to present these complex stock market data in such a way that they gave me a concrete insight into the market situation. The result is very satisfactory so far.

I would like to give you a short example.

A trader friend and I bought a MT4 tickchart a year ago that could be used in the forex market. Although we were at the same broker, our tick chart chart view was always different. No matter how we calibrated the data, we were simply not able to create the same chart image. Now that we are working with real stock market data and a professional prop software, this problem has been solved. Whether we are working in a 1-tickchart or with a volume chart, we always have the exact same chart image. This situation facilitates a joint analysis.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

If you analyze my main screen, you will notice that there are no more typical candles there. Inevitably one will ask the question whether a profitable trade with this data is even possible. First of all, the quality of the data was a decisive factor for me. This data now has to be filtered in our project number eight so that concrete action decisions can be made. For this, it is first necessary to deal with these stock market data closer. I will show some examples from my trading screen at the end of the article.

One reason why I said goodbye to the typical Forex market price scale, because that view is a truth that does not really exist. For this we can do a very simple experiment. Take a transparent piece of paper the size of your screen and draw random horizontal lines. Then place this piece of paper over your screen. You will realize that your marked resistance zones work well. I made this experiment directly on the screen. First, I have arbitrarily plotted horizontal resistance lines in an empty chart. After that, I faded in the candles. In the following video you will see how my randomly drawn resistance zones work terribly well.

Inserted Video

We recognize that randomly drawn resistance zones will always work in a market. However, this is pure coincidence and has nothing to do with actual resistance. You can do this experiment yourself and you'll be amazed how well the course reacts to your resistance zones.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Here you can see the price history in EURUSD within the last 14 months in H4. We humans always have the habit of describing a random price trend with the help of horizontal, vertical or trend lines in order to create an order that can be traced for us. But this supposed order is a false truth. There is no top or bottom in a price because the price is not based on resistance zones, but exclusively on bid and ask. Of course, resistance zones work every now and then, but a reliable statement can not be derived in principle. Excluded are resistance zones that result from supply and demand. However, the creation of these zones requires many years of experience and is supported by the individual intuition of the individual trader.

Everything we see on the chart is nothing more than an indicator that at this moment represents a past price in the form of a candle. This means that everything we see has already happened and with it the past. One of the reasons why I chose stock market data was the opportunity to see part of the future. Now you'll be wondering how stock market data can put you in the future, and for that we need to first learn about the DOM (Deep of Market). A DOM, or Level2, is a source that we receive as a direct data feed from the stock market, providing insight into how other market participants are trading. For swing traders, the order book is often not as crucial as it is for day traders or scalpers.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Let's take a closer look at Point 1 at this DOM. At Point A we see the price leaders and see the spread of 1 tick between the Ask (green number) and the bid (red number). At Point B we see the sellers who placed their sell limit order on ask. The number 1 symbolizes one lot each on the Ask side. At Point C, we see the buyers placing their buy limit order on the bid. The number 1 symbolizes a lot on the bid side. Point D shows with 21 the number of buy limit orders on the bid side. Point E shows with 23 the number of sell limit orders on the ask side. So what we see in the DOM are the so-called limit orders, which were put into the market before and waiting to be executed. And exactly this view is a piece of the future. It shows the willingness of buyers or sellers to trade at a certain price level. Of course, limit orders are also added and deleted at any time, yet it is also a view for the future. Initially, these limit orders are at the respective price levels and await execution. These orders provide liquidity in the market and show the willingness to be picked up at a certain price level. This information is not available in the forex market and thus a serious disadvantage.

What you can not see in this order book are the buyers or sellers who spontaneously enter the market (market order) or possible stops from traders, which are in principle nothing more than a market order. The challenge now is to see if this picture of supply and demand is representative of the current market. Depending on the market situation, these numbers move quickly back and forth and it is often difficult to keep the right overview. However, these settings can be filtered to keep track even in volatile markets. The limit orders are only on the individual price levels and do not move the market initially. Only the aggressive market orders ensure a market movement. An advantage of trading a limit order is reducing the likelihood of slippage, the downside is that anyone in the market can see your order. The DOM is very flexible, you can see the individual volume of the last months at each price level, which saves the view in chart histories. Supply and demand can be seen at a glance. This saves time and is more effective.

Point F

At the price of 1,10050 a buyer gives up a 2 Lot Market Buy Order. The spread is 1 tick. This order absorbs the two sell limit orders on the ask side. (Point G)

Point G

The price jumps first to the 1,10055, (Point H) and the two sell limit orders are in the market. There is a bigger gap between supply and demand in the market, the spread opens (Point I), because there is no further buy limit order at the price level 1,10050. This situation is evidence of uncertainty. If a seller were to place 5 Lot Bid on the market, the price would drop to 1,10040. Gaps are dangerous for traders who work with stop-loss. If this is not guaranteed, it may end up losing more than the stop loss, because the position can not be closed until the next tradable price, that is, the price after the gap. Future price gaps can already be identified in the stock market.

At Point J, we see that the total number of the sell limit order has dropped to 21.

Point K

A buyer puts a buy limit order on the price level of 1,10050 in the market, thereby reducing the gap from 2 tick to 1 tick. (Point L). The total number of buy limit orders increases to 22 lots. (Point M) This information in the DOM is the fastest that can be obtained and is an indispensable tool for scalpers.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

In the following example I would like to show how a price gap arises in the market.

At Point A we see the buy limit order on the bid side. There are 21 buy limit orders (Point B) on ten price levels. On the ask side we see the sell limit order.

Point C

At the price levels 1,10060 and 1,10065 there are no sell limit orders waiting for execution and there are a total of 20 sell limit orders in the market. (Point D)

Point E

At the price level 1,10050 comes a buy market order with 6 lots. First, two lots on the Ask side (1.10050) and then three lots on the 1.10055 price point are absorbed. Another lot of the buy market order has yet to be executed.

Point F

The small gap of 1,10060 and 1,10055 is now skipped and at the price level 1,10070 one lot is absorbed. This initially raises the price to 1,10070. The spread gap is initially 4 tick (Point G). The number of sell limit orders is reduced to 14. (Point H)

Point I

At the price levels 1,10050-1,10065, additional buy limit orders are added, and the spread gap closes (Point J). There are now 25 buy limit orders and 14 sell limit orders in the market. (Point K).

This process has created a positive gap. The market participant, who has given up a buy market order of 6 lot at the price level 1,10050, is already three ticks in the profit by this situation. Additional sell-limit orders were added, thus preventing a downward gap. Depending on the time unit you can see the gap in the chart. Often a gap takes place within the candles and is thus usually no longer identifiable. This means price gaps arise due to lack of liquidity on the ask or bid side.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

We often see in the chart that a price is higher and immediately lower again. This can have different reasons, one reason I want to show you now, which has to do with a lack of liquidity.

Point A

At the price level 1,10050, a buy market order with 24 lots is traded. These 24 lots absorb the Sell Limit Order on the Ask side. The course jumps up to the price level 1,10095. (Point B) The spread between bid and ask increases to 10 ticks. (Point C). The total number of buy limit orders is initially at 21 lots (Point D), but new liquidity is added immediately (Point E). The number of buy limit orders rises to 26 (Point F) and the spread between ask and bid drops to 7 points. (Point G). At the price level 1,10095 a sell market order of 8 lot comes in now. (Point H) This order first goes through the price gap and absorbs 8 lot on the bid side. The price stops at 1,10045 (Point I). There is additional liquidity on the ask side, (Point J) which allows a further downward price trend. On the bid side there are now 18 lot and on the ask page 29 lot (Point K).

We recognize here an interesting phenomenon. 24 lot have pushed up the price by 10 ticks, while only 8 lot, the price by 11 ticks have driven down. They recognize the importance of existing liquidity in the market. And it is precisely this liquidity that can only be identified with stock market data in the order book. In very volatile markets, there is often a lack of liquidity, which ensures rapid price jumps. This often creates high risks, which are underestimated by the market participants.

Now let's look at why we are often not picked up on the market with our limit order. The submission of a limit order in the market is similar to a checkout in the supermarket. Anyone who wants to pay has to queue up in the queue.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

At Point A the price is 1,10050. At the price 1,10055 you issue a sell limit order as you believe the price will now go down. At price level 1,10055 there are still three traders ahead of them waiting to be executed. They line up as number four in the queue. (Point B). First comes a buy market order of five lots in the market. (Point C). The participants in front of them are picked up and they are still the only one on the price level 1,10055 (Point D). The number of sell limit orders has been reduced to 20 (Point E). Now comes a Market Sell Order in the amount of 7 Lot in the market (Point F). The Market Sell Order first absorbs the bid and lowers the price to 1,10045 (Point G). The spread between supply and demand increases to three ticks (Point H). The total number of buy-limit orders has fallen to 14 and possibly additional liquidity on the bid side will reduce the spread between supply and demand.

If I give up a limit order in the futures market, I will see in the form of an approximation on which position I am in the queue. This is an extremely interesting tool. Unfortunately, I do not receive any information about this in the forex market.

Summary

Let's first of all note that liquidity is provided by the limit order in the market, these show future interest on the ask and bid side and provide a rough overview of supply and demand within individual price levels. Spoofing can cause changes. The market order e.g. Sell and Buy Market, Stop loss and Take Profit move the market by limiting or absorbing. The volume of Bid and Ask is the result of these struggles and is responsible for the price changes. If the spread increases and at the same time few limit orders move up, this indicates an uncertainty in the market. Also, a high number of deleted limit orders indicate the intention to fake a wrong offer or an incorrect demand. This can be valuable information. Likewise, one can more quickly identify volatility, absorption, and strong resistance, thereby making better decisions. Therefore, this volume is a crucial factor in trading decisions. Of course, this is not the holy grail, trading will always be a challenge, the question is what data they base your decisions on. To be honest, if I had to drive against a fixed wall at 30 miles, I would rather risk it in a Mercedes S-Class than in a Mini Cooper. Of course, an S-Class costs much more than a Mini Cooper, but that's worth my life. In the stock market environment, we risk our dearly earned money, the question is what data we rely on.

With the DOM in the stock exchange market, I see with Ask and Bid the past, the present and the limit orders a little bit into the future. In the Forex market, I only see the past, because Ask and Bid do not exist. Everybody should think about that.
