Manipulation in the market

Hello dear subscribers,

In the market, there are many conspiracy theories that the big players manipulate the market in their favor is the most known and an undisputed fact. Some even argue that the markets are manipulated only by a certain force, because such extreme market movements can never be generated by a common acting group. We want to take a closer look at this assertion.

What exactly is the interbank market?

The interbank market is the market where money and credit business takes place only between banks. Banks and financial institutions trade with one another in the interbank market, lend each other money and can thus ensure that they remain liquid. Securities, money, foreign exchange, precious metals or derivatives are exchanged in the interbank market. The interbank market is assigned to the money market. The rates of currencies are not determined by a government as long as they are freely tradeable and not linked to another currency. They are based solely on supply and demand. Forex trading is usually OTC, i. E. it is not centrally organized, but takes place directly between the market participants or through a broker. This trade without a central marketplace is referred to as over-the-counter (OTC) trading.

Bank risks are to be spread across the interbank market. Through it, the banks can carry out liquidation of open positions that were previously established in the customer business. Or the banks operate proprietary trading on the interbank market. In addition, interbank trading should ensure sufficient liquidity at all times for the banks.

The interbank market was founded exclusively so that banks could trade with each other, a direct participation of private investors was not intended at the time of founding. At some point, the brokers found a goldmine in it, which is why the forex market came into being.

The biggest "players" in the forex market are governments and the central banks, which generally participate in foreign exchange trading in the interests of the government. Due to their financial capabilities, central banks are able to exert a noticeable influence on the foreign exchange market. In principle, however, they use currency trading only to adjust and hedge their foreign reserves. The next largest participants are banks and other credit institutions. The proportion of private speculators is very low here in comparison.

EBS (Electronic Broking Services) is the world's largest trading platform for foreign exchange in interbank trading. The price, which arises at EBS, is the reference for any FX derivatives. EBS Markets maintains an anonymized central limit order book. FX trading banks can trade on the market and via these hedge funds & CTAs (Prime Brokerage Arrangements). Although the data is collected anonymously, EBS Markets recognizes whether it is a human or an algorithmic interface (AI). In addition to the classification, the EBS regulations provide for a minimum quota life (MQL). This is to prevent the high-frequency traders from the fact that they have only by their speed advantage over the other market participants.

In addition, since there is no specific trade information in the interbank market, this market for high-frequency trading is not quite as interesting as the stock market environment. The big players therefore have sophisticated computer systems to detect inconsistencies in the currency pairs. These disagreements usually last only a few seconds. With so many market participants and the large volume of daily sales, it is more important to keep an eye on the trend and the flow of capital than to recognize an undervalued currency.

Over $ 5 trillion is being transacted daily in the forex market. 98 percent of the transactions are conducted in direct trading between banks rather than through a stock exchange. There is no regulatory authority. Only twelve banks control 85 percent of the market. This means that these 12 banks will invest $ 4.25 trillion per day. Banks do not trust each other and no one provides information about their trading activities. Therefore there is no real volume or an order book in the interbank market. The resulting volumes in MT4 are a pure estimate.

First let's make a comparison in EURUSD

The EURUSD trades daily at $ 1.7 trillion, the proportion of 12 banks is 85% = $ 1.445 trillion, the share of other institutional traders is 10% = $ 170 billion and the retail traders share is 5% = $ 85 billion. In addition to the 12 major dealers, there are an estimated approximately 10,000 institutional traders and 1 million retail traders.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Each of the banks trades an average of 1.2 million lots per day, every institutional trader 170 lots and every retail trader 0.85 lots. In proportion: 1 large bank deals around 1.4 million daily and every institutional trader 200 times more than the individual retail trader. 1 million retail traders invest less per day than a big player. Thus, the size relationships are clear and it is logical that the market is primarily driven by these big players. The big players act and the retail traders react.

With its trading volume in the interbank market, Deutsche Bank has so much experience that analysts and programmers are able to develop interesting strategies from the existing data. This brings clear advantages in the trade. Of course, every big player will try to influence the market in his favor, but having a force to control the hole market is completely impossible.

Why does it seem, that the market makes always the opposite of that, what you are doing right now, and why are not the big players getting in the way each other?

First of all, the world's 12 largest banks are trading to remain liquid and, of course, to optimize their profits. The big players know the markets and are able to see immediately if liquidity flows into or out of a market. Therefore, it is wiser to follow the liquidity than to oppose it. That's why many see it as if the big players are working together. By acting in the same direction, they do so in principle, but for their own account. The retail traders have little opportunity to follow the liquidity and therefore, most retail traders, against the big players, face the market and lose. Interestingly, some banks invest 20-30% of their available funds in the forex market, thereby earning up to 65% of their total profits.

Of course, many tricks and unfair means are used, most of them are in my report: Mad world

That banks are working with unfair means is nothing new and everyone is aware of it. In addition, the Big Boys spend billions on their analysts and traders. Anyone who places himself as a poker player at a poker table with a big player must be aware of the risks he is taking. Most traders are unaware of who they are dealing with daily. That is also understandable, because you only sit in front of your PC and do not see your opponent. I am convinced that if retail traders knew how these big players work, they would be distant from trading. We compete against the biggest world champions every day, it's presumptuous to believe that you can win against them.

Nevertheless, why do 2-5% of traders manage to live from trading in the long term?

In every odds calculation, by chance, a faction is created that survives. The stupid thing about it: A successful trader can never know if his success is based on skill or chance. Of course, good moneyman management, experience, diligence and strategies are crucial factors on the path to success. But we never know why we are successful. I believe that my success is based on pure coincidence, so I do not post strategies, just ideas, so that every trader can create his own setup. And I can only give this recommendation to every trader. Once you have found your way, deepen your knowledge and start optimizing your strategy. Do not let others get you away, but focus on your strategy. That's the only way to success. A proverb says: New brooms always sweep well, but the old ones know where the filth lies.

Do not start to tell of your strategy as the only optimal system. Every setup has to be created individually like a Formula One race car. It makes no sense to want to work with someone else's setup because it will not make you successful in the long run. The biggest enemy is not the big player but the broker. If you trade 10 x 1 lot a day as a scalper, the broker gets $ 100 of it. You have to earn that $ 100 first to avoid losing money. If you lost $ 2,000 after 500 trades, your broker earned $ 5,000 in the same period. If the broker would only charge half the fee, you would even have a $ 500 profit. That's the biggest problem.

I know many successful traders who have been successful with different systems, it does not matter which system you use, it is crucial that you know what you are doing. Claims that scare are often used in the forex market to arouse a need. This behavior is often seen in insurance agents. At first, they scare you that you will be poor in old age and after that they sell you a life insurance. In the forex market, the fear or greed is often exploited by fraudsters. Basically, you should know that you can find all the information for free on the Internet. The challenge is to find the right information. It takes some time, but not more.

The forex market is one of the biggest challenges and whoever gets into the shark tank should be aware of that. To make it, you have a realistic chance of about 5% here. In Europe, 10% are self-employed and 50% of them are successful. That's also 5%.

The only key to success is to try it out.

I wish you a successful trading week

The Matrix

Hello dear subscribers,

Just two years ago, I launched my blog: The Equilibrium, the key to success. At that time, I still got my data exclusively from the Forex market and derived my trading decisions. Looking closer at the forex tick chart, I first became aware of how the volume is calculated in the forex market and what serious drawbacks can arise from it. This finally gave me the idea to analyze the stock market data more closely in order to make more efficient trading decisions in the forex market. The resulting information is consistently positive and can help many traders optimize their trading decisions.

In the past, I have traded most successfully in the sideways markets or even Equilibrium. Now that I have studied the stock market data, it is clear to me today why trading in Equilibrium has worked so well. The sideways markets are used by the big players to collect a certain number of ask or bid and then push the course in the desired direction. During this collection phase, the big players are not so dangerous as the prices move within a range to get their shares together. Extreme price jumps are relatively rare in these phases. As a Scalper I am interested in doing my trade in the market within a short time. Basically, the prices in wavy lines move up and down, the longer you are in the market, the higher the probability of losing your profits again. As a Scalper, I would like to enter price courses that are relatively fast. At first, the breakouts up or down seem to be the fastest course, while trading in equilibrium seems to be very slow. First of all, I wanted to examine this comparison in more detail.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

On the picture you can see a course in H1 over a period of two weeks. There are five equilibrium phases in the area of accumulation and distribution, as well as five strong moves up or down. These five equilibrium phases account for more than 70% of the total price. Therefore, the probability of trading in an Equilibrium is significantly higher and more efficient than waiting for a possible breakout and there acting correctly. In the individual movements of the accumulation and distribution phases, as well as in the respective strong movements up or down, I first analyzed the number of pip and the time. Within an equilibrium or sideways market, I have calculated small possible trends. The designations from point A to J are now needed for our calculation.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

In the picture you can now see the individual movements that I have designated from point A to J. Here the hours were divided by the number of pips. At Point A you can see the pips per hour achieved within the strong movements. At Point B you can see the pips per hour achieved during the distribution or accumulation phases. At first, it seems that in Equilibrium, on average, the faster movements have taken place than in the breakouts. Of course, this calculation is not representative because I only looked at a period of two weeks.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

We zoom in a little deeper into the analysis and let's look at the distribution phase at Point E (Picture # 1). This is where a zigzag indicator comes into play that calculates the average pipettes within a trend. Within the equilibrium, the average trend was 7.2 pips, while the strong downward movement averaged only 4.8 pips. Although the time factor was not taken into account here, you can see that some of the movement in the equilibrium has been considerably stronger. Since this is not a representative calculation, it is possible that we can expect slower movements in an equilibrium. Nevertheless, I am convinced that, on average, over a longer period of time, a breakout will not produce more pips per hour than movements within an equilibrium.

Conclusion:

In only 30% of the time, I am able to carry a trend trade up or down. Sideways movements take place in 70% of the time. Everyone will realize how difficult it is to catch a breakout. But if I focus only on these breakouts, I only have an average of three chances per week. Most movements take place in the sideways markets. There, the achieved Pip per hour are often significantly higher than within the trend movements. Add to that a crucial point: in the equilibrium phases, the big players are much more predictable than in the strong trend phases. Therefore my recommendation is to earn the main income in Equilibrium and realize a possible additional income with the trend trade.

Of course, it depends on the time unit in which you trade. In H1, a trader averages 5.4 pip / hour = 0.09 pip / minute. In the M1 it is already 0.25 pip / minute and in the 8 tick chart an average of 0.69 pip / minute. Why this is so, read in my article:

Scalper = self-destruction in small installments?

In this article, the trend curves M1 were compared with the trends of an 8-tickchart. The number of pip / minute can be increased again if they only bet on downtrends. Here's an explanation:

Who is faster the euro or the dollar?

With an 8-tick chart to bet only on downtrends, brings a possible speed of 1 pip / minute. This is up to 10 times faster than in H1, because a Scalper trading simultaneously 20 individual movements. Of course, the risk increases at the same time. Who drives his car 200 mph has a much greater risk than the one who is traveling at 20 mph. Every advantage often has disadvantages. Realizing when to seize an opportunity is the most important thing in life. But it is almost as important to know when to forego an advantage better.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

When I made my trading decisions exclusively with the forex data, I analyzed supply and demand. I used different indicators that were able to show different trend strengths. In stronger movements, I paid attention to the stronger pullbacks that allowed me to identify the key candle. With the aid of this key candle, I was able to draw certain resistance zones in the chart that helped me with trading decisions. Basically, I could act profitably with this approach. Still, there were some situations where I was either not picked up or my stop was triggered. Of course, scaling could easily improve my profitable trading to earn more. But that would not have reduced my risk. That was the reason that I dealt more closely with the stock market data.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Deep in the market

With the ratio volume / trades you can easily identify the big players. You would also be able to do that in a 1-tick chart, but the data gets there so quickly that it's almost impossible to derive concrete trading decisions from it. The yellow marked fields show a participation of a big player. With the help of the stock market data and an efficient filtering one is able to find this big player participation.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Here we see a H4 chart in Euro FX. The bright fields show a clear participation of the big players at the respective price levels. In order to derive concrete information from it, you first have to switch to smaller time units.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

From this analysis one can find interesting forms of representation in smaller time units. On the left side (point A) we see a filtering which is exclusively designed to represent the big player. On the right side (point B) I tried to divide a M15 candle into different strengths. Red = weak, blue = medium and green = strong. However, this division still needs to be adjusted. If we deal with a 1 tick chart (point C) , we can see the lot of the ask / bid of a single participant. I have observed this representation more closely and I noticed that 10 to 200 lot are traded relatively rarely. When this large amount of lot entered the market, the price has not changed directly to move in a particular direction. This suggests that the big players bring a large amount of lot into the market. Higher bid in the accumulation phase and higher ask in the distribution phase. I've noticed, that for very strong price movements, rarely a high number of lots came in the market. From this one can conclude that in this case, the algorithms of the big players fire a kind of machine gun volley with small lot to push the course in their desired direction. To study these algorithms, I first made a matrix.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

In the picture you can see this matrix on the right side. The red numbers indicate the individual number of bid traded and the green numbers show the individual number of traded ask. The subdivision runs from 1-10 each Lot, right and left next to it I have created the number from 11 lot to 200 lot with the associated time. How it works you can see in my video.

Inserted Video

In the video, we see how the ask pushes the price up a bit. These are only smaller market participants. Then the price is pressed down a bit more. After, the pressure down is triggered by a smaller number of solder. Starting at 2:30 minutes in the video, a big player starts with many 4 lots to press the price down. At the end you can see how the ask side is trying to take control.

I find this matrix particularly interesting because it brings me closer to the algorithms of big players. Over the past few trading days, I have already noticed interesting structures within this matrix. I would like to briefly summarize the previous findings that I could derive from this. When big lots enter the market, in most cases this is not immediately relevant to the price.

This means that when a large order of 50 Lot Ask enters the market, the price does not move up very sharply. The big players have long since recognized that big lots marks leave their mark on the market. However, if these high lots take place within an accumulation or distribution phase and do not immediately lead to a sharp change in price, this is not a disadvantage for the big player. A few minutes later, most of the traders have forgotten about this big order anyway, since the price did not move much through this big order. Some are making the mistake now and believe that this big order has been absorbed and the future price will go down sharply. The price will also goes down a lot, but this is a Stopfishing and most traders are quickly stopped, because the course is pressed up again after Stopfishing. This means that the actual market direction was long and not short.

Strong price moves up or down are usually triggered by the big players with small orders. One to four lots are fired like a machine gun volley and push the price in the desired direction. If a big player with 1,2,3 or 4 Lot trades in the market, it is no longer identifiable. With the created matrix one is immediately able to identify these machine gun blasts. Of course, I'll never be able to get in the market on the lowest low or the highest high.

The first thing I can tell is whether a big player collects more ask or bid within a sideways market. As a rule, after that a fake breakout takes place around the stops of the retail traders to triggers. By now I can identify this stop fishing quite well. I have already posted some contributions about this. Now, when I realize that a stop fishing is taking place and the retail trader stops, I only need to recognize in my matrix when a machine gun fire is fired. If this happens on the right side then I am able to enter the market immediately to be pulled up.

The future challenge is to filter this matrix a little more efficiently and to look for possible patterns. It is clear that the algorithms of big players do not always fire an equal number of bid or ask in the market. This number of the lot is usually random. But a machine gun salvo is always immediately visible. This allows me to get into the market relatively early and let the big player pull me up. With my filter setting, I am also able to recognize when the big player starts to get out of the euro. As soon as I see that, I let myself be driven up a bit by the retail traders who have just joined in and then I am also out of the market. With the pure data from the Forex market I was never able to realize these optimal entries and exits. Crucial to this approach is that the overall picture of the market must fit the reactions of the big players. If it then comes to anomalies, you should postpone its market entry.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

In the past, I have been very happy to deal with the COT data (point 1) to find out how the individual investors were positioned. The problem was that this data was released only every two weeks to provide better market transparency for all participants. Here you can view COT data for free.

https://freecotdata.com/currencies-2/.

If you want to get more familiar with the COT data, you will find a lot of good information here at Forex Factory.

I searched the stock market for a faster alternative and discovered something interesting with the open interest (point 2). Open interest is the number of all outstanding (open) futures contracts on a given market at a given time. This is the total number of futures contracts that have not yet been closed by an offsetting transaction. The open interest increases with each stock exchange transaction, which creates a new open position with both the buyer and the seller, by one (A buys a contract for the first time, B empty for the first time a contract). The open interest remains unchanged in a transaction that opens one position and closes another (A sells his contract to C). Open interest declines when the transaction closes a position for both the buyer and the seller (C sells to B).

Simplified, we could say open interest is the number of open (long) contracts purchased. The number of purchased and sold contracts are always the same. Open interest shows us how committed the market participants are. Back off or build up positions. In the Russian market we have the only opportunity to access the open interest.

I got the euro / dollar data and made some experiments. At point A, you can see how the market participants withdraw from the euro, shortly afterwards, the price goes down. At point B, liquidity flows into the market and prices rise thereafter. First of all, it is still a bit early to make concrete statements about it, but I will stay tuned and report as soon as I have completed further test runs.

There are countless possibilities to link and filter different data. On the one hand that requires a lot of time and a creative think "around the corner". Forex Broker

Hello wiserltz,

a warm welcome on our blog and thank you for your very kind words. Like you, I trade in the forex market, because the liquidity is much better, which affects my execution times. However, this depends individually on the individual broker. Basically you have to be careful with brokers, because after all, they live not only on the spreads and fees. Every broker has to protect himself in the market in some way. As a rule, ECN brokers pass on the positions immediately, others work with their own hedging systems. If the positions of the different customers balance, there is no need for action. If this is not the case, the broker secures by corresponding counter positions in the forex market. Therefore, it can happen that many trades do not take place in the forex market, but only at the broker. If you act only with the broker and the broker does not pass on the position to the forex market, he would make another profit in case of your loss, besides the spreads and the fees. Of course there have been brokers in the past who have manipulated their prices to make further profits.

Personally, I've gotten used to working with virtual stops that the broker can not see. However, he could guess the approximate stops based on my past trades. It takes some time and experience to find an optimal broker. So far, I am very satisfied, because my broker meets the requirements set by me. One of the main reasons for my broker choice: As a professional trader I can trade in Europe up to 1: 400 and in the extreme case of a drawdown I am liable only with my balance in the account. So I would never have to make an additional payment. Basically all traders in Europe have this advantage, but they can only trade 1:30. Once a trader is classified as a professional trader, he is liable with his entire fortune. And in the case of the franc shock EURCHF, the price went down in seconds by 2,200 pip. With 1 lot, that would be a $ 22,000 loss the trader would need to settle immediately. That's a crucial point for me.

As you have already said, the information in the forex market is very limited. This has led me to go other ways to get better information. At the moment I am very busy with the DOM, the Time & Sales List and the Spread Tape. I filter Ask and Bid in different sizes to gain insights. This makes it easier to identify and analyze the different strengths in the market. The stock market information has so far made for significantly faster and more accurate entries and exits. Identification of the big players

[quote=wiserltz;12647267]{quote}{quote} Maybe I missed something. A question about DOM ask/bid:

Hello wiserltz,

In the DOM you can only see the limit orders that provide liquidity in the market. Initially, the market orders are invisible, but once they have been executed, they can be seen in the market. In a 1-tickchart you can see in the Bid and Ask overview 1 market participant each who places an individual order. However, one can not say if, e.g. a 4 Lot Ask Order has been placed by a Big Player or by a Retail Trader. That's why I work with a special software that allows me endless filtering options. Currently I am analyzing the different Ask and Bid which I sort by volume. This results in interesting patterns that are, however, strongly dependent on the market. A retail trader may give up a 4-lot order, but not 20 times in a row in a given period of time. It's also hard to tell if this 4 Lot Ask is a euro buy or dollar sale.

That's why I work with a special software that theoretically allows infinite filter options. First of all, a few weeks ago, I came up with the idea of distinguishing the Euro / Dollar buying and selling from each other. Such an approach is not yet known to me, so this is an idea that I find very interesting.

Basically, it makes a difference whether in the Low the dollar is sold or the euro is bought. In both cases, this is a bullish sign, but when the dollar is sold, a big player can step out of his position and leave the market. If the euro is bought, that does not necessarily mean that the price rises immediately. Maybe a sideways market will be created to collect more ask. With this approach also one would theoretically be able to identify triggered stops. This is very helpful to identify stopfishing.

Larger numbers of lots, placed on the market, usually indicate a collection action within an accumulation or distribution. There you can identify the big players well. To push the courses or push even in certain price regions, the algorithms also like to work with smaller lots to make identification difficult. However, these algorithms can be recognized in the chart and made visible. The decisive factor is the correct filter setting.

However, I am currently implementing this idea in our project No. 8. First of all, some 100 footprint charts have to be examined in different time units (tick charts) in order to analyze certain patterns. Thereafter, the filters must be adjusted accordingly and adjusted to different market conditions (Europe, USA, Asia). After that we will know if this idea will help us. In my post you can find an example.

Deep in the market

If we know the formulas, we can theoretically make everything visible what we need. Whether the results are always correct, I dare to doubt, so it will probably be a longer project. The short-term results are impressive, but it is still too early to make specific statements. I'll stay you tuned and of course publish the results regularly.

CLS received the award for Best FX Market Data Provider at FX Week e-FX 2019 Awards for its CLSMarketData suite.

First, what exactly does CLS do?

CLS is a market infrastructure group providing settlement, processing and data solutions. CLSMarketData is based on the largest single aggregate source of FX Executed Trade data available to the market. The data products consist of the volume data and volume-related data sets of CLS and therefore represent an invaluable resource, as the market coverage historically and currently with intraday offers is big. The data is of particular interest as it comes from actual transactions. The data products are platform-independent and support a broad range of applications, including trading strategies, predictive analytics, best execution, transaction cost analysis.

Which market data reports are offered?

FX Volume - Hourly FX Spot trading volume in 33 currency pairs

FX Flow - An aggregated FX Spot Flow report that shows the direction volume by counterparty type and net direction volume for all parties

FX Price - provides aggregated spot prices in VWAP and TWAP values to further support best execution analysis

FX Forecast - provides viewers with an hourly predictive view of the FX markets so they can quickly spot potential price movements and identify higher liquidity trading hours.

Standardized and user-friendly data records that are made available via an open data delivery

Quality-reviewed and adjusted by CLS to comply with the same reporting convention used by the Bank for International Settlements (BIS) and the Bi-annual Market Reports of the Foreign Exchange Committee.

Increasing regulatory requirements, market behavior requirements, and the understanding of the effects of market movement events during their development are driving forward the demand for timely market data for foreign exchange market participants. Conclusion:

Basically an excellent idea to increase market transparency. The actual FX spot volume data has been calculated every 5 minutes since 2016 and made available to third-party customers every hour. An interesting idea to making money with volume data. If the FX spot volume data has been made available since 2016, then the question arises as to whether ECN Broker and Market Maker can also receive this data. If so, the question now arises why these data are not passed on to the customers. So far, the volume data from the forex is calculated with tick data, which has little to do with the actual volume of bid and ask. A concrete volume presentation could significantly reduce the loss rate for many traders. Maybe that's not wanted by the broker. But that could change quickly. At some point, the first broker starts, forcing the other brokers to follow suit.

CLS update the volume data only every hour. This gives the big players enough time to complete their strategies within the hour, where the others have no actual volume data available. As a result, the big players still have one hour head Start.

As a scalper, this data would not be an advantage, as you have to react more quickly to situations. The alternative is the Euro FX Future data. These data are changed with each tick, giving us a deep insight into the market. The price of the EURUSD and Euro FX is almost parallel in seconds , there are only different prices due to the swaps. However, the volume data from the future can be used exactly in the forex market. The EURUSD in the forex market is about 100 times as large as the Euro FX in the futures market. While the EURUSD trades around 17,000,000 lots a day, Euro FX only gets 170,000 to 150,000 lots. If there are 80 Lot Ask in the Euro FX order book at a price level, one can assume that the Forex market may have 8,000 lots. That's just a speculative example. The liquidity is therefore 100 times larger in the Forex market, which depending upon broker on the execution times can affect. In addition, every trader can get this stock market data for a few dollars a month. Crucial is then still with a corresponding prop software to filter this stock market data. There are different providers for each area with different priorities, which can be found on the Internet.

The retail traders pose no threat to the big players, even if they receive hourly the current volume data from the forex market. Because the actual business of big players takes place in the time when the volume is not updated. The big player trades are therefore not in danger and in addition you can still earn money with the volume data. However, this is still an advantage for CLS's customers. They are usually long-term investors and previously had no volume data from the forex market. At least 24 times a day you will receive a specific volume information. This is another advantage over retail traders. It can be assumed that almost all participants in the forex market now have concrete volume data, except the retail traders.

In EURUSD retail traders trade around 1,000,000 lots each day. This amount is not only worthwhile for the big players, but now also for those who are CLS customers. This situation is a bit unfair. If we compare Forex Forex trading with a football game, beginners without football boots will play against the biggest world champions. Everyone can think about how that works out.

If you have not been profitable so far, that's not because of you, but because of the fact that you just do not have any information from the market you're trading. It's as if you want to land a plane without ILS system in fog. CLS already has 23,000 customers who now have more information in the Forex market than you. That means the market is getting harder for you every day. Begin to deal with the stock market data and learn how to collect the big players in the accumulation phases Ask and Bid in the distribution phases. These big players sometimes go down 20 pip with a few hundred thousand lots, knowing that they can dominate the market and push up or down anytime. Anyone who does not know this way of working, has no chances in this market. And most of the time it's just because of a lack of information.

The never ending story

Hello dear subscribers,

What makes a trader successful?

Looking back over the last 10 years and describing my evolution in trading, would be an endless story. First of all, at the beginning I was distracted too much by different information rather than focusing on one thing. If you try too much at once, you can not spend enough time focusing on the crucial things that drive you forward. In life of a trader is all about the right setup. When I started trading, I was fortunate enough to have been a successful entrepreneur for 20 years. That's why I knew what matters as a self-employed person. The first few years are a real challenge and those who do not give 100%, are faster off the market than they can blink. This is nothing else when trading. The first and crucial point is that you are burning for trading. Arnold Schwarzenegger once said: Be hungry and stay hungry. His 6 rules of success are an example of his insane success.

1. Have a vision.

That's an important point, because those who have no vision can never arrive.

2. Do not listen to the naysayers.

There are many people in your life who tell you, that what you do, will never be successful. Just make sure they are not right.

3. Work your ass off

If you need 8 hours of sleep, you just have to sleep faster. I myself work between 10-12 hours a day and I look forward to every new day.

4.There is no plan B

If there was a plan B, it would not be dramatic to fail by Plan A. Think about it once.

5. You can only feel complete as a human being when you think about what you can do for the people around you.

Everything you do, you get back one day, so give something back and help other people.

6. There is no self-made man

No matter how successful someone is, he has rarely made it alone. Even as a trader you need people who stand behind you. Alone, you create a lot, together with other almost everything.

Success is a concatenation of the right psychological attitude.

At first I tried to write down some things that belong to a Trader Setup. This is like a puzzle, only when it is complete, you can be really successful. But you can already achieve success if some parts are missing. But then you have to optimize your setup over time. Take a look at the things I have noted and answer for yourself how you handle the individual points, what experiences you have gained and what points urgently need to be improved. We have to keep in mind that these points are inevitably connected and build on each other. A good trader regularly questions his points and changes the things that give him a market advantage. This does not always have to do with money, but could also mean more time for the family, better health or less fear of loss.

We traders have a big challenge, there is no one who tells us which of our points needs to be improved urgently to work more efficiently. There is no professional trader who is interested that we getting ahead as a trader. Not even the coaches, who wants only your money in the first place. Your partner would like to help you, but he does not know how. So, we traders are mostly alone. Then one look at Forex factory, in a thousand different blogs, to find the Holy Grail and is in the end more confused than anything else. This is because there are finished systems are offered. But believe me, that works in the long run in the most rare cases. First you have to deal with the system and set it up, the most time-consuming is now the time you need to test this system. In most cases it will not work for you, then you are looking for something else.

Go another way. Take my slide as a thought support, make you now the headings for your own setup. Then fill in these headings with your knowledge, experience and preferences. I recommend you do this in writing. If you've written everything down, you find that there are still some gaps. Now you can research and the vast knowledge on the internet and at FF will help you to fill these gaps. This will definitely get you closer to your goal. Concentrate on the essential points and try not to find a 100% solution. According to the Pareto principle, 80% of the time brings 20% of the results. The rest of the time (80%) is wasted to get 100%, but that is ineffective.

When I focused solely on the EURUSD, some traders told me that this could not work. One should trade at least 5-10 currency pairs. After 10 years I am still a full-time trader and those who advised me back then are again in the employment relationship. So, go your own way, take ideas and try them out. But do not let others bend you. Maybe you are not yet a successful trader, but in many areas, you already know what is good or less good for you. Sometimes one should listen to his inner voice.

Two things will catch up with you on the way to success. The greed and the fear, these things you have to fight every day. Volume in tick chart

[quote=simnz;12651884]{quote} 1. Quite an revealing article.

Hello Simnz,

Thank you first for your kind words. I would like to add something else to my report: Real Volume in Forex

So far, the distribution in the Forex market looked like this:

Big Player = 85% sales and full volume information

External institutional traders = 10% turnover and no information about volume data

Retail Trader = 5% sales and no information about volume data

At present, 23,000 External Institutional Traders receive 24 daily information on the traded volume through CLS

Now the distribution in the forex market looks like this:

Big Player = 85% sales and full volume information

External institutional traders = 10% sales and 24 times a day information about volume data

Retail Trader = 5% sales and no information about volume data

This means that almost all traders in the forex market now have volume information, except for retail traders. This makes it even harder for the retail traders, because they do not have the crucial information. Additionally, CLS now knows how the 23,000 external institutional traders are positioned, which I find a dangerous development.

Since the tickchart in the Forex market gives me no information about the number of ask and bid, I only use it in the price range, as it represents the price much better than in the time chart. The decisive advantage is as follows: In a high volatility phase, a large candle forms in the time chart and many candles in the tick chart. With low volatility, many small candles are formed in the time chart and only a few candles in the tick chart. That means the tickchart adapts to the volatility. There is a lot going on, there are more candles, nothing is going on, there are only a few candles. A fixed time frame is an unnecessary factor for me.

Here you will find the difference how ticks are calculated in the forex and futures market.

The fastest information in the market

Hello dear subscribers,

Every trader dreams of receiving information in daily trading that predicts a possible course development. Various indicators are used to provide quick information. Today we want to look at what representations provide the fastest information to make profitable trading decisions.

Forex market

First of all, we need to be aware of what information we actually receive. Banks or institutions provide different brokers with price data from the interbank market. The interbank market is not stock exchange regulated. These data are processed differently by ECN brokers or market makers and passed on to their customers. From the broker, these course data first reach our MT4 and are processed there. These are three different dates. OHLC, time and volume that is generated from the ticks. Unfortunately, a tick volume has nothing to do with the volume of the stock market, I have already written extensively.

Volume in forex

Two traders who trade with different brokers will receive different price displays. Even if these two traders were with the same broker, the tick data on the MT4 would produce different representations. For this reason, only two crucial data are correct in the forex market: OHLC and the time data. Of course, the price jumps in the form of ticks are usually correct, but it is not possible to derive the correct volume, as in the stock market.

First, this information is displayed in the form of a candle and projected on the screen. In addition, we see next to the candle a price line. The displayed price line in MT4 is the bid price (Bid). In addition, you can also display the Ask price. The ask price is always higher than the bid price and the difference between the two rates is called the spread. As the spread widen, this indicates lack of liquidity on the ask or bid side. When we place a long position, our transactions are always opened at the ask price and closed at the bid price. When we place a short position, our transactions are always opened at the bid price and closed at the ask price. In order to keep an eye on the liquidity, I recommend to show the Ask line in MT4.

Candles are created from the ticks and the set time, which are displayed in the form of OHLC. What many do not even know, this representation of the candle is already an indicator. If we now represent a normal chart, this picture usually consists mostly of the past. The current price line Bid and Ask represents the present and the future is a black screen. As a rule, the past takes up about 90% of the total space required, while the last candle represents the present. Actually, this is a strange representation, because we traders want to earn money in the future and not in the past. However, for the most part we have the past displayed on the chart. Of course, the future cannot be displayed because it would only consist of a black screen. That means we traders try from the past to make a possible forecast for the future. Many beginners have had to learn painfully that this is a challenge that in most cases goes wrong. Roulette and forex are apparently based on random moves, but there is one crucial difference.

A roulette ball in the casino has no memory and the probability of winning red / black is 48.6%. In the Forex market, traders have a memory (certain price levels act as resistance), but the probability of profit is 1:19 or 5.26%. The advantage in Forex is that certain price levels can be declared as resistance or support, which increases the likelihood of winning. In the past, I also made wins with resistance zones, but I later realized that these resistance zones in Equilibrium are being initiated by the big players to take as few participants as possible in a breakout. Since I've only traded in equilibrium in the past, my chances of winning were significantly higher than if I had bet on a breakout.

We've found that a candle is nothing more than an indicator, let's look at other indicators. Most of the indicators are calculated from the price or the ticks and run according to the price. This means that most indicators react more slowly than the price. You realize this at the latest, if you build on your trading decisions on two MA's. The indicators may give a different or better view of prices, but in the end they are significantly slower than the Bid / Ask price line. Even current news brings no advantage, because you never know how the market reacts to it.

A small glimmer of hope are the currency strength indicators in the Forex. With this strategy, you first consider 8 individual currencies instead of 28 currency pairs. In the EURUSD, the dollar or euro strength is determined from the following currency pairs.

USDCHF, USDJPY, USDCAD, EURUSD, GBPUSD, AUDUSD, NZDUSD = dollar strength

EURUSD, EURGBP, EURCHF, EURJPY, EURCAD, EURAUD, EURNZD = Euro strength

The idea of buying a strong currency and selling it against the weak currency will not pay off in the long run because you do not know how the strength of a currency will develop in the future. If one currency is currently weak and the other is very strong, this can change within seconds due to a breakout. Every single currency belongs to a single economy. Some currencies are strong and other currencies are weak, we can not extract this information from a single currency pair chart. If the EURUSD rises, it may be because the dollar is weak and the euro is strong. Maybe both currencies are strong or weak, only the euro is slightly stronger in both cases. The key is to know how a single currency is positioned across the market.

In the case of the EURUSD, we don't have to look at 13 different currency pairs to measure the strength of the dollar and the euro, we just need a chart or two. First of all, this is a significant time saver. If the dollar suddenly becomes stronger in 5 currency pairs over the course of a day, we can see that more quickly in the overview chart. In many situations I found that this ad sometimes reacts a little faster than the price chart itself. That's why I like to work with currency strengths, but I would never derive a trade from them.

If you work with a price chart in Forex, I recommend that you work with a tickchart that forms up to 12 candles instead of 1 candle within a minute. This enables potential resistance areas to be identified more quickly. Since there is no top and no bottom in the price chart, I recommend placing the last candle in the middle of the chart if possible. Than there is enough space up, down and to the right for a possible look in the future.

Future

First, the exchange makes the price data from the exchange-regulated market available to different brokers. The brokers pass this data directly on to their customers. From the broker, this course data now reach our MT5 or our professional prop software and are processed there. This is four different dates. OHLC, time, volume and the number of trades. The volume is specified in the DOM with bid and ask. In addition, the liquidity in the form of the limit order is displayed, so it would actually be 5 different data.

Two traders who trade with different brokers will see the same price displays on their chart. That is a crucial difference to the forex market. Also important is the respective trading platform, which individually dissolves and translates the stock market data. On the MT5 I would not fall back here, because the information is very limited. Individual indicators can be created via mql5, but are very limited due to the programming language.

I recommend a professional prop software, which should be very variable in their settings. Good trading platforms also allow individual programming via C +. A good prop software allows not only footprint charts and volume charts, but also other interesting forms of presentation. An individual attitude of the DOM and the time & sales list is decisive. Similarly, deleted and added limit order should be visible. Pay attention to unique selling points, because these could be important trading advantages for you. A major weakness of all prop platforms is the fact that the number of trades cannot be broken down into bid and ask in all time units. However, that would be an enormous trading advantage today, which could reveal the identification of the big players in any unit of time. This would make it much easier to identify accumulation and distribution phases. If you are in a sideways market and you are able to see if the big players are collecting ask or bid, you are also able to take the movement of the stopfishing and the subsequent breakout. However, the existing platforms on the market are not yet mature enough.

My idea would be to build my own server, which first saves the 1 tick data from the exchange and makes this data available to you again in different time units. Crucial is the programming to get the data that is relevant for a trade decision. On the one hand there are importend small equilibrium in the tick data and on the other hand the number of trades in relation to the bid and ask. I think that could be a crucial market advantage.

First Conclusion:

In the forex market, the price range of bid and ask is the fastest information in the trade in addition to the currency strength. Even in the futures market you could calculate a currency strength, but the effort would be enormous, since you have to store for  28 currency pairs each a 1 tickchart and then merge the data. The result would be sensational, since one would be able to calculate the currency strength in the millisecond range. I am surprised that no one has yet come up with the idea.

In the futures market the current price line is the third fastest information. In second place are the bid and ask, which come on the market in 1 tick chart. Here you can immediately see how much lot (bid or ask) a single trader brings into the market. With a correct algorithm, you would even be able to assign the different trades to a particular trader. The advantage that results from this should be clear to everyone. In principle, the submitted bid or ask are at a certain price level, a small look into the future. By this I do not mean the bid and ask which lead to an immediate tick change, but the large bid and ask which do not immediately lead to a large price change. This is the so-called absorption where the big players e.g.  euro buy massively in a falling exchange rate without significantly slowing down the falling exchange rate. It is a sensational achievement that I admire very much. But this information can also be read out relatively easily. In the first place are the limit order in the market, which represent the crucial liquidity. That is clearly the future, because a trader who gives up a limit order shows the willingness to enter into a trade at a certain price level in the future. Of course, limit orders are also deleted shortly before execution. But if that happens I can immediately recognize this in the DOM and take a counter position. A large fake limit order that is deleted shortly before execution is a great signal for a possible trend reversal. It is clear that the futures data on the one hand give a better idea of future price developments and thus belong to the fastest data in the market. This is an invaluable advantage that a trader should not do without. What matters is how you view the data. It is not the fastest Formula 1 car that wins, but the driver who manages to create an optimal symbiosis between driver and vehicle wins. This applies equally to a trader and his trading setup.

Both the data from the forex and from the futures market bring crucial information for trading. With the help of the future data, you can significantly increase your efficiency again. Therefore, for me both data are an important factor in the trade.

Let's take a closer look and start with the future data.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Point A

Here we see the delta of Bid and Ask. The red line shows the delta of big players, the green line the delta of retail traders. As we can see, in most cases a counter position arises, which is also logical. Because if someone sells, someone has to buy at the same time. The positions of retail traders are usually at a disadvantage, as the big players determine the direction. The delta is not always clear, because the big players also work with small positions, which limits the view somewhat.

Point B

The same view of the delta only in a smaller unit of time.

Point C

Here we see the split bid coming in the market. 1-6 Lot Bid are most common, so they have their own layout. 7-10 lot bids have been combined and the larger bids from 11 lots are displayed on the left with the associated time. The smaller lots usually provide an immediate change in price, while the larger lots are used to pile up bid or ask in the sideways markets. I will go into that again more precisely. An investment of a bid may mean that the dollar is bought or the euro is sold. It can be an order that comes into the market or an order that is taken out of the market (triggered stops example). The respective insight is not allways concrete, but you get a good overview of what is happening in the market. It can also be determined whether the number of bids or ask dominate the market and whether a larger number of lots are being collected.

Point D

The same display as for Point C only for the Ask page.

Point E

Between bid and ask I placed a day candle from the DOM in the middle. On the one hand, this shows the price movement, as well as the spread between bid and ask. This means that liquidity weaknesses can be recognized immediately at the limit orders. The number on the left side is the total volume Bid and Ask, on the right side you can see the number of trades at the respective price level. With this you can also identify larger orders at the individual price levels. Likewise one can recognize possible resistance zones due to higher volumes.

Point F / G

A 1 tickchart for the bid and ask page showing the order in progress. Gaps in order submission can be identified more quickly here. This view is a pure overview for the identification of Bid and Ask on the respective price levels and gives only a large overview what happens in the market. A trade should not take place over it.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

This overview already gives more specific information about what is going on in the market.

Point A

In the DOM we see on the right and left side the total number of ask and bid within the whole contract. These are interesting zones to keep an eye on. In addition to the current price, I receive information about the liquidity of the limit orders, the bid and ask executed at the respective price level, as well as the accumulated, added or deleted limit orders. In addition, the currently added or deleted limit orders are displayed. This is crucial to identify pretended liquidity.

Point B

Here we see the open interest, i.e. the open long positions in the market.

Point C

This view shows whether the euro or dollar is bought or sold. From this, conclusions can be drawn about an accumulation or distribution. You can see when the big players get out of their positions and when they catch the stops of the retail traders. Of course, this information is not always correct because there are too many different situations. However, if one has the overall picture in mind, one can identify these potential errors.

Point D

A 30-second footprint chart with filtering that identifies strong and weak zones in the current price history. First and foremost I need this view to identify stopfishing. This means that short-term changes in trend can be recognized more quickly.

Point E

A 1 tick chart shows the submitted oders of a single participant on the bid and ask page.

Point F / G

The Time & Sales list shows the split ticks of Bid and Ask. The respective view contains the ask and bid price, the price change and the number of lots at the respective price level. In addition, the liquidity of the limit order can be displayed at the time of the change in the tick. The decisive criterion for me is the time display in milliseconds. This allows, to identify concretely the small orders, from the big players.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Let's first look at the 11th of November in EURUSD. Initially, massive ask in the sideways market was collected between 09:00 and 12:00 CET (Point A). Then a stopfishing was done and the course was pushed up to point B. From 2 p.m. 1000 Lot Ask were collected. I knew that the big player was waiting for a lot of volatility in the market. In the evening, there were some appointments that allowed increased volatility. USD Monthly Budget Statement, USD FOMC Economic Projections, USD Fed Interest Rate Decision, Fed Monetary Policy Statement and subsequent FOMC Press Conference. There was a short Stopfishing again at point C, then the course was pushed to the point D upwards. Even if the dollar had strengthened at these meetings, the rate would still have been pushed up. Because during the course of the day, the big players had collected many 1000 lots, which now had to be brought into profit. We see that these meetings are only needed to create the corresponding volatility in the market. What comes out is already clear beforehand. Although news and meetings influence the currencies, they do not affect the strategies of the big players. Let us first take a closer look at point A from 09: 00-12: 00 CET.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

In the 1 tick chart we first recognize the price development in the sideways market at Point A. At Point B, it is noticeable that during this time a larger number of Ask than Bid came onto the market. That already gave the first indication of a possible accumulation phase. Of course, the other market participants also saw these large orders that came into the market. And that is exactly the crucial point. With the information that large orders are coming onto the market, the participants cannot do much at first, because as we can see in the picture, the price was then pushed down more strongly. This has stopped all the participants who have bet on a rising course. Therefore, we must remember that a big player usually only makes big orders, when it is clear that the price does not move directly in that direction afterwards. When many retail traders move up with the big players, some retail traders eventually start to get out of the market. At that moment the euro is sold and the dollar is bought at the same time. This slows down the course and the big players cannot finished their strategy up. How does it usually go? First, the big player buys large amounts of Ask in an accumulation phase. Then he pushes the course down and stops everyone who bought Ask. Then the way is clear, for a course up. This means that large orders are not directly price-relevant. For this reason, the big player doesn't care that you can identify these large orders in the market. The small orders that the big player brings to the market are relevant for the short term.

First, we see how the big player obviously buys big orders from Ask. We can assume that the price will initially not rise higher and suggest that it could come to a Stoppfishing.

What exactly happens during a stoppfishing?

The big player knows exactly that retail traders are trying to follow in his footsteps. By placing large orders in the ask area, the big player signals a future willingness to push the price up. This causes many retail traders to buy the euro as well. Since the big player determines the market anyway, he has no problem pushing the price down by 20 pip to stop the retail traders. He knows for sure that he will be able to push the price up again. The price is now pushed down until it hits the first stops of the retail trader. As soon as the stops are caught, a chain reaction comes down, because at that moment, the dollar is bought massively. Every stop that is caught pushes the price further down and in the end the retail traders ensure that the price goes down extremely sharply. The big player is already starting to get out of the dollar and is pushing the price up again.

Since the big player knows exactly that there is stopfishing, he naturally wants to participate in it. While buying large quantities of Ask in the sideways market, he also buys the dollar to push the price down for a short time. This approach should not be identified by the market, so the big player buys the dollar lot in small numbers. At point A, the big player started buying the small quantities. First let's look at how we can identify this approach.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

First of all, it is important that we can display the time in milliseconds in the Time & Sales list.

At 10: 01: 00.3660 you can see at Point A how a big player buys almost 50 lot bids. The probability that other market participants have also bought bid in this thousandth of a second is very unlikely. Therefore, with milliseconds you are able to assign the small orders to a big player.

Just under 2 minutes later at 10: 02: 52.3690, almost 80 lot bids were bought within this millisecond. Although this large mass of orders was bought, the price only moved two ticks down. This shows how strong the pressure was upwards.

The algorithms that are used are random and not understandable for us. We can see the number of pieces the big players have bought within this millisecond. A 50 or 80 lot order would be noticed immediately in the market, the purchase of small quantities takes place under the radar and is not recognizable for most traders. Especially since the numbers run through so quickly that you are not able to keep track of them at all. For this you should first freeze the time & sales list to identify the small orders.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

In the fields marked yellow (point A), the big player has massively bought these small orders from bid. You can see what happened after that with the course. Only at Point B has the big player once again fired a machine gun volley of small orders into the market, and with the stops of the retail traders, the price has finally gone down more sharply. To identify these machine gun salvos, I like to use the sorted Bid and Ask that I showed in my first slide.

Conclusion:

With large lots that come on the ask or bid side, I am able to identify an accumulation or distribution phase. That shows me the long-term course course. The small orders that the big player secretly collects and do not immediately lead to a price change show me the medium-term price trend. As soon as a kind of machine gun volley is fired between 1-3 lots, this often shows the start for a stop fishing and thus the short-term course. The big player likes to work in the equilibrium with this machine gun volley to keep the price within the range. Of course you can't always rely on it, you always have to see the reactions of the big players in the context of the market. However, anyone who can handle this information is already a significant step ahead of most traders. There is still a lot more information to be considered, we will talk more about that in the next few weeks.

M30 = ⌀ a new zone is created every 4 hours

H1 = ⌀ a new zone is created every 6 hours

H4 = ⌀ A new zone is created once a day

D1 = ⌀ once a week a new zone is created

The futures data are ideal for concrete short-term to medium-term planning. With the time & sales list, the algorithms can be read out when the big players collect small amounts of lots. The DOM shows the deleted and added limit orders, which represent the decisive liquidity in the market. The open interest shows the open long positions in the market. Small and large orders can be filtered in the 1 tick chart to recognize what is collected in the equilibrium. The chart shows whether the euro / dollar is being bought or sold. In addition, you can make the triggered stops visible. The future data help me to find the optimal entry and exit.

The Forex data are ideal for long-term planning, the futures data are ideal for short-term planning. Both datas meet in the medium term. If the information is consistent, the probability of a successful trade goes up. If there is different information, you should wait for a better opportunity. The Forex data is good for making a forecast, with the futures data I can quickly determine whether the big players are approaching or moving away from this forecast. For this reason, both data are crucial for a successful trade.

I would like to go back to the randomness of course developments. Of course, the coincidence is responsible for whether a market order at a certain time period at a certain price level leads to a tick change or not. However, we know that the big players determine the price development in the market due to their investments. Therefore, I believe that the small tick changes are fundamentally subject to chance, but not the fundamental direction of the market. This is prepared and carried out precisely by the big players. This allows calculation of the course price without having to consider the coincidence, provided that the correct information from the futuremarket is observed. Bonnie and Clyde in the Forex market

Hello dear subscribers,

In my last report "The fastest information in the market" I showed which information is the fastest in the Forex and Futures markets. This knowledge is first of all important in order to make the right trading decisions. Since today's report builds on my last post, I recommend working through it first.

The fastest information in the market

The sideways markets (equilibrium) are an important key to success. If you recognize in a sideways market whether it is an accumulation or a distribution, you are also able to take the movement of the stop fishing with you and the subsequent breakout. This means that only price movements are traded that are quick and efficient and thus reduce the risk of a longer stay in the market. The big traders' approach is usually based on the principle: the same procedure as every week.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

On the picture you can see the EURUSD in M1 from December 11th. First the price went down and on the morning of December 11 a big player started buying the euro strongly (Point A). A few hours later, another large buy order from Euros came on the market (Point C). First of all, we have to ask ourselves why a big player places a large order in the market when he has to assume that every trading participant will see this large order immediately. I wrote about this in my last post. A big player places a large order only if he is certain that this large order is not directly price-relevant. By that I mean that placing a large order does not immediately lead to a larger spike upwards. That would also be very ineffective because the big player would be predictable at that moment. As we know, the big players are anything but predictable. First, a big player at Point A buys the euro with an obviously large order. Then there is a small stop run down and the course moves up again.

All participants who goes Long at Point A have been stopped. Then the course went up to Point B. Now the big player begins the second phase. The dollar is bought strong, but in such a way that nobody notices it. The big player uses algorithms that buy the dollar in small quantities. The market participants in the market only see big buy orders euro and assume that the price will have to move upwards in the short term. If the big player were to buy the dollar in large lots, the participants would be confused. The big player knows that he will push the price up sharply in the medium term. To do this, he first has to buy a large number of euros. But he also knows that some participants will follow him. These participants must be stopped up before the spike. I described the reasons for this in detail in my last post. So there must first be a stop fishing before the spike can start up. It goes without saying that the big player also wants to make money from the stop fishing. Logically, he has to buy the dollar at the same price level where he buys the euro on the one hand. To keep participants believing that the price is going up, the big player has to buy the dollar in small quantities, which is exactly what happens at Point B.

At Point C, the big player buys the euro again in large quantities. Many market participants go long and are then stopped again. It is now clear to many that it is an equilibrium and the course will definitely go up. The price continues to move in equilibrium and runs to point D. This price movement to point D looks like the big player is now pushing the price up. But now the opposite is happening. With a machine gun salvo of 1 and 2 lots, the big player begins to push the course down. With this, the first stops of retail traders managed to catch up. Then a chain reaction occurs. Every stop that is caught pushes the course further down. In principle, the stops of the retail trailers ensure that they shoot each other out of the market. At Point E, the big player fires a large machine gun salvo from small solder and pushes the course further down. The same chain reaction arises again and in the course of the downward movement, the big player begins to exit the dollar. At Point F there is no longer a participant willing to trade further down and the Big Player starts pushing the course up. After the course has gone down so strongly, traders are hesitant to buy the euro. An ideal starting point for the big player.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Here I have shown the whole process again with my own algorithms in the future market. You can see exactly where the euro and dollar were bought. At Point G you can see that the big player has already withdrawn from the euro with partial positions. After that, the price went down even more. In principle, it is always the same game that is played. As long as it works, it will continue to be played. Only when there are complications are alternatives sought. It was the same at Bonnie & Clyde at the time, only there were no alternatives in the end.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

We have found that in the futures market the current price line is the third fastest information and the bid and ask that come into the market in a 1 tick chart are the second fastest. The quickest information about a possible price trend is shown by the limit orders in the market, which provide the liquidity. That is clearly the future, because a trader who gives up a limit order shows the willingness to enter into a trade at a certain price level in the future. Of course, limit orders are also deleted shortly before execution. That is why I recommend working with a headmap that takes into account spoofing in the market. This gives me a good overview of possible resistance and support zones in the market.

So we have to consider three phases of big players. Phase 1 is the placing of large orders in the market that can be identified by every market participant. These large orders show the long-term market trend. This is followed by phase 2, the preparation for stop fishing. That is the medium-term course. Algorithms buy small orders in quick succession that cannot be identified in the market. This is followed by phase 3: the big player shoots 1-3 lots with machine gun salvos and pushes the course in the appropriate direction to start stop fishing. The large orders in phase 1 are easy to identify, so we do not need to deal with them.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

With this attitude I identify phase 2, the preparation for stop fishing. At Point A we see the time and sales list, each individual order that a participant has brought into the market is displayed. With the right filtering, you can recognize these small orders that a big player buys. At 22: 59: 00.2590, a larger participant bought 15 Lot Ask within milliseconds. It is possible to combine orders that were bought within a certain millisecond. This makes it much easier to correctly identify phase 2.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Here we see a summary again. At Point A we recognize the large lot that has been released into the market. At Point B, we see the orders summarized in milliseconds that were placed by a larger participant. At Point C, I can more easily identify the machine gun salvos I have described. For this, the individual lots have only been filtered. To recognize the stop fishing, I still like to use a footprint in the 30 second chart, which shows me the triggered stops.

Conclusion:

I don't get the information described here from the Forex market, but only from stock market data. Possible patterns that I see in the chart are in most cases initiated by the big players and give me important information. Overall, I need to be able to read the overall context of the market to increase my long-term profitability. If we summarize all this information, it should be clear that a single indicator is unable to increase my probability of winning. It is also wrong to assume that the market is easy to trade. Indicator winnings are purely coincidental and have nothing to do with the real intentions of the big players.

Therefore, I strongly advise you to refrain from standard indicators and to deal with the stock market data. I have also been successful in the past 10 years, but that was also pure coincidence. However, it was only because I only traded in equilibrium or in sideways markets. The resistance zones I determined were initiated by the big players, which of course benefited me within the equilibrium.

Let us note that it is definitely possible to make profits even without the stock market data, but we have to be aware that this is based solely on chance. If you want to rule out coincidence, you should look at the stock exchange data. A little tip: If you look at the screens of traders from Goldman Sachs or large banks, you will find that only the DOM, the time and sales list and a maximum of one chart without indicators are used there. In order to act successfully, you should work as the successful ones set an example. It may be a big change in the beginning, but it will be a big win in the long run.

The sentence from my last post is so important that I have to repeat it again !!!

It is about the coincidence of course developments. Of course, chance is responsible for whether or not a market order leads to a tick change at a certain price level for a certain period of time. However, we know that the big players determine the price development in the market due to their investments. Therefore, I believe that the small tick changes are generally subject to chance, but not the basic direction of the market. This is prepared and carried out exactly by the big players. This enables a course to be calculated outside of coincidence, provided the correct information is taken into account. This is a crucial point that can give us all hope.

I wish you a successful weekend.
