--- 帖子 #1307 ---
Probabilities of winning with stop loss

Hello dear subscribers,

first I would like to take the opportunity to welcome all new subscribers to this blog. I am very happy about your participation and hope that you will find many good ideas in this blog. This blog is a kind of buffet where different ideas for scalpers, day traders and swing traders from the forex and futures market are available. From this, everyone can create their own individual setup that takes them further. I keep my fingers crossed for you and will continue to try to post creative and informative contributions in the future.

The question I get often asked: Should one work with a stop loss or not?  I cannot give a specific answer to this, as it depends on the individual case of the trader.

First of all, there are three options: You use a stop loss or do not use it. The third option is to use hedge strategies. I also like to use a hedge strategy when I have a good run. Then I run my trade and only trade the individual pullbacks. If I have placed a sell limit order and realize that the big players still want to get the stops above, I also use hedging, to expand my stop. As a rule, I try to get an optimal start with the future data and the identification of the Stophunting. If that goes wrong, I let the trade run into the stop, usually I get out of it manually beforehand. Since I complete 10 to 20 trades daily, there are enough opportunities for a new chance. It is not the daily result that counts, but the monthly result. When trading with money that can be dispensed with when in doubt, trading is much more relaxed, although a loss is always a confirmation that you have overlooked something important.

At the beginning of my trader career, using a stop loss was hell. No matter where I started, my stop loss was often triggert and kicked me out of the market. Today I know that it was the big players who focused on stophunting to generate new liquidity. After so many years they have become so professional that they manage to make life difficult for scalpers, day traders and swing traders at the same time. Initially I was really frustrated when I was stopped, but I was more relaxed when I stopped by myself, even though I lost there too. Losing is not a nice thing, especially when it comes to your own money. However, you have to learn to lose in this game to be able to win. And that takes time.

Many beginners increase their stops, in the event of a loss, because they hope the price will turn bullish again. So the Trade 10 Pip runs into the minus and suddenly the price turns and goes up again. As soon as the price has risen somewhat, most beginners close their trade and are happy not to have lost. If you ask them why they got out, the answer is: the price has now gone up 10 pip, the likelihood is high that it will go straight back down. One crucial thing is saved by the beginner: "It was good to increase the stop loss, so I didn't lose." But one day this habit becomes a big loss. In principle, it's more about psychology than losing a few dollars. Losing unleashes fear of losing, whoever loses more than 50% out of 10 trades, has a difficult time psychologically.

Before we get a little more involved in this area, we have to speak about a few basic things first.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Let's say we have a 80% chance of winning, which is very high in this market. Our risk-reward ratio is 0.5, as we get $ 5 if we win and get $ 10 if we lose. We make 80 trades in profit, earning $ 400. With 20 trades, we make a $ 200 loss. This is initially a profit factor of 2 because we made twice as much profit as loss. We made a total of $ 200 and an average of $ 20 per trade. These $ 20 are our expected value for future trades.

In the second case, we have a 40% chance of winning and a risk-reward ratio of 2 because we earn $ 10 on every win and lose $ 5 on every loss. After 100 trades, we made $ 400 and lost $ 300, which equates to a profit factor of 1.33. Our expected value is $ 10 per trade. Now it is likely that the first example will be more successful than the second example. At first glance, this seems to be true, but in reality it behaves very differently.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Let's first look at the probability that we win. The red bar shows the stop loss, the yellow bar the entry and the green bar the take profit (TP). We do not take spread and commission into account here. In example A we see that the stop loss is as far away as the TP. The probability that the TP will be reached first is 50%. The risk / reward ratio is 1. In example B we use a stop of 1 pip and a TP of 3 pip. The risk-reward ratio is 3 because I have the opportunity to make three times as much profit as loss. The probability that the stop loss will be reached before the TP is 75%. In case C we increased the stop loss to 3 pip and reduced the TP to 1 pip. The risk-reward ratio is 0.25 and the probability is 75% that I will achieve 1 pip profit. The calculated probability refers to a trade that I blindly place in the market without using a strategy.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Point A

In this example we assume that we calculate a stop loss of 1 pip and a TP of 4 pip. The spread is 1 pip. Normally we would have a risk / reward ratio of 4 as we take 1 pip risk and expect a TP of 4 pip. However, this is not correct since we have to take the spread into account as costs. This reduces the risk-reward ratio to 1: 2. The probability that my TP will be reached is 20%. Now we calculate 100 trades that will be carried out. I calculated $ 10 per pip. We close 20 trades for $ 40 each, for a total of $ 800. We close 80 trades at a loss of $ 20 each, for a total of $ 1,600. In total, we have a loss of $ 800. It is interesting that the broker earns $ 1000 over the same period.

Point B

Here we proceed according to the same principle, whereby we set a stop loss of 4 pip and expect a TP of 1 pip. The risk-reward ratio is 1: 0.2. That means I have to win 5 trades to make up one loss. The probability that my TP will be reached is 80%. If we calculate 100 trades again, we will make a profit of $ 800 and a loss of $ 1000 at the same time. That's a total loss of $ 200. Overall, we have $ 600 less loss on 100 trades as in Example A. If we set the stop loss to 100 pip, we would have a profit of $ 990 and a loss of $ 1000. But even with a 99% chance of winning, we would still have a $ 10 loss. Nevertheless, the loss is lower with a higher probability of winning. At first glance, this proves that the further the stop is in relation to the TP, the more profitably the probability works. However, this is a false bill, because holding an 80% probability of winning is already an extraordinary achievement. Let's look at the example below.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

In the previous examples, only the pure probability was initially calculated. Let's assume that in example A, with a profitable setup, we are able to increase the probability from 20% to 40%. That would give us a profit of $ 400. In example B, we increase the probability from 80% to 90% and would also achieve a profit of $ 400. However, increasing the probability from 20 to 40% is easier to achieve, than a increasing from 80% to 90%. In the second case, there is simply too little room for improvement, which makes it significantly more difficult for us. Working without a stop loss certainly means increasing the likelihood in your favor, but it also involves an unpredictable risk, so I would recommend working with a stop loss.

With this example, we can guess that exchange trading is always a losing trade in terms of probability. The advantage of a trader is to influence the likelihood in his favor by generating a market advantage from information that brings a higher probability of profit. In gambling, the cards or the lotto balls have no memory. In trading, certain processes, for example in Stophunting, are always carried out according to similar principles, because they are based on people who have a memory. This makes trading less of a gamble.

In this context, I would like to make one more important point.

I keep reading that traders claim the big players are waiting for certain numbers from Europe / USA or certain meetings from the ECB / FED to make concrete trading decisions that drive the price in a certain direction. In my opinion, that's a mistake. As we know, the big players first have to collect their positions and then push them in a certain direction. Depending on the volatility, these collecting actions can take anywhere from a few hours to a few days. If the Fed were to make a decision that would have a positive impact on the dollar, the big players could only start collecting the dollar afterwards. That would be a bit difficult in this case, since everyone wants the dollar. This means that the big players must have made their decision many hours before the actual breakout. If the big players collected the euro and the FED gave positive news for the dollar, the big players would still push the price up to make their profits. What comes out of the important meetings is less relevant for the big players at first, but what is more important is the increased volatility that then takes place at that moment. The mere fact that prices are going up and down at this moment shows that traders have different opinions. In this back and forth, the big players further shop on and finally push the price in their direction.

Money makes the world go round. We should keep in mind that around 20 million lots are traded in EURUSD per day. The big players trades round 16 million lots. In this respect, it should be completely logical that news, meetings or rumors in no way affect the way big players work. Of course, statements from the FED or the ECB will have an impact on the markets in the medium or long term, but once the big players have collected the euro, they will push the price up, no matter what happens. The meetings used to be a game of luck for me because I never knew where the course could go. With the information I have today, I can estimate and calculate that much more precisely. In 80% of cases, it is already clear where the course is going before a meeting. However, that is only my assessment.

As you know, there is, in my opinion, no concrete upward or downward trends, but always only movements that are aimed at getting traders to stop in order to obtain the necessary liquidity. The goal of a trader should be to trade precisely these movements. Depending on the time unit, there are different movements in the course of a day.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

One should take a closer look at these different movements. Here ten different trends were compared in different time units. In addition to the seven known time units from D1 to M1, I have added three more time units in the tick chart. T32 corresponds approximately to the 30 second chart, T16 corresponds approximately to the 15 second chart and the T08 corresponds approximately to the 8 second chart. A tick chart has the habit of forming significantly more candles when there is high volatility and significantly fewer candles when there is low volatility. This means that with less volatility, no unnecessary space is wasted on the chart.

In the example shown here, an average ATR of the last 10,000 candles was used. The average ATR in D1 was 82 pip in the last 10,000 days and 4 pip in M5. This means that 0.06 pip per minute was reached in the day running and 0.81 pip per minute in the M5. The pip size to be achieved was 82 pip in the D1 and 1166 pip in the M5. The T08 shows the largest fluctuation range with 5774 pip. It is quite clear, that the number of these pips can never be reached in one day in the trade.

The following calculations are pure averages and of course change daily. With a zigzag indicator with the setting 8/4/2, there are an average of 25 trend lines per day in the M5. An average of 12 candles and an average of 12 pip per trend line. However, this does not mean that each candle reaches an average pip because there are bullish as well as bearish candles. If you were to trade these 25 trend lines correctly each day, you could get 300 pip. On average, a trend line runs for almost 1 hour and 0.2 pip is reached per minute. This 0.2 pip is an average for the whole day. From 09: 00-11: 00CET and 15: 00-17: 00 CET the greatest volatility is within the EURUSD. Frankfurt and London are in the market in the morning, New York, Frankfurt and London in the afternoon. Within these 4 hours you can more than double the pip size per minute.

You can find the complete contribution here:

Increase our hourly dare?

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Another point to influence the probability and reduce the risk is the length of stay in the market. Using this comparison, I found that the downward moves in the EURUSD are between 30 and 40% faster than the upward moves. This is an important finding, since I believe that the longer you are in the market, the greater the risk of being stopped by an unexpectedly strong movement. In this case, if I only bet on a downward trend within the EURUSD, I could reduce my time in the market by 30-40%. Provided that the price movement would continue to behave in the same way in the future.

You can find the complete contribution here:

Who is faster the euro or the dollar?

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

I have found that the efficiency of my sell orders is almost twice that of buy orders. That means when I go short I have almost twice the efficiency as when I go long. Of course, this often depends on the trend currently prevailing in the market. In our example, if you only concentrated on the short positions, you would have 200 pip win in the same period without changing your trading strategy. Of course, this result does not have to be so, but the probability is high.

After that, it's all about optimizing the win rate, the pay-off ratio and the expected value in order to trade profitably.

You can find the complete contribution here:

Easy increase in trading efficiency!

Conclusion:

A high probability of winning only satisfies your own ego, but is rather counterproductive in terms of probability. A high probability of winning does not mean that the strategy is also profitable. What matters is what we win and lose on average. For this we need the profit factor. If the profit factor is 1, it means that you invest $ 1 and get $ 1 back. There is no profit from this. If you get back less than € 1, your profit factor is less than 1 and your strategy would not be profitable. If you get back more than a dollar, you will make a profit. The profit factor would be greater than 1, making your strategy profitable. The higher the profit factor, the better the strategy. As an adjusting screw, I would rather work on the risk-reward ratio than on increasing the probability of winning. High odds of winning over 60% with a win rate of 1: 1 are fragile and cannot be maintained in the long run. The first goal should be a profit factor of 2, which you can then optimize. With the expected value you have a basis to calculate future profits.

The three most important values are the total return, the drawdown and the average monthly return. Trading success does not result from the optimization of the hit rate, but a top performance results from the optimization of the exit. And to ensure that we enter the market at the right time, we continue to deal with stophunting.

I wish you a successful trading day

best regards

Michael

Key candles in Stophunting

Analysis of the past week

Hello dear subscribers,

Today's article is again about the identification of stophunting, today we will take a closer look at the key candles. In order to take a closer look at the course of the past week, we need an overview in the daily chart of the EURUSD.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

First, let's look at the price from September 1, 2019. There we see a yellow key candle (point 1), which is a stronger upward trend that has broken a strong resistance zone. Since many traders only got involved in the course of this strong price movement, it was initially not necessary, to look under the zone for stophunting . We recognize that points A, B, C and D were at a similar price level. At point C, many traders, who had placed their stops under points A and B were stopped out. Interestingly, the course went up strong after that. Last week the course reached point D, was rejected again and reached point E earlier this week. I plotted Point F because a key candle was already plotted at the beginning of September (Point 2). This area could again ensure that the course goes up a little bit again.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Let's zoom in a bit closer to take a closer look at the last two and a half weeks. On Thursday two weeks ago a strong key candle emerged which I outlined in yellow. This strong downward movement has broken through some resistance zones and many traders have only entered later the movement. For this reason, I did not expect a stophunting over this key candle. Of course, that could have happened, because I'm not allways perfect at identifying the key candles either. I got the first confirmation last Friday when there was a very strong move up and it stopped in the last quarter of my key candle. In the Asian market on Sunday, the price initially went down a bit. On Monday, I first expected the course to go back to the open price and then head down. I was wrong. My goal at the beginning of the week was the end the purple zone. This zone was reached during Wednesday, but was not breached. Thursday was very efficient, but the price did not reach the end of the purple resistance zone. At first I thought on Friday that the price could move higher again, but with my future data I could see that the dollar was bought strongly. During the course of Friday, the course broke through my purple zone and ran right up to the blue zone below. By the way, on Friday of the penultimate week the price reached an above average Pip /10 value per candle. The number 515.5 shows me a high level of market willingness to bring the price above this high in the medium term.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Let us first consider the last three trading days in EURUSD H1. In this downward trend, four key candles were identified. On Tuesday and Wednesday a strong resistance zone formed at points 1 and 2, which allegedly could not be broken. Many bet on a further upward movement here and were kicked out of the race by the strong key candle at Point B. You can see from the further movement that the big players found it unnecessary to push the course up again to get more stops. On the contrary, another stronger key candle formed at Point C immediately afterwards. A few hours later the course slowed down and an equilibrium developed. Around 9:00 CET on Thursday there was a small breakout to motivate further long traders. This movement ended exactly in the key candle of Point C. When the USA came onto the market, the price went down sharply and a new key candle is formed at Point D. In the late afternoon the course slowly went up again and ended on Friday morning, in the area of the key candle at Point D. Then the course went down more strongly and formed a new key candle at Point F. When the course went up again to Point G, It ended exactly in the area of the key candle of Point F. First of all, the big player is always interested in suggesting to traders that it is an upward or downward movement and then to drive the price in the opposite direction. This trade is usually done with a strong move up or down. Few traders are able to take this movement from the start, so you usually only start in the middle of this movement and set your stop according to your requirements. Since most traders enter the market with a market order, the big players can identify exactly in which area most traders have entered. Most stops that are worth running are located immediately, below or above this entrance. For this reason, stops are rarely above these key candles and show us very precisely where a possible trend reversal can begin.

With the identification of the key candles there are some challenges to be overcome. Different time units naturally show me different key candles. Not every strong movement is automatically a key candle, it essentially depends on what happened in the course of the course before. A key candle automatically results from the fact that it is a movement that nobody could have foreseen. In this case, the big player is not likely to find interesting stop zones above this key candle.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Based on the key candles, the price in the Forex market can unfortunately only roughly calculate a possible turnaround. There is no concrete information in the form of volume and liquidity that can only be obtained from the future market. Let's look at a small example from Friday between 2:30 p.m. and 4:00 p.m. CET. Around 14:30 CET we can see at point A and B that large sell market orders have been absorbed in the market. These were long trader stops that were fished. At the same time, some buy market orders were placed, which pushed the price up briefly. At Point C, strong sell limit orders ensured that Ask was absorbed, which ultimately slowed the price. Then the price was pushed further down. From points D and E we can see that larger buy market orders have entered the market. This could be partial sales of the dollar and the purchase of the euro. Since there was no strong absorption at that time, it was a nice opportunity for me to go long. The representation of the heat map, however, is somewhat inaccurate for me, because you cannot see at what price level how much solder was absorbed. Nevertheless, you have a rough overview of where it is worth taking a closer look. I have discovered an interesting way to make the specific limit orders visible in the market and am thus able to make even better trading decisions. It is true that market orders move the market, but limit orders determine where the market will go in the future. And precisely these limit orders cannot be identified.

That is exactly why we will deal more closely with these limit orders in the future. The big players are forced to collect larger portions of volume in order to generate an advantage. And this collection of volume takes place exclusively with limit orders. The advantage of these iceberg orders is that nobody can see them and there are no major market movements at the same time. In our new project 10 we will then discuss in detail how to identify them down to the smallest lot.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

On September 27, 2019 (Point A) I pointed out that the purple zone is a strong resistance.

At the moment we are in a very interesting resistance zone, which we want to take a closer look at. On April 24, 2017, the EURUSD had a large gap of 178.5 pip. This gap was exceptional because of its size. Basically, this gap is a major resistance for me, because it was a strong demand market, at the time it was created.

Here you can read the post again and find a very interesting auxiliary indicator.

EURUSD where is the journey going?

Of course, at that point in time, I couldn't know whether the price was closing the gap or not. But when the course was strongly rejected, I knew that this resistance zone could possibly work. In such a case, you can look for long trades in the medium term. Next you should identify the key candle. At point A, the price went up again strongly and formed a new high at point B. At first, the price went down unexpectedly sharply and then formed an equilibrium. Many assumed that the price would go up again and were surprised when the price continued to go down. In this yellow move at Point B, relatively few traders were short positioned, but enter the market later. Therefore, there was no reason to go beyond the high of point C because fewer stops were suspected there. A little tip. No matter what time unit you are in, simply look at the individual movements and first draw a possible stop area under each trend reversal. If a turnaround was caused by a strong up / down move, chances are that most traders only entered the market in the middle of that move. The big players will rarely look for stops under these key candles. A trend reversal could then occur within this key candle. However, you always have to see this, in the overall market context.

What is much more interesting, however, is the fact that the price has come back near the big gap. First of all, there is the possibility that the price in Zone D will go up again, but that gap (Point E) could also be closed. That would mean a price slide to at least 1.07300. Regardless of whether the gap will closed or not, the purple zone is initially a very strong resistance zone and could cause the price to move towards 1.25 again. But these are pure speculations that are not relevant at first. The decisive factor is how the course will behave in the next few weeks. Because of the Stophunting, a course always runs in ZigZag lines. We must always pay attention to the key candles that initiate a turnaround that simplifies our forecast for the coming days or weeks.

In my daily trading decision, it is always helpful to know whether we are in a medium-term upward or downward movement. Therefore, as a scalper, you should always keep an eye on the larger time units.

I wish you a great weekend

best regards

Michael

GPBUSD breakout

Hello cedars,

Welcome to our blog and thank you for your kind compliment. Unfortunately I cannot see which breakout it is because I am not trading the GPBUSD.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

First of all, we see that from 11:56 the price looks like it wants to go down. At 11:59 there is a Stopfishing, with the long traders stopped. In this moment sell market orders come in the market, which the big player intercepted via a buy limit order. Then the price was pushed up with market orders and the stops of the short traders (market buy) helped to push the price up. In order to move a price up, it is first necessary that sufficient sell limit orders are available. There are gaps in the upward movement of your chart, which indicates that no sell limit orders were available in this area. First the sell limit orders are eaten up and the price starts the next sell limit orders. If there are no sell limit orders at the next price level, the price level is skipped and a gap is created until if further sell limit orders are available at a higher price level. No purchases or sales can take place in these gaps because there is no liquidity. You can often not see that in the M1 chart. Gaps are created permanently in the market.

At that moment the buy limit orders move up, if there are prospective buyers. It is quite possible that the big player himself placed buy limit orders from 1.30600 in order to support his own price. Because if there was no liquidity, the price would go back completely. At 1.30850 there was either less liquidity or the big player did not use any further market orders. We see gaps again the first time we run down, so that there were not enough buyers with buy limit orders in this area.

Unfortunately, I cannot see at what time the Big Player bought Ask, because to make money he has to buy a certain number of Ask before the outbreak. If he had only pushed the price up without collecting Ask beforehand, he would probably have lost money. This means that the big player has already started collecting his ask from London open or earlier. For that, he should have known a few hours beforehand what would come out of the BOE press release. If the big player had been informed of the result a few minutes before the BOE press release, he probably wouldn't have had much time to collect enough Ask. I rather believe that the big player used the increased volatility to push up his previously collected ask. A very risky game, due to the lack of liquidity. With the right tools, you might be able, to determine where the exit of his position was.

It may also be quite possible that the big player already knew the result the day before. Although he could have prepared for it, he cannot predict how the market will respond. This means that he has to make the decision a few hours in advance whether to buy Ask or Bid. And if he don't have enough money, it can be a big risk. We can see that in many hedge funds that have perished in recent years. The fact is that the big players have better and faster information, like the retail traders, and whether it always helps them is a question that I cannot answer. I recommend to take a look at Stophunting a little, this could significantly increase your chances of winning. You can find the post here.

Key candles in Stophunting

I wish you continued success and I look forward if this blog helping you.

Greetings Michael

Cumulative delta

Hello dear subscribers,

First of all, thank you for your opinions on the subject of economic and trade data. Each trader obtains different information in order to build his trade on it and creates his own setup from it. This setup is tailored to everyone and can rarely be used profitably by another trader. In Formula 1, a racing driver can only be successful with his personal setup because it is tailored to him. For this reason, every trader is right from his point of view if he is profitable with his setup. In this blog you will find different ideas in the forex and futures market to create an individual setup. Supply and demand, COT, currency strength, volume profile, footprint, ask and bid, volume, liquidity, delta, DOM, times and sales list, indicators and heat map are presented and analyzed. There are traders who are with futures data and other traders who are successful with pure forex data. It is tiring to discuss what is best for another because every retailer is different. Everyone is responsible for themselves in this market, but should always accept the opinion of other traders. Of course, you can express your opinion, but discussions usually don't lead to anything. This blog focuses in the current project No. 9 on the Stophunting with Forex data and afterwards in the Project No. 10 we will analyze the Stophunting with futures data. Those who feel like it are welcome to participate in this project. If you prefer another way, you will definitely find your home in the countless great and informative threads from FF, which will take you further or you can create your own thread.

In addition to our current project Stophunting, I am currently analyzing the different strategies of the big players for our project No.10. A very interesting area is the fact that the big players sometimes provide themselves with liquidity in order to acquire a large number of volumes. I will show some examples of this. In addition, I noticed that there is a cumulative delta in the area of future data, but no cumulative ask and bid. There is currently no indicator for this. My prop software only works with C #, and I'm curious to see if I can develop this indicator. In principle, this is not a correct indicator at all, since the volume and the price are an integral part of the real-time data of the exchange and, unlike indicators, do not have to be offset.

If I open a long position in EURUSD I buy the Euro (Ask), as soon as I get out of the position I sell the Euro (Bid). If I take a short position, I buy the dollar (bid), as soon as I get out I sell the dollar (ask). So Ask stands for buying euros or selling dollars, and Bid stands for buying dollars and selling euros. In the delta, the number of questions is first subtracted from the number of bids. This display can be set for a specific time unit or viewed cumulatively. If the accumulated delta suddenly falls in an upward trend, it means that more was traded on the bid. This is an indication that either traders have taken their profits with them or short traders have bought the dollar because they are hoping for a reset or a turnaround. Divergences are predominantly used in the Cumlative Delta. However, it is more interesting to see how the respective cumulative ask or cumulative bid relates to each other. This makes it even easier to analyze possible profit taking. In the cumulative delta, you can only see that the value falls. But if the cumulative ask continues to rise, this could be an indication that it is only profit-taking. This would allow a more efficient way of looking at things. However, it will take a while, but of course I will keep you up to date.

I wish you a successful trading week

best regards

Michael

Key candle Stophunting II

Hello dear subscribers,

Today I would like to take a closer look at the key candles that play a decisive role in stophunting.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

We see an equilibrium just before Point A, and many traders thought that the price could continue to move upwards. Then at Point A there was an immediate downward movement. Few people expected this movement, so there was no reason for the big player to look for possible stops above point B. After that, the price went down and strong resistance developed at the low. There, many assumed that the price could now go up again. At Point C there was again a strong downward movement, which was another reason for the big players not to look for stops in the first half of this movement, so the upward trend ended at Point D. At Point E there was again a strong one Movement down, for which the big players again have no reason to look for stops above Point F. After that, a sideways market formed and the movement at Point G was very strong again. That was initially the reason why the upward trend ran to Point H. With the future data you can always see very well at the crucial points how many traders are stopped in the opposite trend.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

The course of the last 24 hours shows some nice examples. At Point A, around 6 p.m. on Wednesday, there was a strong downward movement where many traders assumed the price would go up again. For this reason, the course at point G and I was not pushed over point A because there were not many stops to be expected there. After an equilibrium, there was a strong downward movement at point B. No further stops were needed via Point D because they were needed for the upward trend. Point C and E once again formed a strong resistance zone that could not be broken. Then the course went up again. At Point F we came to the resistance zone of the equilibrium at Point B. Many hoped for a further downward trend. A strong upward movement broke through this resistance zone and a new key candle was formed. There was a stronger return at the high of point G, which did not have to be overcome with point I, since there were no further decisive stops there. Then the course ran to Point J. Points C, E and J formed a strong resistance zone, where many suspected that the course could go up again. He did that for a short moment, but then there was a strong downward movement and a new key candle was formed. With the upward movement from point L to point M, the big players did not have to look for any further stops above point K because few traders were involved in this downward movement. In the further downward movement there was another key candle at Point P, which was not overcome in the subsequent upward trend.

A key candle doesn't always have to be a strong move, but it should unexpectedly run in an opposite direction that most merchants didn't expect. If this movement then breaks through a certain important resistance zone, one could mark it as a key candle. To train these key candles, I recommend working with an M5 or M15 chart. First choose a currency pair whose exchange rate you do not know and go back in time. You can now draw your key candles using HH and LL as well as typical resistance zones. If you then scroll forward, you can immediately see whether you were right or not. If you were wrong, try to find out why they couldn't see it or switch to a different unit of time. Of course, this will not always work, but it is a small support that can often help you. You should note that the resistance zones are usually created by the big players and you should always ask yourself what the big players are trying to achieve. The moment you think like the big players, you are a decisive step ahead. Of course you can not get the crucial information in the Forex market, we will deal with this in detail in our new project number 10.

I wish you a successful trading day tomorrow

best regards

Michael

Efficient currency pair

[quote=Sesamstrasse;12758114]{quote} Good morning Michael. Incredible what a valuable informations you are posting in your thread.

Hello Guido,

Thank you for the great compliment, I am very happy that the informations help you. I have been dealing intensively with my prop software and the stock exchange data for 1 year now and have come across very interesting aspects that we will discuss in more detail in our next project no.10. The big players work with different strategies, but with the right presentation of the stock market data, they become more and more predictable for me. The problem is that many traders deal with the volume profile, footprint charts and market orders, but one cannot identify the big players with that. So I think the next project will be one of the most important projects on this blog.

I find your question about the currency pairs very interesting, so I created a few slides for you. Basically, I only trade the EURUSD in the Forex market because it contains the greatest liquidity and is over 100 times larger than the Euro FX in the future market. A high level of liquidity in a currency pair often means a slightly lower volatility, but also a high level of stability in the event of a drawdown. First, let's take a look at how I determined my optimal currency pair.

Explanation: I have taken over the following division of the currency pairs major / minor from my broker. Every broker seems to classify this differently, because for me the AUSUSD is more of a major than a minor. For this reason, we should not bother about it.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Under Point A, I listed the main currency pairs and entered the average spread in all volatility phases that my broker calculated. In addition, I determined the average ATR of the last 3000 candles in the M1. This gives the average seconds it takes for a trade to run into profit. In the case of the EURUSD, this is exactly 25 seconds. The CADCHF currency pair, which was the most ineffective for me, took 108 seconds, over eight times as long as the EURUSD, to run into profit.

At Point B I calculated the most important minors. The GBPAUD takes an average of 28.5 seconds to run into profit and could well keep up with the EURUSD. The most ineffective currency pair AUDNZD even needs 138.5 seconds to run into profit.

At Point C I looked at how much loss the major currency pairs make within 1 minute. Here, too, the EURUSD is at the forefront. The GBPCAD loses four times as much as the EURUSD in 1 minute.

At Point D we see that the AUDUSD can certainly keep up with the EURUSD. The GBPNZD loses 9.2 pip in 1 minute, almost six times more than the AUDUSD.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

This resulted in a kind of ranking list, at Point A I determined how long a currency pair needed to run into profit, at Point B how high the losses were after 1 minute. The EURUSD and AUDUSD perform best here.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Now I have created a ranking of all currency pairs, looking at how high the losses and profits are within 3 minutes. This gave rise to a probability of winning. Let's take a closer look at the EURUSD. In 3 minutes you lose about 4.1 pip in EURUSD. This is made up of the spread of 0.5 pip and an ATR of 1.2 pip per minute. In the case of a win, you get 3 × 1.2 pip / minute and you have to deduct the spread from it. The result is 3.1 pip. To trade efficiently, I need at least a 56.9% chance of winning. In the case of the AUDNZD, you need a probability of winning 88.5% to act profitably, that is almost impossible.

At first glance, the first three currency pairs EURUSD, GBPAUD and AUDUSD seem lucrative. The problem is that GBPAUD is a minor currency that sometimes has very high drowdowns. If you can live with it, the GBPAUD is a good choice because you can earn three times more in the same time as in the EURUSD. For this reason, alongside the EURUSD, the GBPAUD would be the only alternative. What speaks against it is the lower liquidity in GBPAUD, which leads to larger drowdowns and uncontrolled swings. That's why the EURUSD is one of the safest currencies in the exchange market for me.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Here I have now compared the most efficient and the worst currency pair. There are 20 trades in 3 minutes with a 50% chance of winning. In EURUSD you will lose -10 pip, while with AUDNZD you will lose -60 pip. That is a difference of -50 pip and a loss six times as high. So we see how important it is to find the right currency pair. The numbers and rankings of course change depending on volatility and spread. Therefore, I recommend every trader an individual calculation.

Compared to many currency pairs, the EURUSD is a rather slower contemporary, but it is most likely to make the most efficient gains. Of course, sometimes you want more movement in EURUSD, which is why I prefer the downward trends because they run 30-40% faster than the upward trends. Overall, I have found my optimal currency with the EURUSD and can set up my eight screens exclusively for this currency pair. This means I have all the important information at a glance without having to switch the view over time and can only concentrate on the market and my trade. I would never trade with a cell phone because I simply lack the crucial information from the stock market.

I hope that I was able to answer your question in detail and look forward to a great cooperation in this blog.

best regards

Michael

Open gap in Euro FX

The fact is that the big players use iceberg orders to collect, which are not visible in the form of limit orders or are very difficult to identify. These collection campaigns often take a few days, so time is always on our side.

Now let's take a look at what happened afterwards.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Let's start at point A. On February 7, 2020, a few 1000 lot sell limit orders were already collected in the zone shown. On Monday, February 10, 2020, the price was pushed up again and further sell limit orders were collected. At price level A, a total of 5,259 lots was created in the area of sell limit orders. On Wednesday, February 12, 2020, further sell limit orders in this price level were collected, in total there were over 10,111 lots in the delta. In addition, the course at Point D managed to walk a bit into the open gap. Monday was a typical gathering day, at Point E a delta of 4,120 sell limit orders was reached. In total, a sell limit delta of 7,662 lots was formed at price level F. Tuesday started with a small positive gap, but it was no longer able to enter price level F. After that, the course ran into the open gap to Point G. The stronger green lines, down the course, are largely exits from the dollar. In order to push the price down further, further sell limit orders would have to be collected, so we should take a closer look today. Another equilibrium could possibly be formed to collect further sell limits and then drive the price deeper into the open gap. In the chart we can also see that there were some exits before Point F and a larger exits before Point G. However, there should still be many 1000 sell limits to push the price further down. We can tell from the limit orders, whether the price is now recovering or an equilibrium is forming. Therefore, it is always crucial to pay attention to the current market situation.

1 volume chart

Hello extjsjquery,

First of all, I hope I understand your question correctly. With my software can display almost all different charts.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

I once created for you (Point A) a 1 volume chart in Euro FX. The problem is, that the chart can only represent 1 volume, if only 1 volume comes in. The exact definition of a volume is the result of Bid plus Ask. Not to be confused with the delta volume that means ask minus bid. At Point B you can see the smart tape, there you can see all non-cumulative market sell orders, filtered from minimum 20 lots. The cumulated market sell orders are listed next to it. Today at 08:21 CET (Point C) a market sell order of 120 lots came into the market, at 10:12 (Point D) a market sell order of 80 lots came into the market. These non-cumulative orders are also shown in a 1 volume chart with 120 lots or 80 lots. So it would make no sense to use a 1 volume chart since most orders are larger than 1 lot.

A 1-tick chart is much more efficient, because 1 tick means a trading transaction. This allows you to quickly find out how much solder an individual trading participant has given up. Under Point E you can see the different ways to create a chart. The corresponding numbers can be changed from 1 to infinity. The charts can be displayed for all available futures. The volume in the future is not comparable to the volume in forex, since the volume in forex is generated from the ticks, while the future volume is derived from bid and ask.

On the topic of volume, you will find very detailed articles in this blog from August 15, 2019, which will certainly help you.

How important is the volume?

I hope I could help you a little and wish you a successful trading day.

best regards

Michael

Problems for the big players?

Hello dear subscribers,

Before we take a closer look at limit orders in our next project, I would like to take a closer look at a big player that I admire very much. Goldman Sachs is one of the best and most professional traders in the world in my eyes. In the past 20 years, this group of traders has achieved above-average results. I have reported about this several times in the past. In the last few days, I have looked a little closer to Goldman Sachs' numbers and worked out a few interesting points. The detailed business data of Goldman Sachs can be found here:

Goldman Sachs Group Inc (GS) SEC Filing 10-K Annual report

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

I used the numbers to create a table for you that lists Goldman Sachs' last ten years in sales. At Point A we see the gains or losses Goldman Sachs made on different trading days. The green fields show the positive trading days, the red fields show the negative trading days within a year. At Point B I have averaged the past ten years.

Point C

On average, Goldman Sachs completed 253 trading days per year, including 221 trading days in profit and 31 trading days in loss.

Point D

Profits were made on 87.6% of all trading days, which I think is an excellent achievement. At first glance, you might think that Goldman Sachs is doing well. However, that is only half the truth. Because what counts is what you earn on these positive trading days (87.6%). For this, I have created a calculation that can deviate significantly from the realistic numbers, as these are only approximate values.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

At point A, I first took an average to create a calculation. The annual reports use $ 25 million increments, so I used the average here. At Point B I also assumed this mean for the losses. At point C this results in the total profit and the losses that I calculated from point D for each year. This resulted in the total profit per day at Point D. At first glance, everything looks excellent.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Goldman Sachs generated approximately $ 51.3 million in earnings from 2010-2014 and $ 37.7 million per day from 2015-2019. This is actually a decrease of 26.5%. For such a professional company, this is already a significant decline. While the profit and loss days have not changed in the past 10 years, the daily profit has decreased significantly.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

In my article: "The new generation of traders" I have already estimated that the big players win around $ 400 million a day. With over $ 40 million in daily earnings, Goldman Sachs would have a 10% stake. Deutsche Bank and other major banks would share the remaining 90% and there are certainly bigger big players than Goldman Sachs. Nevertheless, Goldman Sachs was able to prove over 20 years that they are among the most profitable players, for me it was crucial how Goldman Sachs has work in the past decade.

You can find my contribution here:

The new generation of traders

The big question is why has Goldman Sachs made 26.5% less money a day over the past five years than from 2010-2014? On the one hand, it is certainly due to the high-frequency traders, who make the big player's life more difficult, and the institutional traders, who can access ever better technology with optimized algorithms. Another reason could be the other big players e.g. Deutsche Bank who manage to act more efficiently. In addition, I also believe that there are more retail traders today who work with significantly better profit rates than 10 years ago. The reason is better data feeds and a deeper insight into the markets. Brokers are also interested in keeping their customers long-term and provide their customers with better information today than they did a few years ago.

Of course, we cannot determine exactly why the market for a large player like Goldman Sachs has become more difficult than it was five years ago. We definitely notice that spending on analysts and high-quality technology no longer offers the big advantage. On the other hand, this could also be an opportunity for the professional retail traders who are active in the market.

Now one could assume that if the market gets heavier for a big player, it actually also has to automatically become harder for retail traders. This claim needs to be differentiated because the trading strategies of big players and retail traders differ significantly from one another. If a retail trailer has chosen a certain price level at which it would like to get started, this is immediately possible. An exit can also take place immediately. A big player may have to collect a certain number of Bid or Ask over a few days and then push it in a certain direction. Even getting out takes some time and cannot even done immediately. Of course, the big player can move the market because of his large capital, but there are other big players who have to represent the interests of their customers. This often leads to conflicts of interest that can mean millions of dollars in losses. In addition, a big player is exposed to a risk of loss much longer, since it takes significantly longer to enter and exit as for the retail trader. Last week, the big players bought a large number of sell limit orders to push the price further into the open gap. Unfortunately, many retailers and institutional traders jumped on the bandwagon at the same time. The big players had to create a new plan last Thursday, sold their positions to retail traders and institutional traders, and then pushed the price up. As we can see, collecting bid and ask is becoming an increasing problem for big players.

We retail traders can take advantage of this disadvantage of big players. We can enter and exit the market almost at any time. To make the right trading decisions, we only need the right tools and the right market view. The question is always how to use these options. We will never get the full view, but we learn from our mistakes and get better every day. In the next few weeks, we will be dealing with an interesting market analysis, that I have never seen anywhere else. I am convinced that this could be another milestone on our blog.

I wish you a successful trading week

best regards

Michael

Goldman Sachs

[quote=Dcrs;12772769]{quote} Very nice Michael

Hello Dcrs,

First of all, thank you for your kind feedback. This report on Goldman Sachs was created by accident because I have not been able to understand some situations in the last 4 days in EURUSD. That is why I again dealt with the question of how the big players operate in the market. In doing so, I rediscovered the K10 reports of the past 10 years and roughly readed the 2000 page annual report. From this information my last post about Goldman Sachs arose. To learn how the market works, we need to understand how big players work.

The challenge is that the big players fly an airplane while the retail traders are driving a car. When a pilot tries to explain to a driver how to control an airplane, the driver is overwhelmed. The way big players and retail traders work differs significantly in how they work. The volume chart, the footprint charts and the market profile are exclusively geared towards market orders, even the DOM and the time and sales list almost only provide specific information about the orders that move the market. This may be an advantage in the short term, but in the medium and long term only the limit orders determine the direction in the market. And it is precisely this approach that is not provided for in almost all trading instruments. We retail traders try to track down the big players' planes with a car navigation system. There are streets in the sky, but we cannot find the big players with the market orders because they only place iceberg orders in the accumulation and distribution phases. And these limit orders are almost impossible to locate. That's why volume charts, footprint charts and the market profile don't really help. But I have found a solution, so we have to look more closely at the individual order types. In the past few weeks, I have already developed a few records and strategies that I still have to formulate. It is just a new way of looking at the markets, it is not a system, but a way to improve your setup. It is interesting that we cannot do without the forex data, since they have an indispensable advantage over the futures data.

The combination of futures and forex data, when viewed correctly, gives a concrete view of the markets that has not previously been considered. While the volume trader has felt an advantage in recent years, my long-term approach is exactly the opposite. If you want to follow the big player, you have to act exactly like the big player. Anyone who tries this only by looking at market orders will not get anywhere.

I hope we can start our new project at the end of this week.

I wish you a successful trading week

best regards

Michael

We will now take a closer look at why the price went down after.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

For this reason, no one would have absorbed so many buy market orders at this moment. So how was that possible?

At point B, the big player started to dissolve his buy market order, the price went down and triggered some stops of the long traders. Own liquidity for the big players

Hello dear subscribers,

In my last post I reported over another strategy of the big players, as I have noticed more and more in recent weeks that the big players are increasingly making volume available to themselves.

36 pip move in EURUSD

First, let's take a look at what exactly happened yesterday.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Yesterday around 10:00 CET at Point A a delta in the sell limit area of 2658 lot was created. A big player put round 2000 Lot Market Buy on the market, which he also absorbed with his own limit sell orders. At the moment, the market saw only the strong buy market orders that came into the market, so many go long . The market has been pushed down and an equilibrium is forming at point B, where the big player may have left his short position. At point C buy limit orders came into the market and the price was pushed to point D. The same thing happened there as at Point A. The big player placing large buy market orders, which he also absorbed with his own sell limit orders. The market of course saw this too and wanted to do it right this time so as not to be stopped again. Many position themselves short here. Overall, a delta in the sell limit range of 2404 lots was created at the same price level. Then the price was pushed up.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Here you can see the data from the future market, in the area of the limit order. The strong delta was created at point A and the price was pushed to point B. There you can see that the stronger orders for limit orders entered the market. Then the price was pushed to Point C where the big players again made available liquidity and a large sell limit delta was created. Basically, I cannot yet say exactly which positions are still open and which have been closed, because this strategy is too new for me. First of all, it is important that we are able to recognize when a big player is making liquidity available to itself.

In my last posts I described the differences between big players and retail traders in the area of their actions.

Follow Smart Money !!!

The only disadvantage that big players have is the fact that they cannot immediately enter the market with large positions because there is simply not enough volume and liquidity. As a rule, they have always used the equilibrium to build up their position and had to wait for ECB or FED meetings to push the price up or down in an increased volatility. So sometimes it took them days to build up their position and then realize their profits. On the one hand, this costs time and on the other hand, with your open positions, you are exposed to a certain risk compared to other big players. In my report on Goldman Sachs you can see that the daily sales figures have dropped by almost 30%. 30% less sales with the same risk is a significant factor for a large, successful company.

Problems for the big players?

I am convinced that the big players are currently trying out a new strategy in different currency pairs by making massive amounts of liquidity available to themselves. Basically, this approach is not new because it has been used time and time again, but this strategy has increased in recent weeks. I think the big players are looking for a solution to get liquidity faster.

In principle, this is initially a hegde if you absorb your market buy orders simultaneously with limit sell orders. The positions secure each other, but we must not forget the double costs involved. Of course, the big players do not have the same costs as a retail trader, but they are actually twice as high at this moment. Of course there is now the possibility to first push the price up and get out of the market buy orders on the high. After that, the price could be pushed down to exit the limit sell orders on the low. One risk that arises is that if you exit your market buy orders on the high, you are still in loss, as the limit sell positions are still open and double spread fees have to be taken into account. If the big player then does not manage to push the price down, he automatically runs into loss.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Now let's look at a few other options.

Point A

2000 Lot Market Buy Orders will be absorbed by 2000 Lot Limit Sell Orders. The big player tries to exit his limit sell orders at a loss, whereby the dissolution of these orders could help him push the price up. The strong market buy orders are perceived in the future market.

Point B

2000 Lot Market Buy Orders will be absorbed by 2000 Lot Limit Sell Orders. The big player tries to get out of his market buy orders at a loss, whereby the dissolution of these orders could help him to push the price down. The strong market buy orders are perceived in the future market.

Point C

2000 Lot Market Sell Orders will be absorbed by 2000 Lot Limit buy orders. The big player tries to exit his market sell orders at a loss, whereby the dissolution of these orders could help him push the price up. The strong market sell orders are perceived in the future market.

Point D

2000 Lot Market Sell Orders will be absorbed by 2000 Lot Limit buy orders. The big player tries to exit his limit buy orders at a loss, whereby the dissolution of these orders could help him to push the price down. The strong market sell orders are perceived in the future market.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

I am convinced that this approach is a kind of experiment that the big players conduct to check whether it is worthwhile to provide liquidity or volume themselves. Basically, I think that a hedge makes sense to hedge positions, but I am still very critical as to whether it can be used to develop a profitable strategy. The big player would definitely have a time advantage, since he is able to create liquidity on the market faster. This contrasts with the risk of two positions and twice the cost. I believe that the big players will examine and evaluate this more intensively in the coming weeks and months. The trading range may decrease somewhat if the big player initially leaves both positions open.

First of all, this approach is new and somewhat unusual for me, but it creates a little more movement in the market. A major disadvantage that the big players have not yet noticed: If they provide themselves with liquidity at one price level, this is noticeable in the market. In the past, they were able to collect iceberg orders in the accumulation or distribution phase without the majority noticing. If you now make your own liquidity available, they will come out of the darkness and everyone can see them. With the right tools, it's only a matter of time before one know exactly what you're going to do next. Big players may find a way to make even faster profits , but they are also more predictable. For the successful retail traders, this means a significantly higher probability of winning.

The crucial question we have to ask ourselves: Why does a big player change his strategy? The answer is very simple: Because he is no longer so successful with his previous strategy. If his strategy were successful, he wouldn't change it. That means the big players have bigger problems than they did a few years ago. In this respect, they have a great need to act to increase their daily profits again. This change in strategy shows that they are no longer as successful as they were a few years ago and are looking for a solution. On the other hand, if they don't win as much anymore, that means that retail traders don't lose as much anymore. It is basically a positive aspect, it shows that the retail traders are on the right track.

I noticed that my approach in the past 12 months,  I have come a lot closer to the big players. The price and trends can be calculated much more clearly and efficiently, and breakouts are easier to predict if you know what the big players bought before. You will never get a 100% market view, with the right money management and setup 50% is enough. Every percent that can be improved has a direct impact on profits. I hope that by the weekend I will be able to start our new project number 10, where we will deal with exactly these things.

I wish you a successful trading week

best regards

Michael

Big player experiment "own liquidity"

Hello dear subscribers,

In my last post I wrote about the experimentation of big players on how to make liquidity available to themselves. Tuesday once again showed this impressively. After the course on Wednesday, I have a rough idea how it could have happened the day before yesterday. First of all, I think that two big players have teamed up to do this joint experiment.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

At Point A yesterday on Tuesday 10:00 CET, 2000 market buy orders were absorbed by 2000 limit sell orders. Then the price was pushed down over 50 ticks. At Point B, the big players might have left their dollar position with 2000 limit buy orders. In the area of point C, the big players could have collected around 500 lot buy limit orders again, after which they pushed the price up. At Point D they played the same game again around 5:00 CET. Again, 2000 market buy orders were absorbed by 2000 limit sell orders. The majority of the market has assumed that it will go short again, the same as at 10:00 CET in the morning. The two big players take advantage of this and push the course very quickly and massively higher. At Point E, they placed 4500 Limits Sell in the market and got out of the euro. At that point the market was very bullish and you can see from the candle at Point F that there were enough buy market orders to service the large limit sell order. Of course, the limit sell orders was activated at different price levels so as not to deter long traders. Then the big players bought another 500 limit sell orders and pushed the market down to point G. There they gradually released their still open dollar positions. Then they was complitly out of market.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

The entire experiment would have made a profit of over $ 2 million in the Future Market, but the number of lots in the Forex Market is approximately 100 times larger. That would mean that the two big players would have earned over $ 100 million each with this experiment. Now one might have to deduct the costs and assume that they could not entirely resolve their last position in profit. In order to push the price up and down, however, they also had to bring further market orders into the market, which of course also made a profit. I did not take these profits into account. $ 100 million a day profit is an interesting amount considering Goldman Sachs only earns about $ 33 million a day. If Goldman Sachs was involved in this experiment, you would have tripled your earnings in a day. This would not have been possible that quickly with the available liquidity on the market. However, since the big players provided themselves with liquidity, this was still possible in this case. This day was probably so positive because there was relatively little liquidity in the market at the time. However, the risk could increase dramatically if there is more liquidity in the market. Then the course could quickly move strongly in another direction. As long as the big player has a short and long position in the market, the risk is technically manageable, but it becomes problematic when he has dissolved a position and the market moves strong against him.

Basically, I find this procedure very interesting, exciting and easier to calculate than if you had to collect for a long time. The market movements are smaller, faster, and more manageable. With the right tools, the situation can be grasped quickly and effectively and it is relatively easy to act on the move. In addition, the range is calculable and you can easily see when the big player gets out of his position. As soon as he is out of one position, we know that he still has an open position. In order to close them or bring them to profit, he has to drive the course in the opposite direction again. So we know when a course is going in a certain direction and how far it has to run. I'm curious if this experiment will be included as a future strategy among the big players. If so, we will be able to significantly improve our chances of winning.

The big players have been trading in the forex market for over 20 years, pay billions of dollars for analysts, traders and algorithms and should therefore know the market very well. The fact that they have suffered considerable losses in the area of their profits in the past 5 years shows a lack of creativity in their approach. They are now trying to correct these losses because shareholders continue to expect dividends and an increase in the value of the company. In addition, some banks have achieved up to 60% of their total profits in the stock exchange area. Now they are trying to eliminate their weak point (lengthy collecting at a price level) by providing themselves with liquidity. Of course they will adapt their new strategies, but the “own liquidity” experiment is easier for us to act than if we have to wait for days until the big player has collected his positions. Another advantage is that very few traders know this strategy and can act. Should this procedure prevail among the big players, we only have to scan the individual markets for these situations and enter the market as soon as the big player has dissolved his first position. But that would probably be too good to be true.

I wish you a successful trading day

best regards

Michael

The Big Player bag of tricks

Hello dear subscribers,

Today, the market was once again very interesting and volatile, and the big players gave me the opportunity to discover another strategy. We want to take a closer look at that.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

From 07:00 CET to 10:00 CET I was a bit lucky and was able to do some long trades. At lunchtime we were already 60 pip above the open and at first I wasn't sure if it could further go up. From 10:00 CET there was a three-hour equilibrium at Point A. I saw that the big players placed buy limit orders in the market. That was a nice confirmation, for an upward movement. My exit was at point B, because I saw that the big player started to get out.

The strategy of the big player was again like textbook. At Point A, massive buy limit orders were initially placed in the equilibrium. After completing its collection campaign, the course was pushed up. The respective downward movements in the market were used to bring further buy limit orders into the market. Now there are two things to consider. First, the big player collects a large number of buy limit orders within an equilibrium. In order to push the price up, the big player must buy market orders. That means on the way from A to B he buy a lot of Ask. For this reason, the big player has already started to exit at Point B.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

We can see that again in the heatmap. At Point A we see that sell limit orders of over 400 lots have been waiting for execution, but were not touched at first. First the long traders were stopped again and then the price went to point B. There the big player started to dissolve his euro positions. He has to be very careful, because if he had dissolved all of his position, the price would have run massively down. Therefore, such an exit must be done very strategically.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

The price continued to rise and we can see at points A and B that the big player used the stops of the short traders to get out of a position. At Point C, we see that he has put very strong sell limit orders in the queue, which have not picked up. This means that the big player still had a few euro positions that he could not sell to date.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Now the market started to run down and the big player still had some open euro positions. For this situation he used a very interesting trick. At Point A, we see how the big player, when walking down the course, instructed his algorithms at ten price levels to put strong sell limit orders in the DOM queue. The reason for this was simple: the one who placed the order first is always served first.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

The price continued down to point B. At point C, the big player pushed the price up sharply in his sell limit orders. With these sell limit orders he took over his still open euro position. I think it should have been around 1500 lots. He was now out of his euro position and had 1,500 lot sell limit orders on the other side. That was a smart move, because in the downward course he would hardly have found anyone to buy the euro from him. So he bought the euro himself with his limit orders and thus also bought a bid. Since the market was already running down strongly, its position was optimally aligned.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Here we see again how the price was pushed up and the big player with sell limit orders took over his euro position in small pieces. After that, the price continued to go down. Now the big player only had to get out of his dollar position and he solved that quite easily

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

The price initially went down more sharply and we see at point A that the big player immediately got out of his dollar position. As a result, the price has risen very sharply. The big player was out of all positions and actually did everything right.

Of course, I can only guess whether all of this really happened based on my information and my personal opinion. Nevertheless, it is very exciting to watch the big players at work. Unfortunately, we retailers don't have enough money to use these strategies for ourselves. But we have the chance to study their strategies and to get information based on their reactions that significantly increase our probability of winning. And after all, that's a little ray of hope.

I wish you a successful trading day tomorrow

best regards Michael
