Herd behavior in the market

Fast movements in the market are often reactions of the big players to the herd. This triggers stops that further accelerate the course. If these stops are absorbed by big players at individual price levels, one should be careful. That over 90% of retail traders lose clearly shows that the opposite of what most expect always happens. Unfortunately, many traders are fooled by strong price movements. They always get on at the end of the movement and are eventually stopped, even though the direction was correct. The stop placement should also be reconsidered. Those, who do not place their stops with the herd, have the greatest chance of survival. And where are stops placed? Always below the last low and above the last high.

Many years ago, my opposite trades were successful in the upward and downward movements. This was successful because no one else dared to do it at the time. The stock exchange wisdom: The Trend is your friend has contributed to the fact that only a few have taken a short position in an upward trend.

You are always most successful if you stay away from the herd. In the animal area too, the herd offers only supposed protection. A large herd with many watchful animals reduces the likelihood of the individual animal being caught by a predator because more animals can look for predators while others are at rest looking for food. The presence of many bodies in a group enables a reduction in individual predator risk by simple dilution. The more gazelles in a flock, the greater the likelihood not to be caught by the lion. But a herd of gazelles is easier to spot by lions than a single animal. The gazelle could probably survive longer if it were not in the herd. Therefore separate yourself from the herd and act where few people act. The big players would not be so successful if traders developed more individually and did not develop joint herd strategies in groups.

If 3000 traders pursue the same strategy at the same time, the big players know that statistically 30% of them trade in EURUSD. 1000 traders use similar stop zones, which are safe zones for the big players in order to achieve fast volume. Evaluation of the big player experiments

Hello dear subscribers,

Twelve major big players influence 85% of the Forex market. That's why I've been focusing on these big players for years to better understand how they work. These big players don't work together , but they instantly see indirectly, what another big player is up to. This automatically results in synergies, which many market participants incorrectly interpret as agreements between the big players. It is not a big power that is up against retail traders, the big players have a similar approach and can immediately see what another big player is up to. In my view, no platform for conspiracy theories. At the beginning of February we noticed that the big players are increasingly making their own liquidity available. Up until now, the big players always had to collect in an equilibrium ask or bid in order to push the course in the corresponding direction. The moment a big player himself makes liquidity available, he initially saves a lot of time, but at the same time has two open positions, which he has to bring to profit. There have been some experiments on this since the beginning of February, which I also reported in detail on my blog. You can find the information here.

Own liquidity for the big players

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Here we see a typical situation where a big player provides himself with liquidity. We recognize that the market buy orders are absorbed exactly. These market orders are cumulative market orders that are typically triggered by stops. The first green circle may well be some stops of short trader. If other short traders had subsequently entered the market at this price level, they would very likely have placed their stop above this price level. A big player would never use cumulative market orders to push a price up. Small market orders are used for this and the limit sell orders are deleted at the same time so that he can push the price up with little volume. Therefore, you can not assume that the green circles have been created to push the course massively upwards. This exact absorption can only take place if someone knows exactly that a certain size of market buy orders will come into the market at a certain point in time, at a certain price level. And only someone who executes these orders can know that.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

A few days ago, massive market buy orders suddenly entered the market that at first glance were not absorbed by the same big player. At first, we thought it was a big currency exchange. We had to quickly revise this opinion, since the next day, at a 60 pip higher price level, 1200 lot market sell orders were processed. The next idea I had was that two big players coordinated with each other. But larger volumes are easier to identify by the exchange regulator and the big players will not be so stupid to take such a risk. So how does a big player manage to place large market orders in the market and absorb them at the same time without being noticed? One possibility would be that he works with two different accounts and the algorithms are precisely tailored to these two accounts.

Yesterday around 3:00 p.m., massive market buy orders entered the market again. Then the price went down 100 pip. First of all, it is quite unusual for a big player to place such a large number of market orders on the market. To do this, we first have to consider the different types of orders.

Limit orders

With a limit order, the participant not only specifies the number of orders to be bought or sold, but also sets a price limit. This limit is the amount for which the participant is willing to buy or sell the specified orders. If the participant sets too low a limit for a buy order or too high a limit for a sell order, the order will not be matched. A limit order can be seen as a measure to reduce the likelihood of surprising, undesirable execution prices (price risk). A limit order is issued regularly if the intention is to buy or sell at a specified price, if possible at a better price. In contrast to a market order, an investor can never count on the fact that his order is actually taken into account in the market at the price he desires when a limit order is placed. He therefore runs the risk of going empty-handed or remaining on his inventory.

Market order

A market order is an order to buy or sell immediately at the best available price. It is executed based on the limit orders that are already in the order book. This means that market orders depend on the market liquidity to be settled. Since market orders are executed immediately, the market order corresponds to the best limit order available in the order book. In other words, when you create a market buy order, it corresponds to the best limit sell orders at the current price. However, if the cheapest limit sell order available is not enough to meet your entire market order, your order will automatically match the following limit sell orders until it is finally closed. This process is known as slippage and is the reason why you pay higher prices and higher fees for market orders compared to limit orders. Market orders come in handy in situations where getting your order done quickly is more important than getting a certain price. This means that you should only use market orders if you are in a hurry and willing to pay higher prices and fees

Iceberg orders

The iceberg orders are orders that are hidden behind the limit orders and disguise the actual size in the DoM. The average size of iceberg orders in the Euro FX is between 10-20 lots. Iceberg orders are used to achieve large price jumps with small market orders, to keep the price in equilibrium, to collect or get out unnoticed or to hold a price. At first glance, it seems to be very disadvantageous to work with market orders. Entry via limit orders is significantly cheaper and with the help of iceberg orders, the market does not know what the big player is up to. But the market orders also have unbeatable advantages in certain situations, which we will now take a closer look at.

Whenever I cannot understand exactly how big players operate, I always start with a concrete analysis to better understand the market. I started by comparing three different situations. This comparison results in a big player profitability, which has brought a very interesting result. Let's take a closer look at that.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

In the past, the big players collected Ask or Bid in an equilibrium and then pushed the course in the corresponding direction. Let's start with that.

At price level 1.1000, the Big Player collects 500 lot bids via limit sell orders (point A). Then he pushes the price down 60 ticks, whereby we have calculated 500 Lot Market Sell Orders (Point B). At price level 1.09700, he exits the dollar with limit buy orders. Then he collects 500 Lot Ask (Point C). Now he pushes the price up by 120 ticks and needs about 1000 Lot Market Buy Orders (Point D). At price level 1.10300, he exits the euro with 1500 lot limit sell orders. At the same time, he buys 500 lot bids. (Point E). With 500 Lot Market Sell Orders, he pushes the price down 60 ticks (Point F). Now he comes back to the price level of 1.1000 and sells his 1000 lot dollars with limit buy orders (point G).

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Point A

Here I have described the concrete process that took place in these three price movements.

Point B

The letters refer to the labels on the previous slide.

Point C

Here we see the resulting profits for the big player.

Of course, this calculation is to be seen purely hypothetically, since many other things must be taken into account in the actual course of the course. A price does not just run upwards, but is pushed down by the big player in the course of it in order to switch off the long traders and at the same time get new volume through stops of the new short traders. For this reason, I want to keep the calculation as simple as possible, using the same starting conditions for all three calculations.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

In principle, we see here almost the same process, with the only difference that the big player makes himself available liquidity in the beginning. First he pushes the price down and gets out of his dollar position. Then he pushes the course up at point D and then gets out of his euro positions. Then the price is pushed back to the price level of 1.1000. We have a situation here where the big player only provides liquidity once.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

The resulting calculations can be found here explicitly.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Here we have a slightly different situation, but the price developments in tick are the same. First of all, the big player again makes liquidity available and pushes the price down. There he gets out of his dollar position and pushes the price down to Point E. He gets out of the euro by making himself available liquidity. Then the price is pushed up 60 ticks again, where it finally gets out of his 3000 Lot Ask with iceberg orders.

Let us now take a closer look at this overall situation. At point A, the market sees a large number of market buy orders. Many market participants will assume that the price will now go up. The big player pushes the price down and uses the stops of the long traders to reach his goals faster. At the lower low, he gets out of his dollar position via iceberg orders, collects 500 Lot Ask from the short traders and then pushes the price up. At Point E, he immediately leaves the euro with 2500 lots by making himself available liquidity. The market now only shows 2500 Lot Market Buy orders. Traders see these large orders and know exactly what happened a few hours ago when large market buy orders came into the market. You take a short position and the big player uses the stops to push the market further up. The other traders who were initially waiting now see that the price is going up and start with a long position. Because the price is slowly going up, more long traders come in. The big player is now taking advantage of the situation and is selling his 3000 lot to the long traders who hope for a strong price increase.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

The resulting calculations from slide 7 can be found here explicitly.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Now we come to the overall calculation.

Normal procedure

The normal procedure (trading in equilibrium) requires a total volume of 7000 lots. Since the big player does not have its own volume available, the required market volume is also 7000 lots. The time required is 15 hours, with 467 lots being traded per hour. In total, the big player wins an amount of $ 1,312,500, so the profit per lot is $ 188. The hourly profit is $ 87,500.

Entry with own liquidity

With this procedure, a total of 10,000 lots are traded, less own liquidity of 2,000 lots, resulting in a required market volume of 8,000 lots. 370 lots are traded per hour in 27 hours and the total profit is $ 1,875,000. The profit per lot is $ 234 and the profit per hour is $ 69,444.

Entry and exit with own liquidity

A total of 14,000 lots are traded here, less 7000 lots of own liquidity, resulting in a required market volume of 7000 lots. In 23 hours, 609 lots are traded per hour and the profit is $ 2,812,500. That gives a win per lot of $ 402 and an hourly win of $ 122,283.

The problem of a big player is not his capital, because he has enough of it. The problem is the volume on the market that does not allow him to get the positions he wants. The key point in our comparison is the volume that the big player needs from the market. At Point A & C this market volume is comparable, at Point B more volume are required.

Point C is twice as efficient as Point B. The profit per hour at Point C is 40% higher than normal trading in equilibrium (Point A). The same market volume is required in both cases, although the total volume doubles. In 15 hours, the big player makes $ 1,312,500 from Equilibrium trading and $ 1,834,000 from Point C. This is twice as efficient as Point B. The procedure at Point C becomes more effective the more often the big player makes himself available liquidity for the exit. He can play this game as often as he likes within a long upward or downward trend and thus achieves significantly higher efficiency.

So we can clearly see that the use of market orders by the big players is a very interesting alternative that we could possibly see more often in the future. With this approach, the big players can confuse the market even more. This means they are indirectly able to compensate for weak volumes and at the same time save a lot of money because they no longer have to collect in the equilibrium. When collecting in the Equilibrium, the price has to be kept within a range, that costs a lot of time and money, which is partly eliminated by the procedure of Point C.

There are even more efficient approaches, but I don't want to publish them here in order not to unnecessarily support the big players. I'm curious how long it will take them to figure it out. This will probably not happen, however, because the big players have been on the market for many decades and I am surprised that the expensive analysts and software developers are program such strategies. But they will probably not change anything until they are forced to do it. Just like Goldman Sachs, which has reduced their daily income by 50% in recent years.

It doesn't really matter which strategies the big players pursue, whoever is deeply involved in this market will find out relatively quickly and thus has an enormous market advantage. The big players only change their strategies when their profits drop dramatically. Why should you change something that is still working? But we can already see from the experiments that have been carried out in the past few months that the big players have lost considerable revenue. The retail traders' approach is getting better and, at the same time, it is becoming increasingly difficult to take money from them. It is a kind of upgrade that is emerging in this market and I am convinced that with the new technology, that is available to retail traders today, the big players have to move quite a bit in order to continue to make good profits in the future.

We retail traders are on the right track, but we have to learn a lot every day and say goodbye to old habits. The market will be much heavier in the future and if you miss the opportunity now, you won't have a chance in a few years.

I compared different providers of stock market data, got closer to high-frequency trading and the big players and looked for suitable software that could be used to translate the stock market data according to my specifications. In recent years, I also completed my Oracle Certified Master in Java and programmed some auxiliary indicators for the MT4. You can download the most important ones today. I am currently using my programming knowledge to program C # filter settings for my stock exchange software. These filter settings help me identify algorithms.

A year ago, I met a friend who had worked for the world's largest radio frequency dealer for many years. Through him I got to know a completely new world that has nothing to do with an MT4 chart. The buy and sell offers are displayed on special screens every second. The trading platform does not correspond to our well-known principle of price-time priority. The basis is pauses in trading between 10-50 milliseconds and thus create uniform starting conditions. Just as there is always a fixed volume value in the tick chart, the pauses of 10-50 milliseconds are fixed there. A kind of microequilibrium. With this I recognized again how important the equilibrium is for a successful trade. The focus on the equilibrium is interesting because it shows the uncertainty of the market. From an equilibrium, it can only run up or down. The behavior of these big players is so brutal and merciless that I wanted to find out more about them. With the help of the stock exchange data, I got to know the relationships between the decisive algorithms.

The pure candles or price information gives us traders a wrong picture of the market, because a strong bullish candle does not necessarily mean that someone is buying the euro to push the price higher. Once a big player sells their dollars after a downtrend, a strong bullish candle can also emerge. However, this is not evident from the pure candlestick representation in the Forex. A price does not change because a moving average has been exceeded, an RSI is overbought or a fibozone has been reached, but because market orders fulfill the limit orders. The price is always the result of volume and liquidity, but this information is not available in Forex. The big players determine the market and pursue a specific goal and this can only be recognized if you know what they are up to. Many years ago I thought that I could use the candlestick chart to determine trends and resistance zones. Our brain is programmed to automatically identify patterns in random movements. We always identify random patterns. By carefully analyzing the futures data with my prop software, I came to the conclusion that there are actually no trends and no real resistance zones. The resistance zones we see are initiated by the big players to deceive us, and supposed trends are there to mislead retail traders. In fact, the big players don't pay attention to resistance zones at all, because they create these zones themselves.

Every market has its advantages and disadvantages. I was looking for similarities between forex data and futures data. The art is to use a combination of both dates to reduce the drawbacks and increase the benefits. I use the data from the future and forex market at the same time to get the fastest information. The future market offers the greatest chance of winning, the forex market the best profit distribution. Therefore, I act in the Forex market exclusively on the basis of the future data. I have already described this procedure in great detail in this blog.

The forex market has many advantages over the future market. The price movements are 5 times larger, which automatically increases the volatility. Therefore, the Forex market is much more sensitive, which means that the currency strength, the ATR, my developed Bionic candle and the strength of the different price movements provide more precise data. For this reason, I can not do without this data either. However, please note that my decisions to enter and exit are made solely on the basis of stock market data.

I made a very interesting observation that this indicator sometimes reacts faster than the price. The following situation: The red line of the dollar and the green line of the euro both fall slowly. So we are in balance. Suddenly the green line shoots up. This means that the euro is much stronger against the dollar. A bullish candle is created a few seconds later. I once tried to trade on it for fun. It worked a couple of times, but I strongly warn against it. This type of display takes some getting used to. If the green line is up and the red line is down, it means that we have a strength in the euro and a weakness in the dollar. That speaks for rising prices. If the red line is above and the green line is below, it means that we have strength in the dollar and weakness in the euro. That speaks for falling courses. Two different indicators are required for this display.

It is not the criticism because someone disagreed with me. It is often their questions that give me the material to think about it more specifically. To explain my thoughts, I often use pictorial language and try to make comparisons with everyday things in life. This in turn helps me to advance further developments. When you write things down, you have to think about them longer than when you explain them. However, I am not so arrogant to believe that my view reflects the correct presentation of the market. But the big players with their professional technology, their thousands of programmers and analysts will always lead the way and dominate the market. It will be impossible to catch up with them, but every millimeter that we come closer get brings us decisive trading advantages. These benefits, only come from more information, as the other 5 million retail traders have.

When you start trading as a beginner, it's all about losing as little money as possible. As a professional, it's all about losing less money than the other professionals. We often see traders making insanely high profits and we ask ourselves what we are doing wrong. We are not doing anything wrong. Earning profits is easy, the trick is to keep profits long-term. What we see is an illusory world, they are shown the profits, but never the losses. It's like on Facebook or Instagram. I have reached the peak of success in the business world. In the eyes of people, my life is a single success story. But apart from my work, I have had little joy in my life. Ultimately, my wealth is only a factor in life that I've got used to. The moment I lie in a bed and look back at my life so far, I understand that all the appreciation and wealth that I was so proud of have lost value in the face of my impending death. I can't take the wealth I've accumulated over the course of my life with me. What I can take with me, however, are memories that are based on love and were created with love. Maybe you can afford a chauffeur who will drive the car for you. Or you can afford employees who will earn the money for you. But nobody will be able to endure all your illnesses for you. You have to do it all by yourself. Material values and things that we have lost can be found again. But there is one thing, if it is lost, it cannot be found - and that is life.

I don't know if this letter was actually written by Steve Jobs, but everyone can learn something from it.

I would like to thank all subscribers once again; for your questions, for your criticism, for your ideas, for your support and for your praise.

Fast and furious

Hello dear subscriber,

When I opened my blog at Forex Factory 28 months ago, I chose the name Bionics. Bionics is based on the assumption that living nature develops optimized structures and processes from which humans can learn from their evolutionary course. The earth is almost 4.5 billion years old and during this time nature has developed incredible things that people already benefit from today. A well-known example of this is Leonardo da Vinci's idea of transferring bird flight to flying machines. An example from modern life is the Velcro inspired by Velcro or think of dragonflies and the helicopter. The lotus effect was also brought into our lives by nature, things that clean themselves because no dirt sticks to them. Bionics are research and development approaches that pursue a technical application interest and use knowledge from the analysis of living systems in the search for problem solutions, inventions and innovations and transfer this knowledge to technical systems. The idea of the transfer from biology to technology is the central element of bionics. Anyone looking for a new innovation should steal from nature.

Nature has already developed everything in 4.5 billion years, we humans have not yet discovered it. In nature we find vaccines or cures for diseases that we do not know yet. We will know in the next 1000 years whether nature can be transferred to stock exchange prices. In any case, certain natural laws apply from which we can learn. For many years I have been trading relatively risk-free, short movements within an equilibrium (accumulation and distribution phases) where the big players have collected bid or ask. In these phases, the big players are tame like a sleeping lion. Due to changing market conditions, the big players began to make liquidity available to themselves. This enables them to save the accumulation and distribution phases and at the same time to earn money faster. You can find a report here.

Evaluation of the big player experiments

My trading approach uses only proprietary approaches, because in my view the market is much more complex than many market participants think. A sustainable strategy has not been developed in the past 600 years, so I use my creativity to develop my own trading advantages. I am strongly oriented towards the big players, which influence 85% of the market. Today I would like to present you another creative idea with which I am already working very successfully and with which no one has yet worked. However, this idea sounds completely crazy at first.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

You sit intently in front of your trading screen and wait for the right opportunity to get started. Suddenly our eyes register an opportunity, the nerves send the information to our brain, which in turn controls our hands to make the corresponding trade. We press the Buy button and our computer sends the order over the Internet to our broker, who opens this order for us. We are now in the market, a strong bullish candle has shot up, but we entered the market far too late. Now we are seeing a big player push the price down and the price is getting closer to our stop loss. What should we do? Give the price some air and expand the stop loss or get out now because we missed the entry? We get out and a second later, the price rises sharply again. If we stay in it, the price may be pushed into our extended stop and we are annoyed that we did not exit directly. A situation that every beginner has experienced before, for some it is even a recurring Deja Vu. What just happened here?

Well, we reacted correctly, but unfortunately much too slowly. One reason for this could be a much too high latency that many traders have to deal with on a daily basis. In some cases, retail traders work with latencies of 100-200ms, which bring a large trading disadvantage. Good ping times are 20-30ms, which can usually only be achieved with fiber optic cable. The big players and high-frequency traders have long been working with microwaves that are theoretically faster than the light and reach latencies of 5-8ms. These are worlds that we retail traders will never reach because the costs of this technology would consume enormous amounts. In principle, however, the big players have no decisive advantage because there is a factor that cannot be accelerated even with a latency of 1 ms. This factor is limited by our sensory stimuli.

We humans perceive our environment with 5 senses, I mean the ability to see, hear, smell, feel and taste. In science, this means whole sensory systems. With the help of the external sensory organs - eyes, ears, mouth, nose and skin - visual, acoustic, gustatory, olfactory and haptic stimuli are registered, which are then processed in the brain. Many millions of sensations are registered every day, most of which are only perceived unconsciously.

Which of these 5 senses could theoretically be used for trading? Tasting and smelling would probably be difficult and would fall out. Three senses remain: seeing, feeling and hearing. What sense do we mainly use for trading? The correct answer: the sense of sight, with the help of our eyes. We will now take a closer look at whether this is a good decision.

The sense of sight: Visual stimuli such as images, colors or shapes are the most important for human senses. The sense of sight provides around 80 percent of all information from the environment that we process in the brain. It has the highest absorption capacity of all senses, followed by hearing and touch. The diverse content, messages and associations that are associated with an image can be transported very quickly. Our visual perception is subject to weak cognitive control. This enables key emotional stimuli to be used that automatically force our attention. Advertising benefits considerably from this.

The sense of touch: Haptic stimuli such as shapes, materials and surfaces can strongly influence product and brand perception. In combination with the sense of sight, haptic stimuli ultimately decide to buy a product in a car or furniture store. Haptic senses also help to make the right decision in the fruit and vegetable market. 10,000 receptors sit alone on the skin surface of one hand and wait for signals. In addition, human well-being is created through touch. Compared to seeing, hearing, smelling or tasting, the sense of touch is rather low perception. We rely more on our eyes.

The sense of hearing: Acoustic stimuli include sounds, melodies and rhythms that are perceived through our sense of hearing. The sense of hearing is the most differentiated of all five senses. It is far more sensitive, precise and also more powerful than the eye. Words are processed much faster than pictures. Around 6-10 words can be processed at the same time that an image can be processed by the brain. Our hearing is directly connected to moods. Different tones lead to a different, emotional effect on the recipient and thus determine the behavior. Music can make us cry, the voice of people we love has a calming effect.

What is interesting is the different speed of reaction to different stimuli. People react fastest to tactile and acoustic stimuli, followed by visual stimuli. Tactile stimuli can sometimes be received faster than acoustic stimuli, but the challenge lies in the fact that tactile stimuli cannot be clearly differentiated. This means that our sense of sight is the slowest to react to external stimuli. The sense of sight, from the point of view of the speed of reaction, is therefore rather disadvantageous for action.

From a physical point of view, what our senses identify as simultaneous has not always happened simultaneously. We still perceive optical stimulations that do not follow each other for more than 20-40ms as a single stimulus. The television and cinema industry is based on this. From around 14 to 16 frames per second, the human brain perceives successive images as moving images. Current frame rates are between 24 and 48 frames per second (24-48 Hz). Our sense of touch reacts much more sensitively with 10-20ms. Our sense of hearing cannot temporally resolve two acoustic stimuli that are 3-5ms apart, these are experienced as one sound event. If you output the tones in one ear via headphones, from a difference of approx, 2ms they are no longer felt in the middle of the head, but laterally offset.

First a stimulus must be perceived, then there is a reaction time to implement the stimulus. If you should respond to a stimulus as quickly as possible (e.g. press a button) in a reaction test, you need at least 100ms (0.1s), but usually longer. Intensive training can increase your reaction speed. In the optical range you can improve from 360ms to 240ms and in the acoustic range from 180ms to 100ms. Both hands can be equally powerful. It is interesting that our reactions take place preferably in intervals of approximately 30-40 ms. This means that we are only able to decide over 25-30 decision points per second.

So we first perceive a certain stimulus (candle begins to rise) and need a certain reaction time to implement this stimulus (we want to buy). We press the buy button and now my order must be sent to the broker. The latency is crucial for this. Now let’s look at that in theory.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

At point A we see the total theoretical time it takes us to trade, divided between our three different senses. With the help of our eyes, we are only barely half a second later in the trade, while we could halve this time via sounds.

At point B we see the times that result when we train our reaction time. In the ideal case, we could be in the market four times faster using headphones, than with our untrained eyes. In the example, I assumed very good latency (20ms), which can be achieved via an optical fiber connection. With a poorer internet connection or a catastrophic broker, these times can increase significantly.

Identification with sounds or with our sense of touch beats our sense of sight by a long way. Basically, the question should be asked why we should make a trade decision in the future with the reaction time of our eyes. I have been using the acoustic stimuli with great success for some time. I would like to show you an example. I recorded a video using two different tones for bid and ask. If you watch the video, you will initially have problems to tell the different tones apart. This is completely normal at the beginning, because the senses first have to get used to it.

Inserted Video

In addition to the visual effect in the video, you could hear two different tones that give us specific information about what's going on in the market. The lighter tone was used for the ask, the deeper tone for the bid. I only filtered cumulative market sell orders and cumulative market buy orders from 2 lots, as long as they were created within 1/1000 second. We see the price going up and at the same time, strong market sell orders are entering the market. In the example, we can perceive a rapid sequence of different tones. For this you should work with special tones that are able to react quickly. With these tones you are able to identify different information much faster than with the eyes. The current example was very extreme since I have shown almost all incoming bid and ask. I myself do not work with bid and ask, but with a special filtering in the area of limit orders. When working with bid and ask, you can hear the current volatility in the background. So you can also deal with other things and automatically hear, when more orders come into the market.

I found the first test results with different tones to be very helpful, especially since I selected tones that didn't bother me. With the right filter setting, I was able to capture certain situations much faster and thus achieved a significantly better performance. However, I still used my eyesight too much, which still limits my reaction times. But it gets better every day.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

I developed a strategy from this idea. I got the idea because I was allowed to fly a helicopter myself 13 years ago. Of course, an experienced pilot was sitting next to me, who could intervene at any time. First, the pilot took control to take the helicopter up in the air. A helicopter is controlled with three different taxes. The joystick, or cyclic, is used in hover to move the helicopter to the left, right, front or back. In forward flight, the Cyclic initiates the curves or the ascent and descent. With the pedals, the helicopter can be turned around the vertical axis, and with the Collective, the pilot controls the climb and descent in hover, and together with the Cyclic, the speed in forward flight. With each helicopter, the joystick is operated with the right hand and the collective with the left. The feet are used to control the tail rotor via the pedals. Due to the instability of a helicopter, the Cyclic must not be released in flight unless the helicopter is equipped with an automatic stabilization system.

When we were in the air, I took control. It didn't work at first because my feet and hands had to balance 3 dimensions at the same time and I was constantly thinking about which properties are assigned to the Collective and Cyclic in combination with the pedals. The pilot recommended switching off my head and only flying with the feeling. After a few minutes, I was able to fly the helicopter. It was a little more difficult later to keep the helicopter in the air, but I succeeded a few times. These experiences gave me the idea of receiving and implementing information from trading in a completely new form.

The goal is to completely relieve the sense of sight and to concentrate exclusively on the sense of hearing and touch. The sense of hearing and touch should receive different information from the DoM and the time and sales list in order to make faster decisions. First and foremost, these are the individually filtered algorithms that are intended to address the sense of hearing and touch in different ways. I have developed some ideas that I would like to implement this year. However, this is still a big challenge because it places certain demands on my technology.

Conclusion:

Big players and high-frequency traders are investing millions of dollars to use microwaves to reduce latencies from 15ms to 8ms, but this is of little benefit due to the limited sensory stimuli (sense of sight). What is the use of a tuned vehicle that can reach 200 miles if the road is damaged and such a speed does not allow it? A change from optical stimuli to acoustic stimuli brings significantly greater advantages.

Our sense of hearing reacts 4 times faster and our sense of touch reacts 2 times faster than our eyes. However, we only act with our sense of sight. We can see three-dimensional charts with our eyes, but the response time will always be too slow. That is why I would like to concentrate on sense of touch and hearing in the future. I need 2 different information from the DoM and 2 different information from the times and sales list, which should affect my sense of touch and hearing. Our two brains react differently to signals, and this property can be used extremely well. This would make it theoretically possible to process a simultaneous, four-dimensional information architecture. What is decisive is what type of information we receive and how it specifically affects our senses. By using the sense of touch and hearing, trades could be implemented a total of 3 times faster than with the eyes. However, this procedure also requires special training, since at the same time the sense of sight must be shut down completely.

At first that sounds completely crazy, but when people talked about walking on the moon in the 1950s, they were also declared crazy. Maybe one day trading will take place with special suits that send information to our fastest senses. But that is still a long way off. First of all, we use the opportunities that we have to achieve smaller trading advantages. It is enough if you manage to identify Bid and Ask using special headphones.

Resounding success is always a step from the visible known to the hidden unknown. This idea may be the first step in a new future. We will see.

--- 帖子 #1475 ---
Iceberg orders are much smaller than we suspect

Hello dear subscribers,

An iceberg order is a limited buy or sell order on a stock exchange, where the total volume is not visible in the open order book. You can see only a small fraction of it. In addition to the total number of Lots, the iceberg order defines the peak number of Lots that corresponds to the visible part of the order. After they have been fulfilled, another order with the same peak volume automatically advances until the entire order volume has been fulfilled. This means that an iceberg order is only effective at one price level. The CME only supports two types of iceberg orders: native and synthetic. Four weeks ago I briefly discussed iceberg orders.

20% of the total volume are iceberg orders

Result: Around 20% of the total trading volume is accounted for by iceberg orders, which can increase to 52% depending on the market situation and market environment. Over 50% of synthetic iceberg orders were canceled before they were fully executed. The synthetic iceberg orders use an average of 4 -5 tranches with an average peak of 4-5 lots. The average total volume of complete synthetic iceberg orders is between 10 and 20 lots. It is interesting to mention that the order sizes are often a multiple of 5, such as B. 10, 15 or 20.

A very complex analysis was carried out 8 months ago in the S&P 500 to identify iceberg orders and investigate them. The algorithms used for this achieved an accuracy of 68%. Here you can find the results of the investigation.

Attached File(s)   CME Iceberg Order Detection and Prediction.pdf

776 KB
|
1,544 downloads

In this investigation, it emerged that about 20% of the total trading volume was generated by iceberg orders. There have been several studies in recent years, depending on the market situation and market environment, up to 52% of the total trading volume was achieved by iceberg orders. The iceberg orders are therefore used more often than initially assumed and these are increasingly smaller orders. Iceberg orders are primarily used to absorb the stops of retail traders. However, stops have the peculiarity of being at different price levels, which is why the big players are forced to occupy several price levels with their iceberg orders in order to absorb the decisive volume of the stops. Iceberg orders are used to hide interest in certain price levels.

As a rule, iceberg orders can only be identified after they have been executed. At the moment this is important information, but I am pursuing the approach of identifying iceberg orders at different price levels before they are executed. I will deal with this in more detail in my next post.

Best regards

Michael

--- 帖子 #1480 ---
On the trail of the iceberg orders

What we cannot see in the market (limit orders and iceberg orders) are the decisive reasons for price movements.
Bionics

Hello dear subscribers,

Today I want to show you a trade, that I have recorded on video and used the spoofing for my entry. "Spoofing" on the stock exchanges is a pretense of false facts. Many traders use the order book to recognize the level at which there is greater buying or selling interest. The market often runs to these larger limit orders, which signal a willingness to buy in the DoM. If a big player places a larger buy or sell order that is deleted shortly before it is executed, it pretends interests that actually do not exist in reality. Large limit orders at a price level can also signal a possible trend reversal, because if all market orders are absorbed at one price level, the price will not get through.

If there are suddenly large limit sell orders at a price level in the market with a steeply rising price, there are 3 options. The big player wants to get out of the euro there, another big player wants to buy the dollar or it is a fake. As a rule, the big players do not need large, visible limit orders in the DoM, to absorb large volumes at one price level. The actual project is much easier to obscure with iceberg orders. At this important price level, there are no more limit orders than in the other 9 price levels. At the crucial moment, when the limit orders have been used up, the iceberg orders push additional limit orders to the market and fill the important price level again and again.

The big players use the iceberg orders to absorb the stops of retail traders. If large limit orders appear in the market, this could warn retail traders early. For this reason, the specific absorptions of stops are only intercepted with iceberg orders. In most cases, large limit orders are only a diversion to create a wrong picture of supply and demand.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

If you look closely, there are always two different areas of supply and demand in the market. At point A, the market sell orders run into limit buy orders and at point B, market buy orders run into limit buy orders. Since the order types from points A and B never meet, there are two different supply and demand zones. Different market participants act with different interests in the market.

Demand zone (Limit Buy Orders) = Buy Euros or Sell Dollars

Offer zone (Market Sell Orders) = buy dollars or sell euros

Demand zone (Market Buy Orders) = sell dollars or buy euros

Offer zone (Market Sell Orders) = sell euros or buy dollars

If the dollar is exited in a demand zone, this does not speak for rising rates and if the euro is exited in a supply zone, it does not speak for falling rates. Accordingly, there are two different equilibrium. The combination of market sell orders with the limit sell orders (offer) and the combination of market buy orders with the limit buy orders (demand) to create only an average supply or demand zone will fail. The reason is different interests and at the same time, the incalculable iceberg orders.

This creates some challenges!

1. Identification of whether the euro is currently being bought / sold or the dollar being bought / sold.

For this I use the heat map to show me a certain number of cumulative market orders that come into the market within 1/1000 second. I have described the advantages of the heat map here:

Identification of the big player algorithms

2.The respective strength of the limit orders and the market orders

With my 4D strength method, I get a graphical display of the strength of limit sell orders, limit buy orders, market buy orders and market sell orders. You can read about this procedure here:

Act in the eye of the tornado

3. Identification of Stophunting

The big players are constantly interested in the volume that is absorbed through the stops of retail traders. For this I work with a key candle to determine the stophunting. The downloadable chart with a detailed description can be found here:

Currency strength dashboard and Stophunting chart

4. Market analysis: what are the big players currently collecting?

The price moves because the market sell orders run in the limit buy orders and the market buy orders run in the limit sell orders. The fact that the big players primarily work with limit orders leads us to the conclusion that the limit orders are significantly stronger than the market orders. I would even go one step further and make the claim that the limit orders are really moving the market and not the market orders. You can find a detailed report here:

Which is stronger, market orders or limit orders?

The identification of the decisive limit orders shows us the future market direction. This results in more efficient trading decisions. Here you will find further information, please also look at the links in the report!

First results as a liquidity trader

5. The interplay between limit orders and market orders

Using algorithms, big players are able to completely remove sell limit orders from the market and at the same time push the price up with market buy orders. With this you manage to move the price strongly with few market buy orders. This process is a permanent interplay and the algorithms are programmed exactly on it. This process is very efficient and takes place permanently. Here is an example:

The interplay of algo

6.Our eyes deceive us

Our sense of hearing reacts 4 times faster and our sense of touch reacts 2 times faster than our eyes. However, we only act with our sense of sight. We can see three-dimensional charts with our eyes, but the response time will always be too slow. Here you can find out why and how to optimize it.

Fast and furious

7. How many iceberg orders are behind the limit orders?

This question is not so crucial at first, since basically only as many market orders can be absorbed as the market makes available. If only 100 Lot Market Buy Orders (triggered stops) are available at a price level, only 100 Lot can be absorbed by the Limit Sell Orders. Subsequent market buy orders would then also be absorbed at this price level, but the big players are more interested in stops than in current market entries. This is because stops are more concentrated than simultaneous market entries. The background to this is the stopping rule: above the last high and below the last low. This makes it more likely to find more volume in these stops. It is much more important to know where iceberg orders could be at certain price levels. Conclusions can be drawn from this, at which price level the big players expect larger stops.

For a few weeks now I have been working intensively on spoofing (adding and subtracting limit orders that are waiting to be executed). My software provides me with information about spoofing. Spoofing initially takes place in the area of visible limit orders. If 10 limit orders are deleted in the spoofing display and the number of visible limit orders in DoM does not change at the same time, it can be assumed that the change occurred in the area of the invisible limit orders (iceberg orders). However, we have to assume that these are only native iceberg orders that are managed by the CME itself. Synthetic iceberg orders are submitted by independent software providers whose infrastructure is physically separate from the exchange. These software providers split the original iceberg order, submit new tranches and track their execution. These tranches are indistinguishable from the usual limit orders of other participants, but they are difficult or impossible to identify as spoofing.

Basically, I assume that the big players in the future market work with synthetic iceberg orders to disguise identification. But there is a glimmer of hope. We know that at CME, cumulative limit orders placed as native iceberg orders have priority in the queue. As far as I know, this does not apply to synthetic iceberg orders submitted by independent software providers. This could be related to the fact that a certain fee has to be paid for native iceberg orders. If a big player has to sell iceberg orders in the market within a short period of time, he will very likely fall back on native iceberg orders. If he has already occupied the individual limit levels, this is no longer necessary. We can therefore assume that part of the spoofing can also be attributed to the big player.

Trading virtual stop loss

Hello FXsniper111,

First of all, thank you for your feedback, I am very happy if the Stophunting diagram helps you and hope that it will continue to provide you with important information in the future. Your stop strategy is perfectly fine if you achieve a win rate of over 80% and a risk-reward ratio of 1: 5 with this procedure.

In fact, there are still a few brokers who mostly sit on small islands and like to manipulate the price. The broker you work with is an ECN broker, price manipulation is much more difficult there. I myself compared the price of this broker with the stock market data for more than half a year and I did not notice any irregularities. However, the total costs and the risk were too high for me. The total costs in EURUSD for me, per lot, must not be more than 0.4-0.5 pip. However, spreads have been somewhat higher in recent weeks due to lower liquidity. This was because there were fewer big players in the market that provided liquidity. At the same time, however, the volume was as high as ever. There were larger gaps in the limit orders and a high number of market orders could penetrate the smaller number of limit orders more quickly. This led to increased volatility and at the same time to a higher spread. However, that was not the broker's fault.

Market makers set their own prices for currency pairs because they do not execute orders on the interbank market, but internally bring buyers and sellers together or secure the position of the customer (hedging). In principle, price manipulation could only take place in the environment of the market maker, but never in the interbank market. The interbank market trades $ 2 trillion daily with an average of 92,000 ticks. To change the price by 1/10 pip, the broker would have to invest 217 Lot, that's over $ 21 million. If he wanted to catch stops from his customers that are 3 pip away, he would have to invest over $ 600 million. He doesn't have the money and the risk would be far too high.

I therefore recommend working with a virtual stop loss that the broker cannot see. However, he could use an algorithm to find out which stop sizes are used by customers. If there is a suspicion that a broker is manipulating, I would switch immediately.  As a rule, stophunting can be explained by the clever approach of the big players.

I think it's great that you regularly optimize your setup, that's the only way to get ahead. A little tip at the end:

If you use the Toggle Borders indicator, your frames will be removed from the different charts and you will have a much larger display. You can find the indicator here under: "Indi Dashboard"

Currency strength dashboard and Stophunting chart

The strategy of the big players

Hello Renko,

There are relatively few high-frequency traders in the forex market at first, as they are restricted by the EBS with a minimum holding period for their trades. The big players tend to be medium-term oriented for 1-3 days, with most of them trying to do their business within a day. Goldman Sachs is a classic example of this. However, this does not always work because the volume available on the market fluctuates extremely. If a big player does not make volume available to himself, he must collect a certain number of ask or bid within an equilibrium. I monitor these collection campaigns with a special limit delta chart from the stock market. I can quickly see which way the big player choose. These collection campaigns usually take place at different price levels, whereby they are closer together. Here is some information:

Limit Delta gifts

As soon as the big player has finished his collection campaign, he turns off possible followers beforehand because they could stop his course course through profit realizations. Based on the limit orders, you can roughly estimate how much the big player has collected. If he now pushes the course in his corresponding direction, the heat map helps me to identify his exit from the position. The algorithms are the crucial clue as to when it starts with the corresponding breakout. However, I am just beginning to filter these algorithms more precisely based on the spoofing information. However, it will be a while before I can derive concrete trade advantages from it.

On the trail of the iceberg orders

In the Forex market, this works very well with my Stophunting chart that I posted here. There you will find links with further information.

Currency strength dashboard and Stophunting chart

A scalper also needs this information to find out where the market is at the moment. It makes a huge difference whether the big player is initiating a pullback to lead traders in the wrong direction or whether it is a breakout, to bring their previously collected limit orders to profit. Both courses are usually very fast, which I am looking for as a scalper.

For a swing trader in particular, it is crucial to know what the big player has collected in order to gain a trading advantage. This works best if you take a closer look at the limit orders. My main business is short-term scalps, but I also use my information to make longer-running trades. However, the profits from this, in my opinion, are more based on luck, since the big players always have to react to the retail traders. I can predict the short-term reactions more likely than the medium and long-term reactions. However, here every trader has his own view. As a swing trader, you shouldn't do without the stock market data.

I wish you a successful trading week

best regards

Michael

Algorithms in the DoM

Hello dear subscribers,

In the past few weeks, I have spent many hours identifying the big player algorithms in the DoM. For this I had to create a new DoM with very complex filter settings. I would like to show you the first results of this today.

Every trader is interested in getting price information as quickly as possible. We get the slowest price information with indicators, because they essentially run after the price. The fastest price information in Forex is the price itself. Certain currency strength indicators are somewhat faster, as they sometimes lead the price. The visible limit orders in the DoM on the other hand, are a small look into the future with the exchange data, as they show the willingness, to buy on a certain price level. However, these limit orders can also be deleted at any time by Spoofing. Limit orders can also be increased by the iceberg orders and are thus able to absorb and stop the market orders. As I have already described in some articles, the limit orders are responsible for the main movements in the market.

Which is stronger, market orders or limit orders?

Limit orders that are already in the market and which have been activated by the market orders can of course no longer change, which is why I only use limit orders in the chart to monitor the big players' collection campaigns.

Iceberg orders of the big players

Definitely, with the limit orders in the DoM we have a look into the possible future of the market movement, with the restriction that they can be added or deleted at any time. The algorithms are responsible for adding or deleting limit orders. This is precisely why I have dealt with these algorithms in more detail. If you succeed in deciphering the algorithms of the big players, you can also take a clear look at the limit orders placed in the DoM and thus at the future price trend. And that is exactly the only reason why I am concentrating on it. If the algorithms indicate that a high number of limit orders has been deducted at a certain price level, it is automatically clear that the price will go through this price level. If the algorithms indicate that a high number of limit orders has been added at a certain price level, it is automatically clear that the price will be stopped for now. In order to identify a possible trend reversal from this, it is then crucial to recognize whether, for example, in an upward trend, the euro is sold or the dollar is bought. I've written about this a few times in this blog. So the goal is to identify the algorithms so that they allow a view of the net limit orders.

The visual stimuli such as images, colors or shapes are the most important for human sensory perception. The sense of sight provides around 80 percent of all information from the environment that we process in the brain. You see a lot of numbers in my charts, this is because the brain detects neutral numbers faster than colors. Let's do a little test.

Point A

Here the color name of the word matches the color of the balloon.

Point B

Now try to name the color of the word and not to read the word.

The Stroop interference test is a method for measuring the individual interference tendency in color-word interference. It has been proven that the naming of the color of a visually presented word is slowed down if the content of the word contradicts the color (eg word "blue" in the color red, see illustration). If the content of the word matches the color, however, it is quicker to name the color. Reading is a much more automated cognitive activity than naming colors; This initially leads to the contradictory brain reactions just mentioned when the test person encounters the discrepancy between the color name and the color of the word. Reading is such an automated activity that it is often impossible to suppress reading, although this is required in the instructions (interference).

The different reaction rates to different stimuli is also interesting. People react fastest to tactile and acoustic stimuli, followed by visual stimuli. This means that our sense of sight is the slowest to react to external stimuli. The sense of sight, from the point of view of the speed of reaction, is therefore rather disadvantageous for action. Our sense of hearing reacts 4 times faster than our eyes. However, we only act with our sense of sight. That's why I started to focus on my hearing. Two different tones filtered out of ASK, BID, best BID and best ASK affect my hearing. In my published video, which you can watch at the end of the article, we only hear BID and ASK.

You can find my contribution to different reaction speeds to different stimuli here:

Striking the right note

Hello dear subscribers,

Our sensory stimuli are so limited by our brain that we are only able to perceive optical stimulations that do not follow each other for more than 20-40 ms as a single stimulus. This is depressing because the sense of sight provides us with around 80 percent of all information from the environment. We trade 100% through optical stimulation, which means that we are clearly at a disadvantage in terms of time.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Our sense of hearing cannot temporally resolve two acoustic stimuli that are 3-5ms apart, these are experienced as one sound event. If you output the tones in one ear, via headphones, from a difference of approx 2ms they are no longer felt in the middle of the head, but laterally offset. If you base your trading decision on acoustic signals in the future, you will be able to make decisions 4 times faster than with your eyes. I wrote a very detailed article about this finding, which you can find here:

Fast and furious

The resulting idea is based on the assumption that a trader is unable to identify quickly coming in market orders, to make an advantageous trading decision. As we already know, limit orders determine long-term market movements and not market orders. You can find a detailed report here.

Which is stronger, market orders or limit orders?

Nevertheless, the Big Player also use market orders, to steer the price in a certain direction. The main thing is to get the appropriate volume, in the form of stops, to fill your limit orders. The big players are so precise that it is almost impossible for retail traders to make effective profits. In this context, I managed to make their approach visually visible. I will report in detail on this big player strategy in my next post.

It has been scientifically proven that the brain can record and implement acoustic signals faster than optical signals. For this reason, I took a closer look at the acoustic signals. My first goal was to identify the incoming market orders in the Times and Sales list with two different tones.

Around 90,000 trades (ticks) are processed in Euro FX per trading day. An average of 150,000 lots have been traded in the last 40 trading days, 75% of which between 07:00 and 19:00 CET. Between 09:00 and 11:00 CET and from 14:30 to 16:30 CET, 60% of the total lots are traded. This means that approximately 90,000 lots are traded in about 4 hours. That is an average of 6 lots per second, although 100 lots per second can be traded at peak times. If these market sell orders and market buy orders run down the Times and Sales list at lightning speed, no trader will be able to see these orders with their eyes. Future traders are happy to use only cumulative market orders to keep an overview. All market orders that come in within 1/1000 second are summarized.

There are only two different forms of cumulative market orders that are decisive for me. On the one hand, these are the stops of retail traders and, on the other hand, the cumulative market orders that the big player places in order to push the price in a certain direction. These two cumulative market orders are completely different and should therefore be specifically identified. I will write about this point in detail in my next post.

Theoretically you would be able to identify 20 -25 market orders per second. Unfortunately there is a big challenge. In the Times and Sales list, market sell orders and brand buy orders appear, which apparently run down in a random order. The brain must now divide and differentiate these different market orders. And this division takes a lot of time.

If you put on headphones and acoustically display the market sell orders on the left and the market buy orders on the right, you would theoretically be able to identify 500 lots per second. That is 20 times faster than with the eyes. Due to the reaction time to enter into a trade, the advantage is reduced to four times. But before entering into a trade, you first have to correctly assess the current situation. With two different tones you can do it 20 times faster than with your eyes.

First of all I used two different Windows tones, which take about 100ms to play a sound once. I assigned the lighter tone to the market buy orders, the lower tone to the market sell orders. The output first came from two high-quality speakers that were placed next to my screens. It was clear to me that I could only identify a maximum of 250 lots per second via the loudspeakers, but that was still ten times faster than with my eyes. In the past eight weeks I have been able to optimize my trading decisions considerably. However, there was also a clear disadvantage. In the extremely high volatile phases, a concrete identification was no longer possible and I noticed that my workstation slowed down significantly. I started to study the tones to find out why. The tones I installed took about 100ms to play. I was able to perceive a maximum of 10 tones per second. If 30 different market orders came in per second in high volatile phases, my tones were also activated 30 times, but due to the 100 ms, could only emit a signal 10 times per second. At that moment there was a small jam of sound, 30 tones should be emitted, but technically it was only possible to play ten tones. So 20 tones were swallowed and at the same time slowed down my CPU. I also made a video where you can hear these 100ms Windows tones with an average volatility.

Inserted Video

At the beginning the volatility is not high and the different tones can be distinguished from one another, from 45 seconds in the video the tones overlap and identification is no longer possible. The tones I used initially are based on a WAV file that was 5000 bytes in size and was stereo compatible. As a result, different signals are distributed over two channels, which require more memory in a high repetition frequency.

In order to better distinguish the tones from each other and at the same time to relieve my CPU, I looked for faster tones. MP3 files are unsuitable for this because they require too long a playing time and are mostly stereo-compatible. I found a database that made 3,400,000 different tones available free of charge in WAV format. The selection of tones that reached a maximum playing time of 2ms to 5ms was very small. I found a total of 30 different tones that came into question. If a sound is 2ms long, this does not necessarily mean that the total recording time of the WAV file corresponds to 2ms. Here it depends on the recording technology used by the developer. Another challenge is the clear distinction between the two tones when they occur at a high frequency. So I had to combine different tones to get the best result.

The tones that I am currently using are based on a WAV file with a size of 250 bytes, 44,100 Hz, 16 bit mono. Mono is more of an advantage if you later redirect this tone to the left or right headphone channel. The tone duration is 2ms and is over 50 times faster than my Windows tones. In the video below I used the new tones with approximately the same volatility as in the first video.

Inserted Video

One can clearly perceive that the tones can be distinguished even more clearly. Now let's have a look at how the tones react when the volatility increases significantly.

Inserted Video

From 26 seconds in the video, a small firework of tones starts because a large number of different market orders come in. The tones never roll over and are clearly identifiable even in higher volatility phases. Of course, this is a real mess for an inexperienced listener, but after some time you are able to clearly identify the different tones. Practice creates masters.

These two faster tones also relieved the CPU considerably and has held up well even in extreme volatility phases. One thing caught my eye very positively. In extremely volatile periods, the tones react faster than the Times and Sales list. Before the Times and Sales list was able to display the corresponding orders on the screen, I was able to identify them based on the tones. This could potentially be a significant market advantage. I initially limited this experiment to market orders. For a few weeks now I have started using the tones to indicate the strength of the limit orders. This should result in further insights in order to achieve my ultimate goal. Maybe at some point I will identify the limit orders via the tones and at the same time the market orders via my sense of touch. But that is still very far away.

Conclusion:

The identification of the market orders by means of tones has a 20 times higher advantage than the identification with the eyes. The total response time to make a trade decision improves fourfold. In high volatile phases, the tones are used to identify the market orders before they can be seen in the Times and Sales list. During the entire trading day, the eyes are relieved because you can always hear with your ears what is happening in the market. With the tones you always have the volatility in your ear. If you deal with other things and the volatility increases, you immediately notice this and can react faster. Refraining from the candles and at the same time concentrating more on the price leader in the DoM and the identification of the market orders by the tones has contributed to a significant improvement in my trading decisions. Therefore, I can recommend every trader to take a closer look at these things. Next, I have to filter the corresponding market orders and limit orders so that the tones show me the most important decision points in trading. This is the most time-consuming job. I will of course keep you up to date regularly.

I wish you a nice weekend and a good start to the new trading week.

Best regards, Michael

Volume in forex

Footprint chart in the forex market?

A kind of time & sales for MT4?

Big player is watching you!

Hello dear subscribers,

When looking at a chart, every trader immediately asks where the price could go next. Different indicators are used to identify possible turning points. Fibonacci, MACD, RSI and Moving Average are intended to help determine possible support or resistance zones. Logically, this information can only be calculated from past price trends. From my point of view, a reliable prognosis of a future course course cannot be made from a past course course. This has to do with the fact that a past course in most cases has nothing to do with the future course. Exceptions occur with pullbacks, within an upward and downward movement. The key point is whether the big player is still in position or not. Therefore, any price movement should be viewed as a closed entity, as traders' opinions change at any time. The background for this approach lies in the way big players work. Now let’s take a closer look at that.

First of all, we limit ourselves to the facts. Twelve big players control 85% of the forex market. The winning rate of the most successful big players and high frequency traders is between 90 and 99% and the big players win $ 400 million daily in the EURUSD. The Big Player approach is usually always similar. First you collect a certain number of ask or bid within an equilibrium and then drive the price into your profit zone. For this reason it is crucial to find out what the big players collect in the current course. In 90% of cases, this collective action is carried out via limit orders, using small iceberg orders that are between 10 and 20 lots in size. The price is held within a certain range and driven up and down. Within these price movements, retail traders choose a long or short position. As soon as the price is pushed in the opposite direction, the stops of the retail traders are used to record them with the limit orders. This process can sometimes take hours or days before a decisive breakout triggers the future trend direction.

The big players use 65% limit orders and 35% market orders, while retail traders restrict themselves to market orders. There is no way to get ask or bid in the forex market, so you should always use stock market data. Just looking at the market orders in the future market does not help, since the limit orders determine the long-term market situation.

With a little trick it is also possible to make the limit orders visible in the exchange data. Here we take advantage of a stock exchange law that supports us. The fact is that every market order that appears in the time and sales list must be accepted by a limit order at the same time. This means that every market buy order, simultaneously from a limit sell order and every market sell order, must be taken up simultaneously from a limit buy order. Of course, at the moment we don't know whether a market buy order is a euro buy or a dollar sale. In addition, they do not know whether the limit sell order that has just taken up a market buy order sold the euro or bought the dollar. However, we are initially able to display the limit orders in the chart by simply swapping the colors of ask and bid. I have already written some articles about this, which you can find here

A completely new market view

I use this self-developed limit delta profile to monitor the big player collection.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

On the right we see the limit delta profile of the total volume that was recorded within a certain period. On the left we see the limit delta profile with a filtered total volume that was recorded in the same period. I remove the market orders placed by the big players, which are only used to push the price into the stops of retail traders. All that remains then are the market orders that are relevant for a possible collection. With the help of these filter settings, the individual collection actions of Bid and Ask become clearer and clear contours are created.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Here I have shown the corresponding course. In the filtered limit orders, we can see from points A to C that the collective action in the area of limit sell orders led to the price being pushed down again. For the unfiltered limit orders, on the other hand, there was an accumulation of limit sell orders only at point D. In this area, a big player has collected a large number of questions, so let's look at the entire course of the price and how the price reacted to these zones.
