The green zones that we see here in the chart are actually not resistance or support zones. It is crucial to recognize what the big players collect within an equilibrium and when they get out of their position. The course of a course is usually always similar, let's first look at different upward movements.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Before a longer upward movement begins, ask is first collected. This ask is recorded via the limit buy orders, which are shown here with green lines.

Point A

Here Ask was collected at different price levels, the price went up.

Point B

Here Ask was bought again massively, which speaks for a further rising price.

Point C

This is where the big players begin to step out of their position. To do this, they need Ask from other market participants who believe that prices will continue to rise. They collect this ask with their limit sell orders and thus come out of their position.

Point D

This is where the big players start buying the dollar via their limit sell orders in order to push the price down again.

We notice that the limit order volume increases within a price trend, we can clearly see this on the left picture. In the lower area there is relatively little volume, which increases with the price. This phenomenon can be explained by the fact that as the price rises, the big players collect more and more ask, which emerges in the form of the larger limit sell orders.

After the accumulation phase, a kind of zigzag run begins. Whenever enough long traders come together, the price is pushed down by the big players and the stops (bid) of the retail traders are recorded with the limit buy orders. The big player needs part of this to get out of his dollar position, which he had to take to push the price down. The remaining ask remains in his portfolio and helps him to increase his profit. When the price is pushed up again, the stops of the short traders help the price to accelerate upwards. The higher the big player drives the course, the more ask is in the big player's portfolio. When exiting the euro, the big player must therefore sell more ask than he previously collected in the first Equilibrium.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

When moving down, the same principle is used only in the opposite direction.

Point A

Here bid was collected at different price levels, the price ran down.

Point B

Here again bid was massively bought, which speaks for a further falling price.

Point C

This is where the big players begin to step out of their position. For this they need the bid of the market participants who believe in further falling prices. They collect this bid with their limit buy orders and thus come out of your position.

Point D

Here the big players start buying the euro via their limit buy orders in order to push the price up again.

Of course, the big players are different market participants. When a big player leaves his position, he doesn't necessarily have to open a new position to act in the opposite direction. We recognize that looking at the filtered limit orders gives us a very good indication of the medium-term price movements.

This approach I have presented is medium-term. This is because the big players first collect ASK or BID at certain price levels and only then act in the corresponding direction. The challenge is to recognize as early as possible whether stophunting will take place afterwards. For this you should keep an eye on the short-term area. As a scalper, I am interested in being able to accurately predict very short-term price movements. I have developed an idea for this over the past few months, which I would now like to present to you. An upward or downward movement begins with an accumulation or distribution phase, where the big player collects a certain number of ASK or BID within an equilibrium. Then the hot phase begins where the big player wants to bring his previously collected orders to profit. The big player now moves the course up or down in zigzag movements. In this hot phase, the big player pays close attention to every market participant that enters the market.

As we know, the big players are constantly on the hunt for the volume of retail traders. Stophunting is the only way to trap the volume of retail traders. Retail traders always enter the market at different price levels, but the stops are very close together. This is due to the market wisdom that a stop should always be above the last high or below the last low. My stop is always a pip or two below my entry, when I am stopped it is because I chose a bad entry time. I have long thought about how I can determine short-term price movements as precisely as possible.

6000 institutional traders lose $ 43 million daily and 900,000 retail traders lose $ 90 million a day in EURUSD. The loss rate for institutional traders is 60%, for retail traders the loss rate is 90%. So it is easier to take money from retail traders than from institutional traders. This is largely due to the fact that institutional traders are increasingly working with iceberg orders. That's why I was looking for a way to make retail traders visible on the chart. In the Future Market Euro FX the minimum bet is 1 lot ($ 125,000), whereby the highest bets can be as much as a few 1000 lots. The weakest link in the chain is clearly the retail traders, who achieve the highest loss rate in the future market and also in the forex market. In order to find out in which direction the market is not going, the identification of the retail positions is crucial.

Equilibrium, the fastest trend indicator

Hello dear subscribers,

Before we delve deeper into how big players behave within a longer upward or downward movement, I would like to show you an interesting discovery today that has to do with equilibrium. Equilibrium is the key to success, I have followed this approach since I started trading. An equilibrium means balance and at the same time uncertainty in the market. This situation is a decisive factor for a possible turnaround. A rising price must first be stopped in order to initiate a turnaround. This requires an equilibrium beforehand, but you can rarely see that, inside a candle.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

In one post I compared the market orders with the accelerator pedal of a vehicle and the limit orders with the brakes. The price moves because the market sell orders run in the limit buy orders and the market buy orders run in the limit sell orders. The big players collect their ask and bid in the form of limit orders (iceberg orders), as these can hardly be identified in the market. Usually this happens within an bigger equilibrium. The market orders are primarily used to trigger the first stops of retail traders in order to supply themselves with volume. Exceptions arise as soon as a big player makes his own volume available. Basically, it is correct that market orders move the market, but we should be aware that market orders are also able to stop the market to a certain extent. Basically it is correct that limit orders can stop the market, but we should be aware that limit orders are also able to move the market. The fact that the big players primarily work with limit orders leads us to the conclusion that the limit orders are significantly stronger than the market orders. I would even go one step further and make the claim that the limit orders are really moving the market and not the market orders. You can find the detailed article here:

Which is stronger, market orders or limit orders?

The identification of liquidity is a major challenge, as the individual algorithms of the big players must first be decrypted and assigned to the cumulative market orders. The individual strength of the respective market and limit orders based on my 4D strength analysis is very helpful. Using algorithms, big players are able to completely remove sell limit orders from the market and at the same time push the price up with market buy orders. With a small number of market buy orders you can move the market significantly. This process is a permanent interplay and the algorithms are programmed exactly on it. It was only in the past few months that I became aware of how extremely complex these algorithms are programmed. This process is very efficient and you can find an example of this procedure here:

The interplay of algo

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Within a price, an equilibrium can be identified quickly (point A), but I am mainly interested in the turning points in the course of the course (blue arrows point B). These turning points have no previous, identifiable equilibrium in price and suddenly arise unpredictably. With my key candle from the Forex market these turning points can be localized roughly, but as a scalper I need more specific information. The fastest trading information is provided by the stock market data with the DoM, the Times and Sales list and the heat map. However, this requires a correct filter setting and the crucial information. In the past few weeks I have made an interesting discovery that I would like to introduce to you today.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

On the left you can see the Times and Sales list on the right my DoM, which I have modified a little.

Point A

Point D

Here we see the market buy orders (point F) that run into the limit sell orders. The number 14, after each trade, indicates the number of limit sell orders still available in the DoM (Point E). At Point G you can see the change in sizes, they are an indicator of the limit orders still available on the sell and buy side. With a special filter setting, iceberg orders can also be identified. Depending on the currency pair, there are different sizes that differ in their number. The sizes shown here refer to the Euro FX, which I have used as the basis for identifying an equilibrium.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

In the first step, I assigned certain filter settings to the sizes of Best Bid / best Ask. In the Times and Sales list, the red color shows a strength in the bid area, while the green color shows a strength in the ask area. As soon as an equilibrium is created within these sizes, no color is drawn and a black field is created. Since the Times and Sales list runs very quickly, I used a 15 second chart. Conclusion:

At first, my discovery of generating equilibrium from the sizes seems to be the quickest way to more reliably identify trend reversals. Here, however, I will have to work with different filter settings in the next few weeks to derive more specific information. Of course, there are also errors here that I still have to filter out. First of all, it is crucial to identify the accumulation or distribution in order to recognize what the big players have previously collected. This information indicates the medium-term trend direction. After leaving the equilibrium of the collecting phase, the big player drives the course up or down in zigzag lines. We will talk about this more specifically in the next few weeks. With the help of my key candle from the Forex market, I am able to determine the approximate zone of the reversal points. The equilibrium in the sizes ultimately gives me the information as to whether the key candles I have drawn actually initiate a turnaround. It is important to recognize when a big player gets out of his main position. We will talk more about this in the next few weeks. It should be noted that an equilibrium always takes place before a trend reversal. This has to do with the fact that a course must come to a standstill before it can run in the opposite direction. A car that drives forward can only drive backwards if it comes to a standstill (equilibrium) beforehand. This is a natural law that also applies to the stock market. However, one is unable to identify an equilibrium in the candles within the zigzag movements. For that you have to look a little deeper into the candles and you can only do that with the sizes in the Times and Sales list. Of course I will keep you up to date on the further results.

Currency exchange in the speculative market

Hello dear subscribers,

The foreign exchange market (Forex) is a submarket of the financial market where foreign exchange supply and demand meet and are exchanged at the negotiated exchange rate. Market participants in the foreign exchange market are credit institutions, central banks, the state and large companies in the non-banking sector. Small and medium-sized companies as well as private households have to turn to credit institutions for their foreign exchange transactions. Trading objects on the foreign exchange market are foreign exchange, i.e. book money in foreign currency. The foreign exchange market is the world's largest financial market, with global daily sales of approximately $ 6.6 trillion in 2019. The internationally used reserve currencies US dollar, euro, Japanese yen and British pound as well as the regional currency Australian dollar are the most traded. The EURUSD is the most traded currency pair, with a daily volume of over $ 2 trillion.

The foreign Exchange market enables the exchange of domestic money into foreign and vice versa, thereby converting purchasing power from the domestic currency into the foreign currency. Trading does not take place centrally via a stock exchange, but mostly directly between financial institutions via corresponding dealer networks. Companies, brokers and private speculators are also increasing among the participants. The trading medium is primarily online trading via trading platforms such as the electronic broker EBS and telephone trading. The foreign exchange market is institutionalized through foreign exchange trading. In the narrower sense, this means the interbank market in the context of customer business and proprietary trading. Internationally active credit institutions trade here in the form of standardized foreign exchange transactions based on recognized trading practices with the foreign exchange object. Foreign exchange transactions in turn consist of the basic forms of spot exchange or forward exchange transactions as well as the derived (derivative) currency swap transactions and currency option transactions.

The Forex market is not only used for speculation or proprietary trading, but also for currency Exchange. A common foreign exchange transaction in the private customer business is the foreign transfer to a country with a foreign currency. There is occasionally a need to hedge larger foreign currency liabilities, e.g. B. to maintain a holiday home in a country with a foreign currency or for cross-border commuters who live abroad. Furthermore, the foreign Exchange business for private investors also plays a role as part of the securities business. Larger companies pay their employees their salary once a month, which often means changing currencies.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Especially at the end of a month, the currency Exchange that does not serve speculation increases enormously. In the chart of the Euro FX we see an increased volume of larger orders within 5 trading days (June 26th - July 2nd). The green fields, show a dollar Exchange in euros and the red fields a euro Exchange in dollars. These investments are carried out by larger banks for their large customers. This approach makes it difficult to get a clear picture of the market. As a rule, you can use the limit orders to identify what a big player collects within an equilibrium (accumulation / distribution). If a larger market participant collects Ask, for his speculation, he has to get out of his position with a bid at some point. A currency Exchange, on the other hand, gives us incorrect information. If there is now a big Dollar Exchange in euros on a high, it looks as if a larger market participant is collecting the euro (point A). This could lead some traders to take a long position, which in this case means a loss. If the bank buys this Ask through a limit sell order, it will transfer the euro to the customer's account. He pays the salaries to his employees. Although Ask was bought (dollars exchanged for euros), the position is now finished and you wait in vain for an exit (bid).

As a speculator, I have found a solution that could possibly help you.

Basically, at the end and beginning of a month, you can see that massive currencies are being exchanged. This exchange takes place almost exclusively in high volume phases. With the heat map you can analyze the larger orders more precisely and display them in the chart. Big players often have the habit of placing larger orders of 100 lots or more in the market one after the other. Market orders are sometimes used to process the transaction immediately. Basically, it is difficult to distinguish between a currency exchange and a speculative transaction, but the likelihood of a larger currency exchange is highest between the individual months. That is why one should carry out a more precise analysis especially in these times. In order to facilitate the relationship between supply and demand, I would consider the large orders rather neutral at this time. You can do this by filtering out the larger orders. Of course, you will also filter out speculative orders, but the number of neutral orders is significantly higher during this time. This increases the probability of getting a better overview. If I see several 100 lot orders in the heat map that come in one after the other, I ignore them. That saved me some losses in the past. Therefore, we should act a little more carefully at the end and beginning of a month.

I wish you a successful trading day

Greetings Michael

Analysis for the EURUSD

Hello dear subscribers,

Over 1 million retail traders trade in EURUSD every day, creating 1 million different opinions about the future course of the price. At the end of the day, 50,000 retail traders will have been right, while the remaining 950,000 traders are hoping for a new opportunity. Most of them start with an analysis before trading, taking into account the long-term, medium-term and short-term price trend.

Basically, an analysis can only be made from a past course, but in most cases the future course has nothing to do with the past course, since it has already ended. The vast majority of big players, who control 85% of the forex market, are day traders and try to close their positions within a day, high frequency traders are often only in the market for a few minutes. We find long-term major traders among institutional traders who manage funds or hedge themselves through the market. However, their odds of winning are significantly lower than those of the big players or high-frequency traders.

Our chart consists of 99.9% from the past and 0.1% from the present. The present is the current candle that is currently developing. The past course of the course is always a typical chaos in which we want to put an understandable order. Now indicators, horizontal and vertical lines, resistance and support zones are used to predict a possible price trend. This makes the big players happy, because they produce artificial resistance zones every day to take the money from retail traders.

The market would be much easier if there were only speculators, but billions of dollars are being brought into the market every day that are only intended for currency exchange. In principle, this currency exchange is a neutral trade and should only be viewed as an exit from a currency. However, this currency exchange also appears in the order book and often falsifies the view of supply and demand. Since many trading actions are not always profit-oriented, this procedure makes it difficult to have a clear view of the markets.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

From the course of the price, you can clearly see that less stops were absorbed by short traders, but more the ask, from new buyers. Stops are usually absorbed, here buyers are absorbed. We'll take a closer look at how the big player did it.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

The principle of the big players to start an upward or downward movement is in procedure always similar. At Point A we see the end of a little equilibrium. The price is pushed down and the long trader's stops are absorbed. From point B, the big player first pushes the course up. At Point C, a small equilibrium is created, where the big player collects a large number of ask. Now the price is pushed up strongly and at Point D there is a first partial exit from the euro. This has to do with the fact that a big player accumulates a higher number of ask when he pushes the price up. He tries to avoid this by using the algorithms to control his limit sell orders in order to get through with as little ask as possible, but that doesn't always work. I have described this strategy in more detail here:

The interplay of algo

In the following pullback (to point D) the euro is collected again and the course to point E is pushed up. This is where the big player gets out with his remaining position. Since there are no other buyers on the market, a small pullback to Point F is created. After that, the big player pushes the price upwards and ensures that a new high is formed. This brings buyers back to the market. The big player starts absorbing these market buy oders with his sell limit orders to buy the dollar. Then the course is pushed down. The stops of the long traders' create a chain reaction, which means the price goes down faster.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Now let's look at the situation of Friday's upward movement. At Point A around 2 p.m., a larger number of ask was absorbed and the course pushed up. This upward movement was very slow and sustainable as there was less volatility. At Point B there was a small exit from the euro and at Point C the big player got out of the euro entirely. The hoped-for outbreak did not come because the big player collected all available ask. 1132 Lot Ask were absorbed within 10 minutes (Point D).

The next thing that amazed me was the even absorption of Ask (Point E). These patterns are typical of a currency exchange. A major bank may have helped a key customer push the euro up so that he would have an advantage at Point D when he exchanged the euro for the dollar. If the customer had exchanged their euros at 1.12200, they would have received almost $ 350,000 less than at 1.12450. It is also conceivable that the customer already invested part of his money at 1.12200 and thereby realized an even higher profit. After all, this was an amount of $ 141 million. Currency exchange fees are very lucrative for the bank.

There is also a second option. Due to the low volatility, the upward movement dragged on over 3 hours. During this time, the big player had to buy new ask again and again in order to push the price further up. He tried to get out of his position at point B and C, but failed due to the low volatility. After forming a new high via Point C, he now used the new buyers to get out of his euro position completely.

The third possibility is that the big player at Point B and C has completely left his position and used the situation at Point D to buy the dollar massively.

Let us now analyze these three options with a view to a future course.

1st possibility

If a big player helps a key customer realize a better price to exchange for a dollar, it would be embarrassing if the price went up massively on Monday. The customer might have to do this currency exchange on Friday to pay salaries. If the bank had previously bought a large number of ask in the EURUSD (accumulation phase), it would have informed the customer that he should wait another day or two as the euro could still rise significantly. Instead, this exchange was carried out at Point D. The bank may have assumed that this is the best price for the customer. That would be an indication of a falling euro.

2nd possibility

If Point D was a kind of panic sale of the big player in order to get out of its euro position, it means that the big player does not believe in further, rising prices at this time. First of all, this speaks for a possible equilibrium, since there is no longer a major position in the market. The decisive factor here is what happens within the equilibrium on Monday and Tuesday.

3rd possibility

If the big player has used the situation at Point D to buy the dollar massively, this is a clear indication of future, falling prices. In order to eliminate possible short traders, however, a strong breakout upwards could occur beforehand.

We will see in the next few weeks whether that is enough to bring the price back to 1.10400. Should the price go down again, this zone would be an area where stronger buyers could enter the market again. As I mentioned earlier, long-term price forecasts are very speculative, as the big players always have to react to the retail traders at very short notice.

The big players dominate the market, but if there is a large number of short traders entering the market in a downward trend, the big players have to react. Iceberg orders (limit buy orders) initially intercept a large number of market sell orders from retail traders in order to hold the price down. This absorption usually takes place at several price levels so that it is not noticeable. While the price went down, the big player also filled the limit sell order levels with iceberg orders. As soon as the price does not get further down, the algorithms delete the limit sell orders that have been used and at the same time market buy orders are shot into the market. The big player thus manages to move the market strongly upwards with relatively few market buy orders. That also makes sense, since the big player is short orientated and needs as little ask as possible at this time. As a result, the market literally jumps up and the first stops of the short traders trigger another chain reaction that pushes the price further up. This action will stop short-term and medium-term traders and limit long-term traders in their profits. It is very beneficial for the big player that most traders pull their stops to secure their profits. After a longer downward trend, more and more stops are accumulating in the same price region. The big player only has to stop out the traders, after which he can push the course further down. If despite this action further short traders come into the market, the big player will simply sell his complete short positions to the retail traders, and then push the price up in the longer term. This action occurred between February 20 and 24 in EURUSD, when most of the retail traders were convinced that the open gap (180 pip from April 2017) will be closed. True Lies

Hello dear subscribers,

At first glance, trading appears to be very simple, you open an account with any broker, download the MT4 and you're good to go. As a beginner, you first have to get used to the MT4, that alone takes a lot of time. As soon as you have mastered the MT4 to some extent, the endless search for the Holy Grail begins in the form of free indicators. As soon as you have found a promising indicator, it is downloaded and the test phase begins. The settings of the indicator are continuously optimized until it is finally determined that this indicator does not meet the high expectations. Then you find a new indicator and the game starts over. The best indicators stay on the chart until one day the chart is completely overloaded. After a few years, you find that most of the indicators are useless and you just start to focus on the candles. As a result, the profits do not increase and the losses remain the same. This is also logical, since a candle is only the effect, the cause lies in the different market orders, that run in the limit orders. And that is exactly what we cannot see in the Forex market.

Finally, one tries to find EA's that automatically realize profits. You buy trading books, chargeable indicators and maybe look for the right trading coach. At the end of the day, you will resign and give up trading.Trading is basically like a profession. In order to practice a profession, you have to learn as an apprentice for at least 3 years. This includes practice and theory, you also have to spend time preparing for tests and exams. In 3 years, about 7500 hours add up. Once you have passed the exam, the learning really starts. After another 4 years you have the opportunity to attend the master school and after 10 years you have achieved your master title. A doctor, lawyer or notary also takes about 7-10 years to earn above average. In these 7-10 years you have to be willing to invest time and money to achieve the goal. That is about 20-25,000 hours of effort to then be able to professionally pursue a profession. Unfortunately, that's no different in trading, even if brokers and trading coaches try to convince us otherwise. A trading-coach sit in the Lamborghini, wave with a bundle of banknotes and promise the beginners the blue of the sky. Many believe that if a trading coach has so much money, it must be a good trader. Unfortunately, the opposite is  the case, because most coaches did not achieve their wealth through trading, but through the sale of their seminars.

On the stock exchange, 95% lose their money and only 5% fail to lose money. However, this does not mean that the 5% can make a living from their profits. Only about 2% of all traders actually manage that. The situation is no different for the trading coaches. In my opinion, only about 2-5% of all coaches work seriously.

I would immediately delete any trading coach who shows off his sports car, his property or a bundle of money slips from my list. I would also be careful if someone promises that you will trade successfully after their seminar. This is definitely a lie. The only thing a trading coach can do for you is to save you time in the long term and that's all. Imagine you want to lose weight, exercise or quit smoking. To achieve this, you are looking for a coach. This coach now gives you tips on how you can achieve your personal goal. Whether you actually achieve this goal depends entirely on yourself. It is questionable whether the method and approach of the trainer fits your ideas, in which all these points are crucial for optimal goal achievement. If you are a vegetarian and a fitness trainer recommends chicken as a protein supplier, your vision will not be fulfilled either. Of course there are alternatives, but unfortunately it is a bit more complicated in trading.

Every trading beginner first needs a rough orientation in order to develop.

1. How does the market work?

2. How do the big players work?

3. Workstation, screens, workplace, internet?

4. Time management as a part-time and full-time trader?

5. Shares, Future, Forex?

6. Which currency pairs, commodities, indices or stocks?

7. Scalper, Daydrader or Swingtrader?

8. Brokers, data feeds, software?

9. Money management, risk analysis, leverage, security, stops?

10. Fundamental, chart technique, technical analysis?

11. Breakout, reversal, pullback, range bound, continuation setup?

12. Indicators, EA, candles, tickchart?

13. DoM, time and sales, heat map, volume profile, spoofing?

14. Special aids, sounds, limit orders, iceberg orders?

15. Time units, chart views?

16. Opinions, press, news?

17. Psychology?

18. Continuing education, communication?

19. Daily trading evaluation / analysis?

20. Personal setup?

(In my blog you will find detailed information about all 20 points!)

In the last 10 years, I have adapted and optimized all these points again and again in my own study. I still haven't reached my final goal. I work on my development every day, because every standstill is a step backwards. I have read few books about trading and have never been to a trading coach because their statements have not convinced me. I have taken a path in trading that is second to none worldwide. This method is tailored to my trading style in order to generate the greatest success for me. With the help of a trainer, I would never have found this way.

Most coaches cannot give you a correct recommendation based on my 20 points, because every person is as individual as a thumbprint. If you are a Forex trader and a trading coach tries to reverse your polarity as a future trader, you have to start all over again. Basically, it's always a question of time and money. Of course you can learn something from every trainer and in the worst case you learn how not to do it. But you can usually save the money.

The 20 points I mentioned are the basis of your trading. On this you have to build the most important point, your personal setup. This setup tells you when to get in and out of the trade and unfortunately you have to find out for yourself. No coach can help you with this. If a coach claims that anyway, he is lying. The reason for this lies in our psychology, every trader is differently structured and therefore people, in the same situation, always react differently. Therefore, you will never be able to make the same trades as a trading coach. However, a suitable trainer can save you time so that you can find your suitable setup faster.

If you have enough time, I recommend investing 7-10 years to find your suitable setup. If you can manage these 7-10 years (20-25,000 hours), you could become very successful. With the right trainer you can possibly save 1/3 of the time, but first you have to find the right trainer. But forget to believe that you can trade better after coaching. Then you only know, what to focus on in the next few years.

Let us assume the following situation:

You already have basic trading knowledge and would have to learn 6 more years to become a successful trader. With a coach you can save 2 years and manage to be successful after only 4 years. For these 2 years you save, you are welcome to invest money.

Unfortunately I can't tell you where to find a suitable coach, but I can advise you to avoid the following coaches:

Coaches who advertise aggressively on social media.

Coaches who have their headquarters abroad.

Coaches who boast on money, cars and real estate.

Coaches who claim they can make you successful.

Coaches who scold their competition.

Coaches that offer volume trading.

Coaches who want to change your trading style completely.

Coaches who tell you how easy it is to trade.

Coaches who are cut down their trading products or reducing their prices.

Coaches who don't seem honest to you.

I have nothing against good coaches, only against the bad ones!

Always keep in mind:

If you trade successfully, it depends only on your setup and not on the ability of a trading coach. He may have saved you some time, but only you are responsible for your success. Likewise, you are solely responsible for your failure. In the worst case, you might find that trading is not for you. The most important thing is to stop trading immediately when you realize that it is not your world. This is not a failure, just think of how many professions there are where you would not feel comfortable. Of course, many people dream of financial independence, the chance of becoming an independent entrepreneur is twice as high as in trading. This is also an opportunity that you can take. There is an important sentence that applies to life: We have the chance to start anew every day. We should use that.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

It's not about being in first place in all areas, but about achieving the best price-performance ratio. I could have bought an equivalent CPU, but it would have cost twelve times more. The RAM only plays a subordinate role with these components. If you enter Google: PassMark Cpu, you will find your personal benchmark values. By the way, this helps you to determine the best price-performance ratio if you want to buy a new computer component soon.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Fast and furious

The identification of bid and ask via tones beat our sense of sight by a long way. With this I question a trading decision based on our eyes. Let's take a closer look at that.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Last Friday, 264 lots with 108 ticks (trading transactions) entered the market in the Euro FX within 1 second (from 08:58:48 - 08:58:49 CET). In the chart you can see the individual trading transactions and, below, a breakdown of how much bid and ask were contained in this trading transaction. Please note that this representation is 1 second.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Let's look at an evaluation. If 108 trades enter the market within 1 second, it means that you have 9.2 milliseconds to identify a trade. With our eyes, however, we need at least 40 ms to record information. This means that out of the 108 trades, we can effectively only identify 25 trades. With special tones coming from a loudspeaker, we would be able to identify 250 different pieces of information. With headphones and special sound programming, this value could double once again.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Point A
Here we see my time and sales list, which only shows the market sell orders that are known to run in the limit buy orders. The blue fields show when an equilibrium arises in the area of the sizes.

Point B
With a special filtering of bid, best bid and best ask, this information is passed on to a specially programmed tone.

Point C
This special programmed tone has the property of being completed within 1 ms. However, human hearing is only able to perceive different tones from 2 ms. In order to have some air and to ensure optimal perception, I will program the sound in the 1ms range. I chose a frequency range of 20-100 Hz, which corresponds to a lower tone, similar to a bass. I assigned this sound to the left speaker channel.

Point D
From there, this sound must be sent to a high-quality, external or internal sound card, since the sound card on the mainboard is usually not able to transmit these 1 ms tones to the speakers properly.

Point E
Here we see a time and sales list that only shows the market buy orders that are known to run in the limit sell orders. The blue fields show when an equilibrium arises in the area of the sizes.

Point F
With a special filtering of Ask, Best Ask and Best Bid, this information is passed on to a specially programmed tone.

Point G
This special programmed tone has the property of being completed within 1 ms. I chose a frequency range of 1000-2000Hz. that of a higher note is similar to the treble. I assigned this sound to the right speaker channel.

Point H
From there, this sound must be sent to a high-quality, external or internal sound card, since the sound card on the mainboard is usually not able to transmit these 1 ms tones to the speakers properly.

As we know, the human brain is divided into an analytical, logical left brain and an emotional, creative right brain. Basically there are asymmetries in this area, not both hemispheres of the brain are responsible for everything equally. We should take a closer look at these factors later, but first I did the sound distribution as follows.We hear the different ask tones (course wants to go up) with our right ear and the different bid tones (course wants to go down) with our left ear. Now let's take a look at how this works in practice.

Inserted Video

The tones that I have programmed here are only a rough draft and will be of course yet significantly optimized. Likewise, they are clearly too slow with about 3ms, but they are enough to understand the principle. To make a comparison, three known Windows tones have the following tone times: Windows note tone: 1350ms, Windows Ping: 1100ms and Chord: 650ms. The sounds you heard in the video were 200 times faster than the fastest Windows sound. These are worlds in trading. Maybe you noticed something in the video. There are significantly more tones coming in than there are bid and ask orders. This is because the penetration of the sizes (Best Bid and Best Ask) are included. The bass tones 20-100 Hz are much more memory intensive anyway and it is difficult to save them to less than 2ms. An alternative would be to use medium tone structures for the bid and higher tone structures for the ask. With this one could reach the 1ms range again. Another challenge is to assign the tones to a specific channel. My slogan is: it doesn't work, doesn't exist for me. If my tones don't exist, I'll build them myself.

My personal: what if plan!

I already use my smaller workstation for the MT4 structures and for trade protection. I have already considered the risk of defective water cooling in my workstation, but the processor could overheat and switch off due to poorer air cooling. I have analyzed both situations. I use my high-performance workstation primarily for stock exchange data, but also for trading Forex. If I were to trade via the MT4 on my second workstation, I would have to work with 2 mice and 2 keyboards at the same time. For reasons of efficiency, I decided to control the stock exchange and forex market with a mouse, since I am a seconds scalper.

I have secured myself as follows. I use my second workstation for my Metatrader charts. These run alongside, so I don't have to use the mouse or keyboard. In the background there is always a trading screen that I can access at any time when my first trading screen fails. If the power fails, I still have my cell phone, where I can close the trade at any time. I needed this protection because my virtual stop is no longer active in the event of a system failure. This could have fatal consequences, with the maximum threat to my account balance. However, this credit can always be kept very small by opening a second account, where you can move your money fast. I can save myself an uninterruptible power supply due to my cell phone. If you work with an uninterruptible power supply, you should include the router, otherwise it makes no sense. In 10 years the electricity has only failed 3 times and I was not in the trade. If the internet goes down, one should have the broker's phone number to close the trade over the phone.

Your comment is absolutely right and every trader should always have a what if have a plan. Before astronauts fly to the moon, they must be prepared for all emergencies. What if the food, water or air runs out? If one first start to think in an emergency situation, it is often too late. This is a very important point that everyone has to solve for themselves. One cannot plan all eventualities in advance, unfortunately there is always a residual risk, such as in the franc shock (EURCHF January 15, 2015).

As I wrote in my last article, the tones from the time and sales list and the structures in my specially filtered DoM are an important building block to identify clear patterns in the algorithms. Looking for patterns in the chart

Hello dear subscribers,

Every beginner and advanced Forex trader has spent a lot of time analyzing indicators, systems, setups or certain strategies. It is often a matter of identifying certain pattern structures in order to derive a specific trading decision. We know the best-known pattern identifications from the candle formations. Doji, Hammer, Morning Star and Hanging Man are just a few examples. Likewise, many traders follow certain pattern structures that take place within different indicators or in the course of prices. Today we want to take a look at the different patterns and find out how it makes sense to spend our time on them.

First of all, it is important to find out what kind of data we are getting in the forex market. The most important information is the price of the current course. With the help of time, a candle in the form of OHLC is formed from the price information. In MT4 there are nine different time units that the majority of traders use. We now have two pieces of information, price and time, from which a candle is formed. Since the time is fixed (M1, M5, M15 .....), the price information mapped from it will always create a random candle that looks different at each broker. If the candlestick formation from the price is a random representation, it should be clear that no clear pattern recognition can be derived from it.

Now we come to the indicators. Most of the indicators relate to the price within a fixed unit of time. In this respect, the same applies to the indicators as to the candle. This is just a random representation. It is impossible to derive a clear pattern recognition from a coincidence. Of course there are traders who do not work with time-dependent charts, such as Renko, or tick charts. However, these representations do not bring any decisive advantage either. The background is as follows: The price that we receive in the forex market is only a result. The actual cause lies in the market sell orders which run in the limit buy orders and the market buy orders which run in the limit sell orders. And it is precisely this information that we do not receive in the forex market. There is also the possibility to make a volume visible in MT4, but this has nothing to do with the actual total volume of the market.

In addition, the volume information in Forex does not help us because the volume is only an addition of bid and ask. Bid and ask have nothing to do with each other and never meet in the market, so you should always consider these factors separately. So if candles or indicators in this market are created only by chance, by the given time, a concrete pattern identification is automatically impossible. Of course, we often see that a price is repeatedly rejected at a certain price level and we believe that this is a strong resistance. The big players have so much money at their disposal that it would be easy for them to drive the course through this supposed resistance. In fact, it's always about misleading and stopping retail traders in order to get the crucial volume. This volume is recorded in the form of iceberg orders, so the big players can collect a certain number of asks or bids unnoticed without the majority of market participants noticing. And that is exactly the point. If most retail traders do not know what the big players are collecting, they will not be able to see where the price will head in the medium term. But even if a trader finds out what a big player is collecting, it won't do him much good either. He doesn't know when the big player has finished his collection campaign and he also doesn't know whether the big player will start a stophunting.

As we know, the big players use algorithms to control their market orders and limit orders. I have written a very detailed report that you can find here:

The interplay of algo

The sequence of upward and downward movements is always structured similarly. I would like to consciously speak of upward and downward movements here, because from my point of view there are no trends. The big players always align their strategies to the actions of retail and institutional traders. In EURUSD, for example, this means: 2-3 big players have to align their strategies with 1 million retail traders every day. Unfortunately, you can never tell in advance how the majority of retail traders will react to certain actions. Let's look at a typical situation. There has been a prolonged downward movement and suddenly the price is pushed up. This can mean that the big player exited the dollar in the course of the downward movement, but at this point in time he does not yet have an ask that would justify a stronger upward movement. First the price is pushed up a little and a sideways market (equilibrium) arises. In this sideways market, the big player is now beginning to collect a larger number of asks. After that, the price will continue to be pushed up. As soon as an increasing number of buyers enter the market, the big player uses this situation to get out of the euro. Even if he has already exited the euro, he will continue to drive the price up to attract more buyers. With the help of these buyers, the big player is now able to buy the dollar unnoticed with its sell limit orders and then drive the price sharply down.

In order to ensure a smooth process here, the big player uses specially programmed algorithms that are precisely tailored to his market orders and limit orders. First of all, it is clear that the big player has to collect a certain number of asks at a narrow price level. As soon as he has completed this collection, he will start pushing the price up. In order to push a price up, the big player usually has to invest a large number of asks (in the form of market orders). In order to avoid this situation, he previously occupied 5-10 sell limit levels in the DoM. Shortly before it pushes the price up, the algorithms withdraw the limit sell orders that were previously placed in the market. At the same time, the algorithms begin to shoot market buy into the market. With this little trick, the big player succeeds in pushing the price up massively with just a few lots. To push the price up by ten ticks in Euro FX at the moment, you normally need 600 lots. With this little trick, the big player only needs around 100 lots. The reason for this is as follows: First, the big player collected 500 Lot Ask at a price level to make a profit. If he now pushes the price up and had to spend 60 lots for a tick, the game would no longer pay off. In addition, we must not forget that he will have to get out of the euro again at some point. The less lots he has collected on the way up, the faster he is out of his position.

Now we come to a very interesting point. The big player algorithms were individually tailored to the behavior of the retail traders. These behaviors are always the same, so the big players are also able to use these algorithms on a regular basis. They are very complex to program because they require a specific coordination for the market orders, limit orders and also iceberg orders. It should be logical that recurring patterns are can be identified within these algorithms. The first problem is that there are different algorithms for different approaches. The big advantage here is that the algorithms are adapted, but not completely changed. This means that the resulting patterns do not change much. So if you want to identify patterns, you only have one chance to make the patterns of the algorithms visible. These patterns only appear in the DoM and in the time and sales list, since both representations are independent of time and volume. In addition, you need special software for this, which allows one to use unlimited filter settings. But even with the appropriate software, you are still a long way from achieving your goal, as you first have to find the optimal filter settings.

I use different charts to help me find patterns. The tones are also a crucial aspect that I have already written about in detail.

The hardest way, the algorithms

Hello dear subscribers,

In February 2018, I described the different algorithms of the big players in my blog. I initially looked for a way to read these algorithms in the Forex market, but this was not possible based on the incomplete data. As we already know, only price and time data are given in the forex market. The volume data we get in the forex market is useless. A normal volume is made up of the addition of bid and ask. Since no bid and ask are available in the forex market, the volume is generated from the ticks. A tick is a trade, but a trade can consist of a different number of ask and bid. In addition, a broker is only able to make its own traded volume available to its customers. However, this volume has nothing to do with the actual volume. Even if we had the specific volume available in the forex market, it would be of little use to us. A high volume shows interest at certain price levels, that's all. I find it particularly interesting that the bid and ask are added together, although the market buy orders and the market sell orders have absolutely nothing to do with each other, as they never meet. When a market buy order is placed by a retail trader, it only enters the market as soon as it is simultaneously accepted by a limit sell order from a big player. Of course, a retail trader can also place a limit order, just as big players use market orders. Now let's look at the individual orders.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

The market buy order of a retail trader can represent a purchase of the euro in EURUSD, but also an exit from the dollar. The big player who accepts the market buy order with his limit sell order could thus enter the dollar or exit the euro. As soon as a market buy order is placed, there are four different possibilities.

It is interesting that only the market orders are displayed in the stock market. In my opinion, the representation is not entirely correct. For example, if a retail trader buys the euro with his market buy order and the big player buys the dollar with his limit sell order at the same time, there are actually two open orders in the market. This would mean 1 lot in euros and 1 lot in dollars are invested. In fact, the volume shows us only one lot in the ask but no lot in the bid. But at some point these two orders will be canceled and it could happen that the retail trader exits his euro and the big player exits the dollar at the same time. In this case a lot bid is displayed even though both market participants are no longer in the market. That is exactly the problem, we only receive information about the market orders in the stock market, the limit orders remain in the background. Of course, it is clear to us that a market order must also activate a limit order at the same time, otherwise it would not enter the market. But what the individual participants are buying or selling with their respective orders remains unclear. With the Open Interest you can get more information here, which is only available in the Russian market.

Of course there must always be a buyer and a seller for an order, but if the market is just opening and a market buy order is accepted by a limit sell order, it means that there are now two different orders in the market. One market participant bought the euro, the other the dollar. From my point of view, that would normally be two lots, 1 lot ask and 1 lot bid. But we only see 1 lot of ask in the market. If both market participants exit their positions, 0 lot should actually be displayed, but in fact 1 lot bid is now displayed. Now the calculation is correct again, albeit a little offset. From a mathematical point of view, the variant carried out by the stock exchange is correct; the small change would give the trader a deeper market insight. However, I strongly doubt whether this is what the big players want. You can act hidden in the background with your limit orders (especially iceberg orders) without the majority of retail traders noticing what is happening in the market.

Personally, I wouldn't be in favor of getting better transparency on the market, because better transparency also increases the probability of retail traders winning. This automatically makes it harder for profitable traders. The background is that you can take relatively little profit from the big players because they hardly make any mistakes. Retail traders make the biggest mistakes, and increasing their odds makes it harder for already profitable traders. Of course, our biggest competitors are the big players, but the profitable traders usually only take the hard-saved money from their own colleagues (retail traders).

Now let's get back to the algorithms. The algorithms are nothing more than control sequences with which the big players coordinate their market orders and limit orders (iceberg orders). The goal is to generate as high a volume as possible from this (through the stops of the retail trader) in order to then take it up with your own limit orders. In my blog I have already described a few examples of the coordinated algorithms. I have been working specifically with these algorithms for over a year, although I have been able to identify a lot of specific patterns in them in the last few months. In theory, from my point of view, it is possible to track down the algorithms with the heatmap, the DoM and the Times and Sales list. In addition to optical identification modules, I primarily use acoustic alarm signals that are individually filtered. Depending on the filter setting, it is possible that in certain volatile phases up to 500 different tones come in per second.

First, a tone is requested by the filter setting in my software to pass this signal on to the sound card on my mainboard. With my older workstations, I quickly reached a limit here because the sound card was not able to process this mass of tones accordingly.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

For this I first put together a high-performance computer. Of course, the sound card on the new mainboard was much better, but the tones weren't displayed correctly here either. I bought an external graphics card to try out whether a different graphics card reproduces the tones better. The result was impressive, but when I started other memory-intensive programs, sound overlaps. An important point to properly process the tones is the sampling rate.

The term sampling rate (sampling frequency) is a technical term from signal processing, which, in addition to bit depth and dynamic range, is very often found in modern music production. The sampling rate says how often an analog signal that is sent to our audio interface via a microphone or an instrument is sampled during the analog-digital conversion. The unit is Hertz (Hz). It indicates how many points in the signal (samples) our computer has to remember in order to be able to reproduce it later without audible loss. Typical sampling rates are e.g. 44.1, 48, 88.2, 96 kHz up to 384 kHz. However, as the sample rate increases, so do the demands on our computer.

The Nyquist-Shannon sampling theorem or WKS sampling theorem (for Whittaker, Kotelnikow and Shannon) precisely defines how high the sampling rate has to be for a signal to be able to reproduce it later without loss. This means that a band-limited signal with a maximum frequency “fmax” can be exactly reconstructed if the sampling frequency “fsampling” is more than twice that of “fmax”. This means that if you want to record a signal with a maximum frequency of 20,000 Hz, the sampling rate must be at least 40,001 Hz. Curiously, my internal sound card had a higher sampling rate, but it tried to shift it to my processors. So there were problems. In the end I buyed an internal sound card that works with a sampling rate of 384 kilos of hearts at 32 bits. I'm curious to see whether this will improve the acoustic signals.

Thanks to my significantly faster computer, I was also able to increase the requirements for my filter settings. In my last articles I already talked about the importance of the values of Best Bid and Best Ask. The sizes in the Times and Sales list show me the specific situation in the area of limit orders. This enables me to identify a current penetration rate and also interesting patterns.

In order to display these sizes optimally, I had to create 53 different times and sales lists and filter them differently. I recorded a video for that.

It is also conceivable that the internet line is not able to optimally supply the 53 different smart tapes at the same time. Fortunately, I will now receive my fast fiber optic cable in a week, the work had been massively delayed due to the corona crisis. First and foremost, I am not interested in entering into a trade immediately based on a pattern identification. Rather, it is about using these patterns to find out what market situation one is currently in. The sequence of upward and downward movements is in principle always the same. There is a low point and then an accumulation phase, then there is a movement, then usually a re-accumulation phase, where further ask is collected. This is followed by the movement and an exit from the euro. Finally the rate is pushed up again and in this phase the dollar is collected, after which it comes to exhaustion and a high point. Now the price is pushed down and there is a distribution phase, after which there is another movement. The algorithms have to react differently in different phases. With the appropriate time, I am convinced that we can assign the reacting algorithms to specific phases. With this assignment, the current market phase can then be determined. First of all, you know exactly whether you are in an accumulation or distribution phase. But even within these phases there are different approaches that the big players use. It is now important to find out when the collection phases are over and which patterns can be used to identify the stophunting.

In principle, I would like to use this pattern recognition to set up so-called “traffic signs” in the chart, which show me exactly what is happening. From this, better trades can be planned and executed with a significantly higher probability. With my previous algorithm identification, I was only able to look into the future for a few seconds. With the “traffic signs” in the chart, one could plan a little longer.

That's 16-25 shots per second that the loudspeaker has to fire one after the other. This is not a problem for a good mainboard. With our filter setting, up to 30,000 different tone sequences are produced per minute in extremely volatile phases, that is 20 times as many per second and could be an explanation for the fact that the sound card is overloaded.

In principle, the enormous number of signals is sent into a tube and there is a blockage because the tones cannot be transmitted to the speakers quickly enough. This can be due to the mainboard, the length of the tones or the speakers. So far, no one has had a problem with it, because there was no one who worked with such an extreme number of tones. There is not a single literature on it worldwide, maybe we are really the only ones who deal with it. We will deal with special sound engineers who are familiar with it, maybe they have an explanation for it.

The sound makes the music

Hello dear subscribers,

In the last few weeks I had relatively little time because I had to deal intensively with my projects. I would like to briefly share the first results with you today.

In May I wrote an interesting article about the different perceptions of the eyes and ears.

Fast and furious

It turned out that the ears can absorb information up to 20 times faster than our eyes. From this I developed a strategy to use the tones to expand this information advantage.

Why trade with the eyes when the ears are 20 times faster.

As a result, I replaced all of my hardware in order to be able to identify these tones in real time.

The hardest way, the algorithms

Most recently, I ordered a high-quality graphics card and found that this graphics card did not meet my requirements. It had to do with the latency, which we will take a closer look at below.

The transmission of the data via the bus takes a certain time, there is a delay between the moment when the sound card provides a sample value and when this value arrives in the program (mediated by the driver) or vice versa. This delay is known as latency.

The matter is made more complicated by the fact that it has to be strictly regulated who is allowed to send what via the bus and when so that nothing gets lost or mixed up. That swallows some computing power. In addition, a safety reserve must be built in for the serial transmission of FireWire and USB, which can intercept the interruption of the data stream within certain limits. For this purpose, so-called sample buffers are interposed, which always hold a certain amount of the data stream in stock in order to prevent a gap. These buffers increase the latency (common values are in the range of 64 to 512 samples). Advantage of PCI: Thanks to parallel transmission and high data transfer rate, the buffer can usually can be set smaller than with USB or Firewire interfaces, which reduces latency.

But not only the data transmission is subject to latency, the ADC and DAC components also need a certain amount of time for the conversion, which is around 1ms to 1.5ms - really not much, but it adds up. The last thing in the problematic league of latencies is the audio software or the computer's processor: It must be able to calculate so quickly that the next value for conversion arrives at the sound card for conversion or can be fetched from the card when recording . If there is a gap here, the converters lack the information, or the pending sample of the recording is not saved, which leads to the same result in both cases: it cracks.

Additional latency can arise from plug-ins in the audio program. Not all plug-ins generate noticeable latency. However, a look-ahead compressor must e.g. first measure the level, before he knows whether he has to regulate. Even the fastest sound card driver cannot change such latencies. The fact that these delays occur does not necessarily have to be a disadvantage in every situation. As long as the ear has no comparison to the (direct) signal with no latency, the delay does not matter at all. This is e.g. This is the case with internal mixing when only tracks are played back - whether or not there is a delay of 23ms after pressing Play does not matter. You can even increase the latency in a targeted manner in order to have more computing power available (the processor then has more time until the next sample has to be sent to the sound card).

Latency becomes annoying as soon as there is a relationship between input and output. If you play a virtual synthesizer that is calculated on the computer, you can feel every major delay that occurs between the key press on the keyboard and the sound that is triggered. Even a singer who hears himself in his own headphones with a slight delay will not feel comfortable because the direct signal that he, among other things, Heard over his skull bones with the delayed signal on the headphones superimposed. In this case, however, a remedy can easily be found using direct monitoring. The singer simply receives a signal tapped from analog or directly behind the converter, and thus hears himself almost instantly. This so-called direct monitoring is now part of the standard equipment of audio interfaces.

I was able to determine that a simple USB sound card for € 20 had a significantly lower latency than the high-quality graphics card for € 150. Next, I inserted a graphics card that I controlled via a USB-C input. This was a significant improvement. There are now two concrete alternatives, a high-quality sound card with direct monitoring, which is controlled via the PCI and a sound card via USB-C. Then I have to find out whether the buffer can actually be set smaller via PCI so that the sound is displayed better than via USB-C.

Why is that important?

In high volatile phases my filter settings reach a rate of 500 tones per second. I have already been able to reduce this extreme load by programming my own tones that are in the millisecond range. I control the left loudspeakers for the filtered Bid tones and the right loudspeakers for the filtered Ask tones. The ear can identify different tones from 2ms, so I'm already on the right track. The lower the latency, the cleaner the sounds are reproduced and, in addition, no sounds are swallowed. This is particularly important in order to identify clear patterns in the tones.

My new fiber optic connection will be laid in the next week and a few preparations are necessary for this. I think I'll be ready to go again by the middle of the week. The fact is: The algorithms create recurring patterns in the DoM and the Times and Sales list, while one won't find any patterns in the price or in the candles. As soon as I am further with these patterns, I will inform you about them and give you some concrete examples.

I wish you a nice weekend and a good start to trading on Monday.

Kind regards Michael

Hear the algorithms

Hello dear traders,

Today's post is the longest article I've ever written here. On the one hand, I will go into more detail on my new trading chart and try to explain certain patterns within the algorithms. However, my main project is the different tones that give me much clearer and more effective patterns. This makes it theoretically possible to trade profitably without a chart. I will go into that in more detail at the end.

In the past few weeks I've finalized a few crucial things

1. A new high-end workstation was put together and set up.

2. A fiber optic line with a ping of 4-5ms has been installed.

3. A 75 inch 4K screen replaced 4 of my screens.

4.3 Tones with a latency of 1ms were developed

5. An optimal sound card can now record up to 500 tones per second

6. My workplace has been completely rewired and shielded.

These changes were necessary because I've been dealing with the algorithms of the big players for a long time and intensified this at the beginning of 2020. At that point in time it was not clear to me which hardware and software requirements this step required. I became aware of this when the translation software I used for the stock market data was developed with a completely new software architecture. So far my software, which is programmed in C #, used the CPU to perform the arithmetic operations. Depending on the comparison of GPU / CPU, a graphics processor can be up to 10 times faster than the central processing and control unit of a computer. For this reason, the newly developed software takes advantage of the faster GPU to perform certain computing operations. This reduces the load on the CPU, which can then be used for other operations.

When I started the first experiments with my tones, I used tones that were in the 100ms range and my CPU slowed down enormously in high volatile phases. Even when I developed tones that were in the 1ms range, my old software was so stressing the CPU that the speed of the tones had to suffer. Since the new software relieves the CPU, I can hear clear tones again, even in extremely volatile phases. As I already wrote in several articles, the tones are a decisive advantage in retail, as tones can be perceived up to 20 times faster than graphical representations. The stock market is all about probabilities and a market advantage. The time plays a decisive role for a seconds scalper, both in terms of incoming and outgoing data packets. Of course, I am dependent on the ping time of my broker when placing a trade order.

The data transmission rate for sending and receiving (down and up speed) measures the amount of data that can be transmitted over an information channel such as the Internet in a certain time. To do this, however, you first have to establish a connection. When you visit a certain website, your computer first sends a request to the website's server. According to the motto "I am there and want to request data from you". If available, the server also sends back a data packet and confirms this request. The time span for sending and then receiving a data packet is called the packet delay. Also known as the round trip time (RTT) or ping.

When you send a trade order to your broker, relatively small amounts of data are sent on the journey; the ping is crucial here. The faster your data package reaches the broker, the faster your order can be processed.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Here I made a ping comparison of three different brokers. While it takes an average of 20ms to send a data packet with the first broker, the best broker only needs 10ms. These three comparisons are nevertheless very fast, as there are also ping times of over 200ms. The ping times depend on various influencing factors. The type of broadband technology, but also the distance between the servers, influence the latency period. A normal speed test is of relatively little use, since a server is addressed that has nothing to do with your broker.

You can measure your ping time to the broker yourself with Windows. Enter Windows “Start” “Execution” and then “cmd”. A black screen should now appear. Now enter the following: "ping google.de", this will give you the ping time to communicate with the Google server. If you enter the website of your broker, you will receive your personal ping values. My ping times in the speed test are 4-5ms, but I can only reach my broker in 8-10ms. But the trading orders with my broker in the forex market have a decisive advantage over the futures market. In the futures market there is not always liquidity, while a market maker almost always provides me with liquidity. This means that I am usually faster in the forex market than in the future market.

My developed tones are a great trading advantage as they tell me the current activities of the major market participants. Sometimes I was able to determine that the tones of the market orders and limit orders come in faster than the graphic display in the times and sales list. The advantage is often only in the ten millisecond range, which is sometimes enough to get a better start. The orders in the Times and Sales lists run down so quickly that you can't tell them apart. The tones have a clear advantage here, especially since I have assigned the bid tones to the left and the ask tones to the right speaker channel. I am less interested in the market orders, but rather in the limit orders when they hold up the market orders. As I wrote in several articles, limit orders determine market behavior. The big players collect a certain number of market orders with their limit orders in order to be able to enter or exit. This can be represented faster and more clearly with tones. You will see and hear some examples of this today.

In the forex market we cannot tell from the candles what the big players have collected. We know: the price is only the result of the market orders that entered the limit orders. And it is precisely this information that is not available in the forex market. Nevertheless, one can ask oneself whether one could have foreseen that with the stock market data.

Point E

This allows you to absorb the volume of retail traders immediately or delete the iceberg orders in order to then move the price strongly in your direction with a small number of market orders. Point F

There are a few ways a big player will hold or stop a course.

1. He wants to get out of his position or get out with a partial position.

2. he want the movement to continue, but at this point too many traders are headed in the same direction that need to be stopped first.

3. The big player wants to keep collecting and an equilibrium arises.

4. The big player is out of position and has already collected orders for the countermovement, we are on a high or low.

5.The course comes to an artificially created resistance zone, the big player intends to continue the movement, but wants to give the impression that a trend reversal is taking place. Many retail traders fall for it and are stopped out. This allows the big player to buy new orders at a lower price level.

These are just a few examples, the key is to find out why a course is being held up. Of course, this cannot always be precisely determined in individual cases, but it is possible to precisely analyze where a course was held and these are often decisive price ranges.

Bionic dance

Hello Guido,

nice to hear from you again. This is basically a great idea, but it could be problematic.

The term beats per minute became popular in the disco era and is mainly used today in dance and electronic dance music. Since normal bodily functions of a person run at 72 heartbeats per minute, these are the norm for the question of whether the frequency of the beats per minute has a stimulating or calming effect on the recipient. Tempi with a high frequency (over 72 bpm) have a stimulating effect, while those with less than 72 bpm have a calming effect.

Hip-Hop typically has tempos between 70 and 120 bpm, while House is faster at 110 to 140 bpm. The jungle is even faster with 140 to 190 bpm, while terror tempos over 200 bpm and speedcore and speed metal even reach up to 300 bpm. With the splittercore, the bpm is even between 700 and 1000, which corresponds to 16 beats per second. The "Bionic Dance" would be between 15,000 and 30,000 bpm, which would be very stimulating indeed. I found a very interesting video that depicts the tones between 90-100000 bpm.

Inserted Video

From 2000 bpm it is almost impossible to tell the tones apart. A Youtuber remarked: "Your heart beats in sync with the music you're listening to". If that is indeed the case, 500 tones per second is not healthy. Even an electric shock (50Hz) ensures that our heart only beats 50 times per second. That is still 10 times less than my tone identification of the algorithms in high volatile phases.

Inserted Video

However, the volatility on Friday night when this video was recorded was relatively low. I'll make a recording when Frankfurt, London and the USA are in the market at the same time and an important meeting is also imminent. Some of my friends who work with a similar tone setup because of my motivation find the tones to be a great aid in daily trading.
