Hint! How you can save a lot of time in trading

Hello dear traders,

we all know that screen time is a critical factor in success. Let's assume that it would take a trader 15,000 hours of screen time to trade profitably. Now let's look at three different traders. The full-time trader spends 10 hours a day on the screen, the part-time trader 5 hours and the casual trader 2 hours a day. In five years, the full-time trader will have 15,000 hours of screen time. To get the same screen time, the part-time trader would need ten years and the casual trader 25 years. This would mean that the occasional trader would never have the opportunity to practice this profession full-time.

Today I would like to give you a little tip on how you can shorten these times significantly.

In EURUSD 1440 M1 candles are created daily. If one analyzes the last ten years, one finds that of these 1440-daily M1 candles only about 600 M1 candles are interesting for the trade. On the one hand, this is due to the fact that the price trend is in a sideways market or equilibrium in two thirds of the cases, and thus in a lower volatility. The interesting trading hours in the Euro EURUSD are between 7 a.m. and 19 p.m. This is exactly where Frankfurt, London and the USA act in the market. At around 2:30 p.m. are all participants are in the market.

A trader sits in front of his screen, waiting for the right opportunity to place his trade. Due to market movements, however, we know that relatively little happens over 50% of the time and that the volatility is often so low that it even makes no sense to place a corresponding trade.

Why are there more sideways movements than up or down movements in a price trend?

As we know, the big players in a sideways market have to collect a certain number of asks or bids before they can push the price in their profit direction. Once they have reached their goal, they have to get out of their position and collect a new position, which in many cases leads to a sideways market again. These collect action are often boring because they take place for many hours in a sideways market.

Every trader who works with indicators or stock market data knows that there are certain situations that are particularly interesting for him because he can learn crucial things from them. But he has to spend at least 50% of his screen time waiting in order to be able to analyze these decisive movements. Part-time or occasional traders are at a decisive disadvantage, as they usually have to practice their profession during main trading hours. In doing so, they dont see the decisive movement sequences that would help you to build up experience.

In order to take with you at least a small part of the experience, I recommend that you record your trading screen if you cannot observe the market yourself at this point. There is a free screen recording program that I've been using for some time.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

First you have to download and set up the screen recording program. Then I recommend bringing all relevant charts together on one screen. Then you just start recording and let the charts run when you're doing your job or doing other things. I also found a small video for this video recording program, where everything is explained in detail.

Inserted Video

For me, too, there are sometimes situations where I can't sit in front of my screens and that's exactly when this screen recording program comes into play. To record a 4K screen for 1 hour, approximately 1GB of storage capacity is required, with HDMI resolution only half. When you come home from work in the evening, you can pull out exactly the most interesting aspects in 2 hours and thus significantly increase your learning effect. The most interesting videos of the week can also be analyzed more closely at the weekend.

As a general rule, precautions should be taken if you leave a running computer in your home because of a possible fire hazard. You should also take into account an additional power consumption of around 1KW per hour. If the computer is running 10 hours a day, this is approximately € 2.30 electricity consumption. The learning effect that is gained from it is, however, worth significantly more.

I also created my last video with this program. I only have to optimize the recording of the sounds a bit.

Inserted Video

I would be happy if the idea helps you and I wish you a successful trading week

In addition, I am able to scale my risk and profit opportunities with the number of lots invested. With 20 trades that last an average of 30 seconds, I am actually only 10 minutes in the market of the most volatile 600 trading minutes. --- 帖子 #1544 ---
Increase in trading efficiency

Hello dear subscribers,

Every trader would like to make more money in the same amount of time without taking a higher risk. Today I want to show you a way how you can significantly improve your trading efficiency without changing your setup or your approach.

As I wrote in my last post, you have to deduct the costs from your income to get a profit. In trading, however, it is not enough to offset your losses against your profits. There is one more crucial factor that is often forgotten: the brokerage costs. Of course, there are different types of billing for the costs at the brokers. Some offer a fixed commission plus spread, others only charge a spread only. Even if you are trading with a pure spread, these costs must also be taken into account, as you always start in the minus at the beginning of the trade. Let's take a look at how the spread is created in the futures market.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Point A

Here we see a classic DoM, on the ask side are the limit sell orders and on the bid side the limit buy orders. There is a green number on the price ladder, this is Best Ask. The red number is the best bid. A purchase entry always begins on the best ask side, a sales entry always begins on the best bid side.

Point B

A 16 lot market buy order is now placed on the Best Ask page. The spread is one tick or 0.5 lot, since the best bid and best ask are close together.

Point C

The 16 lot market buy order now literally eats its way into the limit sell orders and at the same time drives the best ask price up.

Point D

We can see that the best bid price has still not left its position. This is because there are no limit buy orders on the left. The spread has now widened to 8 ticks or 4 pips.

Point E

Now more limit buy orders come into the market and the spread is reduced to one tick or 0.5 lot.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Now let's look at an example that has happened to every trader before.

Point A

A big player brings a larger number of market buy orders into the market.

Point B

This literally shoots the price upwards, creating a strong bullish candle. A trader now believes that the price will continue to rise and positions a 1 lot market buy order on the best ask side. The spread is 4 pips or 8 ticks, which many traders only notice when they are already in position.

Point C

Since the price has risen very quickly, the limit buy orders are not able to fill the gap quickly enough. The big player takes advantage of the situation and pushes the price down with relatively few sell market orders.

Point D

The spread now widened to 16 ticks or 8 pips. Our trader is still standing with a market buy order at position 1.10085. Since the price has already gone down by 8 pip, there is a high probability that the stop has already triggered. This stop provides another push down.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

If you want to place a buy order, you basically go to the Best Ask page. As soon as you want to get out of this position, this is only possible via the best bid page. If you want to place a sell order, you basically go to the best bid page. As soon as you want to get out of this position, this is only possible via the Best Ask page. The closer the best ask and best bid side are together, the smaller the spread.

You can enter the market immediately with a market order, but you run the risk of paying a higher spread. A limit order usually ensures that you get the smallest spread of a tick. Unfortunately for most of them this only applies to the futures market, but not to the forex market. In the forex market, it makes no difference to me whether I enter the market with a market order or a limit order, I always have to pay the spread specified by the broker. Of course, with a limit order, the spread is only due if the limit order is filled. Nevertheless, this is a significant disadvantage compared to the futures market.

These were all points why I took a closer look at the spread in the forex market. First of all, each of you is able to visualize the best ask and best bid line in the chart in your MT4. This may give you a better overview. In order to effectively monitor the spread over the day, I got hold of a few different indicators. At the weekend I did the evaluation and I noticed something interesting in the last few weeks.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

First I carried out my spread evaluation in a tick chart, as an M1 would not have made any sense. The difficulty was that most spread indicators do not run on a tick chat. But this is crucial, because so much different spread information comes in within 1 minute that it cannot be evaluated within an M1 candle. You can see a 32 tick chart in EURUSD here. I once tried to mark the different movements with lines. This is not that easy, because within an upward movement there are also smaller downward trends and vice versa. The yellow dots show the average spreads in the different movements. I already noticed there that my spread was significantly higher in an upward movement than in a downward movement.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

I wanted to investigate that more closely and took a closer look at a 2 tick chart. Interestingly, this is where the highest spreads often emerged in an upward movement.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

I evaluated different charts and found that the spreads are on average 40% higher in an upward movement. However, no fundamental deduction can be made from this, as it can look different for every broker and trader. For this reason I can only rely on my own evaluation. This may also have been a coincidence and is therefore not representative.

Liquidity gives us crucial information

Hello dear subscribers,

Anyone who trades in the forex market and only uses forex data has a decisive disadvantage. He is able to see the result of a price war, but he cannot identify the cause. The result of the price war is always the price movement, but what triggered it remains hidden in the forex market. Due to the fixed time (M1, M5 ...), the candles always arise within a random formation. By chance it is never possible to identify a clear pattern sequence that supports a sustainable winning strategy. This means that the chance of winning is well below 50% and makes long-term profit optimization difficult for us.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

As I have already written in many posts, the actual reason for the price movements is exclusively in the market orders that run into the limit orders. The market sell orders (Point A) initially run into the limit buy orders (Point B). The larger the number of market sell orders, the higher the probability that they can break the limit buy orders. The higher the number of limit buy orders, the higher the probability that they will be able to absorb the market sell orders. This gives the result of whether or not the price is going down another tick. It is the same with the market buy orders (Point C), which run into the limit sell orders (Point D).

While the limit orders represent the liquidity, the volume results from the market orders. The amount of liquidity and volume is always the same during an order execution, since a market order must always be accepted by a limit order. A market sell order is placed by a seller, which is placed by a buyer of a limit buy order. This is exactly how a market buy orders are placed by a buyer, which is accepted by a seller of a limit sell order. A market sell order will never meet a market buy order as they always have to run into a limit order. Interestingly, they are still next to each other in a footprint chart, although they have nothing to do with each other. In a volume chart, the market sell orders are now added together with the market buy orders. From this one can deduce that an increased battle took place within this price level, but that was all.

A price movement therefore only arises because the number of market orders was so large that they could completely buy up the limit orders at one price level. But already here the danger lurks in the form of iceberg orders. If there are 20 limit buy orders in the DoM, this does not mean that you can move the price down by one tick with 21 market sell orders. There may be an iceberg order of 100 lots at this price level, although only 20 lots can be seen in the DoM. In principle, it is almost impossible to identify iceberg orders, but with the help of spoofing algorithms and a corresponding filter setting, the probability is high that certain iceberg zones can be identified beforehand. This usually results in interesting resistance zones that you can use to your advantage.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Basically, the price movement always arises from the market orders that run into the limit orders. However, there is still a crucial psychology that is based on the waiting limit orders in the DoM.

Point A

Here we see the limit buy orders that are waiting in the DoM to be activated by the market sell orders.

Point B

Here we see the limit sell orders that are waiting in the DoM to be activated by the market buy orders.

These limit orders represent the liquidity in the market and are at the same time a prospect of the future. Liquidity is the basis for executing a market order. If there was no liquidity, the market order would have no chance of being executed. By placing a limit order, the participant declares their willingness to be executed at a certain price level in the future. Thus, the limit orders in the DoM are, so to speak, an outlook into the future. Unfortunately, these limit orders can also be withdrawn again, resulting in a changed relationship between demand and supply.

For example, if a price goes up and suddenly an above-average limit sell order is placed in the DoM, many participants believe that the price on these limit sell orders will be held up. Some are now exiting their long position, other traders are opening a short position. Suddenly the big player withdraws his large limit sell order and pushes the price through strongly upwards. With the spoofing algorithms, it is possible to find out beforehand whether this is a possible fake order or not.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

We have three important pieces of information that we have to pay attention to. The limit orders in the DoM are in a way a possible glimpse into the future, whereby you always have to include the possible iceberg orders. The executed market orders show the short-term price direction, while the executed limit orders show the long-term price direction. First and foremost, I concentrate on the executed limit orders, which I analyze with the help of my special limit delta. These limit orders are the key to success, as the big players within an equilibrium collect a certain number of limit orders in order to then bring them to a profit. If you can find out at which price levels the big players have collected a certain number of limit orders, this also increases the probability of winning.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

As we know, the EURUSD is not one of the most volatile currency pairs. I measure the strength of the dollar using the seven different currency pairs shown here. The figures here show the percentage change compared to the previous day. The EURUSD reach a medium volatility. Volatility is a critical factor for any trader, but it too depends entirely on volume and liquidity.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Point A

If we have a large number of market orders that run into low liquidity, this results in high volatility. At the same time, the spread increases, but so does our chance of winning.

Point B and C

When the volume and liquidity are balanced, a standard situation arises within which normal trading is possible.

Point D

If the volume is low but the liquidity is high, this results in low volatility. The spread is small, but at the same time the risk of a loss increases as you have to stay longer in the market and uncontrolled breakouts can destroy the profit.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

I achieve my highest probability of winning within normal volatility, because then, with the help of my selected algorithms, I have the highest chances. The highest volatility in EURUSD arises with the entry of London and the USA. Interestingly, my probability of winning before and after is significantly higher. I recommend every trader to make such an individual evaluation to find out when trading is particularly worthwhile. In the last few months I have concentrated more on the liquidity of the limit order. As we know, it is primarily the larger market participants that provide the liquidity, as they can use the iceberg order to collect a certain number of ask or bids unnoticed. Iceberg orders are only available within limit orders. Since the iceberg orders in EURUSD account for more than 60% of sales, it is logical that this strategy should be attributed to the larger market participants.

For this reason we have to remember: It is not the news that determines the market, but the market that determines the news.

Hello dear subscribers,

As we know, the big players collect their ask or bid within an accumulation or distribution phase with the help of smaller iceberg orders, which are hidden behind the limit orders. These iceberg orders are difficult to identify. As soon as the collection campaign has been concluded, the current market situation will decide whether to stopfishing. If, after a completed accumulation phase, the majority of retail traders take a short position, there is no reason for a stophunting and the price can be pushed up. For this purpose, limit sell orders previously placed on the market are deleted and, at the same time, smaller, cumulative market buy orders are shot into the market with the help of the algorithms. As soon as the stops of the short traders are triggered, a chain reaction occurs and the price literally explodes upwards.

In principle, order book trading in conjunction with the Times & Sales list is very advantageous for short-term trading. First of all, every trade from the Times & Sales list is displayed in a tick chart, regardless of the number of orders placed. These time-independent ticks are now connected with a line and our well-known candles (OHLC) are created from this. In the forex market you can also create tick charts, but one essential aspect is missing: the number of orders. It is therefore not possible to display the respective sizes of the limit orders in the DoM in the Forex market. These quantities are a crucial aspect when reading out algorithms.

Forex versus future

The big players can move the markets, but they have a decisive disadvantage compared to us retail traders. A retail trader in the forex market can press Buy or Sell at any time and is in the market with 1 lot. This is because our broker provides the necessary liquidity. A big player in the Forex market trades with a few 100,000 lots and unfortunately these are not immediately available in the market. Therefore, he must first collect this 100,000 lots in order to then bring it to profit. This is one of the reasons why the markets have a 70% sideways movement. There are 3 different ways that the big player uses to realize profits. Let's take a closer look at this now.

Collecting in an accumulation or distribution phase

In 80% of the cases, a collection campaign takes place within an accumulation or distribution phase. The price is kept within a range and the required ask or bid is collected with the help of iceberg orders. The stops of the retail trader are a kind of turbo in order to reach the necessary quantities faster. As soon as the goal is reached, the current market situation decides whether or not to stophunting. If the collection action is completed within an accumulation phase and there are still more buyers in the market at this point, stophunting will take place downwards. Then the course is pushed up. On the way up, the big player has to invest another significant number of asks. Now you have to know that it is much easier for a big player to get into positions than to get out again. The reason for this is very simple. The longer a price goes up, the higher the likelihood that the market will assume a major pullback will occur. If the big player wants to get out of his ask position, he has to find traders who believe that the price will keep going up. The further up a course has gone, the more difficult this situation becomes.

For this reason, the big player uses the pullbacks within the upward movement to sell the ask that helped him push the price up. After all, at a lower price level, he has collected a certain number of asks, which he now wants to bring into profit. If he were to collect the entire ask in the upward movement as well, he might have massive problems near the high to get out of all positions. However, he will only sell the short-term asked ask (to push the price up) if he was able to collect his optimal amount within the accumulation phase. Collecting in an accumulation or distribution phase takes place when the market is in a normal situation. This is 80% the case and is therefore a known practice.

Course push through

In certain market situations it can happen that the big player does not have the time or opportunity to carry out a lengthy collection campaign. Then the course is simply pushed upwards. The algorithms now shoot market buy orders into the market and at the same time withdraw the limit sell orders that were previously placed on the market. The price shoots up and the short trader's stops help accelerate the price upwards. At some point the price slows down because retail traders are no longer willing to place further buy orders. The price is slowing down and the first sellers are entering the market. The big player now intercepts these sellers with his limit buy orders and can buy further Ask. Then the algorithms start pushing the price up again and the stops of the short traders accelerate the movement upwards. This strategy includes what is known as an average calculation. Let us assume that the price moves up by 100 ticks and in this way the big player invests 1000 lots. If he manages to get out of his ask position after 100 ticks, it is exactly as if he had collected 1000 lots at a certain price level and then pushed the price up by 50 ticks. This approach is often used in somewhat uncertain market conditions or in situations where the big player has little time.

Buy up your own volume

A somewhat more risky option that a big player can use arises in times when there is hardly any volume in the market. Since a big player collects ask or bids via his iceberg orders in most cases, he is automatically dependent on volume (market orders). In order to collect this volume more quickly, in most cases he uses the stops of the retail traders. However, if the current market situation is so weak that a below-average number of market orders come into the market, this can lead to the big player making volume available to itself. To do this, he first selects a certain price level, which he places an extremely large limit sell order on. Then he pushes the price to this price level, and his algorithms shoot an extremely high number of market buy orders into the market. These market buy orders are now absorbed by their own limit sell orders. At this price level he has now acquired 1000 Lot Ask and 1000 Lot Bid. The retail traders can now see that a large position of market buy orders has entered the market. They are all trying to take a buy position right away. The big player is now pushing the price down and the long trader's stops help him to accelerate the price down. At the low, an equilibrium arises, where the big player exits his short position and at the same time builds a new ask position. Then he pushes the price ten ticks above the price level where he has made liquidity available to himself. Retail traders know that 10 ticks below this price level is an extremely large ask position and are now expecting a stronger upward movement. The big player uses the fact that an extremely large number of buyers are now entering the market to get out of his ask position. Then the big player is out of the market.

These are the three main ways a big player uses to realize their winnings. First and foremost, he will use the accumulation or distribution phases to collect his orders in peace. However, he needs an average market situation and enough time for this. If one of these things is not given, he has the opportunity to push through the course or to provide liquidity himself. These two alternatives have the advantage that they require significantly less time, but they involve a significantly higher risk potential. Now one could assume that a big player in an uncertain market situation has the possibility of not entering into any trade. However, this is not an option for the big player. We all know that the money the big players own is not their property, but belongs to different investors who expect a certain return. Money that is not invested in the market can therefore not yield any returns. The largest banks generate up to 60% of their balance sheet profits from the Forex market. Money that is not invested in the market is dead capital and that's why it needs to be invested. However, the big players think carefully about the possibilities with which they can achieve the highest probability of winning.

Big players experience the greatest stress when they exit their positions, because after all, this exit decides on the daily return on their capital. After an accumulation phase, the course is pushed up. If you take a closer look at the high of a price trend in the futures market, you will find that it is not possible for a big player to get out of his position with 1000 lots. For this very reason, the big player gets out of his position shortly before the high. Most of the time, we can then see that the price continues to move up for a while before it finally changes into a downward movement.

Of the twelve big players who control 85% of the market, only the first three have extremely high capital. Smaller big players who are active in the market must have an emergency plan for their exit. A smaller big player collected 1000 Lot Ask in an accumulation phase and then pushed the price higher. Now he begins to exit his position with his limit sell orders within the upward movement. Now suddenly a bigger big player comes into the market, who pushing the price down. The smaller big player who wants to get out of his ask position would now be left behind and give up massive profits. For this reason, an equilibrium is first created where the smaller big player tries to get out of his position. In the extreme case, he has to give back a large part of his winnings, especially when a bigger player comes and uses a "course through strategy".

Many traders have suspected for years that the big players form a kind of consortium and therefore work together. However, this is a fallacy because if you work together you have to share the profit. The real reason why the big players so rarely compete is the fact that they see exactly what the other big players are investing. So if a big player collects massive ask within an accumulation phase, there will hardly be another big player who collects bids in the same period. Of course, this inevitably leads to an involuntary collaboration, but this has the disadvantage of sharing the profit. Since every big player wants to achieve the highest possible profits, everyone tries to implement their own strategy as far as possible. Since around 20,000,000 lots are invested in Forex EURUSD per day, there are enough opportunities for many big players. Since we retail traders are unable to influence the market, we first have to find out which of the three strategies is currently being used in the market. Of course, it is also extremely important whether this is an accumulation or a distribution phase.

Conclusion:

As we can see, it is not easy for the big players to make their daily profits either. While they can influence the market in their favor at any time, they may have massive exit problems and need at least a few hours to collect their required contracts. Even though you collect your contracts with the help of iceberg orders, you still leave interesting traces that we retail traders can identify in our favor. The main part of the strategies take up the accumulation and distribution phases. This strategy is the easiest to identify. As soon as a big player makes liquidity available to himself, it is initially unclear in which direction he will push the course first. However, we then have a clear certainty that at some point he will have to return to the price level where he made liquidity available to himself. The most unclear situation is when a big player just starts pushing the course. If you couldn't make out a clear accumulation or distribution phase beforehand, you can be picked up.

As a scalper, I'm on the move at very short notice, but it is also extremely helpful there when you know exactly what is happening in the market. But even with accumulation or distribution phases you can very quickly make mistakes. I still remember February 2020 in EURUSD very well. The price went down and was in the process of closing the April 2018 gap. The big players had already collected a large number of limit sell orders within a distribution phase. So all traffic lights were on green in order to close the gap completely. However, the majority of all retail traders also assumed it and took a short position. The big players simply sold their short positions to the retail traders and then pushed the price 740 pips upwards. Nobody would have expected that.

Only then did the course run down and close the gap completely. Then the price went up 1400 pips. This shows that the big players are able to react very quickly to current situations. Those who are able to recognize this situation with the help of their software have a considerable market advantage over all other market participants. In order to trade profitably in the long term, one has to use the market advantages for oneself. These market advantages cannot be identified on the basis of news, the price or indicators, but only with a special instinct and software that shows you exactly what is happening in the market. Only those who are willing to train themselves daily in this market will one day have the chance to be a profitable trader. The chance of becoming a successful trader in the long term is 1 in 50. Incidentally, you need the same probability to reach three right numbers in the german lottery (6 out of 49). It's difficult, but not impossible.

Good luck this week.

Greetings Michael

Scalping with algorithms

Hello dear subscribers,

When I started trading, I never thought it could be this difficult. If one read the posts of brokers or the self-proclaimed trader coaches, one u think trading is as easy to learn as driving a car. I got my driver's license 37 years ago, during this time I drove 2,000,000 km, was able to complete some driving safety trainings and drove around 300 times over the Nürburgring (race track) to improve my driving skills. At the time I thought I am a good driver, until one day I drove as a passenger, with a Porsche Cup racing driver, across the Nürburgring. It was then that I realized that I could move my car, but that I was far from being a professional driver. It was similar when I got to know the way a high-frequency trader works 1.5 years ago. Here is the full report:

Learning from high frequency dealers

According to the testimony of professional traders, there are very few traders who become successful without a DoM or Times & Sales list. That motivated me because I was trading profitably without a DoM or Times & Sales List and expected an above-average increase in my success if I managed to use these instruments correctly. Switching from the Forex market to the DoM and the Times & Sales List in the Future Market is roughly comparable to getting out of a car and enter in the cockpit of an airplane. You sit there, stare at the DoM and T&S, wondering whether you've picked the right job. In the car you have to consider 2 dimensions, in the airplane 3 dimensions and in the stock market 4 dimensions in order to be successful. This is a special challenge that requires certain cognitive skills. In addition, one has to deal with dry theory about the formation of stock prices in order to understand how the markets work. At the beginning of my trading career, I had imagined it completely differently than I trusted the statements of brokers and the self-appointed trader coaches.

Anyone who claims, trading is very easy, has no feeling about the business, or he just don't like learning the enormous amount of dry stock market theory. Yes, I was lucky to lose little money right from the start and to reach my breakeven point after 2-3 years in order to trade profitably afterwards. But I never had the feeling that I was trading profitably based on my knowledge or experience, but attributed it solely to chance or luck. In the search for the big player algorithms I have recognized in the last 12 months that only the time and volume-independent charts are able to make visual and acoustic patterns visible with the help of certain filter settings. Interestingly, these patterns keep cropping up regularly in certain situations. In the DoM you can see how the limit buy orders on the best bid side and the limit sell orders on the best ask side are being eaten up by the market orders. Two numbers appear at the top of the Times and Sales list (Best Bid and Best Ask) that change so quickly that you can hardly read them. This is the eye of the tornado and that's the closest to the market. My software that I work with is effective and the best for my type of trading, but it too is already reaching its limits for my requirements. However, with the help of my own programming knowledge, I can break these limits. This is very complex and time-consuming, but the results speak for themselves.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Since he has had bad experiences with it in the past, he leaves the stop there. After a total of 3 hours he is stopped with 5 pips and has a loss of $ 50.

I don't care whether the beginner's approach is right or wrong. Of course, you can always find out afterwards what could have been done better. In theory, you can't make a mistake, because in the Forex market you can't know in which direction the price will move in the future. One can at most guess it and thus the profit or loss lies within a certain probability.

You would have had chances in this chart image, because there is a range of 15 pips between the high and the low. I just want to show that it is not that easy for most traders to trade profitably. Of course, this is an equilibrium in the chart, but this can only be determined when it has already arisen. This situation that we see here is an everyday situation, because 70% of price movements take place within an equilibrium.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

At the beginning of my trading career, I made similar mistakes and hoped for stronger moves in the market with my money management. When I discovered that the markets were 70% sideways, I aligned my strategies with that. I would like to describe three different situations in which the risk and the possible profit are identical in each case.

Situation 1

I have already described the following situation in detail. The stop is 5 pips and the TP is 10 pips. The decisive factor is the equilibrium, with the yellow arrow and the subsequent stophunting in order to eliminate the long traders. This gives you the opportunity to enter the market at Point A. Of course, there is also the possibility of entering the market at Point C, but this involves certain dangers. As we know, a so-called chain reaction occurs when stophunting. The big player pushes the price down and the first stops of the long traders are triggered. Depending on how many traders have come into the market at that time, the further down the chain reaction can run. This is also called the typical handle in a falling knife. That's why I would rather get into the running movement within a stophunting than in the opposite direction.

Situation 2

As before, our starting point is the yellow arrow followed by stophunting. At point A, I enter the market with a market buy order of 2.5 lots. The stop is 2 pip, the TP is 4 pip, which also corresponds to a risk-reward ratio of 1: 2. Depending on the entry point, my position can go down by up to $ 40, but the goal of $ 100 would be reached after just 16 minutes.

Situation 3

Here we even wait until the price has risen another pip and only then start trading. Here, too, the position could go down by up to $ 40 but after 13 minutes the target of $ 100 would be reached. The greatest risk with this approach lies in the ATR, which is able to reach a small stop faster. For this reason, back when I was trading exclusively in the Forex market, I focused on the key candles that gave me a good market insight. Of course, those key candles didn't protect me from being stopped out regularly. In my first example, the trader could have exited after 2 hours with a TP of $ 87. This waiting time was far too long for me, which is why I decided at the time to reach my profit after 15 minutes. My focus was primarily on reducing my stops in order to reach the TP faster. With the help of scaling, I was able to determine the level of risk and profit.

Today my stop is 1 to 2 pip and that means that after I enter, the price has to move in my direction immediately. Of course, I am sometimes wrong or get stopped out, but my approach creates many opportunities that I can use every day. In principle, I concentrate on the small outbreaks within an M1 candle, although I do not trade with M1 candles, as I only have the algorithms from the DoM and the Times and Sales list in view. The new tones that I have programmed also help me to get important information about the current market.

Here is a trading example from today, with my current main screen. I completely changed the tones for it. On the left loudspeaker you can now hear the market sell orders and the limit sell orders. On the right channel you can hear the market buy orders and the limit buy orders. Since I arranged the limit orders on the opposite side beforehand, the tone sequence was a bit strange for me. I have precisely adjusted the volume of the 8 different tones on the ask and bid side. In the middle you can see a decibel knife that shows the exact strength of the ask and bid side.

You can see that more bids than ask came into the market at this point, but the limit buy orders were designed to absorb the bid. Since we were in a major downward movement, I knew that the upward movement would only reach a few pips. I stayed in the trade for 85 seconds and got out when the sell limit orders increased massively in strength. I could have achieved 25% more pip, but I'm rather conservative. After 85 seconds I was in the profit with 2.8 pip. Since the M1 averages 1.5 pip / min, I achieved 33% more with 2 pip / min. My risk was $ 180 and the profit was $ 252. That's an RRR of 1.4. A short time later, the downward movement would have overrun me and I would have been stopped. A few minutes later I took once again a small upward movement of 3 pips with me and almost got out of the trade with pinpoint accuracy. As a day trader, I would have suffered massive losses in this situation. I recommend every trader to reduce the stop to a minimum, as this allows smaller sideways markets to be traded more efficiently. 70% of the time the market will be sideways, that's what I would focus on. But without the appropriate software and stock market data, trading in the Forex market is a pure game of chance.

My development towards a seconds scalper, with the help of stock market data, has brought decisive advantages for me. Since there are more small breakouts in the market than larger upward or downward movements, this creates a lot of opportunities for me every day. Additionally, I don't have to wait long to realize my winnings. Within 1 minute it is clear whether I was right or wrong. Because of my ability to scale, I theoretically don't have to place more trades than a day trader. The most important benefit, however, lies in the fact that I no longer have the feeling that my winnings are entirely due to luck. With the help of my programmed tones and the identification of the big player algorithms, I am often able to look a few milliseconds into the future. I can use this situation to my advantage to place an appropriate trade. As soon as I'm in the trade and the small breakout reaches my profit target, that's no reason to get out. If the algorithms tell me that the course is still going in my direction, I will stay in the market until I get contrary information. This also sometimes makes it possible to achieve a RRR of 1:10 or more and even within an equilibrium or a sideways phase.

In fact, I am actually trading for 10-20 minutes a day. Many years ago that was a few hours. I can use the free time to further optimize the identification of the algorithms. I prefer a comprehensible loss to a surprising gain. I can avoid a comprehensible loss in the future, a surprising gain cannot be repeated because it is based on chance. Of course, you can optimize the probability of winning in trading with strategic money management. But to focus solely on that is an admission that all trade is built on chance. The strategies of the big players are not based on chance, but on a calculable constant. The pattern sequences for this can only be found in the algorithms and not in the price, the candles or in indicators. For this I use charts that work independent of time and volume.

Quantum physics has long since found its way into the stock exchanges, but Fourier spectra and correlations between price fluctuations and volatilities do not help me to generate risk assessments or forecasts. Because this view also only brings a random result in the end and is unsuitable for seconds trading. Likewise, the percolation theory is only dependent on probabilities and thus only random in the end.

When I see a vehicle that is moving, I don't want to calculate a probability in order to assess where it's going, but rather I have to find out who is at the wheel and in which direction he are steering at that moment. This is a big challenge, but in the end it can reduce the chance of chance. However, at the last moment the driver can still turn the steering wheel to change direction. But even this spontaneous reaction cannot be predicted with the best probability calculation.

The goal is to be as close as possible to the market in order to get the fastest information. I will deal with this intensively for the next few years, let's see where this path leads me.

--- 帖子 #1575 ---
Ticks in the forex market

Hello simnz,

A tick chart in the forex market only shows the trades that are processed there, but unfortunately not the volume. A trade can contain 1 lot or 100 lots. The tickchart has the advantage that in a great number of trading transactions, for example when economic figures are published, more candles appear than in night-time trading. An upward movement depends exclusively on the market buy orders that run into the limit sell orders. Let's assume a price goes up and suddenly it is held up by the limit sell orders. Theoretically there are now three options.

1. An equilibrium arises.

2. The price breaks the limit orders and continues to rise.

3. The price is held up by the limit orders and is falling.

If a price goes up by the market buy orders and is held up by the limit sell orders, there are only two options. A big player buys the dollar with the limit sell orders or exits the euro. That is the first challenge you have to face. If the big player pulls out of the euro, the chances are high that the price will make a new high. But there is no guarantee that the course will continue to rise immediately. Any upward or downward movement is always in zigzag lines. Many believe that after an upward movement, the price will go down because many retail traders exit the market. This is a big mistake, however, as retail traders are not able to move the market at all. Theoretically, they would be able to do this, but would have to coordinate themself exactly. In the EURUSD in the Forex market there are around 2000 lots at each level in the DoM. That means, in order to move the price by one pip, 20,000 lots have to be invested. For a price to run 5 pip down, 100,000 traders would have to get out of their 1 lot euro position almost simultaneously.

There are ways to determine with a high probability when a price is turning and when it is moving further up. There are different ways of looking at this that are not easy to explain with words. I am currently producing my 6th video, where I will go into exactly these points. So I ask for a little patience. I wish you a nice weekend.

Here is the link to the channel.

https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCCb...zsD2soUtb0CTqA

Kind regards Michael

Effective trading opportunities

Hello Simnz,

to check such a strategy, I would recommend using a strategy tester. He can immediately determine whether your approach is efficient. Although I trade in the forex market, I make my trading decisions not from forex data but exclusively from stock exchange data. However, the stock exchange data is filtered beforehand in order to derive the algorithms' orders. These data cannot be compared with forex data. Likewise, there is no specific time limit for me. The limit is calculated from the pip per minute. As soon as the profit falls below the average ATR value, I am out of the market. For example, if I get 6 pip profit after 40 seconds, I'm out immediately, because the pip value per minute is 6 times higher than the average ATR in the M1. Although I only gained 6 pip, the value, pips per minute, is 9. That means my risk is 6 times lower than the average value. Every second I stay in the market would increase my risk disproportionately. The 6 pips are safe and can no longer be taken from me. In addition, a risk / reward ratio of 1: 3 is a good value as my stop is 1.5 pip and the spread is 0.5 pip. Then I just look for the next opportunity for a new trade. Since I am already satisfied with a pip value of 2 (risk-reward ratio 1), I need a range of 2 pip in total. This results in over 800 chances in the M1 candles per day. Since I am mostly only on the move during the main trading hours, the chances are reduced to 600 M1 candles. So I have enough chances to get a good result even in a small equilibrium. Entering via limit orders would significantly reduce my chances and not bring a better entry price. I prefer to trade the small breakouts up from the start and get out immediately before the big player start a pullback. The danger lies in the number of retail traders who got on within the spike. The more people got in there, the bigger the chain reaction down, when they are stopped. The best high-frequency traders have a win rate of 99% compared to the big players of 90%. Interestingly, the high-frequency traders have a significantly lower risk. This win rate is also my long-term goal, that's what I'm working towards. But that will take a few more years.

--- 帖子 #1592 ---
Hello Uli,

The high-frequency traders are not so dangerous for us retail traders, because they are rarely found in the Forex market. The background: In the forex market, no specific bid and ask information is transmitted and there is a minimum holding period for the trades placed. The main playing field for high-frequency traders is in the exchange-regulated markets. Since these traders operate in the millisecond range, there is no access to this information. Thanks to special programming, the main computer of the high-frequency trader recognizes when a certain address repeatedly buys certain stocks or currencies within seconds. From this a recurring principle is recognized and the high-performance computer gets ahead of the secret buyer. Within a millisecond, very large quantities are bought and a few seconds later thrown back into the market with a high profit. That works in 9 out of 10 cases. I will go into that again in my next video.

--- 帖子 #1601 ---
Do you think any indicator can help in detecting small breakouts? Do you have any indicator for this.

I have sourced attached indicator. The indicator calculates the values of the average High and Low prices during the trading day.

The beginning of the trading day is defined as a parameter.

For example:

Timeframe: H1,

BeginTime: 02:00

For "02:00" candle: HighAvg("02:00")=High("02:00"), LowAvg("02:00")=Low("02:00"),

for "03:00" candle: HighAvg("03:00")=(High("03:00")+High("02:00"))/2, LowAvg("03:00")=(Low("03:00")+Low("02:00"))/2, etc.

Small breakout detection indicator

"Do you think any indicator can help in detecting small breakouts? Do you have any indicator for this."

Hello simnz,

if you set off a fireworks rocket and don't see the fuse, you never know exactly when the rocket will go off. A small as well as a big breakout always comes unexpectedly, that's the purpose of an outbreak. How do you want to measure the parameters in the forex market in order to specifically predict such an outbreak? In the forex market we only get the price and the time, which are ultimately only the result of the invisible market orders in the DoM that run into the limit orders.

Even with the stock market data, this information is difficult to identify. First of all, before a major breakout on the long side, the limit sell orders are placed unnoticed with larger iceberg orders. At the breakout period, the big players' algorithms begin to shoot a cumulative number of smaller market buy orders into the market. At the same time, the iceberg orders (limit sell orders) previously placed on the market are completely removed from the market. This makes it possible to move the price massively with a relatively small number of market orders.

With my tones, which are generated from stock market data, you can hear when a machine gun salvo of market orders comes into the market. However, it is initially unclear whether these market buy orders are also able to penetrate the limit sell orders. Anyone who works with special spoofing information can recognize this withdrawal of limit sell orders. However, it is uncertain whether he will be able to get in market early. When an upward breakout begins, the best ask line jumps up, the best bid line stays at your price level because limit buy orders are not submitted so quickly. This situation increases the spread to double or even triple. A trader who enters the market shortly after the breakout has a major disadvantage. Often the price also drops again because a larger gap has formed. This gap is often not visible because it takes place within a candle.

A possible alternative to the early detection of an outbreak could be a special gap indicator that shows every gap that is larger than 1 pipette in a special chart. It would have to be ensured that every gap is displayed, even if it is closed again immediately afterwards. It is questionable whether special pattern sequences could be derived from this. In any case, this gap indicator could be used to identify gaps in the limit orders. From this one could create derivations, which of course can be interpreted differently. Another problem arises from the broker. These will pass on different gap information as each one provides different prices. I would recommend using real stock market data in addition to the forex data for better market insight.

I also only trade in the forex market because the security is much greater than in the stock market. We traders are always on the lookout for patterns from which to derive trading decisions. Unfortunately, there are no patterns in forex as the price is only random. With stock market data, I can identify patterns that will help me make trading decisions in the forex market. That has increased my probability of winning significantly over the past two years. No one would drive across a street at night without lights. It is dark in the forex market because correct ask and bid information is not available. Therefore everyone should get the light from the stock exchange markets in order to find the road in the forex market. As I noted in my last video, stock market data is the best forex indicator.

Inserted Video

Unfortunately, I cannot help you in the area of Forex indicators, as they have not been decisive for me for 2 years. Stock market data and good stock market software cost around $ 50 a month, these costs come back quickly because with this important information in forex trading you will have significantly fewer losses.

In the ten videos I have produced so far on YouTube you will find 7.5 hours of free information on this.

Pattern in the market

Hello simnz,

Basically, only from my point of view, I can answer your question, whether the indicator you posted helps. As we know, the price is only a result of the cause (Market- and Limit Orders), which we cannot see in the forex market. Since an indicator always lags behind the price, it is logically always slower than the price itself. An indicator in the Forex market only ever relates to the result and only arises randomly, due to the time factor. In my view, it is not possible to derive a profitable pattern sequence from chance.

Nevertheless, users of indicators will see it very differently. An indicator is a kind of worldview. If an indicator of 10 signals shows 7 signals correctly, you can also make profits with it. You just have to be aware that it is a coincidence. Since I want to exclude chance as much as possible in my trading, I am forced to limit myself to the cause indicators.

Every trader always decides for himself which data he uses to make trading decisions. You have gained a lot of experience in your trading, for this reason I accept your approach, although I trade completely differently. There is no right or wrong here, the different opinions of traders only lead to the fact that there can be an exchange market at all. Forex is for beginners, future for advanced

First of all, it is perfectly normal for different market participants to have different opinions on certain topics. If that were not the case, there would be no stock exchanges, because the stock market thrives on different opinions. Different statements by market participants are only based on their own views but are not representative. That means what applies to one market participant does not necessarily have to apply to all other market participants. Basically, I accept any opinion that is contrary to my opinion, because every trader always has to bear his own risk. I also do not find it dramatic when someone trades in the futures market or stock market out of his own conviction. I only find it critical when the statements are followed by an assessment of other market participants. For example: The forex market is for beginners, advanced traders only trade in the futures market. The statement that only professionals trade in the stock market is just as nonsensical as claiming that only the best drivers drive Porsches or Ferraris. Therefore we will now take a closer look at these nonsensical statements and analyze them with facts.

Let us now ask ourselves the specific question what is actually the best market in the world?

Is it actually the stocks, the forex market or, in the end, the futures market? For me, all three markets are initially neutral. There is only one crucial sentence that interests me.

Where can I achieve the highest return with the lowest risk and where can I secure my profit with a high probability?

The forex market was originally not founded for the private sector, but exclusively so that large banks could trade with one another free of charge. It was only about independence from the stock exchanges, which, incidentally, were founded so that private investors could also trade with one another. With great effort, the English were finally able to open the Forex market for the private sector. The intention was a financial interest on the part of the broker. The forex market has grown into the largest market in the world to this day. Just under $ 8 trillion is traded in the Forex market every day. This means that the forex market is 20 times larger than the global stock market and 20 times larger than the global futures market.

It is nonsense to call the Forex market not a real market, even though it is the largest market in the world. Of course, this is over-the-counter trading, also known as OTC, which is not carried out between market participants via an exchange. There is an order book as well as a time and sales list, which, however, cannot be viewed by market participants. When the EURUSD rate is published on television in the evening, it is always the price from the cash market and not from the future market. So the sentence: "The Forex market is not a real market" belongs in the trash can. The fact is that the interbank market is the leader. The stock markets orient themselves at  the interbank marketand not the other way around.

For over 20 years, some 10,000 traders have been trading against each other in the areas of stocks, forex and futures every year. The best traders in the world are selected from these. In the equities sector, an average annual return of 81% was achieved. That is an impressive return, but one that is not achieved by a normal trader in the stock market. It's comparable to Formula 1, and no normal driver can achieve these lap times. In the forex market, the world champions have achieved an average return of 106% over the past 20 years. Now we come to a very crucial point. In the stock market, the participants have concrete stock market data, while we do not receive stock market data in the forex. Nevertheless, it was possible for the best traders in the world to achieve an average of 30% more returns in the forex market than in the stock market in the last 20 years. How can this be explained?

As we know, the volatility in the stock market is significantly higher than in the forex market, which may seem to be the reason why the returns here are significantly worse. The more volatile an asset is, the less crucial big players there are in the market. In addition, high-frequency traders are drawn to the stock markets like mosquitoes to light. How else can it be explained that one trades worse with professional stock market data than without stock market data? On the other hand there is of course the futures market and there the world champions achieved 3 times more returns than in the forex market and 4 times more returns than in the stock market. Why should I voluntarily trade in a market that offers me four times fewer opportunities? That would be illogical and, from the point of view of probability, very ineffective. If I had to make a decision, the stock market would fall out because of the return.

What remains now is the forex and future market. Now of course everyone will say that if you can achieve three times more returns in the futures market you would have to automatically exclude the forex market. From the point of view of yield, that would be absolutely correct, but not from the point of view of security. In the Forex market I can lose a maximum of my existing balance on my account, while in the future market I can theoretically run into the red with € 200,000. This could have a very negative effect under certain circumstances. In return, I have better market insight and profit opportunities in the futures market. For this reason, both markets are crucial for me. Each market has certain advantages and disadvantages. The trick is to combine the advantages while reducing the disadvantages.

What exactly is the difference between a forex and a future trader? As we know, there is no information about bid and ask, no DoM and no time and sales list in the forex market. Transferred it means that the future trader sits in a vehicle that has a navigation system, while the forex trader has to do without this navigation system. If there is a traffic jam on a motorway, the future trader is rerouted and thus reaches his destination faster. The forex trader gets stuck in a traffic jam and will likely reach his goal later or not at all. What options does a driver now have who does not have a built-in navigation system? Now with Smartlink he can mirror his mobile phone on his screen in the vehicle and thus has a fully functional navigation system. If that is not possible, a mobile phone holder is usually sufficient to find the destination with Google Maps. From my point of view, the advantage of the future trader lies exclusively in the deeper market insight through the stock market data. But even as a forex trader, I can get stock market data.

For the biggest big players in the world, the stocks and future markets are far too small.

On some days there are big players in EURUSD who produce over 1 million lots or $ 1 billion in trading volume. A big player in Forex would then be able to trade the Apple share 13 times or the Euro FX E6 5 times completely. Another point, why should the big players move their billions in sales to the stock exchanges when you can trade in your market almost free of charge. If you want to follow the big players, you have to trade in the markets where most of the big players are. And that is definitely the Forex market. If you try to identify specific big players in the Apple share or in the DAX, this is much more difficult than in the EURUSD with the help of the stock market data.

I hope that with this post I could clear up some nonsensical statements. A trader who trades in the forex market is not a madman, but initially does not have as deep a market insight as in the stock market. But he can get the stock market data and thus has even more advantages than a future trader. In the stocks, forex or future markets, we can never determine 100% future price developments. For this very reason, a trader must always work with probabilities. In the last three years I have combined the forex market with the future market and this resulted in a kind of hybrid trader who uses the advantages of both markets and at the same time reduces the disadvantages of the individual markets. In the forex market we trade because of the incomparable security and receive stock market data in order to make our trading decisions. From my point of view, this is the most efficient approach, and it results in a significantly higher chance of winning. My win rate and probability of winning has improved steadily over the past few years. From this I can see a clear development that has a positive effect on me. Perhaps you too use these odds and ideas to optimize your personal situation.

If you want to dig deeper into the subject, you will find my latest video on YouTube here, which you can also translated.

Inserted Video

The most important point is that you can freely decide in which market you want to be active in the future and not in which market you have to act. From this everyone can then assess their own risk and choose exactly the market where the probability of winning is highest. Progress always came from people who were allowed to be creative. But you have to have the opportunity to experiment. That's why I'm happy to be able to make my own decisions as an independent trader. Sometimes just a small idea is enough to achieve great things with it. If that helps you, I would be very happy about it.

I sincerely wish you all the best in trading and keep my fingers crossed for you.

Kind regards Michael

Why a smaller volatility is often better.

Hello dear traders,

Today's post is about the difference between trading stocks in the stock market and currency pairs in the forex market. As always, it is my personal opinion, which of course could clearly stand out from other opinions. The different opinions on the stock exchange are responsible for the fact that trading can take place at all. As you already know, the stock exchanges have existed for over 600 years and during that time no trader has succeeded in developing a reproducible concept in order to achieve constant profits. Neither in the price nor in the candles or indicators are clear, recognizable patterns from which a regularly repeatable trading advantage can be derived. There is no day trader on the Forbes list who is among the richest people in the world. Waren Buffet is in seventh place, but this is a long-term investor and not a short-term day trader. That is a crucial difference.

Of course, we traders need a certain volatility in order to derive a trading advantage from it. However, high volatility does not mean high returns for the day trader at the same time. The volatility pyramid is always contrary to the security pyramid. The higher the volatility, the lower the security. Of course, I can make more profits in a high volatility phase, but on the other hand I can also make just as many losses. We all know the periods of extreme volatility that cause prices to fly back and forth. In these extreme phases, many big players stay out of the market and that is precisely why these extreme price jumps arise.

High volatility can only arise if the limit orders are on average smaller and at the same time the market orders are on average larger than under normal conditions. If the limit orders are so small that they are unable to stop the market orders, there is a real explosion up or down. This creates large gaps within the DoM, which results in large spreads. In addition, the risk also increases at the same time. When the market and limit orders reach an average size, an average market situation arises. This situation is often found in the accumulation and distribution phases. If the market orders are on average smaller and at the same time the limit orders are on average larger, there is low volatility. This situation often occurs when the big players have gathered their contacts just before they are pushing course in a certain direction.

Now we come to a very crucial point, namely the question of who actually places the limit orders in the market? The big players are mainly responsible for this because they mostly use the limit orders to get in and out. The retail traders usually place the market orders in the form of stops, which are accepted by the limit orders of the big players. Of course, the big player market orders also invest to move the price in their direction, but these market orders are immediately resold. You can find specific information in my blog and YouTube channel about the big players.

From this information we can now make the following derivation. The weaker the share of limit orders, the fewer big players there are in the market. I don't mean the situation when a big player has collected in an accumulation phase and then pushes the course upwards. It's about the average volatility within a market. If a market is generally highly volatile, this is evidence that on average there are fewer big players in the market than in markets with lower volatility.

The high volatility enables short-term profits that we lose again due to the spread and the probability of winning. Medium volatility enables us to generate income that we can keep in the long term. It's not about making money fast, it's about securing our profits. And that is exactly what is much easier for me in the euro US dollar than in the stock markets. Since the volatility in the stock market is on average higher than in the forex market, the world champions in the stock market would also have to achieve a significantly higher return than the world champions in the forex market. Interestingly, that is not the case. The forex traders are 30% better and the future traders are even 400% better. Are the traders in the stock market trader actually 30% worse than in the forex market? I am convinced that this is not the case, rather that volatility often eats up profits. More high-frequency traders and fewer big players, that brings high volatility and thus uncertainty at the same time.

You can trade even more effectively if you combine the forex data with the stock market data. If you want to dive deeper into the topic, here is my latest video on YouTube that you can also translate.

Inserted Video

Since I basically want to follow the big players, I also have to be on the move in markets where these big players are present. For this reason, volatile investments like an Apple share are out of the question for me. In the volatility comparison of the year 2020, the Apple share is about four times more volatile than the EURUSD. Increased volatility thus increases the unpredictability of a price. It is therefore clear that it is not the volatility that decides the return, but a predictable influence on the part of the big players. Anyone who is able to see where the big players are collecting has a significantly lower risk because they can be pulled in the right direction.

I wish you a good weekend and a successful trade next week.

Kind regards Michael

A new experiment with my new video scalping

Hello dear traders,

On average, a 45-minute video was uploaded every two weeks, resulting in 12 videos that initially roughly describe my approach. Of course, I would have loved to have discussed these videos entirely in English, but I didn't grow up in America to have a 100% command of the semantics or rhetoric in English. And that is exactly the key point for a lecture to get the words across in an understandable way. First, in my videos, I started to label the slides in English and to speak with German text. As a result, many Germans did not understand the slides.

For this reason, I will be posting all of the text that I used in my last video in English here at Forex Factory. Then you know what the video is about and you can watch the video again in German with the English subtitles. If this goes down well with you, I will gradually post the texts for the remaining videos in English at Forex Factory. Many things may then become a little clearer. You are welcome to give me feedback on this.

Before we start, I would like to thank you once again for your great feedback that I have received from you over the past few months. A very special thank you goes to the following people who strongly supported my contributions.
