So now we start with the text of the new video

In today's post on scalping, we're going to check whether scalping is more efficient and whether it increases the risk.

Every beginner will have experienced the following situation. A course has risen sharply and we are looking for the optimal entry point in the pullback. Finally we found the right entry and put the stop below the last low. We determine the take profit from our previously defined money management. The price is actually moving in our direction and we expect it to hit take profit. Unfortunately, it turns out differently than we thought, and with luck we can get off before our stop. The conclusion after 2 hours in the market, a small loss and with luck even a breakeven. There was nothing except expenses. We sat in front of the screen for 2 hours and earned no money. I had to experience this situation many times at the beginning of my trading career.

Right before I started trading, I became interested in binary options. For example, you could bet $ 100 on a rising price and get $ 70 if you win. The same was of course also possible for a falling course. Unfortunately, the brokers at the time were able to set their own prices, which resulted in a large number of cases of fraud. The risk / reward ratio was also catastrophic. In this case you had to achieve at least a win rate of 70% to trade breakeven. What motivated me was that you could determine the running time. No matter if 1 minute 30 minutes or 1 hour. After just 1 minute it was clear whether you had won or lost. That was the only positive aspect of binary options. Nowadays they are banned in Germany, which from my point of view was completely correct. Over the years I tried to transfer the idea of quick profit to trading. This was only possible in the area of scalping.

In the trading market there are swing traders, day traders and scalpers. If I had to assign these three groups to a specific vehicle, the Swing Trader would get the S-Class, the Daytrader a Porsche and the Scalper a Formula 1 car. Scalping is the most demanding trading strategy, and it is not for nothing that Formula 1 in trading. Very few traders have become successful with scalping, but this was primarily due to the costs of the broker. You have all probably heard the famous sentence:

Back and forth empties pockets. Let's see if this statement is actually true.

A scalper pays a spread of 0.5, the stop is 2.7 and the TP is 3.2 pip. This results in a possible loss rate of 54.2% in the event of a random market entry. Why is that? Because the probability is significantly higher that the stop will be reached sooner than the take profit. The day trader receives the same spread, his stop is 14.6 and the TP is 15.1 pip. Therefore, the theoretical probability of winning here is 50.8%. As a rule, not every trader has such a favorable spread, but this is a basic requirement in order to be successful as a scalper.

We have all played Tetris or Mario Kart before and everyone knows that the longer you play these games, the faster the response times and the better you get. The greatest learning success is usually achieved when you play with friends. Two friends compete against each other on a tennis court to win the game. Player A has been playing for four years and has trained 1000 serves so far. Player B has also been playing for four years and has so far trained 10,000 serves. Both players have the same level of fitness and have had the same coach. Now if you had to bet on one of the players who would win the game, who would you choose? Of course I know that not only the serves decide a tennis match. The probability that player B wins is much higher here.

Imagine a rotten bridge connecting two mountains. 10 m below there is a raging river, it is raining and there is a strong wind. You now have the task of running to the middle of the bridge and stopping there. If you can do that for 1 minute you will receive 150 €, for 5 minutes 400 €, for 15 minutes 700 €, for 30 minutes 1050 € and for 60 minutes 1450 €. You can stand on the bridge for a maximum of 60 minutes, you can also step onto the bridge several times, but you have to pay a fee of € 5 each time. If you fall down all the money is gone. Person A stands on the bridge for 60 minutes and receives € 1,445 for this. Person B walks 10 × 1 minute on the bridge, has to pay 50 € fees and receives 1,450 € at the end. In principle, he deserves the same, but 50 minutes less risk to stand on the dilapidated bridge. Of course, he could theoretically stand on the bridge for 60 × 1 minute and earn 6 times more. The bridge is the synonym for our market when we are in trade and the 5 € our brokerage costs for 1 lot.

In the EURUSD, the average ATR in the M1 is 1.5 pip. The larger the unit of time, the higher the ATR. In the 30 minute range the ATR is 10.5 and in the 4 hour range it is 31.2. The pip value per minute is calculated from this. In the 1 minute range this is 1.5 pips per minute. In the 30 minute range this value is reduced to 0.35 and after 4 hours it is only 0.13. This is because of the zigzags a course takes to run up or down.

Let us now compare a trader who is in the market for 2 minutes with a trader who trades for 60 minutes. Incidentally, it does not matter in which time unit both act. In 2 minutes the pip value per minute is 1.35 and after 60 minutes it is 0.24. This results in the maximum possible number of trades within 1 hour.
If you were to complete the maximum number of trades, the potential would be 81 pips in the 2 minute range and 14 pips in the 60 minute range. This means that the gross potential at Pip is 6 times higher in the first case. Likewise, you could get as much pip within 12 minutes as the one who trades for 60 minutes. Even if you subtract the cost of 30 trades, you have 4 times more net. And for me that is exactly the reason why a trade that takes 2 minutes involves 6 times less risk than a trade that takes 60 minutes. Of course, the costs have to be deducted in each case.

There are 2 important factors in money management. The profit factor, which should be above 1, results from the probability and the CRV. And the winners and losers result in the decisive expected value per trade. It is interesting that as a scalper I don't necessarily have to complete more trades than a day trader to earn the same.

We are in the market for 2 minutes and trade 3.13 lots, the spread is 0.5 pip and the stop is 2.7 pip. The spread and the stop add up to 3.2 pips, and the TP is just as large. In this case, the risk of loss and profit is $ 100. The probability of loss is 54.2% and the earnings per minute are $ 50. We are in the market for 60 minutes and trade 0.66 lots, the spread is 0.5 pip and the stop is 14.6 pip. The spread and the stop add up to 15.1 pips, and the TP is just as large. In this case, the risk of loss and profit is also $ 100. The probability of loss is 50.8% and earnings per minute are $ 1.67. And now comes the big question? With the same risk, why should I only make $ 1.67 when I can make $ 50 per minute? The reason why many traders cannot afford this approach is because of the capital required. To trade 3.13 lots, a non-professional trader must deposit at least $ 10,416. In return, he has an extremely high level of capital security. As I showed in my last video, this also works with 7 times less capital. However, one should always make sure that the risk is limited to 1-2%.

Let's summarize briefly. If I have been trading for 60 minutes, the risk is 6.3 times greater from my point of view than if I have only been in trading for 2 minutes. If I trade for 2 minutes, I have 30 times the trading potential. We are able to make money 30 times faster. If there is a small breakout, it has a much stronger effect within 2 minutes than within 60 minutes.

Maybe some of you can still remember my paper airplane experiment. A paper plane is launched from the top floor of a high-rise building. Below is a person who is supposed to assess where the paper plane will land. The question now is: At what point can the person best estimate the landing radius of the paper airplane? The correct answer: When the paper plane is as close as possible to the person in question. We come to one crucial factor of probability. The closer your take profit is to the current price, the more accurate your forecast will be. As a scalper, I only have to see 2 minutes into the future, as a day trader I have possibly 60 minutes. From the perspective of probability, 2 minutes is easier to realize.

In the last few years I have carried out very complex calculations in EURUSD and have found that a large part of the price developments move within an equilibrium. Movement occurs only in 30% of the time, in 70% the course is in an equilibrium. If, as a day trader, I want to achieve a target of 15 pip in the M1, this is simply impossible in many price situations. As soon as I reduce the target, the probability of a successful trade is significantly higher. I try to end my trade after 2.5 minutes at the latest. I trade between 2 and 10 lots that equates to $ 1 million. I have also worked with significantly higher lots units, but there is a very high risk of being discovered. My TP is 3-5 pips. When I enter the market and the price suddenly moves 5 pips in my direction, I'm usually out immediately. Even if the price goes up another 10 pips after that, that doesn't annoy me. At 5 pips, I exceeded the average ATR three times. I am also looking for trades that can be reproduced again and again. An extreme outbreak is not one of them. My stop is 2 pips including the spread. Depending on how I get into the market, the stop can be reduced to 1.0 pip.

In order to trade successfully with such small stops in the long term, one has to work with stock market data that give a trader a deeper market insight. The decisive point, however, is the individual filter settings.

Let's get to the benefits of scalping

We take less risk and get more money in less time. It may increase the number of trades, which is also good training. With the help of the stock market data, I am even deeper in the market. My win rate is significantly higher and a small breakout is very effective in 2 minutes. In addition, I am able to trade in even the smallest equilibrium and sideways markets.

Of course there are downsides too

To be a successful scalper, you need fast response times. Under certain circumstances, losses can occur faster and the probability is slightly worse than in long-term trading. Since you have to be constantly focused, scalping is a little more strenuous. Due to the tones I developed myself, I don't have to stare at my screens all day, but listen as soon as the market changes in my favor. Exchange data are necessary for this and you either need a smaller margin or a higher capital, since a higher number of lots is traded. Let's take a closer look at the topic of higher broker costs.

The scalper trades 3.13 lots in 2 minutes, the spread costs 0.5 pip and the profit is $ 100. Without brokerage fees, the profit would be $ 115.63. The broker thus receives 13.5% of my profit. The day trader trades 0.66 lot in 60 minutes, the spread also costs 0.5 pip and the profit is $ 100. Without brokerage fees, the profit would be $ 103.31. The broker thus receives 3.2% of my profit. Since the scalper trades with a higher lot, he pays 5x higher brokerage costs, but earns 30 times more per minute.

Maybe I was able to show you that scalping is not quite as dramatic as you often hear. Basically, you can't say that scalping is more successful than day trading or swing trading. Every trader has to adapt his strategy and his setup to his personal sensitivities over the years. Not every trader is suitable for scalping, but you should give it a try.

Of course, the brokerage costs are significantly higher with a scalper than with a day trader. If I win 3.5 pips, the broker gets 0.5 pips of that. That is at least 13%. If you earn $ 100,000, the broker gets $ 13,000 of that. Of course you could get annoyed about it now, on the other hand you could also wish your broker that he will soon earn double that. And that would certainly not be to our disadvantage.

Inserted Video

I wish you a very successful trading week, keep my fingers crossed for great trades and I am happy if my tips help you.

Kind regards Michael

--- 帖子 #1621 ---
With a small laptop against the biggest big players

Hello dear traders,

We hear again and again on the Internet that all you need to trade is a simple laptop to become a millionaire. To what extent this statement is correct, we will investigate in today's article. We'll also take a closer look at the Goldman Sachs approach and how to put together a good trading workstation.

Over 5 million traders around the world sit in front of their laptops or screens every day, hoping for great luck. What most retailers don't see is who they're up against. These big players from large banks and institutions are very professionally positioned. In air-conditioned rooms, countless traders sit in front of the latest screens, which are supported by an armada of analysts. All information is received by the Director of Trading and his strategies are distributed as individual orders to the different traders. It's like an army controlled from one point to hit a specific target. They work with the most modern data centers to send their algorithms into the Forex market. Their strategies are brutal and designed to convey a truth to the 5 million retail traders that really doesn't exist.

Many years ago I dealt with Goldman Sachs, one of the most successful traders in the world. You made profits on 222 days out of an average of 253 trading days. That is a rate of almost 88%. I also looked at their balance sheets and calculated profits and losses from them. Of 100% of the profits that you collect, you only have to give up 6.4%. The profit rate is thus over 93.6% and that on average over the last 11 years. Their expected value averages $ 45 million per trading day regardless of whether they win or lose. The average profit factor is $ 20. That means you risk $ 1 for a win of $ 20. Those are incredible values. Since the big players don't work with stops, I determined the CRV value from the loss days. On average, the CRV value is well above 2. The hit rate in 2020 was over 90%. And the loss rate is below 10%. This makes Goldman Sachs one of the best traders in the world. In the past eleven years, the profit factor has decreased somewhat, but has now stabilized again in the last year. The CRV value has decreased slightly over the past eight years. In the area of the hit rate, ever better values have been achieved over the past five years. That was also a little bit because of the pressure from the shareholders. At the same time, it has also enabled the loss rate to be significantly reduced in recent years. Due to different influences, the expected value has decreased significantly in the last ten years. However, this was again increased significantly in the last trading year. That means Goldman Sachs is back in the game, even though daily earnings are still 21.5% behind the penultimate five years. Nevertheless, these are exemplary values that hardly any retail trader is likely to achieve. Why is that?

First and foremost, there is a massive imbalance between the big players and retail traders. It would be comparable to a Formula 1 car versus a road vehicle. Of course, you could tune your road vehicle to have better chances, but there is always a special feature in the tuning. First of all, the engine output is increased, the vehicle should be as loud as possible and the design should also stand out. In doing so, the safety aspects, which are much more crucial for a vehicle, are often forgotten. In addition to an optimally coordinated chassis, ceramic brakes and the right tires may be a decisive aspect in order to have enough safety reserves at the decisive moment.

A Formula 1 car manages the sprint from zero to 100 in 2.4 seconds and comes to a stop in 1.2 seconds. A Porsche GT3 RS manages the sprint in 3.3 seconds and comes to a stop after 2.3 seconds. A normal road vehicle goes from zero to 100 in 8.4 seconds and comes to a stop in 3.6 seconds. No matter how hard the Porsche driver tries to tune his vehicle, he will never come close to the values of the Formula 1 vehicle. In principle, this is not necessary either. It is much more important that the Porsche driver achieves better values than the average road vehicle. And that is exactly the crucial aspect in trading. We don't have to be better than the big players, but clearly better than the average trader.

In a race, the driver's driving style is more important than the vehicle. Ferrari hired Michael Schumacher back then because his driving style enabled him to get more seconds than Ferrari would have been able to with the best technical development on the vehicle. Therefore, in my next example, I will award a maximum of 20 points for the driving style and a maximum of ten points for the vehicle. In the case of a multiplication, the maximum value is therefore 200 points.

An inexperienced racing driver with a bad racing vehicle gets 50 points. If this inexperienced driver is provided with an optimal racing car, he can achieve significantly better lap times. The score increases to 100. A top driver with a bad racing car is likely to get the same score. The optimum value can only be achieved if a top driver is equipped with a top vehicle. Let us now transfer these points to a trader. An inexperienced trader will achieve significantly better results with a better workplace than with an unsuitable workplace. And it is precisely for this reason that the right workplace is a decisive factor in order to be successful with it.

Of course, traders dream of making as much profit as possible, but unfortunately the reality is different. 90% of traders actually make losses. Having an optimal workplace is primarily about breaking even. And whoever achieves that belongs to the top 10% of all traders. If you were to tell the traders at Goldman Sachs tomorrow that they can only trade with a cell phone or laptop, everyone can imagine what the future success numbers will look like. For this reason it should seem logical that a good trading workplace can only function with a permanently installed computer. In addition to the right operating system, the screens, the workstation and the right accessories are also crucial.

Today we will deal specifically with the operating system and the screen structure. We will then talk in detail next week about the composition of the workstation and the accessories. Let's start with the Apple operating system. At Apple, the individual components are precisely matched to one another. Apple attaches great importance to the design, which is always an individual view. The susceptibility to viruses and malware is significantly lower than that of Windows. When it comes to graphics and image processing, Apple is way ahead. The functionality and way of working with the operating system also have certain advantages. The communication between mobile phone iPad and IMac are second to none. Windows is clearly left behind here. The cloud is also perfectly coordinated with Apple products. On the other hand, there is a significantly high price and to work with Windows, Boot Camp must be installed on the Apple computer. From my point of view, however, this is of no advantage.

Let's look at the Windows operating system. Basically, Windows is much better suited for gaming, which is also indirectly related to trading. The biggest advantage are the individual components from which you can assemble a Windows computer. So you can combine the fastest graphics card with the fastest processor and the fastest SSD. Let's just think of the NVMe m2 SSD which achieves a write speed of 7000 MB per second. Apple does not achieve these values. Significantly more screens can also be connected to a Windows computer. On the other hand, the susceptibility to viruses and malware is significantly higher, which can be reduced with a few tricks. With individual components, graphics and image processing are also significantly faster. The range of software is also larger, as many programs do not run on Apple. Another important point for many traders is the significantly lower cost. This means that with Windows you get more performance and speed for significantly less money and that is precisely what is crucial in trading. For reasons of performance, my choice would always be Windows.

Monitor or TV which is better? Basically you have to know that monitors with 1-4ms have a significantly faster response time than TV sets. You also have a higher refresh rate, which is measured in the hertz. Monitors have a very high pixel density at 4K. In the monitor area, there are more smaller screens and if you need larger screens, it can quickly turn into money. On the other hand, let's compare a TV that we use as a monitor. The response time is significantly slower at 5-10 ms. However, this is not a major disadvantage in trading, since we are not dealing with complex video games. Likewise, 60 Hz are absolutely sufficient to be able to display the course courses effectively. Elaborate games are not possible with it, but we don't want to play either, we don't want to lose money on the stock exchange. With larger screen areas, the pixel density in 4K is of course lower on average than with a monitor. The larger the screen area, the further apart the pixels are. In the TV sector, there are significantly larger screen areas of 55 or 75 inches. And the costs are of course much cheaper than in the monitor area. You can get a good 4K TV from Samsung or LG from 1000 €, for a comparable monitor you often have to pay 3-4 times as much. Anyone who uses complex video games is better off with a monitor; in the trading area, a modern TV is not a disadvantage.

Hertz is the physical unit for frequency. In the case of a monitor, the number of image updates per second is expressed in hertz. In this case, that's 60 frames per second that the TV can display. The FPS translates exactly the same thing in principle. It is therefore only a matter of specifying a frequency, namely how many images a graphics card can generate per second. In the case of the RTX 2080 super, that's over 200 FPS. It is important that the TV has a so-called V-Sync function, which limits the FPS to the rate of the monitor and usually ensures that the graphics card does not get too hot.

You can get good 55-75 inch 4K TVs from LG and Samsung for as little as € 1000. There are other providers, some of which are significantly cheaper and also guarantee high quality. If you need four more monitors, I would recommend LG with 32 inches, as they represent a sensational black and white value. The costs are around € 250 per screen with a flexible 3D wall bracket. Normally, an RTX 2080 would be absolutely sufficient for the 4K monitor, unless you also work with the same stock exchange software as I do, which accesses the GPU of the graphics card. This means that arithmetic operations can be carried out up to ten times faster and a larger graphics card proves to be advantageous here. The cost is around € 800. I would supply the 4 LG monitors with four external graphics cards, as they put less load on the workstation. The cost here is around € 200. The total costs for the screens, including the graphics cards, amount to around € 3,000. If you buy used things you can save up to € 1,700.

Some traders have asked me why I am working with a 75 inch 4K monitor. The answer is relatively simple because I want to focus my important charts on one point. This is a decisive advantage, especially in trading. However, my next large monitor will run in 8K. I work with five monitors in order to save time and not always have to change the charts. The question also arose that one is not able to see all the monitors at the same time. That is absolutely correct, but you have to imagine it as in an airplane. When taking off, you have other instruments in view, such as when landing or during flight. It's the same in trading. For entry I need different information than for exit or while I am trading. My charts are arranged accordingly.

In my last post you can see the same spider web that was photographed from different perspectives. On the right picture you can see that in a certain perspective, the light reflections take on the colors of the leaves and the spider web becomes invisible to the insects. In the Forex market, the course of the course is the spider web. There, situations are created again and again, whereby the retail trader should get a secure feeling of where the course is going next. So we are regularly invited to fly into the big players' spider web. The big players are smart enough to suggest to us on a regular basis that there is no such thing as a spider web.

Trading is incredibly difficult, otherwise 90% of all traders wouldn't lose their hard-saved money. But there is a way out that helps us traders, we just have to change our perspective. However, this takes some time and means a willingness to change. At first glance my developed trading screens look very complicated, but I don't do this for fun or because I have nothing better to do. I'm just changing my perspective to identify the big players' spider web. This information that I receive cannot be displayed on a cell phone or laptop. I hope that I was able to show you that a professional workplace increases the probability of winning significantly. Here is my latest video about it.

Hello dear traders,

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

On the side you can see the individual components that make up my workstation. A processor upgrade to the Ryzen 5900 X is planned for the foreseeable future. My existing water cooling is sufficient for this. An RTX 3070 should also be used as soon as I switch to an 8K monitor. Overall, the PC was tailored to my individual trading programs and stock market software and is therefore damn fast. You can check the performance of your PC on User Benchmark yourself. Then you get the values for gaming, workstation and desktop. The values range from the tree trunk to the UFO. I am absolutely satisfied with my values in the areas of gaming, desktop and workstation. If you have worse values there, that doesn't have to be a disadvantage at first.

As a trader, there are different requirements that a workstation must meet. There are forex traders who work exclusively with the MT4 or MT5, future traders who trade with individual stock exchange software and hybrid traders like me who work simultaneously with forex and future data. Let's take a closer look at the individual differences. In the Forex area, it is crucial to know how many different screens are being used. The number of MT4 charts also determines the required performance. There are different indicators that demand different levels of performance. Another important aspect is the course data that is used in the system. All of these things ultimately determine the optimal computer. The number of screens used is also important in the future market. The decisive aspect, however, is the stock exchange software used. As a rule, it will access the CPU and the main memory. As a hybrid trader, you have access to both the exchanges and the forex data. This requires a significantly higher performance, which must always be individually tailored to the individual tools. In the example that you are currently seeing, 60 forex and 140 different future charts are open. The average trader works with a maximum of 10-15 charts open at the same time. If you try to open 50 different charts, most computers will acknowledge that with a frozen screen.

My development as a hybrid trader took many years, so I was able to adapt my workstation to the required situation again and again. Which requirements do I exactly need? I work with five screens that take up an area of 3 m². The forex and future data run together in a coordinated system. To read the algorithms, I have to be able to open up to 200 charts at the same time. I am lucky that my stock exchange software accesses the GPU of my graphics card, otherwise such a procedure would not be possible. I programmed different 1ms tones myself, but all internal computer sound cards are overwhelmed with it. The computer should be capable of producing and editing 4K films, and as a final requirement, all five screens should be controlled by a mouse and keyboard.

In order to meet all of these requirements in the best possible way, sooner or later you have to deal with the benchmarks of the individual components. For this I like to use the Passmark page, which gives me important and free information. We start with the CPU benchmark. In addition, you can see the average price and from this the value is created, which shows the price-performance ratio. The higher the number, the better the price-performance ratio. In the high-end CPU area alone, there are over 800 different processors. From the 33 fastest processors, I have selected those that have achieved the best price-performance ratio. Now I have determined the current prices in Germany in order to determine my own value for money. As you can see, the processor I used still has the best price-performance ratio. Since I only need the processor for the Forex market and for film cutting, the Ryzen 3900x is completely sufficient. If I were to buy the best processor, I would have to pay 14 times more but would only get 2.5 times more performance. From my point of view, this is unprofitable, especially since I couldn't use the power at all.

Let's now compare different SSDs with a storage size of 500 GB. Many work with the Samsung 860 EVO which has a read and write speed of 550 MB per second. The benchmark is 4352, while the Samsung 980 Pro has 14 times faster writing speed and a benchmark of 30,271. The Western Digital Black also achieves 7000 MB per second and the benchmark is 37,964. Here we see the current prices and the values for the price-performance ratio. The Samsung does better than the Western Digital in this case. In the 1 TB area it looks completely different again, which is why I opted for Western Digital here. As a RAM memory, Crossair Vengeance is unsurpassed, the benchmark speaks a clear language here too. The RTX 3090 is unsurpassed for gaming, but here it comes with a very poor price-performance ratio. The RTX 3070 offers the best price-performance ratio in the upper segment, followed by the 3060 TI and the RTX 3060. With a little experience, these graphics cards can also be overclocked to achieve even better performance. Traders who only want to work with a 55 or 75 inch 4K TV can easily use a GTX 970. I used this card for my first 55 inch 4K at the time. A used card is available from 100 €

The basis of every workstation is the mainboard. I work with an MSI X570 Pro Carbon and have had good experiences with it. I use 2 ME memory cards that are always cloned. As soon as one fails, I can continue working with the current data immediately. Only the operating system, my stock market software and the most important programs are on the cards. The desktop is occupied with 100 MB. My films and important data are stored on a two terabyte SSD, which is also backed up. There are also external sound cards to optimally display my 1ms tones. A 700 W power supply is completely sufficient, as is the water cooling of the CPU, since my temperatures are a maximum of 50 °. If you sit in front of the computer all day, the fans should be correspondingly quiet.

For a Forex trader who works with a 4K 55 inch TV, the following recommendations are sufficient. In future trading you need a fast processor as much RAM and a fast SSD as possible. For me, the graphics card and the SSD are in the foreground, the CPU and the RAM are not that important. Here, however, every trader should adapt the hardware to his software. As soon as the system is up, you should speed up your Windows. Visual effects are completely nonsensical, programs can be assigned to individual CPU cores and unnecessary apps should be removed. Just like a vehicle, the workstation must be regularly maintained and monitored. I have some tips for you on this. The free program Coretemp shows the CPU temperature for each core in the task bar. With the free program Net Speed Monitor, the upload and download numbers are visible in the task bar. To clean my computer, I use CCleaner and Advanced System Care Pro. There are many useful tools there to update drivers or block malware. You also get an overview of the most important computer functions. The program can first be downloaded for free and tested. In addition, I would recommend you to monitor your SSD. The manufacturers provide the programs free of charge.

Fiber optic offers the best ping times, and that is exactly what is crucial for a trader. I myself have opted for a 500 MBit line at Telekom and even get more performance than I pay for. My router is up to 15% more than I was promised, the line is stable and there are almost no failures. I like to pay a little more for that. I use the FRITZ! Box 7590 as a router, which I connected to my workstation with a high-quality CAT 7 cable. Due to the ping times, WLAN is not an alternative. I would also recommend you to optimize the ping values in Windows afterwards, information can be found on the Internet. For security reasons, I would recommend you as a trader to prioritize your data line in the FRITZ! Box. This is especially important when others are also accessing your internet. With the prioritization you always have a constant and stable ping value. If you can't use fiber optics, there is a way to increase your internet speed with LTE. First buy prepaid cards from different providers and use them to test LTE reception. Then get a corresponding LTE router from the best provider. The router is now connected to a high-quality antenna that is aligned with the LTE mast. With the free program LTE Watch you can now optimize the individual decibel values. You can get specific information on the Internet. This makes it easy to optimize the ping values.

Marcel Eris, stage name Montana Black is a well-known web video producer, live streamer and entertainer who mainly deals with video games on YouTube and Twitch. From my point of view, there is no financial disadvantage with the Montana Black Design compared to a self-assembled PC. However, we traders don't need a PC for € 15,000.

If you save on at the wrong end, you lose more than you save. Someone wants to save on grocery shopping and is therefore comparing the best offers. This results in a shopping list at different discounters. On Saturday he drives to the cheapest discounters, to pick up the special offers. The additional fuel costs and the time required alone by no means justify the savings. A petrol station wants to advertise and is reducing fuel prices by € 0.20. You now stand in line for 2 hours. In the end, the tank only holds 60 l and the savings are 12 euros. With a part-time job, you could have earned double that amount or would have preferred to spend the valuable time with family or friends.

There is a very interesting law of the market economy. This was written by John Raskin a British writer and social philosopher. “There is hardly anything in this world that someone cannot make a little worse and sell a little cheaper. And the people who orientate themselves only on the price become the fair prey of such machinations. It is unwise to overpay, but it is equally unwise to underpay. If you pay too much, you lose some money, that's all. If you pay too little, on the other hand, you sometimes lose everything because the object you bought cannot do the job it was supposed to do. The law of the market economy forbids getting a lot of value for little money. If you accept the lowest offer, you have to add something for the risk taken. But if you do that, you will have enough money to pay for something better. "

The rule is no longer: Avarice is cool, but: added value is cool. I hope that I could give you a few tips to optimize your computer performance in the future. If I started trading today as a beginner

Hello dear algorithm traders,

Today I put a new video online on YouTube, as always I'll translate the text into English so that everyone can understand and understand the video. In addition, you can fade in English subtitles in the video. So here we go ...

We all know the sentence, if I could start all over again, what would I do differently? With this in mind, today we consider what things are important in trading, whether a trading coach is an alternative and what you should pay attention to.

I have already answered the question what would I do differently if I started all over again. I would go the same way again and do everything exactly as I have before. With stocks forex or futures there is unfortunately no beginner or advanced market, only a professional market. If you are a beginner in this market, it is like playing against Real Madrid with a district class football team . You can imagine how this match will end and therefore it is understandable that the probability of winning is just 5% and that is why so many beginners fail. The greatest and best professionals in the world trade in the forex market. Anyone expecting an opportunity here must have very special skills.

Everyone who learns something first goes through the four levels of competence development. First there is unconscious competence. I don't know that I don't know or can't do something. A six-year-old child sitting in his father's car is not aware that he cannot drive this vehicle himself. Then comes the conscious competence, which means that I become aware that I do not know or cannot do something. The twelve-year-old, who is sitting in the car next to his father, is aware that he cannot drive this vehicle. The conscious incompetence shows the person that he can and knows something. An 18-year-old learner driver gradually learns how to use the vehicle. At the beginning he has a bit of difficulty with the request inside mirror, outside mirror, look over the shoulder and only then flash. The unconscious incompetence means that knowledge and ability is integrated and runs automatically. A 24-year-old driver who has already covered a few 100,000 km sometimes does not know how he made his daily commute to work or home because he was talking to his passenger or listening to music.

Even as a trading beginner, there is an unconscious incompetence. First you discover a new indicator. As soon as a blue point appears in the low one should go long and when it appears in the high go short. You start to act and immediately the first disillusionment sets in. You quickly realize that although a point appears in the low, the price is still going down. The consequence, the indicator is simply exchanged for a new one and the game starts all over again. At some point the beginner realizes that an indicator cannot predict the future for them, and the fastest indicator is price. Now comes the conscious competence that shows him that a candle is only a statistical coincidence that arises from time and price. After a few years, the mechanisms of a trade run automatically, the breakeven point is reached and ensures that no more losses are made. It is now a matter of optimizing profits. Imagine you had to go on a space walk as an astronaut. You have two astronaut suits to choose from. The first suit is proven and has been used by NASA for many years and the second suit is high-tech with a second pressure build-up where you can survive in space even with a hole in the suit. Which suit would you choose? Probably for the suit that offers you the highest level of security. Where would you invest your money, in the futures market or in the forex market. Probably also where security is highest. In the future market, you are liable with all of your private assets in the event of an unscheduled breakout. In the forex market you are only liable with your credit on the broker account. This can mean a difference of a few 100,000 euros. Now some will say that they only trade in the futures market because there is better data available there. That's right, but you can also use the future market data to trade more efficiently in the forex market. Please have a look at my video: Hybrid Trader, the future of effective trading. There I will show you exactly how you can combine the future and forex data with each other in order to achieve the greatest possible advantage.

Many beginners start with a small account of € 200-500, download the MT4 and start trading on their laptop. Why that goes wrong and which IT equipment I recommend you get in the two videos: With a laptop against the biggest big players in the world; and tips and tricks, assemble your trading PC yourself. Basically I recommend a starting capital of 5000-10,000 € to every trader. Good screens should be purchased for this, the workstation should be tailored to the software, the stock exchange software should be clear and understandable, the data feed cheap, the forex broker honest, the future broker fast and the ping times short. We'll take a closer look in a moment to see if the help of a trainer is required. For the total investment in the area of screens and workstations, we invest between € 2,000 and € 5,000. For this very reason, I recommend trading in the Forex market and at the same time extracting the crucial data from the futures market. For this I would deposit € 2,500 with a forex broker, € 500 is enough with a future broker, because I don't want to trade there. The right data feed is crucial. (You can find all the information in the video)

Then comes the crucial point that makes you a profitable trader. It's about the basics of trading and primarily about understanding how the big players operate and work. Any trader who can understand this will be able to trade profitably relatively quickly.

The challenge for every beginner

Different strategies are tried out

Successful strategies are made worse

Indicators are tested and discarded

in the event of longer losses, the strategy is crushed

Confusing information from the Internet

Stops are being dragged for too long

Profits are taken too quickly

Losses are not accepted (revenge trades)

And the main focus is on making profits rather than making fewer losses.

Let's compare the probability of success of a self-employed person with a trader. Only 25% of all self-employed can make a long-term living from being self-employed. 5% of all traders can make a long-term living from their trading. That means it is five times harder to be successful as a trader. This is where a trading coach could help. But there are a few things to keep in mind.

First of all, the investment in a trading coach should make up a maximum of 20% of the start-up capital. With a starting capital of 5000 € that would be 1000 € for the coaching. I have never worked with a trading coach but if I were a beginner I would expect this for 1000 €. One-to-one coaching that lasts at least two days, or even better, three days or at least 20 hours. One-to-one coaching has the advantage that the trainer can cater to you individually. Joint live trading in the forex market should also take place. Why in the forex market. Because the biggest and most successful big players in the world only trade in the Forex market. By the way, 85% of all global traders also trade in the Forex market. Personally, I would not hire a trainer who is not able to trade profitably in the Forex market. Don't just be fobbed off with videos, videos are good, but the coach should cater to you individually. That brings the greatest benefit and advantage. At the same time, the trainer should be able to explain exactly how the big players in the market work and how they use the algorithms to gain advantages. If he can't do that, I would look for another coach. Ultimately, the trainer should address your strengths and weaknesses individually. If you are only in an online seminar with 30 other participants, this decisive criterion will not be met. Find a real mentor. The trainer should also be able to explain to you simply how you can achieve extreme market advantages with the help of the time and sales list or the DoM. In addition, he should refrain from volume trading, as the volume is only an addition of ask and bid. However, ask and bid never meet in the market, so it is unnecessary to add them together. It is much more important to work out the decisive limit orders in order to recognize what the big players are currently collecting. This is the only way to determine the medium-term price trend. And finally, the trainer should provide you with his personal setup that he works with. When all of these things are fulfilled, you can get coached with a clear conscience.

In principle, it is only a matter of breaking even once. You can do that after an average of 3600 trades. After that, profits must be made and gradually optimized. This breakeven point is the key to any trader's success and that is why I would pay the greatest attention to it. Now comes the big question, how does a part-time worker manage to complete 3600 trades in a short period of time? One possibility would be as a scalper who trades between 1 and 2 minutes. Goal 2 pip TP and a stop of 2 pip. Now let's look at how that could work. A beginner with an unconscious competence completes 900 trades per year, makes 10% profit and 90% loss and trades 0.25 lots. His loss is € 4050, the profit is € 675 and the total loss is € 3375 after the first year. In the second year the profit increases to 20%, the number of lots is increased to 0.5 and the profit increases more than the loss. In the third year the profit increases to 30%, the number of lots is increased to 0.75 and again the profit increases more than the loss. In the fourth year, the part-time trader has reached his breakeven point. After six years he has made up all the losses, is somewhat in profit and then has the opportunity to work as a full-time trader. With good money management, he can make significantly higher profits and improve his odds over the next few years.

As we know, the biggest mistake is to believe that trading is easy. This is simply because you need a certain amount of time to learn this activity. An apprentice learns a trade for three years, the doctor studies and as a trading beginner I try to break even. The craftsman is now learning as a journeyman, the doctor is still studying and the trader is now trying to optimize his profits. After nine years the craftsman is a master, the doctor becomes a specialist and the trader is possibly a professional. First, let's look at the first three crucial years of an apprentice in a craft. He needs 2,000 theory hours and 4,000 practical hours, so a total of 6,000 hours in three years. Let's transfer that to a part-time trader who wants to break even in four years. First of all, during this time he goes through all four skill levels, he needs 1000 practical hours and 500 theory hours per year. To complete 3,600 trades in four years, 900 trades per year are necessary. This means the part-time trader has to be ready to trade 4 hours a day, invest 10 hours in theory on the weekend and complete four trades a day. You automatically ask yourself whether it can be done this way in four years.

Let us assume that it is theoretically possible, it would ultimately still mean a loss of € 12,000 in the first three years and the breakeven point would only be reached in the fourth year. Even after five years there would still be a total loss of € 7,500. What do you think your partner says about it? With the right mentor at your side, you may be able to skip two skill levels and even save two years of losses. This means that after five years you will have achieved an advantage of over € 30,000. If you have spent 1000-2000 € on the trading coach, it can even pay off under certain circumstances.

Basically you don't need a coach to be successful, but a mentor is often helpful if he is there for you at the right moment. A mentor differs from a coach in that he does not pass on a mass product to thousands of traders, but helps you individually. He also does not advertise, but is recommended only secretly. When you meet a coach, first let them show you his personal setup. If he is ready to teach you his setup in a personal single training, you are already a decisive step further. Trading Millionaire, How Realistic Is That?

Hello dear traders,

And that is exactly what will be achieved in the rarest of cases, since every person is different. On the one hand, the trading coaches tell that it is not easy to become a millionaire, but at the same time they get out of their sports car with a wad of money or show their newest villa. Let's start with the pure probability and to what extent it is possible for you to become a millionaire in trading. Let's do a little test for that. Your goal now is to predict the movement of the next seven M1 candles. A candle can only run up or down. We neglect dojis here. Let's start with the first candle, it goes up or down? The correct answer is: The candle run down. Do we come to the second candle that goes up or down? She runs upstairs. Where does the next candle go? Downward. Let's do a little test to understand the probability that you need to become a millionaire in trading. Our alphabet consists of 26 letters. If you have chosen exactly these four letters, regardless of the order, there is a chance that trading will make you a millionaire. From this the withholding tax of € 633,000 becomes due and a profit of € 554,000 remains. We just missed the million.

How the big players manipulate us

Hello dear subscribers,

the new video is online and, as always, you will first receive the English translation. You can find the link from the video at the end of my post.

The reason why so many traders lose is due to the fact that the current market situation is often misinterpreted. This is less due to the ability of the trader than to the fact that the big players are show us a false truth. In today's video we will take a closer look at how the big players manipulate the markets and mislead us in the process.

First of all, I would like to go back to the different proportions of the various markets. In the middle we see the daily turnover bar in the Forex market, a total of 8000 billion dollars. The global stock market trades $ 400 billion a day. This makes the Forex market 20 times larger than all stocks that are traded worldwide. In the future and options market, 400 billion are traded daily and here too the forex market is 20 times larger. The EURUSD is the largest asset in the Forex market at $ 2,400 billion.

If we now compare this single asset to the global stock market, the EURUSD is still 6 times larger than the 51,000+ public companies listed on the stock exchange worldwide. The EURUSD is also 6 times as large as all futures and options on the world's stock exchanges. It should therefore seem logical that the largest big players in the world are almost exclusively at home in forex.

If we look at the 100 largest big players in EURUSD, we see that they trade an average of 166,000 lots per day. That is an average sales volume of $ 16.6 billion, with the biggest big players approaching a sales volume of $ 100 billion every day. The daily sales volume of the world's largest stock, Apple, is $ 8 billion. Now it should also be clear why the world's largest big players rarely operate in the stock or futures markets. As we know, the forex market was only founded so that banks could trade with one another, independently of the stock exchanges. This results in significantly lower costs for the banks. The main intention of the various traders in EURUSD is not to profit, but primarily to exchange different currencies around the world. There are different hedging models and hedging transactions with currencies. Of course, the EURUSD is also used to make a profit, but one should differentiate between the various market participants such as scalpers, day traders and swing traders. There are also different transactions that banks carry out on behalf of customers. Since the twelve largest big players in EURUSD dominate the market by 85%, it should be obvious to specialize in precisely this target group, as these big players leave the biggest footprints in the market.

At the beginning and towards the middle of the month there are regular large currency transactions in EURUSD. However, these can only be read out with stock exchange data. On May 11, 2020 we can see in Euro FX how 1135 lots entered the market in the form of market buy orders. As a rule, these currency transactions are carried out with market orders, since processing with limit orders would take much too long. In this case, the dollar was exchanged for euros. The green circles show an exit from the dollar. The problem with this is that inexperienced market participants see it as buying a euro. Since the forex market is 100 times larger than the futures market, the turnover here was around $ 11 billion. Big banks have the order from different big companies to carry out a currency exchange at a certain point in time. The big bank would like to take up this volume with its own limit orders in order to generate an additional trade from it. However, this procedure is prohibited by the stock exchange supervisory authority. Theoretically, however, there are partner banks that are friends and take up this volume with their limit orders. The only requirement you just have to know at what point in time, at what price level, what number of volumes will come into the market. Then they can push the market in the profit direction and at the end share the profit.

Let's take a look at an example in 5 seconds where 1000 lot market buy orders were accepted by a friendly partner bank with limit sell orders. It was definitely too fast for most of them, so let's take another look at it a little slower. First of all, we see how regularly 100 lot market buy orders come into the market and are absorbed by the hidden iceberg orders. The befriended partner bank had already filled the decisive price levels with iceberg orders hours beforehand, as there was a clear agreement. Gradually, the market buy orders are absorbed, whereby of course one or the other lot also benefits other market participants. After all market buy orders have been accepted, the partner bank withdraws its iceberg orders on the limit buy side. Now massive market sell orders are shot into the market and push the price down. What is happening right now? We take another closer look, when the big market buy orders hit the market. What do you think the retail traders who are seeing this are thinking? They believe that a big player is buying massive ask to push the market up. What most do not know is that it is not the euro that is being bought, but that the dollar is being sold. Many market participants will now also enter the market with a long position in the hope that it will generate a high profit.

After the partner bank has pushed the price 10 ticks down, the first stops of the long traders are triggered. Now a chain reaction occurs and the price continues to decline. The 1000 Lot Limit Sell Order has now reached an average profit of 15 ticks. Converted to the Forex market, this already results in a profit of almost $ 10 million. And we are only at the beginning, the course will with a high probability continue to go down. Now let's look at the situation in the Forex market. Here we see the entry of 100,000 lots, since the Forex market is 100 times larger than the futures market. Then the course was strategically pushed down. The white zone is an artificial resistance zone created by the big players. Many market participants were now of the opinion that the course would go up. With the help of the stops triggered by the long traders, the price was pushed down. That was an excellent starting point to get out of the dollar position with market buy orders. Many institutional traders were of the opinion that the price would continue to decline and were therefore willing to place liquidity in the form of limit sell orders. Overall, this resulted in a profit of around $ 40 million, which the two big players then shared. The market was now up and the major customers for whom the currency exchange was carried out were also satisfied in the end. If the currency exchange had been processed at the blue arrow above, that would have been a clear disadvantage for the major customers. In the end, the winner was the bank that processed the currency exchange. First, she made huge fees on the currency exchange plus an additional $ 20 million. All's well that ends well.

It is precisely for this reason that it is crucial to know what is happening in the market. for many years, I too used to be of the opinion that a big player would buy massively Ask. At the time I didn't understand what was happening. Here we see a situation that occurred last year at the beginning of the corona crisis. Due to the lockdown, many traders were not at their workplaces and were therefore unable to place the crucial limit orders in the market, which ensure low volatility. This resulted in massive high volatility in the EURUSD. The central banks stepped in and within 5 minutes $ 50 billion was shot into the EURUSD. The situation calmed down and then there was a greater equilibrium. Those who identify such situations immediately are able to save a lot of money by not participating in the market.

Basically, every trader has the decision whether to work in the Forex market without stock market data or in the future market with stock market data. Due to the in-depth stock market data, future traders often feel they have an advantage. But is that really the case?

Is the future trader more professional...

• although he is taking a disproportionately higher risk

• Even though he is trading in a 100 times smaller market

• Although he doesn't get anywhere with volume either

• Although he has a win rate three times smaller

• Although he needs more capital to trade

• Although he has to trade at least 1 lot

• Although it is recognized more quickly in the market

• Although he has less information available

• Although it is often slower to trade

• Although he pays more fees

As I have already written in several posts, the solution could be the hybrid trader. Forex and future data are combined with one another. However, some changes are necessary for this. The change in the stock exchange has also changed strategies over the past 600 years. Anyone who works with candle formations, market technology, chart technology or indicators today will notice that they quickly reach their limits due to the way the big players work. More than ten years ago, the hype came from the USA with the footprint chart and volume trading.

Why doesn't volume training work?

First of all, the volume is just an addition of the ask and bid. Bid, these are the market sell orders, that run into liquidity, i.e. the limit buy orders. Ask, these are the market buy orders, that run into liquidity, i.e. the limit sell orders. However, bid and ask never meet in the market and have nothing to do with each other; curiously, they are added up anyway. Of course you can see the total volume with it, but this is the past and I am not able to tell whether an accumulation or distribution has taken place. On the bid side we see a distribution in equilibrium, then a stop hunting upwards and then the course runs downwards. Stophunting has the cheapest price and the low the highest price. The equilibrium has the fairer price. If we now draw in the volume, we will find that the largest volume mountain always shows the fair price. But we don't want to trade in equilibrium or at a fair price, we want to buy cheap and sell again at high prices. It looks the same on the Ask side. This is just one of the reasons why volume trading doesn't work and is based on sheer chance.

When looking at the accumulation and distribution phases, one automatically asks oneself which data is most important in order to make effective trading decisions from it? Let us first look at the accumulation phase, where the ask is collected, there may still be stopfishing, the price will be pushed up until the big player exits the euro at point B. In the re-accumulation phase, ask is collected again, possibly stopfishing, the price is pushed up until the big players exit the euro at point D. In the distribution phase, the bid is collected and the price is pushed down until the big players exit the dollar. In the re-distribution phase, bids are also collected and the price is pushed down until the big players exit the dollar again. If, as a trader, I am able to identify points A through H, I have already achieved a great goal.

As a hybrid trader, this is much easier because my attention is focused on the big players and I try to use the algorithms to find out which limit orders are currently being collected. To do this, I should know the different big player strategies exactly. If it is an accumulation or distribution, the big player is pushing the price right through, making his own volume available or is a currency exchange taking place with a front running on the limit side. I just showed you this situation in the video. Then it is essentially a matter of finding out which market orders fill the special limit orders in order to carry out a collective action. With specially filtered limit orders, this can be seen exactly in the market. From this I create my individual navigation map, which shows me exactly when the euro or dollar is being bought or sold.

It is not the strongest species to survive, nor the most intelligent, it is the one that is most likely to adapt to change. However, change often creates fear, frustration and stress. For this reason, people like to avoid change. When you are forced to change as an employer, there is initially a shock. Rejection is the first reaction to oppose the change. After the frustration, acceptance slowly arises. You start to test the change, it gets a bit bumpy and you come to the realization that it has significantly more advantages than the old way of working. Integration begins with future success. The worst sentence there is: We have always done it this way. Among other things, this could also be a reason why these previously very successful companies no longer exist today. Incidentally, these were the ten largest bankruptcies in Germany.

The biggest stake I traded with was 20 lots. That means I was in the market with over € 2 million, but with this large sum I was hardly able to influence the market. To move the market by one pip in EURUSD, you need between 10-20,000 lots. Now some will say you can move the market with one lot, that's true, but a big player must have invested 19,999 lots beforehand in order, that you can move the market with one lot. I think it becomes clear what I want to show with this. If we are not able to move the market, we have to let the big players take us away. To do this, however, I have to know beforehand which direction it will take in the future. This only works with the help of the filtered limit orders. For the short-term movements, I have to go deeper into the market, the filtered algorithms help me to see exactly where the short-term movements are going.

In the last 5 years the situation on the markets has changed significantly. New algorithms and strategies create more confusion, the error rate increases and the losses increase. The big players are upgrading, the technology is becoming faster and more efficient. Anyone who wants to survive in this market in the long term must also keep up with progress and invest. We may not have the necessary money to implement the same technical equipment as the big players, but those who are creative and willing to continue their education will still have a lot of fun in the markets for the next few years. You don't need a lot of money for this, but you need the right filter settings to see exactly what the big players are up to. A trader needs a market advantage in order to make money and we find that market advantage in the algorithms. It all sounds very complicated, but basically it's easier than you think. We will deal with it more concretely in the next few months, maybewith this informations you will come closer and closer to your goal.

10 golden rules of feedback

The purpose of feedback should be to promote the professionalism of the individual. In addition, feedback should promote openness, honesty and trust in interpersonal relationships as a prerequisite for fruitful cooperation. Feedback is constructive when the addressee receives information about alternative courses of action. General statements are not very helpful here. However, prompt and value-free feedback on specific observations can be a valuable learning aid that can contribute to the further development of the feedback recipient.

Feedback requested

Feedback is most effective when the recipient has asked for it. When a person surprised someone with feedback, he can't hope for a trusting relationship.

Usefulness of the feedback

One should check the usefulness of one's feedback. Feedback should relate to aspects that the recipient can change. If one make the other person aware of shortcomings that he cannot change, this feedback is useless for him.

Rating in feedback

One should describe one's own perception and reaction. It should be left to the other to use this information or not. By neglecting to judge, one reduce the other person's need to defend themselves.

Controlled feedback

Feedback should be controlled, taking into account one's own behavior, expressed as a subjective perception and referring to specific events or behaviors.

Clear feedback

Feedback must be precisely formulated and understandable. The feedback should relate to specific aspects, not generally to the whole person and their overall behavior. If one tell someone they are rude, he or she has little use for behavior change. Therefore, it is better to show what the person actually did and to what extent they prevented the group from developing.

Factually correct feedback

The observation must also be able to be understood by others. Unobjective in the original sense would be statements that are either fictitious or do not belong to the area about which the feedback recipient expects feedback. This also includes those that contain pure value judgments with little or no reference to observable behavior.

Moral feedback

Avoiding moral condemnation is essential. This reduces the urge for the other person to defend himself and reject the feedback.

Observed feedback

One should refer to observations as opposed to guesswork, fantasies, or interpretations. This makes the feedback more believable.

Inadequacies in feedback

One should only address changeable behaviors and not inadequacies over which the person concerned has relatively little or no influence.

Appropriate feedback

We should always give due consideration to the needs of the recipient. If someone doesn't care whether it benefits or even harms the recipient, one destroys their trust. Therefore one should always check the appropriateness of his feedback. Feedback can be destructive if one only see his own needs and not those of the recipient. Therefore, one should think about it beforehand whether one just want to get rid of his own aggressions.

Conclusion:

Since feedback is the feedback on one's own perception, the feedback often says more about the person giving the feedback than about the person receiving the feedback. The inner attitude is crucial. Anyone who looks at the matter with an astonished, curious look and researches what lies behind it, how one's own perception is supplemented, which pieces of the puzzle are missing from one's own understanding, can even deepen relationships and strengthen trust through regular feedback.
