If he doubled the number of trades per day, he would cut the time in half. A minute scalper who trades 2 hours a day on 200 days creates 1500 trades per year and is already at breakeven after 4 years with 1600 hours of experience. With twice the number of trades, he already achieved the goal after two years. The reason why a scalper can break even after 1600 hours is simply the experience of the many different trades. The seconds scalper comes to the same result here, but is able to significantly increase the number of trades again and thus shorten the time to one year. In addition, we can see some graphics that help us with the further evaluation. Of course, all executed trades are shown again individually. We see the entry time and on the left how long it took for the next trade to be completed. 297 short trades were lost, each short trade lasted an average of 2.5 minutes and here we see how many seconds it was in the trade. Here are the data for the short winners, long losers, and long winners. The respective profit and loss, as well as the cumulative value. With this view, the individual trades can be analyzed excellently.

Let us first consider the graphical evaluation of the loss trades. It is noticeable that the loss series get smaller at the end. It is also noticeable that the profits are getting bigger and bigger, although the breakeven point is the first goal. With 705 trades, my friend has only covered 12% of the way to reach his breakeven point. With this table you can of course display countless evaluations in order to get to the bottom of the individual problems. But that would go beyond the scope of today. However, I would like to show you one little thing that ultimately changes the result decisively. A stop of two pips, including the spread, was agreed, which in the end results in a loss of 17-20 cents per lost trade. You can see that at the beginning the stop was was enlarged and then, which became more and more dramatic in the end. Incidentally, only 1% of the stops that were made were successful, so you should generally avoid them. Now I've just made a new calculation of what it would look like if my friend hadn't enlarged his stops. Let's take a look at the result now. Here we see the graphic representation where the stops have been drawn and below what it would have looked like if the stop had been adhered to. Instead of a loss of € 21.70, the loss would only be € 12.45. That's a 43% difference. The CRV would improve from 1.48 to 1.67, which is over 13%. This would also improve efficiency by 13%. The decisive point, however, lies in the expected value, which would improve from -3 cents to -2 cents, that is a huge 33%. Perhaps you remember this table, an expected value of -7 cents was planned for the first 666 trades. Without following the stop, he would already have been -2 cents and would have achieved an even better result. This is a target value that he should only reach after 3,500 trades. Based on the graphics you can see that it is usually not worth enlarged the stop.

There are 1000 ways to achieve the goal. It is important that you know exactly where the individual sources of error lie, because only then can you do something about it. This means that with strategic money management there is a clear strategy to achieve the goal in a relaxed manner. Because we should note: If you make a mistake and don't correct it, you commit another mistake. As it stands now, my friend will reach his personal breakeven point by the end of the year and that within six months. His maximum loss will be € 160. In the next year we will then take care of maximizing profits and gradually increase the number of lots from 0.1 to five lots. He would then be able to generate some € 10,000 in pre-tax income in the next year. Even if it were only half of it or, in the worst case, no profit at all, he would have achieved one goal in any case: his breakeven point. And that would make him one of the 10% of the best traders in the world after just one year. And I think that's a nice goal to get up motivated every morning. Trading with debt capital, demo or real money?

Attached Image

Hello dear subscribers,

the new video is online and, as always, you will first receive the English translation. You can find the link from the video at the end of my post.

Today we're making a big movie , because we will compare the differences between debt capital, demo and real money trading. We look at the extent to which demo trading is helpful and also talk about the different emotions that we encounter every day in trading. We will also look at how we can optimally train these emotions in the future. In the overall result, you will at the end see a clear procedure with which you will have your emotions under control in the future. The choice is yours, you can choose to trade, where your chances of success are around 10%. Or you opt for self-employment where the chances of success are 5 times higher, at around 50%. Are you aware of these probabilities and still want to decide to trade? Okay, then we should ask ourselves a few questions first.

Why do you want to trade, who are you doing it for, in what time should it happen, what is your goal, how do you do it and who will help you? Let's start with the first question: why do you want to learn to trade? There are of course many answers to this question. Freedom, for example, can be one of them. Who are you doing this for For your family, for you, for the future. In what time do you want to reach your goal? Preferably as soon as possible, a realistic point in time would be in four years for a part-time job. What is your goal in trading? Of course the independence, as if we hadn't suspected it. The question is how do you do it? The answer: of course, this is only possible with a clear strategy and support. At the end: who will help you? It is best to have a reliable mentor who may even accompany you for many years. Take a look at my two videos. The first:

Inserted Video

Analysis, what do you need a trading coach for? The second video:

Inserted Video

You should do without these trading coaches and this is how you will find a suitable mentor

In these posts you will get a lot of ideas on how you can possibly find your optimal mentor in trading in the future.

There are basically three different approaches to learning to trade. Firstly you trade with debt capital, secondly you trade in the demo account or thirdly you trade with your own money. Let us first analyze the debt capital. Again, we should ask ourselves a few questions. Why, for whom, in what time, what is the goal, how do you do it, who will help you? Let us first start with the question why would someone want to trade with debt capital? Well either he has no money or he doesn't want to lose his hard earned money. First of all, neither answer exactly suggests that the trader is a professional. Would you give money to a trader who doesn't have one himself or who is unwilling to risk his own money? Now the external lenders have already asked themselves the question and for this very reason an applicant must first qualify for such a loan account. There are different models for this that I do not want to go into in detail today.

In most cases, such a qualification initially costs a few € 1,000 in fees. When you've got the qualification and training, you end up being an order taker. You are only allowed to trade in certain markets at certain times, you will receive clear instructions about your stop size and your maximum drowdown. When you trade you pay monthly fees for the software and the equipment as well as you also pay the spread that you cause by your trade. Of course, the spread is often cheaper, but many ask themselves why they should pay the spread, even though the lender initially withholds over half of the winnings. Now the thing is very clear, you are nothing more than a freelance commercial agent and you should urgently be careful in this constellation that you do not get into the area of bogus self-employment. In what time will you be successful, well that's in the stars, because of course nobody in trading can tell you that. What is the goal? Your goal is clear, you would like to become successful without investing your own capital.

The lender of course also wants to be successful and expects you to give him half of your profit at the beginning and pay monthly for the software and your spread. How do you manage to achieve this? Probably with a lot of money and time. Who will help you with this? Now, of course, the external lender will support you wherever he can, but please do not believe that he will do everything possible to make you successful. Because whether you make it or not is not relevant for the external financier. Why is that? Of course, the external financier has a large number of applicants and prospective traders who are in training. With 100 applicants who each pay € 3,000, that's already an impressive sum of € 300,000. The bad applicants are selected from and, of course, only the best remain in the end. That means the external financier has to sort out the class from the crowd. By the way, if you haven't made it in the end, you can usually not do much with the information you have been taught, since every debt capital lender has his own system that you of course cannot take with you in the end. Most third-party funder systems are a type of franchise, with the emphasis on the second syllable. (In Germany the 2nd syllable has a meaning that would be comparable to the word crap or sh..)

Let's move on to the next challenge, trading in a demo account. First of all, trading in the demo account is a kind of trading in the matrix, i.e. in an unreal environment. Why is this unreal? Well, because you are investing money in a virtual market to which the market ultimately cannot react. Perhaps you've already played with a flight simulator on your computer and actually managed to take off or land an Airbus. Of course, there have been countless attempts to find out whether a passenger could land an airplane in an emergency. That actually went well a few times in the flight simulator. But imagine now that the pilots would have failed on a real flight and you would now have to land a real airplane as a layman. What we must not forget are our emotions and it is precisely these that ultimately ensure that the aircraft does not hit the ground in one piece. It is similar with a real money account in contrast to a demo account. Trading in a demo account affects us more peripherally, because in the end we actually have nothing to lose. Our emotions are not as pronounced as in real money trading.

What I find particularly dangerous about demo accounts is the data that is made available to us by the various brokers. These differ considerably from reality. Here you can see my Bionic candle in a demo account. I used the Bionic candle because you can see the deviations here immediately. There are 23 yellow candles, 17 blue candles and 16 dojis in the M1 chart. And now let's take a look at the real money account with the same broker. All of a sudden there are 31 yellow candles, 21 blue candles and 13 dojis. First of all, this clearly proves that there are different price positions. How am I supposed to learn to trade correctly with wrong price positions? Let's take a closer look at the discrepancy. You see that there are clear differences that, at times, can have great implications. This is not noticeable with the normal candles, but with my Bionic candle you can see the difference immediately. Of course, I also compared the exchange rate data between the demo and the real money account and found a discrepancy of over 22%. That would be a reason for me not to trade with a demo account.

In many of my videos, I have already explicitly shown the effort the big players put in to strategically stop scalpers, day traders and swing traders. The market is regularly pushed up and down in zigzag lines and analyzed which stops are triggered. I will go into this in more detail in one of my next posts. Now imagine that someone is trading with 50 lots in a demo account and is amazed at the end that he has even won several € 1,000. This scenario is so unrealistic, I would like to prove to you why that is so. Imagine that you are trading in the five largest currency pair in the world, the US dollar and the Canadian dollar. You now invest a real 50 lot in this currency pair. In the forex US dollar Canadian dollar, 3.3 million lots are traded every day, that is 2000 lots per minute. If you invest five lots, that corresponds to a minute share of 0.3%. This is already noticeable in the forex market. To fly under the radar you should be 0.1% or less. With 50 Lot the big players have you on their screen immediately, and you can guess three times who will be stopped next? With such a lot size one naturally has to think about other order types than the market order. In the futures market, 330,000 Canadian dollar lots are traded per day, which is 200 lots per minute. If you trade with five lots they already have you on the screen and with 50 lots you are even trading 25% of the total minute turnover. It's a bit like the mouse trying to sneak past the sleeping cat with a loud radio. We already know now, that the demo data differ considerably from the data of the real money accounts in the Forex market.

It is alarming that the future data is also incorrect. Now many will be surprised and say: Why? The data come from the stock exchange and since there is only one exchange, the data must also be correct. Unfortunately, this is not the case. There are different data feed providers that are in turn sold by different brokers. Take a data feed from CTS and compare it with Rhythic. We use a footprint chart for each. As a result, you will find that these two footprint charts show different numbers, even though you are looking at the same unit of time. The high-frequency traders and big players use data feeds that are updated ten times per second. These special data feeds cost approximately $ 120,000 per month. Look, a lot of us use data feeds that cost between $ 10-30 a month. We cannot seriously assume that these data feeds are actually 100% correct. From my point of view, these are data feeds that have already been cleaned up by the high-frequency traders. Despite the not entirely correct data, I still found a solution that was optimal for me. I compared many different forex and future brokers in the euro US dollar and selected exactly those where the price developments were most consistent with each other.

Here we see two tick charts in EURUSD, on the left in the futures market and on the right in the forex market. Of course, we have to note that these are two different markets, but the price movements are almost tickly accurate. By the way, with this representation you can also check exactly whether the forex broker is transmitting exact data. I trade in the forex market and make my decisions based on the stock market data. Since I have compared the forex with the future data, it doesn't really matter to me whether the data is correct or not. It is only important that my data behave parallel to each other. With that I created my own virtual market. There is another important aspect that we must not neglect. From my point of view there are four different types of traders. First of all, there is the pragmatic trader who owes his success or failure to his extravert, speculative thinking. The experimental trader builds on extraverted, intuitive feeling. The reflective trader wins through introverted, sensitive feeling, while the introverted empirical thinking helps the synthetic trader. Each of these four different personalities uses different approaches to achieve the goal. There are scalpers, day traders and swing traders who each pursue different approaches. The pragmatic trader naturally has his greatest advantages in the pragmatic area. For example, he is demanding, determined, strong-willed, goal-oriented and fact-oriented. However, this also means that there can be individual weaknesses in the synthetic, reflective and experimental areas. Only those who know their own strengths and weaknesses can respond individually and thus behave in a success-oriented manner. This is especially true on the stock exchange. I will go into this topic again in a separate video.

Let's now look at the harsh reality, i.e. trading with real money on the stock exchange. Basically, we have already established that we can only bring out our hidden emotions through extreme situations on the stock market. And it is precisely these hidden emotions that we have to train over and over again in order to be able to control them in the long term. And that only works through extreme gains or losses. On this subject I strongly recommend you to watch my last four videos:

Incidentally, these videos build on each other. So we know that you can train your emotions just like a muscle. The question now arises as to how we are able to train our emotions regularly and to condition them accordingly. And this conditioning is ultimately the decisive success factor. There's no point in going to the gym and exercising your muscles regularly if you don't know anything about conditioning.

In my last videos we already talked about it in detail, We start with 0.01 lot, a win rate of 30% and an expected value of -5 cents. This inevitably means that we lose 1400 times in every 2000 trades. In the second phase we continue to trade with 0.01 lots, a profit rate of 35% and an expected value of -3 cents. For every 2000 trades we will lose 1300 times. In the final phase, we achieve a 40% win rate and break even. Out of 2000 trades we will lose 1200 times. This means that with my approach you will lose almost 4000 times. This gives you 4000 times the opportunity to condition your hidden emotions accordingly. Let's take a look at some hidden emotions.

Many traders have the uncomfortable habit of selling too early just to finally take a profit in addition to the previous loss cycle. For fear of losses, very promising trades are not even entered into. Under certain circumstances, it happens that a real series of losses awaits the trader. If you go long the market goes short, if you go short the market goes long immediately. The question is how to deal with this situation. The market is going in your direction and developing well, your TP would have been reached a long time ago, but you always want more. Suddenly there is a strong countermovement, you are just about to break even or even suffer a loss. After you have been stopped countless times, you now do without your stop and achieve very large losses in the process. In certain situations you are unfocused or careless and thereby fail to achieve your goals. The market is moving down and you get in a few times to trade the reversal or pullback up. You will be stopped every time. Like an offended child, you keep pushing the buy button to recoup your losses andyou keep losing again ans again. It gets really bad if you even increase your position. It gets very dramatic if you regularly enlarge your stops. We talked about this point in great detail in my last video. If you don't stick to your own strategy, why did you even impose rules on yourself? With this approach we can put our emotions to the test 4000 times. This is a huge opportunity that will pay off in the long term.

Even if your trading plan is very structured, extreme emotions will screw up all of your odds. In such a phase we let our fear-driven survival strategies coduct. Then come up with statements like: I'll show the market, or this time I won't let myself be stopped. It is really bad if you want to clean up losses immediately. In our life we have been taught that we must correct a mistake immediately. In trading, however, it is exactly the other way around. There you have to wait and see. If we make a mistake in trading, then of course we have lost money. But it must be clear to us that we can only correct this mistake once we have found a new entry opportunity. And that can sometimes take a while. Many traders are also afraid of missing out if a price goes up or down sharply. With my approach, I have a new chance every two and a half minutes, so I'm never afraid of missing out. We just have to be aware that in the beginning we only lose. That is why we focus on limiting losses and working with very small positions. With a clear strategy we only lose a maximum of € 160 after 6000 trades. You can find information about this in my previous videos. After these 6000 trades we finally reach our breakeven point and can then shift our priorities towards profit maximization. With a clever scaling, we manage to build up an interesting profit within a short time. The nice thing about our initial losses, which we kept as small as possible. They are not noticeable in the end. And why? Because at the beginning we trade with a low lot, because we know that we will only lose. If we have our emotions under control, we can turn our position size up at any time and compensate for the small initial losses very quickly. The main reason a beginner loses so much is primarily because of his or her emotions. In principle, one day you have to be able to trade on a large real money account as if it were ultimately a demo account.

Conclusion:

So our goal is to do our trading with as few emotions as possible and to accept losses as the most normal in the world. You can do this by writing down your trading setup, avoiding over-trading and taking small breaks from time to time. Unfortunately, we humans are not suited to holding our own mirror in front of our faces. And for this very reason I recommend you to find a suitable mentor, by the way, this is not a trading coach who only offers you mass-produced goods. --- 帖子 #1676 ---
Read charts correctly

Attached Image

Hello dear subscribers,

the new video is online and, as always, you will first receive the English translation. You can find the link from the video at the end of my post.

Many traders spend their lives searching for the holy grail. You dream of recognizing every turning point in advance as possible in order to earn a lot of money with it. In today's post we talk about how a trader is able to read the charts correctly over the long term. An important topic here are the price gaps that we encounter again and again in the chart. With the stock market wisdom that 90% of all price gaps are closed again, traders often get involved in daring trade executions. In today's post we look at the largest gap in EURUSD that has emerged in the last ten years and how traders have reacted to it. At the end we look at an outbreak and how you can clearly identify it beforehand.

In the last 30 years a total of six large price gaps of more than 180 pips have arisen, the last big price gap was in April 2017. Here we see the chart image in the daily chart before the price gap upwards arose. From the trader's point of view, the price was in a downward movement. If we zoom in closer, we notice an extreme downward course, that was the result of the election night between Hillary Clinton and Donald Trump. Many traders have drawn a resistance zone there and when the price got into the zone it was turned down again. The further trend looked just as bearish at first glance. We all know only too well what happened after that. Between April 21 and April 24, 2017, there was a gap of 180 pips. On April 21, the price closed at 1.07220 and opened at around 1.09 on April 24 at 12:00 AM. This means that the market orders were placed on April 21, 2017 shortly before the close. Had that not been the case, the price would have opened at 1.07220 on April 24 and would then have risen sharply. As we know, however, there was a gap in the course. This means that on April 21, shortly before the close, a large number of market buy orders came into the market and at the same time the liquidity of the limit sell orders was very low.

Since the exchange stopped and the market orders were already in the market, the resulting strong upward movement could no longer be executed. If the market had been open for 1 minute longer, the situation would have been as follows. In principle, this price gap can thus be described as a large, strong candle that was triggered by low liquidity in the area of limit orders and, at the same time, a high volume in the area of market orders. After the price gap arose in April 2017, the price went up to 1.255. In total, it took almost three years until the gap was finally closed again. Whether in the end the gap was actually responsible for the fact that the price went down over two and a half years to close it is pure speculation.

What is interesting, however, is the way in which this gap was closed and we will now take a closer look at that. Before the gap was closed completely, the price had already entered the gap twice. We first consider the situation with the yellow arrow. In the second contact phase, I once drew in the Pip values in 4 hours in the H4. You can find some videos about the pip value per minute on my channel. The findings from the yellow square are the most interesting, so let's take a closer look. The higher the value in 4 hours, the stronger the movement up or down. As we can see, the course is in equilibrium here. The big players recognize from this how many long and short traders are in the market at the time. When a price is pushed up, the short traders are stopped and at the same time, with their triggered stops, help drive the market up. When the big players pushed the price up to 438, it was clear that there was a massive number of short traders in the market. Now the market has been pushed down again to motivate more short traders and to stop the long traders. After that, the market slowly went up. Let's look at the situation again with my specially filtered limit orders.

We can see that massive bids were collected in the limit sell orders from February 13th to 17th. From my point of view, the big players actually planned to close the Gap. We also note that on February 18th and 19th, bids continued to be collected even at the low price. On February 20th, the big players realized that the majority of traders had taken a short position because they all expected that the gap would now be closed. The big players take advantage of the situation and now again sold their short position to the willing short traders. Then on February 21st, you push the price up sharply with the help of the short trader's stops. At the high they started collecting ask and after that the price went up a total of 700 pips.

Now the question arises why the course went beyond the gap. To answer this question we have to go back to April 2017 to find the corresponding key candle. We zoom in a little, stay in the daily chart and notice three blue candles that signal a strong downward movement. We draw a zone in this strong downward movement and see which candle breaks through this zone. This is exactly our key candle that will help us plan the next long trade at a later date. Of course you can refine the zone up to the M1 a bit. You can also find information about this on my channel.

We do the same for the second blue candle. We identify the key candle and draw the appropriate zone. Now we come to the third and decisive zone. Interestingly, this key candle was actually the strongest. We now draw this zone and now go into the future. The course went up to 1.25 and then took two and a half years to get exactly into the zone. After that, the price went up from 1.07 to 1.23. Perhaps that should also be a good reason for you in the future to take a closer look at the key candles.

Half a year later the election was in America. On the morning of November 4th, 2020, I carried out a detailed analysis of the election night and published the following post on my blog at Forex Factory. An exciting election night is behind us and at this point in time the winner has not yet been determined. If you compare the price development in November 2016 with the price development last night, from the trader's point of view it looks as if Biden could win the election. We will see which candidate the voters have chosen. In addition to the exciting question of who will win the election, the course in the euro US dollar was much more decisive for me. All in all, it took a few weeks, until it was actually clear that Biden had won the election so easily. Interestingly, the market already knew that beforehand.

Finally, let's take a look at the outbreak on Wednesday July 28th. First turn your attention to the existing limit orders. There were around 600 limit buy and 600 limit sell orders in the DoM. The big players had collected massive requests in advance and you could see from the stops that the majority of traders were long-oriented. In this respect, the Fed conference was a good opportunity to get these unpleasant long traders out of the market. I also initially expected a somewhat stronger short movement. We look again at the limit orders, which are now around 400 lots on each side. The big players are currently massively withdrawing their limit orders, which speaks for a future breakout. In the middle you can see a bigger box. On the left side we see the strength of the limit buy orders, on the right side the strength of the limit sell orders. And now pay close attention to how suddenly the strength of the limit orders diminishes massively. That's exactly when the outbreak begins. We know exactly that when there is no liquidity in the market, few market orders are able to move the price massively. The big players have used this downward breakout to collect additional Ask at a lower price level. After that, the price was pushed up again and continued to move up over the next few days.

With the help of this information, it is often possible to precisely identify the turning point, even in the smallest units of time. However, you have to be prepared to invest in the appropriate technology and training. In my videos you will find many examples that may motivate you to study the algorithms in more detail in the future. In the next few weeks I have some projects on the program where we will penetrate the market even deeper with very professional programmers. I'll go into that in more detail in my next videos.

Vanities versus constructive feedback

The SWOT analysis

Attached Image

Hello dear subscribers

In today's post, we're starting a new series of interesting information that so far many traders have neglected. The background: We traders often focus on systems, setups, algorithms or strategies without thinking about ourselves first. Success is often so close to us, but we don't see the forest for the trees. That is why we doggedly concentrate on things that actually do not get us any further. Not the volume or a new indicator ensure our breakthrough, but only the knowledge about ourselves. So we are daily in search of the holy grail, without knowing that it is right in front of our noses. In the frenzy of defeating the market, we forget the crucial point, who we are ourselves. Our success lies between our two ears, deep in our brains. And it is precisely this brain that we pay too little attention to and we forget to analyze ourselves in the process.

On YouTube we find a lot of information in the area of trading opportunities. This includes indicators, strategies, setups, certain procedures and equally interesting ways of thinking. In addition, we find numerous descriptions on the market of how we can minimize our risk with the help of money management or different strategies. In order to increase our chances and at the same time reduce our risk, we sometimes have to pay a lot of money if we take the help of some self-appointed coaches. What is often forgotten are the individual strengths that every trader brings and of course the associated weaknesses. First of all, let's refer to the opportunities and risks that we encounter in the market as hardware. In this case, our strengths and weaknesses are the software. I believe that it is clear to everyone that the best computer in the world is of no use to them if the corresponding software that they use does not run on this computer.

How do I want to take advantage of opportunities when I am not at all clear about my strengths and how should I avoid risks in the future if I am not aware of my weaknesses. In order to be successful as an entrepreneur, I first need a so-called SWOT analysis. This SWOT analysis is about the consideration of strengths and weaknesses as well as opportunities and risks of a company. With this analysis, the current state of a company can be recorded in order to initiate suitable strategic optimization measures.

With the internal analysis, the actual condition of the trader is described by first listing and analyzing the strengths and weaknesses. With the external analysis, the actual state of the stock market is determined, in which the possible opportunities and risks are listed and evaluated. The external analysis is also known as an environment analysis or market analysis. The first goal is now to expand the market opportunities with the help of my strengths. Which of my strengths are suitable for this and which are not? How can my strengths increase the chances of realization? The second goal is now to reduce my weaknesses so that my market opportunities do not deteriorate in the future. For example, how can weaknesses develop into strengths or where can opportunities arise from weaknesses? The third goal is: which risks can I counter with which strengths and how can I use my strengths to prevent certain risks. Finally, we ask ourselves the question: where do weaknesses meet risks and which activities should be avoided?

First of all, we know that most traders are aware of the opportunities and risks in the market. But very few actually know their internal strengths and weaknesses. Now comes the crucial question: how do I want to be able to take advantage of specific opportunities and risks if I am not clear about my own strengths and weaknesses? It's just as crazy as the phrase how should I know what I'm thinking before I hear what I'm saying? I know where I want to go, but I don't know what measures to take to get there. That means, until I do not really know what strengths and weaknesses I myself have, I am not able to react accordingly to this very complicated stock market. But thankfully there is YouTube and crazy people like me who might have a solution for it.

As I mentioned in some of my videos, from my point of view there are four different types of traders. The fiery doer, decidedly purposeful and willing to take risks. The blue analyst, precise, level-headed, questioning and strategic. The earth-green systematic, empathetic, reflective and constant and the sun-yellow practitioner, creative, individual and captivating. The pragmatic trader, he trades in different assets, on different platforms, with different software, prefers different strategies, analyzes different key figures and works in different time charts and representations. The blue green and yellow will also use different things for trading. These include scalpers, day traders and swing traders. And there are already big differences here. Let's imagine that a swing trader is a truck racing driver, a day trader a rally driver and a scalper a Formula 1 driver. Now, the truck racing driver gets into the rally vehicle and the rally driver into the Formula 1 car. The drivers will certainly be able to drive the respective vehicle, but would not have a realistic chance against the competition.

That means every trader is as individual as a thumbprint and that is exactly why one would have to deal with each trader individually. Unfortunately, many trading coaches forget that. Learning to trade is not comparable to a dance class, it is about a lot of money in the long term and possibly also enormous losses. That is why it is not enough just to ask what knowledge a future student has. Incidentally, this is also the reason why I can only recommend everyone to stay away from a trading coach and look for a mentor instead. You can find information about this in my videos.

Introverts focus more attention and energy on their inner workings. In groups they tend to observe more passively, than to act and are often described as quiet, reserved and calm. However, introversion is not to be equated with shyness. Extraverts are characterized by an outward-facing attitude. Extroverted characters find the exchange and action within social groups stimulating. You are talkative, determined, active, energetic, dominant, enthusiastic and adventurous fun. The task-oriented person experiences himself coherently and essentially through the orientation towards a topic or a task of interest to him. He feels in harmony with himself when he is enthusiastic about a cause, penetrates a topic or can master a task. Friendships result from a common factual orientation. The people-oriented type is essentially defined by his direct relationships with other people. He is in tune with himself and feels valuable when his relationships are right. Before working with another person, the relationship level must first be clarified.

What strengths and weaknesses the synthetic trader, the pragmatic, the experimental and the reflective trader have, we will take a closer look at in my next post. I will also show you a way to find out which of these traders you belong to in order to create a strengths and weaknesses profile. This could possibly support you more in your capacity as a trader in the future. The banknotes that a customer receives in four different banks are the same, what makes the difference are the cashiers. And that's exactly what we're going to take a closer look at next week.

Hello dear subscribers,

Over 90% of all traders lose long-term on the stock exchange and this is not only due to the sophisticated strategies of the big players. Today we will deal with the points that a trader can influence and change himself in order to reach his breakeven point. In some of my posts I have already mentioned that there are basically four different types of traders who of course achieve their goals individually. There are pragmatic, experimental, reflective and synthetic traders who have different characteristics. In today's post we will find out which category you belong to and of course uncover the associated strengths and weaknesses. This then results in possible solutions that can have very positive effects in the future. The point is not to put the four different types of traders in one drawer, because every trader naturally has different strengths and weaknesses that cannot be compared with one another. This then results in innumerable possibilities.

Each of you work in different markets and assets and there are different opportunities and risks. Anyone who knows their strengths and weaknesses exactly can use their strengths to expand the opportunities in the respective assets and at the same time hedge against possible risks. Those who know their weaknesses and reduce them to a minimum can increase their chances. An awareness of weaknesses also helps to avoid possible risks. The key here is to recognize your own strengths and weaknesses. Whoever knows others is taught, whoever knows himself is wise. Of course, every trader knows his own strengths and weaknesses, the challenge often lies in the small details that are easily overlooked. A small screw that is not tightened can cause a large airplane to crash. And for this very reason it is important to pay attention to even the smallest screw. And that is what we will deal with intensively today.

Today's trader analysis, which we create together, can only give you a rough insight into your strengths and weaknesses. If you would like to deal more deeply with this topic afterwards, I recommend dealing more with the "Biostructural Analysis" or "Insights MDI". 20 years ago, as part of my training, I acquired the trainer licenses for the "Biostructural Analysis" and “Insights” and worked with them for many years. The seminars offered on the market are not cheap, but give a deep and efficient insight into different behavioral patterns.

Let's start with the analysis first. You get 40 different statements from which you choose 10 statements that best apply to you. In order to make the analysis as objective as possible, I recommend that you answer the questions together with a partner who is close to you. I would like to briefly show you why this makes sense with the first question. It says here: When this person speaks, they appear: Confident, loud, behavioral or unemotional. Now one could use the word “loud, cautious or without emotion as negative and for this very reason would tick the box next to "Confident". That could in the end falsify the evaluation. By the way, a person who speaks a little louder will probably be surprised if this is reflected to him because he may not be aware of it. Therefore, get support from a person who knows you well.

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Here you can now see all 40 questions. A maximum of one point or a cross may be placed per question. If you are not entirely sure, it often helps to rule out the things that do not apply to you. If even two things are true, choose the answer that applies to you more often. When you have answered the questions, add up the points, they show you how strong you are in the pragmatic, experimental, reflective or synthetic area. I have now come up with a fictitious trader and filled out the analysis for him. This fictitious trader scores five points in the pragmatic range, one point in the experimental range, three points in the reflective range and one point in the synthetic range. Most of the points show its main potential, the second most points support the main potential and the fewest points show the weaknesses. This means that our fictitious trader has the greatest strength in the pragmatic area, is supported by the reflective area, while the experimental and synthetic area shows its weaknesses. Let's look at some basics first.

The synthetic and reflective trader is more introverted, while the pragmatic, experimental trader is extroverted. The synthetic and pragmatic trader is task-oriented, the reflective and experimental trader is more people-oriented. In our crosshairs, the fictitious trader with his greatest strength is in the upper right area and the support in the lower left area. At 10% each, the weaknesses are in the synthetic and experimental areas. Another important point is the differences in perception. A synthetic trader is often perceived as stiff, suspicious, cold, reserved, and indecisive. But from his point of view it looks very different. He feels himself to be cautious, precise, level-headed, questioning or formal. And that is exactly the difference between self-image and external image. Another aspect is our behavior in different areas of life. Each of us plays different roles in different situations. We behave differently at work than when we celebrate with friends. When we are sick or experience strokes of fate, we behave differently than on vacation, although we are actually always the same person. A synthetic person shows few emotions on the outside and is calm on the inside. This is certainly true when he meets a stranger, but in a safe environment like work, the situation can change. With friends or family, stronger emotions can arise. This means that our properties can change and vary depending on the situation.

Now some will ask themselves which color scheme is the best for becoming a successful trader. Now the circle has a total of 360 ° and it contains four colors. Each color can reach a maximum of 360 ° and thus a particularly high strength. Four colors each occupy 90 °. If the four colors are evenly distributed, there are no major weaknesses, but also no major strengths. The best combination is therefore ten points. Now each of you will say, well, everyone gets ten points. Exactly, that's why it doesn't matter what the color distribution looks like for success. It is crucial that you know your strengths and weaknesses and apply them accordingly to the market. In addition, you only create your personal analysis here and do not compare yourself with other participants. That would also make no sense, since every person has individual abilities that cannot be copied. In our crosshairs we first created the four different traders, let's now look at further properties.

The synthetic trader refers to facts and is able to see details. The pragmatic one also uses facts, but has an overview of the whole. The experimental trader overlooks the whole, referring to his own theses, while the reflective trader looks at his theses in detail. We see that both the synthetic and the reflective trader are able to analyze the details, while the pragmatic and experimental traders see the whole. The synthetic and pragmatic achieves success through thinking, while the reflective and experimental relies on intuition. This results in different synergies within our crosshairs. The synthetic trader is calm on the inside and shows little emotion on the outside. The pragmatic trader agrees, but is stressed inside. In addition to internal stress, the experimental shows strong emotions, while the reflective trader is internally balanced in addition to external, strong emotions. The synthetic one is precise while waiting. The pragmatic, precise and goal-oriented. The experimental is practical and goal-oriented and the reflective wait-and-see and practical.

Although most traders are active in the day trading arena, there is a very high number of swing traders in the synthetic and reflective trader arena. Likewise, most scalpers can be found in the field of pragmatic and experimental traders. The synthetic and pragmatic prefer to work alone, while the reflective experimental like to work in groups. Most fear traders are among the synthetic and reflective traders, while the greed traders are mainly found in the pragmatic and experimental realms. Please note, however, that there are also different levels here. Not only is water cold or hot, it can also be lukewarm.

Concrete chances against big players

Attached Image

Hello dear subscribers,

the new video is online and, as always, you will first receive the English translation. You can find the link from the video at the end of my post.

In my last two videos I showed you how to analyze your strengths and weaknesses in order to increase your chances and minimize the risks. Today we want to compare the strengths and weaknesses of the big players with the retail traders and work out where our greatest opportunities lie. As always, it is my personal opinion, which of course can be very different from other traders. Many traders assume that the big players have formed a secret consortium, coordinate, work together and manipulate prices. However, I see these statements in a somewhat differentiated manner. Of course, the forex market and the stock market are not a game, there is a real war here, which the big players decide in their favor with their superior weapons. The biggest big players don't have to work together because they use similar approaches and therefore see exactly what their competitors are doing. They are more likely to fight against the institutional and retail traders that are losing the most money in the market. We retailers are the largest in terms of the number of traders, but we also suffer the highest losses. To take advantage of our best opportunities, we must first understand how the big players differ from the retail traders.

First of all, the 100 biggest big players who work in Forex EURUSD have enormous capital with which they can move the market. Often this is borrowed capital that usually comes from their customers. The retailer, on the other hand, works with equity that can be multiplied again through the leverage of the broker. The biggest big players in the world work without stops and are even able to push their previously collected orders into the red at short notice without getting into trouble. Most retail traders use stops that the big players need to fill their limit orders. By the way, virtual stops are an interesting alternative for retail trailers to protect themselves from brokers. The big players use iceberg orders on the limit side in order to be able to enter and exit the market unnoticed. Retail traders mainly use market orders to enter the market. Market orders are easier to identify than iceberg orders.

The largest big players in the world use highly complex algorithms that coordinate the collaboration between their limit and market orders. These algorithms are programmed to deal with the misjudgments made by retailers, who often rely on indicators. The big players have to be seen as a kind of army that operate according to clearly defined strategies, while the retailer is left to himself and pursues his own strategies. The big players are not able to get 100,000 lots at the push of a button, so they are forced to collect in an accumulation or distribution phase. These collecting phases can last several days, while the retail trader can get in and out immediately. The big players have a direct exchange or Forex connection, while the retail trader may have several brokers in between. There are significant differences in the speed at which orders are executed. The biggest big players in the world work with a very professional team consisting of analysts, programmers and traders, while the retail trader has to do everything on his own.

Due to the collection campaigns, a large team and clear strategies, the big players are not able to react as quickly as the individual retail trader. Thanks to modern technology such as microwaves, the big players are able to execute massive orders within milliseconds. The retail trader is limited by his internet provider and the latency of his broker. Most retail traders trade on the stock exchange on the side, while the big players work full-time almost around the clock. This also explains the enormous differences in the area of profit opportunities. In certain situations the big players are at risk of generating massive losses. These losses are doubly tragic because it is their customers' money. Due to the legal regulations, a retail trader can lose a maximum of his account balance. The big players work with very high-quality technology in the area of their computers and servers, while many private traders trade with their cell phones or laptops. The big players move the market while the retail trader can only let himself be dragged along. Therefore, a misjudgment often costs more money than if you can move the market.

The big players trade in the Forex market with very low costs, which a retail trader can only dream of. Since we often have several brokers in between, we incur significantly higher costs. However, due to different constellations, the big players take a significantly higher risk than a retail trader. On average, the largest 100 big players trade a trading volume of 166,000 lots per day, in contrast to the retail trader who only trades one lot. The big players use the forex market to carry out a currency exchange or various hedges for their customers. You earn high commissions from this without having to take any risks. The largest number of retail traders use this market almost exclusively to make a profit. The 100 largest big players have specific volume information in the forex market that they even sell to institutional traders. In contrast, a retail trader does not receive any of this information. In my opinion, the biggest big players in the forex market even have an emulated DoM, built from the existing volume and their own information. This deep market insight is not possible for a private trader.

It is also interesting that the big players know exactly how retail traders work, while retail traders do not know how the big players work. The biggest big players work in their own market every day while we are guests in their market. This creates the effect of the home game. The hard skills of the big players, i.e. the technology, the servers and the Internet, are over 30 years old and have grown over time. A retail trader is forced to develop these hard skills first. The same applies to different strategies that have been improved and optimized over the years. Your hardware was built by professionals and is serviced and optimized daily, while a retail trader has to take care of it himself. Over the years, the big players have developed optimal trading software, while the retail trader has to access third-party software. The biggest big players clearly control the markets, which is comparable to a giant ship on the ocean, while the retailer sits unprotected in a small nutshell. Over 1 million retail traders exchange information with each other in various forums every day and reveal very interesting information, while the big players remain silent.

Let us first compare the statements made by the big players with the retail trader and rate them as strength or weakness. In summary, we can see that the strengths of the big players roughly correspond to the weaknesses of the retail traders. Here we can already see the clear dominance of the big players. Let us now consider the clear advantages of retail traders. We know that the big players work with outside capital and outside capital is never as efficient as own capital, since interest has to be paid on outside capital. In principle, this is an advantage, but initially it does not help us in direct trading. The big players are forced to build up their positions for hours or days, while the retail traders can get in or out immediately. This point is definitely an advantage for us. Due to different constellations, the big players are only able to react slowly, while we retailers have a clear advantage here in the area of speed. Of course, the big players can make massive losses and thus have a significantly higher risk than a retail trader, but the big players don't seem to care. In this respect, these points do not bring us any particular advantage in retail.

From my point of view, there are two clear advantages on our part. We can get in and out at any time and don't have to build and defend positions for hours or days. Another advantage is that we can react very quickly in order to quickly buy positions or to exit positions. Another important point is the fact that we retail traders are able to read out the algorithms of the big players with specially filtered software. In many of my videos, I have already shown you how to identify the algorithms of the big players in order to achieve trading advantages. We know that there are no patterns in price, candles, or indicators. However, there are clear patterns in the algorithms. Algorithms are orders in order to coordinate limit orders, iceberg orders or market orders with one another. These are programs that are always called up and therefore have clear patterns.

We have selected our only three chances: We can get on and off at any time, are able to react quickly and can read the algorithms of the big players. Now we come to the exciting question of how can we use these opportunities to our advantage? Well the answer lies in the word quick. If we can react quickly, but do not implement this in our actions, our advantage is wasted. This is one of the reasons why I specialize in scalping, for example. With the help of my Bionic candle in the tick chart, I get a clear overview of the course through the identification of the key candles. As soon as one of these key candles is activated, the algorithms that are read from stock market data help me to make the right decision.

Then everything goes very quickly, the entry into the market, from then on my pip value runs per minute, which informs me about the current risk. My tones help me to determine the algorithms more quickly, which then help me to exit. As we know, the high-frequency traders are clearly superior to the big players with a win rate of 99%. Of course, I cannot compare my seconds scalping with a high frequency trader, as the special technique is not available to me. It's not about getting better odds than the big players, but rather about getting better odds than the average trader. And whoever manages that already has a considerable market advantage. The sentence: It is not the big ones who eat the small ones, but the fast ones the slow ones, is given a special meaning. You will find specific information and ideas in my numerous videos.

Let's get to the summary:

Out of almost 30 points, there are only three points where we are superior to the big players. The entry and exit, the speed and the reading of your algorithms. If you manage to use these three opportunities to your advantage, you can significantly improve your chances of winning and at the same time reduce the risk. Virtu is the largest high frequency trader in the world, and analysts have found that their approach is almost risk-free. For this reason, a small stop of 1.5 pip, a TP of 3 pip within 1-2 minutes is also a comparably low risk for me. With this approach you can still trade very well even in calm market conditions, I have already talked about this in numerous videos.

Something I would like to point to here, based on my own career and experience, in line with what you are saying Michael .....

The big participants are entities or as some people call them, companies, corporations or organizations. Whichever label you give them, they are public, they are present and they are constantly involved as they have to be...it's part of their working model. The big players' iceberg orders

Attached Image

Hello dear traders,

I have produced a new video on YouTube on the subject of Icebergorders, which can also be uploaded with English subtitles. However, as always, you will first receive my English translation. Since the number of pictures at FF is limited, please watch the video after reading the text. You can find the link from the video at the end of my post.

In today's post we will take a closer look at the iceberg orders. What is the difference between native and synthetic iceberg jobs, where and when are they used? We create a profitability analysis of iceberg orders compared to normal limit and market orders and look at some examples where iceberg orders are increasingly used. The distribution of iceberg orders based on the total volume is also interesting. As always, my contributions are only about my personal opinion or experience. The measures available to traders have not changed significantly for centuries and probably millennia since the first type of trading venues were established. The speed with which certain orders are delivered to the exchange, how the exchanges process them and give appropriate feedback has changed significantly. Also, the market data has changed significantly, mainly due to the improved technology and bandwidth. Market data today enables much greater market transparency.

If a big player wants to push the course down, he has to collect the dollar first. He can achieve this with limit sell or market sell orders. Then he has to get out of his position and sell the dollar with it. For this he uses either limit buy or market buy orders. Before he pushes a rate up, he has to collect the euro. This is done with the help of limit buy or market buy orders. To realize his profit he has to sell the euro on the high. To do this, he uses limit sell orders or market sell orders. Now you must have noticed something. With a limit buy or market buy order, the big player is able to buy the euro or sell the dollar. With a limit sell or market sell order, the big player is able to buy the dollar or sell the euro. If the euro is bought, the rate will go up over the long term. If the dollar is bought, the price will go down in the long run. If the dollar is sold, the situation is unclear because we do not know whether the big player has only made a partial sale or is already out of his position. In the event of a partial sale, the price would continue to rise. If the big player is out of his position, an equilibrium would have to arise again, where a new player collects. The same applies, of course, if the euro is sold. For this reason I have concentrated on specially filtered limit orders that show me exactly what is currently being collected. In the equilibrium we see that bid was primarily collected. First the shortraders are taken out, then the course goes down. In the equilibrium we can see that the euro has been collected more strongly. We see the resulting result on the chart. For these individual actions, the big players use iceberg orders, which we will now take a closer look at.

Due to the high demand, most exchanges offer traders who trade large quantities the opportunity to place iceberg orders in the market. Big players want to hide their orders because orders generally reflect the intentions of their owners. Great traders are considered to be more informed and influential than the average trader. If the intention of a large trader becomes transparent to other market participants, it would make it difficult to execute at the desired price. The iceberg order is used to reduce the risk of a strong price movement while hiding the future strategy. This is a limit order in which only a fraction of the total order volume is displayed in the order book. The rest of the volume remains hidden. Only when the still dormant (outstanding) peak is executed will the next hidden part of the iceberg volume be revealed. This process is repeated until the original order is fully traded or canceled. However, this also means that an iceberg order is only effective at one price level. Iceberg orders are nothing more than limit orders that are controlled by algorithms and absorb market orders at certain price levels. We should know, however, that absorption does not only take place at one price level, but always at several.

In the DoM we see on the right side the red limit sell orders which absorb the market buy orders and on the left side the green limit buy orders which absorb the market sell orders. Behind the limit orders are the tranches of the iceberg orders, which are not visible to a market participant and which gradually advance. Let's imagine an iceberg, the visible orders in the DoM are the small iceberg that is visible to us above the surface of the water. The greater part that is hidden from us lies beneath the surface of the water. As soon as the first tranche of the iceberg order has been cleared by the market orders, the next tranche of the iceberg order slips until it has been fully traded or deleted.

The CME only supports two types of iceberg orders: native and synthetic. Native Iceberg orders are managed by the exchange itself. All new tranches are treated as changes to the first order, so the original order number or order ID is retained for the entire duration of the iceberg order. Synthetic iceberg orders are submitted by independent software providers whose infrastructure is physically separated from the exchange. These software vendors split the original iceberg order, submit new tranches, and track their execution. These tranches cannot be distinguished from the usual limit orders of other participants. Identifying native iceberg orders is much easier because the order number doesn't change until the iceberg order has been fully processed. The big players work almost exclusively with synthetic iceberg orders that generate different IDs, which makes identification considerably more difficult.

Let us now consider an example of a flow of native iceberg orders in the Limit Buy area. Just like customers at a supermarket checkout, the limit orders also have to line up. The 8 lots on the Limit Buy side are at the very front and the 10 lots at the back. A 200 lot iceberg order is now placed, which is divided into 10 tranches of 20 lots each. Now the first tranche comes into the queue and slowly slides forward. As soon as the first tranche has been executed, the next tranche is added. This continues until all orders are executed or deleted beforehand. It is similar with the synthetic iceberg orders, they are also the same size, but with different IDs. If different synthetic iceberg orders are issued and are partially deleted by special algorithms, this can make a specific identification more difficult. Let us now take a look at whether iceberg orders are worthwhile, we will make a comparison without calculating costs, spreads or fees.

We start collecting at different limit levels. The price goes up and the big player collects bid on 6 price levels. The price is pushed down 10 ticks then the exit takes place. The aggregate advantage here would be 1,570 ticks. Now the big player does not collect with limit orders but with 200 market sell orders, which are activated by 200 limit buy orders. He also gets out of his position at 1.10100, the aggregate advantage here would be 1,470 ticks. Now the collection takes place through iceberg orders, the price initially runs upwards, where the big player collects 200 lots with his iceberg orders at a price level. The price is pushed down 10 ticks, then the exit occurs at 1.10100. The aggregate advantage here would be 2,000 ticks. This means that collecting with market orders brings 1,470 ticks in this example, collecting at different limit levels produces 1,570 ticks and collecting iceberg orders gives the big player 2,000 ticks. That is an advantage of up to 40%. In addition, the actual strategy is obscured by the iceberg orders.

Iceberg orders account for around 30% to 60% of the total trading volume. Over 50% of orders for synthetic icebergs are canceled before they are fully fulfilled. The orders for synthetic icebergs use an average of 4 to 5 tranches with an average peak of 4 to 5 lots. The average total volume of orders for complete synthetic icebergs is between 10 and 20 lots. It's interesting to note that the order sizes are often multiples of 5, such as: B. B. 10, 15 or 20. The iceberg orders are therefore used more frequently than originally assumed, and these are increasingly smaller jobs. Iceberg orders are mainly used to absorb the stops from retailers. However, stops have the peculiarity that they are at different price levels, which is why the big players are forced to occupy several price levels with their iceberg orders in order to absorb the decisive volume of the stops.

The price has gone down and up again. In the case of the blue arrow, strong absorption took place as it ran up. Many now believe that a large market player will defend this price level in the future. At first the price went down, then came the rude awakening. So now it goes down. Bad luck again, because there was still a stop hunting, only then did the price go down. If there is a very low volume in the market and suddenly stronger absorption takes place, this is noticeable. Stronger absorptions usually do not occur randomly, but are precisely planned in advance. An example of this is a major currency exchange.

A large company wants to exchange the dollar for the euro to pay salaries. This is an exit from the dollar, which the customer bank completes in this case with market buy orders. Normally the currency exchange would be complete, but the volume of 1000 lots would be distributed unused to different market participants. Now a friendly partner bank could place a 1000 lot iceberg order in the form of limit sell orders at this price level and would immediately have 1000 lots on the bid side. Normally you would have to collect many hours for this, but only at different price levels. What happens now? Market participants see that a big player has placed a 1000 lot market buy order in the market and will suspect that the price is going up. The partner bank will, however, push the course down. When exchanging the euro for the dollar, the situation is exactly the opposite. Exit from the euro with market sell orders from the customer bank. And the interception of the volume with limit buy orders from the partner bank. Everyone thinks the price is going down, but the opposite is happening. The currency exchange euro for dollar can, however, also be processed differently. The customer bank gets out of the euro with limit sell orders and the befriended partner bank invests 1000 lots in the form of market buy orders at the same time. Everyone believes that the price will now go up, so there will first be a downward stop hunting before the price then goes up. The same game also works when exchanging dollars for euros. The customer bank exits with limit buy orders, while the partner bank activates its sell orders brand. Let's look at a specific example of this.

The price was pushed up briefly and a currency exchange took place at the high. The customer bank sold the dollar with market buy orders, which the partner bank accepted with a limit sell iceberg order. The other market participants now thought that the price would continue to rise and placed themselves long. The partner bank then pushed the price down, triggering the stops of the long traders and thereby accelerating the price. Partner Bank exited the dollar just before the low. In the further course the partner bank and also the customer bank tried to collect the euro. And then pushed the course upwards together. The next currency exchange took place there. The customer bank has exchanged the euro for the dollar for its customers with limit sell orders, whereby they have also sold their euro positions from the low at the same time. The Partner Bank entered the market with orders. The majority of market participants now thought that the same game as 6 hours ago would repeat itself and are now short. This created a large upward spike. However, that was of no use to the big players, as they could not get out of their major positions at that point. Due to a partial dissolution of their position, the price went down again. The price was then carefully pushed upwards, with more and more long traders entering the market, which enabled the partner bank to gradually liquidate its position. Conclusion in 12 hours: Thanks to a clever collaboration, two banks have made a profit of 200 million in the Forex market. After, the transfer of the 100 million that the partner bank transmits to the customer bank is very exciting. However, there are very interesting design options that would go beyond the scope of today.

This approach is prohibited by the supervisory authorities, but from my point of view it is relatively easy to prove this offense by the banks. Either the supervisory authorities are unable to understand this approach or they accept this state of affairs. It remains to be seen why there are laws at all if one is not able to monitor them. In the end, the stupid one is the retailer who doesn't know what's going on or doesn't have enough funds to take action against it. We can get angry or upset about it now, or we can just turn the tables and use this information to our market advantage. There are exchange software vendors who claim that their system can capture the majority of iceberg orders. In my next video we will talk about identifying iceberg orders and how the software can help us with that.
