Market makers and high frequency traders are the first to react, so their actions are the fastest global news feed, not the news itself. We have talked about this many times. The currency strength I often mentioned is a clear plus in the foreign exchange market that does not exist in the stocks and futures markets. From this you can get additional, in-depth information that gives us a clear market advantage. Incidentally, the rough currency strength can be read off immediately in every chart. Take the EURUSD as an example. Here two different currencies are traded against each other. The first currency symbol, the euro, shows that the euro becomes stronger when the exchange rate rises, while the second currency symbol USD shows that the dollar becomes stronger when the exchange rate falls. For the US dollar Swiss franc, the rate must rise so that the dollar becomes stronger and the CHF falls so that the franc becomes stronger.

On the right we see the green line that shows the strength of the euro while the red line shows the strength of the dollar. The price of the EURUSD falls if the dollar strengthens, the euro weakens, or both factors occur. In this example, you can use the currency strength to identify almost every reversal point in advance. Anyone who knows how to deal with this currency strength has a clear market advantage. In this case, the euro and dollar strength are compared with the respective seven main currency pairs and therefore provide very precise information. Precisely because this topic of currency strength is a very decisive factor in trading, I will once again produce a very detailed video about it. Please also pay attention to the two resistance zones that I drew in at the beginning, we will take a closer look at them in a moment. My first resistance zone did three pullbacks that lasted 3, 8 and 9 minutes respectively. I usually only spend between one and four minutes in the market. The lower, stronger resistance zone only had one return, but it went up a little more in 11 minutes. After that, the price broke through the lower resistance zone. You can find a lot of information about the crucial key candles in my videos. Many traders believe that a big player always buys the dollar at the high and the euro at the low, but that is a mistake, because there is usually little volume at the high and low. That means that not enough can be collected there.

In this case the dollar was bought in the two equilibria in H1 and shortly before the low there was an exit from the dollar. Only then was the euro collected in the subsequent equilibrium. Then the exit from the euro takes place. The euro is collected again, then the exit takes place. The euro is collected one more time and then the exit takes place again. Then the course was pushed down, a new equilibrium was created where bid was collected. Only then did the course continue to decline. The principle is always the same.

In my last video we noticed that with the limit buy and market buy orders, the big player is able to buy the euro or sell the dollar. With the limit sell or market sell orders, the big player is able to buy the dollar or sell the euro. If the euro is bought, the rate will go up in the long term, if the dollar is bought the rate will go down in the long term. If the dollar or euro is sold, the situation is unclear, as we do not know whether the big player has only made a partial sale or is already out of his position. In the case of a partial sale, the course would continue, if the big player is out of his position, an equilibrium would first have to arise again, where a new player collects. The big players determine the market and use the limit orders for their entries and exits and need the market orders to drive the market in the desired direction. To fill their limit orders, they always look for the volume that is most efficiently found in retailer's stops. With the help of the iceberg orders, the big players can add further limit orders unnoticed and thus collect ask or bid without being noticed. Interestingly, the average iceberg orders are between 10 and 20 lots and not, as we previously thought, an extremely high number of lots. Of course there are also extreme absorptions, but they only arise because a large player makes volume available to himself. The iceberg orders have been studied in great detail by various analysts, and it turns out that iceberg orders accounted for 20-60% of total sales. Many small iceberg orders at different price levels make it difficult to precisely identify the absorption and continue to help the big players to dominate the market undetected.

Banks usually have to accumulate many hours within a narrow range in order to then push the price in their direction. For this reason, they are also able to provide themselves with liquidity. While the price is slowly falling, massive iceberg orders are placed in the limit sell price levels above. At the low, the algorithms completely withdraw the iceberg orders and at the same time start to shoot market buy orders into the market. This triggers the stops of the shortraders and catapults the course upwards. The big player now invests 1000 lot market buy orders there, which he intercepts with his own limit sell orders. He is now 1000 lots short and 1000 lots long invested. Due to the 1000 Lot Market Buy Order, the market's reaction is bullish, massive buyers are now entering the market. These buyers are now gradually being intercepted with iceberg orders, with the big player slowly exiting its euro position. Then he pushes the price down and the stops of the long traders help him. At the low, he begins to exit his dollar position. Conclusion in 4 hours 30 million profit, normally it would have taken him at least three times as long to collect in the Equilibrium. We come to the identification of iceberg orders.

There are various well-known software providers on the market who claim that their stock exchange software can identify a large number of iceberg orders. We will now check to what extent these statements are correct. First of all, it is important to understand how iceberg orders are identified. In the case of native iceberg orders, clear evidence can be provided using the order ID. However, only if the same number of limit orders have been executed within a certain period of time. The entire iceberg order can only be reliably identified after the last tranche has arrived. The tranches of synthetic icebergs are normal limit orders. An incoming order is considered a tranche if it is placed within a short timeframe after a previous order of the same size has been executed at the same price. This results in the following clear differences to native iceberg orders. Since more than one order comes into question as a higher-level tranche, the synthetic iceberg order is best represented as a network diagram of orders. Then the executed size of the order is an aggregated amount of the executed volume of each tranche chain. Since the recognition process as such is speculative, normal orders can also be classified as iceberg tranches under certain circumstances. This means that synthetic iceberg orders can only be estimated heuristically and on the basis of a number of assumptions.

In the S & P500, the proportion of native iceberg orders is just 4% and the proportion of synthetic iceberg orders is over 30% of total sales. Incidentally, the share in the euro US dollar is twice as high. In principle, however, it does not matter how high the share of iceberg orders is in the total turnover, the overall distribution of the native and synthetic iceberg orders among each other is decisive. Of all the iceberg orders submitted, the proportion of native orders is 12% and the proportion of synthetic orders is 88%. The largest big players only work with synthetic iceberg orders, while smaller players trade with native iceberg orders on the stock exchange. What does this mean for us? If 50% of 100% of the total volume falls on iceberg orders, iceberg orders can be clearly identified for 6% of the total volume and not for 44% of total sales. Since only the big big players move the market, the clearly identifiable iceberg orders of the smaller players are not relevant in order to make a clear trading decision. Of course, iceberg orders can be identified with any time and sales list. The problem is that many smaller iceberg orders come on the market every day and cannot be clearly assigned to a possible strategy. We retailers try to track down the big players' aircraft with a car navigation system. There are roads in the sky but we cannot identify the big players as they regularly place invisible iceberg orders. And these limit orders are almost impossible to find. Footprint and volume diagrams and the market profile do not help us any further.

The statement of the software manufacturers, who advertise with a clear identification of the iceberg orders, is: We use an algorithm developed in-house to recognize and predict iceberg orders. I think that says it all. I only get specific information from the native iceberg orders, in 88% of the cases I have to rely on an estimate. If I buy a car that only does what I want in 12% of the time, I wouldn't buy that vehicle. The stock market is not about life or death, but it is about a lot of money. That's why I don't work with such software. In addition, I have to work with MBO data, which cause fees that are 3 times higher. The order book only changes when traders carry out new promotions or conditional orders are released according to their maturity settings. Consequently, exchanges generate market data and inform traders of changes. Today there are two different types of market data. Market-by-order (MBO) describes an order-based data feed that offers the option of displaying individual orders and their development. The information of the order includes its unique order ID, the limited price, the size and its position in the queue. MBO usually offers full market depth and describes orders at every price level. Market-by-Price (MBP) describes a price-based data feed that offers the option of displaying the total size of all orders at each price level. MBP can either describe the full depth of market or a limited number of closest bid and ask price levels, e.g. 5, 10 or 20 price levels. At first glance, the upper split limit sell order offers more information, of course, but what is the purpose of these orders? Should the dollar be bought or is it an exit from the euro? Are there still enough market buy orders coming into the market to keep moving up or is the price reversing? I do not get this information, for this reason the MBO data is only a clever marketing strategy for most traders on the part of the stock exchange and the software provider.

We know that certain big players have priority in the queue at the exchanges. This leads to the conclusion that their placed orders are always as close as possible to the price execution. In trading, the rules of exchanges are set in the form of matching algorithms and, in some cases, different latency priorities. These rules can favor certain types of market participants like registered market makers by offering them higher matching priorities or even adding artificial speed bumps for other traders. The Chicago Exchange was the first to propose artificial speed bumps designed to delay the actions of incoming traders by 350 microseconds, except, of course, certain market makers who were allowed to use the freeway. Initially rejected as discriminatory, the proposal was later approved not only for Chicago but also for the New York Stock Exchange and other stock exchanges. One of the arguments in favor of admission was that exchanges already offer an advantage for registered market makers in various forms, including, for example, position determination in the queue. Now it's getting interesting: These rules that the stock exchanges have drawn up can be viewed as fair because they are public. Traders who know the rules of the game can adjust their trading strategy accordingly, may find markets with better rules or choose not to trade at all. This means that as a retailer you know that you will be disadvantaged on the stock market, if you still trade and lose, then it is your own fault because you have previously accepted the rules of the game.

Of course, trading consists only of assumptions that each trader receives based on his or her individual information. The more specific and precise this information is, the more accurately a trade can be executed. In addition, we should know that the more participants follow a similar strategy, the lower the chances of winning. The big players are usually always in a better situation. You have sufficient capital to take on a variety of independent, simultaneous positions with different entry levels. Diversification and the law of large numbers are used to minimize risks and smooth profits. Incidentally, casinos also use these factors by providing several gaming tables at the same time. On this chart, the white line represents the volume of long retail positions in EURUSD at the CLOSE of each M15 candle. What is interesting is how this value goes down as the price goes up. In contrast, when the price falls, the retailer volume of long positions increases. The bigger candles are caused by the stops of the retailers and not by a massive number of market orders added by the big players. In USDCHF, the volume of long positions in retail is falling while the big players take the opposite side. It should be clear who sits on the longer lever. We see that the retailers are on the wrong side almost at all times, which also explains the high loss rates in the retail sector. For this interesting presentation, by the way, many thanks to Hanover, a very creative and professional programmer of the largest trading platform Forex Factory. I will come back to him later. There are a number of different representations of the currency strength meter. In today's post we will also look at whether currency strength indicators that cost money are superior to free ones.

The typical strength indicators give an idea of how much a currency has moved compared to all other currencies against which it is compared. Of course you can use it to see if the dollar is strong in relation to other currencies. You can use a currency strength meter to identify a strong currency and a weak currency. Many traders take advantage of this information and trade the strongest against the weakest currency. We'll take a closer look at whether this is actually a smart idea. Today's comparison is about 8 currency strengths from which a total of 28 currency pairs are formed. Let’s first look at how high a currency’s share of the total turnover of the forex market is. The NZD reached a share of 2.1%, the CAD reached 4.9%, the CHF already passed the 5% hurdle, the AUD reached 6.8%, while the pound reached 12.8%. The first three places are occupied by the yen with 16.8%. In second place is the euro with a share of over 32% and first place is the dollar with over 88%.

Here we can now see how the dollar is calculated in five different time units against the seven other currencies. Let us now compare the eight different currencies to one another. Red shows weakness while green highlights strength. In this graph, the dollar is the weakest and the New Zealand dollar is the strongest. Now you can sort the different currencies in different time units according to their strength, with the strongest currency at the top and the weakest currency at the bottom. This results in the 28 different currency pairs that we can also sort in the five different time units according to their strength. Overall, this currency strength knife is very detailed if you want to have an overview of all 28 currency pairs. Since I personally only work with the euro, the US dollar, of course, only the euro and dollar are relevant to me. From this I filtered my own currency strength meter only for the euro and dollar. The individual columns show the respective time units. In the upper area we see the dollar strength and in the lower area the euro strength. To the right of it I have once installed an M1 chart to show you exactly how this display works. The left column, where the currency strength is calculated in the M1, of course reacts much faster than in the last column, where the monthly observation takes place. Therefore, pay close attention to the first three columns.

First of all, we can see that the dollar strength is in the foreground. And now pay attention to how the dollar is getting weaker and the strength of the euro is increasing. Initially, the euro and the dollar are in equilibrium, and it seems as if the dollar wants to push the rate down again. Now we can see how the euro is getting stronger and stronger, the reaction: The price is being pushed up very quickly. Once again there is a balance between the euro and the dollar, which the euro ultimately decides for itself. Although the price is now fluctuating back and forth, we can see the clear euro dominance, which would still allow an entry to the top in this situation. A slightly different view consists of two different lines running in a 100% value. The red line shows us the strength of the dollar while the green line shows the strength of the euro. In this case, the dollar strength is around 62% and the euro strength is around 30%. First we draw a center line at 50%. We can thus see that the respective currency is strong above the middle line and as soon as it moves below the middle line, it tends to show a weak trend. Let's look at an example of this.

Above are the candles below is our strength indicator. At the beginning the course runs down a bit. In the area of the strength indicator, we can clearly see the dominance in the dollar. Now the course is going up, here the euro strength is clearly in the foreground. There is a brief pullback, but we can already see that the dollar is weakening. The course is now continuing upwards, with the strength of the euro in the foreground here too. Then there is a downward movement, the dollar has a clear advantage. The exchange rate is going up again, interestingly, the dollar rises at the same time as the euro, with the euro still having a slight advantage. Now the price is going down again and we can see the clear dominance of the dollar. When a bullish candle arises, there are theoretically three starting situations. The strength of the euro remains unchanged while the dollar is weakening. The euro strength increases while the dollar strength remains the same. The euro strength increases while the dollar strength decreases. Of course, these three initial situations also apply to a bearish candle. While the dollar strength remains the same, the euro strength decreases. The dollar strength increases while the euro strength remains the same and the dollar strength increases while the euro strength decreases at the same time. This situation would accelerate the downward movement more.

Let's look at another example in an 8 tick chart in EURUSD. On the left is the dollar strength, on the right we see the euro strength. The strength in M1 is in the middle and the time units increase outwards. Now pay attention to the two inner areas, as this is where the quickest reaction can be determined. In the middle we see the strength of the euro and the strength of the dollar in the form of two lines. Below that I have once again drawn the dollar strength individually within the 8-tick chart. If the yellow line is above the center line, the dollar is strong; if the yellow line is below the center line, the dollar is weak. Let us now observe a live price. The strength of the dollar has a clear advantage, as we can see in both the top and the bottom diagram. The price is therefore going down. In the lower area there is initially a small equilibrium, we can see that the dollar is still very strong. The euro is gradually getting stronger and the rate is rising. In this case, the tick chart display actually shows significantly better results than the upper display in the M1. We can see that the strength of the euro continues to have a clear advantage, which also explains that the price continues to rise more strongly. Suddenly there is a small breakout downwards, in the tick chart we can see that the strength indicator only reacts at this moment. The dollar strength in the M1 is increasing and the rate is falling again.

Based on this example, we can see that the strength of the currency is also lagging behind the price. And that is also logical, because after all, all currency strength indicators in the forex market are calculated from the price, and not from the volume, as the volume in the forex market is not completely available to us. Incidentally, the calculation of the currency strength within the tick chart is not entirely correct. This is simply because the other counter currencies would theoretically have to be calculated simultaneously within an 8 tick chart in order to arrive at a correct calculation. The correlation between retail volume and currency strength is very accurate. This means that the retail volume can theoretically be used as a leading indicator just like the currency strength itself. It is also important to know that it is not the indicator that is the decisive factor in trading, but rather how the respective trader interprets the data taken from it. Now let's take another look at our currency strengths on the left. We find that of the eight currencies, the dollar is the weakest while the New Zealand dollar is the strongest. If we look at the NZDUSD during this period, we actually see a stronger rise to the upside. But I generally warn against trading the weakest currency against the strongest. The background is that at the time of entering the market you can of course never know whether the current currency correlation will continue to exist.

We see that the dollar is getting weaker and the euro is getting stronger so we decide to buy the euro. The decision was right and we are getting out of the euro. The euro continues to get weaker and the dollar stronger, we now decide to buy the dollar. This decision was also the right one and we are getting out of the dollar. The euro is getting stronger the dollar is getting weaker we decide to buy the euro. A short time later we realize that this decision was not the best. From my point of view there are some possibilities for improvement in the area of currency strength, for example in the representation of how much a currency changes within a certain period of time. However, the correct way of looking at currency strength brings additional benefits that a trader can use to their advantage. I would never use the currency strength individually to get a market entry. However, it often helps me to stay in the market a little longer in order to make a little more profit. EA Expert Advisor

Hello dear subscribers,

as promised, I translated the content of my new video for you. You can find the video again at the end of the article.

Today's post is about Expert Advisors who promise huge returns for many traders. First we will look at how these EA's are structured and examine their advantages and disadvantages. Then I'll show you how some sellers tune their paid EA's in order to sell them. We are also examining the use of EA's by the big players and looking at the position of the programmers. Expert Advisors, also known as EA, are automated trading systems written in the MQL4 and MQL5 programming languages. They are designed to automate trading activities and can be programmed to notify the trader when a trading opportunity arises. Alternatively, EA's can also carry out all of your activities automatically. Order orders are then sent directly to the server, and values for Stop Loss, Take Profit and Trailing Stop are managed and adjusted. EA's follow different rules to find the right times for market entry and exit.

This can reduce emotional trading decisions to zero, which are often responsible for wide-ranging mistakes. Thus, an EA can provide an emotional stability that could hardly be achieved with human decision-making. In addition, an EA has the ability to evaluate several parameters at the same time, which the human brain would not be able to do. EAs use technical indicators to make a decision. Many factors can be taken into account in this decision, although these must be precisely specified beforehand by the programmer. The EA then implements these decisions in concrete terms, without resorting to emotions. Another important aspect is that the computer always adheres to the trading system once it has been set up, without ifs or buts. An EA is able to act around the clock, offers objectivity and distance. He does not have the negative traits of a trader such as impatience, fear, vengefulness, greedily stressed or tired. However, there are also some restrictions to be aware of when trading EAs. Robots are unable to make intelligent or important decisions. They have no understanding of the market, cannot understand or react to basic data. Likewise, they cannot adapt to unexpected market conditions.

An EA is only as reliable as the quality of the coding. Incorrect coding can lead to unexpected time delays and a small mistake can lead to unpredictable events. When a trader hires a programmer to write an EA for him, it often has consequences. If the EA works at the beginning, the trader is of course the hero, as he has provided the specifications for it. If the EA doesn't work properly after that, of course it's the programmer's fault. Basically, a programmer can of course only program what is communicated to him. Of course, there are also programmers who interpret certain things differently or who do not set up programs in a way that is resource-efficient. In addition, the human brain is able to act intelligently and flexibly. It can recognize complex patterns, weigh several contradicting factors at the same time and adapt to extreme conditions. An EA does not have these capabilities. Most EA's are programmed very simply and primarily follow the approaches of the big players less. This is also logical, since a retailer can enter and exit the market relatively quickly and usually does not work with iceberg orders. Many EAs only relate to indicators that track price. On the one hand, these are easy to program and are less based on an adequate understanding of price behavior.

Data mining and back testing is a major threat in the EAs area. Many assume that what was profitable last year will continue to be so. Over the past few years I have analyzed a few 100,000 candles and found that no identical patterns occurred. Theoretically, an EA should work the same in all markets or realize similar profits. And that is precisely what is not the case. It should also be noted that trend following systems are less popular in the area of EAs due to their low profit rate. It becomes problematic in the equilibrium, since these systems do not work there. Newcomers and beginners prefer a quick and constant profit, especially in the field of EAs, the sellers of EA's have long since understood this and are in tune with it. Added to this is the curious stopping of most market participants, always below the last low or above the last high. These are almost always caught by the big players, which makes it even more difficult to program a profitable EA. Due to the high frequency traders and big players with their algorithms, the market structures change considerably. These factors lead to subtle changes in price behavior, which also dilutes the effectiveness of EAs. Another problem is that you can't implement psychological factors into an EA. That would be important, however, since the stock market is based exclusively on psychological aspects.

First of all, we should ask ourselves why the big players don't work with successful EAs. Every year you have to pay many millions for your analysts, traders and computer experts. A successful EA could save them a lot of money with it. Believe me, a lot of experiments have already been run in this area, where the best mathematicians, physicists, economists and programmers have been involved. But if you compare the risk with the profit, it is cheaper for the big players not to rely on fully automatic EAs. We should think about that. Of course, the big players work with algorithms, which are, however, controlled by hand and monitored by the traders at the same time. However, these algorithms cannot be compared with the conventional price-based EAs. Perhaps some will now argue that the high frequency traders work with fully automatic algorithms. That's right, but arbitrage trading in this area is a completely different topic that cannot be compared with normal trading, as the risks are significantly lower there. It is interesting to note that most of the retail EAs that are sold operate at a high profit rate and low CRV as most buyers are looking for quick and consistent income. But personally, I don't like the way these EAs are advertised and sold. Let's see how easy the scammers work.

We take a moving average, a MACD and an RSI. Now we are trying to coordinate these three indicators with one another in such a way that future and profitable trading directions result from them. We now create these orders as an EA, which generates automatic entries and exits, provided that the criteria we have created are met. We are now doing different backtestings. We use different ASSETS from the area of stocks, currencies or indices. If the return is low or negative, we simply adjust our criteria and the programming again and let the backtestings run until it fits. Let us now assume, that we carried out six different backtestings and there were six different results. Then of course we take the best average monthly result and look at it carefully on a monthly basis. We recognize the first half of the year was a zero number, in the second half of the year the positive return averaged 8% per month. Now we take October, November and December as a basis. This results in an average return of 30%. Now we run our back testing again exactly during this period and of course achieve unbelievable returns. Let's look at an example that I found on the Internet. The participant started with no less than ten euros, let the EA run for four months and in the end won 1 billion euros. If that's not convincing. Of course, he also produced a detailed video so that everyone can see exactly how strategically and precisely the EA is working. Because of this advertising there are some traders who want exactly this EA.

At the end we see the overall result. If this Super Expert Adviser costs € 500 once and 2000 traders fall for it, then the seller has not earned 1 billion but at least 1 million. In fact, it seems tempting to borrow $ 10 from Grandma, then start the EA for four months, and in the end you can retire with $ 1 billion. Incidentally, if you were to use the same EA in other assets or change the period in EURUSD, the returns would look completely different. As we saw earlier in his EA video, some 30,000 lots were traded within a few seconds. In euros, US dollars, 20 million lots are traded every day; that's 14,000 lots per minute. If someone goes into the market with 30,000 lots, that's double the minute turnover in EURUSD and in the futures market that's even 15% of the total daily turnover. Incidentally, 30,000 lots corresponds to sales of € 3 billion.

Firstly, you would immediately attract attention with € 3 billion and the big players would get the volume; secondly, it is questionable whether you will even get an execution with this volume, thirdly, there is no broker who will provide you with a margin, fourthly, we forget about it often the spread, requotes or slippage and fifthly the prices or the candles are random, ie there are no clear patterns in this area. Thus, all subsequent prices or candles are again purely random and cannot be identified using a clear pattern. However, the programming within an EA is based on internal patterns. From my point of view, these factors have to be considered if you want to work with EAS.

Because of this, I am very skeptical of the EAs. Let's imagine that you are trading profitably in the long term. Now start to write down which factors have to come together in order for you to enter the market, how the market has to behave so that you remain in the trade and in the end what has to happen in order to exit the trade. If you write down all of these things carefully, you will find that your many and varied criteria could never be built into an EA. And why? Because there are just too many things that you pay attention to in trading at the same time. Nevertheless, I could imagine that the EAs could also help us in retail in the long term. But only if they show us possible entry points that enable profitable trading. However, it should still be up to the trader to decide whether to enter this trade or not. These hybrid EAs could inform the trader of things that he is unable to see.

The price and the candles are the effect, the cause lies in the market orders that run into the limit orders. Most EA s only access the effects, if you are already programming an EA, you have to realize this in the area of the causes. So consider the DoM and time and sales list as well as the spoofing data. The effect, i.e. the price, the candles and indicators do not bring you anything. The reason lies in the law of causality. Causality means that there is a clear cause-effect relationship between variables. Unfortunately, there are only effects in the forex market. I will go into this again in a special video. By the way, I recommend C ++ as the programming language, as it can implement the fastest implementation in this area.

As it stands, most EAs seem to put money into the sellers' pockets more than whoever is using them. Then honestly, if I invent a machine that predicts the lottery numbers, why should I sell this machine? Well, there's really only one good reason to sell this machine if it doesn't work. This is exactly why I would always recommend a beginner to invest a few years in order to learn trading properly and professionally instead of relying on a machine that firstly you don't know how it works and secondly you can never be sure how long it works. I would never buy an EA myself, because the EA don't understand the basics of the market and he can never make his own decisions. However, this is a crucial point in order to have a chance at all on the stock exchange markets.

To the left of the chart you can see the heartbeat of a trader who is currently opening a trade. Within a short time the heartbeat increases by almost 40%. Depending on the situation, it can also be significantly higher. A good reason to take a closer look at the topic of health in trading, because there are 1000 diseases, but only one health.

Healthy and fit in trading

Hello dear subscribers,

In today's post you will get some tips on how to get healthy and fit through everyday trading. We talk about how to avoid back problems, get fewer headaches, concentrate better on the market and of course also about the dangers of CO2 when trading. I will show you how you can control your heartbeat on the computer screen and how you can possibly improve your health values. With a few tricks you can achieve a lot with little effort. The tips I mentioned are for entertainment purposes only and are not to be understood as medical advice. Basically, I always recommend following the advice or recommendation of your doctor. A few years ago there was a worldwide statistic that showed that only about 20% of the world's population is really healthy. Most of them are not necessarily terminally ill, but neither are they healthy. I found that terrifying. In addition to back pain, depression and iron deficiency, there are many other things that limit our lives considerably. A family spends around € 100 per month on health, which is only around 4% of household income. We humans want to live as long as possible, which is why one should also invest in one's health, which is not always related to the issue of money. The fact is that humans consist of what they eat, drink and how they move. For this reason, in addition to money, you should also invest the appropriate time in your health.

Maybe you know the rule of three. Humans can survive 3 minutes without air, 3 days without water and 3 weeks without food. Let's start with the CO2 first. Carbon dioxide is a chemical compound of carbon and oxygen with the empirical formula CO2. In high concentrations this gas can be toxic to humans. Outside there is a CO2 value of around 450 ppm (part per million). In closed rooms, especially in winter, the value can increase significantly. Carbon dioxide dissolved in the blood activates the breathing center of the brain in a physiological and slightly increased concentration, which means that the brain receives too little oxygen. This is a common occurrence in closed rooms, you get tired and get severe headaches. For values below 800 ppm the air quality is rated as good, values between 800 and 1500 ppm are considered moderate and above 1500 ppm the indoor air quality is considered low. Then at the latest you should ventilate. When I was trading I often forgot about that and it made me tired, unable to concentrate and got a headache more quickly. For this I bought a CO2 measuring device that informs me about the current values at any time and even warns me acoustically above a certain limit value. The test winner at Stiftung Warentest is available from 70 €, an investment that has paid off for me. Since then, my concentration has increased and headaches are a thing of the past.

One of the main reasons for migraines and headaches is dehydration. No wonder, because the brain consists of 95% water. The next time you have a headache attack, it is better to drink a liter of water than to take the pain reliever immediately. We often confuse feelings of hunger and thirst and eat instead of drinking. It can be seen that the cravings are significantly less if you drink enough throughout the day. Our synovial fluid decreases over time. This can result in disc problems, rheumatism, arthritis and back pain. Having enough water keeps our joints supple. Water brings us more beautiful skin because our metabolic processes function optimally. This means that more nutrients can be transported into the cells. When trading, you often forget to drink, which is why my cell phone reminds me every hour to drink a glass of water. So I get around 2.5 liters of water per day. The result: more energy and improved performance, which we need when trading.

With all the contradicting dietary recommendations, one often no longer knows what to eat. Healthy nutrition means: Enjoying a variety of foods! The top priority of a healthy diet is and remains: Eat varied and mainly plant-based foods. The more varied the diet, the lower the risk of deficiency symptoms. A healthy diet is extremely worthwhile. It not only provides you with all the nutrients you need to have enough energy for the day, but also a variety of vital substances that help you stay healthy or - if you are sick - get well again. The right diet has a direct effect on your well-being and your ability to concentrate.

Smoking is the most common cause of death in our industrialized countries, although there are still over 30% in Germany who smoke, but the number of smokers is declining. In 1990, 30% of the 12 to 17 year olds smoked, today it is only 10%. The side effects that smoking causes bring many other disadvantages as well. In addition to yellow fingers and teeth, the stench and annoyance from cigarette smoke is an unpleasant side effect. The nicotine in a cigarette increases the heartbeat by around 20-30%, i.e. a resting heart rate of 80 instead of 60. If you stop smoking and eat as much as before, you still gain weight. That is also logical, because an increased heartbeat leads to an increased consumption of calories. When I stop smoking, the increased heart rate is automatically reduced. In recent years, the e-cigarette has enjoyed great popularity. It's not healthy either, I cannot say whether it is healthier than smoking. According to some experts, the e-cigarette seems to contain fewer harmful substances than a conventional cigarette.It smells less and the cost is even 10 times less. If used correctly, the e cigarette can be a slow way to quit smoking, as you can change the nicotine content individually. Interesting that the big cigarette manufacturers first railed against e cigarettes and are now selling e cigarettes themselves. If you stop smoking, you will not only relieve your lungs, but also your heart.

Most traders pursue their activities on the stock exchange as a part-time job, which means that they have a busy main job and use their free time to learn to trade. A full-time trader obviously spends more time in front of the screens, either sitting all day or standing in front of a high table. Neither is good for our spine, because just walking or lying down ensures an even distribution of our body weight. Changing the sitting position also only provides a short-term remedy. Either you use a treadmill when trading, which is not very practical, or you put your legs on the desk, because raised legs are good for blood circulation. The right desk chair is also crucial. I myself use a typical gamer's chair, the prices for a good office chair are between 150 and 1000 €. You can find suitable reviews on the Internet.

By the way, people spend a third of their lives in bed, which is why I recommend you invest in this area in particular. The right mattress, pillow and duvet is the key to the right relaxation in order to be fit the next day. A very good mattress with 7 lying areas is not expensive. With a duvet, the heat distribution is crucial and the pillow should optimally support the neck. Find out more about it on the Internet. I have been using a sleep app for many years, which informs me about the most important factors in my sleep. Of course, it is clear to me that this information can only be approximate. Nevertheless, you can compare them with each other. Over the years, I was able to try out different scenarios in order to be optimally rested the next morning. I sleep much better when I have eaten less in the evening and exercised enough during the day. Then the next day I am much more concentrated and also more successful. It doesn't always have to be the expensive Apple Watch, there are also cheaper providers such as Fitbit, with which you can also make calls, the battery even lasts for a week and does not have to be charged every day. Of course, these fitness watches also record all sporting activities, which can then be evaluated individually. Whether walking, jogging, cycling, swimming, fitness or bodybuilding, what the right sport is, everyone has to decide for themselves. The only important thing is regular exercise in order to stay fit in the long term. According to the experts, you should take at least 17,000 steps a day, the average for German citizens is just 4,000 steps. Nevertheless, you can always do something preventive for your health.

The reason why many traders cannot break away from their screens is the fear of missing out. As a full-time trader, you should take regular breaks, especially after a previously defined series of losses. I've found a good solution to this and it's called OBS. This is a screen recording program that records all of my trading screens in my absence. This means that I can precisely analyze these times when I was not in front of the screen, even on the weekend. Incidentally, the program is free and can of course record in 4K. Part-time traders in particular can use it to record the market on a daily basis during their absence and analyze the market in their free time. The advantage is that everyone can watch the crucial trading hours without having to sit in front of the screen all day. If you feel like showing your heartbeat on your screen while trading, you can master this challenge with OBS. You may need a suitable fitness watch or a Bluetooth chest strap for this. It is also interesting to mention that the more trades a trader has made, the lower his heart rate will be when he places a trade. So it's just a matter of regular practice. Information on how to connect OBS to your fitness watch can be found in this post on Youtube.

Another headache factor has to do with our eyes, which are focused on the screen throughout the day. The older you get, the more common these headaches become. This has to do with the muscles in the eye that are responsible for focusing visual acuity. Presbyopia begins at the age of 45 and affects many people. Many years ago I had multifocal lenses inserted, now I can see 100% in both eyes until the end of my life. At the age of 57 I can recognize the smallest letters on my cell phone and even sit in front of the screen for up to 15 hours without having trouble concentrating or having a headache. A lot of things related to health can be found in the blood. The most important are, liver values, blood lipids, C-reactive protein, iron, blood sugar, total protein, uric acid and thyroid hormones. The small blood count determines the most important cell classes in the blood such as red and white blood cells, platelets or the red blood pigment (hemoglobin). The more complex "complete blood count" also contains a subdivision of the white blood cells. I would recommend checking these with your family doctor at certain intervals. This will prevent many future problems.

I am neither an extreme athlete, nor a vegan or vegetarian, but I try to eat healthily within a reasonable framework and do enough exercise. From my point of view, the most important thing is to drink enough water every day as it detoxifies our body. I rarely drink alcohol, maybe 1-2 glasses of wine a week. As a seconds scalper in algorithm trading, I complete up to 30 trades a day, for this I have to be absolutely focused and fit at my age. Trading is a passion for me, but not an addiction. I measure my success by strict adherence to my trading plan, not by the size of my trading profits. Since I am usually between 1-3 minutes in the trade, I have 1 hour of trading time per day. I invest the rest of the time on projects in order to generate even deeper market insights. Balance is the decisive goal, I try to avoid the factor "too many" or too few" and try to find a healthy middle ground if possible. Of course, I don't always succeed, but in the end the will is what counts. If you can't do what you want, you have to want what you can. Because to want what one cannot do, would indeed be unwise.

Big players in the equity, currency and futures markets

Hello dear subscribers,

In today's post we talk about the biggest big players in the stocks forex and futures market. We look at the corresponding sales of the various assets and compare them with one another. Where are the biggest big players and why are they not so easy to identify in certain markets? Why is there a higher probability of winning in one market than in the other and how can you reduce your liability risk? Why do some big players avoid certain markets? These are just a few of the questions we are dealing with today.

I've spoken to a lot of traders over the past few months and I've noticed a few things that I'm going to talk about today. There is still a huge gap between forex CFDs and future traders. From the point of view of some future traders, CFD traders are pure indicator traders who have little idea of the actual market process. Even as a staunch Forex trader, I cannot share this assumption. As a rule, a beginner actually starts trading CFDs and develops into a future trader over the years. First of all, we should know that we only trade with probabilities in the stock futures and forex markets. Now we turn our attention to the profit probabilities in the individual markets. We discover some interesting aspects. In the stock market the loss rate is 91%, in the forex market 90% and in the future market 80%. What is striking here is that a clear, dramatic loss rate is evident in all three markets. In the stock market, the profit threshold quota is around 5%, these are participants who achieve neither losses nor profits in the long term. In the forex and futures market, the profit threshold rate is also 5%. The results are diffrent, when it comes to the profit ratio, in the stock market it is 4%, in the forex market 5% and in the futures market even 15%. This means that the profit rate in the futures market is three times higher than in the forex market and even four times higher than in the stock market. Where do these big differences come from?

The stock market is one of the most difficult markets in the world because it is where most high-frequency traders are up to mischief, there is little liquidity in the limit orders and this automatically results in higher volatility. In addition, you need very special knowledge, especially in the area of business figures such as balance sheets and much more. There are many unfair brokers in the forex market, and price manipulation is still taking place abroad. Likewise, high spreads prevent a reasonable profit ratio. The decisive factor, however, lies in the lack of volume, which does not give the trader any insight into the depth of the market. At first glance, this speaks absolutely in favor of trading in the futures market, but there are also decisive points that speak against it. First of all, there is a disproportionately high liability risk in the futures market. With a Black Swan, the risk per one lot is around € 25,000 with which you can run into the red. This minus must then be compensated. In the forex market, this liability is limited to the account balance. You can trade with microlot in the futures market, but this is not recommended for beginners as they can trade from 0.01 lot in the forex market. The account size in the futures market should also be at least € 20-30,000. In order to generate a deep market insight, professional software and a corresponding data feed are required. This may cost an additional 1000 € per year. In addition, the price movements in the futures market are not as finely tuned as in the forex market. This makes it difficult to identify crucial price ranges, especially when scalping. Likewise, there is no currency strength in the future market that we have often talked about in my videos.

The largest asset in the stock market is the Apple share, in the forex market the EURUSD is the leading player and in the future market the S&P. We compare the Apple share in the stock market and in the forex market, the S & P in the forex and future market and the EURUSD in the forex market with the euro FX in the future market. Apple shares a daily volume of 65 million, with a price of $ 121. That's equivalent to a daily turnover of $ 8 billion. With an average lot value of € 100,000, Apple shares would trade 80,000 lots per day. The S&P Future has a volume of 2 million per day with a contract value of 20,000. This corresponds to a daily turnover of $ 40 billion and the averaged lot value is 400,000. The S&P in the Forex market has a volume of 3 million with a contract value of 20,000, which corresponds to a turnover of 60 billion. The averaged lot value is 600,000. The Euro FX in the futures market has a volume of 200,000 with a contract value of $ 125,000. This corresponds to a daily turnover of $ 25 billion, the averaged lot value here is 250,000. The euro US dollar in the forex market reaches a volume of 23 million with a contract value of $ 100,000. This corresponds to a sales volume of $ 2.3 trillion or 23 million lots. Let's compare the number one in the Forex market with the number one in the futures market.

While 400,000 lots are traded daily in the S&P Future, the euro US dollar comes to 23 million lots. The total volume is almost 60 times larger. Now let's look at the distribution of the 100 largest big players in these markets. The 100 largest big players have a turnover share of over 80% in the euro US dollar. That means on average each of these big players trades 183,000 lots per day. The 20 largest big players achieve a 40% share of sales. On average, each of these big players trades 460,000 lots per day. This means that the remaining 80 big players still achieve an average turnover of 100,000 lots per day. In the S&P, the distribution rates are not quite as extreme as in the euro US dollar. On the one hand, this is due to the fact that the S&P predominantly has a large number of institutional traders who are more evenly distributed in their capital structure. Of course, for us retail traders, an institutional trader is big, who trades $ 360 million a day in the S&P. But these institutional traders are small compared to the real big players in the euro US dollar.

The 20 largest big players in the euro US dollar are able to trade the entire turnover of the S&P per day. I believe that you can see that it would make no sense for such a big player to act in the S&P. This is roughly comparable to when we go to a casino to win at the ATM and have a few million with us. The machine would not be able to process that much money that day. Let's take a look at a graphical size comparison. The share of EURUSD in the total forex market is 29%. The USDJPY comes in at 14%, the GBPUSD at 9%, the AUDUSD at 6%, the USDCAD at 5% and the USDCHF at 4%. In 15th place comes the USDCNY with a share of 0.5%. And that is exactly the size of the S&P in the futures market. So far this was probably not so well known because there is no real volume in the forex market.

As we know, the foreign exchange market was founded many decades ago so that banks could operate independently of the stock market and at very low cost. The banks have not thought of opening up this market to private investors one day. Likewise, the origin of the futures markets did not actually lie in speculating on the market as a whole with greater leverage. Futures markets were only used, to secure a price today that could be bought or sold in a few weeks or months. This was particularly important in the area of raw materials and also for crop failures in wheat. This has changed significantly to this day, since with futures and derivatives, short-term speculation is increasingly in the foreground.

The question that arises: does the futures market influence the foreign exchange market or does the foreign exchange market influence the future market? If someone buys arithmetically massive DAX futures, the DAX is initially not automatically affected. Because the DAX is the arithmetical result from the prices of the 40 stocks listed in it. But what would happen if the DAX future rose by 100 points but the DAX itself did not? And it is precisely these differences that are permanently balanced out using what is known as arbitrage. Large arbitrage traders take advantage of these differences at lightning speed. And so the futures markets and the strike prices on which the futures contracts are denominated are inextricably linked. And it is precisely for this reason that S&P Future and Forex, for example, have almost tick-accurate, parallel courses. This makes it possible to use exchange data from the Euro FX to make clear predictions for the EURUSD currency market. But which market influences which one?

If we compare the Apple stock in the future market with the Apple stock in the forex market, the turnover in the cash market is less important. Therefore, the future market will clearly be the driving force here. The turnover in the S&P Future and Forex market is similar, so both markets will influence each other equally. The cash market is the clear leading factor in EURUSD. Of course there are also influences from the futures market, but this is immediately offset by the arbitrage. The fact is that the markets influence each other, which should also be taken into account in trading. The main reason why I only trade the EURUSD in the forex market is the clear distribution of sales among the 20 largest big players. These big players rarely get in each other's way because they know exactly what the other is up to. This inadvertently creates a joint consortium of big players who are thus heading in a common direction. That enables me to identify the big player even better.

In my charts I use specially programmed limits to show me exactly the limit orders that will be relevant in the future. We see that the big players collected bids on the high with larger limit sell orders. The price was pushed down a bit and the bid collection was continued within the new equilibrium. Now the price has been pushed down again and we can see that this time bids were still being collected in two different equilibrium zones. At first there was a little stop hunting, then the course was pushed down. There was once again a short post-buy in the limit sell area and then larger limit buy orders were used, with which the big players got out of their dollar position. In principle, the process is always the same.

A little tip, I know some market participants who basically filter the 1 lot of sales out of the Time in Sells list, because they are insignificant from their point of view. Interestingly, the big players are precisely those who use these 1 lot orders massively within their cumulative orders to push the market in a certain direction, or to include corresponding stops by retailers with their limit orders. Here we see a cumulative market buy order with 11 lots. In the individual display within the Times and Sales list, 75% of this order consists of 1 lot contracts. The cumulative market order with 15 lots consists of 50% 1 lot contacts. And last but not least, a market sell order with 22 lots, which contains nine individual 1 lot contacts. It is precisely these 1 lot of contacts that are used in the market order area in order to be more difficult to identify in the market. In this overview, 121 lot market buy and market sell orders came into the market within 3 minutes, all of which were of course also taken up by limit orders. The number of contacts in the limit area that was interesting for me was only 48 lots. This is important in order to find out what the big players are collecting more. We have talked about this many times in my videos.

For me, a very decisive advantage in the forex market is the higher volatility within the candles, as the futures market moves 7-10 times less in the same period. As a result, significantly more information is passed on within my Bionic candle that helps me in daily trading. Since the beginning of the corona crisis, the big players have started carrying out various experiments in the EURUSD. As we know, your biggest disadvantage is that you often have to collect Ask or Bid for hours or days that can only be made possible by very complex stophuntings. In the last few months, new and interesting strategies have been developed, which have been backed up with appropriate algorithms. We will take a closer look at the strategies they use to carry out their collection campaigns in one of my next videos.

Reasons for Algorithm Profiling

Hello dear subscribers,

As promised, I translated the content of my new video for you. You can find the video again at the end of the article.

In today's post we talk about why it is important to perform algorithm profiling. We use an example to analyze the average sequence of a big player collection up to and including the exit. I will also show you the clear advantages of algorithm profiling and why this is the future. Most traders dream of the holy grail, but when it comes to algorithms, we are getting very close to that holy grail. We know: on the stock exchange there is only compensation for pain and suffering - first comes the pain, then the money! But for this you need an approach that is only used by a few market participants. This increases the probability of winning and gives us an enormous market advantage.

I can still remember when I started trading in the forex market 12 years ago. One day I found an indicator that was relatively simple. It only produced a yellow and blue dot. So I did what had to be done. With the yellow dot, all you had to do was take a long position and wait. As soon as a blue point appeared, the long position should be left and a short position should be opened at the same time. Wow, I thought that’s so easy. As soon as a yellow point appeared, the short position had to be left and a long position had to be opened at the same time. And that's exactly, how one could happily deal with the individual zigzag zones all day long. From 6:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., it would theoretically have been possible to achieve 160 pips times five lots, because you don't want to be too greedy. This results in a monthly income of € 200,000 for 25 trading days. At that time I was still thinking about writing an EA for it, otherwise I would not have had time to spend all that money, as many shops close at 8:00 p.m. How that ended in the end can of course be imagined by anyone. This was a repainted indicator, which although deposited a blue point, but also deleted it again if the price continued to rise. In principle, this indicator is like a defective watch, after all, this watch shows the correct time twice a day. Many years later I came across this indicator again in the futures market, but this is not an indicator that deletes the points or arrows that were once placed. At first glance this seems tempting, but on closer inspection in the M1, you would have incurred losses ten times in a row, which you would not have recovered in the subsequent downward movement.

Quite a few traders have reached their limits in search of the holy grail. The assumption arises again and again that there are recurring patterns in certain situations. But the truth is rather sobering. The fact is that unfortunately there are no samples in the price. There are also no patterns that are triggered by messages. There are no patterns in the candles, because the candle is a statistical coincidence that arises from time and price. Logically, there can be no patterns in the indicators, since an indicator in the Forex market mainly follows the price. Even in even price levels, we do not find any clear patterns. Also not in an equilibrium that 70% dominates the market. Not even in the all-important currency strength. Even if we analyze the exchange data from the futures market, we cannot find any clear patterns within the volume. The only last anchor left for us is the cathedral and the T&S list, but unfortunately I have to disappoint you, because there are no clear pattern sequences either. But there are clear patterns in the algorithms, i.e. in the orders with which the big players control their limit and market orders. The algorithms have different tasks, on the one hand to place actual orders and on the other hand, for example, to identify stops or to play an illusion on the market. In order to represent these algorithms, a time-consuming creativity is required to highlight certain factors. From this, clear patterns can be identified in the limit orders or the key candles can be displayed with my Bionic- candle. The fact is that there are clear patterns within my individually programmed tones. You can find more information on my channel. Samples are also available within spoofing, from which clear future price developments can be derived. Let's look at some examples of algorithm profiling so that it becomes clearer. To do this, we look at a process that takes place at an airport, which runs in the same way over and over again.

We see an empty airplane that has docked at the gangway, I would like to equate this with a big player entering the market. There are different factors to identify this market entry, such as a stronger increase in limit orders. When an aircraft is docked on the gangway, what conclusion can we draw from what will happen next? Well, most likely the passengers will be boarding in a moment. And that's exactly what happens then. Let us imagine that the passengers represent the orders that the big player collects within the equilibrium. We can recognize this in the market, for example, with specially filtered limit orders that are increasingly increasing on the ask or bid side. What will happen when all passengers are on board? Now the plane will go to the runway, as if we had suspected the plane was taking off. The big player has now completed its collection campaign and is starting to push the market. Not in the direction we expected, however. This can be recognized by the fact that the strength of certain limit orders is above average. When an aircraft has taken off, in most cases it has to make a 180 ° turn in order to clear the airspace at the airport. This is comparable to the stop hunting that the big player now carries out in order to stop the traders who are oriented in his profit direction. The strategy used for this is very interesting, which we will take a closer look at in my next video. Now the aircraft begins to climb in order to reach the necessary cruising altitude. In this phase, the big player begins to push the price towards profit. This can be seen from the pulling of the limit orders so that his market orders get through more easily.

On the flight there is now stronger turbulence, the pilot decides to fly under this turbulence and reduces the cruising altitude. In this situation, the big player decides to sell the push orders that he previously used to push the market in his profit direction. This creates a small pullback. This can be recognized, for example, by larger absorptions on the limit side, also known as stacking. The turbulence is over and the aircraft starts climbing again in order to reach its optimal flight altitude. After the pullback, the big player pushes the price back towards profit. We see this in the area of void execution, where sizes are permanently taken out of the market to make it easier for market orders to get through. The aircraft is now almost at its destination and starts to land. In this phase, the big player prepares for the exit, few push orders come from his side, there is hardly any stacking in the profit direction. After the plane has landed, the passengers now disembark. While most market participants are now moving strongly in the direction of the trend, the big player is taking the opportunity to get out of his positions with increased stacking. After the passengers have disembarked, the aircraft is cleaned and possibly even serviced. The big player has booked its winnings and may be out of the market. The number of limit orders is now falling significantly. Of course, it also happens that the big player gets involved again in a re-accumulation or distribution phase.

We have now seen a schedule for a big player. Each of these individual phases is accompanied by different algorithms that have been individually programmed for the respective situation. Each phase is an individual program that controls both the limits and the market orders. Each of these programs has individual patterns that appear again and again in the same sequences. Everyone can understand the following situation. When I enter the market, it would be a great coincidence if the big player entered the market at that very moment. So that will usually not happen. Now let's assume that I come into the market and realize that the big player is just starting his stop hunting. What is the advantage of this? First of all, I can use the patterns in the algorithms to check whether it is actually stop hunting before an outbreak. And now I have the decisive advantage that there is a high probability that I know what will happen next. However, I don't know the exact time yet. With the help of the algorithms, I can read out the point in time at which the big player begins to push the price towards profit and thus significantly increase my probability of winning.

Algorithms are not that easy to program, so it can be assumed that they will be used for many months before they may be optimized or changed. But you get that out relatively quickly and can adapt accordingly to the new situation. Precisely for this reason, one should work in markets that have an unevenly distributed share of financially strong big players in the upper range. You can find more information in my last video: Dominance of the big players. Most people at the airport do not even notice what is going on outside on the tarmac, while the tower has a complete overview of the airport. It is the same on the stock market - most market participants do not know what the big players are doing. So if you want to have the right overview, you have to sit in the tower. For me, this tower is a strategic algorithm profiling, in different market sequences. We have already talked about that.

I have already presented the identification of my special limit orders in many of my videos, this is a rough overview to see in which area you collect or exit. The bionic candle, the strength of the limit orders, pulling and stacking, sell and buy pressure, up to the currency strength are just some of the information that comes together on my 75 inch main screen. The sole aim is to increase the probability of winning through an effective assumption. Scalping is also very beneficial in this area. As Karl Meyer Rothschild put it so nicely: on the stock exchange you have to behave like bathing in cold water, jump in and quickly out again. One of the clearest goals that we are wrong with a trade is to feel right. And that's exactly why I prefer to rely on algorithm profiling. It's like a kind of navigation system to know exactly where we are. We will go even deeper into the field of algorithm profiling in the next few months. In my next post we will first talk about some as yet unknown big player strategies that have just been carried out as experiments in the EURUSD due to the corona crisis and are now increasingly being used.
